The exams are a little difficult and the lecture slides have barely any information on them, but Anna is a very passionate and knowledgeable teacher! There's a lot of extra credit in the class and exams are open note. The class covers very interesting content.
good professor with open note exams. clearly very knowledgeable on the course material

honestly, i only attended two lectures all semester and still did great. very easy, textbook's definitely not required and assignments are absolutely loaded with extra credit. i still learned a lot, the content was fascinating. lovely teacher, and she brought in lots of guest lecturers. recorded lectures in canvas media gallery.
Her lectures are amazing and intrigued me into learning more about the content. However, her tests can be hard, just beware. It is open note and open internet though.

Exams are open note. Weekly quizzes are short but ensure your basic understanding of the material. Content is interesting and Anya (Anna) is very knowledgeable, but lectures can be boring still. The slides can be confusing, as the slides themselves don't really explain the material, it might just be a picture with a couple words.
Really nice dude, easy grader

Dr. Cardentey's sheer knowledge and clear passion for the subject matter were refreshing. You could tell throughout the course that he truly wanted his students to understand the nuances of the region through sci-fi, as it would improve us as students across all of our various majors. Truly recommend!

Expect to participate 1-2 times each class, and make sure you're doing the weekly assignments and readings since those same topics will be brought up during lecture to be discussed. Really enjoyed the times I got to speak with native speakers around the world for 30 minutes, and learn more about their lives while also improving my Spanish.

prof cardentey is amazing! almost all assignments are collaborative, and i left the class feeling way more confident in my speaking skills. 10/10 would take this class again and would recommend to anyone taking spanish at tech!!

Dr. Cardentey was extremely knowledgeable about all of the course material and was extremely interesting and enthusiastic in his lectures in class. This always made me excited to come to class and I feel like I learnt the most in the class, compared to the numerous other Spanish courses I've taken thus far at Georgia Tech.
He made 3rd party assignments that were heavily weighted that would often not work and refused to allow me to redo them or fix the site.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this course online, and it was great. Because there were no in-person lectures, we had to do 50-minute weekly Zoom conversations with small groups, but they were pretty low-stress. Dr. Cardentey gives great feedback and his class has helped me fine-tune my Spanish skills. He is also very caring and flexible. Definitely recommend!

Dr. Cardentey is awesome! He is organized and is nice. We had a lot of interesting discussions in the class and he is easy to talk to. He understands if your Spanish is not perfect and realizes that we are here to learn. He is a pretty easy grader, there is consistent homework you have to do to know what's going on, but it only takes like 10 min

A great professor, he truly works hard to make sure students improve their conversational skills, while also not penalizing students for not speaking perfectly. He is focused on improvement rather than perfection. He does expect engagement and participation but doing the work and participating will help you improve and get an A.

Dr Cardentey was a very caring professor and did a great job of keeping the class engaged. There was a lot of homework but it was graded generously. The professor was easily accessible outside class and genuinely seemed to want his students to succeed. Highly recommend!

This class is the essence of CS in the theoretical and "parlor-math" side. Proofs are relatively easier compared to CS 3510 and discrete, but make sure they're still sharp. Lectures important, OH for the proofs are EXTREMELY important, and reading the textbook for definitions/practice is important too. I messed up with late HWs (21 credits moment).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer. However, his exam grading is really strict and a lot of points are taken on simple things. That said you will learn a lot from this class. It tends to get a bit difficult around exam 3 and exam 4. There are 4 exams worth 21 percent each and around 12 homeworks with some of them having a lot of extra credit and weekly quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very inspirational.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ladha is an excellent lecturer and incredibly helpful and insightful for the right kind of student. If you are well-suited for Computer Science (especially with anything algorithm-heavy), you will thrive in this class. If you find yourself struggling in this class, take it as a sign that CS is not for you.

I enjoyed his class, but he's not for everyone. He can be overwhelming since he talks quickly. I learned a lot from his class, probably the most of any class I've taken. If you're willing to put in the work, he's a great option. Would be nice if he had short breaks during class though. Recitation and plus sessions are super helpful, esp before exam
He is the best option. Those complaining lack skills.

He talks about class content for around 20 minutes each lecture and goes off on tangents for the rest of the class. The class is almost fully test-based, and each test has like 4 questions that are worth 25% each. He was happy about a 40% class average on a midterm for the 75% of the class that didn't get a 100. Don't take this guy.

The exams take a while to get used to, but are doable if you pay attention to lectures. All lectures are on YouTube, so coming to class is very optional. Definitely a learning curve in general, but nothing too extreme. Lectures are clear and concise, tests are difficult but not impossible, and homeworks are time consuming.
Tests are hard, but he's fair
Exams are very difficult.

Ladha was appointed by Allah (Subhanahu wa ta'ala) to serve and spread light unto the students of Georgia Tech. During every lecture, you will certainly feel a divine presence. O' Allah, lead the disbelievers to the truth and they will accept Ladha (PBUH) as their prophet.

ladha is a terrible teacher. his intelligence and mastery of discrete is heavily undercut by his arrogance. his grading is arbitrary at best. his exams are extremely long and difficult, with about ~85% of the class still writing when time called on every exam.

homework takes more than 8 hours a week and doesn't prepare you for the exam at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are hard and the partial credit is unforgiving. Lectures are alright. If you're prepared to spend 6+ hours per week on the weekly homework, quiz, and staying locked, you can get a B or above. Just be prepared for a terrible time with TA's, the professor, and in general. Ladha should absolutely be your last choice.

worst class ever. don't even consider just take someone else. he clearly cannot take criticism either. either he or his tas write their own positive reviews and get negative ones taken down. you can tell the positive reviews are super short and lack nuance, unlike the negative reviews. i don't know how he still has a job at gt. avoid.

This is a decently difficult class. He is decent at lecturing, although he moves EXTREMELY quick. Tests are extremely difficult and often nothing like the practice tests, and he tries to fear monger by saying that if you use AI for help, you're cooked - which I don't believe is true. I and anyone probably could have got an A if I tried hard enough.

You can definitely learn a lot from Ladha's class. It's true that people can get lost in the lectures without prior knowledge of the content. He is highly accessible. The course is test-heavy, you'll find some exam questions very similar to practice exams or homework, while the rest are of medium difficulty problems in Leetcode.

If there was not a grade associated with this class, it would without a doubt be my favorite class I've ever taken. Ladha is a great lecturer, and the subject matter is extremely fascinating. The tests are just so. Damn. Hard. And difficult to prepare for. Sometimes studying can feel futile and impossible, but it's fun at the same time. Duality.

His lectures are actually somewhat interesting. But other than that this class stinks. The homework assignments would take me and my friends several hours each week, and are most of the time just overkill and don't prepare you for the test at all. The stuff he gives you to study for the exams are just stupidly hard compared to the exam.
Great instructor. Hands down the best one for this class.
Absolutely horrible. I legitimately think the TA's write the the 5.0 ratings
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: super passionate lecturer, great if you are genuinely curious about the class. not too hard either, if you go to lecture and actively participate. his textbook and lecture videos make it easy to make up class if you fall behind as well. overall very nice and understanding professor.
Brilliant teacher. Course is on the easier side, but it's been taught very thoroughly.
He is honestly the best option you could take for this class. Hands down.

Ladha himself is a good lecturer and a good person. It's his TA's that make the class a nightmare. Just because they went through hell in their semester they think it's their turn to give us hell back. HW's took 6+ hrs per week and exams had singular questions worth 5+% of your COURSE GRADE. Absolutely do not take this class under any circumstances
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests are completely unrelated to homework, test review, and lectures and are worth 84% of your grade. Homework takes multiple hours and is extremely difficult. TA's are largely useless. It's sad since Ladha is a nice guy and a good lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think Ladha is a chill guy. However, it's pretty clear that the expectations of the course don't really align with the reality. I don't think the exams are fairly written and there should be, at the very least, an exam drop for this class (like other CS2050). The TAs need less power though; they practically run the course and not in a good way.

Take if you are 100% sure that you will attend all lectures + solve all homework + all practice problems + spend a lot of time trying to combine your knowledge from the lectures with the extremely difficult practice problems, and expect even more "creative", harder questions to appear on your exam. You need to practice as if this is your only class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: GOAT! Super accessible in office hours and all his lectures are available online. In fact, the course should get more challenging.

Incredible lecturer and understands the course material extremely well. Posts all his lectures online and homeworks are pretty reasonable. Very exam heavy with 4 midterms and a final that replaces a midterm (if needed). Exams are difficult (basically 4-5 leetcode questions) but graded relatively leniantly.

This class actively regressed my knowledge of discrete mathematics and math as a whole. If God wished to give his strongest warriors a challenge, he would send students to CS2050 Office Hours to face the awful TAs for this class. Such students would emerge Navy SEALs.  Ladha is a terrible lecturer and teaches content that cater to few. Do not take.

Horrendously terrible. He clearly writes his own RMP ratings (or has someone else write them for him - check the two from 12/2/2025). Terrible lecturer, lectures way too fast, writes awful exams that don't test content well. The homework is near impossible and should not constitute adequate assessment for an introductory class. TAs are evil. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: In industry, there is no autograder or project that you can flounder on for days on end until you get it right. There is time pressure, and if you aren't precise under pressure, you are axed. Having a majority of your grade come from test is totally reasonable, get used to it here before it's too late.

Why is this called an intro class. Homeworks take min 6 hrs a week, TAs cant help much, it's too hard. Test reviews are so useless from TAs. If you get a C on 1 exam, no chance of an A.

He's a nice guy, content itself isn't even really that bad, but the class structure is absolutely abysmal. Save yourself the headache and transfer in the credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 84% of grade is exams. If you do minor mistake in your proof, you can loose a lot of points. Exam practice materials are a lot more difficult compared to the lectures. If exam materials included like 5 practice exams rather than just 1 practice exam + a problem set with some overkill problems, class average would probably be a lot more higher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests were way harder than homework and grading is incredibly harsh. Lectures are useless. Avoid at all costs.

Honestly he's a pretty good lecturer. He's very knowledgeable and uses hard examples in class so that test/HW questions don't look like something we've never seen before. I definitely don't like the 84% tests as I got shafted by one and it made it impossible to get an A, but it happens. The problem isn't him, it's the TAs who make bad test review
He writes his own rate my professor rating and deletes negative ones. that should tell you enough.

Exams are a majority of the grades for this class and he stated himself the distribution of grades is an inverse bell curve meaning half the students on every exam get well below a failing grade. On exam 2 I lost 25 points on a problem for not including the method of proof I was using. I would not recommend unless you just love the subject.

The class has gone to dumps. Ladha is a nice guy, ok lecturer….but the structure of this course is truly unforgiving.

The grading is incredibly difficult with no clear guidelines. There is a HUGE lack of communication between him and TAs. 

He admits to making exams too hard but won't do anything about it. My advice - just transfer in this class.

Absolutely ridiculous. Take someone else. Ladha's class is much harder than other teachers. Lectures are very fast and hard to follow and hw is very hard and doesn't prepare you for tests. The tests also have unbelievably harsh grading. Your grade shouldn't be this dependent on the teacher. AVOID AT ALL COSTS, YOU'VE BEEN WARNED.

Exams are deceptively easy; Ladha makes up ridiculous reasons to take points off, almost never related to the correctness of your answers.
Grading on all assignments is slow and harsh.
Lectures are painfully useless. Homework is tedious and does not prepare you for the exams.

Ladha seems to confuse ineffective teaching for rigor. Do not take.

Exams are 84 percent of our grade. Practice exams are much easier than the real exam. Exams have way too many problems for the time allotted (since the questions are very hard). Homework takes 8 hours each week, if you can even figure it out. Every assignment in this class feels like I'm rolling the dice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely splendid. People say he doesn't care about your grade, but that cannot be further from the truth. If you don't want to learn, you will absolutely fail. But if you are willing to learn, to think, and interact with him, you will do good.

Very passionate about the subject material and always made sure to explain thing in detail. I didn't have anything to compare him to but I have heard that his classes are harder than ones given by other profs.

As a professor, Ladha was a good lecturer; however, the class was structured on the assumption that students already have experience in discrete math. Lectures were fast-paced, homeworks required a lot of time and work, but weren't really great for learning, and exams were very difficult.

Professor Ladha is a funny guy at times and is pretty accessible outside of class, however his lectures rarely correlate to what's on the exams and he's much more difficult than other professors. The people who tend to like him are the traditional nerds (no judgement), and the people who don't like him typically have a life outside of their classes

Ladha and the 4510 course he led was definitely one of the greatest course I had at Tech. Lahda has the best lectures. The assignments are all amuzing and inspirational with carefully chosen materials.  Grading aren't too harsh.

It might take a bit of familiarity with proof and passion in math and theory to enjoy. But that's a fair ask.

Not for beginners. He teaches as if you already know the material, only 3 second pause for questions after a problem, and often goes on tangents. Lectures feel like a race to keep up rather than a chance to learn. He might suit advanced students, but as someone who was new to discrete math, I found him incredibly difficult and unhelpful.

Best professor I've ever had at georgia tech. Lectures go really fast and cover a lot of content but are really fascinating. Be prepared to pay attention and ask a lot of questions during lecture though

This course may be a good indication for whether or not a student has an aptitude for computer science and should stay in the field. It is the first CS course that cannot be passed through memorization and regurgitation, and requires interest and ability to do well.

The entire course is on YouTube, which I find very helpful. Not every question is answered on ED, which I guess is ok. I made some friends while taking the course, which was far more helpful than any TA/professor help. Not the worst, not the best.

Ladha is not a proffessor for the weak and disinterested. If you are interested in discrete math or CS theory, definately take him. This class is a great introduction to not only discrete math, but general proof writing, and Ladha will make sure you understand your fundamentals, even if tests can be a little bit hard than other professors.

Homework is long and difficult, generally containing problems that don't help with exams. Exams themself are very tough, and difficult to study for as there are minimal resources in the class. The lectures are face paced, and hard to follow and take notes for at the same time. Overall, more stress than there should be for this class.

Ladha is the goat, as long as you go to all the classes and do the homeworks, you will be fine in the class. He shows clear understanding of the subject, and is passionate about it. Test 3 was hard, and Test 4 was a little challenging, but the first two tests were pretty light. 100% reccommend.
Great prof, teaches concepts well. Class isn't easy but it's pretty fun

DO NOT TAKE LADHA. He is so passionate about this subject but doesn't understand that not every student can comprehend Discrete Math as much as him. He made his own exam which was way harder than other professors. For one exam I remember the TA's telling us it was so much easier than the previous one but everyone agreed that it was much harder,
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
The 3.3 is primarily because of 2050 reviews, I've heard thats not his priority plus he teaches quite advanced things that freshman cant handle. 

Best prof hands down for 3510, you're doing yourself a disservice not taking him. I know its hard, but if you have to take a single hard class at Tech, this is it and probably the most worth it one too.
Great guy and best class ive taken at Tech. Excited for 4510 w him.

GOAT. If you're at Tech to coast and non interested in learning he's not for you. If you want to grasp the most fundament algorithms with insane clarity then attend every single one of his lectures and annoy him in OHs with any questions, they're almost enlightening. Best prof at Tech imo. Plus content of this class helped me land a FAANG job.

Very tough class imo, but Ladha is a cool guy who is generally pretty sane. I'd recommend taking another professor if you want an easier class, but Ladha ensures that you get a good conceptual understanding of the content which I can say that I got. I didn't like how he lectured as it was super abstract and not applicable to hw/exams.

Ladha goes into more depth than the other professors, and his tests are slightly more challenging. His YouTube playlist of recorded lectures covers all of his lecture's content. His homeworks are difficult and time-consuming, but helpful in the end. He knows this subject very well, and is very willing to help and explain.

Ladha is inspirational even if you already knew about the topics beforehand. If you aren't strong in math (at least 5 Calc BC and the likes), expect to work harder. Exams requires more creativity than the other sections. Office hours are very helpful, and Ladha himself occasionally hosts in-person last minute recitations in the TA office hour room.

Don't waste your time taking Ladha. His exams are unneccesarily difficult and the homeworks are lengthy and hard. The only bright side is that there is extra credit and the CIOS does come in clutch, but everything else is terrible. Take Ronnie or Brito.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing lectures with the catch of going at a very fast pace. The lectures go rapid fire with Ladha and he assigns a lot of homework with new topics. Important note, Ladha added on interesting topics near the end of the course for F24, but these segments were added onto the existing CS2050 work. Absolutely recommended if you are more math inclined!

Don't do it
Take Brito

Literally the greatest lecturer I've ever had. Tests were really hard though, even in comparison to other sections, but the questions were really engaging and fun to do. Everyone giving bad ratings got skill issued. Idek if I have an A but I'm manifesting for finals

Edit: I did get an A

He's a funny guy, and teaches pretty well. Lectures are optional, but they're really good for learning the content. I would say this class will teach you algos really well if you go to lecture esp from a math point. Tests are difficult and easy to mess up, so you have to study a lot outside of class but Ladha is accessible. TA's are decent

He's a great teacher and willing to help, but his tests are pretty difficult.

If you're looking for a chill 3510 class take ANYONE but him, if you want a challenge take Ladha.
Usually he will boost your grade by a few points at the end of year.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One thing Prof Ladha does well is teach content relevant to skills required in the workforce. Besides that, homeworks/exams were quite difficult. Little study material was given (no recorded lectures, but had a practice exam for each test and TA-transcribed notes that were okay). Would definitely take a different professor, not worth the struggle.

Algo is a mindset that you need to practice a lot over the semester in order to get into it. Ladha does a good job lecturing, but his lectures are not for everyone. He also really cares about the students. Only main issue I had with the class is partial credit was few and far between which lowered all my exams a lot--but that is mainly a TA issue.

Ladha's lectures are quite interesting, especially if you are someone who enjoys math, but beyond that it's terrible. The homeworks and exams are hard and are incredibly time consuming to study for/do. On top of that, there are literally 0 resources for studying for exams, aside from a mediocre packet written by TA's that couldn't care less.

Overall, this class was tough but definitely fair. Ladha's lectures are good, and the additional lecture notes on canvas were very helpful for homeworks. Exams weren't easy, but there was at least 3% bonus to final grade by the end of the year. 3510 will be easier if you have a leetcode/competitive programming background, but I did fine without too

The professor is clearly very passionate about the subject and topic, but he doesn't necessarily convey the course content in ways that make it easy to understand. You have to put in the time and energy to study the course content yourself. Also, the TA's don't really do much in the course - if you get how the course works you'll get an A.

He is extremely passionate about the subject matter and is clearly very smart, but his lectures often are difficult to follow if you aren't prepared. He is also super chill and very accessible - his office was open every time I was in the computing building. Exams were difficult, but doable. If you go to class and office hours, you'll be fine.

Time consuming hw, but the proofs on the hw and in the lectures are extremely similar to the ones on the exams so you will be well prepared. Ladha gets a lot of hate for structuring his class different from the other 2050s but it's really not that difficult. He's a fun and engaging prof who really wants to teach students as much as he can

Lecture could be a little bit fast but it can be very entertaining if you focus. most of the grade is dependent on 4 test and the test itself aren't too bad. The most test review are ok, but some are very bad but i think it more of a TA/logistic problem. Overall solid prof to learn from

Ladha is incredibly passionate about discrete and an excellent lecturer. He goes far beyond surface depth while also going out of his way to make sure students understand. However, his tests and homework are harder than Brito. I still got a high A and didn't have to spend much time on the class, but I would take Brito if I could go back.

The lectures were highly theoretical, fast paced, and hard to follow at times. Weekly homework was difficult and time consuming, especially if you don't have anyone to work with. If you have a good understanding of the homework and lecture notes, the exams are very manageable. Great if you're up for the challenge, if you want an easy A not so much.
The homeworks are overly difficult and the lectures aren't the most helpful. I found that the textbook and practice questions within it were useful in helping me learn and study though.

A lot of these reviews are incredibly very overblown. Ladha is very fair; he doesn't require you to attend lectures (even though i'd advise so). He also publishes the entirety of his lecture notes, so if you read those you are guaranteed to do pretty well. His HW questions are sometimes hard, but again it's definitely doable using your notes.
was clear on what it took to succeed in the class, tough content but ladha is funny and was even willing to do office hours right before the final. goat

He is very passionate about the subject, and has made me extremely interested in the material too. Other than that, the homeworks are tough and the TA's can't help, with many of them telling me to use ChatGPT to check. There's no extra credit, the exams take so long to be graded, and he teaches in a way where he expects us to understand every step.

Ladha is tough. Had a few tests where our class specifically had a little extra material to cover. But he taught comprehensively and if you want to learn and are willing to put in the work for it, you wont have a choice but to. Tough but very forgiving if you mess up or have concerns about the class. Was late to 2 tests and he let me in to test. A+

Ladha is a passionate and funny lecturer, but the homework was hard to the point where I've had multiple instances where the TAs didn't know how to do the questions. The exam reviews were ok but not the best for studying for the exam. The exams are hard as well.
It was a really difficult course do not reccomend this teacher at all

Lots of conflicting thought. Look, most 'negative' reviews are probs lazy students who didnt study, and 'positive' reviews could be overachievers/TAs. However, the disparity with other profs is HUGE. So much so that many TAs couldnt answer Ladha's HWs. Ok If you like math & genuinely want to learn properly. If not, like me, take Brito/Ronnie.

Lectures were confusing and the professor's handwriting was hard to read. Visual learners will struggle. Homework was graded harshly, exams were tough, and review materials were unhelpful. Miscommunications between the professor and TAs added to the confusion. This class was unusually hard for a 3-credit intro course. Would not take again.

It's my 2nd year here. I understand that discrete math itself is not rainbows and puppies but Ladha's lectures are not great.. especially when you have no background knowledge of any of this stuff. I've watched a YT video and learned more in 20 minutes than his 75 minute lectures. Ladha's passionate/funny, and well, that's all I can give him.

Ladha is clearly used to teaching much higher level classes. His lectures, while entertaining, are theory heavy and often don't correlate with the exams, especially past the halfway point. The class basically requires you to have at least some math theory background knowledge. If you don't, take Ronnie. Your grade will thank you. He's funny though.

Actual paid reviewers dropping 5s. You can't tell me that a class that gives out prep material 3 days before the exam, with bad TAs who don't even know what they're talking about, combined with a lecturer whose lectures are over random niche proofs rather than actual surface material that we should be going over is good in any way. Save your sanity

Professor is overly hard and every other professor is easier. Practice problems were nothing like on the actual test. Lectures are useless and not useful and he goes way too fast. Highly don't recommend.

Take Howard or brito. His homeworks and exams are much harder and HWs have completely unrelated material to the exams. TAs are completely useless and are about as knowledgeable as the average student. Ladha just thinks he's Tony Stark of discrete math or something.
Ladha's lectures and homeworks are very different from the exams and are always much harder than the other professors' exams/homeworks. Save yourself the headache and just take Ronnie if you can.

Ladha is extremely smart and knowledgable. I hear "what--is going on?" about five times a day from the collective class of students. I was never able to catch up on what he was lecturing about until I got to the HW and was finally able to understand. Exam 3 was EXTREMELY hard and is what killed my grade. Probably getting a C unless final is easier.

The worst 2050 professor you can take. His lectures are WAY too focused on theory and fast-paced, his exams are harder than other sections, and his homeworks are the worst. The exam review feels basically useless and answer keys are rarely even given out. DO NOT TAKE.

Worst professor at Tech. He wants only the 10 students who sit next to him in class to succeed. His exams are separate and super hard there are next to 0 resources provided for studying for exams. A practice problem set is provided, which is very different from his exam, and also no solutions to these practice problems are uploaded. DO NOT TAKE HIM
His test are way harder than other proffesor, his avg for exam 3 was around 70 while other classes had high B avg

He breezes through content because he assumes it is "too easy" for everyone and often skips explanations of proofs because he "doesn't wanna" explain. TAs don't know how to do the HWs, so if you were to ask for help, there is a guarantee they will not be able to help out. He said he had a psychotic episode making exam 3- that is was "hilarious" :(

Ladha's lectures are too theoretical and fast, the first 2 exams were on material we covered weeks ago so it was hard to remember. The homeworks are way harder than the exams, and the grading is also harsh, with partial credit given for certain types of mistakes, meaning you could lose almost all the points on a question from a very minor mistake.
Tests are way harder than other profs. Only take if you've done competitive math in the past.

Unless you have an EXTREMELY strong math background take anyone else. Lectures are overly theoretical. I gave up going to lectures and had to rely on Howard's lecture videos (which were only released the week before exams) to learn everything before the exams. Difficult homework that is different than other sections. Exams are graded harshly.
Do not take 2050 with Ladha. Take anyone else. His tests and homeworks are wayyy harder than every other teacher. His lectures are extremely confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think he's a amazing lecturer, and he always writes elegant proofs. However, he goes very fast, so be prepared to learn a lot in short time. Overall, the class is pretty good and I learned a lot.
Lectures were excessively heavy. Wasted time covering useless material with no clear purpose. Content covered in the lecture was very different from the test, and was impossible to keep up with.

AVOID HIM. The absolute worst 2050 prof out there. Apparently a good prof for other CS classes, but his lectures don't correspond to the exams at all, are extremely confusing, and are useless as he only goes over theory-related material barely related to the course. Please, for the love of God take Ronnie Howard; his online videos are why I passed.

His lectures are too heavy on theory. While his first 2 tests are based on more other sections taught by other professors, the 3rd test was made by him for his class specifically, so it correlated more closely with his lecture, but the problem with this is you never know what to expect on a test.

Going to his lectures is pretty much useless. His lectures are fast and very easy to fall behind in. He assumes you already know a bunch of higher level things, even though this is a freshman class. I learned more just by doing the homework assignments than anything he ever taught in lecture. His handwriting is barely readable in lecture as well.

I took Ladha for both 2050 and 3510. I really like his teaching style though I know it is not for everyone. He just lectures and writes on the board and then leaves lots of time for questions. His 2050 and 3510 were probably more difficult then the other sections but is very approachable and one exam is dropped in both classes.

No textbook required (which is actually a bad thing for this class).
Lectures are fast, with unclear explanations, and harder compared to others.
TAs take long to grade, are bad at explaining and unresponsive.
Exam prep material given out extremely late. One time it was 5 days before, not joking.
You can't teach yourself through this class. AVOID.

The lectures are based on getting practical experience with more complex examples of the topics you fill face in your homeworks. Ladha doesn't simply teach for you to pass an exam/do HW, which I like a lot.
Very good at answering questions during the lectures.
Very good at explaining.
Greatest prof so far at Tech, would definitely recommend.

His lectures are complete trash. His notes don't help at all. He doesn't understand how his students feel one bit. I was so lost in all his lectures and he always gets distracted by some fringe topic that has nothing to do with the class.

This class was outstanding, thanks to Professor Ladha's incredible teaching. Despite the challenging content, his generosity in grading and crystal-clear explanations made it manageable. Truly an amazing and inspirational professor!

I loved this class and Ladha is a great professor. The content is difficult but he is generous in grading. He's also really good at explaining concepts. The best part is he records everything on YouTube, so you can go back and watch lectures you missed or didn't understand. 10/10 class.
3510 can have some tough topics and Ladha does a pretty good job of articulating the algorithms. He gives a good amount of extra credit but this class is still a grind.

If you practice study guides and rewatch his recorded lectures carefully, you should be fine for the tests. Professor Ladha also gave a lot of extra credits near the end of semester, and he was even willing to curve the final average via CIOS. He is also very reachable through email or office hours.

This man singlehandedly made me want to drop out of school because of how disorganized and useless lectures were. Almost none of the material covered in the lectures was even comparable with the homework, which was graded harshly. Please for the love of god choose anyone but him for discrete math.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ladha is a respectable professor and does a great job accommodating students. However, his lectures don't fully align with test material and homeworks (first time teaching this course). I recommend doing the canvas modules and practice exams. TA office hours are helpful for homework. No $60 textbook required but instead will be replaced by quizzes.

Ladha is one of the best professors ever. He was extremely passionate, gave very clear lectures, and was dedicated to helping students on Piazza. He's also hilarious. If he is ever a 4510 professor again, please take him.

He is gonna make u think you are about to get a B in the class the entire semester. And then right at the end he fixes it. Trust the process. I didn't believe him at first either. But trust. He's got u.
This class is fantastic to reinforce/fill any gaps if you have already started leetcode/ competitive programming. If not, I suggest waiting another semester before taking.

Hearing about the other teachers, Ladha seems like the hardest one.  His tests were very conceptual and each had an extra credit problem.  Also released a bunch of leetcode type questions where if you were top of the leaderboards, you got bonus points added to your overall grade.

He is a nice professor. Our class didn't even have to by the Zybook because he thought it was unnecessary and too expensive. CS2050 is a very easy class, and I feel like Ladha would be a better professor for harder classes.

For the first few weeks I attended lecture, however most of his lecture content was more theoretical. I skipped class and started watching videos from Ronnie, which was somewhat helpful. if you have a strong math education before college, this class should be light. If you are like me, you need to put in a little extra effort.
Nice professor, but lectures are pretty high level (so they don't relate much to the exams). Exams definitely aren't unreasonable, but they're not easy.

Lectures moved at such a pace that it was either way too fast or just simply off topic trying to prove something we didn't need to know for the exam, very difficult to write notes or pay attention for over an hour unfortunately.
For 2050, he likes to yap. In general, a pretty helpful guy.

Extremely hard professor. There are 5 tests (one test is dropped), which is a lot of work for a class! Lectures are very theory-based with no examples to prepare you for homeworks or exams, which are both super challenging and time-consuming.

His TAs all will confidently lead you in the wrong direction. Don't listen to them about anything. During exams only listen to the Head TA or Ladha himself if he shows up. For homework don't post on piazza, dont use the TA office hours. Just, if u can, get a hold of Ladha (which is very difficult).
Professor Ladha is very passionate about the content he teaches. He is very clear and articulate when presenting his lectures and is very accessible outside of class for questions.

He clearly loves the content and can teach very well. However, the tests are biased heavily to people who are either very smart and can come up with creative solutions or have seen extremely similar problems before from their leetcode journey. If you have one or the other of those traits, you should be fine.

He is one of the most passionate professors that I have had at GeorgiaTech. He was enthusiastic about the content and built an environment conducive to learning.  He clearly conveyed why the concepts matters despite the abstract nature of the topics taught (this is quite a miracle, I hope to have more professors like him)

Much tougher professor compared to the other 3510 professors. Clearly very knowledgeable but not very engaging during lectures. Said in an email he expects students to come out "on their hands and knees." 1 exam every 3 weeks (4 regular exams + Final). Averages for exams were high 70s to low 80s. Homeworks are difficult and time consuming.

Ehhh, not the best lecturer, but doing his homework and preparing for his exams do help for solving interview type problems. Just read his notes (if comprehensible), do some of his practice problems, and watch relevant MIT OpenCourseWare videos

The other rmp reviews are hilarious, you will get violated, and go to hell and back from his 3510. Its a lot harder than every other section, but he is an amazing lecturer and the TA's provide amazing plus sections. By doing Ladha's class you will know how to pass an interview, his course is practical and seriously useful.

Professor Ladha is an extremely caring and charismatic lecturer for 3510. He makes sure everyone is on the same page, taking frequent question breaks during lecture that help regulate the pace. Always available to help in his office, even late at night.
I have lost hope in life due to taking this course. Before, I had dreams of becoming a successful software engineer at FAANG. Ladha put me in my place - the streets.
Lectures seem to be a presentation of his personal research interests as opposed to effective lessons. Grading for his extremely difficult homeworks and exams are all over the place.

The prof is challenging, but the course improves your skills for cs interviews. Teaching assistants often cancel their oh, and it's also difficult to get assistance from Ladha outside of class due to the lack of office hours. However, you will learn a great deal, although finding external support for this course can be particularly challenging.

Not sure why everyone's glazing. He is the hardest 3510 professor and the class genuinely ruined my confidence in myself. The practice exams are unhelpful and there is less opportunity for practice problems in this class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ladha is the hardest CS 3510/11 prof. BUT he will get you a job. Here is your strat: take easy classes if you take Ladha that semester, and make this class your main grind. Apply for all the highest paying CS jobs and practice the concepts as you also do the neetcode roadmap. Don't follow the neetcode solutions, make your own based on class info.

Extremely challenging class. I heard that other professors for 3510 are way easier from classmates. 
Homeworks and exams are extremely hard and take a considerable amount of time to do well. 
Lectures are quite confusing and not helpful towards homeworks or exams. I had to use online resources to learn the curriculum.
Its insane how smart he is. Like actually. Take him, you wont regret it. Also someone please him an whiteboard eraser.

He's a cool guy but has never taught Discrete Math before. His lectures are a mess and don't really have a structured or organized format. Honestly, I've had to learn everything on my own using supplemental lectures and YouTube and the ZyBooks, he is a horrible professor for Discrete. I feel so lost and I know I'm not alone.

Idk how this class is going from a grade prospective, I think the class average in the class right now is a 74% which is kinda insane. Most kids straight up have a C in the class. The exams are incredibly hard. BUT my leetcode abilities have never been more cracked. So if you need a job take ladha. Hopefully he chills out after DP, so the GPA survi
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a great lecturer but the problems really stem from how 2050 is run. Ladha doesn't know what's on the homeworks and he never goes over how to do problems in way the TAs are happy with(the TAs grade the homework). This means that even if we somewhat learn the concepts in class, we can't really apply them on the homeworks.
The TAs are extremely unhelpful on piazza and give unclear and short answers when asked about topics
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor seems like a respectable man, but his lectures are messy and disorganized. As a result, he is bound to miss key concepts and important details that other classes cover. The HW are graded by tough TAs, and his messy teaching style only makes it harder. Your best bet is to buy the ZyBook and teach yourself. Also, lots of HWs!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The TAs for this course are the most unhelpful TAs I have ever experienced. During office hours they give conflicting answers and they give unthoughtful and unhelpful responses on Piazza. I cannot wait for CIOS to give this feedback so hoping this is seen before then and TAs can actually help.
Studying for tests is very important for a good grade. Lectures are very compact.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor with engaging lectures and taught very thoroughly. He was super helpful during office hours and really cares about his students. Class is 80% exams but exams are fair and have lots of extra credit. Receiving an A requires hard work but if you go to all the lectures and understand the homework, it should be relatively easy!

One of my favorite professors at GT! He really cares about his students and does all he can to help them achieve their best in the class. Great lecturer who's very good at explaining the concepts well and making this difficult material interesting. Homeworks are difficult but prepare you well for the exams which are always graded fairly. Take him!!

This guy is a G. Absolutely love his teaching style and methods. He's knowledgeable and cares a lot (even tho he doesn't show it). The content is also really crucial for CS careers and is super interesting. Take him if you get a chance; I promise you won't regret it. #loveladha

I want to share a story about why I like this professor so much. One time after lecture, I wanted to prepare for Exam 3. So, after lecture I went to his office to ask some questions. This man patiently and kindly went over all 15 questions on the practice exam with me for the next *two hours* on a random Wednesday evening. He is a treasure.

CS 3510 is a hard class but I think Ladha makes it as fair as possible. Great lectures and the tests are reasonable. A bit too much homework though (seriously, and multiple times they made a homework due only 6 days after it was assigned)

Great professor, though a little math-heavy at times (especially in the first unit). The course is made to be manageable and the TAs are open to allowing extensions on homework when needed. Though he might not be the easiest option, he is worth taking to learn the content since this is the most important class you take as a CS major.

Ladha is an amazing professor. His lectures are thoughtful and engaging, he responds to questions on Piazza almost instantly, and he listens to his students. Tests are difficult but not too bad. Going to his review session the day before helps a lot.

Excellent professor for CS 3510. Does his best to make the class manageable and to make himself accessible to students. Lecture style is great, it's clear that he's well-versed in the content and enjoys teaching it.

Look up abrahim ladha on soundcloud

Great prof. Great lecturer. Even better singing voice
Was a really good professor overall. Great and charismatic lecturer overall
It might be because he's a young lad but it makes algorithms very fun to learn.

Great course! He is definitely one of the more difficult professors for this course but you'll end up learning a lot. His exams and problem sets provide a lot of practice. Very generous with deadlines and offers a lot of extra credit on tests. Allows you to exempt the final. His lectures can be a little math heavy though.

The lectures were a bit overwhelming at the beginning, mainly because no notes were posted on Canvas. However, as the semester progressed, typed notes were added and more practice problems were released. There are also 10-15 pts of extra credit for every exam. Overall good lecturer, but sometimes he brings up topics that are too hard for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ladha is extremely intelligent and flexible. TA's are amazing and provided many resources. I didn't attend lecture since the professor taught at a level too complex for learning material for the first time, but read the book/watched Abernathy's lectures. I would recommend office hours/actively doing the HW to prepare for tests.

The prof is great overall. He makes a lot of mistakes in the lectures, but a ton of resources are provided for us to learn from. The people who hated the prof either never wanted to learn something themselves apart from the lectures or they wanted free grades. The TA team is pretty solid as well and does all they can do to support the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I never attended lectures but he posts extremely detailed notes for his lectures on his website and he follows the textbook very closely. If you are stuck on homework he releases practice problems with answer key. I always felt prepared for exams. Grading can be BS but gives 2% CIOS Bonus plus rounds grades up plus drops and exam and homework.

His lectures can be confusing and I ended up learning a lot of the later material on my own. But he has a generous grading policy and goes above and beyond to give fast feedback. He gives test grades back within two days, and will give the test itself back so you can see exactly where you lost points. You can tell he cares about his students

Ladha is fine. Not great, but not the worst either. He's impossible to follow in lecture so you'll learn pretty much 95% of the content on your own. Homeworks are really tough but they prepare you very well for the exams (plus there's generous extra credit). While he isn't the best teacher, he is very in touch with students and a chill guy.

Professor Ladha is deeply knowledgeable about the subject and the lectures are rather engaging and well-paced. He is not 100% perfect but will dedicate time outside the classroom to resolve whatever issue you might have.

Professor Ladha really cares about his students and it shows. He is extremely accessible outside class and is always ready to help students with HW. He's extremely passionate about the topic and it's fun to see new perspectives on things. Exams are pretty decent and HWs might take some time but they are fun as well.

Prof. Ladha is really interested in teaching the subject and tries to help students. The class was confusing in the beginning, but it got a lot better as the semester passed. He extends the homeworks and makes the exams decent. Overall good professor.

I am taking CS 3510 with Abrahim Ladha, and I think he's a great lecturer. He gives clear proofs and examples of the algorithms we go over in class. Abrahim is also very accessible after classes and is able to provide counterexamples and thought-provoking ideas on the fly.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is very difficult. The professor almost recites the textbook in class, so if you don't understand it in class, that means you don't understand the textbook. There are no additional resources because the algorithms are taught in a specific manner with certain constraints such that outside examples have differences. Just horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think prof. Ladha is a great person -- he seems considerate, nice during social hours, and overall a cool dude. Unfortunately while Ladha is a great person, he is a terrible teacher. I try my best to follow along with lectures, but Ladha jumps all over the place and doesn't explain what he's doing. The exams/homeworks have been tough but fair.

I thought he is a pretty sold choice for multi, I think he did a good job with including a lot of visuals and simple explanations for concepts. Quizzes and tests were tough but it is not supposed to be an easy class. Use the textbook, practice a lot outside of class, and go to Professor or TA office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: omg do not take him; he was a new professor for multi and he originally had like a 4.8 rmp. his notes were bare and the tests were realllyyyyyyyyyyyyyy hard. he told the class that low 70s are normal for calc 3....................................

One of the better teachers for MATH2551. His exams are generally easier than other teachers, and although his lectures can be boring at times, he is lenient in terms of grading, always looking for areas to give points back. Overall, he is a good teacher. MATH2551 requires effort to grasp some of the concepts, but nonetheless I would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He knew what he was talking about, but tried to explain in math notation that no one understood. He didn't lecture great like Dr. Hunter, yet made his quizzes and tests very similar to his. He was very nice and answered questions, but he was not made for teaching an undergrad math class. I didn't put in too much work and still got a B.

Honestly his style could've been way worse. I think for whatever reason the class didn't do as well as he was hoping and it was partially because no one was using Dr. Lehmann's website to study, which is where he got most of our tests and quiz stuff from. He didn't want to reinvent the wheel for multi.

He's a great person, but inexperienced with teaching an underclassman course. He wrote all lecture notes from scratch with questionable handwriting, so I spent most lectures deciphering instead of understanding. He doesn't post note templates; homework content was not tested. I didn't know what I should know for exams until the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: tbh I learned mostly from studio, do NOT skip it if ur taking multi it's a lifesaver. Lectures could have been way worse, he's good at introducing topics but usually started losing the class during example probs. i agree that it would have been much MUCH easier if he simply copied the alr typed out notes from dr. lehmann, as his exams were similar

I do NOT recommend taking Prof. Abbrescia for Multi. He was disorganized in lectures, both in his notes as well as when explaining topics. When someone would ask a question on ed discussion, he often replied in a negative way. I do not think he was prepared to teach a gen ed class. I would recommend taking another prof.

he's not exactly the most “student” oriented prof, as i think he prefers teaching mainly upper level math majors so teaching a sophomore math gen ed didn't seem up to him. regardless i think he explained topics pretty well and dr lehman's videos could supplement any lectures you missed. wish he had more office hours tho. made tests decently fair

I see why people weren't happy with Dr. Abbrescia, but I was also able to manage an A without being exceptional or great at math. He did a lot to help us after a really bad first exam by giving us a curve and lowering grade bounds by 3 pts and his other 2 tests were pretty fair, j lots of algebra. Honestly I learned mostly from lehmans videos too

Honestly, I thought Dr. Abbrescia did a good job teaching this course. However, I stopped going to lectures both because of the extremely early time of classes and the fact that the entire class can be taught online. I feel he explains concepts well, but can be a bit abrasive on questions.

Dr.Abbrescia's a brilliant guy, but his teaching methods were just not for me. The class was so unorganized (canvas and lecture notes that were barely any notes at all). I just ended up relying on Dr.Hunter's website. If you can't teach yourself or already struggle with calc, then I wouldn't recommend taking multi with this professor.
Lecture notes are hard to follow and mostly illegible. The canvas page is rarely updated. Quiz content does not match what is stated on the canvas page. Does not give study material.

Dr. Abbrescia is not very responsive to his students and does not like to repeat himself. His lectures were so unorganized and confusing to follow, so I stopped going to them and watched the other professor's online ones. The studios never lined up with the content he was on. The first exam average was a 60...only good thing is that he curved it.

Would respond to all ED Discussion posts except for the ones regarding to practice exams, in which he would just completely ignore, so all we were given to study were studio worksheets and Lehmann's exams.

Literally the love of my life; this man changed my entire outlook on mathematics because of how good of a professor he was. Amazing lectures and was extremely caring. We had the chance to resubmit any homework for a full regrade, which helped me learn the material a lot. Exams were very reasonable. It is worth enrolling at a school just to take him

VERY VERY difficult class so prepare to study and review outside of class ALOT but he is such an awesome professor! Very understanding and accomodating of students needs. He even curved our midterm because people performed lower than expected.

What everyone has said so far is accurate. I took Analysis 1 and Analysis 2 (this class) with him, and had phenomenal experiences both times. Clearly very passionate, and nice to chat to. Very knowledgeable, but above all, extremely good at conveying that knowledge. Often draws pictures to motivate a proof before doing it rigorously, which is good.
Wonderful professor, handsome and chill.
Very clear lecturer, made sure that students understand concepts before moving on from a concept, and is sure to answer all questions succinctly.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 10 homework's are 50% of the grade, all of them are super do-able by your self, and will let you submit twice to correct wrong answers. Replied to my emails either within the day (usually within the hour) or the next day. Very chill guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Bro at the beginning of the semester went over the syllabus, asked us if we wanted one or two midterms. We said one, so he changed it to one. The goat.

Also has HW revisions where you can get full credit.
Great Prof, if you have the chance take him!

Best professor I've had. He clearly cares about students and puts effort into teaching. The labs are long and challenging, but they do a great job reinforcing the material and were very helpful at reinforcing material. Exams are fair and closely reflect the course content without being unnecessarily difficult.  (Also he zooms/records lecture)

3/5 for the 3011 with brothers, not really for brothers as a teacher. Junior design was a lot more work than I think it should be, but there is an arguement that it's my fault for doing Junior -> senior design path. Has a lot of energy, good vibes.

Took 3011 with Brothers, this class is a lot of work but the junior design project made me feel super prepared for senior design and he is a great professor - very reasonable and likeable, and teaches the course well

Brothers is one of my favorite professors I've had at tech so far. 3058 is a very tough class, but I really enjoyed Brothers' lectures. He's incredibly knowledgeable and does a great job explaining concepts. The labs are very time consuming, start early and go to office hours. Tests are open note/open internet but still hard because of time limit

Brothers' computer architecture class has been my favorite class at Tech so far. Very interesting content and great lecture slides. Labs are HARD but they reinforce the lecture content very well and force you to understand the concepts. Exams were take-home Canvas quizzes (40 mins, mostly MC from slides, a few short answer) with an overall curve.

Class content was older and a bit less helpful in that sense, but he presented the information very well and I learned a hell of a lot from the class.  He had some times where he was rather derogatory and kind of feed you to the wolves mindset, but it did pressure me to try hard and learn so it worked. The first labs were hell tho and took forever.
Tim Brothers was one of the best professors I have had. Down to earth and a great guy - the idea prof. I wish he taught more.

Brothers was awesome! Took him for ECE 3058. Class was in-person, but zoom was an option and lectures are recorded. They're moderately paced, with lots of information covered. Labs are very time consuming, so start early. Exams are open note, open internet, but VERY time restricted, so be aware.

Extremely caring professor and gives very valuable feedback as your group works on the projects. He tried his hardest to minimalize the bloat in material. Only issue I can see with ECE3872 in general is groups are completely random and you stick with the same group the entire semester.
Dr. Brothers is very understanding and relaxed. He is engaging in class and gives very constructive feedback throughout the design project.

Had this prof for MGT 4026, MGT 4029, and MGT 4043. His classes are straightforward with outlines and lectures videos you can refer back to. I wouldn't really recommend stacking his classes because he puts his exam dates on the same day for all of them.

Great personality and clearly wants students to succeed. Explained all topics so thoroughly that it was extremely easy to understand and cracked jokes throughout. If you have the option, CHOOSE THIS MAN.

Mythical pull of a professor. He explains the concepts well by relating them to real-world applications, and the example problems are essentially the ones seen on the tests. The tests shouldn't be too difficult if you carefully review the packets and pay attention in class. Someone here said he was like a parental figure, and I fully agree.

He's the best!! He clearly cares about his students and tries his best to make accounting fun. He tells you every problem before the test so just review/memorize the problems from the notes and you will do fine. You don't really need to do the recommended textbook problems and he has videos on the concepts if you miss something in class.
Great professor. Lectures are engaging and clear. He clearly cares about his students. Goes question by question when explaining what is going to be on the test. You will not regret taking his class.

BEST PROFESSOR AT SCHELLER! If you're considering taking Accounting 2101 with anyone other than Professor Blunck, DON'T. I can't stress enough how amazing he is. He set up his class in a manner that makes it easy for all his students to succeed. Accounting is a difficult subject, but Blunck made it much more digestible.

Blunck is the most fair professor ever! He prepares you super well for each test and quiz and basically gives you the concepts you need to know for every question. If you pay attention in class, everything else is easy! 
 
Side note: This class is great to prep for interview technicals. Highly highly recommend!

Makes accounting about as engaging as it can be and explains the content very well. He is very clear about what will be on quizzes and exams, so it's easy A if you practice. HW and textbook reading is optional (and unnecessary IMO). 

If you have to take ACCT, take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very helpful

Great guy, the lectures were very informative. You could tell this guy really likes what he does and the material is presented enthusiastically almost ... hard to do for accounting. Made getting through it so much better and I definitely learned way more.

This guy is so sweet and you can tell he likes his students, likes teaching and likes the discipline and is practiced in the discipline. 

He's almost paternal in a sense, which I find endearing. 

I wish all professors were like this. Teaching is about your students learning not about you proving you are very smart or 'weeding out' students.

Prof Blunck is very knowledgable and has much to say on his subject, but he manages to keep his lectures fun and lighthearted nonetheless. I was dreading having to take a business class for my degree, but found myself looking forward to his lectures.
Fantastic professor. Tells you everything you need to know and makes accounting as intresting as he possibly can. Highly reccomend.

I took Blunck for 4026 and 4028, easily one of my favorite professors at Scheller. I am a finance concentration so I took these classes for an accounting certificate and chose to take him twice. He is incredible. His class is well structured and straightforward. It is difficult but you receive what you put into the class. He deserves the world.

The best professor I've had at Georgia Tech, genuinely caring and you can tell he loves what he does. Teaches the topic very well and will go through what general idea the quiz and test questions are going to be about the class before so you know what ideas to focus on. Very funny guy as well and made an accounting class interesting and relatable.

Professor Blunck was phenomenal, def take for accounting! The class before tests/quizzes he gives you the guidelines for every single question on the test/quiz. As long as you go to each class (attendance mandatory), you will not struggle. He also uploads the lectures if you happen to miss the class day. Lowest quiz is dropped

Professor Blunck is the best.  He may be a tiny bit boring at times, but he is an amazing guy and a great professor.  He basically tells you everything that will be on the tests so its easy to know what to study

Professor Blunck is overall a good teacher and dad-joke funny. He keeps lectures engaging although the content is inherently pretty dry. Graded on a few tests/quizzes/final with a small participation grade. Tests/quizzes are not difficult if you study ahead of time, but this class is really memorization-based and you cannot cram day before/day of.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is my first business class at Tech, and professor Blunck's is probably one of the few favorite classes I'm taking. He's very clear about what questions (and topics) are going to be on his quizzes & exams, and he lets you know them a lecture day in advance. He's very fair in grading & overall a great professor who's very knowledgeable.

He is one of the best professors I've ever had! Not only is he super passionate and knowledgeable, he is also very kind and understanding of students' needs. He doesn't usually try to trick you on quizzes and exams, so if you just look over your notes and practice, you'll likely do well. Very fair and sweet, he prints out lecture notes for you too.

Hes the best accounting professor ever. He is really good about explaining things and answering questions. He also gives you credit back on tests if they are graded wrong by the TA or if you made a minor mistake. His tests are manageable and he tells you exactly whats going to be on the tests.

Took him for ACCT2102 and MGT4026. Blunk is the easiest and most sensible professor I've ever had for an ACCT or FPA class. Everything you need to know is in his class handouts, so if you go to class and study those problems, it's easy to get an A (for an accounting class). He also explains what you each question on his quizzes/exams is about.

The class was a bit difficult at times, but it was very manageable even during the summer semester. Blunck is very understanding and is more than willing to help talk through any confusion. The course was a point system with 3 exams worth 100pts each and 9 quizzes worth 10pts each (lowest quiz gets dropped). It's not a bad class. Blunck was great!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: By far, my favorite accounting class. It's complex, but Blunck makes it so easy to succeed. If you've made it this far in the accounting concentration, you've had him before and know how great his classes are. This one is certainly no exception.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: an amazing professor!! would definitely take him again!! however, the class was only graded by participation, quizzes, 3 exams and a final. he prepares you for EVERY single quiz and exam so its hard not to get a good grade on those. tries really hard to make it engaging and helpful to all of his students. definitely recommend!

While this class is difficult at times, Professor Blunck is very understanding and is an overall very good professor. We did have weekly quizzes (as this class was hybrid) but one quiz was dropped and quizzes were not super difficult. While there is going to be effort required for this class, the final was very doable and exactly like the exams.

Took him for MGT 4026, and it's the same style, but with a little more difficult concepts. Only note is that I wouldn't recommend taking 4026 and 4028 at the same time. Better to have the foundation in 4026 first.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Blunck is the only option for MGT 4026, but he's amazing at it. Lectures are informative, and he prepares you very well for exams and quizzes (make sure you review lecture notes before quizzes).

Awesome professor!!! He did a great job explaining concepts in the canvas videos, and his outlined notes were very organized and thorough so you didn't have to add much. He gave quizzes every week but was very clear on what they'd be over. Overall, as long as you take some additional notes and review the materials, you should be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: rly great professor. super nice & responds to emails in a timely manner. class was hybrid so there was mandatory attendance on the 1 day we met (along w in-person quiz). most of the class was taught on canvas via recorded lectures. gave an outline 4 every quiz/test & MC was hardest part. lots of partial credit for short answer Qs. would take again!

Great guy overall. Super nice and caring about his students. His lectures are great and very helpful. Only gives relevant work to do at home. Weekly quizzes are reasonable and easy if studied for. Exams are also very reasonable. The hardest part is the multiple-choice questions. Overall great experience!

Professor Blunck teaches most of the ACCT courses and is great at it. He is also one of the best introductions to college-level courses. Lectures can be boring, but he IS talking about accounting, quizzes and exams are challenging but he tells you what each question is going to test. Probably in my top 5 professors I've had, #1 is ofc Dr. Turner
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved him! He gave us handouts for each unit which were very nice. He would also tell us exactly what kind of questions we would be tested on. He was a great teacher although this class was very hard. You really need to work to get an A.

I really like this professor. I will be taking him again. 

In the lectures, he prints the outline therefore, you only have to take notes on the example problems. It is really great because you can actually pay attention in class. He does a very good job explaining things.

You have 6 quizzes but he drops 1. I didn't really use the textbook.

Probably the most inconsiderate professor I have ever taken a course from. Lectures are heavy with materials and always says he will give extra credit/assignments to boost grades,etc. but never does. I definitely would not take him ever and would steer clear from him if I were you.

His classes are an anomaly, it's harder than you'd like but easier than you'd expect just based on the content and his lectures. Professor Blunck is a pretty cool guy who is very flexible and generous with his grading and bonus points, if you put in a certain level of effort, you will do fine in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Blunck is pretty cool and a chill guy, assignments are pretty straight forward, but you might get tripped on what his hints for quizzes/exams actually mean but all of the answers are in your notes or should be an extension of your understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He tells you what each question on quizzes/exams is going to ask for but the hints are very broad so it doesn't help since you were going to study the entire chapter(s) anyway. The hints are so broad that it can derail your studying, the exams are hard and the hints he gives does not matter, you need more outside knowledge, intuition and guesswork
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Blunck was so good at teaching it felt like he practically raised me.

Best accounting professor at Georgia Tech! Take him if you can. He explains concepts very well and gives clear examples. His quizzes and tests can be challenging but are very doable if you go to lecture and do the practice problems. He is always available and can be lenient in regards to grading if you present a strong case. He's also really funny
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Grade consisted of attendance, tests, and quizzes. Grading was very clear and lenient if you had a strong case. Provided notes and expanded on them during class with examples. Walked through every concept. Told you what was on each quiz/exam and which question. Definitely take him if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He gives you notes hand outs every class. Tests are based on notes, all you need are flashcards. He gives you the topic of each test question the lecture before the test. Literally easiest A, but it is attendance based (and that's how you get the notes/test questions) so show up-- and then promptly zone out. Also super sweet & sometimes funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She really was invested in what she was teaching and really loves what she does. She also treats students as peers and is engaging. She really made class a very fun enviroment. Tests were a little weird (MC) , but after the first test it was easy to see what she would ask. Overall amazing professor and person (it was ECON 2803)
Genuinely boring lectures

All around great professor! Lectures are easy to understand. One homework a week with two attempts. Tests are easy once you do the homeworks and practice exams. There is no final exam just a take-home extra homework assignment.
very kind and fun, the course is just exam heavy so one bad grade on an exam can tank your grade.

Great professor with good lectures. The course itself is a bit challenging if you have never taken economics. The class is also very exam heavy (64% of grade) so slipping up once can mess you up for the whole semester. Overall not too hard or stressful though. Attendance taken only a few times using an access code.

Easy class. Attendance is technically mandatory but you can just show up every other class for participation. Tests make up most of the grade, but they're 25 MC questions and you get a notecard, and the final is take-home. Lectures are useful, but you can just study the slides and be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I can't stress how easy this class with Professor Behrmann is. Attendance is technically mandatory but it's only enforced with participation quizzes that she gives every two lectures. I barely showed up but she uploads extensive notes, and allows you to have a flashcard for the exam. Weekly quizzes are open note and on Canvas, AND, no final.
Take this professor if you doing 2106 fosho - easy A

As long as you show up and do your work, this class is very passable! Weekly homeworks that are not long and are very similar to the exams, plus you get a notecard for each exam. She is very accessible and wants you to do well in her class. Encourages coming to office hours and participating in class.

Easy class, exam heavy. She's very passionate about econ and loves animal facts. 3 exams 64% of total grade, the final is a 5% take home assessment. There's random participation quizzes and weekly quizzes.

Prof. Behrmann is awesome. She is super friendly and is extremely passionate about economics. The class is fast-paced and lecture heavy, but the exams are not that difficult. Assigns easy weekly HW quizzes that boost your grade and allows notecard crib sheet for every exam. Overall, I enjoyed taking this class and learned a ton.

Great professor. Super helpful and willing to answer any questions. You can always go to her office hours for help. Explanations are really good. Weekly quizzes and tests aren't too hard. Participation isn't required most of the time, but other times there are participation checks on canvas. Recommend taking her class!

She is a really helpful and kind professor. Complete your work on time you are bound to get an A. She teaches her class very structurally and the exam questions follow her lecture materials very closely. If it is your first time getting into ECON. Highly recommended. Also she has fun animal facts each class! Added bonus XD

Dr.Behrmann is very caring and fun. She often included fun things that aren't purely the lecture. If you go to lecture, do the practice exams, review notes, since you get a note card on each exam it's an easy A. She often allots time for students to ask questions and is very flexible to meet. Weekly hw which you have unlimited attempts on.
