The GOAT! I never missed a single points in her exams. The test is very easy based on the lecture and homework. she also gives us crib sheet for the exam.

This class was great. The professor was very involved and the lectures were very helpful. The lectures are projected and the content was gone through live with practice questions, not powerpoint style. Tests were straightforwards and fair and just like the lectures. Would take again

honestly great professor! i went to every lecture, and never got under an A on the exams. you have a crib sheet for every exam, and infinite tries on the hw. explained concepts in a simple way, and gladly reexplained if asked. fun animal facts that related to the topic every lecture, shes very passionate abt economics. if you can take her, do it!!!

Super manageable class, very understanding of everyone's circumstances, funny and chill. Tests are only based on her lecture notes, made concepts very easy to understand and took the time to make sure everyone understood. Straightforward class. 3 tests with notecard for each and take home final, weekly quizzes

LOVE HER SM, she's so funny. I didn't go to class bc the notes are posted online and made 96 , 92, and 85 on the 3 exams + 100 on the take home final. Pretty much treated this as an online class. She's the best and you learn the content then take the test which is so straightforward. You get an index card cheat sheet and can use all 3 on the final.
LITERALLY THE BEST PROFESSOR OF MY LIFE. I LOVE YOU RACHEL BEHRMANN!!!

She is great. I found this class extremely interesting due to her teaching. She posts notes and makes herself very accessible. Plenty of extra credit and she removes some more difficult concepts if the class finds them too difficult. Tests are heavy (72%), but she drops the lowest one. 10/10 would recommend to take with her!

If you're taking Macro you NEED to take her. She's the best. The lectures are boring and after the first test I skipped every class except test days and made an A. She posts the slides with her annotations so I just studied those. Practice test are like the real ones and the tests are SO EASY. Just be ready to study a lot if u skip like me haha
BEST TEACHER EVER. I absolutely loved this class, she is very understanding and always willing to help.

Overall really good class! Content is easy if you listen. If you end up skipping like me, just read the slide notes and you'll be good. Professor is funny and personable and you can tell she cares. Class can be pretty boring cause of how lecture heavy it is. Test are easy and short, practice exams were good gauge for tests. Lots of extra credit!!!

I love this professor and my B is my fault entirely. She is truly the best econ professor I have had to this date and am beyond grateful for her grace. Follow the practice exams and the powerpoints in class and you will be fine. Go to office hours after that first exam and you will be okay.

i received a C in that class cuz i did NOT lock in so its my fault. i deffo tried to lock in the few days prior the exams through her office hours and while it wasnt much, it was still VERY helpful for me to improve my exam grade of about 10-15%. There is also a max of 6% extra credit for the final exam. Her midterm exams are quite heavy tho (44%)

This class is reasonably easy. She presents information in a logical manner and is really good at explaining. Her lectures can sometimes be boring. A decent amount of extra credit is offered throughout the semester. The required textbook is lightly more expansive than other sections, coming in at $120 while others are around $70.

Professor Behrmann is great. She gave so much extra credit near the end of the semester. This is not a challenging course as long as you do the weekly online homework (unlimited tries) and study a reasonable amount for the tests. Her lectures are good but they can get kinda boring, but as long as you pay attention, you will succeed in the course.
very good, makes it easy to get a good grade if you attend classes, participation mandatory about 50% of the time, animal fun facts. 10/10
She was very good at teaching and answering questions. She let us have notecards on all our midterms and our exam. She gave a lot of extra credit.

Very passionate economics teacher and clearly knowledgeable.

- All the exams are based on her posted notes
- Lectures can get a little dry, but they are for the most part interesting
- Easy grader (exams are usually curved)
- Weekly assignments based on lecture (these are time-taking) on Macmillan software
- ECON 2100 is a mix of macro and micro

Extremely hard class, DO NOT TAKE AT ANY COST, don't believe these fake reviews, this class genuinely felt like hell. Homeworks were extremely hard and took almost 20 hours per HW. Exams were similar to HW questions but 5 times harder. Extremely hard class and professor.

Definitely the hardest class I've taken at tech. HOWEVER, Dr. Fil is the best. Very caring and great dude. I really enjoyed his lectures, he was very enthusiastic and man do I know thermo now. Fair grader. The homework was a full time job and the exams were brutally hard though.

This class was by far the most work I have ever done. The homework in this class would take around 12 hours per week, and that is not an overestimate. On the final, there were things that we had never seen before. Teaching-wise, a limited amount of foundational concepts were covered, and you were just thrown into the fire to figure it out.

Not the easiest class, but if you put in the effort you will really learn thermodynamics. The homework is long and tough, but office hours are helpful and the problems prepare you well for his exams. I finally understood thermo!!

Do the homework, attend lectures, go to office hours and you will be fine in class. I liked that homework questions were different from those in textbook and similar to what would you expect in his exams. If you get an A on his final its an A in class despite what you had earlier.

Only section that didn't have a take home final, and got the lowest avg on the 2nd exam. The hw's are long, and graded harshly and the lectures are conceptual. I helped other sections study for their finals and their review question were far easier. We got only two review questions per test. Hardest tests I've taken at GT. Caring guy.

Dr. El Fil is hands down the best lecturer I've had at GT. He makes difficult concepts intuitive, often using physical demos that really stick. The homework is heavy. Exams are hard, but if you manage your time and focus on getting partial credit, you'll be fine. This is the professor to take if you truly want to understand thermodynamics.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: My favorite professor at Tech so far! He made thermodynamics interesting for me. It was about what I came in expecting to put in effort for this class. His exams had option of retaking the test and getting bonus points!

Personally I enjoyed each lecture specially when he can simplify abstract concepts. Exams were tough but he allows you to retake the test for bonus! This helped a lot. Very caring and always made sure we got the concept. He knows his stuff really well. Lenient grader with long HWs. Go office hours it makes a huge difference!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Thermodynamics is already tough but he makes it so much smoother! Exams are tough but you can learn a lot from his HW! Super nice guy and helps you out a lot!

Expects students to have 20hrs/week set aside for this class. During exams, it was common to see people crying. The problems were unlike those we went over and were impossible to complete in the given time. Studied for the final for a week, 14hrs/day, and could not complete half of it. HW graded harshly and barely any review material. Ok to reach.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs. He's a nice guy and cares a lot but his expectations are way to high. Teaches purely conceptual in class and then expects you to learn everything on the homework, which is impossible without a software that he doesn't teach you how to use. Class is 20+ hours of work per week. Tests are abysmal and good luck finishing in time.

Definitely one of the hardest ME classes I took at GT, but I learned a ton from it. He really knows his stuff and doesn't shy away from testing you on it. The HWs and exams are tough, but there is a lot of practice to prepare you well. Grading is fair and pretty lenient. Lectures were fun, and I liked the mix of slides and board.
Tough class but learn a bunch!
One of the best professors I have had. Very approachable and genuinely cares about student success.

He is an interesting figure with an interesting career but aside from that, not much recommends him as a good or even decent professor. His readings are adequate but the main problem in the class was his lack of constructive feedback, clear instruction, and preparedness. 60% of class grade was still undetermined by the last week of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Take this class with P. Brecke. Dr. Best has an ego bigger than any other professor I've ever known and enjoys reminding students how much more he knows. Don't ask too many questions or send a single email, he gets petty quick. and most importantly: Do NOT have a different opinion or belief. Your grade will feel his retribution.

Listen there aren't enough characters to describe how horrendous this class was, there's 0 structure, his lectures have almost no relevancy to the ridiculous amount of readings he assigned, 50% of our grade occurred in the last 2 weeks. Don't take stia with him. Wait for a different professor. If you're going into ur last semester, stay for 4 1/2.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Biddle is a very passionate and interesting lecturer, and the class is pretty discussion-heavy.

Dr. Biddle is NOT accessible outside of class. Does not respond to emails. This sucks because each absence from his class is 2% off final grade and it's hard to communicate. However, class is relatively easy and discussion based. I've learned a lot from his class. I just wish he was more lenient to absences and more responsive. He's cool I guess.

Dr. Biddle is a chill and awesome professor. I would recommend taking his philosophy class. Participation counts and the semester is broken into 3 parts: 1. do reading before class and have discussion on Perusall & have discussions in class, 2. individual essay (some in-class time given), and 3. group essay/presentation (in-class time given).

Professor Biddle is one of the best professors that I have had so far. He cares about your grade and also cares that you are actually retaining the information. There weren't any exams and 2 papers. The class isn't necessarily difficult but will be a struggle if you don't do the work and go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Biddle cares about his students, and wants his students to learn. Had to read before each class (1.5 hrs of work) to be able to do his pop quizzes and participate in class (there was no homework). However, pop quizzes are easy - they are very high level. The midterm and final were take-home, and consisted of a few essay questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Had daily quizzes over readings and a final project/presentation. He was a good teacher who would go over the readings in lecture and kept a very reasonable grading structure.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Read the assigned articles and participate a little bit. There are two papers (the midterm and the final), but they are relatively easy. As long as you actually do what he gives you, the class is an easy A. He does come off as if he thinks his opinion is the only correct one though, so if that annoys you maybe find a different prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: My class was a discussion based class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Biddle is a great professor and his lectures are interesting and enlightening. His class consists of daily readings and lectures that clarify the author's message. The only graded assignments are weekly pop quizzes to ensure you're actually reading, and take-home essay exams for the midterm/final. Understand the material and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He Kinda Knew what he was doing but presented it in a bad way. Way too fast.

He often shows up to class late seemingly in a rush - also seems like he is learning his presentation slides as he goes along. Like he is surprised by what is on them. Gets half of the questions wrong and doesn't have a clear format for how he wants to teach. Get someone else, but 2 hour linear you can somewhat learn on your own. For 1553 not 1552
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I went to the first class, and immediately knew it wouldn't be worth going ever again. ADHD, disorganized, doesn't stay on schedule. There are videos posted on Canvas by a much better professor you can just watch instead. Homeworks are very fair, and tests are quite easy. Overall, I would take him again ONLY because lectures weren't mandatory.

I had him for Math 1553. I went to class for the first 2 weeks. He didn't seem confident about what he was teaching and pretty new in general. Luckily, for 1553, lectures from the head professor are posted online. Tests are the same across 1553 as well, so it doesn't matter who you have.
Lectures are ok but he usually doesn't upload notes or slides after class, and sometimes the way he explains things is confusing
I really enjoyed this class. The exams were fair, and the topics covered in lecture were understandable.

First time teaching diff eq. Not a bad or exceptional professor, but still on the better side. Goes through content at a reasonable pace with simple definitions, but the lectures may drag on a really bad example problem or get sidetracked. Definitely not tech savvy or fast to respond but overall a decent choice for diff eq (at least 1st time)

Does not teach well at all, no point in showing up to lectures. Also super disorganized, would never post notes, or announcements. Super hard to reach outside of class, would never respond to emails either. Studio is where I learned everything.
Prepare to sleep. He is quite boring that by the third week maybe 10% of the class attended lecture. Im sure it dwindled after that, but I did not stick around to find out.

Tbh stopped attending lectured after the first 2 months bc they tend to be very slow and boring. I felt like studios were much more helpful to learn content because we practiced what we learn so attend studios and make sure to do the practice exams that are posted because the exams are pretty much the same questions and format.

This professor was pretty decent. His lectures weren't the best, but we got all the content. His tests and quizzes were pretty easy too, and he was very lenient on grading. It's an easy A, and the subject itself isn't that difficult anyways, but I hope I learned it well enough to do well in my future classes.

The quizzes/ tests weren't terrible if you did the practice test/quiz and practice problems beforehand. The class was REALLY disorganized; he doesn't respond to emails and had no ed discussion/ piazza for questions. The class itself wasn't that difficult, it was just hard to follow at times because of the lack of organization/structure.

No Piazza or Ed Discusion (like at all), given one practice exam for each exam that often had GLARING errors, unreachable, exams SIGNIFICANTLY harder than other sections, disorganized, actually one of the worst professors I've ever had at this school. I know for a fact he also does not communicate with the TA's at all. Pray to GOD if you have him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures were difficult to understand, but youtube videos and studio sessions helped. The class is very test heavy, with two exams 17% each and the final 37%. The practice exams follow a similar format to the actual exams, so that is helpful

While lectures are somewhat unorganized, going to class gets you the best results. Doing the practice midterms before the tests helps a lot. Tests are super easy, but professor is unresponsive when it comes to email and Ed Discussion. Grading often takes forever. But because the tests are fairly easy and graded easy, this isn't a problem!

Professor Callis was an unresponsive professor, he did not respond to Ed Discussion posts or emails ever. There were many issues in the class such as quizzes being erroneously given over content we hadn't covered yet, wrongful grades being put into canvas, and not updating grades for students especially towards the end.

terrible unorganized lectures and cannot answer ed discussion/emails to save his life. our section was apparently the easiest tho idk. exams are not horrendous but often harder than his practice exams. quizzes were incredibly unfair and he didn't do much to remediate the consistently failing quiz averages.

Callis is an okay professor. His tests are tough but he gives good practice exams that are somewhat similar to what we see on the exams. Good thing about this class is that the final can replace every midterm. 2 different tests are handed out and one sometimes seems harder than the other.

Professor Callis is an okay professor, his lectures are just a little unclear and unpolished. He definitely requires you to do outside work to stay on pace as his lectures leave you confused. Not the worst though if you get a good TA, but I would try to get someone else.

Professor Callis's exams were really easy. Many of the questions had multiple parts that walked you through the steps of each type of problem. Quiz grading was also very forgiving. His lectures were all over the place and kind of difficult to follow but it was super easy to go to another professor's lectures and get all of the same content.

disorganized, but thorough and clear lecturer. Lectures were a little messy with in the way he teachers, but he got all the information out and as long as you pay attention you should be fine, tests were relatively easy compared to other sections. Very caring professor that cares about his students

Professor Callis is a pretty good lecturer. However, If math isn't a strong subject for you (like me), I would 100% recommend taking this class with Professor Klara Grodzinsky instead. I struggle when math concepts are not explained thoroughly and in depth with step by step instructions, and Prof. Callis doesn't often go into this level of detail.

Very solid dude. His lectures are easy to understand and very concise. While the examples he chooses can be as little easier than those presented on the homework's or exams, going to studios help with that. The class also has many exterior resources available to help if lectures aren't enough. All in all, very reachable guy with a simple style.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As other reviews have mentioned, lectures are not helpful. This semester, Dr. Zhu began his unit by saying that he had put the slides into AI to generate AI lectures for us to watch. He noted that some of it is incorrect so we should use our better judgement to know what is right. After 4 lectures, less than a quarter of the class was attending

One of the worst professors I have EVER had. Do NOT take him if you have the option. He could not care less about the students and their understanding of the material; his lectures are trash and the syllabus is ridiculous. The midterms and final are weighted ridiculously heavily and does not measure what was taught accurately at all.

Ineffective lectures. The grading schemes for quizzes and tests are not representative of processes taught in class, and zero consistency in what's important to understand. TAs are unhelpful and often misleading. Average on half the assignments was under 40% Never have I felt less control over my grades in a class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is one of the worst professors I have ever taken. He made our test too long on purpose, then told us in an announcement that it was designed not to be finished in our allotted time. His lectures are terrible as he faces the board and lectures to himself. The slide decks have to be downloaded to PowerPoint and rearranged for viewing. Tech BME

He is smart and knows what he is talking about, however he is horrible at getting everyone else to understand that. He is tough to understand, and his explanations are never detailed enough to actually give you s good understanding. This whole class is so badly structured I am shocked it is still allowed to progress the way it has been.
Smart and nice, but not a good teacher. The other posts are true.

He is rude, unfair, and he lies. He was grading prof for a study abroad lab (not PI). Was taking full load and wanted research but worried it was too much. He said if you show up you get an A. He gave me a C. When asked why, he said so I would come in. Changed to B but refused A becuz that's for above and beyond. Much more to this but word limit.

Lectures were super dry and confusing - in some cases, students were better off not attending lecture in order to receive a better grade. I only survived because I had Costas Arvanitis for PSS and a supportive TA. Try to get another prof for biomechanics!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
It's awful. Exams are weighted very heavily and the questions on the exams were not representative of any of the material we were given, especially for the second and final exams.
Quite frankly it sucked. Also very unclear on how the class will be curved and the class needs to be curved since almost everyone had failing grades going into the final.

He is extremely difficult to understand and his lectures are super complex. he shows slides with about 10 transitions each and he doesn't really explain what he's presenting. he'll give a super complex example with several derivatives and just click through it in like 30 seconds. you have to do a ton of work outside the class for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Zhu, although very informed in his course material, is often defensive and attacks students for disagreeing with quizzes and exam questions. He expects students to be as well-equipped and informed as the TAs but lacks proper direction in lecture. Lecture is very non-engaging and focused on supplementary material instead of test material.

Just dont take this professor for your own sanity. The class feels like a battlefield, the professor vs. the students. Good luck giving him any constructive feedback on his exams or the course overall, he wont hear students out. Lacks motivation to actually teach, speeds past the math of all example problems and expects you to make sense of it.

Dr. Zhu might be the worst professor I've ever had in the BME department. His lectures are so dry and hard to follow. He gave us questions on our tests that were literally impossible to solve and refused to curve. I also went to office hours and he did not at all want to help us understand the course material, and was frankly a jerk. Don't take him

Decent professor. Cares for his students. Wants his students to understand. One of the best professors that I have in BMED. YOU SHOULD DO ALL THE HW AND THE PRACTICE TESTS!!! HE LIKES TO REPEAT PROBLEMS!!

The graduate lecture videos are also very useful; they build up intuitively. I never went to lecture (didn't know what Brito looked like until the first exam) still did okay (B). A is 100% doable with the grading scheme listed in other review posts. Do not let performance on past exams discourage you: got a 50 on the first exam, 100 on the third.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Brito is a great lecturer! With that being said, the homework (which the exams are based off of) are very different from what's covered in class. There are 4 exams but the final is optional and replaces your lowest exam grade. Definitely do the homework early, go to OH if you feel stuck, and look up Ladha's lecture videos if you still need help
Great personality and always pretty funny/engaging in lectures. The exams were not hard at all if you do the homeworks. Final is optional.

Brito is engaging and funny. His lectures were genuinely helpful for building understanding, and the study guides and practice materials were always provided well in advance of the exams. Overall, Brito is awesome, and this class is perfectly structured and organized. Highly Recommended.

my advice is do not underestimate this class; if you put in the work you'll get an A. there's extra credit on all HWs; lowest HW dropped. 4 exams + final; lowest of the 5 is dropped (can exempt the final if you want). i didnt go to class, just read textbook. make sure you understand the specified textbook problems and you'll be good for exams

Professor Brito was an awesome professor for discrete. His lectures really piqued my interest in the subject. Exams were okay and homework difficulty varied. Despite my poor grade, the lectures were very useful.

Brito is a great professor who clearly has a passion for the material and can keep students engaged. HW seemed like a lot for me but it really helped me learn the material. There is adequate study material for each exam and Brito tries to keep the class as engaging as possible.
What kind of professor gatekeep lecture videos till couple days before the exam?? Class not even that hard but he made it hard to self learn.

This professor and the whole class of CS 6515 is just terrible. I got an A for a final grade but it was a complete waste of time. Sure, you have some weekly OHs and some of them by one of the TAs are really long. But I do hold against the whole staff the fact that they keep reiterating one semester after the other on this class yet it's still bad.

Dr. Brito was one of my favorite lecturers, sometimes the homework was a little unclear and difficult but office hours really felt like a cheat code. The TAs know what they're talking about and will help you if you are confused. His one dropped exam policy was super helpful because I got to skip the (cumulative) final. Highly recommend
Fun, interesting class. Exams aren't too difficult, and the practice exams and textbook are usually more than enough.
i love him and refreshing lectures. great class and lowkey wasn't hard.

He had good engaging lectures filled with jokes.Sometimes at 8 am it was decently hard to decipher some things through his accent but he has lots of personality.Some of the points off are just from this class having hard content which is obviously not his fault.I do hate this class but I wouldn't take this garbage fire content with any other prof.

The process is good inside the classroom, teaches the material in a good way, funny in class. Tests are reasonable and material covered is useful. However, outside the classroom, Dr. Brito comes off as very condescending and hard to reach to.

I had Brito in Berlin, so slightly different experience since class was small and attendance was (mostly) required. I got a lot out of the class by engaging with his lectures (which were good) and participating. His homework felt fair and a good preparation for the exams. It was nice to have a more personal experience due to small class sizes

Lectures were difficult to follow, yet also felt slow. The only posted class notes are the barely legible scribbles produced during lecture. Topics are an almost exact repeat of CS 3511. Learned the material by googling each topic and reading LaTeX PDFs of notes produced by other universities. Exams are medium difficulty, with lowest score dropped.

Lectures are average to high quality. Mostly well explained with helpful examples sprinkled in. Homework and exams are fair save for the often ambiguous and harsh grading practices. One point deducted for taking a totally hands-off approach to the online section and allowing the extremely unprofessional TAs to run wild

Professor Brito's CS6515 class requires work, but he's engaging and accommodating. Leveraging resources like Unstuck AI alongside the lectures helped me succeed. Exams were fair, though the frequent homework was time-consuming. Overall, a rewarding experience.

Brito is a great lecturer. The class started off pretty disorganized but the TAs eventually got their act together. Homework assignments take a long time. Exams are hard but very similar to homework problems. I didn't use the textbook unless I needed clarification about a topic. Didn't have many interactions with TAs.
Eh. This class was a grind. Hope you will have better TAs than I did. Good luck!

Amazing/hilarious lecturer, never a dull moment in his class, and you'll look forward to showing up. The 2051 supplements are HARD, but if you think about them for a while, they're doable. He's always available to help if you can't figure it out, too! All in all, I highly recommend taking 2051 over 2050 if you want to learn something new for fun.

Pretty good lecturer and the homework isn't too bad, it just takes a second to do. The class isn't especially bad when you factor in the fact that Howard posts all his lectures, which brings me to the prime issue, Brito isn't super active. He doesn't respond to any emails and doesn't really post on the Canvas.

Prof Brito is a decent professor and knows a lot about the material, but I wish lectures were more engaging. The homeworks are challenging but helpful. The TA's are helpful if you ask the right things and critical when grading. My advice is to stay on top of the work and give the answer you think they want to hear on exams.

Definitely cares a lot about his students—a great professor to take any class with. The material in 3510 is difficult, and Prof Brito does a great job making it accessible. Recommend reading the textbook for extra practice and learning. Always approachable if you do need help with anything, whether related to the class material or not.

Poorly managed in the beginning, though they sort of recovered towards the middle. Everything felt disorganized, with no plan whatsoever. TA grading is hit or miss. Teaching was mediocre at best; I doubt he understands half of the content himself. 
I don't know what happened this semester; he used to get good reviews, but this was awful.
Lectures are enthusiastic, textbook is great. TA homework grading confusions and mistakes are common, unclear if complex/verbose regrade requests get read, TA office hours might help more.

3510 is thinking class. If you're in it to think, then you're in the right place. Brito is just good at what he teaches and his lectures are engaging. The semester started off a little unorganized and TA efforts were a bit uncoordinated, but TAs recovered quickly and are super resourceful, so long as you take advantage.

Really fair professor. Exams are tough, but this is expected for a high level algorithms course at a top CS school. TAs are pretty terrible at grading. Regrade requests are your best friend in this class; sometimes you go up and entire letter grade. Course organization could be better, but you figure things out after about 3 weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's very funny and teaches like a mad scientist. Very enjoyable.
Stop reporting each other's reviews... Brito is a good professor by himself but he really needs better management with the lecture pace and instructional team.
Teacher is fine but The TA in this class are so bad. Very unfair grading and not helpful. A lot of them need to be reevaluated. Avoid

Brito does not present the information well enough for students to succeed in this course. The TAs were also not very helpful, and the textbook is your best bet. Would not recommend if you want a guided learning experience.

Brito once told us a joke about this home country: In Cuba, we don't say "go to somewhere", we say "escape to somewhere". I would like to quote him on that in terms of my opinion on CS3510: We don't say "dropped this class", we say "escaped from the class".
Absolutely horrendous. Didn't even think to read my solution before taking points off.

Brito is a great professor. Regardless of what everyones saying hes an amazing lecturer who really cares about his students and also makes his lectures interesting. Very cool and interesting class that forces you to solve problems.Follow along with textbook and do a lot of practice problems to succeed. Use office hours!
Nice Guy but pretty hard class. prob gonna end with a B

Brito is a good lecturer. Homeworks are challenging and office hours are very crowded... like 10+ students per TA, so difficult to get help there. Textbook is really good, and lectures seem to follow it closely.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor who clearly cares about students. Textbook is definitely the way to go though.

Brito's class is hard but he is a good professor despite what everyone says. The homeworks are hard, but they definitely help you understand the content. Algos is a hard class but Brito is a great lecturer and cares a lot about his students. He's very approachable and wants his students to succeed.
I wish people could see what people were posting on ed.

Not sure why things changed so much this semester compared to before. The class is rather disorganized with lecture notes being posted after the exam despite so many requests for it to be posted beforehand along with the lack of communications. Homework are graded harshly and standard solutions are not given afterward. Wouldn't recommend.
Lecture content is unrelated to exams and HWs, and Brito is not capable of explaining everything not a in confusing way. Please avoid.
Prof is absolutely great, but the exam is too hard

Cares for his students and helps them succeed by providing great guidance, valuable feedback, and answering doubts. CS 6515 is a required course for most students, made challenging by being graded almost entirely (~70%) on 3 exams, made interesting by his amazing lectures, employing the right amount of humour to keep the dense material interesting.
Goat professor

6515 requires work to do well, but it's doable. Brito cares about his students and is flexible when we express concerns. I enjoyed lectures, though studying other resources also helped. Exams aren't terrible. Main complaints: (nearly) weekly HW is a bit time consuming, plus occasional disorganization and lack of clarity. Decent experience overall

Really good and funny guy! The 8 am lectures were an absolute pain to wake up for, but I still went most of the time. Came in with no experience with proofs, but supplements for 2051 were pretty fun and challenging. This semester had merged lectures with 2050 and a group project/paper.

Really funny prof that will make you enjoy going to lecture. The class was really difficult but he was fair and accommodating, and made it possible for anyone to get an A. TA's were super helpful as well!

One of the more engaging lecturers I've had here. -1 because his lectures were hard to follow at times, and he wasn't the most consistent at making sure to provide supplemental material for us to read/watch. The tests and homeworks were well written and fair which shouldn't be taken for granted. TAs also good for what its worth.
Funny lecturer who knows his stuff. Homeworks can be tedious but prepare you for exams very well. Fair exams.
While some content could be difficult, the actual class was very manageable. Worked on homework in class, and exams were easier than the homework. Good professor.
One of the funniest and best professors at Tech, very engaging lectures and will always take the time to explain things. Made the exams quite easy (Spr 23) and it was not hard to get an A.

Good prof. Talks a little fast. Also, I took the honors version so it was much harder and my friends who took 2050  had a much easier time getting an A. He lowered an A to an 85 which was nice. FInal is also completely optional and can't hurt your grade. Homeworks were difficult and TA's feedback was really bad. Final project also wasnt too bad.

Goated lectures and also hes rly cute. on the three penultimate nights of one of the homework due dates, i dreamt on the first night that i shot myself in the head, the second night that i got into a car crash, and the third night that i got dumped. 10/10 would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolutely the best Professor at Tech! Very helpful lectures and office hours. I learned so much from this class, make Brito teach more classes for the sake of the students! But please hire better TAs: namely please fire the one particular TA for this class that chose to make all students' lives difficult on the homeworks and at office hours.
Britto best Cuban prof in the College of Computing.
Brito is the GOAT
You will learn a lot but will also require a good amount of hardwork.
I took an online course so I did not directly meet him but he was very encouraging during office hours, always motivating us to practice algorithm problems. 5/5.

Disappointing CS6515 experience with Prof. Brito: lack of structure, poor lectures, unresponsive to feedback, no assignment solutions. Course inadequately covers algorithms, mandatory but low quality. Recommend seeking alternatives for better learning.
Absolute GOAT. My favorite professor at Tech.

Brito's lectures can be confusing because he goes fast, but for Exam 1 (graph algorithms) the OMSCS lectures help a lot. For Exam 2 (randomized algorithms) there are no OMSCS lectures so you need to be familiar with his notes. HWs are much tougher than exams and exam grading is lenient (most MCQ and 1-2 FRQ). Overall, it was easier than 3510.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Brito is funny and does his best to make the lectures interesting. Beware though that he randomly did not cover things on the homework. But the homework honestly is what taught me the material the best, so it was no problem. Tests are way easier than the HW's which is nice.

super funny guy! could do with a little less glossing over important topics, but he gives a LOT of examples. homework is very time consuming so get started early. hated this class at the very beginning, but it gets a little easier to comprehend after the initial learning curve.

His lecture style isn't for everyone, but I personally really enjoy. He's really funny and cares about you as a student. Course also wasn't too difficult, he didn't make the homeworks or exams that hard.

Easy class but the prof is soooooooooo bad, doesn't teach the content and doesnt teach the stuff that he does teach correctly. 2051 just adds some extremely annoying programming supplements with laughable autograding dont take it

All of the lectures are amazing! He's such a great teacher and cares a lot about his students. Although the homeworks were hard, I felt that the 3 credits were well worth what I learned in the course.

Being an easy professor who gives high grades despite failing exams does not translate to being a good professor. He never released homework answers or exam answers or even feedback, just whether it was correct or not. This made doing homework worthless. For the final, he explicitly said specific topics were not on the exam--they were on the exam.

Professor Brito has great and enthusiastic lectures. He explains things well. His grading is lenient though the material isn't easy. The final replaces the lowest of the two midterms. One of my favorite professors.
Very straightforward expectations. Explanations are clear, and the TAs provide plenty of resources to prep for the exams.
Very good lecturer and cares a lot about his students. Assignments were fair.

Professor Brito is an enthusiastic guy. He wanted students to learn. However, his lectures are hard to follow and understand. What makes things worse is that he uses his own handwritten notes instead of slides, making it so hard for us to understand his drawings and writings. I give him 3 stars because it is easy to get an A...
S tier lectures. Struggling through homeworks guarantees good grades on tests.

3510 isn't nearly as scary as it appears. The tests are graded very fairly with lots of partial credit, the HWs/textbook/practice is really useful for the tests too as they are usually way harder than the actual test. Brito/Randall are the same HW/test but different time/lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Best class I took. The professor is definitely the star of the course. The lectures are engaging, sometimes tough to follow. The assignments make you think and the exams are designed to be scoring!

Prof Brito really encouraged participation so class was engaging even for a big lecture, and he would explain concepts multiple ways if we had trouble understanding. There was a textbook, but I didn't use it. My only complaint would be that the TAs weren't very reliable, a lot of them wouldn't show up to office hours throughout the entire semester.

This is the worst class that I have ever taken, grad school, undergrad, or otherwise. Absolutely horrendous. The lectures are hand wavy and then somehow expected to turn that hand-waviness into rigor on the exams. Grading is harsh and pedantic.

Definitely a nice dude. If you try, for the most part you'll get a "B". Homeworks are actually kind of difficult, but the exams weren't too bad. I actually didn't have a background in Algorithms at all before taking this course and it was still manageable.

Hilarious, entertaining, and engaging lectures. Brito was a solid 5/5, but his TAs were a little too strict on grading. As well, the homework assignments made by the TAs were ridiculously time-consuming towards the second half of the semester. In comparison, exams and quizzes were much easier.

Prof Brito taught this class with another professor. I am giving prof Brito a 5/5; I would give this class an overall 3/5. The other prof derived master theorem 3 times and did it incorrectly due to a lack of preparation. So it was only the half that Dr Brito taught that I liked. Likewise, only 1 of the Head TAs & 4 TAs were actually helpful.

I had him for 2050 as well and it was about the same experience. He's excited about the course material but you don't really need to go to lecture and most of the HW questions can be found on leetcode/geeksforgeeks. Would definitely take again.

Brito is a really like-able person which helps you pay attention in class. Even though the subject may be daunting, he knows this and he also knows that you need a B to pass. Go to OH. He offered a final assignment at the end to replace any exam/hw.

Homework was interesting (got a little difficult around the latter half of the course), exams were pretty easy in comparison. Brito was a great lecturer. This was my first honors class, and it was a good experience. It's even convinced me to take 3511 in the fall.

Dr Brito is really funny which makes the class really nice but also has an amazing TA team. Tanmoy, his videos on youtube, and his office hours are the entire reason I managed to do well in this class. The class is run very well. I would recommend taking his class.

Dr. Brito is a phenomenal, hilarious lecturer. The homework, though, can be quite difficult at times. Expect to put in around 15 hours or so a week on some homework and an additional 3 hours of lecture. I would still recommend this course if you'd like to make the most out of your degree and are here to learn.

Some homeworks were long and very hard, but he's an amazing, passionate professor. Lectures were clear and not too fast, grading was lenient, exams were easy if you understood the material, and the content and homeworks were genuinely interesting and fun. Brito made me love the topic and I highly recommend the class if you're interested in theory.

Some homeworks were long and quite hard, but he's an amazing, passionate professor. Lectures were clear and not too fast, grading was lenient, exams were easy if you understood the material, and the content and homeworks were genuinely interesting and fun. Brito made me love the topic and I highly recommend the class if you're interested in theory.

My favorite professor so far. Lectures were really, really good. Class was a bit slow however, and if you skipped class, you had to read off of someone else's notes, which could be hit or miss. Overall, worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His lectures go fast, so many of my classmates read the book to get a better idea of the material. The grading wasn't bad, but he said that he is stricter in CS 3510. He is very funny, and I enjoyed listening to him lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Be prepared for this class to be even more conceptual than previous algorithms classes. Brito teaches interesting but difficult algorithms in an engaging way. The homework is challenging but not unreasonable, and you are given many opportunities to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professors Britos class is hard, but maybe thats just because algorithms are hard. Homework requires thought, and exams are very hard. That being said, Brito is an understanding professor. He wants students to excel, and provides many opportunities to improve past grades. I got a B despite failing 2 exams. He is also very entertaining and funny!
He's an amazing lecturer who definitely made the material far less boring than it seemed at times.
Amazing lectures with really interesting examples and topics covered. Loved the class and the homework is harder than the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took Professor Brito for a summer program Intro to Linear class, and his teaching was exceptional. Very accessible and responsive; very clearly cared about his students. If you put in the time and effort (I unfortunately didn't), you'll get the grade you deserve. Best prof I've ever had.

Sp 2021 was a mess. The TA's grading was terrible. They did not grade homework before tests (no way of knowing what what a "right" answer looked like) and there were only 4 HW's and 5 tests (final replaces lowest). Ended w/a curve. The class felt conflictive all the time. I'd wait until TA's change, then take the class again. Brito as a prof is meh

I never had any idea what the professor was saying in class, he does have an accent as well but that really was not the problem, the way he explained concepts just did not make any sense. Zybooks is your friend as well as the textbook, personally I did fine without going to lectures. Just make sure to do the homeworks and recitation helped as well.

He's a hilarious and nice professor. CS 2050 is not too hard especially if you've done something similar before... just do the HW, watch recitations, and attend class. However, the course was structured weirdly where the profs took turns lecturing. Sometimes there was conflicting material between the two profs and also between them and the TAs.

I think the lectures could have been planned out a bit better as they often didn't emphasize the more important parts of algorithm theories - I frequently found myself referring back to material from much lower level classes for clarification. Huge disconnect between Brito and TAs - TA responses seemed intimidating at times and grading inconsistent

Brito was an excellent lecturer, and it was genuinely fun to listen to lecture (can't say that about all professors). Grading in this class is very tough, three tests each worth 25% of the grade; other than that, definitely would recommend.

Awesome lecturer, but poor communication made the class very stressful. Grading rubrics were harsh and seemingly subjective based on the grading TA. There were also discrepancies between what was said in lecture and what was expected on tests and homework. Class material is awesome, but the structure/logistics of things could be greatly improved.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I loved this class and Professor Brito. One complaint however is with the TAs. This is the first class where TAs are less approachable than the Professor and this might be due to how the class is structured. Some TAs were really nice and helpful but others TAs (namely one) on Piazza who would demean students constantly with their replies.

Prof. Brito's lecture is very nice and the pace is very good. However, make sure you actually remember details of the lecture, because the grading of HW and exam is kind of harsh and you will not be happy if you omit details. However, as long as you prepare for the class, then it's good.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Brito teaches the subject well and I found it to be a super interesting class. 4 homeworks throughout the semester but they're pretty tough and time consuming. Grading criteria is pretty strict so be sure to ask clarifying questions and follow the example solutions. There's also a pretty substantial curve it seems (85 for an A this time)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor overall! Definitely things that could be improved about the structure of the class, but Dr. Brito cares about his students and clearly works to make sure the class is fair and manageable.

Brito himself is a great professor. But Sp21 CS 3510 was a bad: 1. HW due dates and Exams were so close together we never got any feedback going into exams. 2. Grading requirements were incredibly vauge before submission but then incredibly strict when grading. So take Brito for 3510 just make sure the curriculum is actually well thought out

Great professor, cares about students and wants them to understand the material. He often tries to explain things in different ways for those who don't get it. I didn't have a bad experience with the TAs This class is not meant to be easy, it's meant to teach algorithms - grades are hard to earn. Class was also curved. I highly recommend Brito.

The class is pretty tough, but Professor Brito explains the concepts very well, answers all student questions, and is accessible outside of lecture. There are only 4 homework assignments and 4 tests + optional final exam. Grading criteria can be a little confusing, so clarify with the TAs to know exactly what they are looking for.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Understanding, super well-designed homework problems / curriculium. Great lectures. Harsh Grading. Class makes you think you're not doing well, but there is a nice curve in the end.

My favorite professor in terms of teaching style. SUPER responsive, amazing lecture. Only issue is that the TAs were really discounted from what Brito was doing so grading was harsh, but Brito gave a nice curve at the end to compensate.

Prof. Brito was a really nice professor - his lectures were engaging and he was charming. He was always open to student feedback and giving more partial credit if you disagreed with a denied regrade request. Plus, he curved the class so 85 was A. Sometimes there was a disconnect between taught material and the ways TAs want you to answer questions.

Professor Brito himself seemed nice and pretty enthusiastic. Occasionally, concepts and their underlying intuitions were not well conveyed, but overall, he was good. However, the 3 rating comes from the grading. It was oftentimes inconsistent between tests and home works -- there appeared to be a significant disconnect between Brito and the TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: An amazing professor that's great at teaching/responding, but this class has the worst TAs I've ever seen. they make the class so much more difficult than it needs to be. It seems as though there is 0 communication between the TAs and Teacher so exams and homework are just graded to a completely different standard than what is taught in class.

Brito is a chill dude, however there's a clear disconnect between him and the TA team. What Brito teaches in class is sometimes not at all what the TAs are looking for, and the grading criteria is extremely ambiguous and subjective. If I were to evaluate just the teaching, it'd probably be around a 4.5 but the grading is so horrible that it's a 3.

Lectures were pretty good, Prof. Brito explained topics well, and homework and test questions were generally fair given the amount of time we had to do them. Learning-wise, class was a 4 or 5. HOWEVER, the grading was simply awful in many ways, and this added so much stress to the class. Prof. Brito could have done something different to help this.

Brito himself is a great guy. He even helped me push a regrade request that was unfair from the TAs. However! That is the problem that comes in. The TAs. These pieces of human filth trying to pad their resumes in order to suck internship recruiter peen do not care about fair grading and just want to get grades in. Thus, Brito's rating will suffer.

Prof Brito was really good! The class was hard, but he was always enthusiastic and made lectures interesting. I learned a lot in this class. The homeworks were difficult and took a decent amount of time, but they WERE fair. Same for the tests. And you got a decent amount of partial credit even if your solution wasn't fully correct. Highly recommend

If you love math, you will love this class as the professor is a fantastic lecturer and has a ton of enthusiasm for the subject. Be warned that hws are fairly long and difficult, but you get out what you put into them--it's an honors section for a reason. Exams are somewhat tough but the grading is fair, plus there are extra credit opportunities.

Doesnt offer any extra credit opportunities and is very test heavy. I still think he teaches well and is very enthusiastic but his grading is very harsh. My least favorite thing is that he assigns homeworks before tests but doesnt grade them on time leaving students with zero knowledge of whether they really know the contents of the test or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Brito is a nice professor in terms of communication, but anything past that which actually matters like your grade or material he is mediocre at best. Grading rubrics are completely illogical and do not reflect your knowledge of the material. The content is easy but how he assesses your understanding is in ALL or NOTHING type, heavily weighted Qs.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the best lecturers I have ever had. He gives clear and concise notes, as well as frequent jokes to keep you entertained. Would definitely take him again.
Very difficult exams and not very accommodating with strict grading!!!!

He's the best teacher I've ever had. He really knows what he's talking about. And he is very caring for students. Every live question will be answered. He also gives a lot of extra credits. But after all, you should still prepare to learn something. Homeworks can be hard and takes lots of time sometimes, but definitely worths it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you are at all interested in math or have prior experience with discrete math, you won't regret taking 2051. Professor Brito's lectures are engaging and he explains things well. Homework and tests were moderately difficult but fair. He is also willing to meet one on one to discuss. I learned a lot and enjoyed having him as my professor.

CS 2051 is a difficult class and you should NOT take it if you are not interested in math. If you are though, this class with Prof. Brito is fantastic. Lectures are great and cover a wide variety of topics, homework is really difficult but thought provoking (TAs graded weirdly though), and exams were fair (but hard). Overall, great but hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: CS 2051 is a difficult class, however, the class with Prof. Brito was fantastic. He is a pretty good lecturer and explains the concepts well and with some depth, and his homework problems are quite fair (although really hard). Exams are also fair (also pretty hard), and he's very responsive to questions. Don't take this class unless you love math.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class is inherently a little difficult for many (like cs2050/2051). That being said, the class proceeded in a structured manner and was logical. As for my complaints, I felt like prof. Brito spent too much time explaining things that didn't matter and not enough on the topics that did. Homework and tests could be rough, sometimes taking days.

Prof Brito explains concepts clearly. He gives good examples and is overall a pretty fun guy. Honors discrete is def harder than the regular but Brito's grading format isn't bad (midterm can replace final, extra credit). I liked the class, but don't take honors if you just care about getting an A. Start hw early and go to TA hours for help!

Professor Brito is absolutely fabulous in that he is not only personable and friendly, but I found him to be a very good lecturer as well. He moves at an appropriate pace, gives lots of examples, and makes discrete math easier than it feels like it should be.
The students for this class voiced complaints together more than once for unfair incidents and the professor consistently responds with defensiveness and denial.

He's for sure enthusiastic about the content. However, his explanations of the subject material is lacking, tending to be disorganized/wordy and at times inconsistent with previous things I've learned. Moreover, grading is inconsistent: his TAs often grade with criteria at odds with himself and what we've learned in class. Tldr: Bad communication

This professor is trying to teach good, but he cannot explain the concept, especially key concept right. I have taken UCLA math proof course before, and comparatively speaking, this professor is far worse than the one taught me in UCLA summer session when I was even a high school kid.

I had him for CS 6515, Graduate Algorithms. The class was a very fair difficulty level, and I think I learned a fair amount, despite not liking the subject. He's an enthusiastic teacher. For anyone needing to take this class, I'd recommend taking it with him.
CS 3510 is a math class, so be prepared for it to be taught like a math class. Sometimes lectures can be chaotic and confusing, but you have plenty of opportunities to understand the concepts better.

Brito really tries to make sure people are understanding things. Good at explaining problems. Had him for algorithms, the class isn't too difficult as long as you put in the work reading the textbook and starting homework early.

Prof. Brito's lectures were always hilarious, though sometimes slightly confusion or chaotic. This latter part is easily mitigated by following some of his consistently great advice: review the material before class. As noted in other reviews, he talks very 'mathy', but this only takes a bit to get used to- and its the smart, concise way teach 3510

Prof. Brito is okay. The first two weeks of lectures in class were pretty chaotic. However, after the first two weeks, the lectures became more methodological and followed a better flow. Prof. Brito is eager to help students, but tends to talk in "mathspeak", which makes the class harder to follow for non-math-oriented students. Ask questions.

Great guy, always so energetic in lecture. He postponed a homework due date to give people more time to finish it, which was very kind of him. FYI it can be hard to tell what TAs were looking for when grading your exam, so go to Office Hours and ask about how to format your responses! My grade improved so much once I started doing this :)

Brito was a great professor. He presented material in a logical way that was easy to follow. In the beginning, his lecture style was a bit scattered, but he improved greatly over the course of the semester and became a lot more systematic. He's very responsive to feedback from students, and did his best to balance answering questions with teaching.
To slow, didn't cover material I'd have liked to see. Too many questions in class.

Linear algebra at gatech is a joke. Class always gets tremendously curved and the professor you take it with wont make too much of a difference. The textbook is amazing and I highly recommend you use it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He knows exactly what hes talking about and hes super kind. He is amazing at explaining things and wants you to do well. He prefers for people to engage with him in class instead of staring at him silently. He also does not tolerate wasting peoples time (including his) so dont show up to class if you arent going to pay attention.

Brito really cares about teaching well and tries hard to make sure there's no questions left unanswered (either in lecture or office hours). 1553 is not easy, so make sure you use the available resources and ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really funny guy- reason I showed up to lectures besides the poll question. This class is difficult in general, but his office hours as well as the TAs were really helpful. His accent can be hard to understand at first, but it's only an issue when he gets really excited about a problem. Final kills your grade and no curve.

Not as organized as some of the other professors but makes up for it during his Lectures. Didn't realize how great of an explainer he is until we had substitutes in the class. Hilarious guy, funniest part was when he read his own ratemyprofessor reviews to the class. Linear algebra in general is hard so don't just rely on lectures/recitation.

One of the best professors you could take. Definitely recommend taking him, especially for Linear Algebra. The only boring part of the class were the mandatory slides common among all departments. Brito is amazing. He wants you to understand the concept: more for your life than for the grade. Also, he makes the class very interesting. ME VOOOOY...!

Brito is a great professor, he's super funny, and made lectures entertaining. He truly cares about his students and wants to see you do well. I would highly recommend taking him if you get the chance.
Professor Brito is great and I definitely recommend taking his class.

If you can take Brito for MATH 1553, do it. This guy is awesome. He will occasionally answer questions with "I'll get back to that" but he almost always does. Extremely funny guy, accessible outside of class if you email him. One of my favorite professors so far.

His tests are easier than the other sections, which is big in 1553. His lectures are pretty funny and entertaining, and he's a really nice guy. At first I thought he was going to be really disorganized, but he really knows his stuff and he's pretty good at teaching if you pay attention.
Hes super funny. His accent is hard to understand and hes a bit unorganized, but hes super cute so I dont even care that Im failing.

Brito's teaching pace is great, and he keeps class very interesting: extremely funny. Sometimes doesn't follow the textbook or slides, but normally his ideas are better and simpler than those presented. Struggled to fall asleep in linear algebra, that's a feat.

Took me a month to be able to understand his Cuban accent. He is not organized. Quizzes every Wednesday given in recitation are 15% of your grade. These points are crucial, because the remainder of the class grade is from 2 midterms and the final. Homework is optional, but you must do them prior to quiz on Wednesday bc quiz is created from it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Gerandy is such a funny and smart guy (& super cute). Tests/quizzes are your entire grade, very difficult, and based off of optional homeworks and in-class examples. The class is a bit disorganized and his communication skills aren't great, but as long as you do the homeworks and attend lecture, you'll be fine. Best math professor I've had at Tech

Class started off easy, but quickly became a bit more difficult. Professor Brito is very accessible outside of class and is very fair! Going to his office hours helped so much, and the reason why I got an A in his class. Lectures aren't mandatory, but highly advised. Push yourself on the homework he gives you, and you'll be just fine!

It is kind of hard to understand his notes but his exams/quizzes are predictable and there is no hw for the class (only quizzes), he gives partial credit on exams and provides practice, the textbook is optional

UNDERRATED PROFESSOR!! We need more profs like him at Tech, he geniunely cares about his students and isn't afraid to adjust his HW/Exams/policies to prioritize fairness for students. Very available to help, he posts about his office hours often and is very helpful even if you are super lost. He isn't trying to trick you, he wants you to do well.

Professor Yip is a very caring and approachable person. His lectures are straightforward, delivering content in a clear, easy-to-understand way. The exam questions are very similar to those in his lectures and on the sample exams. He is always responsive, answering students' questions and addressing their needs.

He's one of the kindest and most organized professors at Georgia Tech. His clear structure made it easy—and genuinely fun—to follow along and learn. He's also very understanding of students' diverse situations. We need more professors like him who truly invest time and effort in teaching.

Professor Yip is a great professor who is not only knowledgeable but also very caring and understanding. He's a little soft-spoken but he explains concepts well and is always willing to spend extra time with you if you don't understand something. He's also very nice and reasonable with grading quizzes and exams.
Professor Yip likes to clap to get everyone's attention. He is a very gentle teacher.

This guy... tests are ridiculous. Never enough time. Homework is extremely long and arduous, so by the time you reach the extra credit portion you have already been working for hours. Testing periods are 300+ people, which are on a lockdown browser. You have to scroll up and down continuously to see the question and code. Also, lectures ramble.

I'm choosing peace and kind words but I really really do not like him. You learn nothing in lecture, have a quiz for participation that's all or nothing in EVERY class, he is disrespectful to accommodations, and I could keep going on and on. The exams are impossible and only test writing like 100+ lines of code 5 times.

Unc did not teach 😭. The coordination amongst the TAs and Stallworth was also clearly not the best. exams took nearly a month to grade and recitation material didn't always match lecture. Best way to study is use all the practice resources provided and practice intensely with MatLab coding (especially if you have minimal prior coding experience).

He was an alright professor. He had the tendency to go on relatively long tangents but did teach the course content well. I had previous coding experience, which made it easier, but it still could have been a lot better.

He gets distracted super easily and rarely covers everything that we were supposed to cover. The homeworks are super lengthy, although they are very good practice for tests. STUDY FOR THE TESTS, OR THEY WILL KICK YOUR BEHIND. Do the extra credit, you will probably need it. Overall, the extra credit and test-drop make up for the lack of teaching.

Professor Stallworth is very funny, but lectures mainly skim topics and attendance is mostly for mandatory quizzes. Homework is much harder and is very time-consuming since you must learn the content yourself. Recitations are hit or miss, tests are super hard, but grading helps.

Took an online section of his MATLAB class. Lectures were optional and he tended to go off topic during them. However, exam review sessions were very informative. 
Be ready for long homework grinds! Do the extra credit!

Professor can go off topic on completely unrelated tangents for 10-15 minutes at a time, but his explanations of MATLAB were solid. Course is very manageable if you have previous coding experience, but can be challenging if its your first time coding (like basically any other coding class).
Like Doug from Up, distracted by everything he notices. Incredibly hard tests and over-worked TAs.

Stallworth is pretty entertaining, but his time management skills are not great (you learn the info the day before homework is due). The tests are the hardest part of the class, especially the tracing problems. Overall, Stallworth is a great guy but a frustrating and difficult teacher for those with no prior coding knowledge.

I got a 58 on the first exam and was absolutely devastated and thought I was gonna fail the class (freshman canon event), but I studied really hard and managed to get an A in the class. I learned the most by going to recitations and the TAs (shout out to Victor!). The MATLAB grader is extremely useful for exams. Lots of extra credit opportunities.

He was very nice, but got off topic very fast and very often. If you have never coded before, you can never miss class, because everything builds off the lecture before. Lecture is optional, but he does in-class quizzes that count for a grade. I will say that I did pretty bad on exams 1-3, but did well on the final and homeworks and still got a B.

Funny guy, but bad lecturer. Goes off topic and rants a lot, making students unprepared for his very difficult tests. TAs are way more useful; go to them if you need help. If you're like me and came into this class inexperienced with coding, you're gonna have to practice A LOT for an A. Self-taught the whole class pretty much... good luck.

Pros: Funny prof, lots of opportunity for extra credit, makes practice exam questions, good TA's 
Cons : HARD exams (graded slow - TA's are overworked) , end of lecture quizzes , useless lectures (to which he is always late to)

Cool and funny guy, but really cant teach the material very well. Maybe its time for retirement.

Nice guy but not a great teacher, he would get very sidetracked and spend half of lecture reviewing material from the week before, making us fall behind on concepts for that week's homework. Homework can be tricky but will prepare you for the tests so actually do it, recitation is goated, each lecture has a quiz at the end with a code.
He was a good teacher when he decided to teach, but he showed up 10 minutes late every day and was often off-topic. Was a very entertaining professor.

He's a great guy but he gets off topic easily. I knew how to code coming into this class and still had a hard time. The tests are VERY hard. Thankfully the final can replace a test grade so that was how I got an A but definitely wasn't easy.

All he does is talk about his daughter or his 2 minutes on the Packers as their kicker. Rarely talks about the topics actually needed on exam. Wouldn't want to blame him for the course structure, except he's the AD and could make this MATLAB class not so 'python-y'. He has super hard tests, and also loves getting power tripping TAs.

He's a funny guy, and I love his stories in classes, but his teaching style just wasn't for me. If I was a complete newbie at coding, I'm not sure I would have been able to keep up with the class. The online videos he has on the Canvas were far more helpful.

He tended to go on rants and not get through all the content needed to complete homework, so often had to find other resources to learn it. Recitation is extremely helpful. He is interesting and funny though!

Went into this course with no coding experience, but felt lectures and recitation were enough to succeed. Homework can be time consuming, but it prepares you well for tests. Also gave lots of extra practice and mock exams to prepare for the tests. Up to 5% EC and final exam is optional. Only gripe is that getting test grades back took quite a bit.

Great professor with lots of knowledge on the subject, which is more evident in the lecture videos than lecture because of the side tracking. There is a daily quiz that you take at the end of lecture as well. The exams will change for next sem so I will not make a comment on that, though the grades coming back takes quite a while.

Exams do not evaluate your understanding. They say they try to give you partial credit but I lost 20 points due to typos on an exam. Besides that everything else is easy and Stallworth is great; y'all are hating on him for no reason. Also the exams should change starting in the spring so that you can actually code (so my complaint becomes obsolete)

If you have a previous understanding of basic CS concepts, this class is easy. He does yap a lot but that honestly kept me more interested/let me pay attention to the lecture. The videos are also helpful to watch, and the homework and exams were hard, but interesting (at least to me). If you put in the work this class is not hard.

He yaps a lot. He gets off topic easily and I got very little from the lectures. He's a funny guy, but I'm there to learn matlab. He has lecture videos up that I watched instead of going to class. The videos were great and way better than lecture.

Dude straight up creates the hardest exams - gives a lot of hw- and yaps about NFL/sports/ or some side quest 50% of the class. Just don't go to lectures and show up in the last 15 mins for the quiz, really. Everyone basically failed Exam 1.

Good teacher when he stays on task. The homework does take a while and sometimes he hasn't taught what's covered in the homework. Attending recitation is helpful and gives extra credit for the class. He knows what he's talking about but it's frustrating when he gets off task. The tests are pretty difficult, but there is plenty of practice available

He's a really funny guy, but gets sidetracked all the time in lectures. Spends half the time talking about his football career and the other half doing an amateur stand-up routine. You will spend hours on your homework, and tests are hard. His lecture notes and videos are really good. Sometimes homework will be due before he covers its content.

Lowkey the goat. Informative lectures as are the recitations with his TAs (+1.25 EC if you attend all). There're like 24 five-min quizzes of which 16 best matter (sometimes you can get a free 100% if lecture is too long). Lectures are fun and engaging through personal stories. 3 exams + final can be dodged. Hw comes with EC part and can be tedious.

Stallworth is a nice and funny guy, but yikes this class is awful. It's put forward as a beginner's class, but if you have no coding experience you will struggle. Get ready to spend hours on homework. There are EC opportunities which is nice. But yeah I can't wait to be done with this and never take another coding course again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
1371 is by no means a "beginner" programming class. Even if you have some experience, getting used to MATLAB takes some time. The homework can be a massive time suck if you're new to programming but the TAs are great during recitation.

That being said, Stallworth is extremely funny and a great guy. Just be prepared to put a bit of effort in.

He's a great guy and pretty funny, but he can tend to get off topic during lectures. I stopped attending lecture and just used the videos provided on canvas, which were amazing! You can learn everything from the videos and go as fast or slow as you need. Recitation is extremly helpful, especially when preparing for exams. Do the practice tests too!
Had him for challenge. Easily the most inspiring teacher I've met. He keeps his students engaged and pushes them to do their best.
SO BAD. TEACH YOURSELF....b/c he tells stories during lecture. Good luck :)

Honestly did not go to class after the first week b/c the online videos are super great. Prof. Stallworth did seem like a really great and funny guy though, and apparently he alludes to exam questions in lecture sometimes. Make sure to do all practice exams to prepare, and sometimes you have to memorize approaches to be efficient (esp. last unit)!

I was TERRIFIED to take CS1371 at tech because...ive never TOUCHED code before, however Mr. Stallworth really does try and teach you from the very beginning assuming no one even knows what a function is. Make sure you go to recitation, he is super funny and made my 8am class a little easier to get up for. GO TO OFFICE HOURS if your struggling

I didn't really go to class due to Stalworth being kinda a slow lecturer.  He is pretty funny and all but he doesn't teach the material all that well imo.  The tests are straight forward just time is such a constraint like u legit need to memorize how to solve problems not solve them during the exam or else u will run out of time.  TIME Y

This was my first CS class, so I was intimidated at first, but Stallworth offers a lot of resources to help you succeed. He does sometimes go off topic during class but he's a funny guy. I learned most of the content in recitation or through the lecture videos on Canvas.

He's an amazing guy, the tests can be a little tedious, but what else can you expect at a Georgia Tech CS class especially made for engineers. The class isn't easy, but the professor does want you to succeed! I say go to lectures, and then fill in the gaps with his videos and recitation. His lectures are slow but perfect for introductions.

Stallworth is a very fun prof, however this does not translate to the quality of his teaching. Most stuff was not gone over very well and homework was easy in the beginning and VERY difficult towards the end. Class seemed to just ramp up out of nowhere. Lectures went over the same stuff 2-3 times yet I still learned most content in recitation.
