He is very helpful, and willing to work with you until you understand it. He has a great personality and always keeps class interesting. He does not allow laptop use in the front of the class. If you want to use a laptop or electronic device you must sit in the back (laptop ally). His classes can be interactive, and he always posts the PowerPoints.

Very entertaining lecturer.  Knows what he's talking about and the tests will always have something that you've seen somewhere before or a variation of something.  Seems like a very approachable person, but acts very cold and impatient when approached personally. Does not curve, but doesn't need to.

He's pretty good at explaining the concepts. He jokes a lot which are funny, but sometimes the whole class gets really distracted..and half of the time I can't concentrate on lecture. The tests are hard..but they are from homeworks and lectures so i can't really complain.

An extremely talented teacher and a very well-run class. Modern Physics teaches you the fundamentals and I feel like I really understand things, instead of just memorizing formulas. Tests are extremely hard but fair, and he doesn't curve. Overall, if I could have him again for Physics II I would definitely do it. I wish more profs could be like him
Physics 2 at GT sucks. Tests are awful. HW takes a lot of time. Weekly Lab Quizzes suck. Compared to other Physics professors, Greco is helpful and fun.

Makes class fun and teaches the basics. Goes on alot of tangents. PRS counts, therefore you need to attend every class. Test are HARD and you will need to study for them. They are nothing like the homework. Online Homework. Need to purchase the book. No Curve. Not easy teacher but fairly decent teacher.

I thought this class was fairly easy, and as such, have missed several classes, but the classes I have attended are essentially an explanation of the material in the book, but with examples worked out on the board. The only thing I dislike about this class is the daily homework, which while helpful seems juvenile and unnecessary in a college class.
Very helpful and a good teacher.  HW is easy webassign; tests are much harder than the HW, but he is good at explaining the basics.
Good, helpful professor teaching one of the hardest intro classes at Georgia Tech. Notes are on ppt slides. Test are very hard, hw is pretty much daily online.

Easily the most fun class I've had at Tech, he makes lecture enjoyable even though it can be pretty dry sometimes.  Very easy to approach, and he always has a joke to lighten the mood.  Makes me want to take more physics

Dr. Greco is awesome. He loves to help his students, and understands that physics is a tough subject for many students. Tests are hard, but that's not because of Dr. Greco; the physics teachers as a whole make one test for all of the classes. He's also a really cool guy to be around. For Halloween he lectured in a penguin costume.

Agree with other reviews. Thought some of the homework and practice problems were harder than the tests. Great prof, teaches really well. 3 extra credit surveys and extra credit on every test. Optional final. By far the easiest of the statics class while still actually learning. 100% pick Prof Bruun if he's teaching statics.
I would like him to teach every ME class at tech! The most chill professor I have ever had. 85 was an A at the beginning of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bruun was an amazing COE 2001 prof. He makes the notes easily accessible and works through lots of examples in class. The grade cutoff for an A is 85, and there are a decent number of extra-credit opportunities, which made it easy to get an A. The homework takes a decent bit of time, but the homework questions are very similar to exam questions
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: great prof! Made it really easy to get an A because the grade cutoff was only an 85. he was super nice and posted his notes, which were super digestable and easy to read. textbook was helpful too. tests were not easy, but again only needed an 85 for an A. also offered good extra credit and would curve. loved this class!

Very unorganized. Good person who's bad at teaching. Grading is unnecessarily complicated and the homeworks take forever. The tests are poorly written and when asked for clarification, he just reads the question again, which is entirely unhelpful and condescending.

The pre-PSS lectures are longer than they should be for the amount of content they cover. His expectations are unrealistic and will lowkey try and gasliight you into thinking that you did not read the instructions clearly, when he CHANGED THE INTSTRUCTIONS after multiple groups submitted and he realized he does not like it

The lead instructor (not PSS) for 2250. Nice guy & fun to talk, but class was severely unorganized with assignments not clearly posted on Canvas (deadlines very hard to find). Chaos ruled and TAs + PSS Professor greatly helped in guidance, but class lacked structure and was a hodgepodge of work to do, found BMED 2310 to be much better organized

He will confuse you and likes to make his expectations seem higher than the actual grading criteria. He loves to yap so he'll ask you super deep questions that you don't actually have to answer or consider for deliverables. Way too much "busy work" for a like 1 hr course and just a giant group project but it is what it is. He is nice tho.
Todd had unrealistic expectations. The homework assignments took several days to complete and contained no practical knowledge.

Todd clearly cares about your success. However, his questioning and guiding is unclear. He will let you redo a portion of the course if he feels your work is not good enough, but then you are missing out on 1/3 of the course material. The lecture content is unhelpful. Why wait until the presentation to tell you that you are on the wrong track?

Amazing professor! I had him for BME 1000 for a few months as my previous professor had left. In class, his lectures were very engaging as he is a great storyteller. Outside of class, he was very helpful during office hours, not only helping me with my queries but encouraging me to go above and beyond with assignments. Would highly recommend!
Homework and tests for this class take an unreasonable amount of time.
Very friendly, engaging, and comprehensible lectures. Chill class in an otherwise not-chill environment. Tries to make the best out of everything.
Very nice professor, but homework and tests  are killer, extremely long take 8+ hours to complete.

He's a caring professor who made this class as easy as it should be while also getting you thinking about your career as a biomedical engineer. Assignments are not difficult at all. Attendance is mandatory and checked. If you take the time and treat the class as a guide for you, you will learn a lot of information that you'll use for other classes.

The best professor I've ever had. Such a kind, caring guy who knows exactly how to guide your thinking to lead you to discover things for yourself, which is very important for 2250. This class is so dependent on how good your prof and TAs are - he absolutely made it for me and everyone else there. Highly, highly recommend.

Todd SLAYS. I went into BMED1000 (not BMED 2400 stupid rate my professor) not really thinking I was going to get much out of it, but you so do if you just pay attention and learn the things he's actually trying to teach you. He is so funny and inspirational and understnading. 10/10 human being and 10/10 class.
Dr. Fernandez is one of the kindest, most considerate, and helpful professors I've had. He really cares about his students which unfortunately isn't common practice at Georgia Tech.

Todd was the nicest professor Ive had at GT. His care for students is exceptional, and he made statistics really interesting. I know a lot of people consider taking ISYE stats, but if Todd is an option I would recommend him. The homework is time consuming but helpful. If you do what he says and stay on top of your work, an A is definitely possible

Goes far in depth about statistical and mathematical concepts, but still interesting to learn about. Projects can be done without a solid understanding in material, but it's more fulfilling to solidify your understanding of concepts. Really caring and interesting professor.

Not sure why this course gets so much hate. Dellaert is a caring professor that listens to students' concerns, and actively tries to ensure students in lecture understand the content. The content itself is quite difficult, but there's more than enough time provided to complete projects and receive full points. No in class exams reduces stress.

it takes weeks for grades to be returned to you. in addition, the criteria for the lengthy reflection portion of projects is extremely unclear, and the weight for each project in canvas is wrong, causing unnecessary stress for students. lectures were also incredibly hard to follow. don't take this class.

I've never felt so entirely lost. Unless you have a really solid stats background before starting this class, it feels like you're doomed to take away nothing. Pretty intense math/concepts and new ones every lecture. Difficult homeworks feel like "so what?" when you finish them. Entirely dissuaded me from doing robotics ever again.

Is very passionate about the topic he teaches, however completely centers his course around a textbook he wrote and a library he created. This feels less of a lecture/course and more of him flaunting his own works and forcing students to use them, even if they can be useful. Homework is long and lots of busy work. Lectures are complex but useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: It's an intro class, and he tries to smack in too much content for what it is. Quizzes were quite difficult with the only relief being they were untimed and open book. Explains way too fast. Projects were a decent amount, and there was a lot of math to cover.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Horrible class structure and homeworks. Lectures are confusing and hard to follow. So is the book, which was written by him and not fully proofread. He is primarily a researcher and delves way too far into hard concepts that make no sense for an introductory course. Quizzes are graded easily are take home and take a while. Haven't learned anything.

The professor is caring, the topic is fun, and his contributions to it are impressive. But the class sucks. Lectures are hard to follow; projects are excessive, poorly made, and not educational; frequent quizzes have many essay questions that are a huge time drain; grading is slow and feedback is vague or missing; review material is non-existent.

I think he's trying to cover so many things in depth. It should be focused on the intro level as the course title implies.  It's impossible to understand the concepts fully, so doing quizzes and projects is like solving 1000*1000 puzzles. I feel like I'm overwhelmed...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: if you want to get turned off from the concept of robotics - take this class! Dull lectures, textbook, and assignments. It's probably easy to get an A, but the class is torturous to sit through. Don't think the textbook or lectures give you enough info to truly understand what you're doing

Took him for both this class and CS 3630. Has definitely improved his lectures, much easier to grasp. In fact, both them and the projects moreso served to increase your curiosity in Computer Vision than challenge your understanding of math. That said, some of the projects do drag on for a bit longer than they should.

He is one of the worst professors I have ever taken. I have 1 semester remaining for graduation. His lectures are absolute garbage which takes 1-3 hours of weekend away. I could spend that time better doing something useful. Quiz questions are nothing like he teaches in lectures. He doesn't care about his students and causes unnecessary stress.

Dr Dellaert is truly more of a researcher than a professor. He literally invented some of the concepts in the syllabus. He deviates a lot into recent research when introducing concepts in class, which I think is a good feature for an introductory class like this one. Would strongly recommend if you want to learn about current trends in robotics.
His lectures are complete garbage. His projects are a complete mess. The class with him is completely useless.

Professor Farvez gives intense lectures. He's very vocal, and his oral skills are through the roof. I've never been so satisfied in such a long, hard semester, but he's honestly the best. I spent a lot of time in one-on-one office hours. Despite the tight deadlines, he encourages hard work with rigid schedules and stiff grading.

Professor Farvez was an extraordinary teacher. He reached above and beyond what should be expected from a professor, and always offered up advice or just a friendly face to talk to whenever his students needed it. Ask him about his youtube channel!
In these trying times, Professor Farvez was honestly a bright spot in a difficult semester. Despite his intimidating accomplishments, he's a humble and nice instructor who truly wants you to succeed.
Professor Farvez really makes you work hark in this class, but you learn so much! One of the best professors and best classes I've had and taken at Tech. Truly lifechanging.
Been a few years since I took his class, but I still think about how great he was to this day.
Not his student, but an old peer of his that's been admiring from afar. Good job bro, keep up the amazing work. You're truly a legend.
After the wild end of the Spring 2020 semester, Professor Farvez was incredibly understanding and made the awkward transition from physical to online lectures seamless. Truly a class act.
Amazing lecturer!
Amazing professor. I don't think I'd take this class with anyone else.
This is one those professors where you know you would talk to again even after completing the course. Attendance was mandatory but his excellent explanations make it mandatory. What a guy
Great person, learned everything I need to know about life from him. Really appreciated guy!
very good. very nice. very yes

I haven't gotten a chance to take any of his real classes yet but I hear he's an overall nice guy. Not too strict and knows Tech students go through a lot so tries to be understanding and lenient with grading. Likes to uplift lectures by sharing memes. Actually not a professor yet but maybe one day.
Take another professor. Readings were way too much, so make sure to study for the exam. Also only graded by a few things.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i used to like her in the beginning of the semester, but the readings were just way too much. also, she does not put grades in until the end of the semester so you never really know where you stand. she does not like when you use the computer in class for some reason? even if it just means taking notes. however, the lectures were interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class itself is really interesting and the professor is the nicest person I've ever met. The one test we had was pretty difficult, but it was mainly memorization. Very reading-heavy, but interesting ones. There was a group project that was pretty easy to do and a final essay/project that was decently designed.

Dr. Farooq is one of those teachers that you simply have to take at GT and she is genuinely one of the kindest and best professors I have ever had. Note to future students though, she does not post grades so make sure to keep in mind the breakdown of grades from the syllabus. Participation is key and can make or break your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Farooq is the nicest woman on Earth. She truly cares for the mental health of her students, so don't be afraid to reach out. She teaches Intro to Social Justice in a unique way by viewing it through multiple lenses like technology or law. I learned so much! Love her.
The most amazing professor ever! I am going to try very hard to take a class with her again. 11/10 would recommend.

Very few professors connect with students the way Dr. Farooq does. She assigns a lot of reading but it's not impossible to keep up with it and most are interesting reads. If you show interest in the class and reach out to her if you're having difficulty, she will help in any way she can. She's incredible and I encourage anyone to take her classes.

Amazing lecturer, maybe not the greatest class for students without an interest in reading and writing, but I loved it! She is incredibly eloquent and smart in everything she has to say. Very funny too, joked and got along with all of the class.

She's a very nice lady and is very clear, a wonderful professor, just I did not click with the class.  It requires a lot of writing and reading.  There is about a novel to read every week and a half.  She encourages in class discussion and is willing to help and is very encouraging.  Her class is for only a few people, but she is a great professor.

Professor Farooq is a very nice woman, her class requires alot of outside reading. Your grade basically consists of your participation and writing. Basically if you can write well this class is for you. She is very enthusiastic about meeting with you to help you out if you need help. I recommend this class.

American culture was actually American lit, have to buy 14!!! books!! presentations,3 absense=lose a letter grade. DONT TAKE!!unless you want to read a novel a week. crazy insane ammount of work with a strict teacher. AVOID!!!!

Pretty tough class with a tough professor. He goes through the material pretty fast during lecture but show up and pay attention during lecture because test questions were similar to ones he did in lecture. Tests were pretty hard and really tested your understanding of the material. Read a textbook, practice, and go to TA office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is a tough grader and doesn't teach you anything that is required for the harder IE classes in the future.

[Duplicate review for more characters] Lectures not mandatory, but no released lecture notes so SHOW UP. Homeworks are decently straightforward, reference the free pdf textbook for additional help. Never went to office hours so can't say anything there. 12 homeworks and 3 very hard and very broad exams is all the class is, assignments wise. Chiller
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grading scale is every 20 points: A = [100,80] B = (80, 60] etc. Very hard and broad material, very hard and broad tests. Made a 28/100 and 20/100 on the two mid-terms, did better on the final (still sub 65), and this absolute GOAT flat curved my finishing grade up an unholy amount of points that I'm not telling as to not set precedent.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I didn't learn anything from the lectures, you learn as you're doing hw. Hw is due on Sunday 6 pm. Shoutout the TAs for the review session tho
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i was a happy girl who always smiled. After taking isye 2027 with foley, all of that joy quickly disappeared. I studied for DAYS for that final just to end up right below the A mark, and he never even told us about curving and wa so unclear. SO hard pls be warned.
Theres only 2 exams and a final which are 5 questions each and no partial credit. Class average on the second exam was a 43% and still no curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: First of all, his lectures are so hard to understand, he has no powerpoints, and does not take lecture recordings. Also, he states in the syllabus if you take your own lecture recordings he should not be in the video. His tests are hard and his practice tests do not have answer keys so you do not know if you are right.

Dr. Foley is very unorganized and teaches in an outdated manner with no online materials. Lectures lack structure, and exam expectations are unclear and inconsistent with past exams. He answers questions but shows little concern for grades or feedback. Final grade details are not provided, leaving grading and any potential curve unclear.

Dr. Foley is a super understanding professor. He is very accessible to answer any questions and clearly knows a lot about the material. It is a difficult class, but his tests are pretty fair and the homeworks are challenging, but help a lot.

Yes Foley is hard. He teaches in a very different way then most. Once you get used to they way he teaches he is not bad! He would let our questions guide his lectures. He was very helpful with all questions. GO TO OFFICE HOURS!! Don't get behind and ask questions when you are confused and you will do fine in the class. He is very nice guy. SHOW UP!

He's an incredibly kind and intelligent professor, however he posts next to no resources on canvas, gives no partial credit, and the textbook does not correlate at all to what happens in class or what is on homeworks/the exams.

Foley knows that it is very test heavy and is very forgiving. If you show that you care and come to all of the lectures, Foley will give you a leg up when it comes to a curve. Foley genuinly cares about his students which can be shown if you go to his office hours or stay a bit after class. He doesn't want to see you fail but you also have to work.

Professor Foley is very knowledgeable and caring, but he is very disorganized when it comes to lectures. Don't skip lectures tho. Exams are difficult and don't exactly cover the topics that you expect it would cover. Although this class is difficult, it is not impossible. Attending TA office hours old exam problems are probably the best resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Foley is very caring, but the class is very unforgiving. 80% of your grade is determined by three tests with no partial credit. Tests are very similar to previous exams (posted online), and he goes over great examples in lectures. Tough with no answer keys, but if you put lots of effort into understanding everything, you will do very well.

Professor Foley is such a sweet & smart man, but a horrible teacher. No partial credit is given on ANY exam which leaves the average scores being around a 50%-60%. Additionally he does provide practice exams but getting solutions, or even a direct answer to questions regarding the test, is IMPOSSIBLE. A TA literally said "I dont remember the ans"
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: NO partial credit on tests - doesn't even look at your work. Example tests from 1998 but NO ANSWER KEYS FOR ANY. time-consuming hw, but only worth 20% and is graded harshly. Lectures consist of him writing all over the board, switching topics with no warning. If you require some sort of structured plan to learn, you probably shouldn't take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Would not recommend taking his class. No partial credit means that getting a tiny part of any question wrong instantly reduces your grade by a significant factor. Practice tests for midterms are given, however there is no way to tell how you're doing on them because solutions are not provided.

Does not do a good job of really making this class feel like a learning environment, he just goes on tangents during all classes. Does not provide answer keys to tests, no partial credit which makes these tests almost impossible. Class is extremely difficult for no reason.

Might be one of the worst teachers I've ever had.
Partial credit on tests = 1 small thing wrong on one of the parts of the questions is an immediate 70%
'Textbook' is a lecture notes pdf.
Canvas is as barebones as it gets.
Lectures ramble on nonsensically.
Provides old tests back from 1998, but does not give solutions to any of them.
8 a.m lecture.

Very good professor -- funny, caring, and explains concepts clearly. The homework can be difficult and time consuming, but if you put in the time, and review notes after each lecture, the tests will be fairly easy.

No partial credit, lecture recordings, or practice test answers; writes on a whiteboard; teaches through examples- it is a big ole struggle bus. Would not recommend taking him even if he's the only option. Great and funny guy, but tests on stuff that's not very similar to the examples in class. Can work together on homework; crib sheet=harder test

Foley is great in lecture and will prepare you extremely well for future ISyE classes. Unfortunately, you will likely have to sacrifice this grade for those long term benefits because this class is insanely hard. No partial credit on tests, homeworks are difficult and he doesn't post the lectures on canvas. He does post previous tests to study
Great professor. Grades are pretty fairly given out and he is happy to help you understand the material. Really personable and knowledgeable professor.

ISYE 2027 was an interesting class with Professor Foley. On one hand, he was incredibly nice and just a genuinely caring teacher (he tried to learn every students name in his class). On the other hand, the class was pretty difficult, and sometimes lectures were hard to follow. Be prepared for lots of homework assignments as well.

Fantastic professor.  Very receptive to feedback and makes lectures engaging, and he's always available via email to respond to questions.  Exams are simple if you really know the material, but no partial credit.  Lectures are usually amazing, but can be slow at times to set up future concepts - don't miss classes though, or you'll fall behind!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Foley is very smart and knows what he teaches. However, he is not a good teacher. Lectures are based on examples and not on explaining topics. Sometimes I did not even know what topic he was giving. I would not recommend this professor at all. He is a very good person but not a good professor. What saved my grade was the curve.

hardest class ever but he's hard to hate bc he's so nice. hw = hard & graded for accuracy. only grades in canvas are hw, 2 midterms, & final. class avg for every midterm is usually an F/low C. class is gonna be curved, but u won't know where u stand until final grades are released. rly hard to get an A unless u devote most of ur time to this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Foley is a good lecturer but that is where the compliments end. he refuses to give partial credit despite it being an engineering course, the homeworks and tests are always far more complex than the examples in class and the textbook is next to useless

Foley is amazing, his lectures are always very well put together and he is extremely knowledgeable . Answers questions in class. Since class is all about probability, no partial credit on exams. Class has 2 exams, weekly homework, and a final. Homework can be tough but the professor answers a lot of questions via email and sends them out 2 everyone
Easy grade, but prof is unorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very unorganized but answers questions

Such a great profesor. He is clearly very knowledgable and knows how to teach to multiple teaching styles. If you take the time to participate in lecture, ask him questions outside -- he makes himself very easily available -- and focus on homework, you will be totally set for an A.

Dr. Foley is extremely caring, understanding, and responsive. He is very easy to reach if you ever have any questions about the material and will make sure you understand the concept after you ask him questions about it. Although his exams are hard, the homeworks give you a cushion and help you understand the material thoroughly.

I really liked the content of the class, and Dr. Foley presented it in a great manner in the online lectures. There is a large emphasis on homework, as it was 70% of our grade, and the other 30% was tests and the midterm and final. Definitely watch the lectures and take notes, as otherwise, it'll be very difficult to do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you have the chance, definitely take a class with him before you leave. The homeworks were very difficult, but you derive properties that help you really understand the core concepts of probability. I dont think I couldve learned better with any other prof for this class. No partial credits on tests, but he always grades on a curve. 10/10.

Foley was honestly my favorite prof at Tech so far, and he made the 8 am worth it. The homework is challenging, but very cleverly made in order to build upon itself and teach the material. Don't be scared when the test averages are super low, he understands and the class is curved. A great and super-intelligent man!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: For lecture, besides going over the material, he also does example problems that appear in the homework and tests. Understand how to do the homework and examples from class, and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super caring professor that wants you to succeed. Not an easy class but if you work hard and do the practice tests you can get an A.

Foley is a great guy. Really cares about whether or not students are learning the material. I would say try to go to as many lectures as possible. Attendance isn't really required, but his in class examples and discussions will really help a ton on exams and homeworks. He usually teaches an 8am, but if you work through waking up, it really helps!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Foley has been the best professor I've had at Tech. He makes classes interesting and easy to understand. There are many tough assignments, but they usually boost your grade and help you understand the class material. You need to go to class and take notes to get a good grade. His exams are tough (no partial credit), but he curves at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Foley is such a sweet old man- he cares so much about his students. However, lectures are extremely hard to follow, and he doesn't post notes anywhere so you HAVE to go to class. HWs: hard af but grades easy. Tests: hard af and no partial credit. But he curved my final grade of 54% to a B, so it all works out. Not a bad prof if you want a B
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Good professor. Hard class. Hard exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures make no sense, I only survived this class because of the textbook- after weeks of begging him to send out the text sections we should be responsible for (his class notes did not correlate at all). Tests are nearly impossible to do well on- 18 short questions with no partial credit. Class is curved a ton but not worth the stress

Dr. Foley really cares about students. He's not that great of a lecturer and his notes are sometimes confusing, but he gives you a lot of homework and tests you over similar concepts. He grades on a curve. I ended up with a grade much higher than I was expecting because of how I was doing so poorly. So I'm definitely glad I took him.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Foley is an excellent professor. His homeworks are time-consuming and difficult, however, they're helpful and the grading is lenient. His exam questions are basically an extension of what you've already done. Use recent past exams and homeworks to study for his exams. Lectures are disorganized, but he's happy to stop and explain whenever.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Foley is a great professor who really wants you to do well. You'll most likely do poorly on every test, but you'l most likely end up with a B in the class. The class isn't that time consuming, and the homework is helpful. Go to office hours. An A is attainable so don't use his GPA as an excuse to be lazy.

Dr. Foley is awesome. He's a great guy. You will end up with a B in the class NO MATTER WHAT. Keep that in mind. He's a stickler for his GPA, so he legit rounds at least 90% of the class down/up to a B. So don't worry if you are sitting at a 50 or 60 in the class. You're fine. HW is difficult. Find old HWs. Practice old tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Very good teacher, cares a lot and is very accessible after class to go over material. However, the lectures can be a bit unorganized at times, and the tests do not have partial credit, so do not be alarmed by your low test score, there is a curve. Also make sure to start homework early, it is long and an important part of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Spent a lot of time studying for this class, but often was disappointed by results on tests (short answer math, no partial credit). Homeworks take hours to complete, and it is difficult to prepare for tests because he doesn't give answers to practice tests. Great lecturer, answers questions; if you put in effort, expect a B.

Amazing professor, very helpful in and out of class, however, there's no structure for ISYE 2027, and classes from previous years do not reflect the content and speed of coverage for the current class. Homework is very tedious but tests are easier. He likes to keep the average GPA between 2.9 and 3.0, so that's how the curve will be determined.

Dr. Foley is by far one of the best professors I've had so far. He genuinely cares about every student and is very clear and specific in his explanations. His tests are fair - they stem mainly from lecture notes and HW questions, but the HW can be quite difficult. However, he always sends emails to the entire class answering questions, which is a +
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had at Tech. The class wasn't easy and homework's are long and difficult, but he is very willing to help, responds to emails quickly, and the classwork and homework are very indicative of what tests will be like. Very nice guy. Would take one of his classes again

Was my favorite course of my freshman year even though it was the only one I got a B in. The lectures are very interesting and very free flowing. They have a nice flow between him directing the lecture and taking student requests for better explanations. If you ever needed help he was there during office hours too.

Foley is a really sweet guy.   However, 80% of his class's grades are made up of two tests and a final, and he never gives partial credit.  The other 20% of his class is made up of 6 or 7 impossible homeworks that very often include things he doesn't cover in the class. He gives you practice exams, but won't give you answer keys.

He is one of the best professors I've had. It's not going to be an easy A. You have to work for it. The hw's are difficult and he assigns them every week, but the tests arent as hard as the hw. If you understand the hw, then you'll do fine in the test. No partial credit for the tests, which messed my grades up a bit. He curves at the end.
Great teacher , solid course.

He was overall a very good teacher. Didn't really use the book much except for a few homework problems. Homeworks were difficult and took a lot of time, but helped teach you the concepts. Tests werent terrible, but you had to study quite a bit. Very willing to help if you have questions though.

Pros: Really nice guy, really good teacher. Cares a lot about the material and his students. You will learn a lot if you show up, pay attention, and ask questions. Tests are pretty manageable. Just make sure you can do his old practice tests and you'll be set. Cons: Homework is every week, and hard as sh!t.

This class is one of the hardest I have ever taken. The homework is insane. The midterms and final are extremely tricky. The course material is not that hard, Dr. Foley just chooses to make it really hard. However, he generously curves the final grades. I never got above a 50 on a test, and I finished with a C. He has your best interest at heart.

Dr. Foley is a great guy.  However, HWs are very hard and most of the time do not involve what we cover in class.  Study, go to the TA for HW, form a study group, and study.  Tests are not bad, but he does not give partial credit so don't mess up.  Don't expect an A if your scores are not 20-30 points above the average.
Very smart teacher. Tests are tricky, but fair. Homework is barely related to material covered in class, and does not provide much help to students for it.
Very confusing class. HW is difficult and takes a long time, and test questions are random. Go talk to him when you need help - better learning environment. (TA's are great for hw help!)
very cool in class. you'll dislike the class when you have him, but after you finish, you'll thank him

hard teacher, but good teacher and helps you learn some important ISYE material. hw was pretty difficult. tests averages were about a 60. good teacher overall. no open notes or calculators. practice tests are pretty similar.
The best teacher for a intro to probability class there is at Gatech. If I had another chance to take this class I wouldn't take it with anyone else.

best way to describe him is the coolest tough professor. his class is based pretty much on student's questions, and homework is based mostly on what we talk about in class. smart guy, explains things very well. exams are not too bad if you STUDY. you need to study, and you need to do hw. he grades on a curve that is based on class performancce
Must go to lectures if you want to learn anything. Very helpful if you got a question. Do all the practice tests and you'll be fine. If you do really well, definetely will get a B or an A.
I thought he was an excellent teacher.  He kept lecture very interesting, and a barely had to crack my textbook.  I would definitely reccomend him to anyone.
No Comments
Easy as nuts! Not an IE major, but Probability is so freaking easy. How could you not get an A in this class? Imaginary Engineers.

I didn't like him, he is very undecisive about his teaching.  He doesn't write stuff until someone in the class says it and if someone in the class asks a question he makes someone else answer it instead of answering it himself.  The homework was ridiculously tough and the tests were easy.

Nice guy but very disorganized class. Everything was posted late and he was frequently late to class at 2pm. Slides were just screenshots of the textbook. Sometimes made concepts more confusing than they had to be, but had a good sense of humor and lectures were somewhat enjoyable. Homeworks were very long.

Excellent and kind professor, extremely hard class. The course material is definitely not easy for a freshman. Be ready to read the textbook and spend a long time studying on weekends. But he curves a lot for us, so even though you get a low grade on exams, you still have a high chance of getting an A.

First is a great teacher. Great sense of humor, clear explanations, and friendly. Homework was heavy and tests varied in difficulty, but mostly hard. I took 2 classes with him and would take more. To the posters below: This might be because he had to teach intro physics to you...
The professor was not really helpful but the class was not hard. Attendance optional.

Rigor can be described as a lot for a humanities course, but it is a good option if you are already interested in linguistics. Sometimes struggles to keep class quiet but is always open to feedback. Mandatory attendance for weekly quizzes. Very kind + relatable for younger students! Would reccommend
She's very open to changing course structure based on student feedback. Clearly passionate about the topic and is open to improving the course to help students as a whole.
If I went to Stanford for my PhD to only make 90k I'd make the course dreadful for the students too. She expects us to memorize 400 slides per test, piquing on the littlest of details. DO NOT TAKE!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amount of effort required for a humanities elective is insane. Also the content is unintuitive and the class feels overwhelming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Too much work for a humanities class.

Im being real: if you're taking this just to fill a humanities requirement, don't. If you want a chill A, this isn't it. Expect ~1 hr of homework, strict on-time attendance (she starts immediately), and quizzes. It's linguistics at a STEM school but not easy only take it if you're ready to put in real work for an A. Plan accordingly and manage time

I was a happy girl before taking this class. If you are not religious, pick one and pray for your sanity. I used to love to speak languages and communicate with my peers, but after taking this course with Professor glass, i went mute.

She was super nice and genuinely passionate about the subject. You don't have to go to class except once a week for quizzes so make sure to attend for those. Homework takes a long time, but there aren't very many. The exams are straightforward, and the portfolios boost your grade. There is no cumulative final exam."

Professor Glass is overall a fine professor. However, beware of the class. Each tests covers 200-275 slides of information and all of it is expected to be memorized, sometimes very specific questions are asked about very subtle points hidden somewhere in the slides. 1-2 hours per homework, 6 hr study for test = A. Topics range beyond linguistics.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Clear syllabus with grading criteria. Textbook was optional. Weekly in class quizzes---not too hard. Usually weekly homework, not too bad. If you use the study guides she provides, the exams are straightforward, no surprises. Good prof, answers emails and in-class questions.

Good at explaining, but not a good professor personally. Harshly grades/treats students she does not really like. During office hour, I asked for advice for homework, but she responded pretty rudely that I should put whatever I think is plausible. Secured a fair grade by overworking. It was a nightmare, and I will def avoid her in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took LING 4813, studying semantics and pragmatics. She does a wonderful job of distilling all the knowledge from the textbook into easily read handouts, and has a wonderful setup for the final paper as well. Each day I looked forward to learning some new tidbit about language that I had known about but never known the name of. Great class!

Really interesting subject mater. Dr. Glass is kinda all over the place in her lectures but the weekly quizzes are easy and self graded. The HW and tests are also pretty straight forward. I would take this class again and would recommend it to anyone else as an easy humanities.

In terms of HW, expect to spend 1-2 hours. Lenient with deadlines so just submit before grading starts. Very relaxed, we stop working on quiz if most people are finished, then we start grading our own quizzes. Sometimes we do in-class activities, which could be fun. Lectures can be confusing as she speakers fast. To enjoy the class, participate.
Dr. Glass is obviously very passionate about linguistics, and will teach you a lot if you are willing to learn. Very understanding with the online structure!

Highly accessible and gave very clear and helpful feedback. Willing to work with students to make the assignments doable and engaging. The class had unusually low enrollment, but I'm very glad I didn't drop it. There were many assignments, but they ended up being very fun and covered a wide range of fields and topics in which to apply linguistics.

I found his lectures difficult to follow, it seems to be a case of "knows what he's talking about, doesn't know how to teach it." He started posting his lectures (which are based heavily on the textbook) after the first exam, and the exams are based off practice problems that he posts the solutions to. Manageable class, and he's a nice guy.
good luck if you decide to take him. he was genuinely the worst teacher i've ever had in my entire life!!

He clearly knows what he's doing but does a terrible job explaining it. He reads the textbook and just does the problems on paper, not explaining how it works. Also has the heaviest accent so have fun trying to understand. Tests are standardized so feel free to sign up for him and go to someone else's lectures or just read the textbook yourself.

Although he does have an accent, it did not interfere with his teaching. He very obviously knew the material well and every concept was clear. Plenty of example problems during lecture. Combined with the studio, I had no complaints with Dr. Goldsztein.

Underrated, knowledgable, and funny guy. Lectures confusing and rambles, but he does teach you what you need to know with a lot of extra stuff. He deserves more credit as a prof. Jankowski's lecture videos are WAY more helpful though. Do the practice tests! They prep you for the tests and final. Take him if you don't get Jankowski. 1553 can be hard

Professor Goldsztein is honestly underrated, although I do see why some people couldn't really learn well from his lectures. I went to every single one of his lectures and did pretty decent in the class overall. Give him a chance before deciding to go to another professor's lectures or watching Jankowski's lectures. Also do the practice tests pls.

He makes class enjoyable but I do not think that I learned anything in class. Luckily Linear Algebra is not too hard and there are a ton of resources available to help you learn outside of class. Overall, all 1553 professors have the same tests and grading scales so it does not matter who you get as a professor as long as you can teach yourself.

DO NOT UNDERESTIMATE 1553. Had to stop going to this guys lectures because he did not explain concepts well at all. Seems like a good person, but his teaching ability needs work. Ended up just watching Jankowski's lectures which is what i would recommend if you have to take him. Also study your butt off for your exams, you absolutely need too.

Lectures were fine, but a little disorganized and confusing at points. I ended up skipping his classes and going to Jankowski's lectures after the first exam. He is a fun professor, but I recommend watching Jankowski's lectures instead.
Lectures were fun to sit through, but the content was sometimes unorganized. Still a great professor but I ended up watching Jankowski's lectures.
amazing at explaining things, I promise you'll do better if you not just go to class but PAY ATTENTION

I love him!... as a person. No but really, you can tell he cares about the content but his lectures confused me so much. I ended up going to class because I enjoyed him and his jokes,but i mainly watched other professors online. He goes through topics very quick and the lectures are not structured at all. class was fun, just not helpful sadly :(

Funny guy. Very funny guy. 

I wish he was as good at teaching as he is funny. 

Tbh all the linear profs are bad except for jankowski. I would take him again bc his classes were comedy sessions.

Ended up skipping class and watching Jankowski's old videos to learn. Went to his class for a comedy session. I'll certainly miss this man next semester bc of his hilarious lectures, but he's DEF not good at teaching. For example, he doesn't introduce the topic, just writes a paragraph, messing something up, sighs, and sounds fed up after.
Notes were not great, ended up just going to Simone's lectures
Goldsztein is a pretty funny guy if you attend his lectures. They aren't the most clear but with the other resources given to us, I feel like he was a decent enough teacher.

Hard to understand during lectures, to the point I stopped going to them altogether. Additionally, does not use the powerpoint notes posted to canvas, instead writing rewriting them all during the lecture (but the handwriting is difficult to read as well), so it was easier to just teach the material to myself. Also, tests extremely conceptual/hard.

His lectures are ok. I disagree with people saying they were awful, but I still didn't get much from all of them. Some were a bit scattered. My TA (Saksham Malik) hard carried me through this course via the studio. Go to a good TA's studio and the review sessions and you will be fine, don't even need the lecture tbh. Better choices, but not bad.
Very bad

Avoid at all costs. Made me feel I'm stupid but turned out he is just a shi**y professor. I gave up on his lectures and started watching old recorded lectures of another professor. Also, gets angry when you ask him respectfuly for something. Sends very weird emails that make you confused on the test.

I presented a problem to him that many students had after a test (in a respectful matter), and he emailed me very angrily claiming I was attacking professors and putting pressure on them. I just wanted to know if we could get partial credit for a problem. So I'm gathering that he is not very understanding or accommodating to students. Beware.

The only thing that I did was go to class and attend the studios and solve problems outside class, and it worked out fine for me. He has some accent when he speaks, but it was totally fine for me. He is a funny guy, and I love his personality. He answers questions enthusiastically during lecture and after lecture ended in the classroom.

Dr. Goldsztein was fine. Nice guy, I just didn't get a ton from the lectures. I learned mostly from studio and Dr. Jankowski's videos. This class was unified though, so it didn't really matter where you got it from.

Frankly, I stopped going to Dr. Goldsztein's lectures because I could not learn anything from him. He is reluctant to answer questions and not accessible outside of class. Linear algebra is already a hard class, and Dr. Goldsztein just made it harder. I ended up going to another prof's lectures. I would not recommend taking MATH 1553 with this prof

He seemed like a good guy and was amusing, but, though he understood the concepts, he had a tough time explaining the concepts of linear algebra, something where a good instructor is key. He also did not answer questions well, especially when students tried connecting them to other related 1553 topics. To succeed, I needed to rely on the textbook.

The textbook is your only friend, but is written badly and relies on you memorizing a bunch of seemingly arbitrary mathematical properties. The course is written poorly and this professor is pretty boring. The lectures are hard to follow from how slow he is. Thankfully, it's not a difficult course, just taught very poorly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly gives very mediocre lectures. I stopped going three weeks in because they weren't at all helpful. Very difficult to follow and didn't contribute anything more than the textbook itself, which is available online and a great resource, I highly recommend using it. Didn't answer any of my emails.

This class was awful. People with other professors did not suffer as much as we did. Dr. Goldstein is nice, but his teaching lacks a great deal of necessary information. I learned most of the information from the textbook and I know I would have failed without it. Practice tests are the saving grace.

goldsztein was funny but his lectures practically never finished the material and then you had to finish the lecture outside of class on your own. my grades drastically improved when i started going to jankowskis lectures instead. homework, textbook, and old exams were really useful
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He did a good job going through and explaining examples of how to do calculation-based problems but mostly neglected to explain conceptual ideas in detail. The class is formatted so that way all of 1553 have the same homework and exams due at the same time. Id say go to you TA or another lecturer if you need help understanding the material better.
Funny guy, but basically have to teach the class yourself.

His lectures are okay, but I wouldn't have passed the class without reading the textbook. He is genuinely very funny and sweet, but the course is really hard, and you might end up teaching yourself the material. He seems to cover everything during lectures, but once you read the textbook you realize how much he missed.

If you can, don't take Guillermo's class. Linear algebra is standardized so the tests and homework for all of the professors is the same, but his lectures are definitely worse than other professors to the point where showing up to class seemed unnecessary. If you take his class, expect to do a lot of self-teaching, but he's a nice guy.
Relaxed guy who liked to crack jokes every now and then. He covered the material well, giving adequate notes with examples. Has an accent but did not affect my learning.
Impossible to understand with thick accent, very slow too. Ended up skipping class and just reading the book. The class isn't a cakewalk, but moderately diligent studying will get you an A
A good professor. He wasnt amazing, but he prepared you for the exams and will answer any questions you have.

He did not explain his problem solving well nor did he answer conceptual questions well. He did not really care for the students. His thick accent was very hard to understand through the lecture videos at times.

GGold is such a cool teacher. He is a funny guy as well. He made lectures for the class to view on their own time and then would answer any questions we had in class. He would go above and beyond to fully explain and walk through any problems which was very helpful. He did have a thick accent but I actually enjoyed it.

Lectures are not the best but are okay if used as a supplement to reading the textbook. His accent is fairly strong but understandable. He is willing to go through homework questions during office hours, so take advantage of that. Overall a funny dude but due to the nature of the material, you probably have to study to get a good grade.

This class is a 2 credit course that ALL majors have to take. the GT math department has somehow managed to make THIS class the absolute hardest for no reason. The professor doesnt even make the quizzes or exams so lectures are completely irrelevant and useless. tests purposely ask you questions in twisted ways so you can only make a B OR C.

He has relatively average explanations that leave a lot of holes and questions even if you read the textbook (I read the textbook, was taking the khan academy course, and used Youtube as well). However, during office hours he is "willing to answer" questions. I cannot express how many times my questions were ignored or my intelligence was insulted.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Very nice and funny guy, I feel like he *wants* to be a good lecturer but he just isnt. Sit up close cuz he talks to the board. Has a bit of an accent but you get used to it quickly. Will answer ANY questions very well during/after class so definitely ask them. Exams are very similar to the practice ones & the textbook+examples are VERY helpful.
Just another one of those classes where you have to learn the material yourself and you have no idea what's going on in the class.

Professor Goldsztein had a tendency of just covering stuff directly out the book, but that wasn't necessarily a bad thing. We never missed a topic or a major theorem and he was pretty good at explaining some of the more abstract concepts. Not to mention he liked to crack jokes. Just make sure you understand and do the homework to do well.

Nice professor that cares about his students, but has a tendency to just go and "run away" with his lectures. If you're not very comfortable with linear algebra, get ready to struggle. The textbook is going to be your friend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: he just reads out of the online textbook and explained things in the most abstract way possible. Recitation and YT videos are better teachers as I often left the class more confused than beforehand. only after the 1st exam i realized i didnt know anything. I never skip class out of principle but this class was the exception. quizzes are easy tho.

He is a funny person, but his lectures are confusing, especially after the eigenvalue chapter. What he writes on the board are exactly the same as what appears on the textbook, and he forgets to mention many important theorems during lectures. However, his quizzes are straightforward, and as long as you put in some work you should be fine.

Dr. Goldsztein is a great person and he is funny. However he does have a heavy accent which can make it difficult to understand him at times. He will answer any questions you have and he wants everyone to understand. As long as you pay attention in lecture and study a little bit you'll pass his class.

This is the guy you take if you want to get an A without having to work too hard. Skipped every lecture and got away without any issues. Exams are practically carbon copies of practice exams he provides.
Dr. Goldsztein is a great guy - he's funny and super chill, but his lectures are sometimes confusing. If you put in work, an A is achievable.

Really approachable. Lectures are confusing but just study the practice tests. Is really great about taking all questions, no matter how basic. Quiz every Friday which is annoying but he tells you what the quiz will cover so not difficult. Doesn't care if you sleep or text in lecture

When you're in class you have no clue what's going on, and it's pretty easy not to pay attention. But, this professor really cares about how his students do, and he is always willing to answer a question. The tests are super easy and the practice exams are basically what you should expect on the actual final. Easy A for most people.
His lectures are confusing sometimes and he has a hard time explaining the material, but the tests are easy and exactly like the practice exams. Good professor
Not much to say. He's not a professor I'm going to remember for ages. Never have I felt that he did not provide enough information, but at the same time he's no messiah if you're not good at math.

He's nice, and but he's not the best at explaining everything. He's happy to explain something multiple times, but it might not be any clearer than the first time. Tests mostly had basic questions, with only two or three hard ones (out of ten questions). This was Honors Calc II.
Loves his students, not the best at explaining and clarifying. Tests can be challenging but he will be fair.

After being behind due to a major change, I was able to catch up with his class. Has a bit of a heavy accent, but wants to make sure his students understand the material, which is always reassuring. Cool guy in general- pretty laid back and approachable.

It's very important to him that his students understand the material, which is more than I can say about most of the professors at Tech. Unfortunately, he's not the greatest at explaining things, so you may have to rely on the textbook or your TA a little.

He is a really nice guy. He actually cares about his students and asks for input. He is always willing to answer questions. He gives practice exams to help us study, which is similar to the tests. I recommend him to anyone that needs to take a course. He has an accent, but as long as you write what is on the board and go to recitation, it's fine.

He wasn't an amazing teacher, but if you asked for help he gladly gave it to you. His test varied on difficulty level depending on the material. The final was decent, but you had to know the material well. Overall it was a good class.

Goldsteinz is a rare breed at Tech. He actually cares about his students. Others may says hes hard to understand but thats only moderately true. He once gave my class an insane test and spent the rest of the semester giving us easier tests to make up for it. I wish all professors are like him. He is a great man. Take him if you get the chance.
No Comments

I had to drop his class midterm. He tries really hard, but he's so brilliant that explaining Calc 1 was hard for him. He even said in class, "I'm not a very good teacher." I don't recommend him for lower level math.

She took attendance sometimes in-class and sometimes using inclass activities which due the same day. Takes a long time period to get back term-test results. The final was cancelled near the end of the semester, so basically the grade will be based on only in-class activities and projects.

The course, as taught, isn't super difficult. Grading is really generous, and tests are mostly based on stuff from the slides. But it's often difficult to follow lectures because things move so fast and so much stuff gets skimmed past. Dr. Garten is very knowledgeable but difficult to reach outside of class.

lectures felt confusing and just like a bunch of info thrown with no coherency or good explanations, when a guest lecturer was teaching with the slides, they said the same thing. Also lecture slides and HW answer keys were not made available until significantly later, grades/exams not given back until pretty late as well.

Sometimes the lectures do not cover everything that you need to know. She rushes through concepts which makes it hard to understand all the material. The class scheme is very simple and you just need to put in extra effort.

25% HW and class clickers, 25% for two midterms and a final each. Tests are all multiple-choice, and the content is relatively easy to get. Good choice for knocking out this course, but make sure you don't fall behind, Units 1 and 2 are much easier conceptually than Unit 3, and the final tripped a lot of people up.
The best lecturer I have had. The class consists of mostly of homework and tests. Highly recommend using office hours, all the TAs were very good.
I love the way 1332 is structured. Never went to class because he recorded and uploaded the videos. Generally love the way he teaches as well as Mary's video, and I love how you can exempt the final!

lectures are pretty heavy in material. homeworks take a long time .tests focus on the stuff you see in lectures and practice tests are also helpful.he explains content well, but its sometimes hard to recall the giant amount of information he dumps in previous lectures. pay attention and review often
Clear lectures, lots of material, and tests that align to the course content. Homeworks take time but there's a lot of resources online and in the lecture to help with that.

Professor Faulkner is an excellent professor. His lectures are clear, well-paced, and easy to follow with annotated OneNote slides. If you pay attention and use the provided pseudocode, getting an A is very doable. Exams are fair and similar to the practice exams. There is also a lot of extra credit and a final exemption option.

Faulkner is a GOAT professor. In terms of learning from lectures, his lectures are far easier to follow than HB's, as he keeps things at a moderate pace with annotated notes on OneNote. He always keeps things straightforward, and if you pay attention in class, it is p easy to get an A if you also use the pseudocode they provide in course materials.

1332 itself is a very straightforward class, and Professor Faulker's lectures were easy to follow and understand-- most of the time I didn't require any review after paying full attention in class. He does speak really fast so if you plan on watching recordings, you'll most likely need to keep it at the normal speed.
My glorious king
Great lecturer, not really too keen on speaking to students personally but he explains concepts insanely well from the ground up. Would recommend!

Literal goat professor. Explained topics so clearly. Exams were very fair and similar to the practice exams, and there is a bunch of extra credit. You can exempt the final too. One thing I recommend is to take the hybrid version because they get recorded lecture videos which are up for a week, and can still attend lectures if you wish.
Very solid professor for 1332. Take if possible

Overall great lectures that are to the point. Explains things well and clearly. 

Uses OneNote instead of a PPT, which is so much better IMO. I hate lecturers that just use slides.
Best 1332 prof. Clear expectations and grading criteria, lots of extra credit and you can exempt the final.

Faulkner is the GOAT. Lectures are extremely well done and informative, and there are videos on canvas if you don't attend. Tests were very fair and you can exempt the final if you do well on them. Homework is manageable, especially with the help of CSVistool. Overall, definitely take 1332 with Faulkner.

Great guy, great professor, great course. I will say lectures lowkey take too long though just watch Prof MHB's module videos on canvas, they explain a full week's information in like 20 minutes. But nonetheless lectures are pretty good for understanding. Try to exempt the final cos it's worth it, exam 1,2,3 are pretty easy imo
Pretty good professor but definitely overglazed on rate my professor. Lectures are not very good for actually learning, but are decent for reinforcing prior knowledge.

Very good lecturer, really knows his stuff. However, he speaks extremely fast. So, I would learn the content before coming into class and then understand while he speaks rather than taking notes. Tests are standardized. Can watch MHB videos as review after going to Faulkner lecture. Very nice guy and good teacher. Also, he posts lecture videos.

He's an amazing lecturer, he is quite funny at times, and to be honest he seems really chill. But the thing is that this class is hard, and you're gonna need to put time into it outside, I'd say study for this class everyday for 45 mins to an hour, especially if you don't understand the content in lecture. Also practice alot with the given practice

Amazing lectures that go well with the HW's and exams. You will understand so much about every data structure and algorithm after this class. Also they added demos this semester which were alright just a little stressful under time pressure.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
1. Extremely knowledgeable TA's who are of great help
2. Great lecturer- love the real life examples
3. Easy homework that aids your learning a lot (dont GPT it!)
4. Structure of the class is smart and fun
5. Exams are tough

Great class! He organizes everything very well and you truly get out what you put into it. I would take any class w/ him.
Lots of cheating and giving away exam questions. His TAs definitely write some of these reviews to make them look better
Extremely good at teaching material, watching his recording + doing practice exams should be enough to do well on exams.

Fun class overall, the difficulty does increase over the semester. Make sure to take advantage of the early tests, as the later ones become harder and harder. He's very good at teaching as he explains almost every concept and goes through examples.

Phenomenal lecturer overall; engaging and funny at times but knows how to explain the concepts of the class really well. I took a hybrid section so I went to lecture in-person one day and watched a recording the other way, both of which were high quality (eventually, I just went to both in-person sections though, since attendance isn't checked).
Great prof, very structured, well made lectures. Always does examples and answers questions well. You can skip the final if you do well on the midterms too!

Go to his lectures if you can!! His explanations of data structures and process for tracing are straightforward and clear. The weekly homework makes you write up the data structures you're learning which is a bit of work but really helps with understanding

One thing I'll add to Professor Faulkner's list of compliments is how well he introduces ideas. He explains what situation you'd find yourself needing a data structure or algorithm before even teaching it- and this made understanding everything so much easier. He's a great professor.
great prof, good lectures, insanely difficult tests, make sure your study for them

I don't usually rate professors, but Faulkner deserves this 5. He talks a little fast in his lectures, but he somehow manages to explain everything clearly. I never struggled with any of the homeworks or exams, and all I relied on was his lectures and CSVisTool. This is coming from someone whose only prior coding knowledge is CS 1301 and 1331.
Cool dude, lectures are mostly useless (at least for hybrid), make sure to utilize office hours. Pretty easy class as long as you utilize csvistool well.
good teacher; difficult class (at least for me).

Faulkner's lectures are the best I've ever seen. He does a great job at giving you the intuition behind DSA to the point where it can sometimes feel like we're inventing it ourselves. He doesn't just tell you how things work, he makes you understand WHY they work that way and why it makes sense for them to be that way. HWs are fine, exams are fair

Dr. Faulkner is nothing short of a genius. He teaches things by introducing the problem first, piquing your interest before showing you how the solution was devised. The class will give some difficulty, but even if you don't pay attention, he gives you every resource you need to succeed x100. You can't go wrong in this class—shoutouts to CSVistool!

Faulkner is truly one of the best professors at Tech. He somehow finds a way to dissect a hard topic to make it understandable to the class. He can answer questions outside of class content and goes deep in a structured way into each topic. Gives lots of opportunities for the class to ask questions. Would definitely recommend taking him for CS1332!

Faulkner was great and an entertaining lecturer, but I ended up watching the online videos instead and using his online notes as a supplement. CSVistool is very useful.

Faulkner is an amazing lecturer. He brings clearly planned out notes and navigates through the topics of the course effectively. He teaches everything you need and sometimes even more! There are so many resources for this course, so there are plenty of ways to be successful. I would love to take another course with Faulkner.
Great professor. His lectures were engaging and really made me learn.

Prof. Faulkner is a great professor for CS1332. His lectures are sometimes a little fast and dry, but he gets the information across in an understandable manner. Exams are also fair, and homework is not that bad (just copy the CSVistool pseudocode if you're lost).
lectures are so easy to understand, exams are super straightforward, if you study you will get an A.

The combo of Faulkner's lectures and HB's videos is great. I appreciate his understanding of the material and his ability to clearly explain the topics of the course. csvistool is an excellent resource. The beard has major aura.

Lectures weren't too helpful but attendance was not mandatory. Video lectures on Canvas from HB were amazing. A lot of resources to succeed. CS vistool is extremely helpful in learning concepts. good prof, but i stopped showing up to lecture after maybe a month lol. i took 1332 hybrid and the class itself is def not a joke - it's been my worst cs class so far.

Faulkner does talk very fast, but he makes almost all 1332 concepts digestible. Honestly I feel like most of these reviews are written by his TAs. He's a good lecturer and understands the material. But his handwriting is SO BAD. Entirely illegible if you want to review his notes. The exams also feel really shoddy and like they want to make hard questions just because they can
Best prof at tech, 100% recommend for 1332, lectures were great

The Best Professor at Georgia Tech. He is hilarious but this doesn't take away from the course content. He answeres the questions perfectly providing just enough information. His teaching style is immaculate, with the perfect mixture of allowing students to think themselves and guiding them to the solution. 
Professor Faulkner is the GOAT

Absolute GOAT, this class is beyond easy so I didn't learn much from lectures, but his notes are amazing and he clearly knows the topics. If this was my first introduction to data structures, I don't think I could've asked for a better professor. Homework doesn't take longer than 30 mins and tests are all super easy.

Faulkner is the GOAT. He answers questions well in class (even those that go beyond the scope of the class), and has very good lectures with time for in-class practice. I went to his class more than any other class and attendance wasn't even required
This man is the goat. Easy to understand class and funny at times. Will take his class again in the future.

reviews.comment: Faulkner is great at using OneNote to draw pictures as he is explaining things that easily breaks down dense topics and makes them digestible. He is funny, tests are fair, and I highly recommend him for the fully in person lecture setup instead of the hybrid

The class was fairly straightforward. Faulkner is a good lecturer, and everything covered in class showed up on homeworks and exams. The Canvas was combined with virtual sections, so finding online resources was easy.

He is probably the best CS professor out there. I highly recommend taking him for 1332. He made the class look pretty easy. Great lecturer. Tests are fair and so is homework but homework can be very long and you kind of have to hope that other students write very in-depth test cases (or write your own obviously)

Not bad

Honestly is probably one of the best professors I have taken at tech. He always explained everything thoroughly and demonstrated how everything works. He also did a good job covering edge cases and explaining the time complexities of every operation/algorithm. Exams were fair as long as you do the homeworks and understand how each algorithm works.

Faulkner is by far the preferred choice for 1332. He shines best during his lectures as he explains every aspect of the course excellently, despite problems with legible handwriting. If you're gonna take 1332 I'd recommend you do it with Faulkner, he's newer than the other professor, but based on her online lectures I'd go with Faulkner.
Favorite CS professor thus far. This dude is so chill and nice. Literally have no complaints.

He is literally the best teacher I've encountered in the CS department so far. I didn't need a lot of extra resources to succeed in this course as his lectures very extremely helpful in making this class easy for me. He presents information in a clear and concise manner and covers most of the edge cases you require to understand.
He is a good professor, even though he can be boring at times. Better than all other 1332 professors. Exams are worth so much that if you mess up on one your grade is done for.

He was the best professor ever! He helped me understand the course material better, and as a result, I ended up getting an A in his class. I really like his teaching style, it was very inspirational. Additionally, this class has a very cool final exemption policy where you can have your final exam exempted if you achieve a test average above 94.

Not a good professor but better than HB. Talks very fast and does not make sure students understand. Course is not structured well and puts a lot of emphasis on memorization over understanding. Grading scheme is awful. Also, Faulkner does not answer emails, so don't expect to be able to get in touch with him outside of class.

Faulkner truly has a gift for lecturing. 

He's able to teach at a quick pace without glossing over important details. He's great at explaining the "Why?" part of material and is great at condensing information as well. He explains his reasoning very thoroughly in his notes, so you can learn the content well even if you didn't go to class.

I loved Faulkner's lectures! He explains concepts so clearly. If you pay attention to lecture, exams are extremely straightforward. He goes over plenty of examples and diagramming. Really can't recommend taking him enough!! My favorite professor at Tech so far.
One of the best CS professors I have ever had; explains every concept in a clear, understandable manner; gives the class a lot of materials to prepare for exams
I love this man. I've taken him for 2050, 1332, and will this summer for 3510, and I thank all the gods there may be that I'm going to be able to take him for that class.

Faulkner is a truly caring professor.  He always answers questions and ensures the content is accessible online for everyone and understandable.  He doesn't care about staying perfectly on track, he just wants you to learn.  The bad thing with that is he has to rush at the end of the semester, but otherwise he is the perfect professor.

reviews.comment: Faulkner is amazing. He speaks very clearly and down-to-earth. The course itself is structured very well and Faulkner does a great job teaching the content. Would definitely recommend for any class he teaches!
Amazing professor! His lectures made the concepts easy to understand and were very engaging. Not a super difficult class if you stay caught up with material and take advantage of resources.
handwriting hard to identify, lectures at a fast pace, 15 weeks have 16 modules need to learn.

Truly a terrific professor. Extremely knowledgeable and caring. His lectures worth always worth attending, even if his handwriting was at times a bit illegible. This class is crucial for CS, and he does a great job making sure that you master concepts.

Pretty good and approachable lecturer who explains concepts very well, though he goes a little too fast that sometimes doesn't allow you to digest the content.
