Data structures and algos wasn't my thing, so I barely squeaked by with a B. But make sure to attend lectures! Faulkner is a really good lecturer (maybe not handwriting tho), and will prepare you well to complete the homeworks.

Faulkner is an amazing lecturer. Overall great professor although his handwriting was hard to read. You can learn from HB's module videos but his lectures are way more concise and understandable. Professor Faulkner does provide a very solid quality lecture but at times it can be difficult to follow along because of his hand writing and talking pace. CS1332 itself is heavily based on exams and looking back in hindsight, all the exams were super fair but do put in the time to study everything and really learn all the coding homework.

Withstanding his handwriting, his socrative polls, examples, and pseudocode lectures in class are absolutely top-notch. AMAZING PROFESSOR!

One of the best lecturers on campus; he was so adept at explaining course material that it was worth going specifically to his lectures rather than the internet in order to learn course material. Only caveat to this course is their reliance on specific implementations of algorithms, meaning that if you learn off the internet, you may lose points.

Great lecturer that is passionate about what he is teaching. He goes through many examples in his lectures that are very useful for the exams. He is thorough in answering questions and if you attend all his lectures, you will be well prepared for this class's exams.

Minor cons are that he speaks pretty fast and has pretty bad handwriting.

Faulkner's lectures are very straightforward, easy to understand, and I personally thought he had the perfect pace to prevent students from getting bored. the goat. sometimes goes too fast, which makes sense given the amount of content in the course, but you can catch up using all the online resources. very well structured lectures and course, and hes a great guy overall

Knows what hes teaching and very knowledgable. Final exemption is also a big plus. Knew the material and taught it in a way where I didnt have to do any outside studying to understand it. Very good professor would def take again

Explains concepts extremely well. Very friendly. Always maintains his composure.
Explains concepts extremely well. Very friendly. Always maintains composure.

Only nit-pick is his handwriting but aside from that he's the GOAT!

reviews.comment: You're in great hands if you're taking his 1332 class! The professor's lectures are very clear and easy to understand and the homework/tests are hard but fair.

The absolute GOAT. It was his first time teaching Discrete in a while I think, but he did a fantastic job and the lectures were very helpful. Pretty funny and nice guy too. In general the class is pretty easy though and his informative lectures definitely put you in good shape for the exams. Definitely recommend if you can take him.
Truly an amazing class and an amazing professor. Absolutely 0 complaints.

Professor is incredibly good at explaining things, even with his somewhat messy handwriting. Great lecturer, you never get bored during lectures. And incredibly helpful when you have any questions. Highly recommend this prof when he teaches 2050 again - he clearly knows what he's doing.

Easy A, but he does have a preference for two-column table proofs which can get annoying.

Absolute god. He is such an amazing lecturer and person. He teaches so well and explained concepts so visually. The TA's provided us with so much material to prepare with. Definitely have to second the statement that he is the epitome of a civil servant. Absolutely loved the class (very helpful for the future btw) and loved the professor even more.
Goatner

Tests are either "you'll have 30 minutes of free time" or "you won't finish the test", no in between. Homework is relatively straightforward and reality checks are free participation.

Talks way too fast and handwriting is borderline illegible. If you want someone slower, take HB. But, Faulkner is very knowledgeable. He's good at explaining things and knows what he's talking about. Exams are fine but not enough time at all. Ridiculous. HW's are fine as well.

Professor Faulkner's lectures are always clear, straightforward, and understandable. The only unclear thing is perhaps his handwriting. That's why you'd better go to his lectures, though now 1332 has online modules that cover all content of the course. An enjoyable and amazing professor.

Highly recommend, this professor was absoluetly amazing. Although the course content can be challenging at times, he throughly explained all of the different data structures and algorithms so that we were prepared for the exams. There's also plently of online resources to help as well, along with practice exams and worksheets.

Probably one of the best professors I've had. Very calm, lectures are great, and he's so good at explaining things. You're always engaged during lecture. Amazing dude with lectures that are very important, make sure you do the homework well cause it prepares you really well for the tests.

HW is boring but fine.

Lectures were S tier (based off the legendary Prof. Kantwon) with a great balance of conceptual practice and helpful in-line comments. He also taught us WHY CS matters, with connections to every field of engineering. The tests are fair, but study >= 2 hrs.

Faulkner was a great professor for 1332. He covered everything you needed to know for tests and homeworks in lecture and he publishes lecture notes(albeit hard to read). Most material is shared between professors, including tests, so choose Faulkner for his lectures.
Loved him for CS 1371! Really great lecturer and funny, too. Definitely would recommend.
All the materials of CS1332 were online and attendance wasn't mandatory but I enjoy going to his lectures a lot. He's patient with questions and does his best to help you succeed.

FOR CS1371. Great professor! Easy to follow lectures, though he goes a little fast sometimes. Posts recordings and notes for each lecture. Material is fairly easy to grasp as long as you pay attention and do the homework. HW has extra credit!
Professor Faulkner has amazing lectures and makes the subject very interesting. He paces the class very well and seems to be one of the most inspiring and funny professors I've had.
Professor Faulkner is an excellent professor for DSA. Great lectures, enthusiastic and a good overall experience.
This man is the epitome of a civil servant.

Really great professor, funny and caring in class and has interesting and engaging lectures. I learned a ton in this class, and felt challenged at the right times, but grading was very fair and you could get a high grade if you tried.

I LOVED THIS CLASS
Faulkner is an amazing teacher. Very patient and caring about students. TAs wrote amazing notes that helped describe the class. Hopefully he teaches 4510 again so I can take it with him

Great guy, very smart and is good at teaching as well. TAs gave great notes. There was a ton of extra credit throughout the entire course, and they are extremely generous on grading all exams, with a very generous grading scheme as well. If you want to get an A in 3510, take Faulkner.

Easily one of the best profs I've taken at tech. The lecture notes one of the TAs wrote every class were really helpful in learning the concepts better and Faulkner is a great lecturer himself. He heavily emphasizes his exams on learning rather than nonsense memorization.

One of the best professors I've ever had. In the lectures after every lesson he teaches he constantly answers questions the class has and actively tries to clarify hard concepts so everyone understands. Gives a ton of extra credit opportunities too! Just study the homeworks and read the lecture notes and you'll get an A.

reviews.comment: Favorite prof in all my years of Tech. Normally in lectures, I always look at the clock to see when it's over, but his lectures are excellent. He has a nice weighting system on exams so they don't penalize your grade too hard and offers a good amount of extra credit. His handwriting is messy but he uploads detailed typed lecture notes afterward.

Prof Faulkner actually makes the material in 4510 extremely interesting. His style of teaching allows you to build intuition about stuff in step-by-step fashion. He answers students question with patience. I like how he provides practice problems during lecture as well.

He is hands down a superb professor. I think he should get a promotion/bonus!

One of the best lecturer's in my four years at Tech. Automata is a hard class but he does a great job at presenting the info in a clear way with just enough explanation to help students understand how concepts connect. He offers lots of small bonus opportunities, and he's nice about asking clarifying questions in class. Definitely take him!

Professor Faulkner was a fantastic professor who geniunely wanted his class to succeed. The dynamic programming unit was a highlight.

Professor Faulkner, despite being new, is clearly very experienced in and passionate for his field. Faulkner's 4510 was definitely a lot of work for me. I depended on weekly office hours and attended every lecture. However, that work paid off. I have taken many CS and MATH classes at GT. Faulkner is a new professor, but is easily one of the best lecturers I've had at GT. He also dropped the lowest exam/final at the end of the year.

CS 4510 with him was my favorite class this semester! Faulkner's a great lecturer, who is entertaining and clear, and who was patient when repeating himself or even when answering my dumb questions. His grading is fair, and he gives tons of extra credit making the class easy and enjoyable, while still feeling like I've learned a lot. 11/10.

Frederic Faulkner is the goat in terms of automata and complexity understanding and communication. He's been an all-around delight to learn from. As someone who typically struggles with test-taking, professor Faulkner has made this class both challenging and insightful without breaking my spirits. You will be very lucky to have him as your prof.

Overall a good professor. He takes the time to explain things well and cares about students. His policy on exams and homeworks are also very fair. Personally I found the material in CS 4510 to be abstract and non-intuitive at times, but taking 4510 with Faulkner was the way to go.

reviews.comment: Dr. Gerona's class is a lesson in life - you can do all the right things like constant studying, attending of the 5ish hours of class per week, doing all the pointless assignments that she gives to you and even the extra credit but still not succeed in her class. Take this class if you need to destroy your mental health for whatever reason.

Professor Gerona's class is a marathon, not a sprint. Get ready to commit serious time to the textbook - every detail will be on the test. If you want to know where two white guys slept in the winter of 1837, this class is for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This midterm has had to be the worst midterm I have taken. It is harder than the coding classes here at GT I kid you not. She will throw questions at you like "How many exes did George Washington have and how many secret wives did Abraham Lincoln have before 45?". Take this class if you want to be buried with Georgia Washington and his wife.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I honestly do not think this Professor is fit to work at Georgia Tech. If she wants to make history so difficult tell her to go to the white house to teach the president history, even Biden wouldn't know what questions she pulls out of her bottom. She honestly makes a bad rep. for history. This is five times as hard as AP U.S history.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Gave me trauma. Your hardwork is not rewarded in this class. Genuinely upsetting experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is so messed up. please avoid this class AT ALL COSTS!!!!  this professor makes everything so confusing. Even though I spent fair amount of time preparing the test, this woman want us to know about the tiny detail of her presentation. don't waste your time on this class

My relationship with this class was more toxic than my relationship with my ex. I put in around 16 hours of work per week, do all the assignments and readings, and I prepare relentlessly for exams. There is nothing I could have conceivably done to memorize the sheer level of detail that her tests require, if you want to even PASS. AVOID AT ALL COST
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you like reading through 905 pages of mostly unimportant textbook information from 1500-1877, completing quizzes that have little to no connection to the class and don't give an accurate representation of the material, and having to memorize how many pounds of meat and canoes two guys ate and built in 1837, this is the class for you.

Why is a history class harder than physics?? Seriously, she expects everyone to have the most minute details memorized out of several hours of weekly readings and hours of lectures. No amount of studying could prepare you for her exams. AVOID.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was harder than every one of my major related classes. Get ready to spend about 15 hours per week on this class, and then barely passing because you didn't remember what color George Washington's uncle's underwear was at the battle of peepeepoopoo.

Truly horrible class. She struggles with technology, gives heavy readings weekly with around 4-5 hours of lecture time per week. Everything you do will contain a quiz. You will have to memorize EVERY detail of the textbook if you want even a semi-decent grade. Many trick questions on the test asking information not in the textbook or class. AVOID.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you're not an AI that can remember every single details on her ppt slides and lectures, do not take her class
An incredibly time-consuming class, mainly because if you don't read the textbook you won't do well. She also doesn't know how to use Canvas properly. Also, her tests are incredibly long.

I'm taking her class online and she is having incredible difficulty using Canvas and other tools/online quizzes, even though we're 4 weeks into the semester. Half of her assignments don't serve any actual use yet students are still required to do them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Not a good professor.

Dr. Gerona's lectures are dull and the tests (50% MCQ 50% essay) are slightly difficult. However, she gives many other grades that are worth just as much as the tests to boost your grade! She is such a kind professor and genuinely wants to see her students succeed. This class is easy; attend class and do the readings and you will succeed!

Do not take this professor. She will change due dates randomly and make it hard to find the new due dates. She grades somewhat harshly on the essay portion of the test and the objective part of the test is random facts that don't relate to the course. Lecture is very boring and I learned basically nothing. Seriously, do not take this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great! had a lot of quizzes as homework (during pandemic) but those really were very simple (mostly questions from the back of the chapter). Each weak had 2 60-page readings, but skip those and just pay attention to her lectures for an A in your exams. I got mostly Cs in all my exams, but she offers a lot of extra credit and the quizzes pull you up
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Feels like a middle school arts and crafts teacher. Views her class as 1st priority and is not considerate of personal situations. Miss 1 class she thinks you missed 3 so make sure she sees you and you conversate with her or she might get you confused with another student in the class who looks like you. Wouldn't she with my GPA again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Remember everything she taught in class and every word in textbooks, or you won't pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr Gerona is a great professor and is super passionate about what she teaches, I wish all GT professors were like her. Watch out for little details in notes though bc she might put them on exams.

Attendance isn't mandatory but it probably very useful because she asks about the smallest details on tests. This class has assigned readings before each class which take about an hour to an hour and a half. She does give a lot of extra credit opportunities which is very helpful (I think you can boost your grade a whole letter with EC).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you are genuinely interested in the subject, Dr. Gerona is a great teacher to have and you will do well with not too much effort. Homework is straightforward, and she often has extra credit opportunities. She is very clear in lecture about what she thinks is important to know and also receptive to questions, but usually p busy outside class.

Dr. Gerona teaches her class in an interesting and new way that I think brings some much needed innovation into what can often be boring history courses. She can be a tough grader but gives great feedback and wants the students to succeed. I enjoyed her class and the others I have taken with her

Dr. Gerona is a good teacher. Meaning she's not amazing and she's not bad. You will do about 60 pages of reading per week. Attendance is 10% of your grade. She keeps up with attendance with a prs. You will have weekly quizzes on a smaller essay book. They are about 5 questions long and pretty easy if you read. Put in moderate effort and get A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Tests are based mostly on textbook readings and (seemingly) inconsequential information presented in class. Studying is required. Her rubric for grading essays is ill-defined and she is not apt for discussion about the grade you received.

Carla Gerona is the worst professor I've ever had. She is very scatterbrained during class her tests focus on unimportant details from 200 slide presentations. She is really quite horrible. If you try to get points back on a test, she will claim that you are the "enemy". Do NOT take her classes. I repeat, do NOT.

You have to memorize every single word in the text book. I heard she was an easy class, but I get bombed on test even if I study. No practice test questions provided. Test questions are vague, and the choices include both 'none of all' and 'all of the above,' which is really annoying.
TONS and I mean TONS of extra credit. I got all low C's on ALL of my tests and I still managed to make an A. Tests are based primary on what she present in class.

I loved her as a teacher! She is very enthusiastic about history and therefore, keeps the class interested, as well. One thing to suggest is take notes on a laptop. This way allows you type EVERYTHING she says. You can make 100 on the tests without even opening the book. As long as you go to class, and type everything she says, you'll be fine.

This professor gets lost in her lectures a lot of the time and sometimes gets behind. While she does get through the material before the tests, a lot of what is in the readings (and on the tests) is left out. Reading is NECESSARY to pass her tests. It's a requirement to go to class, but I found that I learned everything from the books, not her.

very tough teacher, doesnt require class attendance. tests are nothing like class lectures and study guide. basically, you have to read about 250 pages (of history text, which is packed full of facts) before the test (which is only 40 questions). I normally get As and this class might be my first C
Just sit in the auditorium, do the readings, and take the tests.  Not many assignments. NO FINAL.  Just 3 tests and a few assignments that compile into a portfolio.  Needs an RPS clicker.

Fairly easy class - either go to lecture or read the book.  Going to lecture gets you 5 extra points to your grade.  She is generally interested in the subject and listens to the concerns of students often.  Genuinely nice professor that is somewhat scatter-brained, but she knows what she is talking about.
Nice GPA padding, just show up to class and look over the review sheets. Easy A

Very easy class. In fact I've only gone to her lecture like twice the entire semester. It's beneficial to go to lecture to earn 10 extra points through the journal projects though. I never went to class, and studied the night prior on the chapters in the book and averaged an 85 on exams. She provides a study guide for every exam.

Good teacher. The class is easy. Just listening in class should get you a B. You'll have to read the book and do some studying for the A. Just 4 tests, multiple choice, no papers or assignments. Going to class can get you 10 extra credit points. I liked the class, there was a good balance between overview of the material and some in depth specifics

She is an easy teacher who gives you all the information you need to know in class, doesn't require you to go to class, but you can get up to 10 points on your final grade just for doing so.  I hardly study for tests and get good grades just by paying attention in class.

Dr. Wu is really nice but the assignments are so time consuming, the quizzes and tests aren't that hard but there is a lot of content to learn, the homework is really long and there are so many other time consuming assignments, I wouldn't take it again because the assignments are so time consuming

Dr. Wu is very kind and accessible, but the grading in this class is extremely pedantic. I understood the lectures, but I would always be surprised by my grades on exams and quizzes. Luckily, the course is structured so that you should still be able to get an A (projects, etc.) even with the insane grading on tests. Class is A LOT of work.

Professor Wu is easily approachable and accessible. Plus, her lectures are super entertaining (but thankfully she doesn't seem to care much if you do other stuff on your computer as long as you're in class). Overall she's a great professor! Her main downsides are that she gives lots of hours' worth of homework and exam grading is VERY meticulous.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Wu was very caring and wanted everyone to succeed. This class was not very difficult, but it was a lot of work. There were frequent quizzes, homeworks, and readings as well as mandatory attendance. Not Professor Wu's fault, but I still struggled to be interested in the material despite her enthusiasm.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: a lot of people sign up for linguistics expecting to do literally no work because it's a humanities course. professor wu is so sweet and clearly so passionate about the field and our learning, and she always tries her hardest to find a way for us to get enthusiastic about the content. hws can be time intensive, but really nothing bad for gt.

Do not take this class in person, especially if you are looking for an easy A. Professor assigns homework that takes hours a week and is a very significant part of your grade. Homework  and a project was even assigned during spring break with a test being the first day back from break. Lectures are very vague and not well put together.

Great class taught by a great professor.  Very reasonable grading and a fair amount of work.  Don't expect to do nothing in this class and get an A, but also don't expect to put a lot of effort in either.  Lectures are interesting, homeworks add to the lectures, and tests cover material from both.  Two projects that are pretty fun

So easy but very engaging prof. Most of the class is a group project that you work on throughout the semester, but can be annoying to do if you have a bad group. Often lets lectures out early when she finishes early so she doesn't waste your time at all. No exams is awesome. She is just so sweet, well-spoken, and passionate about what she does!!!

Such a good class! The class is almost entirely structured around a group project (no exams!) and lectures are fairly interesting. She is a fantastic professor that values discussion and participation instead of talking at you the entire class. Take her if you can!!!

Dr. Park is the most invested and caring professor I've had at Tech so far! Her lectures were succinct and effective and fairly engaging. She was super accessible to bounce ideas and discuss applications of course content. The final project was chill, and you'll learn a lot if you treat it like a consulting project. 100% take Dr. Park!

literally the best prof at tech, she's so sweet and understanding. no exams, extra credit, lenient with deadlines, and lets us out of class early. don't waste your money on the textbook, you won't need it since all quizzes are online and open note/open internet.

Very sweet, caring, understanding, and passionate about OB. Weekly quizzes based on textbook and other small assignments + large final project due at the end with random group assignments. Have to speak up 3x during the semester, lectures were a bit boring, but always lets us out of class 15-30 minutes early. Overall very easy class

nice teacher overall, she was obviously passionate about ob, but the lectures were boring.  no exams, only a big project due at the end. the only assignments are little reading checks that is open notes and internet, and then like 3 writing assignments that take 30 minutes. attendance was mandatory, but she never keeps us for the whole class time

she's a great prof and very passionate about ob. class is chill and always ends early/or we don't have class to work on the semester long group project. project isnt bad if you have good teammates. there's extra credit too. only downside is mandatory attendance and you need to speak up 3x in the semester

Probably the easiest class you will take at Scheller, there is mandatory attendance but otherwise I don't know how anyone could get anything but an A. She cares a lot about the topics but you will never be tested on anything taught so there's really no work that needs to be done in or out of class.

I love her! She is sooo sweet and wholesome. Her class was so interesting and she is so accommodating to your life and any concerns. She values feedback heavily and ACTUALLY acts upon them to create a better learning environment for her students.I had a lot of fun in her class and I wish her nothing but the best!
The class is extremely easy, she's a bit picky with the final project but attending all lectures is enough to get an easy A.

This queen! Love her. she has great informative lectures in a very low pressure environment. She is a very sweet lady who really just wants everyone to learn and enjoy OB as much as she does. I definitely recommend. If she's not teaching MGT3101 for your current semester, wait until she does and I'm so serious

Dr. Park's class is extremely easy but informative. Grade based on participation, quizzes, and a group project. No exams which is awesome. She is very caring and tries to accommodate students needs and make time to meet with people. Very accessible for the project. Definitely recommend taking her class!

Don't listen to past reviews, he increased the weighting and difficulty of the quizzes, so the extra credit on projects barely helps. Quizzes are insanely hard and graded very stingy. Lectures are just monotone talking for and hour and 15 mins, projects are a free 100 pretty much but it doesn't even matter when the quizzes are that brutal.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Boring, monotone voice that makes lectures not engaging. Quizzes are hard and no practice is given for concepts on the quiz, project doesn't fully help

I thought James was a pretty great lecturer, and he explains a good amount of detail outside of what's written on the slides, so attending lectures is helpful for quizzes. Almost all projects had extra credit so it's easy to get an A. However, I would recommend not AI-ing everything so that you can actually learn the content.

Professor Hays gave great lectures that were really interesting if you pay attention. He is also very knowledgeable on the topic and made sure to connect the material to recent advancements. Quizzes aren't hard if you attend or watch lectures, and the projects aren't bad if you give yourself enough time to work on them.

lectures are not great, prof is unable to answer some questions students ask, really mumbly/hand-wavy, unclear what topics we need to know for the class, but they are recorded. final grade is based on 6 projects/labs and three quizzes with lots of opportunity for extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hays himself is a good lecturer, but sometimes the projects were difficult to understand and wrap your head around. If you pay attention to lecture, you'll be fine for the midterm and exams, but you're basically on your own for the projects, especially in the second half of the class, and those can be really difficult if you don't have help.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures are fairly engaging and he goes over the material well enough. If you don't pay attention you WILL fail the quizzes. Projects feel really poorly written but easy enough to figure out and it's not hard to get an A.

Professor keeps going on random 10 minute tangents before saying "oH bTw thIS iSnT On tHE ProJECT" 
TAs randomly go radio silent for several days at a time
HW assignments feel like they were written by completely different people so they're often more confusing than necessary (Having keywords never mentioned in class, unrelated functions, etc)

He's a decent lecturer but can be a bit rude on Piazza - he is not sympathetic to grading issues. Lots of projects, so start early. No exams, but problem sets can be tricky. Allows for 6 late days to turn in projects. Added extra work for grad students even though 90% of the class is grad students which doesn't make sense. Not a bad choice for CV.

The homework/projects can be a bit of a challenge but it gets much easier later in the semester. Form study groups early and beg the TAs for help. Hays is one of the most engaging lecturers Ive ever had, very good understanding of the material. They were pretty lenient with moving deadlines too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great lectures, he clearly knows the subject well and has a lot of interesting insights into computer vision. Not too hard, and if you're interested in vision, its the class to take!

Super helpful on Piazza, and you can tell from his lecturing that he's passionate about the subject. The projects are reasonable and you have a couple weeks for each. The tests are hard if you don't go to class, but really easy if you do.

Very fair professor, course consisted of a mix of group and individual quizzes, and lots of in-class practice to help you succeed. Did do some studying outside of class and labs were long but never a class I would stress out about. Easy lab science and Zachary makes it a wonderful experience. TAs were great too.

He is very passionate about what he teaches and the lecture material is easy. No midterms, only individual and group quizzes, and optional final exam. Lab is worth like 25% of your grade (and is very easy) so you're practically guaranteed an A if you study the TA lecture notes.

Dr. Handlos is extremely passionate about the material, and he has a way of making you care about it too, even on boring topics I never thought I would care about. He also really cares about the students and is very accessible and willing to answer questions. One time when the class did really poorly on one of the quizzes he even let us revise it.
EAS 1600 was a very fun and easy class, like I was genuinely excited to go to it. Dr. Handlos seemed super passionate about the material and he was helpful during office hours.

Very nice and genuine professor. Lectures are okay but survivable, attendance is "mandatory" but only requires a code to be typed on canvas. Quizzes are very straightforward and sufficient study materials are provided. Overall a great class and a good way to fill the science requirement.
Great intro to weather and a fun class. Handlos is into "ungrading" and uses it for most his smaller sized classes, so this is an easy A if you put in the appropriate effort.

Dr. Handlos is an outstanding professor. Even having no prior experience to weather studies, I found his weather physics course extremely accessible due to his engaging lectures and fun personality. PHYS 2750 was "ungraded" this semester, so it is clear that he values his students' success above all else.

Pretty good class overall. Half of your quizzes will be group quizzes, and it will feel like just about every week there's a quiz. Quizzes are mostly conceptual, so the study guides don't really help, as long as you listen to and review the lectures, you'll be fine. Minimal homework too !

I took EAS 2750. Absolutely one of my favorite profs. Actually cares about students. Amazing lectures, really interesting. Class was ungrading. Great projects. Really nice. Great communication. Great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easy class, 4 group quizzes + 4 individual quizzes, optional final! Attendance is mandatory and there are often in class activities, but most people just do work for other classes in lecture. Labs are really annoying and long (takes at least 2 hrs every time), but easy. He's a very kind professor and obviously very passionate, def recommend!

Prof. Handlos is a great lecturer! He is very passionate about the material and very easy to approach. He makes attendance mandatory, which is totally fine, since we sometimes have in-class activities which are free 100s. We also have either individual quizzes or group quizzes, which are all short and easy if you study the material a bit. No HW :)

Professor Handlos is easily one of the best professors I have had since coming to GT. He is very good at keeping students engaged in lecture and is very passionate about what he teaches. As long as you keep up with the lectures and labs you will have no problem getting an A.

Handlos is very kind and passionate when it comes to his teaching. He has an infectious energy that makes you want to learn more. This is a great EAS Lab science to take. No tests, only 6 small quizzes that counted the same. A lot of formulas but he gave us most of them.

Great professor but made things harder than it needed to be. Some quizzes were quite difficult, and that's especially frustrating for one who just wants to satisfy graduation requirements. Other than that, he is extremely knowledgeable and super passionate about EAS.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Handlos is such an awesome teacher. He is very considerate and caring for his students. Always with a great attitude and willing to help whenever you ask for. Thanks Dr. Handlos!

Super great! Grade is just 6 quizzes at 6 percent each, non cumulative. Final is optional and if you do take it your two lowest quiz scores get replaced. Quiz content is straight from lecture. Your grade is combined with lab, mandatory attendance, and participation. It's a light work course but you do need to study for the quizzes. Prof is amazing!
Relaxed atmosphere and organized course structure, but not an easy class. The course material can be quite challenge and time demanding. You need to work for it to earn an A.

Dr. Handlos is a saint. He is definitely very knowledgable over what he teaches so sometimes there seems to be a gap, but if you meet with him outside of lecture he is able to break it down to the basics if needed. He's one of the most considerate professors I've had at GT.
The class is pretty relaxed, and the professor is very enthusiastic about environmental science. The lectures were often interesting even with two-hour lectures.

Zak is INCREDIBLY knowledgeable and a wonderful resource. This was not an easy class by any means and got into the meat of remote sensing. He explains everything to an understandable level, always. The quizzes were fairly hard, and the final project is a lot especially if you aren't in the major. You do walk away with the knowledge you need!

Professor Handlos obviously cared about his students and actively tried to make class interesting even though it was online. His lectures are helpful and informative and as long as you study and understand the lecture slides you should be able to earn an A.

Zak is a really nice guy, and you can tell from day 1 that he cares about his students. Quizzes could be really difficult and try to trick you. Class averages were usually in the C range, and despite receiving negative feedback about quizzes he didn't change much. I made an A because lab is easy points and worth 30% of your grade.

Prof. Handlos is very enthusiastic about teaching the course. He takes the time to answer every question and is very understanding. I took light notes and mostly followed the lectures during class time. He posts all lecture slides and recordings. I go back to review for quizzes and homework. Quizzes can be tricky, but very manageable!

Super straightforward class: go to lecture, follow along on the slides that you can download. 10 question canvas quiz every other week which is super easy. Short homeworks and discussion posts every once in a while. Lab is super easy if you go to your assigned time slot, an hour of effort, the TA basically gives you the answers. Would take again.

Since switching to online, has made class much more difficult. 3 hour time slot labs take 4-5 hours each week, and on top of that you have a major quiz or 2-3 page homework every week. This is also coupled with graded practice quizzes and prelabs. Together you are spending MUCH more than 4 credit hours worth of time on this class each week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Zak is a great guy with great energy. For this reason, it's almost impossible to dislike him. Nonetheless, the lectures for this course weren't necessarily interesting. I went to lectures for the participation quizzes and just reviewed the slides later on my own. Grading was really fair. An A is pretty much secured as long as you try!

Prof Handlos is a pretty caring and relaxed professor. Sometimes lectures can be a bit boring, but it's all pretty much in whether you care about the subject. You need to go to class because there are participation quizzes. Tests can be a little tough, but labs and discussion posts are pretty easy.
Very relaxed professor and extremely passionate about weather. He is really smart, but breaks complex concepts down so they're easy to understand. Extremely accessible outside of class.

Dr. Handlos is one of the best professors I have had so far. He explains the material well, and always answers students questions about the subject. Very good professor and I would take him again for other classes if I needed to.

Dr. Handlos is a very nice man. You can tell he really cares about his students and is passionate about the material. The material for 1601 is easy enough, though his class (which was entirely lecture based) was pretty boring and I felt like I was wasting time at points. I would take him again though.

Professor Handlos is such a great professor! Although the lecture slides are posted online, he does a good job of expanding on them in class and giving cool examples for them as well. He really cares about his students! The tests are pretty easy, and it's good to go to class to get Learning Catalytics points.

Nice guy who was helpful the 1-2 times I went to his office hours, but lectures were difficult to understand and he wouldn't always make it all the way through them. But, you can just watch the online lectures or find another professor to go to so professor doesn't really matter in here. Whole class takes the same exams so really doesn't matter
Very hard to understand with accent.

Great guy, truly cares about his students and knows topics well. However he uses lots of jargon which makes learning hard and he has a very monotone voice. He also has a slight accent but after a week or two is no problem.
He overcomplicates simple topics and the accent makes it hard to understand sometimes. Just watch the online video lectures that are available to everyone and you'll be fine.
Nice guy and willing to explain if you have questions, but lectures are dry and boring, making it hard to pay attention.

at first his accent can be sort of confusing to understand, but you get used to it pretty quick. his lectures are a bit dry and monotone, but the concepts and material are explained well. however, sometimes he uses confusing notation. he answered students questions very well, and the tests are easy to prepare for with the library of past tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
I have never before encountered, much less been taught by, a professor who is so exceedingly skillful at convoluting the most basic concepts.
Professor He uses lots of jargon. After a while, I stopped going to lectures and had to watch the head pfr.'s online videos. It is not his accent that makes him mediocre.
His accent is very hard to understand and he uses very lofty math terms instead of explaining the concepts in a relatable way.

His lectures were a bit monotone and hard to follow, but the lecture notes were perfect for his tests and quizzes. Handwriting can be a bit confusing but you can get used to it pretty quick. The tests were not hard and are easy to prepare for using the notes.

I had him for both 1553 and 2552, and I can tell he improved a lot after his first semester. Lectures were good, tests were reasonable, and overall nice guy. I didn't perform very well on the midterms (not b/c they were hard) but I got an A on the final and was at an 89, but he rounded my final grade to an A b/c he could tell how hard I worked.
This might have been a math class, but its clear the prof never went to his teaching classes. Lectures were a mix of accent-heavy mumbled jargon, with scribbled notes to match. Avoid at all costs.

His lectures were great. He explained everything thoroughly and doesn't have the accent people claim he does. As long as you pay attention, its a good class. The quizzes made sense and followed the lecture notes.

He does not have a heavy accent like the other ratings suggest, I promise. He is a pretty normal lecturer, not the best, not bad. His tests for Differential Equations are very reasonable. The quizzes are reasonable too. Solid class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor He is nice and knowledgeable, but doesn't present very well. His handwriting is pretty difficult to understand, but you eventually can read it. It can be a struggle with his boring, monotone lectures (especially 8am), but if you do notes after class its pretty easy with his uploaded notes. He also writes easy tests comparatively.

I signed up specifically for Dan Margalit, who was replaced by Prof. He the first day of class. Extremely frustrating. His accent wasn't hard to understand, but his handwriting was awful and he went way too fast for us. Lecture was spent frantically writing instead of learning...less than 10 people were coming to class by the end. Do not recommend.

He's a new professor. Accent heavy, mumbles, bad handwriting, doesn't understand student questions... He was late to our final exam as well... I wouldn't take him unless he's a desperate last resort. I wish I watched the head professor's videos to actually get a better grade...

You can definitely tell he's a new professor... His accent and handwriting makes it really hard to follow along in class (I stopped showing up and watched Jankowski's videos). Instead of learning, it feels like you're just trying to follow his train of thought.

Very clearly a new professor. Accent and bad handwriting made his lectures hard to follow, often wasn't able to cover all the material required in the class period. Most stopped going and watched Jankowski's videos or took notes off posted powerpoint slides (that he does not use). Showed up late to his own final. Hoping he adjusts for the future.

He's not the best teacher, and he doesn't explain things that well. However, attendance is not mandatory, and everyone in the class just ended up watching Jankowski's lecture videos. He does have good style though.

Terrible prof. His lectures were useless. He had a thick accent, terrible handwriting, and was very monotone so the entire lecture you would just be struggling to follow what he was trying to say as opposed to actually learning the course.Just watch Jankowski's recorded lectures and you will be fine.

Prof. Haiying cares very much about her students. She is VERY accommodating. 
Her course was one of my heaviest-- and it was only 2 credits! You WILL LEARN in her class whether you want to or not. 
The homework was tedious, but you had 5 attempts. And the pop quizzes are basically for participation. Exams are tricky only because of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Nice person, but bad lecturer. She has you try to do problems in class after minimal lecturing and doesn't explain how she does them. Homework is extremely difficult and time consuming, but if you are able to figure out and understand homework you will do well on a large portion of the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a fantastic person, but not a good teacher. She explains poorly straight from textbook, and then has you immediately do practice problems instead of her doing practice problems. Attendance is random based on participation "pop quizzes." Homeworks are lengthy and difficult. Her tests are easy homework problems. She grades tests quite easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Avoid this Professor at all cost. Although she is caring, she is not the best professor for someone who does not know Statics already. She just restates information from the textbook and does not actually teach the concepts in class. However, I can say her exams are just problems from the textbook and she is more lenient during grading.

No attendance, but random quizzes in class. She can't teach and homework is on chegg. YOU WILL NOT LEARN IN CLASS. The light grading I've read on RMP is hit or miss. She would grade bad for me, but super well for my friends so beware. Doesn't explain anything, just follows slides, ridiculous for a class that requires a lot of written work shown.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: terrible lectures, super hard homework but graded tests SUPER nicely. homework are available on Chegg and thats what everyone did to finish them. But even just setting up problems on tests and attempting to solve would get you 80% of the points. If you're looking for an easy A and not learn anything, she's great.

As usual at Tech, a nice person but a bad professor. You WILL use chegg to solve the homework problems because what she 'covers' in class is never adequate. What examples she does 'cover' in class is LITERALLY already in the book. Test multiple choice is hit or miss, written portions are intro problems or homework. Avoid her, if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Generally, I don't care what professors I get, but I would recommend against her. She is a very nice person, yes.  However, she did not teach this course well. The homework was heavy and unforgiving, the exams didn't reflect well on what was expected of us, and we were expected to know, and tested on material that other sections were not.

reviews.comment: She was a very nice professor, but her entire teaching style was bad. She would use Mathematica instead of actually solving problems. Exam results had no feedback, didn't know how to solve her own problems during office hours, and gave lots of time cosuming homeworks that never really helped
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It might be a struggle if you aren't familiar with physics before taking this class. Her lectures were quite slow, and most of the time she was just reworking examples from the textbook rather than teaching the material itself. She was also very hard to reach outside of class and not that accommodating to students with ODS testing accommodations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: All the people I met say statics is easy. Not with her. Her CIOS fall 23 is gonna be bad, and I hope she knows why.

Dr. Huang is caring and nice, but not the best professor for Statics. The class is slow, resulting in lectures that don't prepare you for the homework (WileyPlus). You'll have to self-learn if you want to do well in this class. Exams are not representative of what you're expected to have learned. She's generous with partial credit, but still.

Not an awful professor, but if you want to do well, you'll need to be proactive in learning and studying outside of her lectures and the assigned homework. Get started on the problem sets early; if you can do them correctly without assistance using hand calculations, you'll do fine on the tests.

For a core engineering requirement, she sure does not know what she's doing. Homework does not reflect example problems from lecture, midterms are a completely different subset of questions, does not give practice exams/problems or even communicates remotely clearly what a test comprises of. For your sake, don't take her for statics.

She skipped through practice problems without teaching any concepts. Didn't explain anything in class. Used Mathematica to solve problems instead of by hand making it confusing to follow. No structure in the course and test grading criteria was unclear. Grade is based on lots of time-consuming and difficult homework with 2 tests and a final.

Dr. Huang really isn't who you should take for one of your first important engineering classes. She doesn't clearly specify what it takes to succeed in the course and is not understanding nor accommodating. She doesn't teach how to solve, she teaches to use Mathematica, which is not helpful. I really really advise you to take another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is based off 3 tests (including final), you only receive 3 attempts at each homework problem, and the she goes over very few difficult examples in class leaving you confused on the homework. The professor also uses Mathematica a lot and does not go through how to complete the problem. Save yourself the frustration and take someone else.

disregarded ODS requirements, was IMPOSSIBLE to reach outside of class (said we should not expect her to respond to emails because she is busy), could not be worse at lecturing if she tried. Uses mathematica to teach no one understood her code so in class problems were useless. can do well if you teach yourself but this woman is awful at her job.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor is really nice, but doesn't go over a lot of material. She crammed the last 3 chapters (of 6) into the last 2 weeks and it was all there was on the final exam. Homeworks and exams come directly from WileyPlus. Most people used Chegg. If you do not have a good base on this topic don't expect to learn from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Huang is an extremely kind person but her class was equally as difficult. I personally spent 23 hours on the Bonus Homework assignment. Exams are made to make you feel like you failed so be prepared for that. She is opposed to practice exams. You WILL get more partial credit than you think which is a blessing but exams send a major hit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: While a nice lady outside of the classroom, she is not fit for teaching this course. She only uses Mathematica to teach how to do problems and won't teach how to do problems by hand. Lectures focus on examples, not concepts. Uses Wiley for EVERYTHING. Grading criteria are unclear as far as partial credit goes. Takes almost a month to grade exams.

Great professor, teaches very well. Homeworks are tough, but they also account for a big portion of the grade, so be prepared to work on it. Tests are easy if you understand what's being covered in class and do the homoework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very approachable outside the class and if you can't make her office hours she is flexible to meet at other times. Will guide students when they ask for help and is patient. Don't wait to ask for help, the class starts out easy but the coursework (HW worth 20%) is A LOT. Keep asking your questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Huang is such a kind and caring teacher. She did multiple things over the semester that showed her kindness. We didn't really learn that much material in class, but rather worked on practice problems. There were pop extra credit quizzes. The homework is very difficult, but tests much more reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Flipped-course, meaning she teaches nothing/you watch the pre-recorded lectures and read the lecture slides on your own to answer weekly problem sets, but she can check your answers if you ask. Partner work, but could mean you do everything. 5 full lab reports and 1 data analysis w/ presenting 1 lab report at the end. No exams. Easy A if you work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She was so so caring and very willing to help you outside of class if you're having trouble. The hw takes a lot of time though and is usually a lot more difficult than test questions, but the lecture examples were helpful and she gives pop quizzes sometimes so definitely go to class!!

caring, personal, and understanding. the class is pretty straightforward in nature. try not to skip class as she gives out extra credit. pacing was weird as we spent 3/4 of the semester covering 1/3 of the material and then crammed the last bit in the last month and change. HW takes a lot of time but if you understand how to do it youll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Knowledgeable professor. Nice and patient.

Make sure to attend all of her lectures because she checks attendance for a grade. HW is longer + harder than any questions you'll see on her tests. If you study example problems from lecture and do okay on the HW, her tests shouldn't be a problem. Make sure to read the intro slides because she likes having multiple choice q's based on theory
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Her lectures are essentially just her solving problems without much explanation of the theory behind her problem solving or really any non-numerical physics. (The class is exclusively solving problems numerically.)
She's a fairly good grader, but you only have two Midterms and an Exam. The homework is difficult and takes a long time to complete, so start early. She's pretty straightforward in her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor. Grades well, teaches the concepts thoroughly. Very open to questions and has a very helpful attitude when it comes to students who are confused with the subject. She likes using matlab/mathematica in class for calculations so if you like CS her section is probably one of the better ones for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Her order of presenting information is pretty messed up. Be ready to spend 1/3 of the time listening to words that are not elaborated, 1/3 afterwards to actually start learning things, and the last 1/3 to link the two parts and try to make sense of them.

Professor Mary's CS1332 online course is amazing. Clear lecture videos with lots of examples and amazing accessibility through office hours. Exams were a bit difficult (particularly the coding), but hey, it's CS1332. Besides that, I would highly recommend.

Lectures aren't very helpful. Her videos are pretty good and the TAs are very helpful. Basically very TA led. Faulkner taught our class once and he was pretty good, take him instead. Exams aren't too bad and similar to past exams but grades were very test heavy.

The online class. Would recommend if you are comfortable with online pacing. The recorded content is pretty close to what is on the exam and isn't significantly out of date. Just make sure to keep up with the recorded content prior to the exams. Loved the sections on additional topics in theory that wasn't present in the online CS1331 class.

Class is taught completely virtual. Didn't meet the professor until the day of the final exam. Lecture videos are helpful, but reality checks seem out of date with exam difficulty/questions. Demos were a new thing added to the class, which I think was unnecessary due to the fact that we have no projects in this course and the class is online.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a lecturer, she doesn't get through all of the content, makes mistakes, and frequently misses class. However her videos are very good quality and there are tons of resources online, so putting in the effort to making sure you stay caught up with the curriculum is a must and will get you a good grade. Dont go to class and just watch the videos
Super easy class; pretty easy lectures. Wish she engaged a lot more with the class. Also, the lectures were really slow. Take Faulkner

Important class. Very good lecturer for the portion of the class she teaches. Attend class. Very good and accessible TA's, take advantage of them. You need to stay on top of homework and understanding to do well. Grading is harsh on tests, and the material on them seems more complicated and abstract than you would expect from a core understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. HB had amazing lecture videos and was a great person. CS 1332 was a bit more difficult than CS 1331 but there were plenty of resources to help one succeed on everything. Tons of extra credit administered throughout the year as well (about 7 bonus points towards exams + CIOS bonus).
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Probably the most caring professor I've ever had. She wants her students to not only succeed in this class but in your life and career. Her course is tough, but she explains topics well and although I never went to her Office Hours, she seems like the type of professor that would do whatever it took to help you out.
O K HI BYE O K

honestly this class was pretty difficult, only because there are very few things this class is graded by. not to mention you have to have a passing exam average to pass the class. i get it, there are probably reasons why but as someone who had a hard time understanding things, it did not make it any easier that i didn't have any saving graces.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took the online section of this class and Dr. HB has amazing lecture videos that are incredibly helpful and well done! the exams are pretty difficult, but fair enough if you know the content. She's also really understanding, I had to take an emergency absence and she waived any late points I had on the HWs. I would definitely recommend!
She literally has no idea what she is talking about. This course is run by incompetent people and makes GT look like a laughing stock

HB is a decent lecturer; the course is just a bit tough for someone with little prior knowledge on the topics. I know people who claim to have bad experiences with her based on her character, but I have had no issues with her.

She made these ridiculously high-quality lecture videos that are clear, concise, and easy to follow along. Discovering them made studying for exams so much easier. Do not take this class for granted, please just do the homeworks on time and study for the exams and you'll get an A.

Dr. HB's CS1332 class is one of my all-time favorites at GT, due in large part to how diverse the amount of learning materials there are. You can watch the module videos if you're more visual, use the vistool if you're more hands-on, or read from the slides if you prefer text-answers. The tests can be tricky, but are quite fair. Best CS course @GT.

Very difficult to reach professor rarely responds to emails and is very last minute about updates like when the final is. Awful class with some of the worst test on knowledge I've seen just avoid at all cost.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this course 3 times before I passed. There is an annoying test grade policy that makes it to where you can pass, but are still forced to retake the class. All things aside, HB is a great professor. She is caring for her students and is very involved. 1332 is simply a challenging course for those who are not ahead in their CS education.

I learned a lot in this class, and it was low stress. The grading is very fair, and she even lets you exempt the final if you do well on the three exams. Exam content is easier than HWs and is similar to the practice exams on canvas. Lecture attendance wasn't required. Definitely recommend.

Professor Hudachek-Buswell's 1332 class is challenging but rewarding. Her video lectures are clear, and tools like Unstuck study can help supplement your learning. Exams test your grasp of concepts, so stay on top of the material.

Good lecturer, clear explanations. Do not hesitate to ask questions anytime you have a doubt - she will answer your question thoroughly. I had the hybrid section, and her prerecorded videos are a solid resource. Well-organized course as well.

Took this class during the summer. At the beginning, she seemed like she would be a scary teacher, but by the end of the semester it was clear that she was cared a lot about her students and the material she taught. Exams were based exactly on the homeworks and there were plenty of extra credit opportunities.

I took 1332 over the summer, meaning that the time constraints changed the way the course was structured. Professor Hudacheck-Buswell was a great professor that constantly worked towards accounting for the needs of the students. Lectures were only once a week, so I had to make the most of her pre-recorded videos and TA team in order to do well.
Very good lecture videos. Exams were full of gotchas but overall class does a goos job at improving your coding skills and knowledge for later classes.

Great online videos that make attending class irrelevant. Content is very digestible and reflective of the exams. My main qualm with HB is her lack of respect for students that I felt she showed very regularly. Not only to students, but also her TAs. As of right now, there really aren't any bad options for 1332, but keep the module videos in mind.

does not explain concepts well and is passive aggressive. does not care about students. class is very hard and focuses a lot on memorization. exams are difficult and grading structure of the class is awful.

Very slow talker (had to watch all videos on 2x speed...)). Exams are overly difficult and there is a huge emphasis on memorizing time complexity and straight up CODE from the homework. This course has been nothing but a huge waste of time for me; I did not learn much useful stuff. Please revise course structure. Minimum 70 exam average to pass :/
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall the class was just hard.  You need to get a good grasp on the concepts in order to get a good grade.  They post helpful videos so rewatch them if you want a good grade.  Also do the hw since the coding on the tests are based on the hws

Took the async version over summer. The videos were well produced and being able to watch them over and over again was convenient. Coding assignments felt fair, grading was kind of harsh with all of the edge case testing but that's more my fault. Fair professor.
Test are very difficult and should be studied for.

Took the hybrid version and don't recommend it. Nearly all learning is from pre-recorded videos. The videos are well produced and have nice visuals though. Exams + final make 85% of your grade and homeworks can take a while. Felt like there's a lot of emphasis on memorizing rather than fully understanding and being able to synthesize from content.

I think HP is ok I just had her during the first attempt of hybrid in an 8am lecture and when she was facing some health problems. The lectures do NOT teach you material rather it focused more on showing examples from material you should've learned beforehand. Overall it was okay, but the hybrid section will probably get more organized with time.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took the hybrid version of this class and can't say that I recommend it. It makes it a lot harder to learn the material if you're trying to do it all from the module videos. If you take the hybrid option, please go to the in-person lectures anyways, it helps out a lot. Otherwise, the class is very straightforward and you know what is expected.

This professor was outstanding - easily one of the best professors at Tech!  Her class made me wish I was in CS - I'm CompE.  Moreover, she was very caring - my registration time once fell during one of the exams, so she let me take the exam with an earlier section so that I could register at the earliest.  Highly recommend!

Overall terrible course structure (3 exams + 1 final and they account for 85% of your grade, w/ 70% minimum exam average policy). Little to no time on the exams (50 mins to do MC, diagramming, and 2 coding questions).Too much emphasis placed on useless memorization; course designed by someone in Academia with zero work experience outside academia.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I found this subject very easy, but I could see how one might struggle in this class. She's not very good at teaching and really makes me wonder if she understands the material herself sometimes. It's hard to believe that at one of the greatest CS schools in the world, she's the one teaching the most important (i think) class. very mediocre
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lectures and very in depth, go to office hours if needed the TAs are amazing resources. Course is really difficult but arguably the most important class of all CS major. Start Leetcoding right after taking this class.
I really liked her haha

CS 1332 is organized really well by efforts of Prof HB. They provide all the necessary materials on Canvas so it's even ok if you don't attend lectures. Online videos provide more information than taught in lectures. Homework and exams are manageable thanks to all the materials and helpful TAs.

I took the online section, and the lectures left a lot to be desired compared to how involved and rigorous the in-person sections were. You can definitely do well in the course if you apply yourself a lot and really hammer home the concepts, but there is a lot of material to learn.

I took the in-person section, and the lectures were very helpful. HB takes time to go over the tough concepts, but leaves the easier memorization to do on your own. The TAs are good, and office hours are a great resource for the homework which is challenging but  prepares you for the tests. HB usually gives hints about what to study before tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Go to class for an A
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Hands down the best class I've taken so far. The course is super well run, thanks to HB herself and the TA team. Her pacing may be slightly slow, but I think it's alright since she spends a lot of time making sure that students understand the concepts. Her module videos are very good as well. 10/10 class.
HB is a good professor. Her lectures are a bit boring but useful. The homework and assignments are easy in my opinion. There are plenty of resources online to help you succeed.

Unlike most professors, she handwrites her notes - which is SUPER helpful for diagramming, an integral part of each exam. By attending class and taking notes with her, you're actively learning the content. Practice exams are provided before each exam, and they do not stray format-wise from those practice exams. There are a ton of online resources

Took the asynchronous section so wasn't in direct contact with HB. Overall her videos and resources posted online are extraordinary and really prepare you for both the exams and homework. TAs are very helpful for the course and are easy to ask questions. Exams are applications of learned data structures. Maybe the most organized class at Tech.

Amazing lectures! The in depth explanation of data structures and algorithms and diagramming helps learners of different types to all learn the concepts well. The homework and tests were fair and TA's and Professor are accessible, caring, and very helpful in general! Great motivations, resources, lectures, and help! Probably the best class I've had

She was a good professor. She takes time, and writes down materials, gives examples, and goes over the materials. The TAs are the best! Everyone is very knowledgeable, understanding, and helpful. The tests are difficult if not practiced. ALWAYS attend all questions, there are partial credit. If you do all the non-coding question, you will get a B.

HB's in-person lectures were okay, and I did not like how she gave us an exam after break due to GT "changing" their scheduling. However, the resources and recorded lectures for this class were extraordinary! The TA's are also great, and recitation was a great review of the material.

I learned a lot from HB, she has great lecture videos that cover all the content so you don't need to go to lecture in-person if you don't want to. The homework was coding data structures and the tests were a good challenge. HB also cares about her students and she's funny sometimes

Lecture videos very dry but covers content well. Had to use restroom before final, and was not let back into room by TAs despite test not even starting. On another occasion, HB was very condescending and rude over a simple question. Teaching is very average quality, at BEST.

HB is a good professor - she cares about her students and her TA team is really awesome. Her lectures do become quite dry, but she has created an exceptional module system for 1332- you can learn pretty much everything through her module videos, which are concise and teach the concepts really well.

HB was an amazing professor to have, and while the content can be tough at times, there are plenty of resources available to students, and she always picks amazing TAs! Tests can be a little long for some people, especially with a 50 min time limit, but overall she's great!
Overall course very well structured. I appreciate how many different resources there are in addition to lecture, and I wish other courses would be more like hers
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor is awesome. She is kind and caring but also strict when it comes to grading sometimes. But overall very fair. I wish we had more professors like HB!

Great professor. Notes during class were easy to follow, and she thoroughly goes through every example making sure we understand. TAs were amazing as well. The amount of resources they provide is crazy. She gives us the entire online class modules for us to use. They give you all the things you need to succeed, make good use of them to do well.

HB cares. She puts effort into her craft, and it shows. 1332 is a challenging class, but you'll never feel like you've been duped because you're given so many resources to succeed. I wish more professors focused on students' success/imparting knowledge like HB vs crafting tricky problems to show you... how clever they are, I guess?

Very nice professor teaching me CS 1332 in Summer 2022.
Full of easy-to-understand lecture records help me a lot in both time-saving and well-understanding.

Her modules are awesome, she is an amazing lecturer and offers an insane amount of resources. Her TA's are probably the most useful TA's I have ever had. BUT SHE -AS WELL AS HER TA's- CAN NOT WRITE. The test questions for the multiple-choice sections and her socrative polls are worded so poorly that only the writer knows what is being asked.

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS IN SUMMER. Other than that, the TAs were really nice and helpful. The tests were more like memorization test but there were a lot of partial credits. This class should not be hard during a full semester because you need time to absorb the new materials.

-Grading breakdown: 50% quizzes (5 worth 10% each), 25% final, 20% HW, 5% participation
-Course is leacture-heavy, so attendance is strongly recommended
-Quizzes and HW were fairly easy
-HW often done in class with help
-Prof was personable and caring
-Learning curve is steep if you've never taken CS before, but it gets a lot easier

All tests are cumulative, so each test just becomes straight memorization of too many topics and is ineffective at best. She crams so many topics into each test and the timing is awful. Grading can be lenient sometimes but good luck getting a regrade. Homeworks are excessive and u have to memorize them for the test. Exams are not well made at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took her async class over the summer and had too many problems. If u r off campus during the summer, good luck. Async class but has tests in person, i had to email the dean for remote TA office hours and that still took weeks to implement and TA's didnt show up sometimes, and shes a stubborn pain in the ***. Cant admit when she/TA's are wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took an online async version of this course and I really enjoyed the format. The modules online consisted of well-made videos that taught the content really well. I did not interact much with the professor but I did enjoy the class. Grading can feel a bit harsh at the start but there are lots of resources + TAs are very helpful with explanations.

The online lectures that were available were high quality and did a great job of explaining the course material thoroughly. If you wish to succeed in this class, take advantage of the material that is offered along with the TAs. Done well, you have most of the tools necessary to succeed in many other aspects of tech.

Lectures were sometimes hard to learn from since she handwrites notes. But this is made up for by the excellent quality of the online lecture module videos which thoroughly cover all course material in a succinct way. This is a very well organized class with amazing TAs and plenty of resources and a must have for anyone entering the tech field.

Dr. HB is overall a great choice for CS 1332. The in-person option that she offers is a little tougher than the online CS 1332 section since you have to memorize everything for the in-person exams, but her lectures walk through all the content you need to know. Homeworks are clear and reflect the test content accurately. Overall, great teacher!

Above average professor, lectures are really really optional (I went, but know so many who didn't and still did well). So much extra material to learn the stuff. TAs are amazing. So basically do the homeworks, study for the exams, and you should be good.

Decent lecturer, great TAs, and she's very nice but is decently strict. The class is clearly exam focused as the 3 exams and final are 84% of your course grade, and they are moderately difficult. Exams are fair, but the timing isn't too great, forcing you to learn the material thoroughly. However, there's a ridiculous amount of helpful resources.

Really great professor! Kind, knowledgeable, and available. Her lectures get a bit boring and she was absent for quite a few of them, but a great (and really big) TA staff filled in the gaps. This course is pretty heavily dominated by homework, so don't overload yourself on courses and don't procrastinate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Dr. HB really cares about her students and their success.  The TAs in this course are amazing and help her make this course manageable.  There is a lot of work in this course, but it is very relevant to the job sphere, so it is good to learn the material.  There are bunches of resources to help you succeed supplied by her and the TAs!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. HB says it on the first day: DO THE HOMEWORKS TO DO WELL! She provides a bunch of resources on canvas to supplement her lectures (or replace them). If you genuinely put in the effort to do the assignments, you'll be fine. Very fair in the sense that she'll only ask coding questions on material that has been graded. No dropped HWs or exams, tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things
