reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Igor is a fair grader, and I guess he's an alright lecturer, not always the clearest explainer. Sit towards the front of the lecture hall because he's kinda difficult to hear. He also has a fairly thick accent, definitely not impossible to understand, but I had trouble understanding him during 8am lectures. Fair grading scale. 85+ is an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Professor Belegradek can get a little bit confusing during lectures but is always willing to answer questions and really cares to make sure that all of his students fully understand the material in the end. If you make the effort to ask him questions and go to his office hours, you will not regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Professor Igor Belegradek makes sure we really understand the concepts in Linear Algebra instead of just doing computations. The tests are highly conceptual but these tests are based on the practice problems he releases before the test. He always answers questions on Piazza in a detailed and specific manner. Best Math Professor I have ever had.
Igor's style of teaching is difficult to grasp at first, but if you put the time into the class, you will do well. Practice problems and reading the textbook are key to doing well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: It certainly felt impossible to succeed. I skipped lecturesarned through recitations, tutoring, and the textbook. Practice problems are given out before each exam that mimic questions on exam-if you have ALL answers to these problems, you are solid. Obtaining sufficient answers to theory questions is easier said than done; Piazza is a life saver

DO NOT TAKE HIM!!! He is horrible at teaching. He doesn't respect you at all. When you ask him a question he just quotes the syllabus or tells us to look at the syllabus. He has a strong accent and is hard to understand even though I speak his language. He is to fast and the exams our way to theoretical.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Igor was a horrible teacher in that his entire lecture philosophy seems to be based off of two key "facts" - that everyone comes into the class with a background in linear algebra (not necessarily true) and that people understand what he his saying. He is both fast-paced and unclear and makes tons of mistakes in lectures. Take virtually anyone else

Belegradek has a pretty thick accent that takes some getting used to. TAs can be hit or miss for the class. Lectures are organized and informative, but the textbook is easier to understand. Weekly quizzes and homeworks were easy. Tests are typically 20 points over 7 questions, but grading is fair. A is an 85%, B is 70% and so on.

Has an accent and is very hard to understand in lecture. Tests all all theoretical (given this, prove why... ), and he gives easy online homework that takes up a good chunk of the grade. An okay class and professor, but you may find yourself learning it all out of the textbook.

Homeworks are easy. Igor has an accent but is still understandable. Quiz every recitation, pretty straightforward, totally hit or miss though, dropped bottom 3 so it was fine. Tests are all theory and he teaches the class like an honors class according to my TA. Very approachable for office hours. Reading textbook can almost substitute for lectures

He's a very smart person, and he knows his linear algebra, but he isn't the greatest teacher. His lectures are difficult to understand and he cannot engage his students. His tests are also difficult, it's largely based on theory.

Be prepared to teach yourself linear algebra. If you have a hard time understanding a Russian accent, skip lecture. Plus side of the class is getting to use crib sheets during the test and final. Take another professor if you can!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof. Belegradek is a really good teacher who tries his very best to make sure his students are actually learning. The homework takes up to ten minutes every week, he gives out questions before quizzes and tests and usually asks similar ones on the tests. His accent is a little problematic but it's not that big a deal. Grades are curved, 85 is A.

Weekly quizzes on ungraded HW and MyMathLab enforce learning. Tests are straight-forward, and based on the HWreview sheet but can be tough even so. Russian accent forces you to concentrate to follow the lecture. Attendance helps understanding- Igor is very enthusiastic about the material. Grades were slightly curved at the end: 85  A, 70  B, etc
If you take the limit of this guy's awesomeness, it goes to "Infiniteh."

Igor has a great sense of humor, but has a thick Russian accent that may be hard to understand for some people (although not the case for me). My TA was baller so I was ok with the class. Advice: do hw (although optional for the class), and ask questions during lectures or recitation on HW problems you did not understand.
Good class, he just changes numbers from practice test for actual test, plus lets you bring sheets of notes to test

The material was very understandable once it was explained by a great tutor. The professor is completely ineffective as a teacher, his heavy accent and writing make him impossible to follow. He also confuses even himself during lecture, not to mention all the students, he makes very simple concepts and theorems seem inexorably complex.

Got an A. Good teacher. You get a front and back cheat sheet each exam and two on the final. Provides practice tests online and basically just changes the numbers a bit of the actual tests. Not a difficult Calc 2 class at all.

Hey was bad, I'm not going to lie but there were great curves and the TA's were fantastic so I came away with a very good grade. Take him, but do so knowing there will be a lot of study on your own. Another good thing about him is that you can use a cheat sheet on the tests so you can write important equations.

Jumps all over the place, with no organization. I had a hard time understanding him, much less, learning the material. He curves quite a bit since everyone fails the tests. Its a difficult class, but not impossible. Hey, I passed it

Horrible professor, one of the worst, if not the worst one I have ever had at tech.  His lectures are useless because he is hard to understand and he jumps all over the board with his example.  I passed the class, but learned very little.
I did good in the class, but not because of the teacher...he is the worst teacher I have had at Georgia Tech, take anybody but him for diff eq.

One of the worst professors I've had at Tech.  His lectures are very unclear and he is hard to understand when he talks.  Tests were very difficult with averages as low as the 50s.  He was forced to have massive curves.  Don't take this class if you want to learn anything.

Strikes the best balance of hilarious, engaging lectures + excellent teaching that I've seen at Tech. Lengthy homeworks requiring R but I guarantee you'll understand the material better than if you took any other instructor. Only complaint is no practice tests and difficult exams which is unfortunate, but learn the material well and you'll succeed.

Ethan is one of the best professors I've had. He cares for all his students and knows everyone's names. He really wants u to learn the material so his exams are more difficult than the other sections, but it is completely worth it. He's hilarious and u will know way more than the other sections. He makes u learn R and curves! Please take him!
The GOAT. He's so funny.

Makes you feel stupid for asking questions at office hours. HW is basically coding in R, and the exams are difficult with very little partial credit and unnecessarily difficult instructions intended to confuse you. Attendance is mandatory but lectures are very boring. Be prepared for a hard time if you take his class.

Ethan is a great professor. His homeworks can be extensive and take time to complete, but they make sure you learn the material well. His exams are weighted heavily and really require you to know the material inside and out, but he is very accommodating for one-on-one help and will help you succeed if you work at it.

The GOAT!

My favorite lecturer at Georgia Tech. Ethan wants his students to succeed, and as long as you show up and put in the effort you will be rewarded. Please take him for 4031 if you are given the opportunity, and I promise you will not be disappointed.

A genuinely good professor for a very simple class. He was funny, engaging, and taught the material in a fun way. Easy to follow and very well-organized. You'll have to learn R, but this took negligible time. Pay attention to how good (appearance) your homework and report assignments look and you'll do fine.

This class was way harder than it should be. The entire semester felt overwhelming while taking it. I struggled a lot to understand what was happening during lectures, and the homework assignments were extremely time-consuming. The professor used an R program to randomly call on students, which added to the stress of attending class.

Ethan is definitely an entertaining professor & his banter alone made me go to class. Homework can be time consuming, but if you are interested in Data Science & want to learn R, definitely take Ethan. His tests & grading are fair, but beware that there is virtually no practice material for exams.

Most entertaining professor I've had at Georgia Tech by far. He is outspoken and brutally honest about his expectations for his students. This guy made me want to come to lectures, even if just for a good laugh. My only issue is that 60% of your grade is based on one midterm and a final exam, for both of which zero review material is provided.

He has very high expectations and can make you feel stupid if you ask questions. Above all else though, the homeworks are grueling. Not necessarily because of the content but because it must be types in R. I almost lost my mind several times this semester because of having to code the hw which took hours.

Oh my god Ethan blows.  Do not take him.  Such a hard grader and especially for an introductory stats class.  If hes ur only option id go for the math or ece alternative.  His homework is done in R and learning adds so much time at the start of the course.  Also only one midterm and then a final.  Will end in a A/B but only bc I took AP stats.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Ethan's not so bad in general but don't work for him as your boss

Extremely harsh grader and offered an extremely rude response when I reached out seeking better feedback on my assignment. This is not a stats class - it's an R class. His midterm consists of writing your own questions which takes hours, and if your questions match the difficulty of the textbook you'll receive "between a B and a C"
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ethan is the type of professor that you either love or hate. His classes are rigorous but give you an exceptional understanding of the material if you take the time to attend lecture, do the homework, read the textbook and go to office hours if needed. He teaches using R which is free and useful outside of classes. Wouldn't recommend for an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Best and favorite professor I've ever had at Tech.  4031 can be a difficult class, but Ethan explains concepts incredibly well and lecture notes/R codes are very helpful.  Attendance counts with occasional pop quizzes, but his lecture banter alone makes it worth it to attend class.  Sit up front and pay attention - he's an all around great prof.

He's making a class that is straightforward unnecessarily and annoyingly difficult. Lectures are boring and he could've gone over some content in half the time. Refuses to give practice materials for the midterms despite how much it is worth in the final grade.

He's not a bad professor in terms of his teaching; however, this class is a lot more work than the other ISYE 3770 sections. All homeworks are written in R and they are quite time consuming. He has 2 in class "projects" that test your knowledge of how to use R. Also, the final is a decently large portion of the grade. Edit: HE CURVES THE FINAL!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy, though lectures could've slightly been better. Loved his hilarious personal stories, which really helped reinforce concepts, and class was overall easy, except for the final, which was 35% of our grade. Overall, fun guy, but was a challenging professor, who is determined to help you succeed, "make sure to study or you won't do well"
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Somewhat difficult course for people with no background in statistics. The final exam and midterm make up more than half of the grade. He said the midterm was easy so he was going to make the final harder. Did well in every other category except the final, ended up dropping my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His teaching was good and things were fine until the final. For whatever reason, he said that the midterm was easy so he would make the final harder and ended up screwing us over. I worked hard and got good grades on everything except the final. Dropped an entire letter grade and nothing I can do about it

Lectures are really boring. His teaching style is pretty mid. Homeworks are time consuming but I guess its helpful for learning LaTeX and R. Overall extremely mid prof but at least he's kind of funny.

He takes your attendance during lecture, but Ethan's lectures were pretty interesting. His HWs are weekly but pretty easy. The in person projects are a piece of cake as well. A lot of his exam questions are based on HW questions, so as long as you do the hw, the exams will be a breeze.

Did not like his teaching style at first and did bad on the midterm. I realized that you really just need to take his advice from the beginning: understand all the lecture problems and HW questions. He can come off as harsh, but I think he means well. He was true to his word about expectations. And he will bump grades if you do well on the final.

If it's your only option, take Ethan, but if there's a better prof., you could do better. Homeworks are very time consuming, and it's difficult to bounce back from a bad grade. Also, would recommend reviewing R before taking him.

Ethan's 3030 & 4031 are fantastic. He uses R in all classes which is so useful to learn. His lecture style is very structured & straight-forward: attendance is tracked, exams are from lectures. If you do the HW & study the slides, you'll do well in the midterm & final. But also GO TO OFFICE HOURS & ISYE Tutoring, it's heavy content so ask for help!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely not an easy professor, but I learned a lot. Class is very R heavy and time intensive, so stay on top of the lectures and HW.  Exams are in person and HARD and make up the bulk of your grade (1 midterm + 1 final,) but he curved very generously at the end. He may come off as harsh, but he really cares about his students.

Extremely tough grader and grading policy has gotten more difficult post-COVID with exams now in person. He is a good person as a teacher who seems to care, but he takes years to grade, has 8 AM office hours, and is hard to reach at times. He curved his class to a 3.0 GPA, but the averages were very low so you didn't know your grade until the end.

Do not take Ethan for 3030. He cannot entirely control all of these things, but the ZERO-tolerance makeup policy (for exams too), 8 am office hours, extremely late grading, and difficulty I had understanding him in class did not make the class worth it. He curved so the class would have a 3.0 average. Preserve your GPA. It's not worth it.
Lecture can be a little dry, lots of homework, but he is always willing to help. Learning R is super helpful and I recommend taking 3030 with Ethan

Ethan is THE TOUGHEST grader I've seen. Ridiculously unforgiving grading policy, and he openly admits to playing favorites when it comes to final grades (Positive/Negative). He is personally well meaning and nice, but if your interest is in having a good GPA, I cannot recommend this professor. The effort required to succeed is easily above average.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lee is an amazing professor. Gets to the point and tests relevant material. He likes to teach supplemental material as well. Very R heavy but, if you don't know much R, you should still be fine to take the class as he starts off from the basics. Very few grading categories and he can be a hard grader. I'd take him for all my ISyE classes if I could

All notes are posted online so youll be able to review them as needed. He cares about the students and the class is fairly easy, with exam questions coming from homeworks and lecture notes. However, only one midterm which makes up a lot of your grade, and he can take forever to grade (we didnt get midterm grade back for many weeks).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really good professor and nice guy. He's a pretty harsh but fair grader. Tests are the vast majority of your grade, but he prepares you well for them. Even though I did poorly in the class, I still feel like I learned a lot and would take his classes again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ethan is really sweet as a prof and definitely cares about his students. He may try to scare you out of taking his class - DONT listen! He's an amazing prof and his exams are similar to homework and class examples. He wants his students to succeed and you learn a lot as well. Not an easy class, but he teaches it very well with his own examples.

i am not sure why there are so many good ratings even for my semester ending May'20... maybe it's just freshmen being freshmen... this was one of the worst class I had taken... it's like you're back in HS if you're into that go for it. weekly HWs graded hard (if not very). all weight lies in midterm and finals. both graded harshly, no extra credit

The one midterm and final make up a huge chunk of your grade so there really isn't any room for error. But he is extremely clear about what you will see on the tests so make sure you go over practice questions and HW and you'll be set. He'll try to make you drop the class on the first day but don't listen to him; his bad jokes are worth it.

His lectures and amazing but the weighting of the midterm and final can really mess with your grade. I love the way he teaches but you need to practice the HW really well to score great. Went from a C to an A in the class with his advice. Always reach out when in need. He takes attendance but there are three free days. HW is based on the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Midterm is a time crunch. Doesn't give a ton of partial credit, but the questions themselves aren't too bad. Useful/entertaining lectures across the board. He pretty much tells you how the class is going to be on syllabus day and that's the way it is. Would take again.

Never listen to Ethan when he tries to make you drop at the beginning of the semester (he did that with us). Staying in his class was the best decision I have ever made. He is, hands down, the best professor I have had. His passion for his students is unparalleled. His class is also not too difficult and it measures what you know.

(Homework questions are from the textbook.) Ethan is a really good lecturer and gives good examples that help you understand the concepts and he keeps the lectures interesting too. The only thing about his class is (at least for my semester) we mainly had one midterm and the final for our grades. so make sure to study
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I created an account here just to rate this professor. I probably will get a C on this class, but I am pretty bad at statistics/prob. Ethan is in my top 5 at tech. Cares about you, gives you help, pushes you, and even lets you work with TA from his others classes to get help. Classes are funny. Besides, he's a real yellow jacket fun.

He is a very good teacher and he is very willing to listen to his students for feedback. He makes a big effort to give partial credit to everyone in exams. His lecture notes are very complete and useful. Exams are fair in difficulty, he clearly states what you need to do to succeed in the course. I really enjoyed his class!

Very nice guy. Lectures not the best, but puts entire lecture as word doc on canvas post-class. Class made to be easy, but people underestimate class + that's why scores are low. You can pass if you skip class but read + understand notes at home (but attendance is graded so have a friend sign you in) + do HW and check with chegg AFTER.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I really like Ethan's class. He sincerely cares about his students and lecture is very clear. He tells us exactly what will be on the exam. If you do the homework and understand class lecture examples, the exam is going to be easy. I don't think homework is too heavy. Usually 5-6 questions taking up 2 hours each week. Will recommend
Doesn't care much about lectures. Talks random stuff about his family all the time and uses very confusing examples. Passes an attendance sheet every class. Homework is large. Not recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The criteria for doing well in this class is not at all clear. I lost a lot of points on reports because of unclear grading criteria. You only have to go to lab ~6 times per semester though, with 4 lab reports (25% of your grade). These take a lot of time. The lectures were incoherent and slow, but you also only have 4 of those.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Snoozefest! He may be an emeritus prof, but he can't really teach or use technology. Stopped going to class after about a week. Lab reports are graded using a rubric and are very time consuming. Expect each to take 10-15 hours of time. They are tediously graded and the TA's are strict about including specific things. Suck it up and get it done.

Lectures are unclear and unhelpful. Grading was highly ambiguous, subjective, and nit-picky (TAs' fault primarily). Course schedule is structured poorly so if you're in section X you'll have weeks of back-to-back lab reports that are extraordinarily time intensive. Responses on Piazza are vague and conflicting, if you even get one.

This is one of the worst classes I've taken at this school. The lab manuals are incredibly unclear, and the course has major organization issues. The TAs will take points off for things that are clearly in your report, and you won't ever get a report back before the next one is due, meaning you will make the same mistakes over and over.

Dr. Jagoda: course professor. The real reason I'm here is the trash TA's. We had 3 labs: 25%, 40%, and 25% (10% notebook). They couldn't correctly grade if someone moved their fingers for them. Had to put infinite regrade requests for things that were blatantly correct if you took a few seconds to read the reports. Over a month to get grades back.

This class is basically the lab course, and you meet a couple times per semester to go over the next lab. Class is kinda messy (one of our four labs got entirely canceled due to timing issues yay) but not difficult. The labs are graded easy, and are pretty much busy work but also a little fun.

This teacher was good; I saw him like 5 times total. This lab class is not hard, but the grading can be rough if you do not follow the rubrics to a T. Want advice? Separate 15 hours per lab report (four total, 25% each) and read EXACTLY as the rubric says. They are grading if you include everything. Class is only about the writing, not the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AE 2610 is not supposed to be a hard lab class, but with Jagoda, the lectures were extremely boring, and the labs anything but clear. Would definitely not recommend taking with him if you have the choice. During lecture, most of the class was either asleep or doing other work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely poor management of the class, obviously did not care about teaching this intro class. Never once taught his own lecture. Lab materials were poorly written and contradictory, with huge penalties for errors made as a result. This class that is supposed to be very easy became a nightmare of guessing at what the lab handbook actually wanted.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Obviously has no interest in teaching this class, is barely even present at class and relies entirely on TAs to teach. The TAs don't know what they're doing, and the documentation for the labs is so bad that it conflicts with itself, causing you to miss data collection that is required in the reports but not listed in the procedure.

Maybe the best professor I have had. AE2010 is a very hard class, but he is an excellent teacher. He grades the tests himself and is very understanding with partial credit. If you make a dumb mistake but clearly understand how to do the problem, he will give full credit. If you do and understand the homework, you will do well on the tests.

After the first lecture you will be in despair because Jagoda is not a great lecturer. But he is the most caring prof in Tech, all you have to do is talk to him outside of class. He meets with you anytime (even sundays) and as long as you reach out, he will spend as much time as needed 1v1 till you understand it. In short - TALK TO HIM !!

The class was definitely difficult and he isn't the best lecturer, but he's super accessible outside of class. He's always willing to help and I've found he's a lot better at explaining concepts one-on-one. Definitely would recommend talking to him in office hours, he's really nice.

Lectures are not his strong suit. Hes somewhat hard to understand at times and just used slideshows that dont always make much sense. Attending recitations is definitely a must. His class is graded on a really generous curve of around 20% and he grades the homework and exams super leniently. You definitely have to put in the work to study though.

Wow this guy is bad. Lectures were from slides that he didn't make and most of the time were just long derivations with no explanation. There was no way to reference the textbook from his lectures. Overall course grade was never available, just had to guess. Not sure if he graded on a curve even though the class average was around a 65. Don't take.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Sometimes hard to hear, but great professor and lecturer. He will go out of his way to help students that ask for it. Tests were not easy, but were pretty fair

He can be a little scary in class because he calls you out for little things. I don't enjoy going to class because he gets mad at people when they're late and highlights people's errors in front of the whole class, but attendance is mandatory (and he will figure out if you're missing it). The class is at least very easy.

Not lenient or understanding at all, rude and will call you out for the smallest things in front of the entire class. Would've been a straightforward and enjoyable class, if he wasn't teaching it. Super nitpicky, will find something wrong with your work for even the simplest assignments.
rude, will call people out in front of entire class

Too much work for a one credit hour class. Yells at students. You can never do anything right type of professor. Will always find an issue with something you're doing and loudly announce it. You will learn, and he's effective at making his students learn. But you will not enjoy taking his class.

I took Professor Seitzman during Summer 2025. One of the best professor's I've taken at Tech. AE 4451 is not an easy course to take in 5 weeks, and his homeworks are tough and challenging, but his style of teaching is awesome. I suggest for anyone who wants to go into propulsion, to take him.

Dr. Seitzman is the most intelligent and quick-witted professor I have ever met. He has transformed my engineering intuition for the better and I am grateful to have had a class with him. Although sassy, he wants to help you understand the concepts. Homework and exams are tough but if you put in the effort to go to office hours, you will be fine.

Seitzman is a fantastic professor! His lectures were very clear, helpful, and engaging. He gets that AE 2010 is a hard class, and he is happy to re-explain concepts as many times and as many ways as you need so that you get a better understanding both during class and outside of it.

Took his 4451 class over the summer in Limerick and it was one of the hardest classes I've taken. That said, if you like Jet Propulsion there is no class at Tech that will give you a better foundation in it than Seitzman's class. Study up and buddy up for the homeworks, and give yourself time to do the final project. It's hard but valuable.

Probably the best class I've taken. Seitzman is a very good lecturer, but has high expectations, as the homeworks and tests are difficult. If you aren't interested in the subject and just want an easy A, do not take Seitzman, but if you want to learn he's probably the best professor in the department. Go to office hours, hardass about extensions.

The content of the course was not very difficult but Dr. Seitzman's harsh grading forces us to put triple the effort in mastering the content compared to other grad courses. This is not the typical course where you can get an A and come out still not knowing concepts, our final was like a summer packet covering every single conceptual question.

The subject matter is tough, there's no getting around that and Professor Seitzman holds his students to high standards. At the same time, he really cares about his students' understanding and is willing to put in the effort to help anyone who is willing to learn. One of the best taught classes I've taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had. Lectures were 2 hours and I was locked in the whole time. Can't recommend him enough if you actually care about the content.

Dr. Seitzman is one of the best professors at Tech, and his classes are extremely challenging. I struggled on some of the homeworks, and he actually EMAILED ME and encouraged me to ask him for help if needed. I've never had a professor in college go out of their way to do that. It will be hard, but I recommend taking him if you get the chance.

The hardest class I've taken at Tech, but the one I've learned the most from. I did this during the Limerick program, so it was a lot of information and tough homework with short turnaround. The homework took up most of my weekdays, but Dr. Seitzman is a great teacher who will really help you get all the theory and math through your head.

Professor Seitzman might be the smartest person alive. He will not go easy on you but you will for sure learn the material. I recommend taking Jet Pro with him for anybody who wishes to go into propulsion. There will be a lot of work and struggling but the lessons are invaluable. Make sure you go into jet pro with adequate thermo knowledge.

Took AE4451 with Seitzman abroad in 5 weeks, and although tough like his AE2010 class, he sets clear expectations for success and is an outstanding lecturer. He is flexible when scheduling meetings outside class and does a good job of guiding you to answers. High effort yields excellent learning, and I highly recommend taking any AE class with him.

Class once a week for 50 minutes. Spent 1hr on hw a week. In-class assignments are easy, however, there were a lot of them and you have to keep track as each one counts for your final grade. Just complete your assignments, 15 min a piece, and you will get an A. A good professor who gives good advice, although he can be blunt sometimes. Recommended.

Dr. Seitzman is clearly very smart and knows what he's doing. However, he took this 1-credit class way too seriously, and would yell at and sometimes even bark (woof woof) at students. Especially at the start of the year, the grading was very harsh, and it made this class so much more work than it should've been.

Seitzman not a good professor. He consistently yelled at his students and even barked at them a couple times in an effort to get them quiet. He gave too many assignments for a one-credit course. He would put students into groups during class then yell at them when they couldn't find their group even though it was a 200 person lecture.

Prof. Seitzman is not easy. Going to lecture is not required, but not attending only hurts you because Seitzman usually gives important comments that go along with his lecture slides. Ditto other comments on the homework sets: they are long, difficult, and intended for you use notes. Seitzman will challenge you and hammer in concepts.

This course is super interesting, especially due to Dr. Seitzman's expertise and enthusiasm. Seitzman's method involves absolutely hammering the course material into your brain with difficult homework sets; you can expect to spend around eight hours on each of them (around 5 problems). Beyond this, exams are difficult, but open-book/notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Seitzman does not have set office hours, creates extremely hard homeworks that even upperclass student tutors cannot solve, is somewhat degrading when questions are asked or when offering help. Homeworks are not graded in a timely manner and solutions to past homeworks arent given on time before each exam. Please avoid this professor.

Professor Seitzman gives relatively good lectures. He asks lots of questions and is sympathetic toward students. However, his homework is incredibly challenging and does not include values students need to solve the problems (it is assumed we will look this up) with class hw averages around a C.

Professor Seitzman is the best professor I have had at Tech. He understands what it's like to be completely confused and is extremely patient. He asks many questions in lecture to keep you engaged. GO TO OA for topics you are struggling with. Trust me. He will grill you, but toughen up because you will leave a smarter person and a better engineer.

Taking Dr. Seitzman for AE 2010 turned out to be a HUGE mistake. Toward the end of the semester, I had a family emergency arise & to say that Dr. Seitzman was unaccommodating is a huge understatement. Challenging classes & professors are expected at Tech, but I have never had a prof who didn't publish exam keys & whose feedback on tests & HW was NA
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great professor! He will really challenge you and make sure you know your stuff. If you don't he will really nail it home. Definitely makes you work for an A but it is well worth the effort.

2611 is a stupid easy class. Go to lecture, do the assignments, get the A. Seitzman doesn't complicate it, and does present the material in a more enjoyable manner than most prof would. I appreciated his simplicity and the laid back approach to the class.

Dr. Seitzman has very high expectations for his students. He is very particular and makes sure that everything you say is precisely true. He requires a thorough understanding of concepts and assumptions. He was a very valuable teacher for putting you in a solid engineering mindset. Not an easy A, but possible with hard work.

Dr. Seitzman is by far my favorite professor at Tech. I've taken him for a couple of classes, most recently 6450. His lectures are interesting and relevant, and he tries (and succeeds) to make the material really applicable to the real world. His homeworks are time consuming but helpful, and tests are not easy, but straightforward.

Seitzman is a great professor, he is very knowledgeable and great at conveying information in a way students can understand and learn. He can badger you sometimes, especially in office hours, but he does a good job at breaking down the concepts and is very helpful during office hours. Homework are very insightful and greatly facilitate learning
Great professor. Popcorns a bit in class and can come across as intimidating, but very helpful and accessible. Good lectures, fair homework, fun class.   Great hottiness.

Seitzman is heavily involved administratively, academically, and and professionally (through research) with the AE department. Will guide students, but won't hold their hand. Be prepared to show you are working hard and creatively. Straightforeward, accessible, and a little intimidating.
Good

Dr. Sietzman is very enthusiastic. Be prepared to interact because he's big on participation. If you don't read this class will suck. You also NEED to have the pre-recs otherwise you won't be able to understand what's going on. His exams are heavily weighted on conceptual knowledge learned through homeworks. Be prepared to work 40hrs/wk.

Seitzman is a great professor. He's excited about the material and genuinely wants his students to understand the material. Homeworks are time intensive (about 40 hours a week) but the class is great! If you put in the effort you'll know your stuff for sure. Exams are based on conceptual knowledge of coursework and hw.
Not helpful for me at all.
Whenever you have a chance take Dr.Seitzman, do it! He's really amazing, like him so much!
His class isn't super-easy, but he's very helpful, particularly if you drop by his office to ask questions.

Dr. Seitzman is an amazing! He really tries to make students grasp the concept and develops an intuition on the subject which is very essential in eng. He is a good sense of humor. He is very helpful during his office hours and don't be scared to ask question in class. Try to understand every concept he teaches in class and exams should be fair.
Good professor who has a heavy emphasis on class participation. Homeworks are difficult, but cover material in the lectures. Midterm and final were fair.

She assigns readings to look over for about every other class, but you only have to skim them and pay attention in lecture to have an understanding of what's going on. Assignment requirements are communicated clearly and the TA's and Roberts give good feedback, so it's easy to do well on assignments and get an A in the class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If I am being honest, the class was okay. I wasn't always excited, but she was very nice and clear with grading. A lot of unnecessary reading. I never read any of the readings and did fine. I would recommend that you all take her if you want an A. The group project wasn't too bad, but you wont be able to just coast your way through.
Prof Roberts is very reasonable and kind. Class reqs are very straightforward and as long as you do your work, you will be fine.

I expected it to have lighter work than it did but honestly it is worth it for a chill CS class. Lectures are a bit dull but there were a few class activities that I enjoyed. The class is mostly a semester long project that you work alongside a team. There is one midterm and a presentation of the project.

The class itself isn't difficult, but she is an incredibly dry lecturer and it's difficult to pay attention to how she rambles in monotone. Also, grading criteria is not clear at all; despite how easy the homeworks are, it's equally easy to lose points on something not previously mentioned in the directions. Would suggest the other Ed Tech prof.
Pretty solid class, engaging lecturer. Not much to say, you just do a group project about designing an educational technology.

Prof Roberts's Ed Tech class was wonderful. You'll learn a lot during lecture, and she really engages students. The class is what you make of it—if you apply yourself and are passionate about the group project topic, then you will really enjoy it. There is a good bit of writing, which is to be expected. Great class overall!

Teaching-wise, she is great. Very driven and motivated about ed tech. The structure of the class however wasn't ideal and kinda messy.  We would have weekly assignments and not get grades back for months which was frustrating especially since grp projects build off each other. Also this class did not need mandatory attendance smh. super easy tho!!!

Professor Roberts is passionate about her work and her lectures are engaging, but she gives grades for assignments so late that due date for the next assignment has long passed. I and some of my friends have gotten 70s and 80s on assignments with 3-5 words of feedback, but this might depend on the TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof Roberts is one of my fav profs I've ever had. She is kind, respected, and respectful. Her class does require some long paper/essays but they're never TOO difficult, and we never had exams! She makes class engaging and interactive, which I liked a lot. She loves this course and teaching; I would definitely recommend her.

Professor Roberts is a wonderful and inspirational professor. I would definitely take her class again! She really cares about ed tech and her passion for the field really shines through her teaching. If you can take a class with her, do it! You wont regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I think Professor Kim is very nice and smart. However, his grading scheme sucks for such a difficult class. He is adjusting the grading scheme throughout the semester to accommodate, and I am sure he wants his students to succeed, but it is tragic we are being used as guinea pigs for such a disorganized class at the expense of our mental health.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a weed out course, but there is a difference between difficult and down right impossible. No amount of studying is enough to prepare for content beyond the scope of the course. With each exam weighing 20%, averages should not be a 50 on exam 1 and a 30 on exam 2... Only giving a 2 since he's offering remediation and changes for exam 3.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Kim is exceptionally knowledgeable and genuinely cares about his students. His lecture notes are highly informative and clearly reflect the significant effort he puts into preparing them. The exams are manageable and inspiring. He is also very good at answering questions and always willing to help. I would highly recommend taking his class.
Guys! The class average for the second exam was a 31 OUT OF 110 with the highest grade as an 82. I don't know why we're suddenly rating him high?!?!?
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Despite his sternness and high expectations, Justin Kim is a hardworking professor. During class he always makes sure to point out a few test-relevant mechanisms and even adds some nerdy humor. His exams are rigorous but fair... Orgo 2 is a weed-out course. If you read the book when concepts aren't clear, you'll be just fine.

While this professor is extremely difficult and expects a lot of us, I appreciate his ability to take feedback and adjust the course to help. The first two tests have been pretty bad, but he created a method of remediation to get points back. I do believe his expectations are too high but if he continues to adjust I think we can finish strong.

Good lecturer, smart guy. He has bad ratings because the first two exams were way too hard, but hes super receptive to feedback and has altered the course structure multiple times to help us now. Hes a new prof learning what works and adjusting accordingly, I think hes okay now because hes new but will be better in future, again, very receptive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For your mental health, gpa, and overall standard of living, just don't take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
What can I even say?

Much more difficult/less forgiving than other Orgo II professors here. 85 percent of the grade is made up of tests, whose difficulty is off the charts. Unforgiving exam structure, and despite revisions being offered, it doesn't change the class's structure.

If you value your anxiety meds and hairline, don't take this class.

Complete lack of teaching ability and an even more extreme gap between what he believes he is teaching and the content that appears on the exam. Don't even think about taking his section, and don't be fooled by the possibility of remediation, even if the other options don't have stellar reviews. Free yourself.

I've never studied harder for a class, yet I—and the majority—failed both exams. Its heartbreaking to see that no matter how much energy and effort goes into this class, Dr. Kim has zero sense of what is an appropriate difficulty level and is turning students bitter and discouraged. I did every practice problem available and still couldn't finish.

this class actually exceeded the limits of my anxiety medication. Ochem 1 class was less work and I took the  self-study course. I show up to lecture to not be able to hear him or read his handwriting just to get questions on the exam that I have never seen before in lecture or in the textbook HELLO???
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Whoever moderates this site needs to think about life and get an actual job instead of defending Big Kim.
sad sad sad

Tests are impossible. Actually IMPOSSIBLE. You can study all you want; you'll still hand in the test blank (that's how impossible it is). Yes, Orgo 2 is a known hard class, but the other Orgo 2 classes' students are doing just fine. So clearly, this is not to blame on the rigor of the course, but on the instructor teaching the course!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
i just ran out of antidepressants
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had to withdraw from this class. He is one of the worst professors at Tech and needs to be fired. Many students complain about his volume, handwriting, and the difficulty of exams, but he doesn't care. Professor Kim doesn't care about students' success and doesn't take criticism well. The class average was a 51 on the first exam.
this is just sad.

I need to point this out: this man decided to make the class only 85% exams and 15% homework even though he had FULL ABILITY to change that grading scheme. And why did he decide to keep it this way and why did he make his exams nearly impossible for his students so they could be in tears when handing in their exams? Because he simply doesn't care.

He thinks he's the best and smartest professor, but his handwriting is illegible , gives hard exams even though I averaged 3 hours of sleep each night because I'm studying, not really helpful, doesn't take criticism and requests.

He's a nice dude, would be great for grad students who already know the material. With 85% of your grade being exams, and 15% being accuracy based problem sets, there is no padding to your grade. Exams are extremely difficult and at a level of difficulty that should have a crib sheet and are not representative of resources given in class.

The exams are unfair. The lectures are not worth going to because they don't relate to the exam content and the professors hand writing is not legible. The professor has these handouts that he claims are the greatest thing since slice bread, however the professors hand writing is unreadable.

Do not take this professor. Exams were unreasonable and an incredibly high portion of the grade. I studied for over 30 hours for the most recent exam and left with half the problems blank. He is not an enjoyable professor to have, and I would not recommend him in any form or fashion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very unfair exams, not like review materials
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think Dr. Kim forgets that we're learning new material for the 1st time, with our previous knowledge of Chem 2311 being so far back. No amount of feedback and critiques would ever change his mind because of his ego. Apparently he went to prestigious colleges, so he thinks he's the smartest and greatest of mankind. He's not! Opposite actually.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Kim's exams felt significantly harder than the practice materials, making it difficult to prepare effectively. After the first exam, where the class average was very low, the review session felt somewhat tense and not very supportive. I believe when more than 115 students are below a 50, we must reconsider our methods.

I did every single practice problem available (400+ online WileyPlus questions), textbook problems, practice tests, PLUS session practice problems, problem sets, material review, and STILL did not recognize anything on the exam. Miserable experience, I would not take this prof if you can avoid it. I will probably end up dropping this class.

(in-person).This professor does not know how to lecture. Constant complaints about his volume, teaching style, and messy handwriting. Exams are difficult and he's not forgiving. He needs to be reported to the dean for how he is lecturing the course and grading. Entirely self study, but if I wanted self study, I would have chosen an online class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you keep up with the reading and pop into class every once in a while the tests are more than manageable. The lectures are engaging, and while the course is a survey and cannot cover every topic in as much depth as I would have liked, he clearly cares, just respect his time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I honestly don't get the negative reviews for this professor. The quizzes are EXTREMELY easy and the tests aren't too bad either, as long as you study at least a little bit. He is very passionate and an entertaining lecturer. The books that we were assigned are really good and they inspired me to get into more nonfiction!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He assigns a lot of reading (3 books in a semester), and grades based off of exams and quizzes only. He frequently calls out individual students (usually if they're talking or on their phone) in front of the whole class. He seems passionate about history, but I am uncomfortable with him.

Going into the class I thought it would be manageable. Couldn't be farther from the truth. This class is extremely hard because there are no study guides/review for tests and you have to just go based on what he teaches in lecture (random facts not related to the main ideas). You'll end up studying for something that won't even show up on the test.

Dr. Smith made this class enjoyable & the lectures were engaging & interesting. It's important to take good notes during the video lectures as they have little/no words. The assignments he gave were easy to read & the questions are straightforward. He grades pretty fairly & gives feedback. Exams are fine as long as you take notes & do the readings.

I've had two classes with Dr. Smith and he's amazing. Kind, funny, insightful and an enrapturing storyteller. It's true there is no wasted moment in his class, everything is worth knowing and may be tested on. You can't skate by, you have to be interested and invested, but in his defense, Dr. Smith makes it easy to be both. Can't recommend enough!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Smith was a very passionate lecturer. However, he was not a good lecturer for me. He liked to lecture in the form of storytelling, which made it difficult to know what needed to be known for the tests. He also talks very quickly, making it difficult to take notes at times. This class shouldn't have been as difficult as it was.

Dr. Smith is the best lecturer I have ever had. He cares deeply about the content and his students, throws in jokes for his lectures, and makes the lectures engaging. The other comments about having to study obscene amounts to get an A aren't entirely true. If you show up to class and study ~2 hours a week, you will easily get an A.

Smith was very caring and super nice throughout the whole semester. He is always willing to answer questions during lecture. But, lectures can be somewhat painful to sit through even though you can tell he is passionate about the subject. You do have to really pay attention, as the only grades are 4-5 quizzes, 3 exams, and the final
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just don't do it. Everyone here is right. Unless you want to put in more time studying for HISTORY than your STEM classes... If you do decide to not take my advice just withdraw while you still have the chance. Stay blessed.

You have to work to get a good grade in the class.  There were weekly written responses which were actually graded pretty harshly, and you did not have much time for them.  There were reading almost everyday which had content that would be on the test.

Do not take this class if you want an easy A. Your grade is only based on 3 (tough) tests and 5 quizzes, and no extra credit. There is no textbook and his slides are extremely vague, so you need to pay attention in class. On the bright side, he is an engaging professor. Also his political views show up in lecture a lot so prepare for that.

The only things that make up your grade in this class are 3 tests and 5 quizzes. Getting just 1 question wrong means your overall grade drops by 0.6%, and the questions are very niche. He did gives us extra credit but only because he was sick for most of the semester. A great professor, and a great story teller, but not an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is a great lecturer but his tests are extremely specific and it's very hard to do well. Your entire grade depends on 3 tests and 5 quizzes, so if you mess up once you aren't getting a good grade. Sad because this is my favorite class  but my worst grade and I am a STEM student. If you want an easy A, don't take this class. No extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am crying in frustration and laughing at the audacity... Why am I putting more work into this class than my STEM classes - let me remind you this is GT - and STILL getting worse grades? 3 tests make up 90% (!!!) of your grade. No study guides, no notes, no extra credit. Impossible to succeed. Wanna pass? Memorize every word he says. Good luck LOL
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. I wish I could go back & drop this class. 3 tests = 90% of your grade, 5 quizzes = last 10%. Tests & quizzes were ridiculously niche & specific details. He wants you to memorize every word he says. No written notes anywhere. No EC. Everything is MC & confusingly worded like trick questions. Not set up for success whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Smith cared a lot about the content that he taught, and truly inspired students to take a passion to history. His lectures consisted of discussions of the content, so while not necessary, is beneficial to getting a good grade in the class. His tests can be a bit difficult, but if you put in the work necessary you will do fine.

Be prepared to memorize absolutely everything Prof. Smith says. His tests are ridiculously specific, you have to have his lecture memorized and he sometimes puts things in the tests that he didn't even say. The entire grade depends on 3 tests and 5 quizzes, which are all extremely hard. I had a terrible time, don't take this class if u want an A.

Only three tests are given, which your grade depends on. Every single word he says in the lecture should be memorized, as well as every reading given, which are all stupid things that do not lead to an overall understanding of history at all. Irrelevant content, irrelevant class, terrible grade for a humanity.

Prof. Smiths class is extremely test heavy. The tests are 50 questions, 50 minutes, and the questions are incredibly hard. His lectures have practically no words so you basically have to write down every thing he says because his test are very specific. Your entire grade depends on quizzes and tests. Way too hard for a humanity.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Smith is a great teacher and very passionate about what he does. However his class structure is archaic. You have little to no wiggle room time wise during the exams, the lecture slides have almost 0 words on them so you need to take detailed notes, and there is no opportunity for bonus points. Tough class for a humanity.

This is not the class to take if youre looking for an easy A. Although hes very intelligent and his lectures are very good, his grading scale for this class is quite egregious. Be prepared to study hard for exams in this class if you want to finish with an A. Theres easier classes to take for your legislative credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Smith was caring and willing to help me, but even when I put in the work and had a tutor I was still unsuccessful. He does not allow for any type of grade bump or extra credit so you get what you get. I would not take this class again, it was too tedious and unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: An overall great professor. I came into the class expecting to be bored, but he made every lecture quite interesting. Good listening/notes are extremely important, as unwritten lecture content will be on quizzes/exams. Review notes from time to time in case of pop quizzes, which are very short and specific. Everything from lecture is worth knowing.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The best story teller ever

Professor Smith was a great professor. He acknowledges that every student has a different background in history. His lectures were engaging and it felt like listening to a storyteller. However, he also has a good control over the class. There is no "textbook", just required readings, which saves you money.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: can't stress enough how lecture heavy this class is and people still skipped bc attendance wasnt mandatory. The tests and pop quizzes are not hard if you pay attention & take good notes on every lecture. He does talk somewhat fast to cover the content, but he makes his lectures storylike and very interesting (first history class I've EVER enjoyed)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Theres no textbook so if you miss a lecture youre kinda screwed. Theres also pop quizzes that you cant make up. Tests are multiple choice and pretty straight forward. The hard part is he says so much information that anything could be a question. It was hard for me to write everything and remember everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: For a class about a decently boring subject his lectures were SO interesting. He was really fun to listen to however it is a ton of information. We had to read his own book for the class but it was super interesting. As long as you come to class (pop quizzes) and stay up on reading its a fun class. Still kinda hard tho tbh

Professor Smith was a great story teller. He made history interesting. Be ready to write though because he speaks SO fast!! Would still take him again because he is a super nice person and I actually enjoyed history with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Reading is not from a textbook, but from other books (based on this year) which are on tests. Lectures are great and tests are not too hard if you study.

The only class I truly looked forward to this semester. His lectures are amazing. I leave each time feeling like I just gained a new prospective to life. Take good notes in class, and study them right before the exam and you'll do fine. There are books you will have to read. This class is graded by 6 things, so each one counts. Don't slack off.

Dr. Smith is a great guy and a great lecturer. You can tell he really loves teaching the material and his lectures are always interesting and engaging. Always available outside of class to review the concepts, ask questions, or just talk. Go to class and read the books and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr Johnny Smith is one of the best professors at GT. Do what he says, which is read your books, and take good lecture notes, and voila! You will probably be on your way to an enjoyable history class and a comfortable grade. Lectures are very entertaining and informative. Paper notes only, but this is no biggie. He loves to talk after class as well.
John Smith is a great guy and great professor. He really knows his stuff and truly cares about his students. Also, his tests are pretty easy which is a plus and no papers!!!

Definitely the best professor I have had at Tech, and definitely my favorite. He is a really great guy and easy to get along with and have conversations with. In fact, I still keep in touch with him and will be taking another class with him. I hated History in high school but I loved this class and really enjoyed his lectures and teaching style.

Dr Smith has been my favorite professor so far at Tech, even though I'm not a huge fan of history.  It is clear that he loves his job and the material he is teaching.  He and the TA's will be explicitly clear about what you need to do for an A, you just may need to ask them out side of class time.  Test are non cumulative and easy.

I've always hated learning about history, but his enthusiasm made history bearable! You can hear excitement in his voice when he lectures (even though it was a morning class) and he's very willing to help you if you're struggling!

He's an awesome guy. His lectures are actually entertaining to listen to, and his quizzes are 2 questions long and only cover info from the previous lecture. His tests are 25 MC and 1 essay on a historical novel he assigns. The readings are actually really interesting, and you MUST read the books to do well on the essays. Final is not cumulative.

No Homework, Short Quizzes on previous lecture (was to my detriment), you will know exactly what to expect. His TA's can be tough graders on the Essay portion of the Tests which are on Historial Novels you NEED to read. Final is not Cumulative!!!

Loved his lectures. You can tell he really loves what he is teaching. Although he spoke really quickly, he would slow down if you asked him. He was very funny and friendly. As long as you attend class and pay attention, you can easily get an A.
Professor Stroud is a decent professor, but the exams are graded so much harder than needed. You have to give the exact answers he is looking for and the exams are weighted a lot.
Grade is composed mostly of exams. Exams are graded so harshly and there is no cushioning.

Super engaging professor and talks a lot about his own research and other research at Tech. As long as you can validly explain your answer you'll get credit. In-class activities are really helpful for test-prep, and he drops 6 (so you can miss 6 free classes). Grading scheme is pretty test-heavy, but the tests are all written so grading is fair.

Professor is really nice and cares a lot about the students. He also does not accept any bs from his students and believes you should put in 110% work. He cares A LOT about ecology and genuienly passionate about his work. He is tough grader and he looks very specific answers which is sometimes difficult to figure out during a test.
Nobody is excited to attend an Ethics course, however Kirkman does a great job making his lectures interesting. Writing isn't too hard and neither are the exams. Overall a solid ethics class
Should be a free class but makes it way harder then it should be. His grading scale made no sense.

Only grades for the semester are weekly essays and a final project. He gives lots of feedback on the essays which sometimes is super harsh. Classes were him talking about the assigned readings with no slides or other material, he just talks at you for 75 minutes. He was very friendly and the class didn't demand too much, overall a good class.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He gives you a lot to read, a lot to write, and can sometimes feel like he's harping with his feedback and unwilling to just say "Good job". But he does actually care- if you talk to him just a bit outside of class, do all of your work (as tedious as it may be), and take his feedback seriously, you can almost guarantee an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: 3109 online meets MW for 50 minutes, discussing ethical topics, these meetings are not bad and you don't have to participate.  Friday discussions are on case studies where you can discuss and debate an ethical dilemma from an engineer.  If you get a good TA, this class can be great
Very unclear expectations of the final project, basically just lectures the whole entire class with no slide show, so he's just talking at you the whole class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I hated participating in this class as his responses to any thoughts were usually critical. Grading is extremely unclear, leaving you unsure of where you stand in the class. Very tough grader when it came to the weekly commentaries.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class GPA is high, I feel like it would be easy to get an A if you put in the effort he asks. That being said, the final project effectively determines your grade, and this is frustrating because you need a perfect score (no partial credit) and everyone knows how bad group projects are at Tech. Easy class but stressful if you don't like risk.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Kirkman talked a lot during lecture. He was clearly passionate about the subject (and a lot of other subjects too), but in an 8 am class it was kind of grating. Definitely agree with a lot of others here about unclear expectations regarding grading and what the final project even was. LOTS of reading, but overall it's fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Kirkman is incredibly knowledgeable and leads great conversations. But the course design and structure is imprecise. He does "ungrading", which alleviates stress, but makes the grading criteria unclear. The learning outcomes are vague, and he does not hold back on feedback, but he does care and is open to criticism.

Dr. Kirkman is a great choice for this course. This semester he operated on a principle of self tracking your progress throughout the course and then discussing with him at the end of the semester what grade you think you deserve based on participation, what you learned, etc. Don't know if it will always be like this, but it was this semester.

I took 3109 with Prof. Kirkman in the summer. In this class you need: 1. Use 4050 minutes read the materials that he asks for, write a short essay (about 300 words is enough) every week. 2. post three discussions ( pretty simple and easy) every week. 3. A friendly final project. Hes a nice grader overall and class is easy for CS and Engi student
Grading criteria purposefully confusing. Take a different humanities if you can. You can get a good grade, but you won't learn anything and you'll leave with a bad taste in your mouth.

Kirkman is hard but fair.  The readings and weekly assignments can become cumbersome if you have a lot going on.  Great attendance isn't a necessity, but you can get a lot out of the lectures if you do attend regularly and pay attention.
Weekly Writing assignments get to be a bore.  He grades hard, TAs grade easy.  Attendance is not necessary.

Preaches about how much he hates "death by powerpoint" and then lectures directly from slides posted online. Easy B. Really really difficult A. Just hope that he doesn't grade any of your tests or papers and lets the TA's do it.

Easy class. Rather dry lectures. Attendance is NOT necessary at all. Midterm exam and final exam are literally same format, same weight, same grading scale. TA's grade most papers and grade really easily. If he grades your paper, watch out, he'll tear it up and ruin your chance at an A.
Super sweet and great with communication. Clear grading criteria. Super passionate and in-class participation are relatively easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: she def cares and is very accessible for help outside of the class. she does truly want her students to succeed and structures 3003 highly around getting feedback. good lecturer, boring topic. the tests in this course are a bit tough but the grading scheme allows for leniency. can average B on tests and a B on the term paper for an A.

Dr. McCann is by far one of the best professors I have ever had at this school. She is kind, knowledgeable, & very passionate about what she teaches!! I would take as many courses as I could with this professor since I not only feel like I learned a significant amount, but also enjoyed this course so much! Also I took 3003 with her, not 3001.
Very caring professor who really cares about you. Tests can be tricky if you don't come to class and pay attention to what she verbally says. Also, I took 3003 with her not 3001.

Very kind and understanding, I had her for 2001 and 3003 - she teaches well and seems to genuinely care. Class structures for both were Not The Best, but I dont think that's on her. Out of any of the neuro teachers she co-taught with, she explained things the best, if not a little fast though. Highly recommend taking her classes.

there were readings before EVERY CLASS and major assignments due the same week as major exams. She co-teaches with Holder so she's better in comparison to her but the class can be very heavy and the tests are sometimes unnecessarily difficult with very particular grading. She wants her students to succeed (i think..). No final, term paper instead.

Out of the 3 NEUR 2001 professors, she was the best. Her lectures were engaging and interesting and she made sure that we understood all of the information. The unit 3 midterm (the unit she taught) was extremely straightforward and easy, especially compared to the other 2 tests. Overall amazing professor.

Truly Incredible. Your grade is almost entirely decided by your effort, poor exam performance if often recoverable due to generous grading, extra credit, projects, attendance, etc. Difficult material but Dr. K is masterful. Homework will take a large amount of time but is really rewarding and extremely useful.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The best professor, creates such a safe space for learning. Sriram's care for the subject and his students shines through in his engaging lectures and flexible class structure. HWs take a long time and exams are difficult, but you learn extremely relevant skills. Super smart, pick his brain, go to OH, and you will come out knowing so much more.

Genuinely might be the best professor at Tech. Incredibly smart, amazing lectures, interesting office hours, great grading policy. Your grade is based on the effort you put in. If you want to actually learn, take him. Reconsider which classes you want to take purely to get Sriram. 85% of the knowledge I have actually retained came from his classes.

Aero may be hard, but Sriram makes up for it by being one of the best profs in the AE department. Super accessible outside of class, great lecturer, and cares about the students (he's one of us). If you ever have the chance of taking a class with him or meeting him, take it. You won't regret it.
Wanna learn aerodynamics at GTAE? Sriram. Hotel? Trivago.
simply the goat

CFD with prof. Kalathoor was a great experience. Exams were certainly tough but fair, provided you studied the content properly, and homework assignments were definitely on the longer side. The project was a big time sink but very rewarding once the simulations finally gave realistic solutions. Highly recommend, he was a great lecturer and resource

Put plainly, SK the best the AE department has to offer. He wants to see you succeed and actually learn something. Super accessible. Always answered emails. Super understanding and willing to work around tough situations. Great lecturer. Super interesting guy. Just overall amazing. Best instructor I have ever encountered at Tech.

Dr.  Kalathoor is a very knowledgeable and inspiring teacher. He genuinely cares about the success of students and is pretty much accessible outside the class. Textbook was not required. He provides everything you may need to get an A. There was 3 HWs and 3 exams and a project for extra credit.

Took him without knowing what I signed up for and I am so insanely happy that I did. Kalathoor might be the most caring and involved instructor I have ever had and that is no small feat. He made 3030 enjoyable, engaging, and informative without ever sacrificing the student experience. Class was at 5:00-7:00pm and I never  once wanted to skip it.
Lots of extra credit, amazing lectures, very approacheable, posts everything you need to know. Highly recommended.

Sriram is an awesome professor!! He's such a loving guy and cares so much about his class, he essentially wrote his entire own textbook for us. He gives lots of EC (it amounted to 15% overall course EC), had no final and in its place a fun, free-range final project. Really knowledgeable professor and allows an exam dropped and one regraded.

For reference, I took this class in Spring 2024 - her first class. She was incredibly nice and explained topics well when I reached out for help. She moves really fast in lecture but she does give practice exams which are helpful and representative. This was probably the easiest Chem class I've taken at GT so far and I'm not that smart.

Dr. Kim is a nice professor. But she reads off slides during lecture and makes attendance mandatory for in class problems.  Her tests are similar to the practice and recitation problems, so just study those. She gives extra buffer points on tests. The final was so much harder than all of the tests, but she lowered the grade boundary, thankfully.

She is very nice professor, but her lectures are awful because she makes many mistakes and is very hard to understand at times. The only reason to go to the lecture is to do the mandatory in class problems.

The best way to succeed would study by yourself and go to recitation.

Also her tests will have many errors, so ask questions during testing.

Be prepared to have the slides read straight to you every single class. There is no point in showing up for class at all except for the fact that an in-class problem, for what you literally just learned. The final was 33% of the grade and half of the material wasn't even gone over. Emails are hardly even answered.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Kim's lectures were sometimes a little confusing but she was very nice and gave bonus points on exams. Additionally, she gave lots of extra credit and even lowered the grade boundaries.

Dr. Lieberman isn't the most engaging lecturer, but her lecture videos get all the information you need across and her tests were very easy and fair. The flipped classroom is not as bad as the other comments say. Other professors might be better, but if you take it with Lieberman you have nothing to worry about.

flipped classroom is terrible. you have to learn everything alone and the videos offered are so terrible. I had to watch another random professor on youtube to learn anything. she sounds so uninterested in what she is teaching and sounds like she wants to be there less than you want to be. DO NOT RECOMMEND BIOCHEM WITH HER!!! TAKE WITH SOMEONE ELSE

Dr. Lieberman is an amazing professor! She's funny and knowledgeable. Bchem-I is hard to grasp and master, but her flipped classroom helped take time to learn content outside class and address all concerns in class. You also see real life application in class through group activities. If you put in effort, you will get so much out of this class!

Was not considerate and many times showed video lectures of herself during in-person lectures rather than teach. On the rare occasion that she taught, she was condescending to students who asked questions about course material. Her exams were fair, except for the 3rd exam that was made more difficult because too many people were doing well.

The tests are fairly difficult but you can pass if you really study. The homework though almost had nothing to do with the test. Also she was also not very considerate of students who were struggling in the class and she was not lenient if any problems arose even technical difficulties.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have had at tech. Does not know how to use technology. Her test are too difficult for the time given. Would not recommend taking.
