reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Lieberman is amazing! She is humorous and fun and makes class exciting. The only drawback is that some of her tests may be difficult, but the lowest test grade is dropped :)

Dr. Lieberman is the quintessential example of a professor who is only here for research. She does not really care about the students and does not lecture well. Lectures often focus on topics nothing to do with exams, and homework covers topics not discussed in lecture. To survive you must memorize the textbook. Worst class I've taken at Tech. 0/10
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She assigns a lot of in-class busy work/small assignments, and didn't always spend much lecture time teaching/explaining actual content. Her tone can be a bit off-putting at time, especially if she thinks it's something you SHOULD know (i.e. doesn't consider that you might've forgotten things you learned in other classes).

Her tests and quizzes are decent if you study really well, though there were some questions that came out of nowhere. She's kind of condescending in office hours and so was the TA (both unhelpful) so find a good study group. Overall good course, informative, interesting lectures. Don't slack, study hard, and this course will be easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Her tests and quizzes aren't bad, as long as you study and understand the material. I liked her lectures, not the most boring professor. However, she does have an attitude when she feels challenged by students. So don't use your phone or turn over a test or quiz paper unless you want to be scolded in front of the whole class. You've been warned.
The TAs grade the tests unjustly taking points off for no reason…
This class is very fast paced and not to mention, the free response on the exams are difficult and long. You basically have to study by yourself, the textbook helps alot.
dont take her class tests are really heavy on material with no cushioning at all.

The most important thing to do is to read and take notes on the textbook, as her lectures are basically regurgitating that. You can get around the participation by doing the learning catalytics from home; going to the lecture isn't necessary as long as you read the textbook. The tests can be difficult, but reading the textbook helps.

Her tests are so hard, and she barely gives us any grace on the exams. The wording of the exam questions are so wordy and difficult, and doesn't reflect anything she teaches in class. Very dissapointed..

The lectures don't help. And the Tests do not reflect what is taught or even the information on the textbook. Her test are worded so badly its like she wants to fail you. And not enough time on exmas..... DO NOT TAKE THE CLASS.
Her lectures covered all the material needed and made sense. The exams were not too difficult but sometimes she covered material very quickly in class so it made it difficult to follow.
Already a week into this class the amount of busy work is insane.

She's very sweet and it is clear she's passionate, her lectures are just not engaging at all. I have no clue how I passed this class. I went to her office hours and she was definitely very helpful there!

Talks way too fast, and there is so much content. Assignments every week that were essentially busy work, most of them unrelated to biology. Lots of unnecessary information in lectures as well, like long case studies that were never on exams. Need to know essentially all content in almost perfect detail to apply to difficult exam questions.

Took for cellular and molecular biology lab. Poor grading criteria and a lot of work. Even the TAs would complain about how much work they had to put in. She also did not follow teh syllabus and make pre lab quizzes for completion like she said she would.

Dr. Kerr is an extremely passionate and excellent teacher. I am not a bio major and did pretty bad in this class, and while I did not enjoy it too much, Dr. Kerr and Dr. Smith's excitement made the class enjoyable. Definitely go into class and with enough sleep though, as I blame my failure on poor sleep, bad studying habits, and lack of passion.

Lectures are pointless as they don't encompass the whole textbook and you are tested on the textbook material. There is a writing assignment every week that does not reinforce material. However, Dr. Kerr is very good at explaining material and answering questions. Also, Dr. Kerr gives a lot of good study material to use before each exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: SHES AWESOME, prob best professor u can get. very good at explaining topics and super approachable. only downfall is that there is a lot of material in this class. its not her fault but just a lot of content

Dr. Kerr and Dr. Smith split the lecture material, and both did an amazing job explaining the content! Dr. Kerr is super sweet and she answers questions really thoroughly! She believes 1107 works best if students read the textbook and take notes before class, then strengthen their understanding by attending lecture and asking questions.

She talks fast in class but it's all very understandable. You can tell she knows what she's talking about. I think shes a great teacher and super easy to reach for help if you're confused. Shes very kind.

Truly surprised that Dr. Kerr does not have a higher rating on this website. She is one of the kindest profs at GT and a clear lecturer. Like any intro bio, this class has a lot of content and requires a good bit of effort. But she is a passionate and willing to answer any question w/o making a student feel small for asking. Literally my queen.

some assignments are completely unrelated to biology. Like why am I learning about cornell notes if I'm not going to use them? She talks really fast in the lecture as well, so u should read the material beforehand.

Dr. Kerr is an amazing teacher. She very clearly cares about what she is teaching and is always ready to help during office hours (very accessible outside of this too). Also, there are a lot of good study resources available that make the tests pretty easy.

Dr. Kerr truly cares about her students, and this is clearly shown through her eagerness to teach and her transparent expectations/grading. At times, she does go a little fast during lectures but all of the content is pulled from the textbooks and is clarified in the PowerPoints posted!

It's very clear that Dr. Kerr wants her students to get As in the class. There's A LOT of content in the class, so her lectures are very fast-paced, but she does a very good job covering it. She's clear with what she expects from you and what you need to do to be successful in the class. When she tells you to use something to study, USE IT.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Kerr is a nice person, but she goes very fast during lectures. This is probably because the amount of information in this class is extremely extensive, so the textbook is mandatory to keep up. The tests are fairly straightforward, but because of the amount of content, the questions are quite specific. Thankfully, there is in-built extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Kerr's lectures are really fast, but if you read the assigned textbook reading and take notes on it beforehand, you're well prepared to understand what's going on in lecture. The written homework assignments might feel pointless, but if you do well on them then you have a good grade boost and don't have to worry about test scores as much.

I really enjoyed Dr. Kerr's lectures. At the beginning, it was hard to keep up because she talked so fast, but after the first unit or two you get the hang of it. Read and take notes on the textbook before class even though it's incredibly dense, otherwise you will be lost. Exams were fairly easy if you've been keeping up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While her lectures are very fast-paced, if you do the notes before class and keep up with the content, you will be successful. She cares about her students, and is very approachable during her office hours. She includes a lot of wiggle room in the grading system, so it is easy to get an A in the class.

She goes so fast you cannot possibly take notes, and doesn't explain things well. She doesnt take time on the parts that are the most confusing, and goes on long tangents about stuff that isnt relevant. There are assignments unrelated to the content are harshly graded, and take up time. During office hours she is condescending and confusing.

Wonderful professor. I knew nothing about biology coming in and still managed to pull a good grade. She explains things perfectly! There is a lot of reading and assignments to do, and the writing assignments can be tedious, but overall definitely worth it. Participation is the main grading criteria which was also great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very nice, but spoke very quickly during lectures. Easy to access outside of class but a majority of the class is mainly based on the online textbook, so I would just say to rely on the textbook and actually understand the material. Lectures were semi helpful but relying on the lectures alone will not guide you to an A
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is a decent lecturer but make sure to read the online textbook before class. She spoke super fast, making it hard to understand her at times. Nice but the lectures are REALLY dry. It was hard staying awake at times. I would say that the tests are fair, just make sure to read the online textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, I like the way this course was structured. At the beginning it was very difficult to figure out what they wanted you to know, however, as the semester progresses you begin to understand how to study and what is expected of you. Professor Shana spoke way too fast and when she taught me and my fellow peers did not understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very passionate about biology. She gives great lectures, however talks extremely fast to the point where I would often have to consult the powerpoints outside of class because she talked faster than I could type. She gives 1 second for group discussions (not an exaggeration). Extremely lecture heavy & attendance matters. Overall, a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Passive aggressive if the class don't know a slight little detail.Her content was really hard and her explanations was basically repeating the same thing from the lecture or textbook. Exams are so hard and almost impossible to pass and the final was also catastrophic; 70 questions and probably only 20 of them were from the semester's content. Avoid

In-class assignments show little relevance to biology, existing more for political reasons than for improving your education. Assignments are then graded by TAs who lack proper oversight and take off for the smallest reasons. The exams poorly represent topics, and the final lacks structure and coherence. Poor communication of expectations.

She is very sweet and works well with students. You will have to go to lecture to participate in the in class assignments which can open at different times during lecture. You are given an online textbook read which I would recommend actually reading because it helps with the class content which there is a lot of.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's a very sweet and caring professor that wants everyone to succeed in the class. 100% recommend. As long as you read the online textbook and take notes on what you read, you should be fine ! Also the homework and in class activities are very helpful and graded based on participation, not accuracy.

BIOS 1208 is very very content-heavy, but Dr. Kerr makes it doable. I'd recommend either doing the readings OR going to lecture, as the two are pretty much the exact same, and it's super repetitive. Grading is super kind as exams are worth such a small portion of your grade. Just put in the effort and you will do well in this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: lecture just goes more in depth on reading u need to do before class. just review recitation slides and LC questions, and you'll do great on exams. in 1208, we were allowed a notecard with notes on each exam. dr. kerr is very kind and is clearly passionate about biology! she truly wants you to learn biology, and her course is relatively stress-free
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Kerr was a very engaging and thorough lecturer and was responsive to feedback. The flipped classroom style was very effective for me and this should be an relatively easy class if you do the readings, which there can be a LOT of. Try to stay ahead early on because the last few midterms are tougher.

Her lecturing was pretty clear and interesting. Reverse classroom structure, but still taught in class so it was redundant. Unnecessary writing assignments. Content was very easy first half, but hard second half. In class participation, but grades participation and HW based on completion. Grading system makes it easy to get a good grade.

This class was incredibly reliant on the textbook, which was dense and hard to get through at times. As this was a flipped classroom model, Dr. Kerr usually brushed over topics in class and focused on the more "difficult" topics, which only helpful at times. The grading scale was incredibly helpful, and so were the recitations.

It is pretty easy to make an A and the class is not too much work. One thing to note is that there is quite a lot of at-home reading assigned. You can get by without doing the reading but your life would be a lot less stressful if you just did the reading.

Her lectures are very quick and information-dense, but ultimately not necessary because of the flipped classroom model and in-class participation questions you can access from anywhere. The class is easy if you read the textbook and watch videos. The tests are similar to the practice tests. Grading scheme is very forgiving.

Dr. Kerr personally is very kind and passionate about biology. This class is not hard necessarily, but is a lot of textbook reading, writing assignments, and learning catalytics work. I did not attend lecture as pretty much everything covered was in the textbook/IKES/TICAS. Test scores averaged around a 75 and participation points are easy to get.

Dr. Kerr is a great organismal professor. Syllabus lays out grading clearly and writing assignments are built in to give students wiggle room. Exams are easy given you have a rudimentary understanding of class content. Textbook is a lifesaver. Readings are dense but skimming and attending class will get you a high A. Accessible and values feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Kerr is a sweet professor, but I thought the pace she went at for lecture was ridiculously quick given how dense/much material there was to cover. Fair amount of busy work, and the questions from the exams were sometimes on the most trivial little detail that did not stand out as important. The textbook is your best friend for this class.

Dr. Kerr is a respectable and caring professor. I personally didn't like how the course was delivered (textbook heavy and sometimes 1-2 hours for each assigned reading lecture as a refresher) but I think the course is fair if you do all the readings and maximize participation (easy points), you can get an A in the class since exams are open note.

Best lecturer I've had at this school thus far. Super clear and concise instruction even though she covers a lot of dense material. She's super approachable and cares a lot about student success and learning. Only downside is the class has a lot of busy work and requires a decent time investment outside of lecture
Lectures were very heavy and lots of material was covered so get ready to memorize but Dr. Kerr is a very kind professor who definitely cares about the class and her students.

Dr. Kerr is a really nice professor and she cares about her students. She makes changes to the class based on feedback which is awesome. Lectures pretty fast. Make sure u do the Learning Catalytics. The textbook is free & online but u have to pay for access to LC. She makes the class so that participation matters more than ur test performances!

Dr. Kerr teaches fast. Really fast. Her lectures move so quickly that I didn't take notes. You'll have to read the "online textbook" - it's free and not official, so don't worry about cost. She's very nice and passionate about biology, and the tests are straightforward (and honestly not that hard). No quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great teacher. No pop quizzes, but sometimes the textbook (put together by her) did not cover the in-class material. Knew what she was doing but would go on tangents at times. Sweet, but a LOT of work. Participation in classes counts and if you don't take notes before lecture from textbook, good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's a caring prof, but the way the class is structured makes it super contentheavy. I regularly spent 15+ hours study for each exam (there are 4 plus 1 final). Bio lab is also really time consuming. I never went to lecture, but learned from the textbook. Concepts aren't hard, just the sheer amount of material. There is 6 pts extra credit though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She was passionate and cared about her students.

If you are choosing between taking bio or taking eas, take eas. This class is stupid content heavy and so much memorization is involved. Dr Kerr is really nice and she really cares but this class is a ton of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Kerr is really knowledgeable about what she's teaching, and her enthusiasm comes across. She does talk fast, but it wasn't to the point of not being understandable. She expects a lot of participation from the class, but as long as you do the reading and participation assignments and come to class, you should be fine.

She is clearly very interested in Biology and wants her students to succeed. It can a lot of work, but go to every class, do all the homework, and study using the learning objectives and you can get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: People give Kerr a hard time because they don't get the best grades with her. She knows and loves what she talks about. Learn and study with her learning objectives and you'll get a B at least on the tests. Very clear lectures, so use them to study, and you're pretty much golden.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Reasonable, nice, and cares about your success. Class consists purely of lectures, so come to class having read the assigned materials and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Kerr is an approachable professor and enthusiastic about the subject. She goes a bit fast in class but is willing to explain more in office hours. Her style of teaching is half lecture half group activities/questions.

Kerr seems approachable and nice when you first start out, but it is quite the opposite! She talks faster in her lectures than any human should ever be able to speak. Be prepared to "infer" (her words) what parts of the book you should be reading because the readings don't match the homework or the lectures and of course not the test.

For me, Dr Kerr does not seem to grasp what she is talking about or communicate it very well. Maybe she has something going on elsewhere in her life but I have found her to be inarticulate and not especially helpful. Maybe it will improve... Here's hoping!

She speaks fast in her lectures and didn't go as in depth on some topics as I would've liked. She very much expects you to come to class having read the blog and the textbook. Her tests aren't too bad if you put the work into the class and go over learningcatalytics sessions!

You  need to go to class. The PowerPoints have little text, and the book doesn't always cover everything you're expected to know (like in-class examples). That said, Dr. Kerr is a very dynamic and engaging lecturer. I didn't reach out for one-on-one help, but she answered the questions I did have fully and respectfully.

I saw the other rating, and it's accurate. She appears nice and approachable but when contacted one-on-one does not care about the success or feelings of students. Also, her lectures are a little all over the place because she often loses her train of thought and often can't answer questions confidently.
Seems really approachable in class BUT BEWARE if you go to her office. You will likely see students in tears.  She is not known for her personality!

He made sure he recieved feedback and used it to become a better professor. Very willing to help students get credit back on assignments and did test corrections for exams. Also just entertaining in class. He had attendence as extra credit. Overall made the class enjoyable

He cares a lot and takes feedback which he reacts to quickly.  Had a couple knowledgeable entrepreneurs, investors, and lawyers talk to us.  Did a class project giving us experience in pitching and coming up with problems/solutions.  Provided great resources for us to learn ourselves.  Easy class teaching new perspective, not much knowledge tho.
Really interesting class, and does his best to keep things contemporary when possible. Absolutely recommend taking, if you have the choice.
If you read the textbooks and do the homework all the tests are very easy.

Prof. Stendig is a great guy, he definitely cares about his students. I didn't really love his lecture style, so I did most of my learning from the textbook which was pretty effective. Offers lots of Extra Credit opportunities (atendance is extra credit) and test corrections, which I highly recommend doing.

His lectures didn't vibe with me. I ended up textbook grinding the class since the lectures didn't help me with the class. Overall, the copious amounts of extra credit and help he provides to excel in the course make up for the somewhat lacking lectures. I overall enjoyed the class and think he was a great guy but the topic for me was just bad.
He is a phenomenal Professor, deeply cares about his students, is very passionate about economics, and is frankly hilarious. Gives a lot of extra credit and second chances too. 10/10

He cares about his students, is a very funny guy. He is older and likes older music which he plays at the strat of every class. The class itself is easy, if you have taken any econ class before. Only two test which were worth 45% of final grade. the other 55% is from easy assignments every week that actually help. Definitely recommend taking.

This professor cares very much for his students and offers as much extra credit and help as he can. The class itself was more difficult than it needed to be because there were only 2 tests and they were very heavily weighted which is what made the final grading stressful and difficult. Overall an amazing teacher.

Lacey was a very poor lecturer, most of his lectures I didn't gain much. Essentially you teach yourself to get a good grade and he relies heavily on you reading the textbook front to back before each lecture. He also makes mistakes here and there in the lectures, overall underwhelming.

class was not too bad, he's a good teacher. just make sure you understand the hw problems well and youll be good for the exams. there is an in class assignment everyday but it is a participation grade

Overall, I had a lot of fun in this class! The tests are worth a lot and are not the easiest I've taken, but you have a lot of resources available (textbooks, officer hours, etc) and he's always happy to talk and offer help or discuss random math things. We love Dr. Lacey he's the goat - would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Lacey is an amazing professor! The class isn't a walk in the park, but if you put in the effort, you'll get the results you want! Always open to talking with students and helping them whenever necessary.

I kind of had a hard time following him at times so I definitely had to do a lot more studying outside of class. However, I think he was a pretty lenient and generous grader. I thought the stories he shares about his life experiences were interesting. He gave a lot of homework but also it was useful for studying. Attendance is part of the grade!!!
Lectures can be hard to follow. Otherwise, happy to help if it is sought, and is a very generous grader, with less emphasis on minutia than understanding.
Great Professor. Tests are weighted heavily but you will do well if you study for them and he is a generous grader. Would definitely take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tests determine 85% of the grade. Tests are hard, and lectures are not useful.
Only depended on exams, 85% of the grades are exams. Making intro level math class extremely hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The 3 exams (2 22.5% midterms, 1 35% final) make up 80% of the grade, so it'd be hard to recover. His teaching of the content was fine as he knows his stuff. He often made small mistakes; he doesn't like being called out on said mistakes. Very light on homeworks and is a generous exam grader- all things considered, keep up and you'll be fine!
He acts like he is on tenure. 10% off of hw if you do it completely wrong. Easy A as long as you can do a course without needing a professor.

Very little feedback, homework completion based but does not give back answers, does not like when you point out errors in class, exams much harder than practice, light grader but don't expect to actually learn anything in his class.

Professor Lacey cares about the success of individual students! He is one of the nicest professors I have ever had at GT, and his course gives a rigorous understanding of real analysis. I initially failed this course, and finally got a C, and he still told me I'm a wonderful student at the end of it all.

Very nice and understanding, attendance is not mandatory and all lectures livestreamed, he also records review videos afterwards, however, lectures can be a bit dry and it feels he doesn't explain concepts/intuition for a few things taught in class. Tests are easy as long as you have done the homework.

Look if you're good at math, take him. If not, avoid. He pulls numbers out of thin air, makes lots of mistakes, doesn't really teach concepts. I had to basically teach myself the entire course, without knowing where to even begin or what the concepts even were. Never took stats in high school, so I was just lost for the entire semester.

While he clearly wants students to succeed, Lacey can be a very dry lecturer and didn't do a great job at getting the intuition for linear algebra across (mostly power points about how to perform calculations). Grade was exam-heavy; exams were fair, but make sure to do lots of practice problems.
I enjoyed the class. I had to study quite a bit but it was fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's an ok lecturer, the lectures will teach you how to do problems but the concepts require reading the book (midterms are concept heavy). Your grade is basically your 3 midterms (tests worth 70% total). I ended missing the A border by 1 question on the midterm which sucks. He did not bump my grade up, which is respectable (fairness).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dual Enrollment student taking first ever college class. And, quite literally, the worst class ive EVER taken. Did not teach/explain anything well, took lectures straight out of the textbook (which wouldnt be bad IF he took time to actually read it), and often confused himself working his own problems and asks you, the confused student for help.

Expect the following in each lecture: 1. "Oops! Did I make a mistake?" 2. "How many minutes do I have left? I don't think I can finish this example." And yet in his own words, he is "a leading expert in Fourier series." Year in, year out, despite constant critiques, Lacey never attempted any improvement - always coming unprepared for the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He messes up in examples and confused me right from the start. To do well, read the textbook, do the MML hw, and the TAs are usually amazing. I pretty much never went to a single lecture, but watched many of the recitations. This class is one I definitely struggled in because it was basically self taught. Good, nice guy though. Tests are fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Oof worst math class Ive ever taken and I like math

Lectures were awful. It was extremely difficult to get the important points out of his lecturing. He often wasted 10 min at the beginning of class talking about irrelevant info such as hurricanes, voting, etc. Then he would complain that we didnt have enough time to finish that section in the chapter. He rarely went back to finish them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He doesn't really go too much into details in his lectures.

Dr. Lacey is funny and cares about his students but his lectures were difficult to understand. If you zone out for one second youve lost the topic. Sometimes he would start a question get excited start another problem and never finish the first problem.
Sometimes during lectures he'd solve the example questions wrong, and just say "I forgot how to do it" or he'd just rush through it and not finish the question Seems nice tho!

Lacey is in general a good guy and I believe he does genuinely care about his students, however teaching just isnt his thing. There were times when he would be going through example problems and he would get stuck in the middle of them, give up, and move on. We missed a lot of important concepts this way. I pretty much taught myself using mathlab.

Decently good lecturer, and he cares a lot about his students. Exams weren't hard. I'd venture to say that 1554 with Lacey is easier and less work than several 1553 sections... only downside is that he tends to teach at 8 am

I took this class as a distance student, so I might not have had the full experience as a campus student. Lacey in general, is very thorough on some concepts while at the same time skips over some important concepts. This was the first year he made a final, and it was EXTREMELY hard. However, he is a kind and understanding teacher, and compensated.

Take what I say with a grain of salt. The course constantly changes. First off, he's a great person. Tests are fair (the sample tests are representative of the actual thing), homeworks do help, and Piazza is amazing. Ask for help early, and you won't have to later. Biggest regret? Not asking for help early on. Lacey is an amazing person.

I am still in his linear algebra class. He has these awkward moments where he asks the class a question and nobody responds. He's a nice guy and he fully understands the content and he can convey the content well. He does a good job of conveying the definitions of terms and how to solve problems. Also check his wikipedia page. Yes. He has one.
The class is easy you can self study and not attend lecture and still get a good grade.
Really dry, only talks about theory and never really applies any of the ideas
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Lacey really does care about his students. He is not the best lecturer, but is really helpful in answering questions. Practice quizzes were a big help for actual quiz questions.

Prof. Lacey is one of the best professor I had at Tech. He is a great man and an extremely knowledgable professor. Unlike other ratings said, he explains the material well, and really motivates you to explore further. His 4 midterms partitioned the classes to 4 sections which is actually a really good set up.

Dr. Lacey is a great man; he genuinely tries to improve the lives of students as well as helping to fix the racial and gender divide in mathematics. Unfortunately, he can't lecture very well, but the class is easy enough to get an A if you just read the textbook.

Michael Lacey is one of those teachers who knows his stuff, but has trouble getting it across to his students. That being said, his tests are so easy, if you know how to do the practice quizzes, you will do well on the real thing. Final exam for us was literally just another of 5 quizzes, and it wasn't cumulative. He can be unintentionally funny.

Not the most vivacious guy out there, but his lectures got across the material well enough to me. If you are math savvy, you should do fine in his class. If you have struggled in the past with college math, you will probably do poor in his class. Seek a different professor if you need a really good lecturer to learn math.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: not very good at lecturing which makes material that should be very easy feel much more difficult
He isn't a good lecturer, the tests are tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Bad lecturer - don't take his class

He's not the best lecturer, but he does genuinely care about the students. He is there if you ask for help, and he does his best to help when you do ask. His lectures often had some sort of participation such as in class assignments, so attendance was mandatory. Otherwise, his tests are a tad on the tough side, though he does curve if necessary.

He is very smart, and i'm sure makes a wonderful researcher, but is rather lacking as a professor. His lectures were confusing, and his tests were impossible, but the quizzes were easy, and on occaision quizzes were based soley on attendence.
Not the best way to start at Tech.  While this class is hard regardless, I would recommend looking for another section.

This techer is by far the worst that i have had in a while. His lectures confused me even though i have done the stuff before. I definately do not recommend Prof. Lacey to anybody...Had a really good TA though...Leslie Myles.

I've taken calc before and I got totally lost in this class. Homework, lectures and tests are like three different classes, none relevant to each other. The test questions are the hardest possible questions he could ask. Does not collect homework.

This is probably the worst calc 1 teacher at GT. It seems as if he prides himself on failing incoming freshman. He cannot teach at all and is the very definition of a researcher/HORRIBLE teacher. His lectures are often so complex that half the students do not even attend them anymore. I definitely DO NOT recommend.

Grading for the homeworks is completely arbitrary. Despite increased effort each time + starting to include include extra figures and analysis in my homeworks, I ALWAYS get the average score (87) with no feedback on how to improve. There are 5 homeworks, a group project, and a final. Wont grade the project proposal (been a month) and its due soon
No rhyme or reason to grading. No rubrics. No feedback. Syllabus changed in the middle of the semester. No explanation ever as to what grade you received. Most frustrating class I have ever taken.

There are no rubrics, no explanation as to why you lost points. Grades are based off of vibes strictly. I asked for feedback, she replied weeks later and said I lost points for not including something that wasn't listed as a requirement and was told it's common sense to include it.

The teaching style made the material difficult to follow, and assignment directions and rubrics were often unclear and contained several typos. Grading relies heavily on the Turnitin AI detector without room for discussion, which made the class super stressful.
No rubric for grading. Never get feedback on why you lost points. Changes policies and syllabus in the middle of semester. Will flag you for AI without you ever using AI.

You would think a CS professor would understand how AI and LLM models work. Kept getting docked for 'using AI' when I did not and all online AI checkers show less than 10%  AI detection. She did not care and said she only trusts Canvas' AI detector and that her decision is final no matter what. Stopped replying to emails and discussion posts.

Extremely rude to students when providing criticism. It's like tough love with no love. Grades are seemingly arbitrary and she can just decide that a student's contribution to a group project doesn't matter. Everything in this class is essentially just up to the professor's whim / a quick skim of materials rather than any specific rubric.

Lectures basically teach nothing, yet attendance is mandatory. The homework rubric is unclear, hasn't been updated since the millennium with bunch outdated links, but it's still the course's best part. The group project and description are a total mess. Only she knows the real rubric, which changes with every announcement. She is rude to students

Professor has really high standards for written homeworks and the final project. There is a weekly writing assignment with really high standards, adding a dose of stress to all of your Fridays.
The grading criteria is extremely vague. There's no rubric, which makes it feel just down to her personal opinion.
She is also extremely rude to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course felt like a bunch of nothing information. Every lecture was equivalent to a simple google search that could have given me all the content I needed. The professor was also difficult to listen to, and I don't believe that she was a great lecturer despite making attendance mandatory.

Not recommended, especially if you want proper feedback on grades. No rubrics. You get peer reviews on essays, but no reasoning for how grades are given. Same for projects. Sent an announcement stating all grades will be released but never happened. You get overall letter grades despite numerous missing graded items.

Good, friendly professor; cares for students and is accessible outside of class. We had to do some biweekly projects which were centered around some technologies like web crawlers, caching/optimization, etc. No final exam but you get a 10-15pg paper which is pretty easy, and a team project (your choice of topic).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Students are expected to behave like mindless drones, and instructed to drop the course when they seek guidance. If they do manage to appease her TA lackeys, they will find their minds deformed by the same delusions Ling Liu holds, their thinking fixated on a zero sum game, long detached from any spirit of collaboration or semblance of humility.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Worst course, worst professor I've ever seen. This course has nothing to do with Big Data. Reading and Writing is heavy, come with a solid essay writing skill, or you will get negative attendance points even because low HWs/Final grades. The project workload is also the heaviest I've ever been through. Not to mention how rude she is to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Used profanity words to comment on students' work. Public humiliation for times. TA and professor only reply to Ed post when they want to, most of the posts were ignored. Grading rubrics is arbitrary, you only see your entire semester long project grade at the end of the semester. Grades automatically curved around 85. Don't waste your time here.

Extremely rude to students, poor lecture content and delivery. Assignments and course syllabus is mostly outdated. Note that the course name is misleading, and is not a course related to handling of big data.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: absolutely the worst professor I've ever had at Tech in all of 5 years. not a single other comes close at how genuinely rude and uncaring she is. class topics are essentially chosen at random and are unrelated to the course. during project demos, she would interrupt groups and publicly humiliate them. stay away from this course if she's the prof

Genuinely a crashout, rude, grades hard for the projects and has a huge final paper. Haven't finished yet, but I've heard the curve is huge because of this. Most of this wouldn't be too bad if she wasn't extremely rude too.

This professor is extremely rude. Her grading guidelines make no sense. She speaks far too quietly during class, and even the course material is terribly structured. Although, she does curve a lot, so there's that.

This is not a Systems course. This is rather a collection of topics the instructors is excited about. The same is reflected in the assignments, project-topics, and the review subjects. This class felt more ML and LLMs heavy than Systems heavy.

Also, lectures felt very vague, and most of the learning happened during the assignments and projects.

I have been in GT CS for 5 years and this is THE worst of all the ones I have taken. The instructor is knowledgeable about the content she teaches. However, she is extremely rude to students and makes the course overly arbitrary. The rubrics for assignments are vague and the workload is too heavy for the final paper. Time wasted.
Using public humiliation as a form of motivation is not valid. I don't need to know that another student is doing poorly in the class or is going through "family issues"

The CS6220 course experience is one of the worst at GT CS. TAs are non-existent. Homework is poorly designed with little instruction on what to do. Grading is quite random as well with no clear standard. However, if you just need an easy A and don't care about course experience, this course might actually be pretty nice.
Rude, too much paper writing, a lot of work expected on the group project and then another paper on top of that.  Barely teaches anything and invites lecturers only to question them herself.

Dr. Liu is extremely passionate and knowledable about the content. However, while the content of the class is useful, there's no practical application assignments which help you understand if the content has truly been learned. Also, the course load of is heavy, which includes the homeworks and the final paper which is 15-20 pages long.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Ling Liu is a mediocre professor that is further hindered by her lack of effort. Homeworks aren't graded by her but by other students. We are also assigned a ridiculous 15-20 page essay which adds nothing to the class except extra stress and work for no reason or learning purpose whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The course topics are incredibly disjointed. The project, final exam, and participation grades are not given by the end of the semester, and the TAs and prof do not respond to these complaints on EdStem. The homework is tedious, and the grades are artificially curved to give most people 80-90. The participation requirements are  convoluted.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible teaching. She speaks random stuff in class which is not at all connected and doesn't make sense.

Dr. Liu knows the content of the course and is actually very passionate about the content she teaches; however, I can confidently say that this was one of the weaker classes I've taken at Tech - especially in the info thread. The grading is completely unclear, it's hard to find correct information about assignments, and the assignments are too hard
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is really passionate about the lecture content and extremely knowledgeable. That said, the grading criteria are extremely unclear and hard to follow yet worth so much of our grade. The class has been backloaded where ~70% of the class grades come from the last 1.5 weeks of the semester. The final is a 15-20 single-spaced paper.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Liu is very enthusiastic and knowledgable on the subject taught. You can learn a ton from programming assignment if you pay time and efforts. I hate to say this but the workload is extremely heavy unless you like writing papers. The final paper is a 1015 pages single spaced paper which is 3x more than other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Aweful
Awesome!
Lecture may get “boring” at times as it usually doesn't directly relate to assignments, but an interesting class and great professor nonetheless.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Prof. Rinehart is very passionate, but she can also be very strict, is not afraid to call out and raise her voice at students for being on their phone/talking in class. The 3 sketchbooks are not difficult but are time consuming and graded harshly. They're due immediately when class starts, if its 1 minute late she will call you out in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Michelle's lectures were genuinely interesting & VALUABLE for us architecture students. Lectures become warzones for staying awake if you're not genuinely interested, so take notes, draw, etc! You're graded on 3 sketchbooks + 2 digital assignments that give you a month each, so PACE YOURSELF! Your grade depends on your time management + attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class had the opportunity to really engage students during their first year but instead chose to show us a slideshow every day. Weirdly timed (5-6pm) so kind of hard to be engaged. The assignments were lengthy but not hard at all. Not super nice to put into portfolio once you're past first year. Weird about sick excuses. Shes not bad per say.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class only has a few assignments. You have a month for each; just pace yourself. The actual class is just her talking about architecture and buildings. She prefers us to just sketch during class. She will like you if you actually engage with her in class.
She was weird. Content was interesting.

The professor made lectures bearable by sharing personal stories about some of the places on the slides and strongly encouraged class engagement. You are graded only on work outside of class, which is time-consuming but straightforward. All assignments are graded based on completion and effort, so getting an A should be easy; don't procrastinate.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are amazing! She gives a lot of work but it isn't hard work, as long as you do what is asked you'll get a 100. It seems intense but it really does a great job of teaching you how to quickly sketch. She truly cares, she even made my class brownies!

I actually had her for ARCH 1060, but that was not an option. She took attendance in every class. The lectures were helpful to gain architecture knowledge, but they were not required to get a good grade in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took History of Architecture in the Late short summer session. This was a hard class to cram into a 5 week period, and the class lectures were virtual. Lectures got repetitive, but Rinehart is caring and dropped a quiz at the end of the semester to boost many of us up to an A. Summer session composed of 4 main quizzes and many opinion essays.

Architecture studio, in general, is a lot of work, but Michelle is probably one of the best critics of the freshmen studio. She rambles a lot, but she gives great feedback. Critics care about your grade, but Michelle goes a step beyond. If you ever get her, congrats, but just be ready to hear an extreme amount of stories.

I took her class during the summer. We had 5 open-note tests and a final. I didn't use the textbook at all. Its very lecture heavy so DO NOT MISS A CLASS. Anything that she says in lecture is fair game on tests. She's very energetic and knows her stuff. She's been to almost every place that she talks about in lecture. Very inspiring.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class definitely requires you to pay attention in class every single second because you will be quizzed on everything. Michelle does care about her students success and if you need help, she is accessible. With the right amount of effort, this course is very easy. The book is not required but does help supplement lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Most of your grade comes from exams which are based on the lecture materials, so it's important to take good notes. There's lots of opportunities for easy extra credit, take them it will make you less stressed at the end of the semester.

Exams are worth 60% of the overall grade, but many of the problems are very similar to the problem sets so if you complete the problem set you will be fine. The lectures can be a little confusing at times, but Prof. Pineda Torres does a good job of conveying information in an understandable way. There are also several opportunities for extra credit

Dr. Pineda-Torres is incredibly cohesive, articulate, and nuanced when discussing concepts. She values the theoretical as well as empirical sides, which gives realistic insight into economic research and its applications. If you do as expected in the syllabus and speak relatively frequently in class, the course should be very manageable.

New professor, huge busy-work assignment every few weeks. Professor over-emphasized her concern for academic dishonesty and seems to actively hunt students who cheat. Easy A if you do the work, don't take the class for granted just because it's easy. You'll need to show up to class for quizzes and be prepared for busy work out of the textbook.
I haven't gone to class since January. It is April. I have a 99% in the class.
No attendance required, just do the work and do it on time and you are guaranteed an A.
Very small amount of work, everything is open note.
No attendence required, just do the work and do it on time and you are garunteed an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i love this woman. attendance isn't mandatory, tests and hw are super easy, and theres soooo much extra credit its impossible not to get an a. also shes lowkey pretty funny
I stopped going to lecture a few weeks into this class. There is hardly any work to do for this class and it is super easy. Definitely the best choice for the Wellness requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor to take for health! She was great, attendance not mandatory, and work very light. Love her!
Her class is all tests that are on canvas, and asynchronous. Attendance not mandatory, and up to 4 extra credit points through different things during the semester. VERY EASY class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely easy class. Definitely take 1040 over any of the other health classes if you can. You don't have to show up at all to this class if you don't want to. Only 8 grades, 3 tests, 3 quizzes and 2 writing assignments but they're graded really easily. My high school health class was more advanced than this.

Highly recommend!! Attendance not mandatory and she cancels in-person classes occasionally too. You don't even need to fully pay attention in class to do well. The tests and quizzes are easy, and as long as you do the assignments on time you're chilling.

Take her for APPH. Attendance was not mandatory. Tests are super light if you use your resources ;)
Can't recommend more. Probably spend 1 hour a month on this class and I have a 97%.

This professor is so funny sometimes.This is a health class no one goes to after a while so people just stop coming and no one responds to her questions in the lecture so she'll crack jokes at that and it's honestly amazing, this professor deserves so much better because at the end she takes it so sweetly and still makes lectures fun and engaging.

Super easy class. Attendance isn't mandatory so stopped attending classes early on. There's 3 exams, 3 quizzes, and 2 writing assignments. I would just be very careful about not missing one of the 8 things because ur grade will drop hard. There's also 4 points of extra credit in case you mess up a bit.

Wonderful professor and is so easy— this class is definitely designed to be a brain break from all your other classes. You don't have to go to lecture to do well, but she interacts with students and checks in with them so it can be a really nice break through your day. Content was super easy and all within the notes and extra credit is available.

The easiest class I have ever taken, I heard of some APPH 1040 sections having time consuming group projects. Rosbruck had 3 unproctored exams, 3 unproctored quizzes, and 2 writing assignments. Class barely took any time, I stopped attending lecture after the first exam. There's also up to 4 points of extra credit.
I didn't show up to a single lecture after the first week and got an A. Easiest APPH class, take her if you don't care at all about APPH (like most students).

Very easy class. For the online section, all assignments were very easy to do and did not require much time. In addition, the exams were all open note, so the entire class was a very easy A as long as you did the work. There are plenty of opportunities for extra credit as well.

Her online class was very easy. All the tests and quizzes were open note and all her questions are answered in the notes. She has extra credit. Overall this class took almost none of my time. There was no final.

Extremely easy class as everything is online. As long as you read the syllabus and do the exams, you should be fine. Exams were an accurate reflection of material learned. Class did not require an abundance of time to be spent on it. Highly recommend Prof. Rosbruck for APPH 1040 as it was very easy and minimal effort was required.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely take her for APPH 1040. I didn't even watch the lectures and got a good grade. Quizzes and exams are open note and most answers are online. If you put in effort for the written assignment you will get a 100. Easy class and low time commitment.

Didn't attend class once and got a 97 in the class. Tests are worth 72% of your grade but they are extremely easy and questions are pulled directly from the notes. Tests are also open note. Rosbruck offers SO MUCH extra credit (up to 4 percentage points to final grade) so I can't imagine not getting an A in this class as long as you do the tests.

She is not a bad professor. It's health so you dont really learn anything important, but she does not make it more work than necessary. The only annoy part is that the tests, which are only multiple choice autograded by canvas, would take around a month to get back to us, which makes no sense.

It's hard to not get an A in this class. Use the textbook and slides on tests and quizzes, you don't need to go to class. Use your brain when doing the other assignments, and you will end with an A. Tons of extra credit if anything happens.
You have to try to not get an A in this class.
Online tests and quizzes. Did not show up, easiest class ever.
Class is extremely easy especially with exams being online and open note. Don't really see how anyone rates her beneath a 4, she has a sense of humor and cares about everything she talks about.

The class is very easy; most people don't show up to lectures. Midterms are taken online in your own time, and lectures are cancelled on the days midterms are due. Rosbruck clearly cares a lot about the topic and seems excited/energetic every class. No final exam.
Really easy class, although it is not the highest in terms of structure and quality. Did not attend any lectures after the first few but still managed to easily pass.
The easiest class I have ever taken, never went to lecture, just online quizzes, and open notebook exams. 10/10
Requirements to get an A: be a living human being (Optional)

If you have a pulse, you will get an A in this class. Never went to a single class except the first day. 8 total assignments (3 quizzes, 3 exams, 2 assignments), everything is open note, online, and take home.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easiest class ever, barely need to go. Rosbruck is nice and her exams are online so you can take them when you want during the day of the exam. Barely any assigments, no final.

I imagine this is going to be one of the easiest classes I will ever take in college. As long as you stay somewhat aware of deadlines there is no reason you shouldn't get an A. The tests are all online at-home tests and are free A's as well as quizzes. There were only two assignments and both were very easy.

Not hard. Barely attended class although would recommend watching lectures before exams because some test info can only be found there. Textbook isn't that useful. Best part is she gives lots of extra credit. Worst part is you can't miss a single assignment/turn in anything late for credit. Stay on top of deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was very easy. But, if you miss an assignment you're already down a grade letter. There's extra credit in the end - about 3 - 4%. so it can raise a 88 to a 91.
Super Easy A. Practically no homework, no final, and all of the tests are open note with answers easily searchable in the textbook and guest lecture slides. Didn't learn much, but it's health.

Really easy A. Exams/quizzes are open note and straightforward and she gives out a lot of extra credit at the end. No real need to go to class, just make sure you look over powerpoint slides before the exams

No need to attend lecture. Go through the slides that she posts, maybe read the textbook if you are interested. Only a few, very easy assignments and quizzes. Tests (online, proctored) tend to get detailed and specific at times, but the material is straightforward nonetheless. Study a little before and you'll be fine. Three midterms, no final.

Don't bother going to lectures unless you're genuinely interested. The tests cover very specific things from textbooks, lectures, etc., but you can still get an A if you don't attend lectures. Lots of extra credit opportunities. I've heard other APPH 1040 professors are easier but honestly it doesn't matter.
There's nothing much to say. The assignments are super easy to get an A on. Exams and quizzes are open resource.

Attending lecture is not mandatory. more than half of the class stopped attending class after the first couple of weeks... She records the lectures and posts the lecture slides weekly. I'm not sure if it was due to COVID-19 or not, but exams and quizzes are all online and taken open-note at home. It's a super chill 2-credit hour class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Stopped going to lecture after the first week. Do your assignments on time and study an hour and a half before the 3 exams. No final.

It's a Health class at a technical university. Don't expect great things. Don't need to go to class because it's the same as reading the textbook, and overall you can forget about the class until an assignment or exam is due.
Nothing much to say, honestly. In the online period the class was pretty easy. 3 tests and a few quizzes. Lectures were all asynchronous and not really necessary to watch. Might be harder in-person.

Took this class online, Buzzport said sync but we only ever watched async lectures from 2017/2018, which is sad because I really did want to learn the curriculum here. Also never ever got responses to any of my emails. Def don't need the textbook. But the class was really easy and I got an A easily so there's nothing I can really complain about tbh

Easy A. Couple quizzes and small assignments every few weeks and that's it. No final. Entire class ended up being async (no live meetings/lectures), but it honestly was kind of nice to not have to worry about lectures for health on top of everything else. There's no reason to not take her, so she gets a 5.

I took this in Fall 2020 in a virtual environment due to COVID. It said on Buzzport that the class was going to be synchronous, but there was never a single live lecture. In fact, she used recordings from lecture that came from 2017. Other than that, I would say the class is pretty easy and just do the work and don't forget the tests.

Rosbruck made health the easy class that it should be. I went to most lectures and found them interesting and relevant. I didn't purchase the textbook and kept up fine. The tests were a bit tricky, but all the info is directly off her slideshows. She gives a ton of extra credit opportunities, so you can get an A even if you get Bs on all the tests.

Health is a stupid class already, but the tests were unnecessarily difficult. Some questions were statistics that didn't really feel useful to the class. Rosbruck is a cool person, just not the best professor
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Clear lecturer. Attendance not mandatory or necessary but still go if you can. She gave me extra credit for coming. HW is on Pearson and is easy. Don't read textbook at all. (Don't buy Pearson with textbook. Save money.) 3 tests are fair. Study the slides really well. Know the statistics. Statistics from slides are on the test. Do all extra credit.

She cares about her students - tons of extra credit, gave us extensions for almost every assignment after the online transition. Lectures are amazing, but her tests are oddly specific and you need to study for them. Assigns readings that most people don't do, but they are helpful for the tests. Overall an easy A with just a little bit of effort.
Lecture is super boring and exams are really specific on minute details briefly mentioned in class.
Class is a joke as long as you do the work and memorize the slides before tests. There's no final which is nice.

This class wasn't too hard, and there were lots of opportunities for extra credit. She covers everything you need to know in lecture, and the content is also in the textbook. Overall a pretty easy class.

Read the book, do the book's practice questions, and look over the PowerPoints. Tests are rather difficult, but between the extra credit and easy homework assignments, it's not hard to do well. She's a very enthusiastic, clear lecturer, but many people don't show up for class. Guest lectures are almost as important as content lectures for tests.

Health a pretty straightforward class. I like the energy that she has when teaching the material. During the lectures, you don't need to be alert 100% of the time, since the exams are not too difficult. I especially appreciate the countless extra credit opportunities she gives.

I only went to class to take the midterms. You only need to study the powerpoints since she pulls test questions straight from there. Don't waste your time reading or even buying the textbook. With the extra credit, it's an easy A if you just study the powerpoints. Not sure what these other reviews are talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Does not lecture well and tests are ridiculous in why they ask for. You are tested on very minor details of one part of a lecture. Extra credit is helpful but still a tough class to study for.

Her class is confusing, no one really knows what's going on and her reply to everything is "reach out to the TAs", who never respond. APPH is supposed to be an easy class, but she makes your life difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Easy class, enjoyable professor. She's a pretty good lecturer as well, which makes a class that I don't really care about a lot better. She's very well educated and has had a lot different life experiences that add to her ability as a professor.

Go to lectures and (sometimes) read the textbook- if you do this, you'll pass tests and get an easy A. Don't need to put in much work. She gives 4 extra credit points to your grade if you do some easy assignments. She definitely designs the course to NOT be work heavy, and she doesn't want you to stress about the class. It's supposed to be easy.

Health is incredibly easy with her. Either go to lectures or read the chapters (there's no need to do both) and you'll be fine for homeworks, tests, and quizzes. You can also get up to 4% of your total grade in extra credit assignments which are quick and easy.

Professor Rosbruck is your best bet for 1040. She knows what she's talking about and is very passionate about the material and her students. There is a chance for 4% extra credit, and as long as you study for the tests (which can be surprisingly hard) and keep track of deadlines, you'll do okay. Most work (quizzes & assignments) is online.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof. Rosbruck is very passionate about what she teaches and makes health as interesting as its going to be. The tests are a bit harder than you'd think they'd be, but if you go to class and do the abundant extra credit you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lots of extra credit given. Posts all lecture notes and guest lecturer notes to course page- really likes to have guest speakers in class. You will do better on the tests if you go to class since some questions come directly from the lectures. Funny in class. Easy quizzes and online assignments.

First, textbook is needed for this class. The textbook is extremely useful when it comes to studying for tests, but she posts her lecture slides on T-Square as well. The tests are simple enough and no trick questions are in them, so they are easy as long as you study properly. Homework and quizzes are easy, and she offers extra credit at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Inspirational class! Makes you care about your health and understand the importance with scientific data to back it up. You get to apply a lot of the knowledge you learned with interactive class work. Rosbruck is passionate, caring, and is a dynamic professor making health interesting to learn about.

Rosbruck was an awesome professor.  She manages to make a class of over 250 students to be discussion based and interactive. She truly cares about her students and is enthusiastic about the material. I find her teaching to be inspirational and it got me to care more about my health and the importance of health on all levels not just physical.

More lectures were given by guests from Health Promotions than by the actual professor. The lectures Rosbruck gave herself were terrible. However, tests are easy except for a few inevitable questions on random statistics. Read the book, take the class somewhat seriously, and you'll make an A.

I didn't show up to class unless I had to turn in an assignment (she makes you do it in person) & all I did was read the book before the tests & I got an A. She lets you know exactly what you have to do/know to get a good grade & puts everything on her syllabus. She's also very enthusiastic about teaching. Loved her, definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Going to lecture is all you need to do to get an A really (that and do like 2 of the extra credit options), but you'll still do fine if you don't go and simply read the notes she posts online. Personally I thought she went too fast during lecture, and sometimes you had guest speakers who were really interesting
Don't need to go to lectures, do the extra credit and all the online assignments and read the book.

I barely ever showed up to class and still got an A. The lectures and guest speakers are actually really interesting but attendance is not mandatory by any means. Rosbruck is very nice and she cares a lot about her students. Tests are easy as long as you read the textbook beforehand, but I never took notes. Overall she's the easiest health teacher.

Easy peasy class if you put the work in- either read or pay attention to lectures. Guest lecturers are sometimes there and their info will be tested on. Just come to class and use common sense if you want an automatic/easy A. There is also up to 4 points of extra credit available. 3 Tests, 3 Quizzes, 3 Homeworks.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class was very easy. She loves to pull questions from an online test bank which you can find using questions in the back of each chapter. 3 assignments are given but are easy 100's if you do the work. Encourages participation in class but no one ever shows up because it's not necessary. Guest Lecturers are important though for test questions.

You can either come to lectures or read the book and pass without a problem. Lecture notes are always posted to T-square. Offers up to 4 percentage points of extra credit. Requires just about zero effort, which is, coincidentally, how much effort the professor puts into the class.

Dr. Nezafati is a GOAT! He is a very understanding and caring professor who takes time to make sure his students understand the concepts of class, not just a pattern for problems. PSS was very helpful, and his lectures reinforced material well. The homework was time consuming and quizzes were hard, but by the exams you were good and an 83 was an A.

Dr. Nezafati cares a lot about his students and if you're going to take bmed2110 definitely take it with him. The class itself is a lot of work but if you take the time to watch the lecture videos and understand the homework, the quizzes and tests aren't terrible.

Great teacher! 3 exams (1 was the final) - each one was based on what we had learned since the previous exam so nothing cumulative and each one had 3 attempts (with grades averaged). Explained everything very well. Rounded my high B up to an A (I went to every class and did every assignment) and I'm very thankful. Very manageable class!

Big emphasis on group work and applicable skills (real life data studies, academic writing and review, etc.). Go to class because the slides are heavily abbreviated and only make sense in the context of his lecture. About 1 HW/week

Dr. Nezafati was very enthusiastic about the material. He explained everything very well and was very helpful when asked questions. He emphasized the small details, which are very important for this difficult course. He also made the online lectures this semester which were great. Definitely wouldn't want to take this class with anyone else.

Dr. Nezafati has been a great 2110 professor, especially with learning such different concepts than normal classes. He has always been very open to questions and helping outside of class. He seems to really enjoy the material and makes the class a lot more interesting. There is a lot of homework but TA hours are always really helpful (PAUL!!!)

He is a very kind professor but is not a great lecturer. His lectures are not very informative, and they are often disorganized. You have to go to class because Point Solutions tracks your location, but they are not super helpful. YouTube will be your best friend; StatQuest with Josh Starmer is much clearer for conceptual stuff.

BMED 2110 is a difficult and intense course. However, Professor Nezafati made it as manageable as possible and fun. He is by far the best professor for this class and makes complex topics understandable. He also makes his lectures very engaging and fun. I love him, he's one of the best professors at GT
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really nice guy, very enthusiastic about the material, easy exams. Awful group project, long-winded explanations. Take Shu Jia instead if possible.

Really nice professor, explains concepts really well, and most experienced 2110 instructor. Really cares about his students, the structure of the course, and the BME program in general. Goes on long tangents sometimes.

This class is the weed-out and is naturally hard. Don't stress about it too much. Nezafati is a great prof, but I didn't like how the instructional team was 3 profs. It made the content more confusing than it already was. I would recommend asking questions early on if you get stuck. Falling behind in this class is easy to do, and you will get lost.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Nezafati's first priority is to his students. Although the weekly homework problems are difficult, he makes practice available every week, and his office hours are also of great help, both in-person and on MS Teams. If it were my call, he'd teach every single demo session too! Great teacher, great guy!

Class is hard, but he explains concepts very well. Super approachable outside of class, I asked him stuff after almost every class period and he didn't get annoyed and helped me understand the concepts. Similar to COE 2001 and CHBE 2100 since 1-2 equations are used to solve problems. Also, an 83 is an A, so you can't complain about tough grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He was very helpful inside of class and always told you what you needed to know before an exam. Some parts of the class were harder than others, but there is a lot of slack given. Do what they tell you to and you will probably get an A. He can be a bit long-winded at times, but he does so to make sure everyone knows what is going on.

He is one of the most genuinely caring professors you'll ever meet. He always made the effort to be as accessible as possible to accommodate his students. 2210 isn't easy and it's very work heavy but Nezafati gives very fair quizzes and tests. All around great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a great professor, but overcomplicates things a little. Very particular about how you should do certain problems. That being said, the way he teaches you to approach problems is very methodical, which I like. Starts to get difficult during energy section. 83 is an A. Can potentially drop a hw and a quiz. Tests/quizzes are fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is the best professor I've had at Tech. He is accessible outside of class for several hours every day, highly responsive via email and wants his students to succeed. The content of this class is difficult but on par with most professors. The course is super homework heavy and quizzes are difficult, but the midterms and final were fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Nezafati is always willing to help, he truly cares about his students. He is very clear of what is expected of students and provides plenty of material for practice.

Dr. Nezafati was one of my favorite teachers! He's always accessible outside of class for extra help and makes the material easier to understand than the book presents it. The tests are extremely fair, but working with others to understand the material in this class is the key to succeeding. Would definitely take him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really nice, really caring, and really clear. Wants you to do well, you just have to meet him halfway.

Dr. Nezafati was an excellent professor. He is incredibly passionate about the subject as well as his students and wants to see you do well. He has a clear outline of what he is looking for on tests/quizzes/hw and grades according to that. Make sure you do all the hw, it takes forever, but it is the best practice for tests/quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures of 2210 will be divided between several prof. Dr. Nezafati was happily in charge of teaching the energy balance section. Go to office hours of prof and TAs. Create study groups. Go through problems over and over since many concepts may be merged into a few exam problems. TAs for this class was Cassidy and Brandon who were really helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Nezafati truly cares about the success of his students. Yes, BME 2210 is a difficult class, but Nezafati encourages you to set up appointments outside of office hours and email him with questions. His English is okay but you will do well in this class by practicing problems, not by simply listening to Nezafati talk.

The class itself is very difficult but he doesn't make it any easier. He is still learning english so it would be very hard to understand what he was saying or meant to say. I would be afraid to ask him questions because he can be very defensive (since you didn't understand him to begin with) and doesn't explain it very well.
