reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Moss is a very good lecturer, it does take him a bit to get to the point sometimes but he's very enthusiastic and engaging with what he teaches. He also posts all his lectures to Canvas. Labs were essentially just mandatory recitations were never on-pace with the course (as in they were almost always ahead), making them a drag to go to biweekly.

overall he's a kind and chill teacher. he does have a hard time getting to the point in his lectures but other than that he's a great prof. unfortunately, i got the worst TAs possible which makes the class more challenging than it was supposed to be. they're incredibly unhelpful, rude, and straight up ruins the class. other than that good prof
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: CS2110 has been my favorite class I've taken at tech so far. I think the course is designed very well and you have a lot of resources to get help. Moss himself is really nice, but his lectures are a bit long winded and he does tend to go on rants sometimes about only adjacently related topics.

Great lecturer, answers questions, and generally just knows what he's talking about. Uses Microsoft Whiteboard, which I prefer over PPT. 

In fall 2025, the class was project-heavy (45% of grade), but you're guaranteed 100% on projects if you keep up with the content and work hard.

He's a great lecturer, breaking things down simply and traces through examples. The hardest part is unfamiliar content, but review and find a TA during OHs for project help early and you'll be set. I'm taking him in the fall with projects weighing ~60% of your total grade, so you can afford to struggle with the quizzes like I did.

Such a great lecturer; really cares about his students. Lecture is important but lab is even more important, so keep going to lab if you want to do well on your projects in this class. For preparing for quizzes, you're better off reviewing project work and homework.

Moss lowkey does too much in his lectures but clearly cares for students/the subject. TA labs are very helpful and most people would just go to those if attendance wasn't mandatory for lectures. Projects are light and quizzes can be slightly difficult but honestly are not that bad.

Honestly, I am just dropping a rating here for the TAs. Moss is such a boring lecturer in my opinion (have zoned out in basically EVERY lecture), but the TAs make it all worth it. I would genuinely describe office hours as a religious experience. I have learned weeks of content within just a few hours!!
Easily the worst OMSCS professor I've had the displeasure of working with. Not accommodating, very unreasonable, would not recommend taking a course under his instruction.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor. Class was not easy, but it was project-based for fall 2024 session. Lots of projects, had a final as well. Just go to lectures and focus.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Moss was a good lecturer for what can easily be a very boring and difficult subject. Homework can sometimes take a long time, so start early, but he did his best to keep our class engaged in his lectures.

Moss is a good lecturer that understands and cares about the material, but I found that he wasn't the most engaging; the last half of the semester I just watched Forsyth's recorded lectures instead. Moss was always very available and adept when I asked him followup Qs after class. I like the 2110 Quiz/TL format better than a couple midterms.
Very caring and respectable professor - downside was that lectures weren't that engaging.

Don't get me wrong you can tell he's passionate about what he teaches, but I found his lectures to be incredibly boring. It lacks a lot of depth and he often goes over things not ever covered in the quizzes. I stopped going to lecture and solely learned everything from lab/textbook. As long as you do those two things, you should get at least a B

I;m an ME major minoring in CS. This is a hard class, but Moss does an excellent job teaching it. This is my favorite class I've taken so far. You cover so much content, but his lectures make it very digestable, and they are very relevant to the exams and homework.Would reccomend to everyone
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures were alright. It doesn't go as much in depth, but it's still pretty important to go as sort of a direction. Labs are where it's mostly at. Do NOT fall behind, as they cover a lot of material. I was behind 1 lecture and it took me almost a week to get back up to speed. Homeworks were really interesting and online lectures vids HELP A TON!

Professor Moss is a decent engaging professor, but he makes really simple concepts seem confusing and difficult with how he explains them. His notes system is atrocious and makes learning more difficult as he spreads his notes throughout Canvas modules instead of just using files. It's hard to retain the things you learn in this class.
Good lectures, very well structured course overall, gives good career advice

Moss is a good prof that knows what he's talking about and knows how to teach it. Class this semester was graded on 5 projects, 8 homework, 4 quizzes and a final. The content is pretty easy to figure out if you look on YouTube or read the textbook, so lectures aren't really needed. It's still helpful to attend or go to recitation if you want an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was a pretty good professor regarding notes and introducing the Topics. Lab sections were actually very good to help you on projects. Projects had an autograder that didn't have any hidden cases. Quizzes were fair as well. All your turned-in work...should be your work... as circuit sim used for project 1 & 2 has really good cheat detection.

Class is pretty easy, lectures are just him reading out of the textbook and elaborating. Projects don't take more than an hour or two each, quizzes are easy as long as you did the project. Very passionate and will answer any questions you have, but this class is standardized so it doesn't matter who you take.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: CS2110 in general is a well set-up class. Projects (take-home homework) accounts for 50% of the grade, and it uses autograders, so it's basically free 100s.  Moss is a good lecturer overall, but goes on tangents sometimes and has the occasional tendency to overexplain ("do you guys know what linked lists are?")

I took this course in Fall 2023. Moss was a great professor who broke down database topics very well for those new to the subject matter. There was a semester-long group project, so make sure you get a good group and don't get randomly assigned. Tests were difficult if you aren't great at SQL, but they were fair. Worst test grade was dropped.

2110 was a great class. There were 4 small quizzes instead of any exams, which were fair and closely matched content covered in class. The projects are simple, but one of them requires you to meet with a TA for a "demo".

Moss is a thoughtful and enthusiastic prof but, you learn the most stuff in lab, projects, and hw. Projects are autograded and 50% of grade -sweet. hw 20% and not bad. Ask questions and pay attention in lab, study the practice quizzes they provide, and start projects early and you won't stress. Very interesting and important class, learned a lot.

Honestly, I don't think it matters what professor you get for this course. Mark Moss was fine but don't know many people that went to his lectures. The labs and office hours will teach you everything you need to know. I would highly choosing a lab that you can consistently go to.

Kind of terrible at teaching. Maybe 5% of whatever he yaps about in lecture is actually useful for homeworks/projects/exams. Basically self-taught myself the entire course from the textbook which was effective but required me to invest so much extra time.

Not bad, but certainly not good. Lectures are dull and very surface level. Doesn't cover the material that will be on the exam or hws at all. Enthusiastic about the subject but can't really teach it, thus no one shows up to lecture. Lab and OH is where you will actually learn the material, so the professor doesn't really do anything at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's one of the best, most detail oriented professors I've had. He explained SQL so patiently and thoroughly when I was struggling with the content that by the end I felt very comfortable with the language even though I had 0 experience with it in the beginning. 10/10 recommend his class

I literally never leave comments on rmp but Dr. Moss is one of my favorite professors!! I will say that a lot of his lecture content doesn't have much to do with the exams, but if you look at HB's videos they help a lot with that. His lectures focus more on real world connections which is helpful for internships

I see why they call the course "SAD" now. This class isn't that hard once you learn to just wait for other students to slowly decipher his arcane instructions on this discussion board. I think the Zodiac Killer gave more clear instructions than this guy.

Very dry lecturer that had way too much fluff. Quizzes were easy but easy to mess up if you got a few wrong. Project phases are easy if you have a good group but otherwise are an absolute nightmare. Felt like I learned more from the project than actual class.

Moss is a great lecturer and keeps you interested in whatever topic is being lecturer about. The class setup feels fair as a student, and gives a lot of leniency by allowing half of the mini-exams to be replaced by the final.

Just an all around good guy.  Very caring and accessible to students.  Intuitive material coupled with understanding instructors (3 of 6 mini-exams can be replaced by an optional final) helps significantly for doing well in this course.  If you don't do well in CS4400 with Dr. Moss, it's most definitely your own fault.

I really liked the lecture style given by Professor Moss where he is able to teach materials by either having us follow along or presenting examples without merely reading off the slides. The course is graded by 6 mini exams and 3 project phases but he does provide a lot of resources for you to study. Overall, a very chill and respected professor.

Moss gives you an absurdly large amount of resources to learn and prep from + his lectures are very effective. The only way you fail this course is if you don't use one of the countless practice exams/problems he gives out before every exam. Group project is good chunk of grade so be warned

amazing professor, either do final project or final exam will replace your lowest assignment score. Although sometimes he's not in his office hours, he's pretty easy going and can explain things pretty well

Moss is a great lecturer and makes all course content very understandable by walking you through all of the concepts. 90% of the grade is based on 6 mini-exams and 3 projects, the lowest of those can be replaced by taking the final or doing the 4th project. For the mini-exams, the corresponding practice exam is exactly like the mini-exam.

Moss is a decent professor that makes his class interesting. Unfortunately, the class is not a very well-structured course. It spends too much time teaching SQL and not enough time teaching actual theory for databases. I still have many questions about databases after taking this course and I wish I would have had them answered.

I was really looking forward to this class, but unfortunately the structure made it quite annoying. The group project was where I learned everything. Thankfully I had some SQL experience, so it wasn't too hard. The TAs were really hit or miss. Communication was poor, and a deadline for one of the project phases was changed the day before it was due

Organisation lacking at start, but overall structure was clear. Go to class, figure out what is graded and HOW, and it's pretty manageable to get an A. If you start the project phases on time, you're solid. TAs are helpful. Make yourself accountable and it's doable to get an "A". Tests are EXACTLY like practice sessions. I slacked off and got a B.

I had Moss for 4400 and I thought he was good, so I chose him over Forsyth. This was a mistake. I have no disdain for Moss, but the course is organized extremely poorly. Assignments were released late, tests and projects took months to be graded, and the "living" schedule we were given never aligned with what we were doing. It's just not run well.

He's a nice guy but this class is designed poorly. My main problem is that he leaves a lot of the Piazza, OH, Project related things up to the TAs and they're horrible. I mean these TAs don't show up for Office Hours half the time and when they do it's useless. Dr. Moss usually steers important questions to the TAs amplifying their ineptitude.

Very poorly organized class. Project requirements change on due dates. TAs rarely show up to office hours and when they do don't know what they are talking about. Quizzes take the average of 7 attempts which prevents students from practicing. Unanswered Piazza posts. All in all one of the worst classes I've taken at Tech

Doesn't respect students. Very unclear grading policy. The project is designed with tons of mistakes and wrong data.
Update project right before due day and give no extension
He's amazing, but you knew this already.

Mark Moss is a great professor. He provides ungraded practice material for all the concepts covered in class so you can adjust the amount of time you put in based on how much practice you need. I was brand new to SQL before taking his CS4400 class and now it is the programming language I use most frequently in my career.
Difficult class but one of the best for probably the most important class as a computer science major.

I felt guilty for missing lectures. His lectures were boring sometimes but most of the time it was interesting and tied in real-world applications and examples. Mini-exams were the first I've ever encountered here at GT and grew to like them. Prof Moss would often end class early. This his last year teaching 1332 he told my spring class personal.

Good professor! He's very organized on Canvas & has lots of helpful resources. Obviously knows his stuff and makes analogies in lecture to help you understand material. Lectures are a bit boring,& grading was slow, so it was hard to know how much effort to put in for studying & on the group project. Take with friends to help with the group project.

Genuinely do not think it's possible to fail this class under Moss. Open note exams (EVEN THE FINAL), 2 weeks for homework, and a dropped HW and exam. Absolutely cracked. Recitation rly helped (I went every week), TAs are awesome. I do wish we had less pseudocode and more forced understanding. His lectures could have also been more straightforward.

The class is laid out poorly. The canvas page is a mess. Your grade is made up of a project, 3 mini-exams, and a final. The project was ok. The 2 mini-exams and final have widespread cheating. The 3rd mini exam is a demo with limited time and confusing directions. If you screw it up, you will not get an A. The TAs were awful, but Mark is nice.

I preferred the recitation slides and lectures a bit more bc they were clearer and more simplified. While moss is very enthusiastic and knowledgeable, his lectures can get a bit convoluted and draw away from the main points imo. HW was pretty rough and time-consuming to me but they're lenient with curves. Overall would take 1332 with moss!
Really such a nice guy and a great teacher. I'm probably going to get a B in the class, just because of my own failures, but I would still take him again.

The course itself does not force you to understand the material in any way (major gripe). Homeworks were very uninspired. TA recitations were awesome. Moss himself is a passionate and knowledgable guy. Goes above and beyond in his lectures. Moss does have the potential to be rude at times though.

He did well with a class that has admittedly quite dry content, speaking with energy and clarity, as well as trying to paint a broader picture of why these things were important and some relevant examples of where they might be used, such as in OS and database applications. Homeworks and tests were all very realistic and fair.

Nice professor, explains concepts well, if you already know SQL will be a little boring at times. Tests decently easy and open note. Group project is tough at times if not already pretty good with SQL

I love Mark Moss so much. Hes a really good lecturer and makes hard concepts understandable. The only thing is that he has mini exams every other week and the other weeks where you dont have exams, hw is due. So it is a lot of work but its manageable and really fun. Tests were hard in the beginning but got easier as the semester went on.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Moss is such a nice chill guy, and this class was never stressful. The exams were exactly like the practice exams, so if you sufficiently studied practice tests, the actual exams weren't bad. The group project phases were not too difficult but could be time consuming. He has a relaxing nature and really cares about his students! Take him!

Professor Moss is a great choice for this class. His lectures are good but slow; I'd recommend watching their recordings on 2x speed. The quizzes are easy if you use the practice quizzes, but the group project phases should ideally be started as early as possible. Also, the optional final phase is a lot of work but graded liently.

Moss' lectures do not reflect the exams at all, which are much more difficult. Make sure to take the practice quizzes and find a good group because it is impossible to switch. Not as easy as previous semesters, but it is super easy to get a B, so it does not take much to get an A. TAs are so flaky so do not wait last minute on exam/project help.

Good lecturer, although class can sometimes drag because he strives to answer all the student questions (which is a good thing). As long as you watch lectures and start the projects on time, it's impossible to not get an A.

His lectures move very slowly, I could not follow them. However, the homework and lecture slides are enough to learn from. I probably learned more in this class than any other this semester. His tests were not honorlocked. Overall a very manageable and effective course.

Last semester was the darkest period in my life, but I really enjoyed this class and felt that I learned a lot. Moss is a robust lecturer and cares about his students. Lecture prepares you well for the exams. The final group project where you write complex SQL is genuinely tough but you get ample time to do it, and it won't kill your grade.

He is such a solid dude. It's obvious that he cares for his students and knows his stuff. He goes above and beyond to make sure you understand the content. The exams are very similar to practice exams.
The lectures are amazing. Homework is the best resource for you to understand course concepts and do well in exams.

Professor Moss is passionate about the subject, willing to help outside of class, and is a good lecturer. Manages to teach the material in a clear and understanding way. However, do note that he goes quite slow during lectures. There is no mandatory homework, just quizzes, and a group project. Find a good group for the project.

Easy class to get an A in if you show up and pay attention. Mini exams are easy and the lowest one is dropped. They often come from practice exams so you wont be surprised. The group project is manageable as long as you plan and start in time. Overall, very nice class even if lectures can be a bit boring. Moss clearly cares about the subject!

Dr. Moss is the best. Do two things, and you'll do fine in this course: attend and listen to lectures, and DO THE HOMEWORKS. The homeworks are the real key to much of this class, they let you know the data structure in and out.

You have to go to lecture - most practice problems are done in lecture and it's really helpful. He talks pretty slow, so be prepared for that. A great professor though and you can easily get an A if you do the practice quizzes before the tests. Project can be tough at the end of the semester, but the beginning it's easy

Professor Moss is a really great professor! He is really clear during lectures and goes through problems step by step so they are easy to understand. Even with online lectures, he made a clear effort to engage with the students in chat. There is also a ton of practice material and resources for this course so everyone should be able to understand.
CS 4400 is a very difficult class but Professor Moss makes what would be an awful experience considerably more bearable. He is a strong lecturer, and is very passionate about what he teaches.

CS 1332 with Dr. Moss was a great class. My one big problem with Dr. Moss is that he tended to get distracted at times during lectures, but he makes up for it by having very intuitive lectures. He is also very considerate, moving exams based on student circumstances. Homework and exams are the standard affair for an introductory CS class.

Dr. Moss is overall a fantastic lecturer. He gets distracted at times during lectures, but he more than makes up for it by really explaining a large majority of the concepts in 1332 really well, especially for someone who has never encountered this material before. Homework and exams are standard difficulty for an intro CS class.

Professor Moss is super nice and his class taken online is very easy because the tests are open-note. The homework grading is sometimes pedantic but start early and make sure you don't make any easy mistakes and you're good.

Dr. Moss is one of the nicest professors I've ever had. His tests were super reasonable and based off the HW, he'd clearly flag what we should study, and he was very willing to answer any questions students had. He was overall a good lecturer but occasionally bungled an explanation. Lots of projects; read the textbook for help, which is fantastic.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: 1332 with Moss is great cause his lectures are much more engaging than Dr. HB's. Other than that the course is functionally the same. HW is time consuming but never overly difficult. Tests can be hard but the 1332 team gives tons of resources to prepare. Moss is a great professor but tbh wasn't too involved with the course besides lectures.

Professor Moss is a great lecturer and explains the concepts well. He is also very upfront with what is tested - in our semester, we had 6 mini-exams and the lowest was dropped, along with the usual group projects. He cares a lot about his students and knows what he's doing.

The tests are very doable if you read the slides. Don't bother with the textbook. The only annoying thing is the project. It's a lot of work. Other than that, not a bad class. Not much work for most weeks, until you get into project crunch-time. I studied for the tests the day before every time, and made an A.

Prof Moss is chill. He is very funny and passionate about lecturing and genuinely cares about his students by giving out extra credit on every test. Just review exactly what he tells you before the test and you will get good grades. Make sure to get into a good group for the project, haha.

Dr. Moss is so kind and easygoing. He gives extra credit on every test so the averages are usually pretty high. If you read over the slides and go to office hours for the group project, you're set up to make an A.

Lectures are extremely slow but he does explain things well, and you can just read the slides and practice exams to study. Exams can be a lil tough but are curved by 13 points so it's not too hard to get an A. The final project was not too difficult if you've done fullstack but just very long, and you may just want to take the final exam instead.

He's a friendly guy that really cares about the well-being of his students. Unfortunately, his teaching style was super disorganized & unhelpful so I mostly skipped class and read the powerpoints on my own time. 3 midterms were hard, easy, and average difficulty respectively. Final project was cool and really reinforced the course content.

He is a really sweet professor and his class isn't bad. The first exam is pretty hard always so don't let that get you down. Definitely would recommend doing Phase 4 instead of the final especially if you have a CS major in your project group so that you have one less final to study for. Overall, just study well for tests and have a good group.

CS 2340 is an absolute joke of a class. It focuses on a big group project that is very easy, and there are 2 mostly MC tests that are almost verbatim from the PowerPoints. Moss is a solid professor, and attendance is absolutely not a prerequisite to do well in this class.

Dr. Moss is a very fair professor. Guidelines to the class were clear, due dates and assignments were always fair, and he is 100% a nice guy. Lectures were also good- He is a funny guy, Georgia Tech just seems to be a tough audience. Textbooks referenced were good and free for Georgia Tech students. Only awful thing was the grade turnaround time.

This class was mostly based around an extended group project, which was challenging but had clear guidelines. Lectures are not really important, but you do have to understand the material from the textbooks to get a good grade on the tests/projects. Dr. Moss is a really sweet guy, too. Easy to get help in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Just an overall really good dude. Cares a lot about his students, very easy to approach, not intimidating to ask questions to, he's a baller. He also really knows what he is talking about and can explain it in an easily understood way.

Moss is a great guy. Super nice and funny. I would say that as an IE major myself, this class was pretty easy. Kinda touches on the end of CS2316 stuff. The last project (I did the heavy weight GUI in Python Flask) was challenging, but I had a solid team with half CS and half IE members so we got through it well. Highly recommend Moss!

Excellent lectures, ton of extra points. Quizzes are easy, but the final project implementation was flat out unreasonably hard. Luckily, this implementation was only 5% for lightweight, but it can be very time consuming anyway and TAs themselves didn't know how to do some of it. Easy A but not a pushover class anymore just because of the project.

Professor Moss truly cares that the students learn the material. He is extremely open to questions and spends quality time answering relevant ones in class. He is respectful of his students and his lectures are clear and all information is relevant.
Listens to students concerns and tries to rectify them accordingly. Encourages and gives a lot of tips to students when they are feeling bad about their grades.
Good professor, listens to feedback, really wants students to learn. Makes it tough, but fair (most of the time). Really challenges you.

Kind of confused by all the low ratings. I had Professor Mackenzie for my online accounting 2101 class. It was very easy to follow along with the online lecture and guided notes. She explains concepts very well and in depth and makes it easy to understand. Exams were mostly multiple choice and were not to tough.

Accounting was new to me so I had to put a lot of time and effort into studying for this class. The professor is pretty nice, although sometimes what she says about the level of difficulty in a test is not true. The homework takes forever. If you can avoid the hybrid class, do because I think in person would have been better.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Accounting is like learning a new language so it was extremely difficult at first, each test is worth a big chunk of your grade so be careful. She is a good professor with the hybrid class, and prepared us well for the exams. Don't fall behind, or else its extremely hard to catch back up and truly grasp the content as the tests are in depth
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: dont do it

Took ACCT 2101 hybrid this semester. Lectures are straight-forward and ended early most days. The mandatory Connect homework was annoying (and also $130) but helped for exams. VERY test heavy, but I only needed the study guides to get As. Final group project is pretty light too. Definitely enjoyed the class more than I thought I would!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor MacKenzie was great! I took the hybrid Accounting I class with her, and the guided notes helped you to do well on the practice problems in class. She tries to start the class with fun brain teasers and the classes don't last the whole period. I strongly suggest taking ACCT with Prof. MacKenzie.

idk if all the other reviews just were horrid test takers, but this was actually one of my lowest effort classes. read the syllabus, watch the lectures, do the practice in the notes, show up to class (or not honestly) and u will be fine. group project was annoying but manageable, plus done by thanksgiving. boring teacher but what can you do...
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly just avoid this professor, your grade is based on a few exams and the material given to practice for them are not helpful at all
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The person saying the other reviews are just people being sexist, as a female, I can confirm that is false. She just sucks—Period.

Those of you who are coming in to take a pretty easy class. Well think again, this prof sucks. Tests are terrible, material isn't helpful and weighing of each category is ridiculous. HOMEWORK THING ALSO COSTS $130 dollars.

Prof. Makenzie is nice and truly wants students to succeed. The class met once a week, so expect a lot of Connect HW and quizzes on your own time. It is VERY exam-heavy (3 tests = 65% of grade). It is hard to recover from one bad test score, so study hard. I ended with a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Mackenzie is a fantastic professor! She makes herself available for extra help sessions and was very clear on what it would take to succeed in the class. Would take again for sure.
Midterm tests and final exam account for the majority of the grade. You can have 100 on homework and quizzes and still do badly in the class. Proud to say I got out of this class, barely.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ignore reviews saying she's "cocky", they are sexist, she has no more ego than any other prof. "Flipped classroom", lectures posted and practice in person. She's a decent lecturer, exams are super easy if you just watch the videos, show up to class, and do the homework (I did this and studied very little otherwise, breezed through).
The professor was nice and caring, and always got to know the students. The only issue was that grades were test-heavy. Study guide was helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor MacKenzie was good in the beginning of the semester, but after exam 1 something changed. Weekly meetings were not at all engaging. Exams worded extremely weird and did not include examples from the lectures. Very quick to respond to emails but overall would not recommend at all, not even to my worst enemy.
SO ARROGANT If youre wanting to take this class b/c it is online do not. genuinely not worth it.

A nightmare class. She is rude, attitude, and cocky. Why is she cocky? Exactly. Idk. Typically an A student but she sucked. The person saying she tries to get to know her students is false. she will send out one email to everyone asking how they are and change the name out and then probably never respond again even if you do. do not take.

Most of the other below 3 comment sum up her personality. She has an ego and a horrible attitude. Grades distribution is simple, just straight up quizzes and exam. Homeworks dont even help and they are on connect. The connect itself costs like $100+, and also super annoying to do, but this is like only 10-15 % if the grade.

DONT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. SHE ABSOLUTELY SUCKS. GRADES ALMOST SOLELY ON TESTS AND DOSENT EVEN PROVIDE PROPER MATERIAL FOR IT.


SAVE YOURSELF FOR THIS TRASH PROF
She like doesn't teach or answer questions, she's just passive aggressive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took the online ACCT 2101 course. There are 3 midterms (honor lock is used) and each is 20% of your grade. She has recorded lectures, weekly (open note) quizzes, and Connect assignments. Course is not too difficult if you put in effect; Prof Mackenzie is super responsive over email.
Pretty good class...took it async and was pretty manageable. She makes accounting pretty easy and is really understanding. Try's to get to know students too.

This class was hybrid this year. The class itself is not too difficult; the lectures are online with a weekly in-person class which is really helpful. The exams aren't that hard, and you are done by thanksgiving. It can take quite a while to connect all the concepts together, but once that happens the course shouldn't be hard.

dont take her, she is just so boring and very monotone, and with accounting this literally made it the most impossible thing to focus on. the class is very test heavy and you need to do good on the exams. i would honestly just wait and take it another semester with a different prof shes just not good at teaching.

All she gives you are guided notes and even if you can do them/understand them they do not help on the exams. she uses extremely wordy and difficult questions as if this isnt an introductory level class. take another prof if possible. literally your whole grade is based off of exams. she also rude
attitude problem. would suggest taking another prof. but she wasn't the worst. extremely test heavy, but there's no final so at least we're done by Thanksgiving break.

(Hybrid) She has a sassy attitude but if you never go to her for help it's not a problem. I took accounting in hs so it was easy to relearn/understand. Guided notes are KEY to do. Some classes she goes over content not in the guided notes that will be on the exams. Great if ur not trying to learn (IE student) n just want an easy, independent class
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof MacKenzie is chill the work each week is light of just watching videos for lecture, doing an online quiz, and doing the online assingment. Lecture in person is also useful shell do practice problems and re explain the concepts from the last weeks lecture. Exams were easy usally about 20-25 mcq and 2 written questions.

The only thing this class taught me was to FIGHT for my right to be educated. The course material including kaltura videos was inaccessible and prevented from me throughout the whole semester which was half the class.

Prof MacKenzie is a fantastic teacher and it is clear she cares about her students. As long as you pay attention in class and review your notes before the tests, you will be fine. The homework assignments are nothing like the tests, so don't stress about them.

Easy to follow lectures with guided notes, and at first you may not get the concepts but asking her during or after class makes it really easy for it to click. The tests aren't hard but it would be nice if we could get them back when reviewing answers just to see what we got wrong. Lectures did get boring sometimes but the guided notes clutched up

MacKenzie was a great teacher! I didn't know anything about the subject going into it, but she teaches accounting in a way that is very understandable. It's easy to drift off class, but I would pay attention to the notes in lecture, as they are much easier to understand live. The tests are mostly mcq. We got a guest speaker and free pizza once too.

3 midterms + a final each worth 25%, but she dropped the lowest one. Homework was worth 25%. 

Attendance wasn't mandatory, but you need it to do the notes. Bring the notes on Canvas to class and fill them out during lecture. Understand the packets and you've got an A on the test. Take professor Mackenzie if you want to understand accounting.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests are hard. Notes are useless. DO NOT take with her. TAKE other prof. Especially online section.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class has 3 exams and the Final (lowest one of the 4 is dropped). I recommend redoing the notes on your own to study. Make sure to know what the Journal Entire for each transaction on the notes is even if it's not stated. You don't have to read the textbook for the class but it's a good tool for extra help.

Good lecturer and clearly explains the material.  The homework assignments can take a bit of time but they also over prepare you in a sense.  The 3 midterms are very easy as long as you make an effort to study a bit and you can opt out of the final with an A.  Overall a really manageable and well taught class

It took ACCT 2101 online with Dr. Makenzie. She is an excellent teacher and her TA was amazing. The class is difficult but Dr. Makenzie was always reachable by email and very willing to answer any questions.

Lack of clear instruction for activities and exams are very difficult even if you memorize all her slides. Otherwise she is really sweet and does provide a little extra credit, especially towards the end of the semester. I didn't use the textbook. I do feel like I learned a ton but be prepared to memorize a ton and work extra hard if you want an A.

Accounting is a very hard subject to learn for the first time, however Prof M makes lectures super accessible, easy to follow along, and detailed. Her guided notes were amazing resources to use. She is welcoming and will go over things as many times as possible to make sure you understand. She is the best teacher for first time learners.

Professor Mackenzie is awesome! She is highly knowledgable in the content of the class and provides all of the resources necessary to be successful. Attendance is not mandatory, but lecture notes are not posted online, so going to lectures is necessary to understand the material.
The course is overall light, concepts are easy, but the exams particularly the multiple choice can be quite tricky. Class average is usually around 75-80% and there's no curve.

Take notes during live lectures and when watching the recorded lectures. For the readings, I recommend focusing on what is taught in the recorded and live lectures rather than the entire chapter. She gives as much partial credit on tests, and is always available for questions. Great prof! She made it clear what you needed to do to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: shes a bad communicator. she doesnt answer any questions about exams, the most she tells you is how many questions there are. the only thing besides lectures and exams are assignments but they have 0 relevance in preparing for the exam or understanding the concepts. its not a hard class but everything is so convoluted and inconvenient to do/study
not the worst thing ever but it gets frustrating sometimes how she explains certain concepts or questions about assignments, you need a lot of extra commitment to get an A

Its an easy B like someone else said here, the content is super easy but the questions she derives from the content for Exams is based on her experience as an auditor so there is a leap in difficulty due to it requiring real-life experience & a ton of professional judgement, which you don't have because you most likely arent an experienced auditor

Has very little experience teaching so does not understand what would or would not be beneficial for students to know for assignments and exams. Can't really explain concepts beyond the definition in the slides/book or with a very simple example. Take this class if you already have some familiarity with auditing or you will feel lost due to hw/exam

She won't answer any questions about the test, review sessions are all Q's and no A's. A good chunk of the questions on the exam are convoluted, weirdly worded questions that require mental gymnastics. The class is an easy B but anything more will require you to spend a lot of time on this class and memorize paragraphs of definitions verbatim.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: What an awesome professor! Professor MacKenzie provided lectures with guided notes that made the class a breeze to follow. The material could get somewhat tricky for homework, but going back to the lectures was very helpful. She is very clear regarding her expectations, which made the class very straightforward.

I had Professor MacKenzie for Accounting 1 and Audit. I really enjoyed taking her! She is extremely knowledgeable, and I really could tell that she cares about her students. I feel like I learned a lot from both classes. Her tests were very fair and the notes were very helpful.

Dr. Mackenzie was really nice and caring towards her students. Her lectures were dry and she would just go over the facts. Very rarely did she ever explain things and when she did it was confusing. I left the class with a bunch of random knowledge but not a substantial understanding of Accounting at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: She gives out packets for each chapter, and they are SO helpful!! She presents the information in a very straightforward way. Class isn't math heavy and really intuitive. She gave a little extra credit every once in a while on quizzes or tests. Super nice and gives great explanations.
class is pretty easy + mackenzie is a pretty good teacher. I would definitely take it with her if you have the chance.
Amazing professor, Gives a tons of extra credit. My only complaint is that she cancels class regularly and posts online lectures instead.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really good professor. Provides amazing notes. Has a tendency to cancel classes and keeps online classes instead. However, overall lectures are very clear. The exams are similar to practice questions give during class. posted a 5 % extra credit lab and also gave a 10 point extra credit question during exam.

i think people aren't noting that her notes are actually really good. I learned a LOT from them, really they are the best way my friends and I learned the content for 2020. I understand the async part wasn't excusable but yall at least give credit where credit is due.

One of the least professionally run things I have ever been a part off. Exams run by TAs without guidance and a majority of lectures where canceled without makeup. Enough extra credit given to help guarantee an A, but I would recommend anyone else so you can actually learn the material. Complete self-study, but lecture videos provided.

Honestly don't understand the hate. She is basically async but her lectures are great and if you really lock in you can easily get the content. This class was still pretty hard in my opinion especially the hw but the extra credit and curve at the end makes getting an A easy. A low stress class where you can focus on learning material which is great

Everyone is undercutting the fact that you do not necessarily need ECE 2020's knowledge to succeed in future ECE classes, so it is absolutely okay in my honest opinion that she is somewhat inactive in class so long as we get A's, seriously. It's not that deep.

She curves super generously so you will probably get an A, but you will come out very unprepared for the future. This is why she has decent reviews, her classes are always super easy and she turns them all remote with pre recorded lectures. Paying 17k out of state tuition for this level of teaching is embarrassing. Do not take for 2020.

Lectures basically all online (as other reviews say), some are Zoom and others are prerecorded videos from years ago. Notes are spread across multiple different places so it's hard to compile and understand everything. Midterm 1 content is easy but gets way harder after. Not hard to get an A but came out of the class feeling unprepared for future

Nowhere to be seen. In-person class, but provides online pre-recorded lectures or disorganized handwritten notes. Important information is often hidden in multiple paragraphs of written fluff. Made it very difficult to learn the material.

She registers her classes as in person but then moves them to remote EVERY SINGLE SEMESTER. As someone who needs to be in person to learn, it is extremely frustrating. She just posts pre recorded lecture videos as if it was always planned to do this. I went into ece 2031 knowing very little. Avoid at all costs, take a prof who actually teaches

This class was more difficult than it needed to be. It was listed as a synchronous course, but the professor stopped giving lectures after the first week. Tests weren't bad, as they were similar to the mock exams given. Overall, I got a good grade but did not learn much.

No prior knowledge for class- the first unit's lectures all explained it well but after that became more confusing and harder to follow with lacking explanations and only recorded lecture videos to follow. Felt harder than it should have to learn the content properly and get help for it. Didn't learn much. Self study course as someone else said.

Professor Bhattacharya curves generously (more than she states), so most students get an A. However, she was often absent and her lectures unclear. Homework, labs, and midterms are tough and graded harshly, but the final has enough extra credit to help your grade. Fine if you just want credit, but not ideal for building a strong foundation.

Lecture videos were fine and sometimes helped/gave the answers to the homework. Labs were straightforward and not that long. The first exam caught me off guard due to the length so had to lock in after that. Make sure you have time to watch 3 hour videos for each lecture over the summer.

Course was very hands off. Async 2 weeks in and self studying is default. TA's did majority of all grading, to be precise, all grading I believe. Recorded/posted lectures were helpful when self studying. Tests were difficult and open book (so moderately hard with notes) with mock exams posted before the tests. A self study course tbh.

This class should not have been as difficult as it was. It's tough to learn online when the prof isn't really accessible and everything is async.

Other than that, her videos are pretty good and the tests aren't too bad. She is also caring, gave me 2 extensions after I emailed her.

Took her class online during the summer. She hosted class during the first week, but never did so again. All we got for the rest of the semester were lecture recordings from years ago at 360p quality. Class/content itself is not bad, and her "mock exams" are very similar to the actual exams. She also allows cheat sheets, so the tests weren't bad.
This professor makes the class async 2 weeks in. She dors not match with the textbook so you can't get outside help. She disappeared man this sucks. World class education my ass.
I had no prior knowledge going into this class but her explanations are amazing. Take her if you can for any course ever

Very prepared, well organized. Also good at explaining the material but be prepared to have online zoom lectures. Attendance is not mandatory and she opens a zoom call every day and records every lecture.
She's patient and nice. Recommend.

She's nice and explains things well, but where is my professor man. This class started synchronous remote and is now asynchronous. You can catch her on office hours, but they've been changing from 3pm to 8am. This class should be easy and I might just be dumb because I'm struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: HW is much harder than the topics covered in the lecture, but the exams are very similar to the mock exams she gives (but slightly harder). This is a class you should probably not take online since there is so much info to cover. Otherwise, the prof is chill.

Probably would have been better in person but this class was run very poorly online. Be prepared for random assignment dates, policies that change at a moment's notice, and unclear instructions for all labs.
This professor did a great job of teaching circuit analysis. She couldn't always attend the class in person but her online lectures were extremely helpful when studying for exams.

Very interesting course and Bhattacharya's notes are very organized and easy to follow. She frequently cancels classes, we probably only met in person around 50% of the time this semester. She is very accommodating and moved midterms and homework deadlines when the class requested. Overall I enjoyed it, but her zoom lectures can be boring.
Explained material very clearly and set expectations upfront. Two midterms and a final that accounted for 70% of the grade but weren't particularly difficult.

Amazing lectures. All of them are recorded so catching up is very easy.
Exams are super fair.
However be prepared to have randomly canceled classes (Online instead).

She is very nice and is good at teaching this class. The exams were very easy, the labs were pretty easy, and the homework was hard, leading to a high GPA and averages. But, if I am paying good money to attend a university, I want my teachers to be in person teaching. She fully left halfway through the year, leaving us with a TA who I felt bad for.
Was absent most of the semester, but was accessible essentially immediately to make up for it with good prerecorded lectures

She was, while she was around, a very nice and caring teacher. She frequently cancelled class but always had a video lecture or zoom call ready. However, she went on medical leave very early on into the semester, and left a grad TA (who, granted, was an awesome dude) in charge of the class. If you're bad with online lectures, you won't learn much.

Prof Nivedita is one of the best teachers I had at Tech! She reached out to me after I performed poorly on a test and explained how I could do better going forward! I haven't seen a more caring Professor! Her class notes are also amazing and she explains hard concepts clearly.

I took her a few years ago and she was very nice and caring (responds quickly but cancels every class), but does not teach you the material. I know it can be tempting to take a class for an easy A but if you care about your education, please do not take her for 2040. I am still struggling to catch up after having her as a professor in 3040/3043

Amazing professor! Would take her again and again. Everything was so clear and her notes were so detailed and clear as well. Truly enjoyed the class! She's caring and approachable, and always ready to help. Class was asynchronous and had many TAs, which was great! Tests reflected exactly what we learned in the lectures, very useful material!

Prof. Bhattacharya is a very caring professor and can explain tough concepts to students very well. However, she has a habit of turning classes originally advertised as in-person to solely online classes. She has done this numerous times in different classes too. Once again, really good professor, but that is my only criticism.

A good amount of lectures ended up being remote, and she posts all the materials in terms of notes, slides, and lecture videos which is very helpful. The lectures are very slow pacing and have a lot of examples which could be good or boring.

Dr. Bhattacharya is the only professor I've ever had that has cared enough about me to check in after tests. She has an awesome sense of humor, & always made time to meet with me when I needed it! Her class wasn't easy, & I felt that it got disorganized towards module 6 & the final exam - but over all the professor alone made this class! 10/10 prof

She is the best. Extremely helpful at all times, very kind and really just wants to help you learn. She is very quick in email response time and is very willing to help you with any questions on the homework and is super understanding. Class went from synchronous online -> async but her video lectures are good and she explains concepts well.

Prof. Bhattacharya is an amazing teacher and her class notes are the best! She provides a lot of learning resources and explains concepts very clearly. But what stands out most of all in my opinion is her respect for the students.

Prof Bhattacharya is extremely knowledgeable and very good at explaining difficult concepts. I understand problems so much better once she explains it. She is also very kind and understanding and helped me with a homework very late at night before it was due.

Overall, Prof Bhattacharya is a great lecturer and very caring as well as understanding.  She patiently answers any student's question during lecturer and with minimal wait time outside of lecture (i.e. piazza/email).  The only reason I don't give a 5/5 is because she lectured online the whole semester; the class was supposed to be in-person.

She was a true gem virtually. Whenever I needed some clearing up or had a question on piazza, she answered in LESS THAN AN HOUR. Her lecture videos were very well done. Even when I had technical issues on the first exam, she let me email my exam to her with no complications, she was totally understanding. I WISH I COULD TAKE HER AGAIN!

One of the best professors at Georgia Tech hands down. Professor Bhattacharya is very caring and she really just wants you to understand the material. If you have any problems she will understand and help. The only downside is that the class was fully online this semester, but at least the lectures are recorded.
Easy but asynchronous lectures make hard to learn. We did not finish the material in time which was later in 3043 so I wasn't well prepared.

She's good at lecturing, but is so lazy. Class went from in-person, to online zoom calls, to asynchronous classes from PREVIOUS semesters, and she cancelled review sessions over and over again. All of her excuses is because she's "feeling unwell."

Professor Bhattacharya was very knowledgeable and delivered clear and informative lectures.
She doesn't go too fast, and you can tell she cares about her students. Also answers questions thoroughly.
Very clear on how to succeed in the class, and she provides numerous resources like class notes and practice
exams to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bhattacharya is one of the best professors I have had at GT. She is very accessible and helpful. She will respond to emails very quickly, and if your question can not be answered via email, she will set up a private call with you. As a non-ECE major, I felt she did a fantastic job at making the content understandable and not too complex.

This is my second course with Prof Bhattacharya. She is extremely knowledgeable and very compassionate. Her lectures and notes are amazing and she explains hard concepts in a clear manner. Her classes always fill up very fast so register early!

Prof Bhattacharya is the best teacher I have had at Tech! Although she was ill this semester, she did video calls all the time to help students. She once hopped on a call with me at 11pm on a Sunday as we had a HW due. She really wants her students to succeed and is very passionate about teaching and the subject matter. Her class notes are the best

She is a very lenient grader and gives a lot of extra credit, but lectures are a drag and poorly delivered. They started as going into class to watch a video call, and turned to watching asynch recordings of previous semesters' lectures instead, making the class feel very unpersonalized. Many of my classmates and I have never even seen her face.

Really caring professor, even gave extra credit opportunity. Really cares about teaching. Homework was reasonable, and the projects. Grading on exams was reasonable. Would def recommend taking her again!

Professor Bhattacharya did a good job overall at teaching ECE 2040. Class grades tended to be pretty high, but this semester most of the course ended up being taught remote asynchronously (although it was listed as fully in-person). So a lot of it ended up being self-taught through videos and notes. Lecture was about 2.5 h/w and homework was 2 h/w.

Prof Bhattacharyas lectures and notes are amazing. She was very accommodating throughout the semester and I learnt way more than I expected. The videos were very helpful in studying for the exams and overall the course prepared me for a career in Computer Engineering.

Bhattacharya is one of the most caring professors, always willing to help students or move deadlines/exams upon request. However, my experience turned quickly from (expected) in person to fully online asynchronous. She would just post lectures from previous semesters which led to lack of interaction/motivation. Tainted my experience.
Learned so much. Difficult class but Bhattacharya makes it much better. Class was very flexible but don't fall behind
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's so kind and caring. I found out that I had three midterms land on one day (one of them being for her class), so I emailed her about it on a Saturday night, and 10 minutes later, the test was moved forward a week. Her lectures are great: she makes relatively hard concepts easy to understand, and if you ever need help, she's there for you.

Dr Bhattacharya is the G.O.A.T.  simply the best. She taught a rather difficult online semester and was remarkably patient and understanding. I never had a more caring professor at Tech. Take all her courses.
Dedicated to teaching and the university, but not very responsive when communicating over email or in person.
She's the best. If you can take her. Made 2035 and a tough online semester so much more bearable. she is the best.
Legitimately one of the most caring and understanding profs ive ever had. Theres no better teacher for 2035.
One of the best professors at Tech!! She has no flaws as an instructor (at least, I haven't seen one yet)
The class is heavy in material, but Professor explains concepts very well. I really enjoyed this class and learned a lot
She's super caring and really wants you to succeed. She can go super fast during lectures, but always willing to answers questions. Take her!

She's an amazing professor. She cares so much about her students, gives back great feedback, is very knowledgable and the class is a breeze if u pay attention. For ECE 2020 I can say for certain you should take her class.

Really caring professor and provides practice content for midterms. The HWs come from the textbook and if you don't understand something, she is always willing to help outside of class. Honestly, one of the best ECE professors here at Tech.

Professor Bhattacharya is the most caring professor I've had so far at Tech. She is super considerate and accessible out of class, her lectures are clear and her notes are easy to read. Definitely the best ECE 2040 professor.

Prof Bhattacharya has so far been the best professor that I have met at Tech. She is very caring and considerate of her students in these difficult times. Her lectures are amazing and very clear and her notes are very well written. I had a great learning experience and she was always there to clear any doubt almost any time of the day. TAKE HER.

Best Prof I've had so far! She is so caring and makes sure everyone understands! Will go out of her way to answer any and all questions! It is true that it is an easy class compared to the other sections, but if you're worried you won't learn, fret not! The learning is still there! The HWs are especially informative and the labs were neat! TAKE HER

She is literally the most caring and nicest Professor I have ever had in my entire life. This is my first year at tech during a stressful time, and it is so nice to have someone as caring and kind as her as a professor. She constantly helps and reaches out to her students and is very attentive to where we are struggling.

She was so sweet and really cared about all of her students passing. I had when everything was online and she would answer/check any of my work or questions. She was super understanding and always helped TAKE HER

Probably the best professor I've had at tech. She cared a lot for her students and the material and took the time to explain everything in detail. One of my homeworks didn't upload correctly and she emailed me to let me know and gave me extra time to submit it. She was always there if you had a question! 100% recommend
Prof Bhattacharya is very kind and caring and spent a lot of time outside of the class to help me. Her lectures are great and she provides a lot of supplementary material to study.

This class had a fun theme and was very light. We had 3 major assignments that were all given 3 weeks before they were due. Grading was easy and clear, and the attendance/participation grade comes from discussion posts in Canvas. I had a good time in her class she is very flexible!
She was extremely caring and nice to all students. Made it very easy to understand her and the lectures were entertaining.
very accommodating
Really nice, got a lot of free time during class, cares a lot about the subject (picks good themes), nice grader.

She was an amazing professor. Her English class topics are always so interesting. She was always so caring and kind. She really fostered a love for English that I never really had before college. She doesn't do book reading, instead more focuses on movies, excerpts, theories, shows, etc. Also, her feedback is tasteful and helpful. :)
She was one of the best teachers I've had here at Tech. Definitely take her class if you can.
Professor Dey Roy was amazing! She truly wants to see you succeed, and found a way to make a 5pm class enjoyable. As long as you write the papers and speak in class, you'll be totally fine!

I took Dr. Dey Roy's ENGL1102 class over the summer, and I absolutely loved it. Every day was interesting, and we frequently watched movie clips and had debates. Grade was based on a few major artifacts and one final portfolio. Extremely funny, kind, and accommodating professor, would 100% take her class again.

Dr. Dey Roy is one of the best professors I've had in all of literature. Our class focused on Disney's literature and critical analysis in the pieces. She definitely cared about the students, and helped everyone whenever necessary. Her grading was constructive and accommodating. Participate in class; it's worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Dey Roy was very caring and kind with students. The class was very fun and only had a few projects as grades and a final portfolio. What is needed to make an A is very clearly written in rubrics. We often watched movie clips and class discussion was a huge part of class. Occasional readings but no other homework besides that.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was super nice and cared for us a lot, but sometimes got slightly political. She never said anything outright, but the topics we discussed and her point of view could make you a little uncomfortable if you oppose her. However, I never had a problem with it, just kept my opinions to myself. She grades very easily and there are few assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Dey Roy was super kind and easy to talk to. Gave extensions and cares about what you have to say. Grading is pretty simple- 3 bigger assignments (one every month) and a final portfolio.

Dr. Dey Roy was an amazing professor that made this class particularly fun to take. She was very kind in grading and gave lots of feedback when you asked for it. She was also very accommodating with absences and extensions. As long as you show up to class regularly and participate you'll be set.
Best english teacher you could take. Really loves her students and is super clear on how to get an A and it takes very little work. Super easy class.

Her Disney theme was extremely engaging and the class was a lot of fun. You needed to be contributing to class discussions and there were a couple of readings spread throughout the semester, but overall I did not spend more than an hour outside of class every week. Fun class to be in!

Dr. Dey Roy was very kind and clearly knowledgable and passionate about what she taught. The class was quite easy, with most of the grade made up of three major assignments, and no final. We had readings and sometimes had to watch movies/clips before class, but other than that the class wasn't a major time commitment. I'd absolutely recommend her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Roy for CS2340. She was an amazing professor, very fair grader, great lecturer, and a genuinely caring person. Would recommend!
She was a very kind prof. The material was boring but the project was fun.

She seemed sweet but led to a huge amount of stress and uncertainty throughout. She failed to communicate, gave no support for the entirety of the project, and had material that was riddled with mistakes and inconsistencies. 
She misled about changing due dates, if she would regrade, and what we were being graded on. Workload was also insane.

Course is already poorly structured, but professor somehow makes it worse. Course relies on a group project where your group can make or break your grade. Lectures are super dense of information that is pointless outside a few filler assignments and exams that build off of a fraction of the group project (AKA 99% of your work). Hope for a good TA🙏
Helpful class. Easy A. Roy is pretty good.

The class is project-based with plenty of extra credit. You can choose your own team, and the projects are manageable with good planning, but they require a lot of learning outside of lectures. The midterm and final are fairly difficult due to the broad range of topics, though CRIB sheets are allowed and very helpful.

I would advise to take another professor for 2340. She gives a midterm and final exam on top of a pretty heavy workload for the projects. I did not learn much throughout the class. Grade depends on the TA you get for your project (some are not good). She is a very kind professor, but I think other sections are less work.

Prof is good, lectures are a bit boring, but the notes on them are good. I think she does a good job for what this class is. That being said 2340 is dependent on your group (I did not get a good one and TAs can only do so much) I really hated this class because of that. Make sure to fix your group by the 2nd sprint b/c you can't change after that.
Project based class that's an easy A if you get a good group. Prof. is caring and a good lecturer.

Caring professor, with too much work assigned. Sprint projects were very long, especially if your entire team wasn't 100% on board. That combined with extra work, exams, etc. was a lot to deal with. She also seems a bit jumbled sometimes, when lecturing especially early on in the semester when things are still getting going.
Just project based, a couple midterms but take home. Just focus on the projects and focus on participation.

Despite the course begin hybrid, Roy was a great professor. As long as all work is completed, it's difficult not to get an A, even with a bad group. The midterm consists of an individual portion (crib sheet allowed) and a project group portion. The final is completed as a group and is not difficult.

Roy is honestly a good prof, but this class is kinda hit or miss depending on your group. She's fair with grading and actually cares if you're struggling, but a lot of the work relies on your teammates pulling their weight. If you get a solid group, it's not bad, but if not good luck lol. I like that you can showcase your projects at the end.

If you are reading this, do not take Nimisha. Her sprint requirements are incredibly unclear and convoluted. This makes the assignments incredibly frustrating and time-consuming. On top of this, the tech stack (Android Studio) sucks. We learned literally nothing remotely applicable.

By far the most rage-inducing class I've taken. Please take Pedro

The Fall 2024 semester saw a hybrid online/in-person class, which was no fault of hers. She is clear on grading and the A is easy with a good group. One midterm, which is easy if you keep up. She is very accommodating in the event of getting a bad group (you can choose groups of 5-6). Project grades are dependent on TA evaluation. Okay course!

CS3300 this semester had a focus on AI, which lined up with Prof Roy's research focus. The group projects are manageable if you have solid teammates. This semester the criteria were very open ended which made it difficult to know exactly what we needed to complete. The emphasis on testing and AI seemed not fully baked sometimes too.

Genuinely isn't even Professor Roy's fault entirely. The class is poorly designed and your grade is entirely based off the random group you receive. Luckily for me I had an amazing randomly assigned team but for others they weren't so lucky loll. Roy is caring and she tried her best to make sure everyone got a decent grade. Bad class, nice prof.

The professor was a decent person, but the class structure was really awful. Lecture videos were incredibly long as opposed to something like 1332 where videos were max 13 minutes long. Hope you get a good group that are able to plan out sprints and not start them the weekend they are due.

Roy is a good professor, her in-person lecture reviews were nice. The project is manageable, as long as your team is willing to put in the work. Opportunities for EC as well. The only thing I did not like is the hybrid setup of the course, so if you want to really learn, you have to watch online lectures. Great professor, but try to avoid hybrid.
Prof Roy is great, but the async class is so not it if you actually want to learn the material.

I took this course in Fall 2023. This course is an easy A with Roy. There are a number of assignments that your group must complete throughout the semester, but none of them are hard. She was also very lenient with due dates. She seemed detached from the course, since the goal of the class is to have your group operate professionally with a client.
3300 was fun this semester. We used AI tools for developing projects. Would recommend.

Would've given a 2/5 a month ago, but has improved the structures of the course (Sprints 3 and 4 were clear, plus my familiarity with Android has increased in this time). The group project is challenging without much instruction, but the TAs were generally helpful. Though, she will not be teaching until Fall 2025.

Don't know if it's the professor perse, but the class is just implemented poorly. It's a hybrid course with a semester long group project, so unless you're doing this with friends, get ready for the majority not even trying in your group. The project is also very vague in what it wants from you and I learned very little from this course all in all.

Prof. Roy did a great job with the hybrid format, although I am not a fan of the format.  She figured out a balance between hybrid, providing long-form videos with in-depth notes while summarizing the important details in class. Getting a good team in class really helps.

Dr. Roy has insane expectations. The Sprints are vague and confusing at best and have tight deadlines, not the mention the ridiculous amount of required features and the pedantic guidelines for the GitHub repo. She does little to help when it comes to group conflicts and shows little to no sympathy for struggling groups. Take pedro.
The professor is very caring towards the success of the students. I have an amazing group and we are loving the project.

absolutely horrible. tas are unhelpful and don't care about the class, and each sprint has functionality we've never ever learned in class. rubrics and instructions don't match, and we all end up stressed asf before the deadlines because no one answers helpfully on ed discussion

Taking 2340 in the hybrid model (75 min/wk). Sprints contain a significant amount of work and contain very specific requirements in order to receive full points. On top of that, we are expected to watch 2+ hours of lectures and complete time consuming modules weekly, equating to more work than the non-hybrid class. She's nice but avoid if possible.

agree with other reviewers in that ur experience rly depends on whether u get a good group or not. MAKE SURE u get a good group (or switch) so ur not bogged down by project work all sem like me 😭 class is p hands off and material isn't too difficult, but assignments + tech (android studio) can get annoying and stack up if ur not on top of things
Enjoying the class so far! I recommend but your success is dependent on how good a group you get assigned/you choose.
Prof. Roy has been great. The course is hybrid, so it is a bit difficult to manage things around teammates. But overall, I'm enjoying this course and learning a lot.

Prof. Roy is overall a great Prof! She cares for students and tries to make the lessons enjoyable. Not really her fault, but if you get a bad group, this class will suck (groups are assigned somewhat randomly and hard to change). The exams are not bad as long as you make some effort to study. Overall I recommend taking classes with her.

Roy seems like a reasonable professor, but she advocates for a strange class structure. The main project has little relevance to the design patterns taught in class, is very tedious without a competent group, and seems like just busywork for the most part. Also, requirements for diagrams and assessments are often unclear.

Pretty easy class with a group project, 1 individual midterm, 1 group midterm, and a group final. There's some participation here and there and extra credit almost every class. Really sweet prof. who genuinely cares about her students and is trying to make the course better and more rewarding for everyone.
Great professor. Design patterns and principles are industry standard topics that I learned. Project was cool and rewarding but had a steep learning curve.

Good professor, but terrible class structure. There was very little correlation between what we did in class and the project implementation and TAs were largely unknowledgeable and unhelpful, which made the sprints basically impossible. Take Pedro, your life will be so much easier.
Professor Roy is a good professor. She's a good option for 2340 and pretty accommodating to students and their busy schedules.

This class is probably the worst I've taken here during my time at Tech. Attendance for this class is mandatory. The class is at 8 AM, and if you miss five classes, they will fail you. How nonsensical. This class is the epitome of "this could have been an email." If you have to make attendance mandatory, make your lectures worth my time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really nice professor who really cares about students. For instance, a project was due on one day (on living schedule), but there was a canvas mistake where it said it was due 5 days later, so she moved the deadline to 5 days later to accommodate. Some of the content (design patterns) is boring, but the class teaches app development and Firebase.
Enjoying the class so far. Recommend her.
Just a good professor.

The course contents in this class can sometimes be mundane but you can really see that Professor Roy put in a lot of effort to make the class fun with the post lecture Quizizzes and group activities. The group project ended up being very fun for me and not only I learned a lot more about design patterns but also made some really good friends along.

Roy was definitely the nicest professors at GT. She cares about students' feedback about the course and would change her lecture styles accordingly. She was not the most interesting lecturer, but I can't blame her for it as the course itself is very boring. The group project was fun, but the TAs were not the best at the most times.

Her as a professor was fine for me, she had decent lectures and provided EC in class. But, beware the group you choose, try to meet your teammates and choose them before they assign you teammates because some people in this class are absolutely useless but not the professors fault. It's just the TAs are the backbone of the class so good luck.

Outstanding professor to take for a class that people only appreciate after getting an internship. There are a lot of people who are just rude to a really good Professor. Professor Roy makes the class interesting and while there are a lot of work, people need to keep in mind this is not a 2 credit hour course.
She makes a boring class like 2340 fun by her lectures and quizizz.
She is very nice and caring about the learning process of the students. She is very flexible too.
Changes grading criteria last minute and doesnt excuse assignments for valid things like interviews. Heavy accent too. Don't take her.
Prof Roy is so caring and she teaches so well.  The class is also fun because of quizziz.
Great teacher!
Professor Roy teaches complex topics very well. I loved having her as my teacher.
Useless class, dumb grading scheme for project
Professor Roy is a great teacher. She is very enthusiastic about the material and teaching. She really cares about the students. Highly recommend.

2340 is an awful class, but Professor Roy did a good job running it, and was very responsive to questions and overall helpful. The midterms and "mini-assessments" don't weigh a lot but require you to actually learn the "content", which led to poor performance that seemed to bother her more than it did the students. A fine professor for a bad class.

LOVED this professor. She was so kind and helpful and provided us with whatever we needed to succeed in the class.
