Content wasn't the most interesting, but we learned a good amount and were able to come out of the course more prepared. Lots of extra credit opportunities and pretty relaxed assignment load.

Pretty great teacher. Was very receptive to feedback and genuinely wanted to improve the course. Lectures are pretty fast, but I found that to be a plus. Overall, 2340 as a class just sucks, but Prof. Roy tried her best to make it somewhat enjoyable.

This class is incredibly boring and monotonous(regardless of professor). It was her first time teaching, so she mainly just read off the slides adding to the boredom. The tests are easy but the individual portion of them are focused on incredibly mundane details that are hard to memorize. Overall, not the worst professor, just an awful class.
Amazing Professor. Highly recommend her classes.

This was her first semester teaching a large class, and she could benefit from some better content organization. Also, taking away crib sheets for exams was the dumbest they ever did on this course, as quizzes/midterms now test on the most little insignificant details.
She is a great professor and helped me understand the practicalities of early stages of software engineering well.

By the nature/structure of the class itself, it feels pretty boring. Stopped going to lectures a few weeks in. Before both of the mini-assessments, all you need to do is go through the lecture slides a few times. Kind of poor classroom management, but that's also because everyone was super rude and would talk over her, so not all her fault at all.
He explains things well in lecture. The exams align with the lecture well and there are a lot of practice problems that help.

Made physiology very interesting and made topics relatable. Exams were straightforward, but some questions were difficult. Final exam was light, 60% of it came from previous midterms. You can do well by going to class or self-studying with the book. Homework = easy grade booster. Pre-lecture quizzes were annoying timing-wise, but he dropped a lot.

the course is a lot of memorization but he seems passionate what he is talking about. the tests are pretty straightforward as long as you know all of the learning objectives and almost everything on every slide. he will emphasize in class what is important to know so that is helpful and he does try to help his students

Dr. Birol's lectures were extremely helpful, and I felt that exams accurately reflected content taught in class. Pre-readings were required for this class. If I did not understand a pre-reading, I knew that if I went to class Dr. Birol would clarify it for me. Great teacher!!
To do well, attendance isn't necessary. Just rely on the textbook.

Birol is kind/willing to help students succeed. Lectures are boring (not really his fault, physiology is just boring). Homework/assignments are easy grade boosters. Exam questions are SO TRICKY. Read very carefully and prepare to study hard for all the tests. Several midterm questions reused for the final, but still plenty of new ones.

Dr. Birol co-taught this class with Dr. Richards. Birol is clearly passionate about biology. I went to 70% of the lectures and made an A. He is a good speaker and helps us understand material better. The only issue is that some of the exam questions were based on what was said in lecture and not found in the slides, but it wasn't that big of a deal

co-taught w/ robbie richards. birol focused on animals and was generally better. didn't ramble as much. he tries to draw focus to what goes on the test, but there's just a great amount of content. recitation is helpful. some tests focus on what is explicitly talked about in class and not clearly shown on slides, but attendance isn't mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: he's clearly very knowledgeable about the subject, but sometimes the lectures are hard to follow solely based on the obnoxious amount of material for the class. there is a lot of reading and sometimes the questions on exams were worded very weirdly. other than that, he's actually a nice guy and would crack a joke every now and then.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Taught w/ Richards (who carried). Goes through lecture material very fast but often explained it in a confusing manner. so long as you take notes on the readings(especially if birol is teaching for that day) and lecture, study LOs and do practice exams you'll get an A. TAs office hours/recitations/exam review sessions helped get an A too.

This class has been my favorite class at tech yet! Dr. Birol has a very fair grading policy in my opinion. Exams are not weighted too heavily which allows room for improvment. I did not start the course off strong, but if you attend lecture, an A is very likley. Plus, his lectures are great. He relates topics to things in the real world!

Did not teach genetics that well, and the tests were way too long. Gave extra credit though. The homework was also very difficult, but you get two attempts, and the first attempt tells you the answer.

Before each lecture, students are expected to read a "chapter" of the assigned textbook. The readings weren't hard but they were dense. He reiterated the readings in class so lectures were redundant. He does go over homework/assignment questions in class (if time permits); however, sometimes the powerpoint and the readings contradicted each other.

Consistently admitted to not knowing information he was supposedly teaching so I ended up learning more from TAs/ the internet than him. He is very distant from students and the grading criteria was extremely vague. Co-taught this course with Torres and there was little discussion between the two about the logistics of this, creating confusion.

He is very knowledgeable in biology, but is not always the greatest at explaining the material. The class has a lot of material that is overwhelming to memorize and learn, and tough. exams. Hard to study for exams because they cover so much content, and you are tested on some minute details. TAs were decently helpful.

I had Dr. Birol once before in 1108 and I was excited to have him for physiology but was incredibly disappointed by this class. His lecturing made this one of the most boring classes I have ever taken and the grading was heavily based on tests that asked questions that were so specific, making it difficult to do well despite studying heavily.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the best professors I've had at GT. I've had him for both BIOS 1107 and 1108, and I recently had him over the summer for BIOS 3755. He is very passionate about his teaching, explains content in depth, and welcomes questions form the students. Attend class because the powerpoints are posted but not everything as in depth as class.

Great professor, this was one of the most interesting classes I've taken at Tech. Dr Birol is a very good teacher, but his lecture slides are awful. You will not do well if you do not go to class because the lecture slides do not contain much content. Tests are hard but if you go to class you'll be fine. He recycles test questions for the final.

A lot of the tests had extra credit and all you really had to do was do the readings and finish the learning catalytics to get a good grade.  Stopped going to class towards the ends but still did good on the tests cuz of the readings.

I never really went to class and studied two days before my exam. Just read the textbook and take notes you will be fine. Heavy on memorization though. Homeworks/participation is graded on participation not the actual grade which was really good. The homework questions were similar to the ones on the test and he reuses questions for the final!

Great professor, used recycled test questions on final. However, if you don't like reading, you're going to fall behind fast. Bit of an accent, but didn't interfere with my learning. Also, you're going to have to spend 12 dollars for the program he uses for homework. Taught the course with Prof. Datta
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are based off of things he emphasizes in class so make sure you go. Take really good notes in class and study them + the powerpoints and you'll get an A. Tests are kind of hard/detail heavy, but the final is really easy because probably 80% of the final is recycled test questions (which you have access to for studying).

cares so much about the students and the material. he does tend to get distracted and go on tangents, but he is such a good lecturer. i recommend using flashcards for any classes he teaches because it's definitely a lot of memorization and understanding of the material. loved taking a class with him and wish i could take more.

Dr. Birol is a great professor. He is truly passionate about what he teaches, and it only makes you more interested in the subject. His lectures contain a lot of information, but he explains it clearly and leaves time for questions. His tests are closed notes and do need a good amount of memorization, but if you go to class you should be fine.

The class has a lot of material that is nearly impossible to memorize and learn, with dense exams. The textbook is poorly written with grammatical errors and it is hard to study for exams due to the amount of content and because you are tested on the smallest details in the textbook. If you are looking for a simple class, do not take this one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class only just became closed note and that's obvious. There is far too much information to learn before exams and while he says he doesn't expect you to memorize the material, this is a lie. If you work hard, you will do well, but I would pick a different class if you're just looking for an easy A. There's also so much homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. He is extremely caring and understanding, and he is truly passionate about biology. The class is not bad at all if you pay attention and keep up with the material.

Very well-spoken and very passionate. The setup of the class is nice where you learn the content the night before and he teaches it the morning after (reinforcing knowledge). The class is now closed-notes, even though it was open-note in the past. Crib sheet on final. Textbook is tedious but worth it to read. Exams were not hard at all.

The textbook is extremely tedious to read. All the exams are just random details from the textbook. There's a lot of information and lectures move extremely fast. He's a great guy and very passionate about bio, but his lectures can get overwhelming with unnecessary information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing and passionate lectures. Be ready to STUDY STUDY and MEMORIZE. SO MUCH CONTENT! But a good professor!

This class is full of random details that you must find in the textbook. In person lectures don't help much as the exam asks the most minute and randomly detailed questions. You have to memorize the craziest small details that is not covered. Overall, I expected this class to build off 1107 or AP Bio but I couldn't be more wrong.

If this class is required for you, GOOD LUCK!! Horribly structured course with a bunch of non-correlating information. Lectures are all around useless, slides are horrendously formatted, key points conveniently cut-off. Very passive aggressive if you have questions. Exams are all random details from the readings, neglecting the bigger picture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures consisted of the same content covered by the textbook readings required to have been completed before class. Tests consisted of very specific questions from the textbook, oftentimes neglecting bigger topics from the course for smaller sections of the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
He's alright.
The class itself is not difficult, but most of the content feels useless.
In my opinion, lectures are only useful because he sometimes tells you what you should know/ not know what's on the test. Other than that, its pretty much useless. 
The tests contain specific textbook questions and other random information as well.

All information on tests comes from readings that are done outside of class. Lectures during class are vague and consist of reused pictures from the readings. Tests are not open-note anymore and questions on the test are very specific from the readings
I do not know much about Dr. Birol's lectures since I never went to class, but the online resources provided were more than enough to understand all the material required and tests were a breeze.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very poorly structured course with tons of content that is touched on once and never mentioned again. Although the tests are open-note, you have so little time it's not feasible to search through everything (I had ~400 pages by the end of the semester). Professor doesn't seem to care about students and just speeds through lectures

Dr. Birol is a great professor. He covers all the material you need to know in lecture which is nice. He also emphasizes the important concepts in class so you know what to write down/ study. He's very nice as well and engaging in class. Definitely recommend.

Dr. Birol was a good lecturer and was excited about what he was teaching. It is helpful to do the reading before class as the course has a lot of information, and he doesn't always cover everything in lecture. Overall, he's a good professor - the class is just a lot of information.

The class was very easy. Tests are online. zoom meetings of classes, making attendance, not mandatory. There are participation clicker points in the class, and there are several writing assignments all of which are fairly easy.

Great lecturer and passionate about his units within this course! Goes at a great pace (unlike Montoya) and wants students to thrive. He makes sure that everyone's questions are answered. He was definitely the BEST bio professor by a long shot! We were begging for him to come back at the end of the semester because Montoya was so rough.

Dr. Birol is a pretty decent professor. He's a bit more understanding than many other professors and does some things to account for students having off-days. He's also fairly interested in the course matter. However, the class itself is super information-heavy, so get ready to absorb a lot of info.

Emphasizes studying ABC but tests on XYZ ~500 slides of notes this semester of stuff to just memorize which sucked. You then get to the test, and after studying all the important things emphasized (all the steps of transcription/gene repression) you get asked only about genomes. Very frustrating because there are no practice exams or crib sheets.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Birol is an amazing professor! He can be very direct at times but he is truly passionate about this subject and that makes it a super enjoyable class. If you do the work in this class its not difficult to do well, just make sure you keep up with the readings and listen to the lectures, which you can come in person or join online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Birol was one of my favorite professors this year! He has an undeniable passion for the subject and is incedibly understanding. There is a lot of content on each exam, but if you read the textbooks and quiz yourself on the concepts and learning objectives, you'll turn out just fine. The scientist spoltights and LCs are nice grade cushions, too!

He honestly could be a little warmer to students but overall he's pretty straightforward with what you need to learn if you pay attention. He definitely isn't the type of person to hold ur hand the whole way but he's nice with the extra-credit and LCs to help boost grades. If you want to pass you need to work for it. Just wish content wasn't dense
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Birol is in fact clearly passionate about biology and his lectures are far more than just reading from a powerpoint. In fact, this class made me very intrigued about evolutionary and ecological biology. However, whoever made the final was so out of pocket for that. All our hard work for an exam that was mostly a topic we spent a couple days on.

I was excited for physiology after taking anatomy but this was an awful class with so much lecture content and reading that it wasn't even that helpful for the tests since they tested really specific things or processes. wouldn't recommend him for physiology
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Birol is fantastic! It is open-note and open-book because he places an emphasis on you learning the material. If you stop showing up to lectures halfway through the semester and Ctrl-F on every test, you won't do well though. It is a lot of info and you need to know some of it without needing to look it up. Pretty easy, highly recommend it!
He goes through a crazy amount of material and his exams test you on such specific information. It's hard to tell what will be on the tests. No study guide or practice tests.

Birol is one of the worst teachers I have ever had. He makes his tests overly difficult and is not open to the student's concerns. The test is in 50 minutes and I have to search through over 500 pages of notes so you're set up for failure. He doesn't respect students at all/very passive-aggressive. I would avoid him if you need to take BIOS 1108.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Birol is very passionate about biology, and while I did not care at all and only took this class because I had to, it did make it a bit more bearable. He taught the first and last units and I did the best on those two in terms of test grades. He is easy to reach and a solid guy all around

I was excited to take physiology but his lectures are so dense and he runs through them so fast that it's so hard to know exactly what to study for tests even if you combine the lectures with the readings.
Dr. Birol is the best professor I have ever had for biology. He is nice and the tests are not that hard. Highly recommend!

Lecture content is super heavy and feel like he's competing in a race to finish lectures as fast as possible - before you can even process one topic he's already moved onto a new one. Exams are MC/SA and the amount of material can be pretty overwhelming if you don't review every week. I was excited for this class but Birol really dulled my spirits
Great professor who is willing to explain concepts as much as needed. Lectures is very notes and discussion heavy, if you attend lecture the tests should be fairly easy.

Birol is a good professor but I would say the best part about the class is the resources. I was able to do well even as someone who does not love bio. His lectures are good but sometimes do not always cover all the information. Reading the sections and asking questions can for sure fill any gaps.

Easily one of the top profs to take for bio, and I'd take him again. Super chill, caring, gives extra credit opportunities if possible. Pay attention in class tho since certain topics that are glazed over once or heavily emphasized can still be mentioned on the exams. Email responses are prompt.Give back the same energy he gives and you'll be fine.

This class was taught with Dr. Harrison and I think Dr. Birol was better at explaining some of the concepts and more accessible and willing to discuss material out of class. He was new this semester but by halfway through the course you wouldn't be able to tell. The examples he goes over in lecture are the same as the ones he puts on the exams

Dr. Birol is extremely thoughtful and caring! He responds to emails, and always tried finding ways to explain material in a different way if you were confused. I didn't go to office hours a lot, but when I did, they were super helpful and you could tell that he cares a lot. He's also unintentionally funny, which made lectures fun. Loved it!

I dislike biology and this class did nothing to change that. On the other hand, it's a manageable A in the class. Make sure to stay on top of the written assignments and just use the website links from the syllabus, and you should end the class with an A. Make sure to participate! Attendance is not necessary at all. *(Taught with Colin Harrison)*
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Birol is a great professor! He is always willing to help students and always answers his emails. He also knows biology really well.
Amazing guy. Just make sure you attend class because he WILL look at you sideways if not!
Pretty easy class but there is some work each week. The professor really cares about the class and expects students to engage in class.

Loved taking this professor! I learned a lot about Cuban immigration to America and more about assimilation of Cuban Americans into American culture. The papers and weekly speaking also helped me improve my fluency and depth of knowledge of the Spanish language.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor with very engaging lectures videos. He is an easy grader who focuses more on giving you tips to improve your Spanish than the content of your work. Allows for plenty of time to complete projects and didn't give any tests.

A passionate and funny professor. Expects a lot out of his students in upper level classes. Sometimes expects a baseline of knowledge in other subjects (ie, got upset at class for not knowing economics principles.) Remember, upper level Spanish classes are moreso random history classes just taught in Spanish. Expect to read a lot.

Great professor. He put in so much effort in his lectures to make them engaging and professional. I actually enjoyed the video assignments. By the end of the summer semester, I felt more confident in my Spanish just by having those assignments weekly. Very flexible and nice.

Dont take this if you don’t really understand Spanish or are doing this for an “easy” grade- you have to participate and MUST understand what he is saying.  That aside, I loved it and his teaching style. He is very helpful and gives great constructive advice. I’ve taken more than one class with him and he is a great Spanish professor.

Celger knows how to push you to the next level of fluency - if you put in the work, he will give you detailed feedback on your writing on how to sound more natural, better diction. Participation matters a TON, but he uses the hybrid format to help - if you don't talk in class, you can submit an online vid of you speaking for weekly credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Cleger is awesome! This was an asynchronous, short summer course & I loved it. The course material was interesting & he always made his lectures easy to follow & fun to watch. He's so kind & really listens to our feedback/questions. All around an amazing person & I hope to take more of his classes in the future! Assignments weren't bad at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Don't take if looking for an "easy humanities". My spanish has improved more w him than any other class in my life. He pushes his students to think at an advanced level (beyond conversational) - ie. we wrote a research paper in Spanish and he walked us thru the project. No tests, only speaking/writing/reading. only take if serious about Spanish

Take any other Spanish course besides Cleger! He doesnt grade assignments until after finals and does not communicate grading criteria. He does not use Canvas, he uses Whatsapp. He doesn't grade based on your Spanish, he says his class is an HTS class. He is aggressive when meeting 1-on-1. He takes critiques personally and isnt fair with students.

Do NOT take this professor online. Maybe he is better in person, but he uses FB as his method of communication and class discussion instead of the school's Canvas interface. I was consistently frustrated because I was confused as to what I was supposed to do each day/for each assignment.
The class was harder than I thought it would be, but Cleger is super nice and a pretty good lecturer!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. I participated in the Peru LBAT and we was very engaging during class as well as on excursions. If you put a fair amount of effort in, you will definitely succeed in his class. Very nice guy, super approachable and understanding, and great professor. Definitely take his class if you have the opportunity!

He's a good professor, and will like you if you participate in the daily discussions. This course covers a lot of really easy concepts/themes from high school english, just in Spanish, so it's not difficult content. There's readings for every class, and several essays. If you do well on the first exam, you don't have to take the second one.

I took Smart Cities in Latin America & Spain with Cleger. It was difficult at first because he really expects you to participate and speak frequently. Once you warm up to the class, it becomes a lot of fun. He puts a lot of effort into lecture - we built apps, rode electric bikes, and tried virtual reality glasses. 10/10 would take the class again

Cleger means well, and you can feel it... The classes he teaches though are absolute bullsh*t, and everyone knows it. As such, the assignments are quite convoluted. He is there to help, but really the whole affair of pretending to learn is exhausting. If he likes you though, easy A... take someone else, or take it at your own risk.

One of those professors that think their class is the only class you have.  Way too much work, requiring us to have documentated conversations via webcam with Spanish-speakers in other countries, in addition to regular homework. Which was ridiculous mostly because it was a COMPOSITION class... I would have understood for a Conversation class...

He is a really cool guy and cares for his students. I didn't do as well as I would have liked but mainly because I didn't participate in class that much. He is difficult, but maybe just shouldn't be teaching 3111. I recommend him to people who are very knowledgeable of Spanish.
Osvaldo is the man!! He is adorable, and I absolutely love this class. He is very smart and entertaining. If I could retake this class, I would. Osvaldo is amazing. Highly recommended.

Cleger is such a pro. His classes are interesting, easy, and informative. You'll always ba able to get a lot out of his lessons, and he's kind of a pro in general. You should definitely take his class if you get the chance.
Too technical, experience given for granted, too many speakers.

One of those teachers yaps each and every class period. This class has a lot of potential, but unfortunately, professor Asensio makes it far too theoretical. If you want a relatively easy class and need to fulfill degree requirements, take this class and push through. If you want to learn, STAY AWAY.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Offers no learning value.

Decent lecturer, very disorganized class. Files were extremely disorganized and deadlines kept moving, there were two textbooks and it was often unclear which one he was referring to. Many exam questions were exact copies of homework questions, but no crib sheet or equation sheet. Letter grade was unknown until the end of the semester.

He attempts to keep us engaged in lectures. He shows derivations in lecture instead of applications, but HW and exams test on both. Weekly HW that's graded on accuracy, but textbook usually has answers. 80% of grade is from exams that reuse HW problems. He'll give more weight to your 2 midterms OR final, whichever you do better on.

Dr. Orlando was an overall good professor. He was enthusiastic about all of the topics he covered, and I learned a lot. Files were not organized well on Canvas, and homeworks came up at random. There is a big white paper project, but everyone does well on it. The midterm and final were not too bad, they just required a lot of heavy memorization.

The class/content was just hard itself- thermo/derivations. He posts hand-written lecture notes and goes over them in class; he'll tell you to read (I never did), but he clearly states what will be on his exams. Review sessions were helpful; study the homeworks. There were 2 exams + 1 final with 2 possible grading distributions. EC given.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Has handwritten notes that are really disorganized instead of any PowerPoints. During lectures, he goes on tangents. Tests are difficult but predictable. Extra credit involves reading scientific papers (most of which are his) and reviewing them. Class was fair enough, but it was disorganized, which made it a lot harder.

Dr. Orlando is a great lecturer, but the class felt disorganized at times due to the nature of notes (no slides, only handwritten notes) and the grading scheme (he doesn't tell you what the A or B cut off is and there's random extra credit and participation points that aren't clear where they end up). Overall, good class but lots of effort needed.

Engaging and professional lecture videos. Foundation-level homework that demands a good understanding (also tedious without automated workflows). Fun final project (also time-demanding, plan ahead!). Very flexible online course. Course content could be overly picky and focused on details irrelevant or easily Google-able in actual programming work.

I greatly enjoyed the course series. I've taken several well-structured courses, but not all remain engaging. His enthusiasm for teaching is presented through a dynamic style, reflecting dedication to both the course and his students—a rare quality in my eyes as someone returning to uni after 10 years and knowing the value of maintaining passion.
No CS class should test you on the date when companies acquire one another.

The course is largely run by TAs. Exams are 55% of your grade and are inconsistent with homework, and use short study guides (sometimes with incorrect answer keys) that don't match the difficulty. HW is occasionally busy work but sometimes helpful, and the video lectures are informative. Omojokun is hard to access and not great with accommodations.

At time of writing, 3 tests are worth a combined 55% of the final grade. Despite the concepts being relatively easy, this makes the tests unreasonably stressful. The homework is mostly busywork and incredibly annoying. Nearly all of the difficulty in this course comes from the work being an absolute pain to complete.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As many of the other comments have said, this course is test heavy. Homeworks are simple, and are good indicators of how much you logically understand. TAs aren't the best, but the prof himself is decent. Tests are trick question levels of difficult, and expect your grade to be solely based on your test average.

Homeworks are simple enough to understand but you don't get to see all of the testcases up front for them. The only practice material for exams are 1-2 pdfs or questions along with videos that can put you to sleep and exams are harder than any practice you use. Dr. O also does not respond quickly to messages and the class is essentially ran by TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: First time getting anything below an A in a course. Takes multiple days to reply to everything no leniency.

I took this class online with the Distance CS program my senior year of HS. Professor is nice and lecture videos are well structured. Make sure to review all the details, however, as exams are super detail oriented. Homeworks are the worst thing about this class, they take ages to complete and have a million hidden test cases.

The online class is just ran by the TAs, and the weekly HWs take a couple hours max. Tests can be hard tho and there isn't much study materials given, but overall not too bad. Grading does take FOREVER and your grade is essentially just based off 3 midterms and a final, which can be a problem if you aren't a good test-taker.
Great Professor!
very very bad

Took 1331 for dual enrollment, class is pretty much run by TA's. Final grade is pretty much just your tests and final, so you will have to prepare for the tests. Tons of extra credit on the last homework and the final, which helps a ton. Pacing for the tests is a bit fast, but other than that not too bad of a class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took him for GT cs dual enrollment, and he was a pretty good.

Funny how all of the good reviews are in the same exact language.... took this class right after 1301 (did very well) and it was terrible. Lecture videos were super surface level and homework was cooked. Tests were super difficult. Grading took forever, prof was impossible to reach, TAs ran the class and had little experience. Do not take!

He is good at teaching the earlier material and gives helpful advice when asked. However, some of the later units were harder to comprehend, the homework is unnecessarily difficult, and grades are delayed for 1-2 weeks making it kinda frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Omojokun explains challenging concepts in a clear manner and provides lot of examples. He builds up on the concepts at a good pace. The homeworks were very interesting and included building popular games like battleship. He also goes the extra mile to provide recommendations for OMSCS applicants based on their performance in CS1331.

With experience in other programming languages, I found the course did an excellent job of helping me apply my existing knowledge to Java's specific implementation. The lectures were well-structured and easy to follow. The inclusion of regular homework and quizzes was helpful for reinforcing the concepts and ensuring the knowledge stuck.

I came into this with just an Intro to C course. This Java class broke down complex concepts clearly. Despite being fully online, Professor Fisayo was accessible and responsive. His passion for teaching shows in his lectures and makes the course enjoyable. I'd take him again if possible.

The class was difficult and primarily run by TAs. Your grade is based on 3 exams, final exam, and 9 homeworks. The exams and HWs are a lot harder than the lecture videos, which are pretty basic. This class is good if your looking to self study, but getting a good grade is pretty difficult.

horrible prof, doesnt do anything for class it's all run by TA's. the exams and hw are so much harder than the basic lecture videos. he never responds to emails and doesnt even show up to exams. take it in fall or spring w a different prof

Dr. O did not do anything for the class except his pre recorded lecture videos that only covered basics. Exams and HW was so much more in depth and harder. There's no curves and barely any extra credit. Grade depends on 3 exams, final, and HW. The TAs run the class and they do have OH everyday. Definitely do not recommend taking his class.

The class is entirely run by TA's and graded heavily on only 3 tests. The videos are vague and spoken in an overly condensed academic language, as if the viewer already knows the topic (also, who explains lines of code without even highlighting it?). External resources are your friend; prior knowledge is imperative. Not even close to Joyner's class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dont take his online section. The class is run by TAs an grades are basically exam scores. Homework takes a lot of time and they have hidden test cases.

Never responds to emails, hard to reach. The class is basically led by TAs. Lecture videos are so basic and exams and hw are so much more in depth and difficult. No curves or enough extra credit. Don't take his online section unless you already know java.

I took Dr. Omojokun's CS 1331 class via edX. The professor did a great job by making the video lectures both thorough and engaging to suit the online format. His explanation of the four pillars were just what I needed to understand the actual, tangible benefits of the OOP paradigm. Dr. Omojokun was very responsive when I reached out for help.

The video lectures are easy to understand and follow along with, but grading at times can be harsh and somewhat unfair. For example, most of the homework is fully auto-graded, meaning that, if you have a single typo in a print statement, you can lose 20+ points on the assignment for failing tests. The majority of tests are hidden, as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures only cover the most basic case of the topic which prof is fine at explaining. While the hws are a lot of work and very edge case heavy. The hws have an autograder but the autograder will not test every case that they actually grade your hw on. Most of your grade is from your 3 exams and the final which don't have many resources for.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: On the online section, the homework is just tedious, not difficult. Overall fine recorded lectures online but have never actually interacted with him as the class is primarily ran by the TAs. This class exists if you don't want to go to lectures. Annoying thing is heavy weighing towards tests. Mileage varies with how well you learn asynchronously.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: What people say about the grading is true. It's dependent on a few exams. I think the lectures and the practice makes up for this. I did the bare minimum: lectures (no notes but followed along) and did the practice exam the day of the test and got a low A. I'm not a CS major so I'm unsure how he is for the advanced courses they have to take.

As a dual enrollment student this was one of the hardest classes I have ever taken. Dr OO was never available and his TA ran the whole class. The tests were very difficult and conceptual and didn't have much coding on them. The homework's had a lot of hidden tests, so you couldn't know if you made a mistake until you saw a 70 on the homework. 👎
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Enjoyed Dr. OO as a person when I met him. May just be online but very little interaction outside of videos. Grading is very exam heavy, around 80%, so not the section for a bad test taker. Took forever to grade with lots of TAs. Hated the lack of transparency with final exam/grading. Head TA Ignacio is great. EC for hackathon, tests, and HW10.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Pros: 
Practice exams follow the real exams
Cons:
Grade is overly dependent on 3 exams, Did bad on the first and couldn't recover
Takes forever for grades to come back, at least a month
Score gets canceled over the littlest thing. Dual enrollment students definitely try to take the exams in person
Other comments about homework are true
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Decent class with clear lectures. 10 tedious homework assignments (20%), 3 memorization-heavy exams (54%), and a final (26%). Prof & TAs are lazy--grading tests takes months, and the final was never even graded. Extensive proctoring so scores can be canceled for tiny issues. If you already know Java, course is alright; otherwise, not a great idea.

MASSIVE shift from Joyner and completely on your own, the professor and TAs take Eons to grade, the camera policy for exams is pretty invasive (the WHOLE room is checked not just your desk), exams are long with not enough time, got first exam score after the drop deadline AND my final and final grade isn't in despite the class ending on the 1st
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took the online course for flexibility.  Tests were in person though, so it's not fully online.  He does try to meet students out in campus, which is nice but I was only able to make once.  The last homework made the class totally worth it.

Overall solid experience: clear lecture videos, lengthy but relevant HW assignments, and difficult tests. I wish that the class incorporated a project grade or exams that allow you to run and test code (like Joyner's online 1301 class). My main gripe is that exams took SUPER long to grade and often weren't available until 5 weeks after the test.

The most difficult professor I've had yet, my first B. The 10 homeworks that you spend at least 2 hours on each is only worth 20% of your grade. The 3 tests are worth 54. The study guides do contain some of the test material, random things pop up. Only extra credit is from tests. Grade is a mystery until the class ends. Never got a midterm grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. OO is a nice guy but I would not recommend taking 1331 online unless you are extremely confident in Java already. His TAs are useless, never reply to emails, you can forget about office hours because they're never there. Tests are hard. Essentially, if you are good at Java, take this class, but if you're not, pick a good in person prof

The tests given do not correspond well with the material from class. The professor is very hard to reach and cancels many exam grades over minor details related to online proctoring, resulting in 3 tests making up ~85% of the grade for many students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Homework assignments were long, repetitive, tedious, and generally didn't benefit student learning, as well as having hidden test cases. Exams were more focused on testing your memory than your programming ability. Professor is very paranoid about cheating, and your exam scores can get canceled for little to no reason. Exam grading took 6-7 weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I dual enrolled this class. Would not reccomend. Class is pretty much TA run. Professor O's only interaction is via video lectures. Homeworks were extremely difficult. Exams were only tangentially related to lecture material. The book is your friend. I barely got a 90

If I didn't know Java prior to entering the class, the course would be very difficult. OO never interacts with the class beyond pre-recorded videos, and the TAs are near non-existent. The homework has invisible test cases and unnecessarily restricts certain features like making helper classes. Take only if you already know your stuff.

Took this online. The lectures are extremely surface level while the homework was impossible with extremely low averages. Tests were very difficult and not a representation of the material learned. Dr O was completely absent from the class which was virtually run by TAs who seemed undertrained. No one I knew liked this class, take anyone else.

Prof. Omojokun's course was invaluable! As an undergrad, I struggled with OOP concepts, but this class clarified key fundamentals and boosted my confidence. Its rigor proved online learning's effectiveness, inspiring me to apply for OMSCS. His humor made lectures engaging and memorable. I highly recommend his class! 😊

This course was relatively easy but informative. The profs responsible for the course did their best to create engaging lecture videos coupled with little skits, so it was more enjoyable to watch than most classes.

Professor Omojokun's lecture videos were clearly presented and well-enunciated, making them easy to follow.  The homework assignments were appropriately challenging, and really push you to apply what you learned.  As long as you go through the material, you will be able to do the homework with no problem.  This was a great introductory class.

Good, but somewhat absent professor. There are structural issues with the course; some of the material is well edited but other material, such as the polymorphism section, could be better explained and lack depth. Overall I would take a in person lecturer. Dr. OO is a good professor, I would take an in person section but not an online section.

Prof. Omojokun was a great presence to have in class, and overall made it more enjoyable and engaging. However, when he wasn't there it made him feel missed in class, and made me wish we saw more of him in CS4010. Nevertheless, a very good professor.

The class can be challenging, but Professor Omojokun presents the material clearly with examples. Engaging with the content and using resources like unstuckstudy for study prep helped me learn a lot. Overall, a valuable introduction to Java and OOP.

Professor O is completely uninvolved in the class and most of the TAs are nonexistant and unhelpful. Homework was extremely challenging and the content taught definitely wasn't enough to complete the homeworks. Also, the new content after test 3 was really rushed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The teacher is useless, and the TAs are rude. Homework is hard and autograded with hidden cases (perfect autograded score but 70 or smth actual score), with no regrade requests. Tests are hard to finish in time. I'd choose another teacher for better policies and TAs, as this is a definitely a weeder class with standardized tests between classes.

I feel like this class is kind of a weeder class for CS and the exam goes into so many nuances that its more of how much you can memorize than if you know how to code. You pretty much need to learn every single detail he tells you in his lectures in order to do well. He's a nice professor though.

Probably the worst class I've ever taken. As a DE HS student with no Bs, this class will be my first B. Did bad on one test and cannot recover. TAs are lazy. Idk if the professor even looked at the class once this whole semester. Tests are set up to make you fail. Don't waste your time and effort on this class.

This class doesnt feel set up for you to succeed. The homeworks are autograded but for some reason they dont do all the tests, so you can turn it in and get all the points then when its graded get an 80. The tests are horrible, you have to code on paper and theres barely any time. you have to know useless stuff and they are a big part of the grade.

Worst GT CS class I've taken. Tests are full of Java trivia type questions which are not designed to test your understanding but how much you know about the irrelevant aspects of Java. Omojokun's team of TAs are also really lazy and would take forever to respond to emails and to grade our assignments (even those autograded ones). Stay away.

Online course, however, exams were in person and on paper. HWs were difficult, but as long as you watched lecture videos, they were doable. Lots of resources outside of class if you need help. Overall, a great course, but sometimes, you don't get the answers you need. All of the profs that teach 1331 seem average, but Professor O was pretty good.

Professor Omojokun presents course material in a clear manner with plenty of examples and a few jokes as well. All new material discussed is built upon previous coursework which helps to maintain a steady flow of learning and a consistent thought process. If you need assistance, Professor Omojokun is willing to help and provide guidance!

entire grade is dependent on a couple tests. questions are often unclear. one was based on what was bolded and what was not, but nothing was bolded. It was worth like 9/30 points on the exam. Both him and the TA's are completely inaccessible. if you can take this class with another professor please do.

Took the class online over the summer and it was setup very poorly. The prof. was not always helpful in explaining the content. The tests were also difficult because of this and they felt like they were made just to trick you. The final project uses JavaFX, which you will not see at all until the very end of the course. I suggest another prof.

My main problem is that the instructors/TAs don't care about their class. Olufisayo does not respond to any messages, and even TAs don't respond after days. Office Hours are practically non-existent. I only suggest that you take this class if you can handle learning and doing everything by yourself with no help from the instructors.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took the online version of the class presented on edX. Would recommend as a great starting point to Java/OOP. The homework can be a little challenging, but ultimately doable. Having an assignment at the end of each module reinforces practicing Java syntax and thinking from an object-oriented perspective. Definitely felt like I learned a lot.

Learned a lot about OOP concepts in this course. I recommend this class over the other 1331 offerings. Homework is offered once a week. Make sure you're doing it & understand it, as your exams are very code-heavy.
He's friendly and invites online students to meet up for lunch since.  Final project was big learning experience.  I finally wrote a program I could show off.
80% of the grade is based on 4 tests, which are very detailed oriented. The rest of the grade is from weekly homework assignment that can be very tedious.

I virtually studied CS1331 which was instructed by Professor Fisayo. He conveyed the course clearly by demonstrating Java code writing and testing on many exercise cases. His teaching style is rigorous and humorous.
I look forward to learning more courses from him along the journey to pursue a master's degree in computer science.

Almost our entire grade was determined by exams, which were on paper?, and time-consuming homework. I asked multiple CS major friends for help with homework assignments after going to the TAs who were unhelpful and condescending, and they all said the homework was very difficult for an intro class and incredibly confusing. Do not take!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Homework assignments were often posted late and constantly edited, and submission box with the auto-grader also often came out quite late, sometimes two nights before due date. Tests feel somewhat unrepresentative of relevant topic, and the format of them were quite poor as they were on canvas. Professor felt completely uninvolved, mostly ran by TA

Dr. Omojokun uses very simple and clear examples throughout the lectures, which makes complex notions such as recursion or abstraction easy to understand. The homework might take some time to solve but overall Dr. Omojokun provides students with very informative and clear content. His lectures are a lot of fun too!

Dr. O.O. is the goat. The class itself is fully online and can be confusing/difficult at times, and the exams can be difficult. Hw sometimes either easy or extremely tedious. However, prof is super chill even if he isn't very active in the class. Would recommend out of any other 1331 teacher.

I enjoyed the valuable materials taught by professor Fisayo in this course, Java Object Oriented Programming is deep and challenging but yet this course uses examples learning approach to makes it a little easier to understand, I would like to thank professor Fisayo for his hard work on this course.

Tests are worth 80% of your grade, making it almost impossible to recover from one bad performance. The lectures are shallow and useless, the tests unlike any of the practice given. I don't know my final exam score or final grade, and did not receive a response when I asked. The "professor" is very absent, and even disses his students to the TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really frustrating class. Dr. O facilitates this class directly through his TA's while he's merely a shadow. And even then, the TA's (who do a lot of work) are pretty obviously learning as they go. Homework is EXTREMELY varying in difficulty (one had a 55% avg???). Tests are nit-picky and a bad representation of your knowledge. Take another class!
If you are a de student and want to get rejected from every possible college including Lanier tech choose this prof. In the middle of the test I started to wonder if I was even on the right unit

I took online 1331 with professor OO and I'd say he's a good professor. He's got a good sense of humor and his lectures are good too (I'd put his videos on 1.5x speed if I were you). I highlight extra credit because the final Java FX assignment provides 60 points worth of extra credit! There's a decent amount of HW but nothing besides that.
I took the async version of 1331, and the course felt fair. The videos were a digestible length for every concept, and the homework assignments never asked too much of me.
Learned way more than I thought having taken a prior Java class. Programming projects can be time consuming but he gives flexibility in submissions and extra credit.

Professor Omojokun's class (dual enrollment CS1331 online) feels like it is not set up for the student to succeed. Graded by only a few assignments (80% exams / 20% homework) that are not similar to coursework and are tangentially related to the lectures. TAs are unresponsive and unhelpful, while Professor O was only active 2-3 times on the forum.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tough class and lots to learn but offers flexibility at the end.

The tests are weighed very poorly, there are only 4 exams and they make up 80% of your grade. If you bomb a single test it is impossible to bring your grade back up. OO only showed up twice in Piazza, the course was essentially run by the TA's. The homework also took many hours, far too much time than what was necessary for a course of this level.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: First CS class @ tech and made me hate CS so much, Landry's and Aibek's (in person sections) tests was much easier than OO and lecture videos were horribly designed and didn't help in understanding the concepts in depth beyond surface level. Homework was very vague and autograded. TAs werent helpful, went to Landry's TAs instead for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible course.  The online material is terrible for preparing you for exams.  All the exams are in person which makes no sense for an online course.  If you want an A in this course, you will have to carry yourself because the materials provided in the modules will not set you up for success.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take an in person section for 1331. Omojokun's homeworks and tests are extremely ambiguous, instructions are not clear ever, Piazza responses are really bot-like, i.e. they give you hints instead of actual instruction. Since the course is asynchronous, it's hard to connect with fellow students, and his tests are on paper... like who codes on paper?

Almost 1% of my final grade was determined by a question on the test that asked, "What year was java made."  The tests are designed to make you lose points, very tricky niche questions.  Modules do not go sufficiently in depth on the concepts (in my opinion).  If you do bad on any exam, which is most likely, it is near impossible to recover.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor OO seemed nice enough (for the grand total of 3 times I saw him the entire semester). The lectures were informative, but you are expected to know every small detail mentioned in the videos. Most of the lectures were made in 2019, which is fine but also feels a bit low effort on his behalf. Overall, the prof and course were disappointing.

Professor Omojokun's lectures were wonderful and I recommend taking his classes. The class projects were really good and they were closely related to his lectures so if you are stuck with the projects, you should go back and watch the lectures again. You will learn a lot by finishing them and passing all the tests from the projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Had to fly in from California and no exceptions could be made, was originally on the waitlist for a while so I couldn't even drop this class after. Crazy that this class was asynchronous online but exams were in-person and written?? Offers some extra credit but the tests are so long with little time

I probably squeaked by with my A.
I was worried about doing the course online, but he does a decent job simplifying complex topics though some topics are probably more advanced for a intro programming course than needed.  I'm guessing he doesn't define the required topics to cover though.

I thought that the amount of effort put into the creation of this class was just pathetic. The lecture videos used are of such poor quality that any random YouTube video would explain the concepts better. It's a complete waste of a class if you are genuinely trying to learn new content (I already knew most of this so online was better). HW was ok
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: OO rarely appears: it's all TA run. The HW is good and is where I learned the most. Tests are often difficult and cover niche concepts. Pay attention to syntax, especially capitalization! Even if it's not a coding question, they will check. I'm not a CS major by intention, but the class was alright. CS majors would enjoy it more.

This class was essentially entirely TA ran. I only saw the professor during major exams and he rarely answers questions on piazza. His lecture videos were okay but lack details, you're better off finding yt videos online. 80% of the grade depended on 4 exams and a lot of the questions were memorization based and some weren't even relevant.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Never saw OO, but our TAs were amazing. The lectures were all pre-recorded and released on Canvas. One hw due every week (helps you pace yourself really well). Grade depends a LOT on exams; sometimes they're really confusing (topics not covered in recitations or emphasised in lectures), but are similar to past exams (get them from friends!!)
Tests - 80% of class grade - full of trick questions and/or topics not covered in lecture.

Never heard from the professor, so hope for a good TA. 10 homeworks, one a week, not too difficult. Three tests, average difficulty, make sure you study - they count a lot. Final exam questions were worded terribly, very hard to understand. Will probably need to watch YouTube videos to fully learn. Grading takes a little while. Little extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Adequate difficulty for an introductory class. Your grade will heavily depend on exam grades. Most of it is review if you have taken AP Computer Science A.

The lecture videos are pretty brief but cover enough to do the assigned homework. You don't really see the professor much outside of his videos, so your experience is based on your TA (shout out to the head TA in the dual enrollment section). Also, idk who makes the instructions for the final but I had a stroke trying to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Lectures are ok but you definitely need outside resources to help in this class, I recommend CodingWithJohn on youtube. Keep up with your work or you will fall behind. We had a great TA and he's probably the only reason I got an A. Professor is not very involved in the class. If you're taking the class hope you get a good TA.

I took the online class as a Dual Enrollment student. I thought his pre-recorded lectures were pretty good but you may need to use youtube every once in a while to clear up understanding. Not much interaction with him, but from what I got, he seems like a great teacher.

Boring lectures that don't really cover much at all and don't really translate to tests well. Use YT videos to learn content - much better. Homeworks are fine, TAs take a long time to grade tho. Class/content is not difficult but the class is poorly designed and doesn't do a good job of actually preparing you to do well on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You'll mostly interact with the TAs in this class. With that said, this class was not for beginner programmers. The modules alone are not enough to do the homework. Exams are a challenge and test small details but extra credit and the bonus homework project help. Watch the lessons early as possible to start homework and seek help if you get stuck.

In the online section so idk much about this dude but his class is butt. Homeworks take months to go in gradescope, 40% of the content is useless (not really his fault), tests are on paper (in person section has online tests), TAs try to give you as few pts as possible on tests, lecture videos are slow even on 2x speed
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I finally understand Big O!!!

I tend to prefer asych classes and have performed well in them before. However, this class is horrible. The videos hardly cover the basics and then ur expected to apply that to the really complex hw's. Feels like you are trying to code without rly understanding how or why any of it works, which makes it rly difficult. would not recommend

I thought the course set was extremely informative and easy to follow. Additionally, the presentation of diagrams to illustrate the inner workings of certain Java concepts allowed me to grasp ideas quicker as a student who has no prior CS experience. The professor very clearly cares about the subject matter and the homework is thought-provoking

The homework was really the only way I learned the information well and could apply and implement it. I didn't have any Java experience prior. The videos are decent, but if you really want to learn the information you'll need to do a lot of studying. Tests are very hard if you don't study, so prep well in advance. TAs give you lots of worksheets.

Comprehensive & challenging homework coding exercises, which had a lot of edge conditions that needed to be accounted for - but is also a great litmus for testing one's knowledge. I do wish there were a textbook recommended in the syllabus as going purely off the videos & lessons can be a bit difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Online videos were pretty entertaining.  Maybe one module too much for an intro course.

I was in the online section. His videos and canvas modules in general were pretty high-quality.  There was no book requirement but it's worth getting the one he recommends.  Recitation is key, especially for JavaFX if you have a Mack.

The class isn't too hard, but it is extremely disorganized; the TA's basically run the entire class and the professor feels nonexistent. Took them almost a month to grade each exam and most of the homework grades weren't even released until the end of the semester, while the synchronous 1331 sections had their assignments graded within days.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The tests are fair but a time crunch. HWs can take a decent amount of time so start early!

The workload was decent. I would recommend getting the prerecorded lectures done early in the week so you have a lot of time to do the homework. That being said, the TAs heavily influence the experience of the class and it isn't great. Grades are due on the 6th and I still don't have grades back from months ago. Either way, it's a good course.
The tests were a time crunch but fair and the HW were pretty easy. The prerecorded lectures are entertaining and go pretty slow too.

The async course is pretty good. I prefer this method over in person. The only set back is the HW. It jumps in difficulty very early in the semester. The TA's are a lifesaver and the lectures are short and straight to the point. I would 100% take this course again and other async cs classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Homeworks are projects, so plan accordingly.  There were 8 this summer and after the 4th one, they require about a week so don't waste time like I did.  Thankfully he drops the lowest HW and gives extra credit. Otherwise I would have gotten a B
You get to learn more than programming which is cool if you've already had experience coding in high school.

class was well organized but the lectures were not rigorous enough to be useful for the homeworks, which took 4-12 hours each time. professor was considerate of a personal situation i had but when i had to make up the exam in person he came off as irritated, uninterested, and rude. LOTS of mistakes were presented in recitation so i stopped going
Plenty of extra credit to make up for early screwups, especially in the final create-x project which was fun.
Awful professor. Extremely rude and unresponsive with emails. Does not show any sympathy to students' situations outside of class.
AWFUL! TAKE SOMEONE ELSE IF YOU CAN!!!!!!!

The convenience of this class is what sold me on it originally, but I was not prepared for it to be much more difficult exam-wise than the in-person section. Take notes and study a lot! Answer keys for study guides weren't released, making the class harder than it needed to be. There needs to be more difficult examples in the lectures too.

TAs and piazza were super helpful/responsive, video lectures made complex topics easy to digest, exams not surprising or out to trick you, HWs+study guides+recitation+taking notes on videos/taking time to actually understand material = success in class. start hw at least 3 days early to be able to ask questions & get help. overall a solid class
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took Omojokun's async class, which was pretty flexible with my other commitments and was a pretty easy class. If you are learning Java for the first time, make sure to set some time aside for the homework, and his tests do test somewhat obscure Java scenarios, so put in the work accordingly. Otherwise, this was a great class compared to others

Very accessible and student-friendly asynch format. For most assignments, we could see our grade immediately on Gradescope, even if there were hidden tests. I do wish his TAs provided more information like study guide answers ahead of exams, but overall I would definitely take Omojokun again.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I honestly liked this section. Async lecture videos were straightforward, short, and concise. I wasn't prepared for the exams to be kinda difficult, but I think it's just CS1331 in general where you have to memorize stupid things. STUDY for the exams and actually take notes from the videos!!

Extremely long homework; it takes an entire week (and is barely worth 20%). He is somewhat sweet and funny in his videos, but God I find them boring and long. Exams are 90% memorization, and not reading something properly means you're losing a lot of points. Piazza is only slightly helpful; office hours are always helpful. I appreciate his effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: took async, material was good, homework was manageable. Tests can be difficult if not studied well for, but extra credit on final helps.

Prof. Omojokun is concise and the async lectures have no rambling, and he tries to keep it entertaining. The HWs actually utilize the taught concepts but takes a lot of time. The grading structure is awful, HWs are 20%, midterms are 54% and the final is 26%. The tests confusingly require memorization of an entire structure of a class/random facts.
You have to keep on with this class because homework takes a while. Overall, this class is convenient since it's ASYNC.

In Prof. Omojokun's asynchronous class, there were multiple online modules in Canvas, which stored pre-recorded lecture videos to explain each of the OOP concepts in-depth with helpful examples. To succeed, take notes from each video, design your own test cases for the homework, and practice answering questions from the study guide! Good luck! :)

I took the asynch fall semester. His videos and modules are amazing and well produced and the course is flexible. Homework takes a long time (6-8 hours) and is graded kinda harshly. You might have to figure out on your own. Exams were alright, on the harder side. Some qs I didn't like were from brief and specific parts of the module.

Dr. Omojokun is an excellent professor who is very willing to help students succeed. His asynchronous format for 1331 is incredibly flexible and allows students to customize their study methods. Although the exams are tough and make up 80% of the grade, there are a number of extra credit opportunities given. I highly recommend taking his course.

Dr. Omojokun was a great lecturer and made his videos interesting. He clearly knows what he's talking about and makes concepts easy to understand. However, his homework took a minimum of 6 hours, and there was a new one every week (only 15% of the grade). The tests were incredibly difficult too, and they tested things that he mentions in passing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: It took while to get used to the async format but eventually got a hang of it genough to do decently in the class. There's lots of stuff covered in the class but the modules explain things pretty well.

Dr. Omojokun taught this class jointly with Professor Huffman. She handled the lectures and Dr. Omojokun was there to help guide conversations and link course concepts to Computer Science. It was very helpful having him there. In my experience, he always responds to emails. Though, it might take him a day or so to respond.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Unfortunately, he does not respond to emails, which is disappointing and makes exams SUPER HARD! HW takes the whole week to be done, and it only accounts for 15%. The class is very test-heavy, and his tests are not the best in testing what you have actually learned.

Homeworks can be hard, but if you start early and do a little bit everyday it really is not that bad. I personally did fine on exams, but a lot of my peers were frustrated as the tests seemed to focus more on memorization rather than coding abilities. Tests count 60% of your grade and the final is 25% so class is definitely test heavy.
Entertaining lectures, which helps for a non-major like me
Just don't take the class. The homework takes 5+ hours to do sometimes but is only worth 15%, his lectures do not help and you have to teach yourself, and his tests are very hard for an intro course

I took 1331 with OO async in fall 2020. The grade weights when I took it were pretty bad and unfair imo. OO is a pretty good lecturer though. Paying close attention to the modules was the main way to pass the class. Homeworks and exams were fairly difficult and intensive. OO was fairly accommodating to students, apparently unlike other 1331 profs.

Online course, he puts up all the recorded videos and notes at the start of the course. HW is a lot, so start it early. I never needed to go to his office hours for help, but he did offer them. I mostly used the TAs for hw help. Tests are very fair, so pay close attention to the details or else you will loose lots of points.
Tough course, but great guy! Good lectures, very understanding, and super accessible.

I liked the online async format -- short modules worked bc long lectures don't keep my attention all the time. OO himself interacts very less with the students but that's prolly bc of the nature of the course. TA's are helpful, so is HW. Tests, like others mentioned, can be a bit weird, but as long as you take notes, understand stuff, you're good!

Many of his test questions do not really test your understanding, but rather your, at best, useless memorization of arbitrarily specific facts. Like one of the other reviewers said, exams are quite unfair, and by the way, the tests are copyrighted! lol To be fair, he has policy of replacing your lowest midterm grade with your final, if it's higher.

I took the online section of his CS 1331 class and I found it to be pretty good! The exams are a bit unfair in my opinion, but that is the case for all CS 1331 classes, it's not a professor issue. Otherwise the structure of the online course is extremely good! It's self paced with hard deadlines enforced by homework. Overall, great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took an async class so there wasn't that much interaction with OO. However, TAs are very helpful. The homework assignments are sometimes long and require a lot of testing so you should start early. I found the class pretty easy mostly because I have taken several programming courses before.

OO is a good choice for a CS professor who makes the most of the Online format. He doesn't have lecture videos and instead posts many videos for each topic that u watch at ur own pace. The homework would always be difficult, but the tests were always decently easier than the HW. Don't fall behind and start the homeworks early and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: OO is a good prof, but the issue with CS1331 is more to do with the fact that the tests are notoriously awful. Lots of true/false and multiple-choice questions test seemingly random knowledge of java/OOP. Coding HW is pretty fun and not too hard if you put in the time. OO is a good lecturer and is organized. Only real difficulty comes from tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took him online. His video lectures are short and to the point, which is helpful. You have to do some Googling for the later HWs because not all info is in the videos. HWs took generally 2-6 hours, but otherwise weren't bad. For tests, closely study the content in the videos. You lose a lot of pts for silly mistakes so watch out but otherwise easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His video modules contained all the information you needed for tests, and it was nice to be able to watch them multiple times in the online format. I found his videos quite engaging and funny, which really helped make the class interesting. Homeworks sometimes went beyond the modules, but the tests never had anything he didn't teach us. Great prof.

Tests were straightforward and tested mostly concepts that were stressed upon during lecture videos and coding that is mostly the same as the examples. Pun game is strong. Homeworks are made by the TAs and range from taking 1-2 hours to taking 6+ hours, and may require some googling/ stuff that's not entirely in the modules. Overall, good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: His lectures should be more detailed to help with the homework problems. He always uses easy example problems in his lectures which kind of leaves you hanging with the difficult ones. Not too accessible outside class, responds very late to emails, and is extremely strict with deadlines even under special circumstances.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Had him for online CS1331. Everything is very clear and tests are straightforward.

Took him for CS1331 in the summer. His explanations were very helpful but it doesn't hurt to google the murky concepts. His tests were also very fair and straightforward if you actually watched the lecture videos and did the homework on your own. He also gave grade replacements and extra credit on the final exam. 10/10 would highly recommend.
Gave lots of flexibility to allow teams to do what was best to get the project done. ZenHub requirement was sort of a bust, but I wished our team actually used it.
This class was difficult, but one of the best I have taken at Tech. Projects were hard and can take up a lot of time, but they were graded very fair.
Wish I had him for 1331

Omojokun remembers students names which was cool to see in a large class. I didn't get an A due to the difficulty of learning to program without any prior experience. However, I'm thinking of switching to CS as a major after this class. Unfortunately it's not that easy to get in.
Humor kept me awake during the long summer courses.  Lectures were also example based which gave me a sense of accomplishment if I could do what he did.

Tries to make lecture material clever but instead wastes time with arbitrary examples made up on the spot and full of mistakes. Recitation and online guides are your saving grace. Take the tests SERIOUSLY. Homework is a small percent of your grade and unbelievably time consuming but can show real computing application and is worth while.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He spends too much time on examples that don't even go into much depth regarding the course material, and he often makes mistakes. The classroom atmosphere is relaxed but his speaking tone is somewhat monotonous. Honestly, don't bother sitting through 2 hours of lecture. Spend that time working on the homework instead (there's a lot of it).
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Makes lectures interesting with his examples and humor. He utilizes clicker questions, live coding examples, and the board to their full potential and thus explains concepts quite clearly. Homework is basically a small project every week, and extra credit is offered in the form of clicker questions.
lectures use humor and clicker feedbacks for the most part.  summer classes can be too long for programming classes though, you can catch up with the book if you miss class
