Lectures can seem very long (especially the 1 hour 45 minutes lectures in Summer), but he gives generous extra credit, the homework is pretty manageable, and the tests are fine if you study.

Great 1371 professor!  Unlike most people's experiences, I learned almost everything in lecture rather than recitation.  If you do the homework and go to Omojokun's lectures, the class is easy, and I had no coding experience when I started.

Best of the 1371 professors.  You don't need to know code before hand.  He explains everything in terms that are easy to understand (no necessary jargon).  Of course most of the important things are covered in recitation but I found Omojokun's lectures as good review.

Solid professor. I came into the class with no coding experience and nearly pulled an A, and it was solely thanks to Omojokun's lectures. He gives clear, concise lectures that provide a good basis for the homework problems and provides plenty of PRS questions for practice. He's also really entertaining. The best option for 1371 in my opinion

Good professor if you have never done any programming before. 99% of material on the tests and homework will be taught in recitation though so I mostly used lecture to do homework. Tests aren't even made by the professors, just as an fyi.

decent professor. knows what hes doing. 1371 seems like its gonna kill you, but its not so bad. paying attention helps. tests are always hard, but theres a huge curve + grade replacement on the final. hws take alot of time, but he explains what you need to do pretty well.
Very helpful professor, you can ask your questions during class and if you still don't get it, he'd offer to take your problems after class. And, he has a deep,  interesting voice!

Omojokun's a great professor. Really laid back class. 1331 is straightforward and about 60% of it is AP Computer Science Material/Level of difficulty- however, it is not an easy class to get an A in. Practice Java , understand the concepts and  do the homework. Getting a B is very easy, but OO will make you work for that A.

Really laid back, very open to discussions and questions in class (yes, even in a huge lecture hall). Explains stuff very well, and is very easy to listen to (not dry at all). Tests, hw, etc is all given by the department.
Decent prof

His class is incredibly laid back, making it easy to ask questions. In fact, he seems to "wing" his lectures, and teaches in a "so yeah,whatever" style. Nevertheless, he is a good teacher. The assignments, quizzes, and tests are fair.

He reads off the power points provided by the book publisher. He doesn't go over the examples with great clarity either. He goes straight by the book so attending lecture is not required. Attending them is pretty much like him reading the content from the book to you word for word. His exams are easy so getting an A isn't that difficult.
Makes himself very approachable, which is good cause I didn't always understand what was covered in lecture.
Material taught is very useful for statisitics research

Dmitrii Ostrovskii is highly knowledgeable and supportive. He's very accessible outside class and gives great help in office hours, including useful research feedback. He also provides strong resources. The presentation/paper discussion (instead of an exam) was very helpful for grad studies.

Prof. Ostrovskii is a fantastic teacher for a challenging subject. He presents high-dimensional statistics with clarity and insight, connects theory to intuition, and is very thoughtful in his explanations.
The professor is a really interested person - enthusiastic for math and is able expalian some complicated conception from the nature of math.

One of the best math profs I had at GT. Dmitrii is knowledgeable and clear with well-structured notes, plenty of textbook references, and intuitive and interesting examples. He will make you think and put real time in, but well worth it and makes one really learn. Highly recommend PhD students to take a class with him. Prereq in analysis is helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Expert on statistics and relavant math topics. His teching can be very close to the state-of-the-art research in the area, thus can be expecially beneficial for PHD students.

Prof. Dimitri is fantastic, knowledgeable, clear, and fair. He breaks tough ideas into simple steps, uses vivid examples and links theory to practical problems. Questions are welcome, and his notes are well structured. I built a strong foundation in math and Linear Algebra and would gladly take another class with him too. Highly recommend.
Dr. Ostrovskii is an outstanding professor. I learned a lot of really useful math in his class.

Higher effort (and higher reward) than I anticipated. I think he understands what he teaches on a much much deeper level than teaching the class requires. Attendance isn't mandatory, but it's fun to see how passionate he is about the material. Definitely take if you care about getting an A (plenty of opportunities to do well) or you like research.
Very mathy. You can follow along and learn a lot if you like math. Plenty of extra credits, very available to answer questions.

You should take his class if you want to do math. I think the bad reviews come from people who expected high school level lectures or dislike math itself. He's very smart, I learned a lot in his class. Lectures were tough, yes —as a math class should— but grading's very soft. And his availability is without exaggeration the best I've had in GT.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nobody went to lectures because nobody understood what he was talking about, even studio TA's were confused about his curriculum, but gave opportunities for extra credit to make up for any mishaps when it came to exams. Let us do an extra credit assignment that if done correctly, would bump your grade yup a full letter.

Do not take under any circumstance.  Completely awful lectures that no one attended. Even the TA didn't understand what he was teaching. He was completely unprepared for class and exams, and gave a bunch of extra credit to make up for it

Dr. Ostrovskii dives into the conceptual meaning behind differential equations. Solving the problems requires practice, but if you understand the derivation behind the problems, then remembering steps will be easier. Even though his class is lecture heavy, the slightly more complex exams are balanced out by the extra credit opportunities offered.

He is a great professor and is very knowledgable about the subject. His style of teaching encourages thought and reinforces subject matter well. He is very accessible and supportive outside of class in case something doesn't make sense. Overall, he is a nice and fair instructor who prepares students well.

He was very bad with organization like the canvas did not exist for the first 2 weeks of class. Lectures were difficult to follow, and the TA explained everything so much better. He gave a good deal of extra credit making up for it though.
Very passionate and knowledgeable about the subject, but not the best lecturer. Gives plenty of extra credit

Proof heavy lectures that don't prepare you for exams, exams that test you on calculus rather than gauge your knowledge of differential equations. Definitely likes math but resents students who he perceives as dumb. Whole course felt like I was being punished. Gave bonus because everyone didn't do well.
Hard to understand lectures and was often not clear. Just use the online videos for this class to learn the material.

Lectures were impossible to even hear, most people ended up not going. It's not a difficult class to self study if you watch another professor's lectures but be prepared to put in the work. Practice exams are really helpful!

I took Dmitrii's class in Fall 2023, and he wasn't that bad honestly. A lot of people didn't like him because he taught more proofs and focused on conceptual understanding than other professors, but I enjoyed that and liked his class. However, because he focuses on proofs and strays away from examples, you need to put in some work outside of class.

Great teacher. Definitely knows his stuff. Entertaining lecturer and lectures are very important. Tests make up 80% of grade and they are never curved so be prepared on test days. Overall very reasonable and makes the class enjoyable.

Pierron was not good for dynamics. It was his 2nd semester teaching it, 90% of grade is from exams (2 midterms, 1 final) and 10% is from HW. HW is just write 2 questions about the problem. Spent too much time deriving equations, attempted examples, didn't finish them and sometimes was wrong. Class attendance dropped so much after a few weeks.

Avoid if bad at physics, otherwise you'll be fine. 2 midterms + 1 final = 90% of grade (9 problems total). Takes off a lot of points for messing up the math, but also gives 70% for just showing you know the process. 
Depends how you look at it, for me it made the tests more stressful and that didn't go well with my other classes.

His lectures were clear and well structured, and the homework was a breeze. However, 90% of the grade was from the exams (40% midterms and 50% final exam), so you absolutely must do well on them. Fortunately, all of the problems are from the textbook, so pracitce well and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Pierron is a great professor. While the class itself can present difficult problems, Dr. Pierron's lecture style involves working through a variety of different scenarios using a game plan that can be applied to any statics problem! 90% of your grade is from tests, but he's a fair grader and you know what to expect each time. Caring guy too!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy, eager to help. Prepares you for exams well
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Has this annoying thing where he makes you put two "questions" you have on your homework. I forgot to put them on the first HW and got a zero, which was annoying and made me get a B in the class. He's not a bad teacher, his exam questions are usually straight from the textbook so just do all of the textbook problems and its an easy 100 in the class
Love this man. I like how he teaches and he's pretty funny. The tests were fair and he gives plenty of study material.
I did not understand what he was saying, but his heart was in the right place.

the goat. defo take him if you can. such a cool person and an even better professor. class is not too difficult either if u listen to lectures and study material that he highlights in class. TB is a waste of time, only do past papers and HW and you will be absolutely fine

Great option for thermo. HW is an automatic 100 as long as you do it and tests make up 90% of your grade (lowest one dropped). Not much time/work if you understand the material well and can do well on the tests. Baguette/10 would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Homeworks are an easy 100%. However, 90% of your grade are the exam problems, so if you think that you don't have to practice, think again. But he is forgiving and gives you 70% credit just for proving that you understand how to solve the problem, 30% doing the math behind the solution. But don't miss lecture, he usually doesn't upload notes often.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A great option for this class. You know exactly what kinds of problems are on each exam, and he even gives you a sheet reminding you the steps to take. The sheet also breaks down percentages as to how many points each part of the question is worth. Good lectures as well. Don't sleep on homework or exam review, but a great professor all around.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Lectures are super informative and he has a sense of humor. Homework assignments are completion, and the two exams + final are most of the grade. Very accessible through office hours.

The class itself is kind of weird, you have to solve problems using 1-2 equations. For people who've taken CHBE 2100 or BMED 2110 this class is a lot like that.

Professor Pierron is the absolute best, ever! I do not say that lightly. Yes it's hard, but he gives you all the tool you need to understand the material well. Don't skip class because the textbook isn't half as helpful as he is. If you have a question, ask after class or in office hours because he will work with you till you understand. 11/10 prof
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: 90% tests meaning one bad test and little chance for an A. really informative lecture though
One of the best professors I've taken at Tech hands down. Amazing person, clear grading criteria, no surprises on tests, basically all the good stuff here and you can't go wrong taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class seems hard if you have no prior knowledge, but the lectures cover everything you need to know for the test. If you listen well and follow along with the practice problems in class, you could get a good grade without studying for the midterm since he teaches the content very thoroughly. Office hours are helpful if you are struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really great guy, but average professor - Though, most find him to be a good professor. He knew the material very well but sometimes had a hard time explaining the easier topics because of his deep understanding of the subject.

Honestly, one of the best professors I've had this semester. He is incredibly understanding and explains the material in a way you would understand. If you email him for help, he will set up an appointment immediately to address your concerns. Be careful on the exams as they are weighted heavily on your overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: He was honestly a blessing this semester despite what was going on. He is super understanding toward his students, even giving 24hrs to do all exams. He is pretty good at explaining things and takes the time to go through multiple practice problems during class, and fields all questions. Only complaint is that the exams are very heavily weighted.
Super understanding, funny, and lenient grader. He is one of the best professors I've ever had!

He has been great during COVID. His lectures are straightforward, and we have 24 hours to work on each exam. You just have to pay attention during lectures, and actually do the homework(he gives you solutions for the homework, he wants you to attempt them and submit any questions for a grade). Class grade based off 2 exams + final (90%) and HW(10%)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great guy and professor! Lectures have a lot of examples and less theory, which worked really well for me. Notes can get kind of messy, but nothing horrible. Gives a lot of practice problems for students during class, which makes some lectures more of a recitation. In person attendance during COVID. HW submit and pass, exams very chill. Recommended

Really really nice, funny and caring. Homework super easy, gives 100 if you just submit it. Exams kinda hard but it would be an understatement if I said he grades fairly. He helps you, gives credit to everything, somehow makes you get a good grade. Lectures a little boring but even though thermodynamics is hard, he will make it easy for you.
Prof pierron is the best. He goes through the material very well and gives logical steps for how to work out each type of problem. Tests aren't horrible if you pay attention in class and do the hw.

Professor Pierron explains complex thermodynamics in accessible and understandable ways. He is accessible outside of class and cares about his students. Gives a Word for test prep and tests are reasonable. Thermo takes a lot of work, but if you put in the hours of study and homework you can do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you are good at mechanical physics, then this class is perfect for you. There were few graded assignments (7 HW's worth 10% total, Exam 1+2 worth 25% each, & Final Exam 40%) so if you can learn the material, you'll easily make an A with little work. However, if you struggle with the material or are a bad test taker do not take this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a good professor who makes lectures entertaining. I really like that he engages the class and makes jokes along the way.
Great prof. Great at explaining material. Test takes most people the whole class to finish and abut challenging but overall learn a lot and also make funny comment as well

Definitely one of the best teachers at GT. I joined late GT and I had hard time to adapt, I didn't had much time to do my homework. He gave me a lot of advices and was interested in my situation. Rather than this, I will add if you are interested in understanding fatigue at a grad level, you should definitely take this class without hesitation.
Best teacher I've had at tech. Very organized and tests are easy if you do the hw. You can make do without a textbook in thermo.

Probably the best teacher I have had at Tech so far.  Great at explaining the material.  Cool, funny guy as well.  If you ever have questions, go talk to him.  Not too much homework and the tests are easy if you pay attention and go to class.  Definitely recommend.
Great class. Explains material clearly and is willing to help students.

There are so many things I want to say but not enough words in the English language to describe how goated she is. All I will say is she has never given a student below an A in her entire history of this course and she gave out max score on every assignment as long as you did it. Goated person and goated course.
One of the best professors at GT! She is quite caring and provides great feedback on assignments. This was an overall easy class but engaging.

I took KOR3415 online with her. The best professor ive had at tech, she is so sweet and genuinely cares about her students. she is very understanding, and her feedback on assignments is so kind. best prof ever
I don't usually leave reviews but I had to for her. She is absolutely the best. Simply take her if you're still deciding. She is so kind, understanding, and thoughtful. 사랑해요 선생님!
The kindest professor I've ever had. She is the absolute best and cares deeply for her students. Please take a course with her, she's amazing.

I can not even begin to describe how amazing of a teacher Mrs. Oh is. She is caring, kind, funny, and a great teacher. She always has a smile and never makes anyone feel left out of the class. She wants you to succeed and asks how you are doing even outside of class. 100/10 teacher and would take again if I could!
Very sweet professor; and took time and made sure that every student individually understood the content without being condescending.
Best teacher I've had in my 4 years at college. Great lectures, very funny and easy to understand. Also brings snacks for students.

Professor Oh was incredibly kind, funny, and helpful. She made the class fun with plenty of games and snacks. We moved pretty quickly in lecture but homework was graded easily, so it was easy to make an A in the class if you studied. There was less emphasis on speaking and practice, but she provided office hours for those looking to talk.

Professor Oh is the best! This is my second semester taking Korean with her and I wouldn't change her for anyone else. She's so caring both inside and outside of class; very understanding if you're having trouble/miss class; lectures are interesting. If you're deciding on taking Korean, make sure you take it with her.

Learning is always hard, but SSN Oh puts more focus on our actual learning and understanding over our grades. She's extremely caring and a very light grader. She's very available for help and often holds in class sessions and gives us snacks. I'm retaking her for 1002 and she's continued to be passionate about teaching.

Professor Oh is an amazing teacher! Her classes are always very engaging and she's always available to help students when they need. Despite being an online course, she encouraged us to come to her office hours and her in-person classes for extra help. She's an easy grader and provides great feedback on every assignment, and is overall encouraging.

Dr. Oh is such a warm-hearted, kind, and caring professor. She is dedicated to teaching and encouraging her students. I have never met someone with such a kind heart. I had her during COVID (2020) and she still remembers me personally! That's just the kind of person she is. I'd take all my courses with her if I could. 1,000,000/10.
Great class! I took Korean only to satisfy my humanity's requirement but this class was unexpectedly awesome. She even remember's and celebrates everyone's birthday.
She's really sweet and the makes the course pretty easy to do well in. It's an easy A if you are willing to do the assignments and put in a little time into learning the material.

She is the most caring and understanding professor I've ever had. I always feel comforted and welcome in class! She is also very accessible by phone number or office hours. Getting a good grade is easy in this class bevause she gives you opportunities to make up homework or even get extra credit after the final.
Korean class feeds me.

I love Oh SSN, she is a really fun professor. Unfortunately, her class gets a little confusing at times, and she would go on tangents often. But, whenever I ask her individual questions about Korean, she would give me great feedback and explain everything. The course itself having bizarre vocab lists, I wish they had more useful words on the list.

She was extremely fun and enthusiastic about learning Korean. All of her activities were fun and she went above-and-beyond to make sure we understood Korean and Korean culture. She was extremely accesible and went out of her way to help if you wanted it.

I don't even know where to start! She's absolutely amazing and super caring! She makes learning Korean so much fun, and the way she engages the class is really nice. She is super accommodating and you can tell that she really cares about you and your progress. If I could take her for my other Korean classes I would!

Professor Oh is by far the kindest most enthusiastic lecturers you will meet at Tech. She genuinely cares about her students and dedicates so much time outside of class (even during school breaks!) to help students practice Korean. She is so wholesome and is incredibly flexible. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Oh SSN is an amazing, charismatic person. She cares so much for her students and is encouraging and bright at every step. She is so kind and she really wants you to not only succeed, but really get a feel for the Korean language and culture. Definitely take her.

Professor Oh is so sweet and amazing. She truly cares about each and every student. I definitely recommend taking intro Korean classes with her. If you need help, she replies to emails very quickly and will help. She is very positive and wants all of her students to succeed.
Continues to be the best prof I've had at Tech, and one of the kindest people I've ever met
The kindest professor at Georgia Tech. Takes the time to write out personal emails to each student about test scores. Fun class and relatively easy if you do the homework

The nicest person I have met at Georgia Tech, maybe ever. Korean is a tough language, but Oh SSN really goes above and beyond to not only make it easy, but fun too. Lectures are interactive & enjoyable, and tests mirror HW. There's a ton of vocab quizzes, but only worth 10% of the grade. She cares deeply about her students & wants you to succeed.

Fun class. Professor is always excited to teach students Korean. Lots of vocab quizzes, but they're straight forward and easy. Tests are not difficult and if you're ever struggling, she is more than happy to help. Easy A. Homework is given often as well, but graded very generously.
Professor Oh might be my favorite person ever. She is extremely helpful and makes learning Korean really fun. I can't wait until next semester with her.

Obviously, with this being a language class you'll have homework but the textbook and workbook are cheap.  Professor Oh is great!  Vocab quizzes are often but easy.  Tests are more about application of the language.  There's also a recitation session.  There are a couple of simple projects. Overall, a great GPA boosting class.
Professor Oh made me love Korean! She's amazing! She is super helpful and really does everything to help you learn the language!
Awesome professor! Though attendance isn't mandatory, his lectures are so fun that it makes me want to attend voluntarily. Super flexible with grading and assignments. Super funny also.

pay attention to the lectures because virtually all of the exams are based solely on the lectures - his powerpoints are a little confusing to follow. exams are very easy (open note, not proctored, at home). you can tell he's very passionate about his work and psychology which is refreshing for a college course. very nice and easy to talk to.

Dr. V. was very caring and genuinely wanted us to learn how to meditate and practice mindfulness. The class was very easy going. Lectures consisted of meditation and learning about different techniques. Assignments included weekly reflections, a term paper, and two open-note exams. He also offers extra credit and is very responsive via email.

Verhaegen is an excellent lecturer who loves the subject and has really fun lectures. The class is dead easy: do your diary every week (takes 5 minutes), do your experiment credit for free points, and the tests are open internet, async and unproctored, so good luck NOT getting an A. Extremely easy, extremely fun, highly, highly recommend him.

Dr. Verheghen was a breath of fresh air among the profs I've had so far, every lecture was engaging and funny, I would go for the enjoyment of it. He incorporates activities that actually help teach the topics learned. Tests are very straightforward and applys the concepts from lecture.

Professor Verhaeghen is by far one of the best professors I have ever had. He has a kind and welcoming personality, his class is designed to encourage participation and minimize stress while still being incredibly educational, and I always looked forward to attending his lectures. He very clearly cares about his students and loves what he does.
Dr. Verhaeghen is a wonderful professor who makes his content very interesting and very evidently cares about students. Attendance isn't mandatory but going to his lectures are definitely worth it

Dr. Verhaeghen is one of the coolest professors I've ever had. He has very interesting lectures and makes you want to go to class. Exams are online and open note and there are only 2 exams and a final paper that is reflection based. As long as you participate and show effort, you can do well in his class.
Dr. Verhaeghen clearly loves what he does and has a fun time lecturing and including personal tangents. He is super kind on grading and if you just do the work you'll do well.

Dr. Verhaeghen is very caring and interesting as a professor. He always apologizes for possibly mispronouncing my name but he actually reads it right. He uses fun anecdotes and activities to make the lectures engaging and helps us focus even if its remote. Would definitely take his class again if there were options.

Excellent, funny professor that does his best to make online lectures engaging. Very knowledgeable on the topics discussed and usually has anecdotes to tie into lecture topics. Definitely wants his students to succeed and comes off as very caring. I took away a lot from this class and would take him as a professor again if possible.
Dr. Verhaeghen made each lecture fabulous to attend, and he managed the task of making online lectures with no one to bounce off of engaging. I was always excited to learn in his class.

Dr. Verhaeghen is a great professor and fantastic person. You get a lot more out of the class if you attend lectures, and he makes psychology really accessible. I am sad that I didn't take a course with him earlier.

Probably one of the coolest people I have ever gotten to meet. Incredibly laid back - just wants you to understand the material and have a good time. He is one of my favorite lecturers but is extremely humble. The tests are good at measuring your understanding and there's few unnecessary assignments. Would take him for every class ever

Dr. Verhaeghen is so kind and caring about his students. He understands how stressful Tech is and does his best to structure his class to alleviate that stress. If you put in the work, you will get an A!

No textbook is used for this course and exams are entirely based on lecture/slides. This can be a bit on an adjustment if you have more of a reading-based learning style, but Dr. V is a really talented and engaging lecturer.

Dr. Verhaeghen is so caring about his students and about psychology itself. There's no textbook for his class - it's all based on his lectures, so you gotta go. But he's a super engaging lecturer. Tons of real-world examples about psych, and occasionally walks us through an experiment on ourselves. Tests are fair and come straight from lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Wonderful and funny teacher, really cares about his students and always has something interesting to share.

Dr. Verhaeghen is a sweetheart and is very knowledgable about psychology. He is good at lecturing but his powerpoints are so long (like 200+ slides) which makes them really hard to go through. Grade is mostly comprised of 3 exams w/ essays and a final project; exams are somewhat challenging & require application of concepts (some stuff not in ppt)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 3012 Intro to Cognitive Psych - Very knowledgeable, approachable, down to earth professor - Lectures are amazing, very engaging and lots of fun demos! -He cares about students (he was always checking in on us during the coronavirus transition to online), allows a double-sided crib sheet for exams to reduce anxiety
He is amazing !

Verhaegen is very funny. Most of the lecture time is spent telling stories, most are funny, a few aren't. The class is graded on 3 midterms and a final (1101). Tests are just fine if you attend lecture and read your notes the night before

I took his Mindfulness and Meditation GT1000 and it was one of the best choices I made first semester. He is extremely caring, knowledgable, and a really cool guy. I would definitely recommend him for this class. If you show up with and open mind and participate, you are basically guaranteed an A.
Really great funny guy I always forget to do my diary entry though because it's due saturday night.

enjoyed lectures -- he's very funny (but a little quiet sometimes) basically only grades are weekly diary (free 100%), tests, and end of semester project study slides and go to class  tests will be very easy for you
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Pay attention during class and take notes. Tests are very easy. Enjoy the class and you'll be fine. Don't forget to do your weekly journal entries (basically a guaranteed 100% in the gradebook).

The course material is fascinating, but Dr. Verhaeghen brings even more fun to the lecture with his quirky personality. Just show up to lecture and do your crib sheet, and you'll be set for the tests.

Dr. Verhaeghen is a very sweet man who wants to make sure his students learn. His lectures can be pretty boring. His powerpoints are slightly annoying, they don't have much "structure" so they can be hard to follow when reviewing. Tests can be detailed sometimes.  He allows crib sheets for every single test, and they could be front-and-back.

Awesome professor who is extremely enthusiastic and understanding. The lectures were always fascinating. The class wasn't extremely demanding, you didn't have to write thousands of papers; although the tests did cover a lot of material. Really enjoyed this professor.
This professor is awesome! His lectures are always so interesting and he makes complex content seem so simple! I definitely want him as a professor again!

4 Midterms, 1 Final, 1 of 5 dropped. 80% of grade. Its a tough class and Perkins' poor handwriting and math/textbook heavy lectures makes it harder. His monotone/boring lecture style makes it hard to focus even you do attend. However, his homework's are very similar to the exams which are hard but fair and well written to fit the course material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: the class would not be hard if the lecture were actually readable but his handwriting was so bad, the tests and hw were pretty fair but the practice exams caused so much anxiety before the tests

He's ok. As other reviewers have said, his handwriting is AWFUL, making class notes very hard to decipher. Verbally the lectures are alright though. Homeworks and Tests are tough. Course communication is lacking, as he doesn't use canvas. He's clearly very knowledgeable but just not the best at making the content digestable.

Will is great! I agree with the other comments about his handwriting, but because his lectures align so well with the textbook, you don't really need his notes.  The homework can also be a bit hard but the exams only cover the real basics of each unit and with all the partial credit are pretty easy to get A's on.  He's also just a super nice guy!

you can tell Prof. Perkins is a knowledgeable and a nice guy. but he has one of the worst handwritings ive seen at tech (doesn't use slides) and uses exact word for word from textbooks

The HWs and Tests are doable, but they give out the most outrageously terrible practice exams and study guide. Half of it is not his fault; just a terrible course.
too much annoying hw, bad handwriting

Phys 2211 is very hard  (at least for me) and considered a weed out still but Dr. Padukka truly cares about her students and wants you to pass. Her office hours are helpful and she will even ask in lecture of hundreds of students how she can improve her teaching to help students to better on tests

The availability of Padukka was frankly incredible. The semester I took her, she had a zoom meeting you could join that ran along side the in person lecture. Padukka lectures were also very good. She covered content at a good pace and always allowed opportunities to ask questions. Always willing to help students, even if they needed extra help.

Great lecturer, kind, and always ready to answer any questions. She also streams her lectures if you can't (or don't want to) be there. Make sure to look at the GPS and homework when studying for exams

Dr. Padukka is such a kind and caring professor. Really makes an effort to help her students understand the material. Also understands physics really well! Do the homework and GPS problems (just do as many practice problems as you can), they really help with the exams.

Pretty straight forward physics class. She is absolutely amazing and super kind. Attendance is part of bucket points so you don't have to show up. Notes for her section and all other sections are posted online. Labs are super annoying, but online and peer graded. Also pretty good late policy.

Super nice! :) She answers all the questions students have in class or during office hours and even offered extra supplemental classes for those who have never done physics before. She does go through problems super fast, sometimes it was hard to keep up. All lectures are streamed online, but it's physics, so go to class or you'll fall behind.
Nice professor, pretty approachable if you have questions during/after lecture and lectures are filled with examples. Lectures are also streamed and uploaded online.

She's very kind and lectures are straightforward and full of examples. If you've taken physics in high school (algebra based even) this class is a breeze. Attendance can count towards bucket points but isn't required to get full credit in the category. Lectures are streamed online so you don't have to go in person.

Padukka is a great lecturer! She is good at explaining concepts and providing examples; however, the class is usually behind and we hardly finished each topic from every lecture. With that being said, she really cares about the success of students and goes out of her way to help!

Physics is notoriously difficult at GaTech. However, Padukka did give some good detailed examples in the lecture that helped greatly. The rating I gave is not her fault, but the fault of how this course is set up. I am simply not a fan.

Very good. Accessible, lectures are broadcasted recorded and the lecture notes are posted after every lesson, and approaches us like she actually wants us to do well in the class. All you can really ask for to be honest
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: streams her lectures so her lectures are super accessible!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Great lecturer. I'm not great at physics but she made this class much better. She was always happy to answer questions after class and clearly cares about her students. Her lectures are also recorded in case you can't go.

Professor Padukka has immense respect for her student's. She is always willing to answer questions and makes sure that the lecture material is understood without spending too much time on one topic from the goals of that day. Yes physics is hard, but she did her job well and made it bearable.
Avoid this guy at all cost if you wanna save your grade. I'd give 0 zero stars if I could. His exams are so much worse than the other classes for no reason.

I would give zero stars if I could. Professor docks points for not showing work in the exact format he has in his head. Students shouldn't be punished for actually understanding the material. If the answer is right, the thinking was right. Avoid if you have any other option. Your grade will reflect his inane standards, not your actual knowledge.
Powell is a really good lecturer and works very hard (especially in office hours) to ensure that every student has an understanding of the material.
Great professor across the board. Clear expectations, fair exams and homework, provides practice midterms/finals, best handwriting I've ever seen across all my schooling. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Powell is one of the greatest professors I've encountered- not only are his lectures phenomenal, they're accessible for people of all ability levels, and he is very approachable for question and clarification- including mid lecture.

Best professor I had this semester. Very passionate about abstract linear algebra. Exams and quizzes are manageable if you are willing to work. The class was tough due to many abstract concepts but it was fun and worth it. Definitely choose over MATH 1554, but expect to work harder.

The class material was so hard for me, but that's typical for Multivar at GT and wasn't really because of the professor. He's one of the better ones for this topic in my opinion. He's clearly knowledgeable and engaged in this topic and explains it quite clearly. However, the tests were like two levels more difficult than the practice and lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although professor doesn't really matter for large classes, I will say this professor teaches like you're reading a mathematics proof textbook. He introduces topics in a very formal and theorem based way followed by examples I found helpful. It works for some ppl and doesn't for others. He's a knowledgeable guy, but remember it more abt the TAs.

I liked Matthew Powell's classes! His lectures are all recorded online, so you don't have to go to class to stay up to date. He has really nice handwriting, super organized, and really knows his stuff. Super chill and kind guy. He really makes you think on his tests tho. If you want to get a good foundation in multi, take his class!!

He gave me a higher grade than I deserved which I'm very grateful for and why I'm rating him higher than I would have normally. However, his midterms were nothing like the past midterms he gave us for practice. I also had a hard time understanding his lectures. Also I think he weighted the midterms way too heavily and they were graded harshly.

Great lecturer and posted everything online. I attended lectures maybe 3 times the entire semester and scraped by with an A. Would have been way easier if I actually showed up, which is how calculus classes tend to be. His video lectures were great and the textbook is one of the few actually decent calc textbooks.

I really liked Powell. He was funny and you can tell that he truly cared about teaching. His lectures were a bit tedious at times, but he posts them on Canvas after class. His handwriting is IMMACULATE. Would recommend.

Prof Powell was a nice guy, but his long, yapful lectures were brutal. His tests were also hard next to the simple practice in class and practice for the final. His tests normally had one or two items that were mentioned once in lecture and never again. You may notice how many times I mention tests and that is because 3 midterms are 75% of grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: OK lecturer, but very hard tests. He makes them much harder than the practices for some reason and compared to other teachers. Avoid if you wanna do your best

{J}:There really isn't anyone like him. I mean come on, what a man. His tests are so unpredictable and {O}:exciting that you really never know what's coming next! I was on my toes the entire semester. His {K}:powerful voice and deep tone strike the multivariable knowledge straight into my heart. Prepare to {E}:learn a lot about your self respect :D

Avoid this guy at all costs. Lectures are 75 minutes of pointless rambling for 10 minutes of real content. Exams cover random throwaway comments from weeks ago, not the actual material. His voice is worse than putting a cheese grater to my ear and yet somehow sleep-inducing. You'll leave more confused than when you started. Total waste of time.
Intuitive and engaging lectures (which are also recorded). I believe the exams are noticeably harder than the other sections, but not to the point where it should affect a letter grade.

I emailed him about something important, and it took NINE days for him to respond. His lectures were detailed, but confusing. I only understood the material when my studio TA explained it in a better way. My advice - do/go to everything, the homework, the studio worksheets, the lectures, the studios.

A good teacher who helps students understand the difficult topics that multi presents. At first the class in general seems very complicated but you get the hang of things as the course goes on, and the teacher will make it as "easy" as possible for you to be comfortable with the topics as well.

Don't be fooled by the bad reviews. Powell is a very good teacher, multi is just a class that combines linear algebra and calculus so people dont do well. His lectures are very clear and paced well, and you are encouraged to ask questions or solve examples in class. I would definitely reccommend taking his class.

Mathew is not a very good lecturer. I found his lectures very uninteresting, and the examples he teaches don't prepare you for the exams at all. The examples he gave in class were very easy and simple but the test questions were much harder. I definitely recommend taking a different professor.
Pretty good lectures and tests were very similar to practice tests. He also gives plenty of examples in class that are similar to exam questions.

Professor Powell was decent, examples in class were fairly similar to exam questions. Lectures were fairly dry but mainly because of the material and not the prof. Exams are fairly easy if you attend lecture.

Matthew Powell is everything you want from a teacher. His tests are similar to his practice tests, and the final is a grade replacement for the midterms. For Fall 2024, he made the final extremely achievable if you studied. Overall, I definitely recommend taking him because he is fair with grading and a great lecturer.

Matthew Powell was not a great lecturer. Our tests were incredibly difficult compared to other sections, and we had constantly lower averages than the rest. Lectures are boring, and the examples he gives you do NOT prepare you well. TAs are the only saving grace for this class.

He is an okay professor. His lectures are boring and not very engaging. He talks too slow, and terrible at explaining. His exams are more difficult than the other sections, and it doesn't help that his TA's this semester weren't that great. The only good thing is that he records his lectures.

Powell is a nice dude and is very good at teaching, but his exams are weighted heavily and are much harder than what's seen in class. On the 3rd midterm, each multiple choice question was worth 10% (which comes out to 2.5% of your FINAL grade). Tough to get an A, there are easier multi professors, but if you want to really learn, Powell is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good lecturer, made concepts very clear. Records all lectures. Tests are kind of hard but I feel that the questions in lecture were good preparation unlike what others are saying. Just go to lecture and studio and you will be ok. You do not have to take the final unless you want to replace a midterm grade, useful if you have a lot of finals

He's not that bad of a professor, but he's not that good either. Some of the topics seen on the test sometimes weren't what was gone over in class which is what I think contributed to the low average test scores.

Dr. Powell is a good lecturer, but his exams are notoriously difficult. His sections averaged around 10% worse than the others for each midterm. He showed a lack of empathy towards students worried about the exam scores during class. It honestly feels like he's trying to prove himself as a tough professor, as this is his first year at Tech.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: smart guy but the material he chooses to teach in his class gives off the impression that he has no idea what he's talking about.
He berates students

If you want to learn real-time embedded systems, look elsewhere. If you want recycled lecture videos and a professor who spends more time ranting about “grade optimizers” than teaching, welcome aboard. Condescending, disorganized, no clear grading policy. I learned nothing except patience.

Calton's Intro to Enterprise course was the most disorganized course I've taken at Tech so far. No way to tell grade at ANY point during the course and course was set up in a very unfriendly way. Don't EVEN think about asking for a rubric or guidelines. Lectures were useless rants about “grade gaming” and “industrial age learning” . . . Beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rude professor and very unapproachable for questions. In lecture he just plays videos of himself. Once after class, he made a student cry when they asked him for feedback on the project proposal. His assignments are really vague and he doesn't doesn't provide a rubric for anything. I do not recommend taking any classes with this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I've had my fair share of professors at Tech, and I can say without a doubt Mr. Pu has been the most delusional. Every lecture has been spent talking about redoing the grading scheme and "industrial age students" that I'm not even sure what the class is about. The entire grade is based on one project with 0 guidelines and 0 feedback.

Learned nothing from this class. Lecture material doesn't matter at all. The prof will just scold you for gamifying his class and complain about "industrial age students". At the end of the semester, nothing will have been graded, and you will get 0 valuable feedback on project deliverables.

I know you're reading this and thinking: "He can't be that bad, I'm sure everyone else is just overreacting to a bad semester".

He is that bad. You will learn little in this course, be graded on one project, not be given any feedback on that project until there are 4-5 weeks left in the semester and the feedback will be negative AND unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This guy thinks he's the messiah of teaching. Instead of lecturing and grading assignments, he plays pre-recorded lecture videos during class and rants about how students are "industrial age learners" and "grade gamers" who are trying to get a good grade for no work. Be prepared to learn nothing in his class  and listen to useless rant twice a week
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far the worst professor I've had at GT. Only plays video lectures during class, but attendance is mandatory. He is extremely defensive and belittling. For every question you ask, he claims you are "grade gaming" and is on a crusade to destroy "industrial age thinkers." Fails to provide any actionable feedback or rubrics. Do NOT take his class.

Professor Pu has fallen victim to "Industrial Age" teaching and is what I call a "course gamer". He plays videos of himself ranting about unrelated topics while he stands next to his computer, glaring at the students. Being in his lectures is unreal, and I'm still not sure if this whole class has been an elaborate prank on me.
He's so goodlooking!
When professor Pu says "neeeeeed" about something, he means it!

Prof. Calton Pu is a great researcher. I know many students doesn't like his style. But I feel he is training students for a research oriented study. He does not want you to listen to his video lectures, but gives attention to the project that you will be doing. His feedback for projects are to the point, but you should be open minded to accept it.

I have never seen someone in my life so unapproachable and defensive when talking to them. Anytime you try to ask for clarification, he will tell you that "you have been conditioned in the ways industrial age thinking". 
All he does is play videos of himself during lecture, which have nothing to do with embedded systems. Awful, do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Read 2 papers/week and write a 1-page report.
Lectures are recorded and useless, attendance is mandatory. He rants about "industrial age classes", "gamified questions" & "optimizers" 
Incredibly defensive.
Vague descriptions of assignments and project omitting critical aspects you are expected to include leading to harsh grading. Unclear feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Unproductive class, lectures "ALWAYS" sidetracked by the prof discussing made-up L1/L2/L3 learning strategies and his vision for change
Project accounts for 65% of the grade, but lacks clear expectations, obsession with LLMs despite this being an "embedded" course
Grading is subjective, with no rubric provided, and the professor is condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Things he will do:
Rant about "industrial age" learning
Rant about "optimizers"
Shill his new method of teaching where he actually does no teaching at all
Grade on a whim and refuse to disclose or clarify why he failed half of the class

Things he will not do:
Teach Embedded Systems
Teach in general
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: No worth taking

Dr. Pu is by far, the harshest professor I've ever had at Georgia Tech. He is extremely unapproachable and will label your questions as "gamified learning strategies" when they are reasonable queries about expectations for course assignments. He does not respect his students or value their well-being.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Unenthusiastic, mean, and treats you like a child
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
-Very condescending and patronizing in communications (calls questions noise, very defensive in emails, etc)
-Disorganized class, Plays recorded lectures during class time
-More focused on crusade to end “gamifying” classes than actually teaching
-must write ~4 single space pages per week+ project writeups 
-No project rubrics
& more cons
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He asked us to summarize each lecture in which he only played pre-recorded videos reading each word on the slides out. Two reading assignments on each week requiring one-page commentaries. He was extremely MEAN when commenting on project proposals, showing his perfect mastery of rhetorical questions and sarcasm. DON'T TAKE THIS COURSE!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: NEVER TAKE THIS COURSE. Firstly, he is very aggressive and inconsiderate, and any reasonable request is called gaming his course. Secondly, most self-drafted semester-long projects are said to be worthless, and he expects us to produce more creative and better projects than commercial products. Do not let this course be your nightmare.

Pu is the most inconsiderate and laziest professor at tech In lecture we watch videos of him softly mumbling slides in a thick accent 2-4 papers due weekly The week where our semester group project proposal was due we had 4 papers due An extension was requested He responded by blaming students whom he called noise makers for gaming his class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Replays video lectures during in-person class times. Will repeatedly interrupt you during office hours. Dislikes being questioned on the structure of the class to the point of sending long rant-like emails not even a month into the semester. Incredibly time consuming class with most of the difficulty coming from the interactions with the professor.

Despite being somewhat easy, this was by far the WORST class I have ever taken. He just played videos of himself talking during class, which were incredibly boring, unclear, and unnecessary. The requirements for the class are unclear, which he justifies by claiming that its about "autonomous learning." Poorly structured and poorly taught. Beware.
He replays recorded lectures of himself during in-person lecture (which takes a long time to set up each class). Exceptionally dry and unclear about expectations.
An easy course with a number of reading assignments. Learnt a lot on the term project. Grades well and is good at class lectures.
Awesome!

unorganized + needs a writing class since he's bad at writing coherently and without grammatical/phrasal errors making it harder to answer basic questions. When questions arise during exams, he wastes precious time by simply reading the question again. I also have eyes. That is unhelpful.

He is approachable one-on-one outside of class, but grading is very strict and can feel snarky. Assignments often lack clear guidance, yet points are deducted for minor errors like spelling. The class may feel discouraging, but students can improve by adapting to his expectations.
Snarky and rude. Picky comments and feedback on work. Could/should have shown more kindness towards students. Don't take his class if you're looking for respect.

He was super nice, but not the best lecturer. A lot of the example problems were never finished and he does have a bit of an accent which made it hard to understand him. Exams were exactly like the homeworks and you got 3 attempts per question. He was also very generous with partial credit. If you study the practice problems, you should do good.

He's a decent, not great lecturer but has a really good understanding of the material and gives good advice. Tests and homework assignments are very short with multiple attempts per question and generous extra credit. The tests are very heavily weighted and the final is 40% though.

Final is 40% of your grade and honestly its really manageable (his lectures are hard to get used to but hes really sweet and answers questions), hes very generous with partial credit and almost always grants extensions if you ask.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: easy to follow if you pay attention in class. very similar to physics; if you understand physics this class will be fine. the only thing is that the class is very test heavy (exam 1 15%, exam 2 25%, and final 40%), but the homework helps set up well for the exam problems

Bad lectures, hard to understand. Left practice problems unfinished. Gave good partial credit on hw and exams. 3 attempts per question on hw and exams. Exam questions came directly from textbook, which had over 100 per chapter. Self study class basically

Any shortcomings are forgiven by how easy his exams are. You get 3 attempts per question from the same question bank as your homework. However, I'd still recommend going to lectures as he gives many useful tips on solving problems efficiently and does example problems.

He was nice and very caring about the students. He provided multiple office hours throughout the semester and he gave really generous partial credits, especially for the final. Tests were three attempts each and they are from the online textbook so if you do most of the textbook questions, you could get the same question for the exam.

It can take a little time to get used to his lectures, but once you've done that you're golden. Pay attention to the example problems and ask questions. He's a caring guy if you're confused, although he can come across as a little intense. Tests were insanely easy: 3 attempts per problem and super generous extra credit.

Sweet, funny dude. Terrible lectures involving unclear steps, undefined variables, and half-finished problems. But this is overshadowed by his wonderfully easy tests: 3 attempts for 3 textbook site HW questions + crib sheet + generous partial credit. When confused, the internet + the TAs can be your friend.
Recommended.
3 attempts on every exam question, super chill nice guy, great office hours, best statics professor at this school, all exams are easier than HW

Never completes his example problems in class and teaches like the class already know the material. I learned more by skipping class and watching YouTube videos. Nothing he said helps and he is incapable of explaining things in an way that makes sense.

Def Bods is difficult, but he knows that. The homeworks are very difficult, but the tests are much easier, so if you can do the homeworks, you can ace the class. Participation worth 3% (w/ 10% excusable), 11 homeworks worth 20% (w/ 2 drops), 2 midterms worth 19% each, and a final worth 39% that he curves. 2-sided cribsheets/exam, but they stack.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor. Def bods can be a little rough sometimes, but he is good at explaining the concepts and will go over them again if you ask questions. Would take again 10/10. The homework is from the most recent ed. of the textbook, but I just checked it out of the library when I needed it, and I relied on his lectures and slides for the material.

Very kind and approachable professor who is always willing to help and accessible during office hours. However, in-class examples were often hard to see due to small writing. Piazza responses were sometimes indirect, and grades were released very late, making it hard to know how I was doing before the drop deadline.

Really nice person, very clearly cares about students. Would even go out of his way to talk to me outside of class. That being said, he's a pretty dry lecturer and he teaches off slides he did not make. He does not answer most piazza questions with anything other than 'talk to me after class or in OH'. However, homeworks and projects are easy.

Professor Zhang is a very good lecturer who describes the content in a very methodical manner. The projects, while really involved, were super interesting, and I feel like I understand a part of Computer Science that was opaque to me before this class.
I met my SO in this class :)

Took ECE6100 (x-listed with ECE4100 & CS4290/6290). Lectures are not recorded so attendance is mandatory if you want to do well on exams, though, they are very engaging. Exams are a little tricky but there are ungraded "homeworks" with very similar questions and you can make a crib sheet. Labs are fine if you know C/C++ and are fairly scaffolded.
Great class

Awesome lecturer but slides aren't so good and lectures are not recorded. So attendance is mandatory if you actually want to understand content. Also made the first lab worth 4% of final grade due during the first week (while registration is still open). Exams are difficult purely bc of the amount of content you need to know, there is a lot

Great professor! Probably the best lecturer I've had at GT. Teaches with slides but in the most ideal way possible by using them as support, not as a crutch. Projects were fairly simple if you have decent C/C++ knowledge. Tests were a little difficult as they were modeled after the ungraded homeworks, but doable.

Lectures like he's telling a story–makes potentially dry content exciting. Projects were excellent (if a bit hand-holdy), with smooth debugging and problems interesting enough to ponder AFK. Tests felt hard, but there was so much curving and extra credit by the end that lower quartile class grade was a comfy A. Kind prof who will brighten your day!

Took CS6290 (crosslisted 4290/ECE 4100/6100). Lectures extremely engaging and helpful. Tests a bit different than lecture content, but studying previous exams and practicing computations helped. Final was ‘Do-No-Harm'. Projects were well structured with TA debug outs. Small extra credit opportunities were given. Favorite prof at GT, he knows a lot!

He himself as a professor explains concepts about Quantum Computing well. The problem is that all of the preparation we did (quizzes, labs, and practice midterm) did not compare or prepare us for the content on the midterm. I found that midterm to be exponentially more difficult than anything we had seen and most of the content was brand new to me.

Had this professor for ECE 3056, so this class had a lot of overlap in terms of content and projects. Very knowledgeable and inspirational about the topic. Tests were fair, with practice tests from previous years given as well. Projects were mostly simulations of concepts discussed in class. Pitches his special topics course when given the chance.

The labs are 40% of the grade. 2 tests + final each at 20% each. The final was given as "do no harm". You should make an A on all of the labs. The results you should receive are given, and you can compare. The prof is a very accomplished researcher and engineer and gives great lectures.

Lectures were off powerpoints, along with back and forth discussion between students and professor. No electronics allowed. Extremely knowledgeable of the topic and very inspirational. Projects were models of concepts taught in class, coded in C with skeleton code provided. Tests were fair and similar to old tests he had given out. Definitely take.
Best professor ever at Tech. So clear and confident of his topic and very inspiring. taking his integrated class next semester

She is super passionate about film and also extremely educated. The lectures can be boring since she doesn't follow a specific curriculum, but cool. The entire grade is based off attendance, your final, and weekly film screenings. She def gets strict when it comes to the final project and your essay/film ideas. Do NOTTT take it at 5pm

Very sweet and passionate about film. Lecture isn't always the most engaging since she's speaking the whole time. For final projects, there were creative options (short films, poster series) or you could write a 10 page paper. She's always open to questions and is very willing to help or give feedback.

SO MAD!! I DID ALL THE WOR AND OUT SO MUCH EFFORT AND STILL RECEIVED A C+
PROFESSORS LIKE THIS SHOULD NOT TEACH.

I think Dr. Wang is the victim of a poorly executed curriculum. She is a wonderful and bubbly human being, but she failed to pique my interest in film. Her class is strictly attendance mandatory (25% of grade) but absolutely does NOT need to be at all. She's worth taking as a professor in general, but I would avoid this course specifically.

Professor Wang is sweet and caring. But most of the grade goes to the midterm and final essays, which must be 10+ pages long, personally, I found that a bit annoying. There's a screening and a discussion about it on Canvas every week but you only have to finish 7 discussions for the semester.

Professor Wang is very sweet and cares a lot about her students. Lectures are long but the topics are often interesting and it isn't vital that you pay attention or read the textbook. The only grades are attendance, a weekly discussion post on an assigned movie, and two papers. She is very lenient on extensions for the papers and easy to contact.

Professor Wang is a very nice person, but I found her lectures incredibly hard to follow. I took her class in a short semester but, still, the lack of any structure in the lectures made it hard to retain the information. Also, she isn't very tech-savvy, which got in the way of remote learning. All that said, the content was interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved Professor Wang. A very interesting class with lots of movies to watch. As long as you participate and keep up with the movie schedule you will be fine.

Shes an amazing human being who really cares for her students, but she has no idea what shes teaching. She has no business teaching anything about film because she clearly has no idea how making a film actually happens. She has no technical knowledge and only outdated knowledge of techniques used in film.

Qi is the sweetest. She genuinely loves what she teaches. Her lectures are thorough but not very linear/organized, so it's hard to take clear notes. Few assignments, but she makes it very clear what you need to know/study for the tests. As long as you keep up with the material and get organized before tests, you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Qi is amazing!. However, this class is dependent on 2 test grades and a final essay. I am personally not a fan of this, and do much better with project based learning. You must take notes in lecture and be attentive, but then again it's only 50 min every other day. If you're ever struggling, she's the most caring prof you'll ever have!!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Best professor I have had at Tech by far. Explained the content very in-depth with ample access to resources and practice problems outside of class. Would not take any other professor for Orgo 1.

The best orgo professor by far, not an easy class but if you go to lecture and get help when you need it you'll be fine. They started doing a hybrid section for this class recently as well as the normal 3 day a week class, DO NOT TAKE THE HYBRID ONE. Everyone I know from that class got way worse grades, her lectures are what make the class doable

Pollet is the absolute goat of organic chemistry, and it makes such a daunting class feel very simple. If you go to class, attend recitation, and do everything that's expected of you (as clearly outlined in the syllabus and weakly threads), an A is more than doable.
Orgo is hard, but she makes it worth it! Super helpful with all content and really cares about students well being and grades in general. If you get the opportunity, definitely take her for orgo!

Orgo is a hard subject, but she makes it as digestible as possible. Exams are (mostly) like the practice materials she posts, and the grading scheme is structured so that getting an A is very manageable and a B is almost guaranteed.

She is so great with her lecturing style! She makes it clear what she is looking for, and she is very available to her students. The course itself is difficult, but she makes it as easy as she can. She is super sweet, and I would recommend taking this class with her!

She is the sweetest teacher ever! She truly wants all of her students to succeed and does so much to help. Her practice tests are amazing and the key to doing well in this class. The course picks up a lot after the second exam, so be prepared but definitely a doable A and a very easy B.

Pollet is great! Very easy to get a B if you attend most/all of the classes (PRS-based system). The class is set up for you to succeed - take advantage of recitations. It goes a little fast after synthesis, so be prepared.

Pollet is a pretty epic teacher. She has a wonderful french accént and tests are fine. They're often similar to the practice tests with the exception of the occasional curveball. Pollet does however like giving out extra credit for CIOS and midterm surveys. The PRS can be annoying at times as attendance and correctness matters but ok.

Nice but strict lady. French accent but not so heavy you can't understand. Called me out for not doing classwork during class (I was reading the textbook instead of doing practice problems) but the next week she asked if I was feeling better and more prepared. Her answer keys are hard to decipher. Extremely lenient grading scale (super easy B).

Took the hybrid course with her (attendance required once a week & Thursday exam session). Lectures are engaging & informative. In hybrid state, reading the textbook is CRUCIAL as there is only so much she can cover in an hour per week. Lowest exam of 4 is dropped. Online hw and quiz per week. You can dodge the final if exams total is high enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The instructor doesn't provide much guidance. The lectures feel more like information dumps than actual teaching, which makes it hard to grasp the concepts.

Dr. Pollet is genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had. She makes organic chemistry easy to learn. She is extremely accessible outside of class and gives amazing support when you ask for clarification. If you are taking orgo 1 try to get her.

She is a good chemistry professor who wants her students to do well. There was a TON of extra credit given throughout the semester, that you didn't have to do too well on exams to get an A. However lectures are kinda disorganized. She jumps in the topic and goes too fast without giving a brief overview.

DO NOT take the async class if possible, I did not have a choice and really regret it. She is a caring professor who is very knowledgeable but her videos were so unclear and I rarely got anything out of them. Some of the exams I took had questions I had never seen in my life...first time I ever studied and felt horrible after taking exam

Orgo is def a hard class in general but Prof. Pollet did a good job at making class engaging. I took the hybrid section and I would not recommend it if ur not a self learner and can stay on task with a majority online component, because I def should be utilized my time a bit better. Lots of study material is provided and attendance is mandatory.

Super passionate and incredible professor. Orgo is hard, but she makes it doable. Old exams and recitation packets sometimes contain problems nearly identical to the actual exams. Go to recitation and do the extra credit. Do not fall behind in this class. Ask her for clarification after lectures, she's good at explaining. Great TAs.

I love Dr. P. I think I did so well because everything was super clear on how to succeed. On day 1, she said to practice everything and utilize all the resources given. You have a lot of resources, but they all are really helpful in their own way. Also, just do the extra credit. You'll thank yourself later. TAs are the best too.

I didn't think that you could get a chem prof better than Shepler but wow, Pollet surpassed all my expectations. Her lectures are incredible (she's hilarious) and she's always super helpful in office hours. Very fair grading scheme & TAs are also by far the best I've seen (shoutout Nathan + Ariane!). Lot of work but I looked forward to every class.

Orgo is a notoriously hard class, but from the start Dr. Pollet laid out exactly what was needed to do well with fair grading. The exams are similar to the practice - she is not a teacher who tries to "trick" you. She is extremely accessible outside of class and is one of the kindest individuals I have met. If you put in the work, you will succeed!

Dr. Pollet made Orgo 1 actually doable. There is a lot of preparation for the exams, and if you go to recitation/exam review sessions you can easily succeed in this course. Dr. Pollet cares a lot, is funny, and keeps the content interesting. 10/10 recommend

Absolutely amazing teacher. In order to do well in this class you have to put in a lot of work but it is very worth it. Opportunity to exempt the final if you do well enough and the exams are not unreasonable. Lot's of outside of class practice and practice to get better. She is incredibly sweet and caring too. 10/10!!

I was expecting to struggle because in the first place orgo isn't easy, but I do think Dr. Pollet does an amazing job at thoroughly explaining the concepts, reactions, and how to approach problems on exams and assignments. She and TAs do a good job of "brain-washing" and pounding concepts into your head so you'll remember things better. Loved her!

Pollet is a great lecturer and makes organic chemistry very easy to understand, using lots of practice problems and examples for participation credit in lecture. She is engaging, and TAs are tons of help in lecture and outside. It is easy to feel confused in class, though, since she covers content quickly and moves to examples. Study outside class.

Dr. Pollet is very good at organic chemistry, and the overall class structure was great. Yet, she is very easily angered and seem to get more strict and discourteous to students as the semester went on. If you do practice tests attend lecture you will be fine. She does leave some key topics out of lecture and requires videos at home.

Made lectures interesting and knew material well. The studio section (no in person lectures) can be difficult because it's a lot of self-teaching, but she posts a lot of supplementary resources, and she and the TAs host several office hours/recitations each week.
Makes organic chemistry a very enjoyable and understandable topic than it seems. Extra credit opportunities and can exempt the final. She is very knowledgable and is super caring to her students!

For as hard as I heard orgo was, Pollet made it much more manageable and understandable. It still takes a lot of work to stay caught up, and to get lecture credit with the online in class questions you do have to go to lecture, but the work was what I expected and Pollet was a good teacher.
Funny, passionate lecturer. Makes a hard subject much more interesting. Lots of practice problems during lectures, which is needed for orgo. Highly recommend.

She was a wonderful teacher- after the horrors of gen chem I was worried, but she genuinely made orgo such an easy topic and tried really hard to help everyone. She has a ton of built in cushioning with grading, so even if you do bad on an exam you won't be affected too harshly. Was really funny and really prepares you for orgo 2. Take her asap

Expected students to spend 9-12 hours outside of class reviewing lectures, and additional time doing homework and assignments. The exams were tricky, and the review guides were misleading. I had to hire a tutor outside of the school because the orgo team was not very helpful and often did not seem happy to help:(

Amazing professor for orgo! She cares more about you learning the content than trying to get a specific letter grade. She has a lot of things in place to help you succeed in the course and the practice tests helped a lot. She goes over content fast in lecture but other than that it was a great course.

Dr. Pollet was very nice and cared A LOT about orgo. That being said, her lectures weren't always the greatest, but still got you everything you needed to know. She offers a good bit of extra credit, and I think the tests were fair. Lots of resources outside of class.

dr pollet was a joy to have as a professor! she is very funny, and i always looked forward to her lectures. i can thank her for having an amazing orgo 1 experience. her class is very straightforward, and she makes it clear what she expects. plenty of practice exams, and final exam exemption is available if you get an A average on exams.

She makes orgo 1 so easy. She isn't really a geat lecturer, I learned all my content through the Wiley textbook (great textbook btw). There's one homework and quiz every week, all graded for accuracy but multiple attmpets on hw and 2 on the quiz. Exams are very easy if you study past exams. she reuses lots of past questions for MC. Take her!

Awesome professor but the class is built for students who are strong in chem. If you have struggled in Chem, be prepared to do a good amount of work outside of class. Pollet explains things very well and the textbook is super easy to understand. All of our exam averages were in the 70s. Her grading scheme has a 70 as a B, so you'll definitely pass.

Dr. Pollet was an amazing teacher who greatly improved my appreciation and understanding of organic chemistry. She is passionate about the subject and that shines through in her teaching, which helps her students succeed. She is a fair teacher who listens to her students and genuinely wants everyone to succeed in the course.
