I am happy with my grade in the class, but being in the hybrid course, I don't feel that the once a week studios necessarily helped me all that much. There was incredible amount of work I had to do outside of class to learn the content. The extra credit opportunities were nice though, and the exams were pretty fair.

Dr. Pollet teaches orgo as if its poetry - as someone a little hesitant about taking this class, she made it very easy to comprehend. She's super approachable for questions too, but you definitely need to practice orgo outside of class if you want to do well.

Dr. Pollet is an incredible professor. Needed an 88 for an A and a 70 for a B. Opportunity for 5% extra credit. Made orgo enjoyable by breaking down complicated topics into an easily digestible manner. Possible to exempt the final, but the final is generally more difficult than the midterms. Practice problems are the best way to learn.

The best prof I have ever had, the orgo is hard regardless but she makes it infinitely better. She is the prof that got me to switch my major to chem. She is truly that inspirational. She is also quite funny, her accent can make it a little hard at times, but not an obstacle of concern at all.
Prof. Pollet is a great instructor (a slight accent but not too difficult to understand) and allows you to exempt the final as well. The course and tests are fast-paced but very achievable.

Pollet was an amazing prof and I loved her lectures. Orgo 1 was difficult and I often had issues with the TAs grading my exams but I enjoyed every minute of lecture. Would definitely recommend Pollet, but be prepared to put a lot of effort into this class.

Dr. Pollet is a great lecturer and her orgo class is more than fair when it comes to opportunity via final exemption and test drop. The TA's grading were a little off at times but the rest of the class was fantastic.
Dr. Pollet is passionate about organic chemistry. It makes the class more engaging for the students.

Dr. Pollet is one of the best professors I have ever had the pleasure of learning from. She speaks chemistry like it's a language. She takes her time going through her lecture slides, constantly asking questions and pushing you to learn deeper. One of the nicest people I have ever met, she could probably fail me and I would say thank you.

Dr. Pollet is among the best professors at Georgia Tech. She takes organic chemistry, a known difficult subject, and makes it enjoyable and almost entertaining. You can tell she truly enjoys the concepts she is teaching and that makes a world of difference to a student. If you get the opportunity to take her for CHEM 2311, do it without hesitation.
Dr. Pollet is bad at lecturing and the class is poorly unorganized. She spends a great amount of time on things we do not need to know for the test.

I am not smart and did bad in gen chem. Dr. Pollet explained things so well in lectures-- she didn't expect you to have any prior knowledge and explained things from the basics. There was so much practice in lectures and barely anything was on the test that we didn't explicitly go over in class. SO much extra credit too and an 88 counted as an A.

Dr. Pollet is one of my favorite professors at Tech. She is super caring and her lectures are always extremely helpful and fun. She's truly passionate about orgo and does everything she can to share that passion with her students. She has extra credit and an opportunity to exempt the final with an A. Orgo is a hard class, but she makes it so easy.

Dr Pollet is a great teacher, but her lectures can be confusing and poorly organized at times. However, she tries her best to make orgo as intuitive and doable as possible. She offers tons of extra credit and is very caring. Would definitely take again.
Dr. Pollet is extremely caring and flexible, but orgo 1 is going to be hard regardless. Sometimes her lectures can be confusing, but her tests are fair and she offers tons of extra credit.
chef's kiss

I love her lectures, but the content goes by QUICK. You need to be on top of things or you will fall behind. Some people don't like her lectures because she speaks to you as if you are an organic chemist which works for some (like me) and not so well for others. Grading is reasonable and you get good partial credit. There is final exemption.

Dr. Pollet cares about her students and wants them to do well. Exams can be tough but there are a lot of extra credit opportunities. Her lectures are interactive and make you want to learn more. Would definitely take again.

Dr.Pollet was overall a great and caring professor. Her lecture style might not appeal to some, as she goes through most of her content in pre-lecture videos, and then goes less in-depth in class, mainly with with an in-class question-based approach. She gives tons of extra credit, is accessible outside of class, and can explain topics well.

Pollet is truly the best at Gatech, she genuinely cares about her students and finds a way to make Orgo fun. She offers a LOT of extra credit, so it's quite easy to get an A/B in the class even with terrible test scores. 
Sidenote: she has a strong French accent, so for those who are not really fluent in English it might be hard to understand her.

Great lecturer. Clear assignments and expectations. Gives extra credit on exams. Can exempt final and is manageable to exempt as well. Use orgo as a second language textbook rather than the course textbook, makes life much easier. Dr. Pollet was always accessible by email or in person as she would always hold office hours before lectures.

The bulk of information is included in pre lecture videos, which in my opinion didn't do a great job of explaining material. Probably necessary to do some work on your own in order to understand the material fully.

I absolutely love Professor Pollet. She made organic chemistry (a very tough subject), easy to digest and even enjoyable. There is a bit of homework but nothing crazy. Unlike other professors, she doesn't rely on lecture videos outside of class to teach the material. Gives lots of extra credit opportunities and is super understanding and nice.

Dr. Pollet was an excellent professor and by far the best professor I have had at Tech. The class was difficult as any chemistry class is expected to be, but she made it easy and engaging allowing me to learn and enjoy the class. Her and the two TAs this semester were very helpful and accessible. The plus leader was also great.

Dr. Pollet is one of the best professors I've had. As a person, she is extremely caring and hilarious. Her class is hard, but it is possible to get an A if you use additional resources outside of class. The tests are very difficult but partial credit helps.

She does a really great job during lectures of explaining everything, but her tests are hard. I would say that she knows her class is hard, but she definitely makes it possible to get an A. She has a lot of study resources though to succeed.
Great professor and extremely helpful. Definitely take her for chem 2311 over any other professor. Class is hard but A is doable with built in extra credit, weighting, lowest grade forgiveness,  etc.

Dr. Pollet is a great choice for the course. She makes lecture engaging, she's extremely knowledgeable on the content, and has A LOT of supplemental material and videos that are great for practice and mastery of the content. She does go a bit fast during lecture, but do the HW, practice a lot, watch her pre-lecture vids, and you'll be great!

Dr. Pollet is super sweet and witty, very thorough with her material and also understanding with her students. Most of the issues I had with the class were with the design of the class itself/course load, but she was really nice regardless. Participation holds a lot of weightage in this class, so go to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Pollet is a great choice for CHEM 2311! Orgo is a hard course alone, and will be a course you will need to fight for your grade. The thing that saves most students is that a 70 is a B, but an A is 88, so you need to work for the A. Easy to pick up extra points, like participation, homework, and quizzes. Lowest midterm is dropped. Would retake!

Really great professor, she definitely knows her stuff. Also, Dr. Pollet has a lot of experience teaching orgo 1 at tech, so she knows how to teach this class as well as I could've asked for. This is a difficult class and an A average on 4 exams and 10 quizzes lets you exempt the final. Do the practice tests before each exam and you'll be fine

Dr. Pollet is a professor that you'd want to hang out with. She is witty and always has interactive lectures. But she does not do a good job explaining concepts and many times skips the basics, so studying before lecture is recommended. There are many EC opportunities so don't fret a bad test grade. Also, you can exempt the final.

As far as gt classes go its not bad. It's a lot of people's first more abstract/conceptual class so that is why orgo gets a bad reputation but professor pollet gives a ton of resources to be able to learn. I showed up to class did the homeworks and studied only the night before for the exams and got an in the class. Exempting the final is harder.

TAKE POLLET!! SHE'S THE BEST
Course was hard as expected, but she really cares and makes an effort to help students learn and succeed. Awesome office hours and lectures, I wish I could take her for orgo 2 but she doesn't teach it. She also gives opportunities for ec and bonuses. As long as you put the work and have determination you'll make it out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I can barely understand what she says and she gets annoyed when students misunderstand her or ask questions in class. She expects you to just know everything and has an attitude. Very unapproachable and has in class participation questions for accuracy. The tests are extremely hard and she does not prepare you for them.

Dr. Pollet is one of my favorite professors at Tech. She is a great lecturer and explains things well, and has a great sense of humor and personality that makes them very enjoyable. It is clear she cares about her students and her work deeply. Tests are very difficult, but expected because it's ochem. Can exempt the final if you have an A average.

Very friendly and approachable, made a tough premed class easy to digest. Lectures were super informative. In-class PRS/TurningPoint questions are graded (no bucket system), but 90+ is achievable since you can collaborate with neighbors. You can skip the final if you average 90+ on the quizzes and 4 midterms. Extra credit with discussion forums.

Dr. Pollet is a very fun and engaging lecturer. Her lectures can be very heavy, but they are not tedious. She uses PRS system for class participation and you have to get answers correctly to get the full points. Her tests can be quite hard and she doesn't give a lot of partial credit. There are extra credit assignments but they were worth 0.02%

Shes hilarious and engaging! The tests are difficult, as expected in orgo, but her grading is forgiving (in the end, not in the moment). Shes really passionate about what she does and she has such a quick wit that keeps you engaged.

Dr. Pollett is clearly an expert, but not a fantastic lecturer. She is not a bad teacher, but this class structure is very harsh and the only thing that saves it is the fact that a 70 is a B. Her exams are incredibly difficult with tough rubrics and her quizzes tend to be completely random. Overall not a bad choice for orgo 1, but be ready to work.

She is really funny and caring, but the tests can be really hard and arbitrary. The class is half flipped: half videos at home and half content in lecture. She's overall good though, but not an easy A.

Yes, Pollet is witty and fun, but that doesn't make up for her lack of teaching. Seriously be prepared to learn all the material by yourself. She does offer a good bit of extra credit which is nice, but you're ultimately stuck learning organic chemistry on your own. Weekly quizzes are 5 questions. Exams are take-home and the final is in-person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The subject is tough, but Pollet's lectures are great (but only if you come prepared to class). The quizzes were horrible - it was more luck than studying that determined your grade. The questions were random, so students had quizzes of different difficulties. Test were extremely difficult; the lowest test is dropped if you don't exempt the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I loved taking CHEM 2311 with Dr. Pollet! It's a tough class for sure, but her lectures are informative and enjoyable. I would definitely recommend reading the textbook as a supplement The tests and quizzes can be frustrating as quizzes are random and test grading is not too clear, but that is more of a reflection on TAs. Highly recommend Pollet!!

Professor Pollet is great. Lots of resources and great accessibility. The class structure is not as great. All questions on the weekly quizzes are of random difficulty and the tests have unclear grading criteria. It doesn't help that Orgo I is one of the hardest classes in general (though, the steep grading curve and exam exemption is very useful).
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed taking Dr. Pollet's class. She is an absolutely enjoyable teacher and really knows what she's talking about - she was really funny and caring about her students. I also liked the structure of the class. As long as you understand the material (which I found incredibly hard) you'll be okay. The grading scale is friendly.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: 1315 goes hard and fast. You can't skip a single day. But prof explains things VERY well. You just got to put in the work. And make sure you go to recitation and PRACTICE, but she gives you all of the practice problems and tools you need to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Pollet is really nice and gave several extra credit opportunities throughout the semester which helped. Overall, the class is really difficult and the pace is really fast so falling behind is really easy. You will definitely need outside resources to help because the lectures aren't enough to understand all the material.

Pollet cares about her students and is very approachable, but the class is HARD. You genuinely have to do practice problems every day, review material, and go to office hours/PLUS to do well, which isn't realistic for all. The class has a weird curve, and a 50 on every exam gets you a B (but getting a 50 is HARD). Failing averages on every exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She gave 11 to 14 page tests and got mad that no one was submitting it within an hour. She'd start talking in french during class, and I still don't know what a constitutional isomer is.

I'm sure Dr. Pollet is great in the in-person setting, but virtual learning with her was not the best. Throughout the semester, she shut down student feedback from mid-semester surveys and was unresponsive to some concerns. She does have pretty long tests but provides lots of study resources. Be sure to do homework and participate!

I believe she is a good professor, but had a harder time transitioning to online. The units were taught out of order, and lectures could get confusing. The tests are difficult and long, but you can bring your grade up with homework and participation. A 70 is the minimum for a B which makes it a manageable class.

This class is hard and while she explains things well-ish, there's still a lot of concepts and things that aren't well explained, which leaves a lot of holes so you will want to read the textbook and find another source to help you. You can also look forward to having your homework questions ignored on Piazza so make friends with your classmates.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Pollet is an incredible professor who really cares about her students. The class is tough for obvious reasons, but she does her best to help all students succeed. Make sure you don't fall behind on the material, and use the many resources she has provided. Overall, I definitely recommend her if you want to have a good grasp of orgo.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Pollet is probably the best professor I've had so far. She's witty and engaging but also makes sure you know the course content very well. Her office hours and review are very helpful, I would definitely recommend her for Orgo I.

If all of my chem professors were like Dr. P I wouldn't be so worried about those classes. She is an amazing teacher and truly cares about her students. Her lectures are actually somewhat entertaining. Definitely one of my favorite professors at Tech.

Probably the best professor you will have! Very funny and witty, and she structures the class so that you will have every opportunity to succeed. I didn't get to skip the final, but I loved the class and worked hard. This class is very hard and you need to study weeks in advance even, but you'll enjoy Dr. Pollet as a professor.

Dr. Pollet is one of the best professors I have had at Georgia Tech. She is extremely helpful and goes to lengths to make sure her students are doing well. The class is challenging and needs attention to make sure you do well in it, but having Dr. Pollet makes it remarkably manageable.
Professor Pollet explains the concepts in class very concisely through her powerpoints and makes organic chemistry more engaging than ever, but my opinion could be biased as a chemE major

By far, the best chemistry professor I've had at Tech. Dr. Pollet explains concepts in a way that makes sense. There are many opportunities for exam practice questions; start them early, and ask for help on questions you don't understand at office hours. Dr. Pollet wants her students to do well and creates an environment that fosters success!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Take her. She's great.

Extremely Difficult class if you make it harder than it is. Don't rely on the tests to do well in this class, do every single homework and go to the lecture for the PRS Questions, they will really help you out at the end. Dr. Pollet is a fun and caring professor if you give her a chance, don't make this harder on yourself!
Organic chemistry was made even more difficult due to her tendency to lose her trains of thought halfway through explaining things.
She is a good teacher but doesn't explain things thoroughly. The class goes very fast and the tests are very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Pollet was is an amazing professor. She makes lectures very enjoyable and is very good at explaining concepts. She cares about her students and wants them to succeed! She is always willing to help you in office hours and makes things clear to understand. Do the practice tests and study your notes/textbook.

Dr. Pollet loves organic chemistry and loves teaching. She makes lecture fun and is very approachable outside of class. She can go very quickly sometimes, but I think that is the same in every organic chem class. Tests are hard, but if you study in advance and do lots of practice problems, it is a very manageable class.
Dr. Pollet is amazing! She is so passionate about Organic Chemistry, which is shown through her lectures. She also very kind and helpful in office hours as well.

Dr. Pollet is a fantastic professor. She is entertaining and explains the concepts well. She is definitely enthusiastic about organic chemistry and very knowledgeable. Dr. Pollet seems to have fun at lecture and will make herself laugh multiple times a lecture.

Dr. Pollet is a really great professor, she knows what she is talking about and is very engaging. She has a great sense of humor and can relate to students well. Go to recitation and put the work in and you will do well.

Orgo is hard, no matter who the professor is, but Pollet taught the material in an engaging way. The class was taught in Scheller and I always made it on time and rarely skipped (skipped because I wanted to study for other classes). She's kind enough to record her lectures, so if you do have to miss a class, it's easy to catch up.

Pre-Lecture videos are posted for each chapter - very helpful to watch before class since the course covers a good bit of material. Clicker questions every class for a grade. Every test had at least 5 bonus points to be earned; she is generous with CIOS points/midterm survey points when it comes to exams. The class was initially curved.

Professor Pollet is a SOLID choice for Organic Chemistry I. She knows exactly how to communicate the material clearly enough to be understood. Her pre-recorded video lectures set you up for success in class if you watch them and take notes. Take her stuff seriously and pay attention. She's also hilarious, so get ready for some good belly laughs.

She's a really good teacher but this class is probably one of the harder chem classes here. She explains things really well is fairly enthusiastic in lecture shes also a really cool person and is willing to help. Don't fall behind on material tho everything builds on itself

She obviously loves the subject and cares a lot about her students. The course covers material quickly, but she does a HUGE amount of things to help us (recording lecture, posting notes, solutions, answering Piazza, etc.). She probably puts as much time outside class into the course as her students spend studying for it. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a great professor and a nice, sweet human being who cares about her students. Her lectures are good but can be fast-paced and overwhelming if you don't read ahead. I suggest printing her pre-lecture notes out and taking notes on there. Tests gradually get harder, so try to do well on the first two. Take advantage of recitations and reviews.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Pollet is the nicest professor I've ever had. She really cares about her students, and makes class fun. Work on the homeworks with other people and review the recommended readings before the test. If you're struggling, go to recitation or her review times. It's not hard to do well
She is awesome. Very understanding. Moves really fast and her tests can be difficult, but I give her a thumbs up.

Cares about her students and tries to make class fun. She does move very quickly but she suggests reading the textbook before class (which I never did). Exams are easy since they are identical to practice tests which are posted online, along with worksheet solutions. She's ready to answer your questions after class. She's a bit disorganized.
Hard class. Decent professor. Somewhat confusing and lectures fast. ALWAYS go to recitation and do all the homework. First two tests are exactly like her practice tests.

Dr. Pollet is a solid choice for organic chemistry.  Definitely an above average teacher.  At least for survey the class moves very quickly but the tests are fair and the grading policy is clear.  I would highly suggest going to lecture because she often has useful tips for exams in there.  Highly recommend her classes.

Dr. Pollet is charming but ruthless. She moves through an insane amount of material. She's an engaging lecturer but routinely goes so fast that I get lost and take away nothing from the time in class. She's very accessible outside of class, and pretty helpful. You'll like her, but you'll end up hating life because the scope of the class is absurd.

Dr. Pollet is awesome! The class can be tough but she is always willing to help. She has a French accent but is fairly easy to understand after the 1st lecture or 2. She makes her lectures interesting, but she goes through the material pretty fast. Definitely work the practice problems. Her grading policy is generous.

Very good professor; definitely recommend. Clear expectations for the course; genuinely cares about your learning. Hilarious while teaching and definitely passionate about the subject. Get to drop lowest test and final exemption policy so always a plus.

her lectures are the key to success, especially the problems she does in class. study carefully, and be sure to ask her for help during office hours. sometimes it may be hard to understand her during lecture, but it gets easier with time.
Great professor - I loved this class!  I found her lectures very interesting, and she is very helpful.
Pollet is seriously one of the best teachers I've had. She engages the class and is really easy to talk to.

Pamela Pollet is AWESOME! I loved taking her class. I was a biochem major at the time I took her Orgo 1 class. I since decided to change my major, but I'm getting a minor in Chemistry, just because I get to have her for Orgo 1. She offers several help sessions, a recitationwk, and there is a way to exempt the final by getting 90 on all tests!!

Lectures aren't the most exciting but cover everything on the tests. Helpful but infrequent office hours. Generous class policies/extra credit and the tests are reasonable but not easy by any means. Can be hard to follow the lectures because they move so fast and cover so many topics, but that's just combo for you. Would recommend her in general.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Weekly quizzes are time-consuming to prep for but not bad if you review lecture notes. The textbook isn't bad for this course but I mainly prepped for assessments using her lecture notes. For her exams, the best way to study for them is to go through the practice questions released before each exam (problems mimic those practice questions).

Theres no extra credit on quizzes, only 20-30 points on tests (but its usually EXTREMELY hard to earn even one of these). Quizzes are weekly and difficult, and theres only two tests and a final besides that. She does give other extra credit opportunities that I would recommend taking advantage of. Its a hard class but I heard she's the easiest.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The professor's grading structure has changed from previous years; there is no EC on quizzes and only a little on exams. The content and lectures are mind-numbingly boring. Homework is not graded so the exams are weighted heavily. I went to her office hours twice, once she was late the other time she did not show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She gives a HUGE amount of extra credit that it's almost impossible not to make an A. She is a great lecturer and explains concepts clearly, and she's very good at explaining what you're expected to know for exams/quizzes. She gives 20 pts extra credit on quizzes and 100 pts (yes, 100 pts) extra credit on tests. You can exempt the final (95+ avg)
Gives a lot of extra credit. Very good lecturer, clearly communicates what it will take to get an A.
Quiz every week so be prepared and ask questions often. Not the easiest MSE2001 class, but I learned a decent bit, just make sure you know the material in-depth and do the optional hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I was going to write an indepth review but each semester there are at least 100 students in each MSE class. There are only ~23 reviews here that span over a few years. If you rely on rate my prof to chose classes, but are too lazy to help out future students and write your own review. Im not going to bother either. F U guys

Dr. Qin is SO caring and gives great lectures. However, she's a very tough grader, and oftentimes expectations for assignments weren't super clear because of that. The expectations are high and can be tough to meet. Overall, I learned a lot from her lectures and assignments but this class will be more effort than you expect if you are an undergrad.

Dr. Qin is truly a caring teacher! Her lectures always cover lots of material, but the textbook is also very useful. Tests and quizzes are exactly as previous resources she provides so pay attention to her words and past resources. She is funny and very attentive to the success of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Holy hell what kind of grading rubric do you smoke Dr.Qin??? I can write an entire page on the structure of Amorphous Glass and you simply skim it for like 2 key words and grade me on this??? Takes off points for not simplifying fractions or square roots. Seriously change that damn rubric and maybe assign a textbook written in the 21st century?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her exams are like this: you are given a question with ten unknowns and asked to solve for five, but you are not told which five. And even if you get the other five unknowns correct, your answer is still wrong. People literally word vomit on the exams to hope something is correct. She's nice, but horrible grader. Would never take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The lectures in this class had a lot of vocabulary usage, making the lecture concepts hard to grasp at times. However, the homework and quizzes were very useful in preparation for the tests. Dr. Qin had very good review days and office hours before exams and was very caring. After the first exam, this class was very enjoyable.

Dr. Qin is a great lecturer, but the rubrics for her tests can be extremely specific with word choice sometimes. There are weekly quizzes, but they are open note and internet, so as long as you go to lecture, most of the questions aren't too bad. The class isn't easy, but it is usually fair. She usually hints pretty heavily about exam questions.

Dr. Qin is a fantastic professor but her greatest strength is her lecturing. Despite the 75 minute run time of her lectures I never felt like my time was wasted by being there. She can be a tough grader but her tendency to stick to the rubric makes that hard to criticize. Her tests are not easy but they are fair you just need put in the effort.

She is a nice lady but she grades way too harsh for how difficult the class should be. Never clear on what exactly she wants in answers and then takes lots of points off for not mentioning specific 'buzzwords'. Accent is kind of hard to understand at times. Only plus is her tests are pretty similar to old exams so make sure to study those.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: No quiz, easy take-home exam, the lecture is a bit boring, but I do learn some foundamental knowledge of Nano.
Never clear over what she wants for answers, overly strict on grading system given the amount she actually teaches. Great person but way too harsh for a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There are quizzes every week, so make sure you're in class on those days. Her tests are EXACTLY like her practice tests so if you memorize those and past quiz information, you should be all set for tests. However, she is a super hard grader so if you miss even the smallest detail it's possible you only get half-credit for the question. Super nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Qin is great. Her lecture is the sum-up of the textbook, and you don't need to read the entire textbook. Some lectures are confusing, just go to her office hour. Her tests are fair, and easy if you do the homework, and old tests. She is very caring, don't hesitate to ask her any confusing concepts

She's a sweet lady, but really bad for grading. I feel like all the tests were rote memorization, and if you even skipped a step, or had them backwards, you'd miss the rest of the problem. She emphasizes a point by writing it on the board and banging on the whiteboard with her index finger;it drives me nuts. Tests count a lot. Quizzes every week.

Dr Qin is the most caring professor I had! Super accessible and has many extra practice opportunities during office hours to help learn the material. Her lectures are good but can be confusing at times. Weekly quizzes and no graded HW are a pain, but if you keep up with the textbook it's not horrible. Really strict grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As person, I liked Dr. Qin. She loves talking to students and having them show up to office hours. However, her lectures can be confusing and she doesnt explain concepts well. The quizzes are alright, and exams are pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Her lectures aren't super helpful, but its a fair class. All exams are very similar to past exams. If you put in the grade an A is very very doable. Weekly quizzes to keep you on top of material.

Best there is in MSE2001. Her lectures are sometimes hard to follow, but she posts all notes and practice quizzes/exams. There are weekly quizzes (drop 2 out of 11) but they are a blessing in disguise. She is the best balance of easy A or B and actually learning something. She is down to earth and understands students may not prioritize her class.

Qin is great, nice, & helpful. KEY TO AN A: During her lectures and office hours, if you listen to her, you'll hear tons of hints as to what will be on the test and by the time it shows up, you'll basically know what exactly is on it. The tests and quizes are also basically the exact same every semester so just study them & you'll do great.

Nice teacher, very accesible. Her lectures are extremely fast paced. Her tests went from very hard to exactly like the practice ones.. from what Ive heard though her tests are hard compared to the usual multiple choice for this class. Shes also quite picky with grading.

Dr. Qin puts in a lot of effort to be accessible and helpful for students. She cares that students learn the material and tries to keep interest high in the content. Tests are relatively straightforward if you read the textbook and lecture notes, but grading is very strict which can make getting high grades difficult.
Really nice and accessible professor. Her quizzes and test are not hard --- if you go to class and pay attention. Be very detailed in your answers tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Qin is very enthusiastic about MSE and explained the material in a very understandable way. Her PowerPoint slides used lots of pictures and diagrams, which was helpful. She is always willing to help and cares about her students. If you attend class regularly and read over her notes you can make an A. She gives quizzes to encourage attendance.

Tests are basically past quizzes and homework. She answers emails extremely fast and is very helpful in office hours. Easy A if you put in a tiny bit of effort. Lecture notes are enough to get an A easily.

He really cares about his students and is very passionate about teaching. After a rough exam 1, he was very generous and gave a bunch of extra credit. He asked how he can better prepare us for the next exam, and answered students' requests by putting practice problem sets in Canvas that accurately reflected future exams.

It's his first year teaching an American class. A lot of the current reviews were written just after Exam 1. He saw we struggled on Exam 1, sent us a very heartfelt apology, made the hard questions extra credit, and made our second exam more in line with other sections. He's not an amazing lecturer, but he's a very nice guy who clearly cares a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tests are far more difficult compared to the other sections both this year and in previous years. Exams include content outside of the curriculum and content that he said would not be on the exam. His lectures are a bit monotone, and he gives homework during academic breaks. Overall nice guy but would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super nice person and professor. He very passionate about what he teaches and you can tell. However, if all differential classes were theory heavy I wouldn't have a problem, but comparing test to different sections it's kind of ridiculous. If you like theory take it with him, if you want an easier A just take it with someone else.

Professor Ried is a great professor. The lectures and tests are theory focused, yet he cares about what he teaches. He wants his students to succeed. When he gave a hard exam, he clarified he did not intend any harm, and gave a great curve for the whole class. He is very caring and is energetic during lectures every day.

I am pretty sure this is his first class, so he didn't really have a great grasp of what type of exam to give. He sounds like a nice guy in class, but the first exam was diabolical. There are a lot of improvements he can and should make as a professor overall, but outside of that exam, I cant really hate him. Pray in his next class he improves.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I will say this. Professor Reid is a very kind and caring man, and he genuinely does seem like he wants success for his class. I emailed him to speak a bit louder and a tiny bit slower during lectures, and the very next day he made the improvement. That said, he operates using the European style of teaching, which can be rough if you're like me.
solid prof, made the class engaging and easy
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Made a really hard topic very digestible to someone who has never seen any of the class material before. Tests were just as difficult if not easier than the homework problems, which made the class much less stressful. Would definitely take one of his classes again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was very kind to students, lectures are well organized and very clear. He uses great examples and lectures are very interactive. HW are not very hard and they help you undertsnad the topcis better,

Amazing professor, but he's not for everyone. His grading is tough but he clearly cares about your learning. He gives a lot of extra credit & will sometimes post lecture recordings, but don't skip class. There are a few group HWs & several long individual HWs.

Dr. Zaidi was fantastic for my introduction into AE. His lectures, although not often, were plentiful in information and engaging. The rubrics were super clear, a full calendar of assignments was given, and grading was extremely easy. There should be no reason you do not end with an A. Great class.

The two major projects just throw you in the deep end with little knowledge on how to do them but just ask someone at the makerspace and they'll tell you know to do it. Just do all assignments and it's an easy A, just more work than necessary for the 2 major projects. He also very clearly loves his job.
Very nice and caring professor. Since it's AE1601 the workload wasn't that bad, but as a professor you can tell he cares for each of his students. Definitely someone I want for future classes.

its AE1601, prof doesn't matter cuz its an easy A class. Just turn in work. Can't say much about Zaidi cuz I skipped basically every class but not too bad of a teacher. Turn in your work, understanding of problems, especially cuz the TA was so involved w my class. Make friends with AMS though, helps for projects.

Had this prof for 1601 and he was a great lecturer who put in effort to have engagement from the entire class despite the class size. He set up group projects and to give students a taste of what a career in AE would look like with some pretty fun group projects. Just dont procastinate!

Had him for 1601 and he's got to be one of the best lecturers on campus. Very passionate and constantly tries to improve the class for students. He's lectures are valuable and he expects you to attend all lectures so you are getting your worth. Took him over the summer; 3 hr long lectures and you have to work every single day on thermo to succeed.

Goated lecturer. Take if you really want to learn the fundamentals of thermodynamics and fluid dynamics. It's insane that the course combines both, but he really makes an effort convey information properly without diluting the material. That said, the class is tough but manageable if you make the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Personally I really enjoyed attending Zaidi's Thermo lectures despite the difficulty of the class. More than difficult, the class just has so much content that is thrown at us in such long classes. There are readings before each class but they are not necessary to succeed at all. Just do the homework early and understand the problems.

Exam 1 & 2 (each): 13.3%; Quizzes (3): 13.3%; Individual HW: 20%; Group HW: 10%; Final: 23.3%; Attendance: 6.6%. Thermo is tough. However Zaidi makes it feel "achievable". He truly cares about understanding the material and it shows with his personality in an 8 a.m. lecture. Quizzes and Tests were tough but clear. Would take him 100% again!!

Thermo is a tough class, but Zaidi is a really good lecturer and clearly cares about his students doing well and learning the material. His attendance policy is pretty strict and homeworks can be a little tricky sometimes, but exams are fair and only cover the material we learned in class.

He is really good at explaining the subject in a way that is easy to follow and he makes his lectures engaging. That is why he makes attendance mandatory, and bc he tells you in his lectures stuff that might be "seen later," and it is literally the answer to a test question he will ask you. HW isn't unreasonable, usually good test prep. he's goated

AE1601 is a very easy class no matter who you have, but Zaidi was not the best. He overexplained a lot of material that we didn't really need to go over. In addition, he would say "um" every 5 seconds. But nonetheless, AE1601 is a very chill class with fun projects. Zaidi will help you with questions but it might be overdone.

You need to show how you cancel your units, follow a pointless homework format, be not even a second late to class, etc. This is not an easy class in terms of content already, and Zaidi and his TA are working together very hard to deduct points from your HW, quizzes, and tests for the most trivial reasons you can imagine
Horrendous professor. Inhumane amounts of work and terribly difficult tests. Not worth taking.

Dr. Zaidi makes you swipe your buzzcards at 8:25 AM for attendance, so beware if you're even 30 seconds late. It feels like most AE profs (Zaidi included) have no idea how to actually teach a class, even if they are "experts" in the material. Lastly, I'll just leave it at this: title IX should've been pulled on this guy a long time ago.

Very strict on attendance (don't even be late). His lectures are some of the best in AE and he is very thorough on teaching the subject. The exams are very difficult but you just need to make sure you practice a lot and understand the vocabulary and concepts.
Good lecturer, awful professor. Inhumane amounts of work coupled with impossible tests and an incredibly tough grading scheme. Take someone else for your sake.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely do NOT take Dr. Zaidi. A truly awful grader with no sympathy for his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely hard, unforgiving professor. A good lecturer, but that's about it. Tests are incredibly difficult and NO partial credit is given for incorrect answers, despite tests being worth 63% of the grade. 27% of the grade are extremely difficult homework assignments as well. There is no curve nor extra credit. Avoid taking him at all costs.

He's an amazing professor who loves what he is teaching. There is a lot of content and he does well in making sure he goes over all of it. A lot of reading is needed especially since the class should be 5-6 credit hours instead of 4 credit hours (Zaidid even said this).

No partial credit given with no curve. Extremely time intensive and an overall unhealthy course taught by an extremely strict, difficult professor. Solid lectures. Not worth the pain you will endure, however

Insanely strict attendance policy. Ridiculously hard exams and extremely long homework. He's a good lecturer, but you will not have a great experience with him. Absolutely no partial credit is given on exams, and you are expected to digest an unbelievable amount of content with no room for error. Do NOT take him if you want a good experience.

An inhumanely strict, extremely difficult professor. A great lecturer, but not much else to say about his class other than the fact that he makes it as difficult and unforgiving as possible. No curve whatsoever and disgustingly difficult tests make sure there is no room for error whatsoever. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Zaidi clearly cares about his class and his students' learning. His attendance policy is draconian and is very inflexible if you are sick or have extenuating circumstances. Despite this, he is one of the best lecturers I have had at this school and I feel like I learned a lot. Genuinely would take him again, even if it increased my stress greatly.

Dr. Zaidi is a great professor and lecturer. This class, however, is extremely difficult, albeit much more bearable than his thermodynamics course. HWs are hard, and tests are harder. Despite this, I'd suggest taking Zaidi for this course. You will learn a lot and he is a very friendly and proactive professor.

Professor Zaidi is a fantastic professor and lecturer. However, note that his class is HARD. His tests are ridiculously difficult and his HWs are exceptionally tedious. If you take his AE2220 course simultaneously, you will have exams on the same day, including the final exam. He is great, but if you want an A, this might not be the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I had him for Thermo and Dynamics in the same semester and it was the hardest thing I've ever done so far. However, he's a great lecturer and although the classes are hard, he tries his very best to be a good professor. The start will be hard, but it will get better as it goes. Do a BUNCH of practice problems and if you do you should be okay.

You will do well if you put in effort. Attendance was required, but he made sure it was interesting. He's funny and really caring. One of the best professor's I've had. Will memorize every student's name and genuinely cares about your aspirations and interests. Some assignments were a little nitpicked (TA grading) but he helps with any questions

AE 1601 gave surprisingly a lot of work for being a 1 credit hour class. However, this wasn't a bad class in the slightest. Zaidi gives you all the tools you need to make it work, and it's up to you to innovate your own solutions for the projects. He's also really caring and considerate with the submissions, so just turn things in on time. :)
Zaidi is a good prof and knows what he is talking about. For 1601 just beware that assignments are nitpicked for seemingly no reason, but you will still get an A as long as you do all the work.

Probably the best professor to take for 1601, he knows what he's talking about and can easily find the solutions that are bugging you during your projects (A model rocket and a glider). Fun guy to talk to, and makes an effort to connect to every student. Fell asleep in class often (not his fault), and still managed to do pretty well.

if you go to class and put in the effort you WILL do well. i am not even one to normally go to class but it is required but he makes it worth your time. class is very fair, lectures are interesting, he is funny, and he cares a lot about his students. he memorizes every students name. best professor i ever had.

I had this professor for three classes, AE 1601, AE 2010, and now AE 2220, and I spent a lot of time in office hours. This professor is one of the best in the AE department; however, the content he teaches is difficult. Get this teacher; most people get an A or B. He has the most TA help. Pro-tip, go to recitation, or at least review the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great choice for a professor for a class that will be difficult no matter who teaches it. He sets out very clear expectations about homework and attendance, and as strict as they may be, they really do help you focus on the class. Alternates between group and individual homework, and gives extra credit if you turn it in early. Tough, but great.

Dr Zaidi is an amazing professor if you follow his class guidelines; he has lots of rules to make sure everyone succeeds. Lectures are very dense, so zoning out in class can cost you a lot. He frequently goes over past material though. He clearly cares a lot about his students and doing well in his class might be more accessible than you think.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Zaidi is an amazingly good professor and will make time for you if you ask in advance, even not during office hours. He goes somewhat fast, which can get really annoying at times, but recitation definitely helps with that.
Lots of work but he teaches the class very well and the exams are very reasonable. One of the best lecturers I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Zaidi is by far my favorite professor taken at Tech. He is amazing I have taken AE-1601 and AE-2220 with him and he is amazing. Be prepared to work hard but as A.E.'s this major isn't easy so just give it a good solid effort and you will do just fine. I wish he did higher level courses because I would take his classes in a heartbeat.

Best professor I had this semester. Zaidi is very good at getting straight to the point while also providing great explanations. He gives a very good introduction to the aerospace field, so I would definitely recommend taking this class in you first year if possible. He is very good at responding to discussion posts and will help if you just ask.

Zaidi is a very capable instructor. He moves quickly through material, but answers questions well. His lectures focus heavily on derivations and leave the problem solving to the homework sets, so be wary of that. Class is mandatory for participation points, and I encourage going regardless because lectures help set up the foundations for problems.

Dr. Zaidi's classes run like well-oiled machines. Lectures are very to-the-point while still giving enough background information for the derivations to make sense. Homeworks are short, but extra practice problems are provided for exam preparation. The exams weren't exactly easy, but if you adequately prepare for them you'll be fine.

Dr. Zaidi is one of my favorite professors I have had. Granted AE 1601 is meant to be an introductory class, but he made it very enjoyable. You could tell he was passionate about his work and cared about all the students. Almost everyone in the class got an A as long as they did the work.

Prof. Zaidi is awesome. Lectures were super interesting. Clearly goes over all of the material (although sometimes quickly). If you go to class awake and prepared to learn, you'll do well. If you don't stay engaged then it gets difficult. Study homeworks and go to recitation. Dedicate time to the class and you'll do fine.

He makes sure to give as many resources to students as he can in order for them to succeed. So many office hours available; if you ask questions he will answer and try to really help you understand. He's very passionate about making sure his students learn.

Dr. Zaidi is a very nice professor. On the other hand, his tests were not particularly, and there was a lack of consistency in them. Difficulty varied widely, and the final was substantially different than the previous exams.

The material in this class is a lot, but Zaidi sets clear expectations of how to do well. His lectures are incredibly thorough and interactive. Tests are tough but fair. Taking this class made me know the material by heart which will be incredibly useful for future classes. Zaidi cares a lot about his students' success, highly recommend. fav prof
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This course is just as hard to take as it is to teach. Despite this, Dr. Zaidi was amazing, not to mention incredibly professional.  If you follow the workflow as needed and are patient you will get an A in the class.  Zaidi's approach to teaching inspired me to want to do well, and you feel good when you can manhandle this behemoth of a course.
Just plain bad. If I could sum up my experience with him it would be just as well as Geoff Collins tenure. Never take him

Professor Zaidi clearly knew how to teach the class and taught it amazingly. The only gripes I have about this class is that it was at 8:25 am and was a two hour lecture. Neither of these aspects are in Zaidi's control so make sure your class is not at this time.

Had him for AE1601 Fall 2021. He is the fastest talker on the planet. If you focus, though, you will realize that everything he says has a purpose and thought behind it. He is a good professor because he will teach you exactly what you are supposed to learn. Semester was front-heavy with work, but relaxed at the end. He knows what he's saying.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Interesting class

The lectures are way too specific for an overview class and are meaningless to the work you'll do. Assignments are easy but graded extremely poorly and don't reflect the work you put in. Still, it's not a difficult class, you just have to be picky about the rubric.

Really cool professor, cares a lot. Go to class! He covers a lot of material in lecture and usually goes over homework as well. Class was pretty easy, fun and informative but be warned: I found that the workload was a little bit inconsistent. Some weeks, by no exaggeration, had less than 5 minutes of homework. Others were way worse.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Zaidi is very accessible outside of class, and he clearly enjoys teaching the subject. At certain points, he did go too fast, but this class is introductory so understanding the concepts is the most important, which he teaches well. If you take this class, I'd recommend not focusing heavily on taking notes, and more on listening fully.

Prof. Zaidi cares a lot for his students and gives really good lectures. Lots of homework and quizzes that are fair content-wise but can be graded harshly. He tried to make the most of the pandemic situation and offered multiple extra credit opportunities. Did seem to get frustrated at times with students requesting accommodations.

Dr. Zaidi made the most out of an online format due to Covid-19. His lectures are incredibly clear and helpful, and he is very passionate about the course. Cares a lot for his students and helps you if you email him questions. Lots of homework and assessments that are tough but fair. Definitely requires a lot of work and time.

I liked the content, even though there were a ton of lectures. But maybe Dr. Zaidi isn't cut out for virtual because most of us struggled in the class, and he almost never listed to our worries or accommodated our concerns. Because of this, this class was very draining and depressing even though it could have been fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took him because he had good ratings and I'd heard great things from friends. I don't know if it was COVID, virtual, or what, but mine (and most of my classmates' experience) was not the same this year. Interesting lectures and I ended with an A (due to a huge curve), but the extreme stress, unfair quizzes, and brutal grading wasn't worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He gives a lot of hard homework and the assessments are tough and fair. He is very strict but is very passionate about the material he teaches and ensures that his students learn a lot.

One of my favorite professors I've had at Tech (taken at GTL). Homework is tough, exams are tough but fair. Zaidi will do whatever it takes to ensure you understand the material and internalize it. He cares about student success and it shows. Be prepared to work in Zaidi's class, but you'll definitely learn a lot. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great at actual teaching, tests and quizzes are usually very fair but the grading on all assignments is very unforgiving. Kinda hard to find outside of class, and you will need to find him outside of class. Will deduct points and give you a lecture about your work ethic if you're ever late. Crib sheets allowed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Zaidi is a very knowledgeable professor who genuinely wants students to learn the material and not just memorize it. With that being said he gives a lot of difficult homework, but tests and quizzes aren't as hard. He's sometimes a little hard to get in touch with. Overall great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Zaidi was someone who could really pique interest in the subject. Despite it being condensed into a three month course at GTL, he paced the course amazingly well and I kept showing up to class expecting something new every time. All in all, I would highly recommend you take him if you're really interested in AE, because he sure is.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Zaidi really tries to improve his student's learning process. Because of this he expects people to read the book before class and to attend most/all lectures. No late work accepted. Also, he will call on students at random in class and expects people to have read. His exams were pretty straight forward but he won't give practice exam materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Decent at actual teaching; however, the class is filled with too many arbitrary rules. Grading for homework and tests is done harshly, although tests are fair. Homeworks are very lengthy and demanding. His class policies are uncompromising and he is unwilling to accommodate special circumstances. Do not take if you plan on traveling at GTL.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Zaidi is an incredible professor. I went to his lectures not because it was mandatory but because it was worth the time. His explanation added to the textbook in a very helpful manner. That said, keep up with the readings. Homework is hard but he is available to help and the tests are easier than the homework so just put in the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took 2250 with her, very easy so I took 2255 asynchronous over the summer. Similar difficulty to 2050, not bad. Just learn how to do the homework and memorize the excel formulas before exams and you will do well. Dr Rudchenko is so sweet and truly cares about her students. Loves talking about AI for some reason. Take her over any other prof!
Tests were easy very similar to practice tests. There was a bit of busy work. Group project was alright she does assign groups. Overall, chill professor

Dr. Rudchenko was very passionate about the material, and she always sought to keep the class engaged. She made the lecture slides and videos easily accessible, so if we had to miss class for some reason we could still complete the excel assignment outside of class and get full credit for that day. Exams are easy if u do the hw and practice tests

Class is more work than needed. Tests are on MyLab (Pearson) and are relatively similar to practice tests and previous HW questions, so I'd recommend using those to study. If you go to class, do the HW assignments, and make a good cheat sheet based on everything in the HW, practice tests, you'll probably end with an A. Still a lot of work though.

super confusing canvas to navigate. hard to understand prof in her emails but overall very easy class. just annoying constant busywork. i would just do everything ahead of time so u dont have to submit participation every other day.

Canvas page is the most chaotic thing I've seen in my whole life... often hard to navigate. Spams emails and announcements and there's a TON of busy work with this class. Her exams are similar to practice tests- second exam was noticeably the most difficult but that could have just been me. Still pretty doable to get an A.

Love Tatiana! Easy class, but lots of busy work. There's so many assignments and parts that make up your grade that even if you miss a few, your grade is still fine. There's a participation assignment every class, but she posts videos on Canvas on what to do. 3 tests (super easy, basically same as practice test, & lowest replaced w avg of 3),.

She is a very sweet professor and the class is very easy. A lot of people complain about the amount of work but each assignment takes between 5-30 minutes so it's really not that bad. If you do the practice tests and the homework all of the tests will be really easy. Overall, not the most engaging class but it is really easy to get a good grade.

She is so sweet and a good professor, but the amount of work was ridiculous. I took the online course and things were constantly due. And it wasn't super clear what to turn in sometimes. Her forcing us to submit the excel Mon/Wed/Fri did force me to learn it though. The short essays and 5 page essay at the end were very unnecessary though.

Literally the easiest class ever. Got a 100 on every exam and homework. The AI project is extremely silly, but you get so much time to do it and it doesn't take long. A LOT of weekly homework but it's easy. She is hard to understand and a little crazy, but worth it for how easy the class is.

Easiest class of my life, but it was so filler class. Didn't really learn all that much from this class, it's like if AP stat was way more lax and some excel. The AI project she did was kinda dumb and pointless (she is so obsessed with AI it's kinda crazy, but at least you get a free Chat subscription from it), but project was easy.
It is very hard to understand her so all of your learning will mostly be on your own. Also much of the work has very little meaning so its a lot of time doing busy work

The class was very easy, but by the end its so frustrating and feels so pointless. She's very hard to understand and I feel like I learned nothing from the class. I would rather take a class from a slightly more difficult teacher to actually learn something. There is way too much busy work and homework as well.

Can't understand her accent at all. The material is easy but too much busy work. This class could be simple, but it is drawn out and as tedious as possible. The grading is not too tough. Forgot half of my assignment but she didn't take off credit. She isn't tech savvy either and felt her lectures were useless.
Insane amount of work.

shes so awesome and super funny and makes class fun, lots of homework but it all ends up being the kind of stuff on the test so in the end its helpful. exams are just like the study guide. excel heavy but pretty straightfoward. would totallllly take again
She is extremely friendly and a very kind soul.

This class is on easy material with the most work possible. Prof is really nice but she assigns so much busy work. This class could be so easy and simple, but it is drawn out and as tedious as possible. The grading is not too tough. There are lots of extra credit opportunities and dropped assignments. Overall, her class is annoying but not awful.

Take her!! Dr. Rudchenko is the sweetest and wants her students to succeed. The class is one of the easiest classes I have taken at Scheller and she makes it as stress-free as possible. There is homework but the exams are very similar to homework questions.

I did not enjoy this class at all; it was a headache. There was lots of work and assignments constantly due (some I didn't feel were necessary). They weren't difficult, but annoying. She was extremely unclear with the project guidelines. Focus on practice exams and homework to study for exams as they are similar problems to the exam.

Tatiana is a nice professor; she is caring and gives many resources for students to catch up. We have a lot of online videos to make sure we get the concept right. One thing I may add, though, is that we had Friday HW and that can be a bummer at times because its an added on assignment day submission. Do practice tests, pretty similar to tests!

There was a lot of busy work for the class, but it was nothing difficult. After the in-class, Friday asynchronous assignments, and the practice test, the exams were a breeze. All exams were on Pearson and were similar to the practice test. Rudchenko is funny, and the accent wasn't too harsh...was used to it within a week. Take her for the A.
Lots of busy work, everything is due at 10 PM but the class is extremely easy. Practice exam is literally just the exam with different numbers inputted. Professor Rudchenko is very sweet.

Class material itself is easy to comprehend especially if you have taken AP Stat in high school. There is  a lot of busy work in the class but nothing unbearable. Highly recommend doing the HWs and practice exams to be successful in this class. Overall an easy A

Honestly, she's a great professor. There is a lot of busy work, yes, but it kind of works well because if there is something you didn't understand in class you have plenty of work to figure it out. She also offered students to attend class via zoom halfway through the semester which was nice. She can be hard to understand at times but she is funny.

Dr. Rudchenko is definitely the best pick for MGT 2250 and MGT 2255! She is pretty hilarious and cares about the success of students in the class. But note that there are A LOT of assignments that you need to complete and just generally a lot of busy work. The material is not too hard as she provides detailed study guides and practice. TAKE HER!
she's hard to understand and there is SO much busywork outside of class. never learns anything in class and she doesn't even know her own excel sheets

i (& many of my peers) were baited by the positive rmp reviews for this prof, but im here to say - DO NOT TAKE. she's hard to understand and gives SO many assignments it's insane. material isn't even hard but there's sm to keep track of. i get 10+ email notifs a day from the class canvas. obsessed w chatgpt and schedules random assignments.

She is very enthusiastic, but isn't always coherent and keeps having issues with her own Excel sheets. Also weirdly obsessed with using ChatGPT for things it can't do very well (I think Tech is pushing it overall though). Exams are very easy but there's no partial credit, lost 20% due to a dumb math error that affected a multi-part question.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is a lot of easy busywork. Exams were exactly like practice tests that were also required for a grade. 3+ assignments a week, including an asynchronous friday class and many poorly made videos. Several times the class detours into hyping ChatGPT rather than the relevant content. Ruchenko is nice but hard to understand and out of touch.

The rater saying there are classes on Friday probably misunderstood the syllabus. To be fair, it does say asynchronous classes. But that just means you have homework. I'm currently taking this class and it is very easy. Exam question are taken from the practice test and homework. Be warned, there's a lot of homework, most due at 12:10 PM or 10 PM.

taking her for mgt 2255. she assigns so many assignments that it's insane. she doesn't always understand how her own excel sheets work. she assigns so many useless tasks that literally serve us no purpose. sometimes hard to understand with her accent, but that's not the main issue.

THERE IS CLASS ON FRIDAYS. It isn't shown on registrar, it's online. I just started taking the class so I have no real rating other than the fact that she likes CHAT-GPT and has a heavy accent. I can't believe this isn't on the registrar, this is ridiculous. Is this even allowed?

Easy A, but insanely annoying class. So much work outside of lecture mostly because she wastes so much time either rambling about chat-GPT or trying to figure out how her own excel sheets work, which she should know as its the only thing taught in the course. Not to mention the extra online lecture on Friday that isn't shown in registration.

You DO NOT need to read the textbook to do well. I was reading it the first two weeks, being a nerd, but it doesn't help you at all. I find her tough to understand vocally at times because of her accent, but the in-class WS's, HW's, and practice tests are all you need to know, going into test 3 with a 100% just from that.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class was pretty easy and straightforward. The tests were very similar to the practice tests. While there was a lot of assignments and homework to submit, everything was straightforward to complete. You could even miss up to 6 classes without points being taken off. I would not take any other professor for this class.

Dr. R is so beyond awesome. She sets everything up for you to do well, and it is basically a guaranteed A. She even streams her classes on Zoom so you can attend virtually if you need to, but is also super forgiving with attendance (you can miss up to 6 in-person classwork assignments with no punishment). Would take her again any day!

This class is set up for you to do well. We primarily use excel and the formula sheets for tests give step by step directions. They are very forgiving with late work (never took off points). Dr. Rudchenko is the sweetest so I definitely recommend. I learned a lot and the class felt very low pressure.

light work class. helpful material that was taught for outside the classroom. Really improve your excel grade. Amazing teacher who gives you opportunities to get an A. Practice Test = tests essentially.

The hardest thing about this class is remembering to submit all of the assignments, but otherwise this is a very straightforward and simple class. Knowing how to do all of the homework problems is essential for the exams, but you are allowed a crib sheet for every exam. Rudchenko is very lively and energetic, so lectures are generally pretty fun.

I LOVE Dr. Rudchenko! She is so caring and absolutely hilarious. She loves what she does. Her grading criteria is extremely lenient and very clear. It is easy to succeed in this class if you do all of your assignments. I would recommend not missing class because a lot can be covered in one class, but I found the material very enjoyable and cool.

I LOVED PROFESSOR RUDCHENKO! She is the sweetest professor I have encountered at Georgia Tech and only wishes the best among her students! I scored low on my second exam and she motivated that I could still get an A and not give up! I ended with an A and highly recommend this professor for MGT 2250!

I went into this class hearing all the positive reviews and was surprised at the experience I had- very heavy with busy work. Constant homework/busy work and the Canvas is pretty disorganized. She is a sweet lady and means well and is very accessible, but I don't relate to the experience everyone else had. A little hard to understand

Rudchenko makes this class very easy! She practically shows you what to do and guides you the entire way. Her exams mimic the practice tests and classwork/homework she gives, so it's nothing out of the blue. We do have textbook pages, but you don't necessarily need to read them, as it's a very hands-on class.
Really easy class! Take her!

Was 1/2 in person 1/2 async when I took it, very clear expectations. Just attend the lectures, do HW on time and study your classwork for tests and you should be good to go. Very hard not to get an A.
This professor was very enthusiastic about what she was teaching. The homework and tests were fairly easy. If you keep up with all the assignments, you will do very well in the class.

TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!  "mandatory" classes but she posts everything online and does not take attendance. Tests and homework are easy if you pay attention in class. She is great at explaining what to do and gives more than enough material for you to succeed. Gives practice tests that are almost identical to the real tests. Ended with a 99.99%
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the most entertaining classes I've taken at tech. She's a little bit disorganized with her lectures but with a little extra effort, I learned a lot. She makes her expectations very clear and is a whole lot of fun to interact with.

Rudchenko is an amazing teacher, one of my favorite so far at Tech. I was awful at statistics in high school but excelled in this class. Homework are very helpful for the tests and she is very forgiving in grading.

She is nice and you can tell she cares about her students. The material is pretty easy too. Though her canvas is SO disorganized it's actually overwhelming. Nonstop canvas notifications that important stuff gets lost. There was a paper that was only mentioned in the syllabus.
Her class is easy, so you can get an A if you just submit your assignments on time.

She's really easy. You'll get a high A as long as you go to class and do the HW's. Practice tests are almost exactly the same as the exams, so do that before taking the exams. This class is a lot of busy work though, but if you took AP Stats in high school, it'll be a breeze. She has an accent but you get used to it by week 2. She loves to teach.
This class was extremely easy. The professor is super nice but doesn't speak English very well and isn't the best lecturer.

Mrs. Rudchenko is one of the best there is at Georgia Tech. Her classes can be confusing sometimes due to her strong accent, but she ensures that everyone is on the same page and understands what is going on. The tests and homeworks (you get multiple tries on homework) are pretty self-explanatory and easy.

An amazingly caring professor with wonderful TAs. You'll be very supported in this class. It's honestly an easy A and kind of basic, but I did learn useful excel skills. She's hilarious and makes everyone smile.

Dr. Rudchenko is always a solid choice. She's funny, kind, and helpful. Easy class if you just make sure you get the work done. Clear grading policy and relatively easy course. Had her for this and Management Stats, and I love her every time I take her.

Dr. Rudchenko is awesome! Shes super nice and willing to support you in any way. The class itself is very easy; If you use excel, you're good to go. Her accent is hard to understand at first, but you will get used to it pretty quickly. There are daily 'quizzes' which get annoying, but they aren't worth that much so you can miss several.

Dr. Rudchenko is the SWEETEST! She began every email by reminding us that we are welcome and supported in this class! All assignments are completed on MyLab. She posts example Excel documents and videos explaining how to do almost every problem!! This class is super easy to get an A in if you just put minimal effort in. 10/10!!

Professor Rudchenko has been the best professor I have had at tech so far. She is always available if you need help, and her lectures are well put together. If you do the homework, and study the practice tests, you will get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor!! Very sweet and nice. Would recommend. Also took her for MGT 2250 and it was the same level of difficultly if not less.

Spring '21 Asynchronous Professor Rudchenko is kind and sent encouraging messages throughout the entire semesters and the TAs would always leave positive messages in the homework comments. The homework has multiple attempts and she posts "study guides" for them so there's no reason to not get an A. Also the tests were open note. Practice tests ftw

(Taken during COVID-19 Fall 2020.) Absolutely loved Dr. Rudchenko. With this being an online, async class, it wasn't too difficult, and she provides a lot of resources to get the homework and exams done. Basically, if you can use Excel, you can do this class.
Tati is hilarious. Her handouts were a ton of paper (and repetitive) but very helpful to look back at. I loved the way she taught too!

Her accent is thick, but she did alot of videos that weren't her speaking. I learned everything in that class without difficulty. I really loved how it was taught and the way homeworks/tests were done. There's a practice test for every test. She was super helpful when I wasn't sure about something. LOVE HER!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easiest professor at the school probably. AND she's hilarious, super high energy and makes everything super clear. If you don't take her class you're doing yourself a disservice

She was hard to understand at first but after the first week it becomes easy to understand her. Accurately outlines what you need in order to make a good grade in her class. She's very understanding and super accessible outside of class as well.
