reviews.comment: Not a very inspiring class. Exams were pretty easy (all multiple choice) but I didn't retain much.

Dr. Nair-Reichart is a good choice. She is willing to help her students. The content for the course is manageable if you read her lectures and do the homework. Tests are quite long, but they are durable.

Great professor. She does an excellent job of explaining the material. Though she has a habit of rambling on random topics, they still help you in enhancing your understanding. Super approachable and compassionate individual. Would recommend any day.

Lectures were often more confusing than helpful, but the material and tests weren't difficult if you read the book and do the homework. Attendance is mandatory because she claims to focus on class participation. Very kind and caring person, but not a great teacher. No final exam, and the lowest test of four got dropped. Overall not a high workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Her lecture slides are posted so you don't HAVE to go to class, but she does a really good job at embellishing on the material and providing examples so it's worth your time to go anyway. Exams were tricky at times but fair, just read carefully, know your vocab, and do the practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very compassionate person, but not a great professor. All slides are posted online and she reads directly off the slides during lectures, so no point in coming to class. NOT A BLOW OFF CLASS! Exams are nothing like the lectures, homework or practice questions. Don't expect an easy A (even though it's econ).
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really didn't learn much, but it was easy I guess.

I had Dr. U as part of the Oxford Study Abroad Program, and he was great! Most of our classes were group presentations to make it more interesting than him just lecturing to us for 2 hours. Each group had 2 presentations, and they made up a big part of our grade. He tells you exactly what to expect on the tests and makes sure you're prepared.

Doc rules! He is the funniest, most understanding, most caring choir director I've ever had. We sing lots of music each semester (I counted 34 pieces one year), and a lot of it is weird and challenging, but it's so rewarding.

Doc will not learn your name, but that doesn't mean he cares less. Very funny, very... different. Definitely not like any other choral director I've ever had before. He's a little eccentric, but I've learned so much from him. Very good professor, even if you think he's insane sometimes. ( in a good way. Love u doc
Doc is awesome
Online singing can be a definite change. But, Jerry is very fun and he writes all the music(very skilled by the way). Easy A if you show up.
He is a great choir director. He is super funny and really cares about his students.
Dr. U is great! He makes sure to engage the class and makes the topic entertaining.
Hilarious, the best, especially when in Glee club because he acts like a college kid especially with his jokes.
Doc is great! He's really funny, and Glee was the best "class" I've ever had. Plus, you get graded on showing up and trying to sing. If you do that, you get an A.

I LOVE Dr. U!!! He changed my life. I had never sang before and was very nervous. He is just such a great person to be around, he really understands people in general and he loves them too. He is hilarious and the class is just a good time.

Best guy in the world!! I had never sang before, but he is so motivating! I came to this class just to have fun, Dr. U cracks jokes the whole time. He encourages an awesome sense of community. Basically, practices are twice a week and then a final performance..if you go you get an A. this teacher is one of the most loving persons I have ever met
Doc. U is an awesome instructor.    A++++++ Instructor.  Coolest dude alive.
Dr. U is the best!
I love you
Uelzmann was very invested in the content he taught! He got to know his students personally and gave individualized feedback!

I loved him and enjoyed the class. He's very nice and clearly very knowledgable and passionate about the topic. Class wasn't super difficult, just a decent amount of reading/listening. There's a few papers and a project among other things, but it's not super time-consuming.

Uelzmann is fantastic. He's really passionate about post war literature and lectures were so engaging. He does tend to get really enthusiastic, which often leads to him speaking moderately quickly in German, just be aware of that. The whole class is taught in German, but he's super nice about explaining words you might not know. Highly recommend!

German 1002 online via VHL Central pass/fail: It was an easy free elective class (if you are taking it pass fail). I did the minimum work possible to pass. VHL is nice but kinda frustrating when you miss something like a capital letter and it docks you points. Overall laid back learning environment and easy P/F class.

Absolutely wonderful man. Clearly loves teaching and is very engaging. Loves his wife and kids, and 90s German music. Has great sense of fashion, sporting tasteful Pink Floyd and black shirts, not to mention V-necks. Classy dude all in all.

The class I took, about post war German literature, was really interesting. I'm not much of a literature or reading person, so believe me when I say that this class was really fun and very interesting. Take it if you can.

Dr. Uelzmann is easily the best german teacher I have had. I had been taking german for 6 years when I started 2001. I took that to get an easy A. However, Dr. Uelzmann challenged me and turned me into a better student. He also was very sympathetic to the fact that I had mono. He really cares for his students and his class content. Take Uelzmann!

I highly recommend taking Jan when you can. Seriously, he is one of the funniest, enthusiastic and approachable teacher I have seen. He speaks mostly in German, but adds actions to make you understand what he is saying. Also as a final example, he laughs with the class about the world wars whereas all my previous teachers took offense!

I enjoy this class very much. You really have to pay attention to follow along because he makes a point to speak German to you most of the time. Homework is due nearly every class period but it never takes too terribly long.  Classes are fun, and he is extremely approachable and has a sense of humor.  All in all, a very good professor.
Grade depends primarily on exams + case projects, lectures are repetitive, exams based on textbook material not lecture material
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His class isn't super hard but his lectures are trash and he goes on tangents and doesn't grade anything so you really have no clue what you got in the class. The tests aren't on what you talk about in class. He says the textbook is optional but if you have questions he says it's in the textbook.
Currently in your class giving you a 1 star review cuz I hate you.Your always on some BS. Your voice is annoying and your jokes are always duds. At least you don't get mad when I'm on my phone.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His class is great for people that prefer to learn from the textbook. It is not good for people that rely on lectures to learn. Reading the textbook took forever but it was the best preperation to get an A in the class. There is a group project, however, if you consitently work on it all semester and follow he rubric, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Ulgado is wonderful, absolutely hilarious, and definitely great for services. His lectures are straightforward and clear. With only a little study, you'll do pretty well on all the quizzes. The biggest part of the semester is a group project, but you should be able to knock it out pretty easily. Definitely take for a breeze of a class.

Whatever you do, DO NOT take this professor for MGT 3300. Find someone else. His lectures are stuck in the 90's and the examples are super old and not useful at all. Came in with an interest in marketing, and I don't want to take any more marketing classes at Tech if they're like this. He doesn't communicate or use Canvas at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Do NOT take this class. He does not communicate grades at all and tries way too hard for what's supposed to be an easier class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Strict on projects

you learn practically nothing during lectures. His powerpoints have no words on them, so good luck using them to study Our last test average was a C with a curve and several questions thrown out because he doesn't write them himselves. Insanely hard tests that don't even go with the lectures and he grills every student after their group presentatio

Terrible professor. Not only is he the most unfunny and engaging professor in Scheller, but he grades based off of attendance so get ready to go anyway. attending lectures literally feels like throwing my time away which sucks considering its 1/6 of your grade. He is also very much against the use of tablets and laptops.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good person but terrible professor, grades are scarcely communicated (no canvas), ambiguous instructions for assignments and tests, random attendance, draining lectures, you'll find him funny b/c his lectures are so bad that any form of stimulus verbal or otherwise will impact you 100,000% more than it would normally.

Attendance is random and you don't know how many times or when hes going to take attendance in a semester. You either get an A or fail his tests (read the book), case analysis assignments are also A or a F (be specific and use key terms from book), presentations grades are unknown forever, lectures are the worst. Overall, a 0/10 experience
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: The class divides into groups to present cases throughout the semester. You have to write analyses of the cases you don't present. Your grade is made up of the analyses, the presentation, and the tests (3 including final). He tries hard, probably too hard. Funny/obnoxious. Gave a present for most improved test grade at the end. No phones/laptops.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: This man does not use Canvas at all and throughout the year it was very challenging to see what grades were coming from where and even what added up to my final score. I understand wanting assignments turned in hard copy but communication between teachers and students especially on grading should be open and frequently updated.

First off, this man is an absolute character. One of, if not the funniest professors I've had at Tech. Lectures are entertaining which is good since you can only miss 3 or 4 throughout the year. Tests are difficult for a business class but if you read the slides and ppts you're fine. Only assignments are 10 cases, 3 tests, and attendance.
Prof Ulgado is one of the worst prof I've taken at tech. His class was so unstructured and he did not teach. Be prepared to teach yourself and have no idea what grade he is going to give you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Ulgado sets very high standards for his class and treats us like we are professionals. His lectures are a bit dry, but there is lots of material to cover and he tries to make it interesting by providing examples. Tests are easy if you read the book. Do the extra credit, even if you don't need it

The professor genuinely seems like a cool guy who is very knowledgeable, but he's condescending if you don't understand advanced concepts he touts as basic. Quizzes impossible to prepare for, no matter how much you study. He teaches concepts in class + textbook is informative, but the quizzes test situational what-ifs and suck and are unfair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While his slides are clear and he communicates the material somewhat well, his quizzes and exams are obtuse and impossible to prepare for. I understand the material. This material makes sense. However, every quiz and exam is a roll of the dice.

Prof Vlad is a decent professor. First half of the class was very theory heavy. Second half was more projects and assignments. Weekly quiz and they were difficult, which would be open for the first 10 mins of class. One midterm which was worth 30% of your grade. It's not an easy class you can breeze thru.

Took blockchain section with Vlad. Fantastic dry nerd humor. The theory lectures (1st half) are hard but Vlad does a great job explaining. Has the audacity to ask the class if a quiz was easy when the median is 60. Projects, both research and programming, are fun and good additions. Not hard to get an A if you try
Teach what you don't test. Test what you don't teach. That is his motto.

God awful class. Teach yourself to code, no instruction or guidance, fill out the notebooks to perfection after 20 hours of banging your head against your keyboard, hope TA is helpful, over rely on AI cause whats even happening, take exams with unforgiving autograder, heres some math sprinkled in here and there. whole course needs to be redone
The lectures are completely unrelated to the exams and the professor clearly doesn't care about teaching or whether students actually understand the material.
By far the worst professor I've ever had.
Unnecessarily difficult course
I think professor Vuduc gave up on teaching a long time ago. Google could teach this class better. Tests do not reflect anything actually learned. Do yourself a favor and prepare for the worst

The pace of the course is quite quick. All the work is through Vocareum(similar to Jupiter), but the app has issues with connection and others. Vocareum may grade you wrong because it only recognizes commands given during class.The class is online and there's little support from instructors.The class needs a lot more instructors to help students

Super kind and caring professor. Lectures were fine but often felt random. Majority of the grade was projects. Feedback on them came very late and sparse. Grading was generous to make up for that, but there wasn't much opportunity to improve. Easy class, but I wish I had learned more.

If you enter the class with no Python or coding background, you must spend lot of time in order to get to a passing level.  This is the nature of the class and the discussed topics, the more you practice the better you will get.  Do as many practice problems as you can to prepare for test.
Awful Awful lectures and doesn't impart information well. Verbose and inconsistent in teaching style
While the lectures weren't tied to the projects that closely, Dr. Vuduc cares about his students and is very knowledgeable in the subject of simulations.

CSE 6040 is theoretically a class where you don't *need* to know python, but it definitely makes the class a whole lot easier. The class technically starts out with the basics but ramps up so quickly that it can be daunting if you're not familiar with Python from the get-go.

Not a fan of Professor Vuduc's highly informal teaching style in CSE 6040. He has a "casual" meeting/conversation style lecture sometimes with another instructor that I found very distracting and hard to understand. Would rather he taught from a book in clearer terms.

There are no lectures whatsoever. A few poor videos and that is it. You're expected to teach yourself everything. Professor only shows up at the first office hours, last office hours, and one in the middle, and he only talks about the exam. They could easily remove him from the picture and the class would be exactly the same.

The homework is entry level to intermediate coding which is great since they advertise it as no coding experience needed to succeed. The tests are expert level coding. Reading posts by other students you can see the TA's rarely answered any question, so it is all on the person to read as many articles online as it takes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took Vuduc through the online MSA program, so I'm not sure how his teaching translates to in-person lectures, but I was pleased by the course. Tests and homeworks are straightforward and not difficult. However, the lectures often aren't enough and can be a walkthrough of homework problems, so you have to understand the material on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: lots of reading and essay writing, course is structured more like a humanities course than a CS course. take robotics instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: take robotics instead if youre a cs major

Attendance is required one lecture a week as he gives quizzes based on readings (they're either through Canvas with a code or paper and pencil), and these quizzes are very specific so you have to actually read. The rest of the class is very chill (though it depends on the TA) and easy to do well in. Plus the content is actually pretty interesting!
Professor Varma cares about the students and would reach out to you regarding accommodations. Lots of readings and has weekly reflection&discussion based on course material. TA is also very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great and chill professor. Lots of reading/writing and some of it can be obscure and hard to comprehend, but many readings were super interesting! You very much get out what you put into this class. If your TA is nice it's not hard to get an A (except he has weekly quizzes that are worded so weird and are hard, and are 20% of the grade).

Class is overall pretty easy. LOTS OF READING!! I only went to class the day we would have quizzes bc his lecture style wasn't beneficial to me but I enjoyed the structure of the class. ACTUALLY READ THE READINGS because he will ask the most specific questions on weekly quizzes that you wont know unless you read it (even though they are open note)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: He really knows his material. I only participated in about half the classes (i.e. the days we had quizzes), but even then I could tell just how good of a lecturer he is. Looking back, I do regret not attending and paying attention to every single lecture, because I think I would've gotten a ton out of this class. Weekly discussion posts and papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Respected

reviews.comment: Professor Varma is undoubtedly one of the best professors at GT. When you truly immerse yourself in the subject matter, it becomes clear how brilliantly and clearly Professor Varma can explain really complex concepts. Be prepared to read extensively and think a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took CS 7651 with him (option wasn't available). 100% would recommend, he's definitely the best lecturer I've had and is super responsive to questions. As someone who originally wasn't very interested in the course content, I found myself attending class regularly.

100% recommend for those into ML. Imo varma is the kind of professor that makes you want to go to class. He's in touch with recent research trends and presents in an interesting / engaging way. Honestly, you could skip class and put no effort in and get an A, but it's the kind of class that you'll gain a lot from participating.

Professor Varma is the most engaging professor I've had at tech, and he makes the subject approachable and understandable to most. The lectures are definitely worth your time to attend, and if you can go in person he makes an honest effort to get to know his students, and appreciates feedback. Lots of papers weekly, but they're all engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: A lot of weekly work: two readings, discussion post, quiz, short reflection paper. But as long as you stay on top of everything the majority of those are graded very nicely. Prof puts a lot of effort into the lectures and actually listens to feedback from students. Readings can be a bit dense. No tests, final paper instead of final
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor is a nice person and very helpful. However, be prepared for a heavy workload—there are weekly assignments that you cannot skip. Cryptography itself is a very challenging subject, especially if your math/CS foundation isn't the strongest. It's a tough course, but you'll learn a lot if you put in the effort.

Professor Mooney designs challenging courses which will prepare you for the real workforce.
I've taken nearly every hardware security course and computer architecture course via Professor Mooney.
The content is incredibly in-depth and applicable to "real-world" and "life-after-college".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Mooney is a great person but lacks in teaching capabilities. The materials are not organized, nor is his teaching style. The slides lack in content, clarity, and so does the verbal lectures. The lectures may be recorded, but they are not very useful. Homework is assigned every week too so be prepared for that.
Prof. V is so inspiring.

Exhibits exceptional enthusiasm for the subject matter, maintains a warm and approachable demeanor, encourages active student participation, and demonstrates a high level of expertise and conceptual depth.
The quality of the projects done in the class was better than a conference.
This guy is so cool!!
He is very enthusiastic and knowledgeable on optimal control and very accessible.
This was a class on writing and reviewing robotics papers. Amazing. He also invited special guests like Mr. Klaus for a seminar.
Very enthusiastic and knowledgeable. I still use his notes for my research.
Genuinely cares about the students and their learning. I would definitely recommend taking his classes.
Dr. Vamvoudakis made this class so interesting. He is always accessible and wants us to learn.  I will definitely take another class with him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Vamvoudakis has great intentions for his students but his lecture style is jumbled, rushed, and difficult to keep up with. Regularly nobody would answer questions in class and he'd just keep going after a few minutes. Very understanding and willing to extend deadlines and work with students, but overall poor lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The lectures cover content not needed for exams, and the exams contains material not covered in lectures. Instead you must read the textbook to do well on exams, and do the textbook practice problems. Also, you won't learn any aerospace applications, only theory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I finally learned controls. Prof. V and the TAs were very helpful and my final project provided me with an opportunity to test my knowledge.
A lab class with a way to show how controls work

He could care less for student, he teaching makes no sense and you need read the book and use other sources to pass this class. Overall one of the worst profs in the AE department and makes the tests super hard without preparing students for the material. His PhD student taught better than him! Hope they change the instructor for this tough course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Known as one fo the worst AE professors, he does not disappoint! He only teaches from his notes which are riddled with mistakes and makes fundamental mistakes in class that shows he does not know the material himself. The tests are based mostly on the book yet his teaching is not. I would not recommend him to anyone!

Be extremely wary of Yang's jet propulsion course. The department made him restructure the exams, so the class is no longer easy. The disorganized lectures throw hundreds of facts that you must recite on the exams with no notes to bring along with you. He also asked a question on the final that was material that actually was not even covered!
They made him change his curriculum, so it is no longer an easy class. Uneventful lectures and bizarre grading scheme. He's still probably better than all of the alternatives.

Yang is THE expert on propulsion, but his class will not teach you anything useful. The AE department recently made him change the course structure from online async tests to all in person tests and a project. It was obvious that this did not work well this semester, and the lectures did not prepare us at all for assignments. Very disappointing.

Incredibly disorganized and the whole class was just trivia at best... He's a nice person, and I wouldn't be writing a review if he hadn't just destroyed the class with a the final exam. He completely lied about the content, class was in uproar, and it wasn't possible to even get 80% unless you had equations that weren't in the 600 slides he gave.
He gave us a Christmas, halloween, and thanksgiving gift in the form of half of our final exam and asked for several peoples autographs, most entertaining teacher in AE at gt.

Dr. Yang is the most entertaining and kind AE professor at Tech. It's very conceptual and you'll learn the basics of propulsion engineering, as well as some economics behind the scenes. He may not make you a propulsion master, but he has some industry secrets up his sleeves and truly cares about the real-world success of his students.

Prof. Yang is probably the nicest AE prof you'll meet. His lecturing leaves something to be desired: not very organized and sprinkles *very* important facts here and there without any special detail. Homework tasks are mostly explanation based and not numerical which can be good and bad depending on how much you value being a propulsion engineer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: SUPER NICE GUY, but class had poor organization. He posts great resources, but hard to really parse their meanings in a useful way. Exams are open note and open internet, but will test your time management. HWs are more explanation based than numerical based. He does drop hints on what to expect on HWs or exams which is nice. Good, but not great.

Dr. Yang's class was the most unorganized class I've been in. No communication whatsoever about what is expected on exams. Sure, I wasn't a perfect student and should have gotten a B, but in no world did I deserve a C. The TA was unnecessarily harsh and basically did not know what material (or lack thereof) was being covered in lecture. Never take.

Dr. Yang is a great guy, and a fun lecturer that will teach you a lot about jet and rocket engines. However, his class on the other hand, has a complete and total lack of structure. He arbitrarily ramped up the difficulty midway through the semester, and the final exam seemed like a combination of trivia with complex thermodynamics on the side.

DO NOT TAKE. Dr. Yang is a nice guy but you will not learn a single thing. He expected us to do complex thermo problems without having taught any thermo. The grading was very harsh, would not take again.

Prof. Yang and his class are what you make it; for me, he was one of the best professors I've ever had and the knowledge and enthusiasm he brings to the class are what makes GT the #1 AE school. He wrote half of the books in jet and rocket propulsion- be ready to listen and enjoy. This is a lecture class, but for me, it kept me in AE.

Dr. Yang teaches at a very conceptual level. Exams and homeworks sometimes included calculations that hadn't been covered in class so try to take this right after thermo. The final project is the design of 3 different engines and analysis in MATLAB. The conceptual level topics did not provide enough material for the project to be done.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: If you value getting an A rather than learning anything, take him. Yang is nice, caring, and funny. He's also quite possibly the worst teacher I have ever had. The format of his course is disorganized, and his assignments are nonsense. I can confidently say I learned nothing in this class, and most of my peers feel the same way. Don't take him.
You'll get a good grade. You'll learn a lot of stories. Don't expect to learn enough propulsion to become a chief engineer

TAKE HIM! TAKE HIM! TAKE HIM! HE'S THE BEST! Jet & Rocket Propulsion is supposed to be one of the more difficult classes in AE, but the way Professor Yang teaches it makes the class so much easier than it would normally be! He asks students to suggest midterm questions, and HE LITERALLY ALLOWS YOU TO DO TEST CORRECTIONS FOR FULL CREDIT BACK!

Yang is amazing. Homework problems are directly from concepts discussed in class. Exams are take home open note and consist of conceptual questions (there's very little math) that from the homework, or sometimes he will tell you the exact questions and answers in class. He moves fast though since there's a lot of content to be covered in AE 4451.

Dr. Yang is probably my favorite professor I've had thus far. He's extremely knowledgeable, and his teaching style of AE 4451 focuses heavily on conceptual understanding and engine design considerations rather than mathematics. He very clearly states what will be on his midterms and is even willing to tell you the answers to it beforehand!

If you're looking for the math behind jet propulsion, this class isn't for you. If you're looking for a conceptual explanation of it, why it works, and the evolution of jet/rocket propulsion, this is your guy! Talks fast, so make sure you record, b/c pretty much everything he says is important. His class is more of a hist/evolution of jet/rock prop
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class--Respected

reviews.comment: Dr. Yang is not a bad person. He is more of a businessman than an academic. He teaches mostly superficial and top level concepts. Don't expect lots of mathematical understanding of propulsion phenomena. If you ask something more in depth, you will be told to "read it by yourself". Slides are a series of pictures and lack explanations.

Overall she was okay but is very rude over emails. I had missed a lecture due to personal issues and she didn't accept it. I had discussed the issues I was having and she still seemed to not care. I was very surprised since I had heard good things about the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. van de Wouw made synth lab one of my most favorite courses I've taken. This class is supposed to be super difficult, but she made it so manageable. I knew exactly what I needed to do to get an A, and it wasn't unrealistic. She explained what should be difficult organic chemistry topics in simple terms. I took orgo 2 concurrently and was fine.

The specifications grading makes this class very easy. For every assignment, if you meet enough requirements on the rubric you get a grade of "complete". The only semi-hard part was the technique finals. The token system means you get to redo them if you fail, so you'll be fine. Easy and fun class, professor was very sweet.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class itself seems pretty random honestly but she's a great professor. She tries her best and really takes into account student feedback to treat this as a 2 credit course (she inherited the course). Specs grading can seem really weird at first but it works out in the end so I wouldn't worry too much. Sometimes the work felt like a waste though

Specifications grading makes this class easy. Dr. van de Wouw is kind and approachable. Your grade really depends on the TA you have but most are chill. Token system to re-attempt assignments really helps. Everyone gets an incomplete on the first lab report; don't panic, you can revise it.

Great professor. Only issue is that the pre lab lectures were mandatory (only 1 skip given) but they were honestly helpful in doing the pre labs and the post labs so I would reccomend going. She gives out a lot of "tokens" than can be used to resubmit assingments throughout the semester. Everyone I know got an A with minimal stress.

Synth lab was a class I was worried about taking but she made it very manageable and interesting. She is newer to teaching the course, so she is very open to student feedback about making the course fairer to students. She cares about everyone being successful and prioritizes that.

Great instructor who changed the class structure/grading to better fit students' needs. All the assignments are pass/fail, which felt intimidating, but they're not super difficult after doing the same ones for each lab. Pre-lab lectures feel annoying and inconvenient time-wise, but they really help with the experiments and writing post-lab reports.

During our 5-9 PM section lab, van de wouw is always there helping out and having fun with the students conversing with them. Additionally, she understands that student's have other obligations and works to address this constantly (with her easy specs grading scheme and removing certain assignments). TA Feedback, though sometimes harsh, is fair.

Dr. van de Wouw really listens to her students and tries to modify the course to best accommodate their needs. She genuinely cares about making sure that Synth Lab is a reasonable course that students can still take a lot out of.

She is new to GT and chem 2380. Seems to be trying to make the course easier for students as it is a pretty labor intensive class as designed by a previous instructor. She is open to student feedback, but lectures are not at the best time.

Attendance is mandatory with only 4 "freebies"
She does NOT post notes, and spends exactly 2 seconds on each slide.
Not like the notes will help you anyways though-- the exams are nothing like the class material. Also for all that work, the attendance is only 10% the rest of your grade is exams and the final

She rushes through lectures and her tests are not as representative of the course compared to other MSE professors. She doesn't post lecture notes since she deems that unfair to students who didn't attend class, which makes it really hard since she rushes through everything.

MSE isn't a very hard class, but there is a lot of content. Professor Milam is unfortunately very disorganized and always making mistakes in lecture. She ends up rushing through the slides (which she is really just reading at you). On top of this, she will not post her complete notes, so if you miss something, good luck. Don't take Professor Milam.

She seems to mean well, but is often disorganized and behind in lecture. I found that for our exams, we usually finished learning the content the last class just before the exam, which provides little time to study. Most other professors teaching the course at the same time were further ahead than us.
worst course ever

Overall, professor Milam was a good teacher but sometimes the way she structured her class and tests made things feel a bit more difficult/stressful than they should have been. She covered the content well but gave lots of quizzes/tests with relatively few practice materials, so you were on your own for studying.

She's not the best professor ever, but she's not as bad as every other reviews say. Lectures were great, she made sure to review everything thoroughly. I found myself studying 3 hours for weekly 4 minute quizzes and her tests often did not give sufficient time but that was really the only issue besides slow grading. It's clear she's passionate.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although many of the assignments (quizzes and tests) took a while to get back, the class overall was generally good. If you studied what was covered in the notes and applied a bit of common sense to the topics, you'd be fine. I enjoyed the class and would recommend Milam to anyone taking MSE 2001. Very easy to get a B, due to grading distribution.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Milam is not the greatest professor. Besides MSE 2001 being already a heavy lecture class, she only graded by a couple tests, and was very clear that she wouldn't give any extra credit. there's no hw and she rarely stayed for office hours. She didn't solve the problems but said that we needed to know them for tests, and tests were hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this professor for 2001. Fails to give back multiple choice quizzes in a timely manner (over 2 weeks at times), gives almost no guidance on what will be on exams, makes you memorize completely pointless and trivial things, 4 minute pop quizzes weekly that start the minute class begins yet she's often late for class. DO NOT TAKE HER
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Milam does a great job with a subject that is inherently dull to most people. She is kind and answers all questions, and her problem sets on exams come directly from practice ones that she posts for you (easy). Sometimes grading is slow but she never hesitates to explain why. If you actually put in the effort you'll get the grade you want.

The only study material she provides for her many exams is quizzes (which significantly impacts our class grade). Despite this, she does not release the answer key or graded quizzes before the exam.
Her lecture notes do not highlight what she considers important, and no online material is helpful to supplement what she is trying to teach.

Absolutely awful professor. She takes a month to grade multiple choice tests. We had a multiple choice quiz a week before our test and she is not going to grade them in time, so we have no idea if we got anything right or wrong on the quiz. She is bad with technology, and gives no type of study guide to prepare for tests. Terrible teacher.

She has terrible boring lectures that have made me hate learning. There is no way to prepare well for any tests or quizzes. The class is terribly organized. She is the slowest grader ever and almost all of the questions are multiple choice. Don't think these MCQs are easy, they will be on something completely different than what you study for.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The worst professor I have ever had
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not really sure why she became a professor since she is horrible at teaching and makes learning incredibly difficult. Reads off a sheet of paper and calls it a lecture. Discourages questions during class, inaccessible after class, the fact her gpa is >0.5 less than every other prof for this class says it all. You're better off.

This woman has killed the motivation and passion more than any other teacher I've ever met. It's ridiculous that she's still allowed to teach following her multiple crusades against student mental health. She doesn't teach she just expects you to memorize everything and only explains basic ideas not the important concepts. You will learn nothing.

She's not very good at delivering lectures and her way of grading is not fair.  She tends to not explain things and expects you to memorize the notes down to the core as opposed to understanding material.  She's not worth taking just to get the credit wait a semester the class isn't a pre-req for anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible professor who does not care about her job. Completely kills students' passions which is the sole thing a teacher and mentor is not supposed to do. Do not take this class with her no matter what. She doesn't deserve her job and needs to be fired or barred from teaching ASAP.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Like other reviews have said the amount of unnecessary stress that this class has caused has damaged my mental health. The fact that we have trick questions that determine 20% of the grade on a quiz is truly exhausting. She makes learning hellish in the most mundane way possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Do not take MSE with her if you can avoid it. Lecture notes are not posted and tests are heavily reliant on the notes. The textbook "isn't mandatory" but she makes you responsible for test material that she does not cover in lecture. The lecture time dedicated to certain topics over others is skewed which makes it hard to study adequately.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She gives tests that are graded completely unfairly and gives random quizzes all the time. Also assigns no homework so there isn't much to do to study except study her outline lecture notes which tend to be unhelpful since her lectures are very dull.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This woman singlehandedly made me dread class. Every minute spent in her class is a minute of my life that I will never get back. She does not care about student mental health, understanding, or growth. She lies about tests and is the only teacher I've ever known to actually use trick questions. Do not take her class under any circumstance.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Outside of lectures she would provide little to no resources to students limiting their ability to perform at a decent level in her class. She also chooses to format her class in a way that is harmful to students grades and understanding.Take ANY other MSE class besides this one. :)

I was frustrated by her teaching style, she wrote irrelevant things on the board just to erase them a moment later, and she focused more on easy stuff and not enough on harder material. I'm also upset I got good quiz grades and 94ish for three tests, but a 75 on one test and ended up with a B, I feel like the weighting could have been more lenient.

Dr. Milam seems like she had the best intentions for class, but her system is seriously flawed. Its impossible to pay attention to lecture when all it is is her showing us prerecorded lecture without a chance for interaction. Also, tests are graded on spelling which is just incredibly cool ��. Posted notes were also completely covered so pointless
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class wasn't helped by its heavy subject matter, but Prof. Milam's lectures were quite dry and made it very difficult to get a grasp of the course materials at times. The textbook was decent but what was most frustrating was her incredibly picky grading standards and unfair testing. This was simply an uninspiring and often frustrating class.

She grades you on spelling and puts the wrong answers into Canvas so your grade at the end of quizzes aren't accurate. We had ONE homework assignment due on 9/4 that she hasn't graded yet worth 10% of our grade (twice the weight of the final). She has two tests on insane amounts of terms that you just word vomit onto the exam. Should've dropped lol

Prof. Milam is an amazing lecturer. She breaks everything down into bite-sized chunks. Make sure you go to every lecture because she gives pop quizzes and she doesn't upload any notes. Here test were pretty fair, but if you want to get a good grade make sure you know basically everything she puts on the board.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Milam is probably hands down the best professor for MSE at GaTech. She has a unique way of teaching that will make you really learn the subject. But don't go to her class thinking that it would be an easy A. Professor Milam will make you work really hard for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Lectures were pretty boring but she explained things very well. Tests were very detailed and were graded pretty hard. The class is basically a crap ton of memorization with a little bit of geometry.  The concepts were not hard, but she does not post any notes online (or grades for that matter) and the tests are based off the notes from class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Good teacher and good lectures.  Book wasn't really necessary for anything, except a couple vocab words.  Memorize the class notes and vocal terms cause that is the majority of the tests.  Also you need to know any calculation she puts on the board!

Dr. Milam is a very good lecturer and clarifies difficult concepts well. She is also a  busy lady, so it was sometimes hard to meet with her in office hours. Just make sure you understand everything very well before  each lecture bc she gives pop quizzes. There's alot of stuff to know for this class, so just stay on top of it and you'll be fine.

Milam isn't really available for consultation out of class (multiple people in class haven't gotten their tests back and today was the day of the final). She also doesn't give partial credit for minor spelling issues and will probably give you 24 on the definition of MSE even if you're in the major specific section. Take Qin instead.

Dr. Milam understands her subject very well, but she does not come across as enthusiastic in her lectures. The class was very boring, which I was very disappointed by as I truly enjoy the subject. She does not post grades nor does she post answer keys to past quizzes or tests, making it hard to study if you have lost any of them.

Yeah, okay, maybe she was a good lecturer, but that's the only thing she's got going for her. She had ONE office hour per week, and BOTH times I went(one time I contacted her beforehand) she was not there for it. She doesn't put ANY grades online, so good luck figuring out how you're doing in the class. She's also not very nice.
Never posted anything on t-square.  Made it difficult to know what grades were, but outside of that great teacher.

She's very helpful and easy to understand. Gives great notes. You have to go to class, because she gives pop quizzes. The tests aren't bad if you go to class, read what she asks you to read, and study.
Easy teacher, all you have to do is listen in class. The material is a review of high school chemistry with some additions.

She is easy to understand,helpful after class,and easy to communicate with.  However, her tests are hard, class attendence is a must because she gives test material and pop quizzes.  Dont take her unless you have to.
really good teacher.

Took during F25. Exams were open note/laptop, and were generally alright. He didn't post practice exams but going over the homework and recitation questions helped before the exams. Lectures leaned theory heavy but still manageable.

He's *fine.* Thermo is hard, his homework are good to practice, most of what he says in lectures is irrelevant. You need to learn a number of formulas and how to apply them. Seems like he leveled the Fall 25 grade distribution to be a bit lower by making the final rly challenging, but if you learn the homework and concepts exams are relatively fair
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is nice and always there to help, the course wasn't that difficult, of course you have to study and work on a final project, he is very fair at grading.

Professor Sun is very knowledgeable on thermo- and fluid dynamics. His lectures tend towards the abstract, spending most of the time deriving equations rather than working through examples.
Homework was graded very late. Very little time was given to look over corrections before the final.
Exams...were lenient. Ample resources provided.

I'll write what people really care about. The class is hard, but he allows the use of laptops for access to lectures and tables during exams, yes most of the students around me had their own notes/formulas included. All of that together with just paying attention to his lectures (actually attend them) and it's a really easy class. All formula based

Probably an easier thermo section compared to the others but hes incredibly unhelpful duirng office hours and is often just rude for no reason. His lectures go through little to no practice problems and only does derivations. Posts 0 practice exams. All exams open note&textbook, but he grades harshly. I have a personal vendetta against this man.

From my experience, Dr. Sun's Thermo and Fluids class was relatively easy compared to my peer's. The tests are very closely related to the homework. The recitation attached with this class was very helpful for my learning and a great study tool that summarizes the course content well. I recommend taking this course with Him.

Very nice and class was generally not too hard. He doesn't post notes tho so you have to get the content from lecture or from someone who went to lecture. Homework wasn't too hard and exams were pretty similar to the homework. Also didn't really grade the hw harshly at all.

A lot of the lectures were based on how to solve problems, rather than gaining a solid conceptual understanding
Didn't do a good job explaining the conceptual part of fluids like Mach wave vs Shock wave, shock waves in tubes, PTs, stagnation props.
Lectures were a bit disorganized. Tests and HW were fair.
Not a good or bad prof.

Professor Sun is definitely one of the better thermo professors, his exams are easy, and homework is mostly understandable. His lectures, however, are rather disorganized. While he is easier than other professors, he is not a great lecturer. Had to learn everything from the textbook or recitation.
Great professor who knows his stuff. Exam questions were based on homework problem sets (and were honestly easier). Class felt very fair, would highly recommend if you're taking thermo.

he's an good professor and answers questions very well but the class content is very difficult and lecture heavy. only had 2 midterms, homework, and the final. recommend paying attention and always going to him bc he was always willing to help. the content was difficult for me bc its a theory heavy course but he was always willing to re-explain
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Sun understands the balance between teaching teaching a class to achieve grades and teaching a class to learn the content well. He is personable and while he is sometimes difficult to communicate with online, he is fantastic at answering questions before/during/after class. You can tell he cares about teaching the content and tests are fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is curved by 5% (A is 85%) and there is extra credit. HARD class, but not the worst. Lectures and homework is harder than tests (tests are heavily weighted). It's not an easy class but the professor is understanding, gives HW extensions, answers questions, explains concepts patiently. It's a tough class, take it with Dr. Wenting.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures are the single most important thing in this class. Do not miss them. Prof Sun is a solid teacher and will do his best to help you understand the concepts if you have questions. Work hard on the homework; it's harder than the tests, and if you understand the homework, you'll be ok on the tests.

Dr. Sun is a great person and an even better lecturer. AE 2010 is a hard class, so you will struggle quite a bit to get all the material down. But Dr. Sun is really good about breaking down complex concepts and moving through a lot of material really efficiently. Besides class, he is a cool person, and has a pretty rare but genuine sense of humor.

Do not take. Lectures are confusing. She gets confused by her own slides, so how are we supposed to understand? Clearly doesn't prepare for lecture. Midterm (early, easier topics) had mean and median of 50ish. Exam not returned to students so no change to learn from mistakes or contest bad grading. Free content (books, YouTube) more helpful.

If you want to learn whatever she's teaching, find a free online course and teach yourself. You will have to teach yourself regardless, and her involvement just adds to the confusion. She never releases rubrics for anything, whether it's a homework, project, or presentation. She doesn't care

Very disappointed after finishing this class, was meant to focus on Neural and Behavioral Data but Prof Wu essentially turned it into a core Machine Learning class, with unclear slides, tangential and contrived explanations, lack of appropriate expectations and shoddy homework assignments. I did fine on the class but it was a serious waste of time.
Loved the lectures, and the TAs

Horrible lectures that don't teach anything, super incompetent TA's who don't bother to help at all, and really hard homeworks. I hate this course- only thing I got out of it is a group project. I absolutely hate this class, the prof, and the TA's
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are ineffective for learning course content compared to following the syllabus and searching on Google. Notation in the class slides is unclear and inconsistent, causing confusion during lectures. The pace of teaching is too fast, with important details glossed over. Overall, the course seems unsuitable for beginners.

The lectures are way too technical and move way too fast, even for people who have a strong math and programming background. Homeworks are extremely confusing and the "extra credit" questions are not fair. Furthermore the grading policy is constantly being changed and updated without clear communication to the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Too many terminologies make lecture hard to follow, many of them are not necessary to be introduced at very first. The definition of this course is ambiguous -- is it for experts or tyro? For experts, the course content is too out of date. For tyro, nana, it's not that friendly. Prof. Wu usually won't explain the foundation stuff. take again?No.

Some homework and exam problems are worded so confusingly and different from what's taught in lectures that make you wonder if she reads her homework and exams before giving them out. Piazza questions can be left unanswered for days but when students complain, it's apparently our fault for not "not having an idea of the workload".
Boring lecture, total waste of time. The homework also makes no sense. No help before the exam. Make easy topics complicate and irritating.

Class is very fast paced and you can fall behind very easily. Doesn't post lecture videos for whatever reason (even though attendance is mandatory?). Her grading and syllabus are harsh, but she cares about students and is willing to help if you go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Big time commitment for this class but it is not insanely difficult. If you go to class it is very manageable and any questions can be answered in office hours. Class is five big software assignments with a final group project/presentation that is very simple. Do not fall behind otherwise you will struggle to catch up.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Wen does not respond to emails asking for help, not flexible with students, lectures on exercises loosely related to the assignment but does not provide instructions on how to repeat the work. Class and grading overall can be frustrating because instructors will say something in class and then directly contradict that statement when grading.

Dr. Woodbury cares a lot about his students and wants them to succeed. Just make sure you keep up with the homework deadlines as they aren't the midnight standard. Attendance isn't mandatory, but there are in-class work (for credit) that you may miss if you skip class. Make sure to use the scheduling site to setup an appt with him if you need help.

I do not have a good experience with this professor. Difficult to get a hold of and not very willing to go out of his way to support individual students. His lectures are hard to follow along with the criteria he is producing. Some may disagree but not the professor for me.

Very awkward, both him and his lectures. he only cares about student from econ Econ club. He likes to brags his jd degree that wasn't even from an ABA accredited school. Also weird that Econ department let a lecturer lead the undergrad program.
The exams are a big part of the final grade. He was okay and does offer a little extra credit.

Class meets in-person 1x a week. I'd recommend showing up to that class because of occasional in-class assignments and extra credit opportunities. The exam's are very similar in structure (MCQ, Multiple Select, and FRQ). FRQ were always practice problems. MCQ and Multiple Select were difficult, I'd take notes on textbook chapters. Not-too-hard A.
make sure you go to class because he will spring assignments on you. Easy class if you pay attention and do some studying for tests.

Take him!! I have nothing but great things to say. If you do the homework on time and study the practice problems he gives, you have absolutely nothing to worry about. We also only meet once a week instead of twice. I've thoroughly enjoyed his class so far, I'm understanding the content, and don't feel stressed at all. HIGHLY recommend.

Woodbury is a good professor. Class has two parts: watch online lecture and answer some homework questions online, then in class he builds on the lecture and you do a worksheet graded on completion (so go to class). You have 2 midterms and 1 final which combined are probably 60% of your grade. Tests & class not too hard. There is some extra credit.

I initially had no interest in economics but he managed to make me enjoy the class and like econ.  Class is pretty tough for a GED imo but very doable.  If you do all the homeworks and do well on the final he will round up ur grade very nice guy.  Like I did very bad on exam 1 but very well on final so he gave me an A despite being at a ~88.

Class time was useless, no study guides, no TAs, just him and the fact that he knows nothing about the textbook. Had no office hours on finals week, his in person ones were when everyone has class. no direction on tests, but are weighted so much, the rest is completion. Many people between a B and an A. somehow better than bolton's grading scale..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor and keeps lectures pretty light (he has async lectures with more detail). He is really clear on how you can do well in the class and what to look out for in exams. Even if you don't get a lot of extra credit during the semester, he'll bump up your grade if you're close enough and put effort in the class.

I took 2100 with Dr. Woodbury and he was an excellent instructor. He was accommodating and kind, and many times allowed the students to make a collaborative decision regarding exam dates. He also provided extra optional assignments at the end of the course for students to boost their grades. He cares about his students, and is a great teacher.
Dr.Woodbury is one of the best econ professors at Gatech. So nice and very helpful, really really learned a lot from him. Very funny too

Great professor! Emphasizes that students understand the derived, practical concepts from mathematical models to succeed. Exams reflect this by asking questions that require reasoning through different models with no math necessary. Personally would prefer a bit more depth to the mathematical models, but an awesome professor nonetheless.

Incredibly chill dude and was gave informative and interesting lectures in class. I had his 8am class and managed to stay awake so it definitely isn't a boring class. The tests are all written response but as long as he gets a general idea of what you are saying (& you aren't just wrong) it shouldn't be hard at all to get an A in this class.

Dr. Woodbury is great! The class is organized into pre-lectures and lecture time with paired in class activities. He cares about students' success and is accessible outside of class. I recommend reading the textbook and taking advantage of any extra credit opportunities. Not too difficult as long as you study and use available resources.
I was amazed by how such a person who basically doesn't know about anything besides the textbook became a professor at GT. Plus he's not a nice person in general.

Dr. Woodbury is a fantastic professor and I would highly recommend taking his class. His exams can be a little tough but as long as you're putting the work in and participating, he makes it very easy to do well in the class. Lots of extra credit opportunities available as well

He definitely was a tough grader and the class weighed exams pretty high, but his online lecture videos were pretty clear. He was also fairly clear on his grading criteria for exams. An average professor at best--the class didn't teach me too much about macro, but wasn't too intensive except for the exams.

Prof. Woodbury is a really great professor. his exam are NOT multiple choice, they are free response. harder or not idk. Definitely teaches you a lot more about macro economics and is very kind. he gives extra credit work which boosts grades. and is a very understanding and caring professor. Definitely would take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: very understanding and engaging professor. bad luck if you got his 8am. he will ask you to speak in front of the class, especially if you look like you're falling asleep. but he'll also tell you so much in office hours and bring candy after halloween
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The actual classes weren't super informative because we just went over homework but he is super receptive to questions during office hours and a really sweet person. Grades test pretty intensely but give a ton of extra credit so it is possible to get an A even with poor test grades.

One or two lectures posted on Canvas each week to watch to prepare for class. The class is mostly discussion of the material, and engaging in those discussions usually leads to discussion of what will be on the exam. ASK QUESTIONS or you won't do well. There are a ton of opportunities to gain extra credit, so take advantage of them!

He is very random when it comes to grading and what he likes. It was hard to figure out how he wanted your answers. You have to go to office hours to get answers to the homework and you have to participate in class a lot. Best part is he gives LOTS of extra credit opportunities. Also, it's completely points based, no weighting.

The format of this class makes it very un-enjoyable. He won't lecture in class and posts lectures to watch each week where he just reads from minimal slides. In class, you present your homework and do problems from the textbook. He is a pretty harsh grader which sucks considering the two midterms and the final are heavily weighted.

He does not teach the material well. His lecture videos are him reading word for word from the textbook, and if you ask him a question outside the realm of the textbook he does not know. He grades very harshly for someone who does not teach well. Seems like most my class won't make an A in the class. He makes the class way harder than it should be.

Good professor and knows what he's talking about with Econ. Make sure you participate in the questions he asks the class because they tend to be similar concepts to what he has on the test. Tests are graded pretty harshly, but you'll get a lot of extra credit throughout the semester. Make sure you talk about institutions' influence during tests.
Great professor overall. Teaches concepts well in-depth. Work on projects ahead of time. Just grind practice exams and midterms will be fine.

Honestly if you spend a good amount of time on the projects, you should be set for the class. I got a 50 on the 1st project and still ended with an A after doing extra credit on proj 2. Exams are fine as long as you do the past exams she gives out! Pretty fun game project.

Dr. Wills is a great professor and I would highly recommend her for ECE 2035. I was teetering between taking 2035 or 2036 bc I'm EE, but I chose to take 2035 because I heard she is a great professor and that was definitely true. Clear lectures and expectations. Just make sure to pay attention in class and you will be ok!

Very easy class, exams are very easy as long as you practice. Start on the projects way ahead of time. Lots of opportunities to get extra credit and good grades. Weak lecturer in my opinion, but not too bad. Overall, class was very fun and the content was very interesting to learn
She's a nice lady. she always will try to answer your questions to the fullest of her ability. the work takes some figuring out regardless. take her if you're taking 2035.

I wish I did better in this class- the first project was hard and I randomly bombed a test I thought I did well on. Through all of this though, Linda has been the most caring professor I have ever had. She is patient and very fair, which reflects through her TAs who are the same. Go to her and TA office hours, they are awesome!
Linda Wills is soooo caring and nice in test grading!
I will forever miss my goat Rudrunshu Datta
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Just a good professor.

Dr. Wills is very good at what she does, she understands the class and its contents well and does a great job of understanding the class. The tests are tough but she is fair on grading, the projects are a time sink but not too difficult. She is always willing to help students so don't be afraid to reach out to her.
Wills is a good professor. Take her if you can. Weren't the most engaging or funny lectures, but good.

Her enthusiasm is awesome and she clearly wants us to succeed and learn a lot.  Sometimes she can be monotone so class can be boring, but the content is incredibly fascinating.  This class has by far been my favorite class at tech.  I will say the projects are actually challenging and intriguing, so I suggest to give it more time than you'd think.

I would say that ECE 2035 is a very tough course. Dr. Wills has helped me out a lot outside of class and she does care about her students. I think the style of teaching is very hard to understand the topics. This course will take a lot of time but there are different ways to do well in the course with the way the grading is.
God Bless Linda Wills

Very project and test heavy courses. TAs are hit or miss but professor Wills is an amazing professor. She developed most of the content for the course and knows exactly how to teach it. Do the extra credit for the first project and START EARLY! Do not get behind like everyone does. You will thank your past self when that day comes around.
Professor Wills is one of the best professors I've had at Georgia Tech, she cares so much and will set aside time to help you if you ask for it :)

Absolutely take Prof. Wills for 2035. Super caring and helpful in office hours. GTAs were helpful but UTAs were mostly clueless. I thought the exams were pretty easy and past exams are provided but averages were around 75. Homeworks and projects were good and taught a lot! I enjoyed the performance based grading of the first project.

This class may just be very difficult because of the topics but the lectures are hard to follow and the projects given in class have a very rigorous timeline that was pushed back because of how fast it was. The tests are difficult but are graded in a fair way keeping the average at least a 75.

2035 is hard already as is but Wills is very understanding and willing to work with you on anything. Her office hours helped me understand the concepts better but beware of some of the TAs, they are literally no help. Start the homework and projects early because they are very time-consuming and confusing. Prepare to dedicate 15 hours each week.

The secret to this class is if you are stuck go to Dr. Wills office hours. Even if you are not in her section the other professor is usually not the best. The TA's are absolutely useless for this class, do not go to them for help, they never know what they are talking about and they will actually hurt your grade more if you get help from them.

ECE 2035 is brutal, but Dr. Wills makes this class super accessible and interesting. She genuinely cares so much about her students, and will help you out if you're confused with the projects/content or find yourself in a rut with the workload. There's no question about it, take Wills for 2035.

Professor Wills is tough and will require you to learn in order to pass tests and complete the projects. However, she is very available for discussion and highly flexible on due dates. If you need an extension, she'll grant it. If you need suggestions, she'll readily help you reach a solution. 10/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A real gem of a professor. She is extremely caring and wants everybody to succeed. There is tons and tons of extra credit available, and tests are extremely fair. Would highly recommend.

Dr Wills is a great professor for the 2nd year ECE student. 2035 is a lot of work, which is kind of annoying, but it strengthens your problem solving and makes you think, and she will guide and help you if she can! There's also so much extra credit. Hard work is rewarded, and she notices! Lectures are chill. Make a good life decision and take her!

Honestly my favorite teacher I have had at Tech. She gives great lectures and is a very caring and generous professor. There was a lot of work to do in this class but you learn so much and she gives plenty of resources (office hours, TA office hours, extension resources) to lighten the burden. TAKE HER FOR THIS CLASS IF YOU HAVE THE OPTION!!!

Dr Wills is a caring professor but the course is extremely and often unnecessarily hard. Dr Wills often explains incoherently and its hard to follow from one concept to another. At the end it felt like I learned some techniques and skills but did not acquire any knowledge.
Her class was extremely hard for me but she is perhaps the most caring and nicest professors/teachers I have ever had. Just an absolutely amazing human being.

A real gem. She cares so much, and teaches really well. The projects are admittedly hard, but you learn so much by doing them, and when you're done, it feels amazing to look back on what did. Extremely friendly and easy to approach/talk to.
Absolutely fantastic professor.
She's super nice but her class is unnecessarily hard. Not sure if it's her fault but one of the hardest classes I've taken
She was great.

Was honestly probably the best professor I've had here at Tech. She was extremely passionate about the subject and helping her students. Very accessible and reasonable. Also offers heavy EC on projects which is helpful, especially for those who may not excel on timed exams.
Very accessible and cares about her students. Offers extra credit on both major projects. Tests are manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Awesome prof! Go to lectures, start projects early and get the extra credit, and ask when you need to (prof and TAs are all very accessible). Grading is relatively lenient. No textbook needed. Just take her! Compiler Appreciated.

Great choice for ECE 2035! Engaging lectures that provided practice for exams and examples for homework. Projects have lots of room for extra credit. Tests are not too difficult, but you definitely need to prepare for them. She is always willing to go over questions in office hours or at the end of lectures.

Don't even scroll any further down the page! JUST TAKE HER!!! Tips: - Start the final project as soon as you get the PDF. I started the final project the week before thinking I would have enough time but was not able to finish - Don't undermine the extra credit - Practice exams are golden resources for the exams. Do as much of them as possible
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: ECE 2035 is a very hard course in my opinion but Professor Wills teaches the content really well and offers many resources to students and is really generous.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Wills had sometimes convoluted lectures, but she's very easy to understand, answers questions carefully, is extremely accessible and is really understanding and caring. 2035 is a very well structured class and a lot of emphasis is put onto projects with opportunities for extra credit.

The best professor in the ECE department, period. She needs to teach some higher level ECE courses because many of those courses are poorly structured (which is why I switched to CS), and we need professors like her to teach them (also considering the fact that she has 3 degrees from MIT!!!!!!).

2035 is a class with rather difficult material, but she is so passionate about it and teaching that you can effectively pick it up, and if you don't immediately, she is one of the most generously available profs outside of class I've had. She truly cares about each and every one of her students and their success. The last project has generous EC.

A genuine teacher with a very kind heart. She actually increased class size pre-semester to accommodate me (an international student) who could not register early, took personal interest to ask why I did marginally in the beginning of the semester and gave extra credit just to emphasize the fact that I completed the projects by myself. A+ prof.

Very good lecturer. May get confusing at times bc she is very passionate about the content and knows it well. More than willing to help you after class. Content is difficult. Study hard. Start homework and projects early, and use Piazza. Never misses class. Attendance is mandatory to pass, bc online resources don't explain it all & text is useless.

Prof Wills was great for 2035. Sometimes she can be a little scattered during lectures but she is very intelligent and knows what she is doing. If you don't understand something in class she is very approachable during office hours and will help you. The projects can be difficult, but some involve extra credit. Tests can be tricky. Study study.
Very helpful

Nicest lady ever.  Explains material clearly and always offers to help you privately.  Brought candy and cookies to class several times.  Super-easy project that was basically a free A test grade.  Tests are extensive and thorough and require some studying.  Fun class.

he has good things and bad things about him. he does like to intimidate and show off how smart and powerful he is. also during the class he's always going off-topic and making jokes, so i learn maybe half the material in class. this guy is just doin too much.

on the other hand, i think he means well and is a pretty funny guy

The kind of prof they make movies about. Hilarious, engaging, AMAZING lectures. Yes tests are hard, but very very fair, if you put in the work an A is very achievable. Got a B because of daily quizzes- the one awful part of the class. Do NOT miss a single class. He really cares for students and teaches you what ISyE is all about.

Amazing person and teacher. Lectures are quite clear and explanations are great! Quite a hilarious teacher too. However, any absences or getting caught off guard punish your grade a lot since there are quizzes every class. Exams are also quite hard.

most difficult prof ever he makes fun of students but disguises it as "tough love" he thinks his class should be our top priority and humiliates students for not understanding concepts. if hes so committed to us learning the content why doesnt he teach it? he wastes everyones time by spending class time having side convos w his select fav students
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Having Damon as a professor my freshman year of college changed my life. Easily the best professor I have ever had at GT, made me passionate about industrial engineering and taught me that hard work will pay off. The course is pretty tough but if you follow his steps for success and put in work outside the classroom, you will do great.

Damon is quite a character, as you can see from the other ratings he is very polarizing. I thought he was great and funny but I see why some people don't like his personality. Anna the TA is great though. Daily quizzes every day, 2 midterms which were fair, do all you can to not take final, I hear its impossible. Life lessons will be dispensed.

Damon is a character. An experience. He's the kind of prof you hear stories about. His class is not for complainers. He will shape you up. Yes, his class is super hard, but you will rise to the challenge. You're gonna have probability down by the end of it. He's funny and has a lot of wisdom to share as well. TAKE HIM!

Super unprofessional and never responds to any emails or texts. Final is way too difficult and includes stuff never even covered in the class. If you do not get 92+ on both tests, you are gonna get an A. Barely learned when he was teaching, but actually learned stuff with the TA. Content is easy overall, just do not do bad on a test.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I do agree that some of the lectures aren't very efficient. However, Damon is a solid lecturer and the HWs provided were clutch. Going through those problems are what determine what grade you are going to deserve(Not Graded). The first two exams aren't as bad as you expect but I have done anything to have exempted the final. Anna was great too.
