Damon spends basically the entire class making fun of some random kids instead of teaching the lecture. He also has no office hours and doesn't respond to emails or texts. The TA is much better. Tests are relatively simple but if you aren't able to exempt the final, you are basically guaranteed a B since the final is impossible.

Never actually learned much during class, but went for the daily quiz. Damon yaps about life, goes through a couple of pages of the notes, and tells you to learn the meat of the content by yourself. Anna, the TA, was much better at giving lectures and is incredibly helpful. The final exam is hopeless, so forget about exam replacement.

Damon is a great professor. He tells you on the first day of class what he expects from his students and how to make an A (a ton of work). Exams take the content learned in class and make you go a step further which I definitely struggled with. Overall, if you want to learn probability and how to be a better person/student, take Damon 100%.

Very difficult course, Damon is nice, but I did not love going to class every day, he is a very reasonable person though. You definitely earn the grade you get in this class. Attendance is mandatory because there are quizzes at the beginning of each class. Anna the TA is amazing though, she gives a lot of credit for the quizzes.

Daily quizzes to start the class were sometimes unfair. Spent too much time of lecture with banter. Requires LOTS of work outside of class. Kept me awake at 8 AM. Gave good life advice and good teacher if you want to spend time learning on your own and making a friend in class.

Very hilarious and engaging, knowledgeable guy. Grading was harder in the second half of the sem since people were doing well in the first half. Verbal quizzes every class were stressful, questions sometimes out of notes, sometimes randomly hard. Exams mostly fair, but the review that said they got a 98 and 99 is definitely not a norm for the class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Kept everybody super engaged even for an 8am. He is a tad scary and not afraid to pick on you in the name of being funny. The hardest part of the class was having a quiz every single day. The tests were VERY fair (I got a 98 and a 99 and exempt from the final with minimal effort). All homework is optional but it does help you succeed.

Damon is an amazing professor! He's entertaining and teaches the material in a way that's easy to understand. The material isn't that bad but the class is a lottt of work. Quizzes every single class but questions are taken straight off the notes or homework. Exams are similar to the homework problems too.

Amazing professor. He keeps the students engaged for a 75-minute lecture and shows how it's applicable in day-to-day life. While the test questions are harder than the example ones in class, they're not harder than the optional homework, so use that to study. Definitely take this professor if possible.

THE BEST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD IN GEORGIA TECH!!! EXAMS ARE HARD BUT YOU JUST HAVE TO PERFORM! HE IS NOT ONLY GREAT AT TEACHING HE IS ALSO GREAT AT GIVING ADVICE AND LIFE LESSONS. 
HE IS THE BEST!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: There's an easy quiz every morning over the last class's topic and random extra credit. If you've had any subject on logic/sets this class is a joke with him. Tests are a random spike harder than the questions in class, but not impossible, go through past exams before the test and you'll be fine. Take this professor if you can.

Favorite professor I've had so far. Made the 8am bearable, engaged with the class, made us laugh regularly. Communication outside of class is limited to the TA's mostly, though. Exams were graded somewhat inconsistently. 100000x over, take Damon if you're able to. Any qualms with Damon pale in comparison to Foley etc. for ISyE 2027

Damon is one of the best teachers I have had so far at Georgia Tech. His lectures are engaging, and energetic, and he strives to get the best out of his students. However, in doing so he has a quiz almost every class, and tests/quizzes consist of 95% of the final grade. He also dosen't believe in curving grades. Overall he is an amazing professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I loved this man. I had him over the summer of 2022 and he was the best thing to happen to me as an IE major here.

This professor is probably the least competent person I've ever had to deal with in academia. His test questions are incoherent, his grading is seemingly arbitrary, and his tests often have no relation to the material taught. Dealing with him outside is class is virtually impossible. He is rude, disrespectful, and does not care about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The best professor. He cares about his students - goes above and beyond to make everyone feel involved and motivated by having an insane amount of office hours, learning everyone's names (in a class of 60+), and by giving practical life lessons and even bringing in guest speakers to ensure we are successful both in and out of the classroom.

Damon is the best professor you will ever have. and he knows it. Holds so many office hours to go over questions, learns everyones names, and instills the confidence to make you feel like you can handle IE. Class is definitely hard but insanely rewarding. He makes you want to go to class and study and be successful. Make sure he knows who you are.

Damon is one of the most caring professors Ive ever had. He goes above and beyond in lectures, learning everyones names and keeping things engaging. Hes also given many small lessons to help as well, from getting ready for senior design to negotiating salaries for an internship. Definitely take his class if you ever have a chance!
By far the best professor I've had at Tech. He expects you to learn a lot, but the level of care he has for students is unmatched. If you work hard, he will make sure you get the grade you deserve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: One of the most caring and invested profs I've had. Tests are hard but do what he says to study and you'll be fine. Group project at the end of the semester to replace the final is not too bad, just make sure you start well in advance. No mandatory homework but do them to understand the material. Short quizzes a week, use this to boost your grade

Damon's lectures are pretty clear, and the homework helps a lot. However, there were 20 quizzes and 2 midterms over the summer, which is an obscene amount. Some of them are really hard. He is extremely fair though, which means if you put in enough work (much more than what is supposed for a 3 credit-hr class), it is possible for you to get an A.

Damon is definitely the best professor I've had at Tech. He gives you a short quiz every day, but they extra credit questions. If you read and pay attention, your quiz average will be over 100. His tests are very fair and lectures are very engaging. If you put in a little bit of effort every day, you will EASILY make an A.
Damon was one of my favorite professors at Tech. His class is a lot of work, but you will get out what you put in. Genuinely cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Damon is one of the BEST professors I've ever had. He genuinely cares about the success of his students. He gives a clear outline on how to do well in the class and if you follow it you will get an A. But, Go to office hours!! He will sit down and work problems with you and answer questions until you understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Damon was a really great professor who genuinely cares about his students. He gives "fun" quizzes which are pretty easy but you have to go to class. He gives clear guidelines and what you should be doing in order to do well in the class. Go to office hours and make him know your name. He does final grade replacement which saved a lot of people.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Truly has a passion for the topic and cares about the students. Most classes start with pop quizzes based on the previous lecture. There are two midterms, each worth 20%, very reasonable questions. Not hard to get an A as long as you don't skip class! Final group project is 25% of final grade, still very reasonable difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's fair, but tough. Very charismatic, but is very strict about grading. If you put in the effort (and I mean effort), then his class will be enjoyable. Beware of "Fun Quizzes" that account for a significant portion of your grade. If you go to class, study, and do the (optional) homework, then you will be fine. If you skip on on of these, you fail
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Damon is one of the most caring professors that I have had at Tech. He makes you work for your grade, but he wants his students to do well. He holds office hours each week and is willing to answer questions and work with you. He always gives pop quizzes, but if you attend class and do what he says they aren't hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors at Tech. Very understanding and caring. He definitely makes you work for your grade, but its not hard to make a good grade in the class. Hes really intense at times, so if you like to keep quiet and not participate, you should probably take someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Pretty intense. Kinda scary in class but if you read and do the hws you should be fine. Only gave 3-5 min for quizzes and by the end of the class they were pretty hard. Was helpful in office hrs. Will definitely make you work for your grade. Didnt give much partial credit so be warned
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is a great teacher. I took him as an 8 am for the summer, and I never fell asleep in his class. I'm sure that I have fallen asleep in every class besides his, regardless of the time of the day. His lectures are specific, and he always keeps you on your toes. However, he is a great and funny guy and incorporates that in his lectures. quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs. His test questions are weighted so that you will make a C if you miss the hardest question. His final is also weighted to be almost 70% of your grade. There are much better and more fair professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Took him over the summer. Daily quizzes count for 25% of your class grade and many of the questions are "Wow"problems meaning that you will not be able to solve them within the time frame given. His tests are way too difficult for an introductory class. I recommend looking into other professors for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Daily quiz count for 25% of the grade and they are not easy. Tests are much harder than the practice tests. He talks super fast. He always calls people randomly during the class and asks questions that no one knows the answer.

By far my favorite professor in the ISyE department. Really makes you earn your grade, but he also makes you want to do well. There are tons of pop quizzes, but if you review before class you should be fine.

Dr. Stern is amazing. His lectures are so amazing, and you can tell he is really passionate about the class. His examples during class keep you engaged and this was genuinely one of my favorite classes I took at Tech. Test questions comes from lectures as long as you go and study a little you will be fine.
After completing 5 in-class assignments, you never need to come to class. The tests can be self-studied using the slides in a few hours the night before. Very easy class.

He is a very fun/engaging lecturer and I enjoyed the content. Some tests questions were tricky and he would add in minor details that he would only say in class. The final consisted of some of the hardest questions taken from the 4 midterms, but if you go to his office hours to review your tests it will be easy.

Dr. Stern gave great lectures. He does a lot of story-telling to keep the lectures engaging. Beware of the random attendance checks. His assignments didn't take long to complete. Exams covered material discussed in class, so if you study and remember the material, you will pass :)
Dr. Stern is one of the best profs at TECH!

Dr. Stern is very good at making the lectures engaging and adding humor. Very little work outside of class, the assignments are very easy and not very time consuming, and the exams are over the lecture content. Attendance isn't mandatory but he does give in class assignments sometimes. You can miss a few without hurting your grade. Would take again

Dr. Stern is very fun to listen to and adds lighthearted humor to his lectures to keep them engaging! He always makes sure everyone is on the same page before moving on and never makes anyone feel outed for asking a question. Just make sure to go to class because most of the test material will be pulled from lectures! I would absolutely take again!

Great prof. Technically not mandatory attendance, but there are several random in-class assignments (only 5 get graded, the rest get dropped so missing several lectures will not hurt you). Tests are straight from his slides that are on Canvas, with just a few questions from lectures that you can usually guess correctly.

I took PSYC 1101 with him. Attendance was not mandatory but there were random participation assignments given throughout the year. He gives very engaging lectures so attending class is pretty fun. I went to lecture often so exams were not very difficult. I would highly recommend taking this professor for a great time in introductory psych!

Attendance isn't mandatory, but the lectures were the best part of this course! I spent maybe an hour outside of class otherwise: his lectures were clear with great analogies and examples. There are random in-class participation grades. Great professor who makes a memorization-heavy class really enjoyable.
Best prof ever

Dr. Stern is easily my favorite lecturer in my time at Tech. His lectures were fun and engaging, and his assignments were directly tailored to them (he also posted all his powerpoints, but they don't quite have the same depth as his lecture). Assignments were all doable, and overall the class was awesome. 100% recommend.

Dr. Stern makes every lecture fun and memorable! I genuinely enjoy that class and look forward to it. The lectures are very engaging and interesting. A lot of information is covered in a short time, but exams and assignments are pretty straight forward. Be sure to keep track of dates as he does not give reminders often
Stern should be a go-to for anyone taking intro Psych. Transformed what could have been a tedious, memorization-heavy class into a pretty decent time overall. Cool dude.

Funny professor, engaging lectures. Everything is clear and on the slides making the tests fairly straightforward if you can just process that information. Work is minimal, basically just 30 min per week outside of showing up to lectures.

Great lectures, even though not technically mandatory, show up anyways

Easy class. Weekly short reflections, occassional in-class assignments, 4 larger assignments, and 4 hours required research participation, but it's all very low effort. Exams are multiple choice + fill in the blank. Exam 2 has a low average, not because it is harder as Stern claims, but because he gives no reminder or announcement for it.

William Stern is the best professor I've ever had at GT and inspired me to get a PSYC minor. Social Psychology, specifically was amazing. He covers a lot of material yet still keeps it engaging and easy to understand.

Easily one of the best professors I've ever had. Dr. Stern made me excited to learn about psychology every week through interesting, informative, and entertaining lectures. He's incredibly charismatic and his lectures are quite clear. Attend lectures and you'll do well on all the exams.

Dr. Stern is a very enthusiastic lecturer who uses modern and relevant examples to teach the concepts his class covers. He covers all of the test material in his lectures and always takes time to address questions as thoroughly as he can. He also holds review sessions which double as extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Stern is an amazing professor! His lectures are incredible (textbook is available but definitely not needed if you pay attention to lectures) and entertaining. Would definitely take the class again!

i had him for social psyc. and loved it. it's an easy but informative class, just be careful with assignment deadlines, as he won't always remind you. extra credit is awarded for doing well in review sessions, but you probably won't need it. he's understanding with a lot of personality.

Prof. Stern is pretty good at teaching the content. Lectures can be a bit content-heavy but he uses a lot of pictures and anecdotes to make it easier to process. Participation isn't mandatory in the sense that he takes attendance, but on random days he will give an in-class assignment and some exam questions ask about examples he only gave in class

Prof Stern is a fun prof to take any psychology class with. In social psyc, if you attend the lectures, study for the midterms and the final, and turn in all the assignments on time, you will succeed. His lectures are very clear and the papers are quite easy. Just put in your side of the effort and you will succeed!

Dr. Stern is a great professor! Grades consist of short reflections, random in class activities, 4 short assignments ~500 words during the semester, and 4 research hours obtained by surveys or alt. assignments if

Professor Stern is a great professor! He cares for his students and is very accommodating. He also makes lectures fun and adds a healthy competition in class. Quizzes are pretty decent and not many assignments in class. I actually learned in this class without taking much pressure at all.
I uhhhh think this uhhhh class is uhhhh pretty uhhh buns uhhh don't uhh take this uhhh if you uhh want a uhh good gpa.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very Monotone, and very quiet professor. Used to finish lectures 30-45 minutes early. However, class participation dwindled from 300 students (plus waitlist) to about 10 students. Professor is very hard to listen to and learn information from. TAs + other professor were great.

This class is free no matter who is teaching it. I think most people finished with an A pretty easily. Weiching is a very quiet professor so lectures aren't that useful, but the quizzes were fair and the TAs responded quickly on Ed.

The lectures were: uninformative, uninteresting, and difficult to understand. The slides were vague and did not help with algorithms or a general AI understanding. The projects oftentimes were due around the time all of the content was covered in lecture, making them difficult to complete early. Quizzes were always a gamble.

He's probably a smart guy, but not a great teacher. I just watch CS 188 videos on Youtube. This year they introduced quizzes for the first time, and the quizzes aren't that bad if you just watch the videos.
I got offers at Nvidia, Amazon, Citadel, and JaneStreet after taking this class with Weiching Ma. Thank you!

Please do not take this guy. He could be an expert in his field, but the problem is you don't know what he's talking about. He is so mind numbing and boring. I've seen sessions where less than 10 people are in class. The only reason people show up to class is due to the attendance quizzes.
Um just look at the berkely videos if you have to take this guy
All the people writing positive comments for this guy are joking. Don't take this guy please.

Boring and does a horrible job of communicating the complex topic that they put him in charge of teaching. 5 people out of about 350 show up to his classes on the days that he doesn't force us to come to class. He mumbles through everything and does not explain anything in sufficient depth for you to answer the quizzes. Watch the Berkeley videos.

Like the other true comments say here, all the good comments on Weiching Ma are likely fake or made as a joke. On a real note, Professor Ma is arguably the worst professor I've had at Georgia Tech yet. He clearly doesn't care about his students' understanding of the content and frankly can barely speak English. Seriously, do not take this guy.
Every single good review you see is not written by a student. No student in class thinks he is good at what he does
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He writes his own reviews and spams good reviews. Do not take his class.
This guy writes his own reviews

I, ummmmm, think he is, ummmmmm, a great professor.

He knows, um, his, um stuff, ummm, very well.

um, so yeah. this is the rating

Probably the best lecture prof I have had at Tech. Every day I was excited to show up because his lectures on AI were so inspirational. If you can choose any professor, choose Weiching Ma. This class is a slam dunk. The quizzes are weekly but after the lectures and he basically gives all the answers.
Dont listen to the poor review, students leave this class with an in-depth understanding of Artificial Intelligence and a deep appreciation for modern technology.
Good stuff

The 5 star reviews you see is probably fake. No human would ever type like that so its either him writing reviews on himself or he is getting someone else to do so on behalf of him. Don't take his class, monotone voice sounds like he is just reading off a script, not interactive at all and hard to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Weiching Ma is a really bad lecturer and seems as if he doesn't bother to try to help students understand the fundamentals of this class.

Prof. Ma transformed CS3600 from a challenging AI course into an incredible learning journey. He broke down immensely complex topics into easily digestible bits. He really does have a gift for turning lectures about artificial intelligence into real intelligence! Weekly quizzes were also super easy, basically just the lecture slides. Easy A.

Weiching Ma is very passionate about teaching Artificial Intelligence to students with a basic computer science background. This course is very beginner friendly, only requiring a Python background, and TAs teach students how to use the environments required to do homeworks. Each homework is explicitly explained in lecture.

Horrible lecturer. I'd rather hit my head on a wall for an hour and 15 minutes than attend his lecture when the only content he covers is “ ummmm uhhhh ummm… uhhhh”. Spare yourselves some brain cells and take a different professor. Also the homework is just unrelated completely. terrible class. TAs unorganized too.

For 3600, Weicheng Ma is probably an average professor. The class is well-structured enough that the professor doesn't have too much of an impact. However, he kept ending class after 20-30 mins 
(for a 90 min class) so I eventually just stopped going to lecture. He has the tendency to be quieter so make sure you sit near the front row.

Prof. Xiong is a good professor who makes lectures enjoyable. The class is straightforward, with weekly assignments due Fridays and two tests. Assignments focus on HTML, CSS, and JS for data visualization, while tests cover lecture material. Attendance is technically "required", but slides are posted online, so it's manageable if you miss class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Super chill professor, she has interesting lectures which are easy to follow, especially with the countless examples she gives. The homeworks are intriguing but not too hard and the labs are available through Git and pretty self-explanatory. Only 2 tests and the class ends before Thanksgiving. Overall would recommend.

Cindy Xiong is a good presenter. Most hws were about coding in HTML, CSS, and Javascript and working with D3. They weren't too bad but we weren't given any instruction during class on how to use D3 so you have to figure it out on your own. There are two exams, no finals. The class finishes before Thanksgiving so that is nice. Would recommend class.

Dr. Xia is caring, yes, but it can be hard to stay engaged during his lectures. I might be biased because I had lecture at Kendeda, and it was hard to understand him due to a combination of his thick accent and loud air vents in the building. The TAs were helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy and good lectures, though they are long and packed with info. He is not the best at explaining concepts or helping with homework during office hours but hes genuine and is there to help. Tests are hard but he is a very generous grader which helps a lot. overall good

Shuman is an excellent choice for Statics. Lectures are done on whiteboard and are very engaging. Explains concepts really well and goes over old physics/math concepts if you need. Homework is on WileyPlus and takes 2-3 hours a week max. Exams are 88% but are very easy if you do the homeworks. TAs are also great if you even need help.

Shumans lectures were very good, he could simplify concepts into digestible ideas. I took in the summer asynchronously, 88% of grade comes from tests (2 midterms and 1 final), 12% comes from HW. HW wasn't too much, typically one HW a week through wileyPLUS. Provided practice exams and a practice final. Great professor to take statics with.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quite good at lecturing. Very kind and caring. Gives you all you need to succeed and doesn't make the class too hard. If you are unsure which Statics professor to go with, Shuman is a safe bet.

Amazing professor. Made things easy to understand with examples. Make sure to do recitation problems, they're harder than test problems. Tests resembled the homework and were easier than some of the other professors tests Ive heard of. Taking statics with Xia is a fun class and easy A
Super nice and wholesome professor who is always enthusiastic about teaching
Professor Xia is really great at lecturing and made the material easy to understand. The tests are also very doable if you study.

The cutest man you will ever meet. He is so nice and is also incredibly invested in his student's success. The HW's are online and only have three attempts so be sure to be careful. The exams are generally pretty easy (good thing because they make up most of your grade). His vibes give off adorable grandpa (he is young though lol).
Overall a very good professor.

Would definitely recommend Professor Xia. His lectures had lots of examples and he explained everything very well. Gave lots of practice before the exams, and the exams were fairly easy as long as you understood all the material. Overall, Professor Xia was great!
Dr. Xia was extremely enthusiastic about the course material and gave easy homework sets (WebAssign) and exams. Lectures were clear and concise, based mostly on statics principles.

Took him for 2001 and 3001 - amazing professor, great at explaining concepts. Generous grader and he does curve. He's honestly amazing at taking a hard class like def bods and making it digestible. Best prof I've had at Tech in 2 years here. His 3001 was 100% exams (no graded HW) so make sure you're practicing consistently. Must attend in person!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Even though the lecture was online professor Xia was very enthusiastic about the material and always willing to help out his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Hard course, but kind professor will help you to face and understand it. He always give a quick feedback.
Dr. Xia is a great professor and made Fracture Mechanics very interesting. I wish I could take more classes with him. He answered emails very quickly and his tests were average difficulty.
Tough course, great teacher

Super amazing teacher. Had him for statics and def bods, and he was really great for both. Everything is very manageable, he explains very clearly, and is extremely understanding and accessible outside class.
His tests are fair, and there is not a lot of homework. He grades pretty easily as well. He is a very nice guy but his lectures tend to get pretty boring since the material is a little bland.

Professor Xia makes the information very understandable and is very interested in the subject he teaches. The homeworks due are doable and good practice for the midterm and final. Both are worth around 80%, but are pretty fair. His curve at the end is pretty helpful as well. He makes cutoffs for A,B,C,D,F based on the scores at the end. Great prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lecture are kind of boring, but that's really the only con. He makes the class super easy and slow-paced (compared to my friends in other statics classes) which is really nice.

Really good professor for statics. He went to the effort to paint a whiteboard in his house to teach us when we had to switch to online learning. Overall great professor. Do the homework and use his short study guides (has similar problems to the tests).

I took his class for statics and he was definitely easier than the other statics professors my friends had. His lectures ran over time by a couple minutes sometimes, but they were very thorough (rather dry though). Tests were lightly graded, and difficulty was reflective of the in-class examples. TLDR: Show up to lecture, study examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best professor I have taken in Tech. Very smart guy, makes everything simple and grades generously. Always helpful and makes def bods eaaaassyyy. His problem sets have answers online from old textbook pdfs. My advice: attend every class (you actually learn) and take notes. You won't even have to study much if you do this.

Took him for summer online course. He was one of the best professors I have taken at Tech. Gave good lectures, didn't waste any time, solved example problems in class, gave fair quizzes. Not too many homework but could take some time, but he was always available to help even via email. Would recommend to everyone!
Good choice for a statics professor. Makes everything simple. Not too hard
Great guy and great class. Makes learning Def Bods bearable!
Overall an ok prof. Communication can be hard because sometimes because her native language is chinese. The lectures are very long, a lot of self study to get a good grade.

she def cares but sometimes things get lost in communication. lectures are boring and long and tend to focus too much time on things that dont matter while the important parts get looked over quickly. she is always willing to help. the tests are fair but hard. she tells u what the frq is on and the mc is just a gamble that you hope and pray on.

She's a great person, but her native language is Chinese, so she's not very good at explaining concepts in English. Sometimes kids would ask questions and she would just repeat what she said earlier. If you're fluent in Chinese, there were some kids who apparently got a lot from learning with her one-on-one. Otherwise, self-study.

This lady does NOT want to be teaching and she makes sure you know it. I don't think a single ounce of original thoughts went into her course materials. Everything is either lifted from previous semesters or from MIT. Terrible lectures and the slides barely help. The exams have no rights being as hard as they were given the teaching quality

Hardest class I've taken so far, and I had to take this class for my SEC minor. The lectures are extremely unclear, most of my learning was done in the TA office hours, which were very helpful. Exams were pretty difficult, but do-able, and consistently had averages in the 60's. The last programming assignment required in-depth C++ knowledge.
Terrible lectures and course management. Clear lack of interest in teaching or student outcomes.

Grad and undergrad sections have exactly the same hw and exams - this is a grad-level course. Prof assumes you already have extensive CS knowledge and is awful at explaining complex concepts - as a CS minor, this is the hardest class I have ever taken. If you are forced to take this class, be prepared to put in an insane amount of effort.

Expect 100% self learning. I did self-learned a lot from the programming assignment. But the material is poorly organized and not explained clearly. You can't learn anything from class because it's mostly rephrasing the slides. Take Srinivas's class if you can, you need his notes to understand the material anyway.

Very cool prof, but the course structure is terrible. Packs too much information per lecture. If you are taking many courses or have major research priorities, this course will leave you learning most things very superficially, except MPI. Programming assignments (26% of grade) are challenging & graded unnecessarily strictly (no partial credit).

Frankly confused by some of the positive ratings here... 
1. PA2 was mismanaged, where a 100 on the autograder didn't lead to 100 in the assignment (that wasn't made clear)
2. Concepts in lectures not explained rigorously, which should be expected for a class like HPC

This was the first time that I saw students get penalized for trying to answer questions on an exam. She gives partial credit if you leave the answer blank however if you try to answer it and are even slightly incorrect you get ZERO credit. Make it make sense.

Profs lectures are technical and fast-paced, so you have to absolutely lock in or else you will get lost. As such, I felt that I learned so much about HPC through this course. Projects and HWs were challenging, but not ridiculously hard. Exams easier than HW. Great prof overall, would def recommend this course with her if you are interested in HPC.

HPC is a very very difficult class. Prof. Xu had great subject knowledge and would frequently listen to student feedback, but assigned problems that I believe were more difficult than necessary to learn the course content. Overall I think she did a pretty solid job for her first semester teaching this course.

Extremely hard professor. After the final, the class average was 69% (before being curved). 70% exams, rest homeworks and projects. Normally classes with high percentage weight on exams have easier homeworks and projects. This class, the homework and projects were harder than the exams. Avoid if possible.

I admittedly did not put as much effort as I could have for this class. However, the class itself was not at all enjoyable. He is extremely hard to focus on and does not post his handwritten notes (only the template), so class attendance is a must. He was nice, but not sure I would take this class again.

Class is not nearly as hard as people make it out to be. You just have to study. Personally I didn't really learn well during lecture because he would run through examples, but that's just my learning style. He was really good at explaining things you didn't understand though, and very accessible outside of class.

His lectures are straightforward as long as you pay attention and his guided notes are great.  There are a fair amount of online homework assignments, but they are broken into 4 sets that are due at the day of each midterm.  Tests are usually the same level of difficulty as the material covered in class too.  Take him for a manageable A

He is a very sweet guy. It's hard to focus in his class & lectures are boring, so most ppl struggle. I heard exams used to be very similar to the HW, but not this sem. A lot of ppl in class struggled for exams, few finished them before the time ran out. If you find acct interesting and don't mind self-studying a lot outside of class, take him.

reviews.comment: Guided notes like accounting 1, its hard if u don't lock in every once in a while, he's a solid teacher

He is very sweet, but his lectures are rather boring, I find myself zoning out quite often in his class. The class structure is test heavy, with the 3 highest exam grades counting for most of your grade. Random attendance quizzes so if you miss a class you could miss out on points. Memorize formulas and review heavily to do well on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: boring boring boring but if you do the homeworks you should be fine

I took this class in Fall 2020 (corona semester) and it was pretty simple. 4 homework assignments but they take up a lot of time. 4 exams which are medium to hard. Definitely use your resources for this class and you will be fine. 1-2 extra credits and a case study.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice. straightforward teaching style. Must memorize the formulas and how to do examples from his packets, and youll do fine. Tests are almost impossible if you dont. Study hard for the tests. He curves up at the end based on natural breaks in class averages. Very nice and willing to answer questions.

Suuuuuper boring and accounting is already a hard topic to make interesting. One of the worse professors I've had but it's hard to find someone at tech who can really teach accounting well and fair, so just bite the bullet and take him if he's the only one teaching the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took accounting 2 with Dr. Kuang and really enjoyed the class. He is very friendly and approachable and definitely shows that he cares about the students in his classes and wants them to succeed. The class is mostly built around working through handouts that he provides in class that are mostly what make up the tests. Overall great professor!

Not the easiest class but everything you need to know for the tests is presented in class. He provides notes that you can fill in while following along. Tests are doable and he curves your final grade based on class performance. I had an 87.7 and still got an A

Professor is super nice, accommodating, and shows genuine interest in the subject.
Grade is just 4 projects and a few homework throughout.
I didn't learn tha much more about DSP (Heavy lifting via ECE4270) and while there were interesting concepts of the applications thereof, it wasn't presented in an interesting manner.
Clear message always! Willing to take her course again!

Nice person and always willing to help, but she does nothing to make boring classes exciting. Graded on a couple projects and homeworks that were really easy so you won't learn much. The extra credit assignments are really interesting and everyone could easily get over 100% in the class. The class was hybrid but she made it completely virtual.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Xingxing's lectures were some of the highest quality I've seen. His HW was really difficult, and he only gave us around a week to do each one. The pace of the class was also quite fast. However, he was extremely caring and considerate, and the whole class able to bond really well with each other.
Weeks of MW and midterms in a row. Less than a week between assigning the HW and the due date. Great lecturer, but disorganized and grades cruelly

He's a really nice professor who knows the subject well and tries to help students as much as possible but the course (Graph Theory) was simply brutal. I had a 4.0 before this class and got a C on it - the final was simply impossibly hard.

He explains concepts quite clearly. The homework problems are pretty challenging unlike what I have experienced from other classes at Tech. It's nice how he pushes for us to use formalized mathematical notation so that we would have the "same language" as mathematicians. This is probably my most challenging class, but I hope to get a lot out of it!
Dr. Yu was always very thorough in his lectures. In office hours he was very helpful too. I was never bored during thermo with him.

Organized teaching methods, follows textbook. Homework load is big but will train you for tests. curves at the end if he felt that the class need that. Take him if you can, overall he is great and very sweet teacher.

Yu went primarily along with the Graph Theory text, but he supplemented it well with lectures and pruned unecessary sections. The clarity of the lectures and the problem solving made this class great, but with a slightly higher than average workload. I highly recommend it to Math and Computer Science majors.

Still taking this course but really like the research presentation portion of the course and the D3.js labs are really useful. Assignments can be a little tough to understand but Dr. Yang or the ta's are pretty quick to respond to any questions. Just make sure you start assignments early.
Overall really great and interesting course! Really loved the TAs! I recommended the course to a few of my friends as it was really fun doing web development and making visualizations in d3.

Well-run class with clearly graded homeworks, labs, and projects making up most of the grade, tests are tough and memorization heavy. Usually no attendance required, 1 lecture a week and the other day is a coding lab on assignments. Dr. Yang himself is pretty caring, funny, and knowledgeable, and some weeks are very heavy, but overall great prof

This teacher is known to have practice exams and as long as you do them you should get an A. However, fall 2025 was the first semester in 2 years that he changed the content of the tests and quizzes. This cooked me because I depended on the practice tests.

Lectures were sometimes hard to follow because of his accent. You can figure out the material by watching Sebastian Fernandez, plus diff eq is not a very hard class conceptually. The exams and quizzes were pretty easy. The TAs also grade fairly leniently. Just keep in mind that the final exam is worth a large portion of the grade at 37%.
Never went to lectures, but quizzes and exams weren't too difficult and were similar to the review problems and studio worksheets.
Nice guy, but lectures were useless. 5 quizzes 1 drop, final worth 37%. TAs were very lenient with grading/partial credit.
Chill class. Never went to lecture, just watched Sebastian youtube videos or looked at studio worksheets. Just do all the problems from studio and you're set for exams.

Lectures were not mandatory and, quite honestly, not needed. He has a strong accent, which makes him hard to understand. Studio is 1 point extra credit on your grade if you have 80%+ attendance. Grade is quiz and exam-heavy, but similar to studio practice problems. Sebastian Fernandez on YT if you need more help with the content.

Although lectures were not mandatory and only about 15% of the students showed up, he has passion for teaching and wants his students to follow through and learn. Only downside is his strong accent is hard to understand. Studio is all-or-nothing EC if you have 80%+ attendance. Final is required. Sebastian Fernandez on YT if you need more help.

Lectures are just okay. He's not a bad lecturer, it's just that his notes are really, really thorough. Notes are posted online, which is good. Regardless, I recommend that you show up at the studios because they're super helpful. Questions from studio worksheets are similar in format to those on the quizzes and exams. Grade is quiz/exam heavy.

Went to the first lecture and it was the worst thing I ever sat through, so I didn't go again. Nonetheless, stuido and practice problems are really all you need. Test were weighted heavy but not terrible to get through. Quizzes are what you need to look out for. Sebastian Fernandez is lowkey overrated and not really needed either.

Professor Chen is a very reasonable professor who does his best to make the content interesting even though honestly probably not his fault diffeq is just kind of an easy class. He's pretty accessible out of class and just generally a reasonable guy even for accommodations. Liked his class and this prof
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Chen is a really nice person, but his lectures could be pretty hard to understand. I personally learned better from studio/Google. Tests are pretty straightforward- no difficult computation or edge cases or intentional tricks. 3 homework questions a week, extra credit for CIOS/studio attendance, but heavily weighted final so be careful.
Don't need to go to class, Seb fernandez + studio worksheets + review problems and you'll get an A in the class with ease.

This professor randomly decided to make his exams twice the length of every other 2552 section halfway through the semester. He is frankly pretty rude and unhelpful during lecture as well. Sebastian Fernandez videos are the only reason most of this class knows what is happening. Take a different section. Not too crazy of a class with a better prof.

Didn't attend many lectures, but learned almost everything through Sebastian Fernandez and studio. Chen's lecture notes were very long and hard to decipher. The 50-question review packet is really helpful, and exams were mostly very easy.
Lectures were boring and useless, but the tests were exactly like the studio worksheets. Definitely take this professor, it's probably the easiest A out of all the diff eq sections.

XYC's lectures aren't the most interesting, honestly you can learn everything from the studios. Final is worth 37% of the grade, 2 midterms worth 33%. Not too difficult of a class, but its also diff eq.

bad guy but W option for diff eq if for an A. boring lectures, kinda rude. otherwise class is free. 2 test 17% each, 37% final, 5 quiz 1drop 24%, 15 hw 2drop 5%. many pdfs of old test, quiz, final out there and don't change much each year. has practice Qs on canvas. go to studio and watch sebastian fernandez on yt. very easy, confident i got an A
lectures can be boring, but he cares about the topic. sebastian fernandez videos help
He doesn't speak English hard to understand

Professor Chen is a very dry lecturer and can come across as rude. It doesn't really matter, though, since Sebastian Fernandez on YouTube is a great teacher so there's no need to go to class. Tests and quizzes were very similar to the practice problems and were very fair.
Chen himself is an awful lecturer. Watch Sebastian Fernandez videos on YouTube instead of going to lecture. His quizzes and exams are super easy and short so I would take Diff Eq with him if you can.

SUPER EASY. Watch Sebastian Fernandez videos, no need to go to class. Quizzes and tests very fair, tests based on quizzes and studio worksheets. Final exam based on past tests and quizzes, everything very fair. Do the studio worksheets and you'll get an A.

Considering you can learn 2552 from Sebastian Fernandez, you don't need to go to lectures for diff eq. What makes XYC a good pick is just that his tests are incredibly easy for this course. Take him if you can, the material itself is not hard and XYC does nothing to make it harder.

I never went to a lecture, but the studio sections are super helpful. The TA's will teach you how to work through the problems and the quizzes are the same as the studio sheets. The exams are also exactly like the studio. Don't go to lecture unless you want to and just go to studio - the class is not hard if you lock in in studio.
Took this over summer, didn't go to most of the lectures and learned most of the content from Sebatian Fernandez and his notes. Quizzes and Tests were pretty easy.

Definitely take this class with Chen. His exams and quizzes were fairly easy, compared to the review problems we did. Lots of partial credit. He has an accent but honestly, you don't even need to go to lecture if you pay attention in studio.

Dr. Chen is a great professor. His tests and quizzes are extremely easy, and they are easier than the review problems he gives in his big packet. Sometimes he yaps in his lectures, but he is very thorough. Very kind guy.

Lectures are slow and boring and you can learn everything from the lecture slides and studios. Sudios are up to 2% extra credit if you attend. The review packet is really helpful but also way harder than anything on the quizzes/tests.

If you have a great TA, you can learn the majority of the material just in studio. Chen's lecture slides are also quite comprehensive. His tests are much easier than the studio worksheets and his review packet, although I found the final to be a bit of a curveball.

Diffeq with Chen has to be the easiest class I've ever taken at Tech. The class material is intuitive and Chen's quizzes and tests are completely free. Lectures aren't great but anything you don't understand can be found on the internet and you'll be fine. TAs will typically give the 2% EC at the end regardless of studio attendance.

Professor Chen is the most straightforward math professor I have had at Tech in terms of expectations and grading. He likes to go into detail in lecture but if you understand all his review problems you will do very well on exams. The only con I can think of is the fact that grading is done out of only 3-4 exams with minimal or no homework grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chen is perfect if you want an A and dont wanna go to lecture. His lectures are extremelely hard to pay attention to: boring, monotone, thick accent, not engaging, and waste time explaining simple algebra. He has good notes you can teach yourself with and the tests/quizzes are mega easy which is all you can ask for from a math prof a gt tbh.

The lecture is recorded and posted on Canvas so you don't have to physically attend the lecture. Quiz and Midterm problems are quite easy. The Final is very similar to the problems that appeared in midterms and quizzes. Studio attendance counts towards the final grade (maximum of 2%). You can definitely get an A in this course.

Probably one of the easiest diff eq professors. Lecture attendance is not required and all the material can be learned from TAs in studio and/or Sebastian Fernandez on Youtube. Quizzes and tests are similar to provided review problems but way easier.

Take him for diff eq. Easiest, most straight forward class. Not much variety in tests year-to-year. Never went to lecture, only went to studio. Hes not an amazing professor but the content is not tricky so you'll do fine studying with friends for exams/quizzes.

A breather compared to any other math class I've taken, but only because of Chen. Makes quizzes and exams super easy. Lecture is very long and not engaging, so watch recorded lectures at 2x speed. Sebastian Fernandez is helpful, but quizzes/test/homeworks are incredibly similar to lecture. Studio is extremely helpful.

Lectures are uninsightful, robotic, and difficult to learn from. Learn from TA/Sebastian Fernandez. Diffeq class material is easy to grasp, it's a mix of linear & calc and Chen tests us on basic calc2/integration by parts only. Final had one basic Euler's Method question, the other nine q's were a lot like ones from past quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All his questions on quizzes/exams are mild and doable

Not really difficult if you review the slides he posts on Canvas and lecture videos. Studios will give u added 2 points to your final grade which is great. He's grading criteria isn't too bad; on quizes and test he'd give you partial credit for questions.  I recommend going to studio sessions which will give u extra credit points and preparation
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: not the most entertaining lecturer, but he teaches you what is needed. look at past exams for study materials and attend studio! assignments/exams are very fair and are not designed to trick you

I personally did not find this class difficult at all (scored a 100 on everything) but I also used every single resource given to me because I enjoyed it (textbook, lectures, recitations). Just show your work on quizzes/exams and make sure to follow submission guidelines for end of the semester extra credit.

Professor Chen is great because he's easy, his grading is very favorable. The content can be difficult at times but the tests and quizzes are super simple and based on the problems done in class. Also if you want extra help just look up Sebastian Fernandez on Youtube. He's can be difficult to understand but follow his slides and you're fine.

Terrible lectures, I watched Sebastian Fernandez's MATH 2552 lecture series for the whole semester and was fine. Other than that, quizzes/exams are generally straightforward. Final exam was a little harder than expected, but it was fine because all previous quizzes/midterms were pretty doable.

Professor Chen is a solid choice for this class. His lectures are a bit lack luster; reviewing his amazing slide deques and finishing his comprehensive practice problem set should be enough to do well. His exams and quizzes are easy given when I took his class in Fall 2020, he he allotted a lot of time for them and they were open note.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Like most math professors at Tech, he doesn't really care about teaching. If you read the textbook though, you'll be fine. No need to attend lecture because he has a thick accent. Quizzes and tests are pretty easy.

Diff eq is not really hard but it was a breeze with Dr. Chen. His review packet prepares you well for quizzes/exams, being that if you understood those, the real questions would often be an easier and reduced version. Super active on Piazza, on top of things, clear grading, just take him for diff eq if you don't want a hard time.
Very fair and understanding.

Very bad at lecturing with an extremely heavy accent. Very hard to understand. Tests and quizzes aren't too bad. Heavily relied on other sources for my knowledge. Take him but don't expect to learn from him.

Doesn't know how to properly teach material to students by any means. His dull math lectures consisted of reading off of a prewritten notes sheet. I stopped going to lecture after the first week. Watch Sebastian Fernandez on YouTube and you too will never return to lecture. I would take again because of how the class is structured.

Chen is a terrible explainer. Majority of the class never attended his online synchronous lectures, but instead used YouTube videos and recitation to learn the material. He was lenient with changing the homework due date when needed! His homeworks, tests, and quizzes are pretty easy (thus why many ppl passed without learning through him).
He's extremely diligent about responding on Piazza. If you ever feel stuck, consider viewing Sebastian Fernandez's channel on YouTube.

Chen is not the best professor, but his class is the easiest class I have ever taken. Just review the lecture notes a day or so before the quizzes and tests and you'll be fine. Most of his test and quiz questions are ripped straight from his lecture notes.

Dr. Chen is a great lecturer, but you may have trouble understanding his accent. However, it should be fairly easy to understand after a few classes. The problems in the notes are fairly similar to the questions on his quizzes and exams. If you show up to all the lectures and recitations, you should not have any problems getting the A.

Chen has a little bit of a heavy accent, but you get used to it quickly. He has the entire schedule, hw problems, and lecture slides posted from day 1 which is very nice. His lectures are fast paced, but it's fine because the notes are available on his website. His quizzes and tests are very easy, and aren't meant to trip you up on old calculus.
I didn't attend a single lecture. I just watched recitations and did the worksheets and it was an easy A.

Chen is honestly a good professor. For 2552 the exams and quizzes were pretty easy but the best thing you can do for yourself in this class is look up Sebastian Fernandez on YouTube and use his videos. Did this all semester and didn't even need to go to lecture or recitation.
If we read and understand the slides he gives, then it is not hard to get an A. Quizzes and tests are pretty close to the examples in his slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I was worried because I wasn't following him in class. Look up Sebastian Fernandez on youtube. He covers the entire course as an old GT TA. Lectures are useless. Homework takes no time. Tests and quizzes are extremely simple. He uses 3 different grading weights to determine what gives you the best overall grade and uses that.

Go to recitation and that's all you need to do for this class. Tests are really easy, lecture is boring. He's not the best lecturer but his notes are really well-organized and he gives a lot of review material too.
His quizzes and tests are easy overall. Lecture is not useful, recitation and online notes are all you need to do well. Easiest math class I've taken.

This was the easiest math class I have ever taken. Prof Chen's lectures are not entertaining and sometimes even confusing, but all of the quizzes and exams are a super easy. At the beginning of the semester he states that whatever final grade we get will not be curved, but you understand why when the average for the final is an A.

Didn't go to lecture after the first month, recitation and the occasional online notes are all you need. Almost always uses the same questions for exams/quizzes as previous semesters, so if you have a friend who has taken him before it really helps. Easy A but you might leave the class not feeling like you really know differential equations.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Chen is a REALLY bad lecturer, but at least his class is really easy. Tests and quizzes were not too complex. Go to recitation/studios, do some studying on your own (watch Sebastain Fernandez' Diffeq videos on YouTube) and you'll be straight.
Class is extremely boring. Go to recitation for learning the material, and you will prob get an A. The tests usually ask for basic understanding of the material

Don't even count on going to lectures. Cuz, it straight up boring. Easy math class by far, just 2 midterms and an exam. Hw set every week but just 3 questions with unlimited attempts. Textbook not needed, and recitations are a great way to learn the material fast. Easy work ;)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Chen is really underrated. Exams are a joke as long as you have an idea of the material. Seriously, take him if you want an A.

He got bad reviews since taking away crib sheets and assigning homework now apparently; Not best lecturer but still easiest class I've taken at Tech. He gives HW but its literally 3 webwork questions w/unlimited tries. Test questions are exactly like exam review sheets. Do HW, review sheets, and watch sebastians 2552 youtube vids (no txtbk needed).
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very straight forward. Easy to understand. Lots of HW. HW gets super tough, but not mandatory. Tests are extremely simple compared to hw. If you can do the test review well, you can easily get an A. Pros: Very straight forward. Easy tests .Cons: kinda tough to approach or reach out of class.

Really poor lecturer and tough grader. No one attends his lectures and your performance in the class is completely reliant on how good your TA is. No crib sheets for any exams, including the final. Mandatory homework is also given now.

The worst professor at tech. Almost the entirety of my recitation skips lecture at this point. I wouldn't be surprised if there was a single digit number of people who go. I learned more by playing tetris in his lecture. He doesn't respond to emails, and will try to make things harder if people are doing well. Honestly, he shouldn't have his job.

He gives homework and took away the crib sheets for the tests and made them harder overall. Despite that, nobody goes to his lecture because it feels like a waste of time and most of us were taught by our TA.

Absolutely terrible lecturer. Hard to understand, boring lectures. Hardly anyone attends. Your experience in this class is completely based on your TA. (Mine was also horrible). No crib sheets anymore and tests are harder.
note to everyone, I'm in his class right now (spring 2019) and he now gives homework and no longer allows crib sheets on the exams!

His tests are relatively easy compared to his lectures; I stopped showing up to class after the second week and got through the tests pretty easily. Final is a bit harder, as can be expected. Going to recitation and knowing how to work his problems (both "assigned" and the sample ones in his lecture notes) helps a lot; homework isn't mandatory
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: His notes are basically his test. He posts his notes on his website so you can go back and look at them. There is nothing but lectures in his class and they can be a bit boring but you get to learn a lot from them. If you go ask for a regrade, you generally get the points back. The posted notes and the crib sheets made this an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Xu Yan Chen knows Differential Equations very well, but he comes off as very rude during office hours. His tests and quizzes are really fair, and as long as you know the required material (on his website), you will get an A. Lecture is pretty much a waste because he will just read off of the power-points which are on his website.

Entire grade is based on tests, quizzes, and the final, so homework is unnecessary. His accent is difficult to understand at first, and honestly there's no point in trying because he's scattered and confusing anyway. Just go to recitation and you'll be fine. You get a 2 sided crib sheet on all tests and quizzes, so still a pretty easy A.

Definitely the easiest Diff eq prof. He recycles a lot of questions from the past for his tests and quizzes. Didnt go to lecture and did well. TA's are crucial though. My Ta was how I learned the material. Final was a bit of a challenge but not too bad.

Once you get used to the accent, you will learn a lot from this guy. Still, Prof Chen is a solid choice for those who are looking to pass without going to lecture. Listen to your TA, and you can get an A. However, I would recommend going to class as well.

Chen's lectures are quite boring, but diff eq is pretty boring too. He does a great job of preparing you to learn the material by doing tons of practice in class. His quizzes and tests are very very straightforward. I just took the final and it was harder than I expected for Chen, but honestly it wasn't difficult compared to other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: he explains pretty clearly what he is expecting you to know. he explains topics clearly, and there are no surprises on tests and quizzes. understand the topics and the class will be easy

Make sure you go to class and write down/take pictures of every one of his handwritten pages of notes so you don't get surprised like I did on one of his quizzes. Grading can be harsh, -30% on one quiz for small things like forgetting to simplify an answer with addition of like terms. Uploaded slides are extremely helpful. Textbook is useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: 2552 is an extremely easy class. If you can easily do the worksheets given in recitation, you can get a 100% on every test and quiz. Lecture isn't necessary, as most slides are uploaded. Recitation isn't necessary either.
Tests are really easy, you don't even need to go to class to learn since the lecture slides are pretty clear. Lectures are basically just problem solving and no theory.

By far one of the easiest classes I've ever taken...I never attended lecture, but I attended all recitations for the worksheets. If you complete all the recitation worksheets and work out the practice exams (which is by far more complicated/requires more work than the actual exam), you will get an easy A. His exams and finals are a joke.
Class was really easy. Only went to recitation. Cannot understand his accent and his teaching is poor.

Dr. Chen explains things clearly in his lectures with plenty of examples. He is engaged with the material each lecture and generally explains concepts very thoroughly. The only thing that he could really improve is how he responds to questions, which he often has difficulty answering.

I loved this professor. This was the easiest class I had in a semester and I learned a ton about differential equations. He's very very good at explaining things and extremely fair in grading. Favorite math professor at tech, would recommend to anyone taking DiffEq
Tests are very easy, homework can sometimes be a little difficult and time consuming. Chen is a pretty good lecturer but it didn't seem like he really liked it when students asked questions.
Not a easy-going prof. Tests are very easy. Recommend to take the class, skip the lecture and study by yourself.

The class itself isn't terribly hard BUT Chen is EXTREMELY inaccessible and inflexible. A friend who had an excuse through the Dean was still not permitted to make up a test, for example and thus failed the class. There's only grades for Midterms (2), quizzes (4), and the final. He gives a 2% recitation bonus.

The class structure itself is very easy to pass and get a good grade in, but Chen himself is an absolutely awful, rude, and pretentious guy who is impossible to have a conversation with. If you're happy learning everything on your own, go ahead and take the class, but expect ZERO help from Chen. I really, really, disliked him.

Pretty clear in lectures but his first language wasn't English, so if you ask a question he might not understand what you mean right away. In any case, his lectures had a lot of practice problems and his tests were way easier than the homework, if you pay attention you'll do really well!

Chen's tests are easy, yet they check your abilities. It is really very easy to get an A in his class for 1552. I strongly recommend (especially if you already know a little about integrals because his accent can be a little difficult to understand). He assigns less homework compared to other profs (though the sums are hard).

good, incredibly fair professor. tests are very straightforward, quizzes are a little harder but do-able. he will drop your lowest quiz, test, or nothing (whichever gives you the highest grade). final is difficult but not ridiculous. not too friendly but respectable. lecture is boring and long but not mandatory.

He is the easiest Integral Calc teacher! He posts all of his lectures online, AND he lets you use a crib sheet on every test or quiz. Class average was 20% higher than all the other sections. His lectures were beneficial and he would crack funny jokes in class. Also, his Asian accent is very clear and was NOT a problem at all. I HIGHLY recommend!
His tests are extremely straightforward and easier than the practice tests he gives.

Take this professor!!! He allows all of your written notes for his pop quizzes and you can use one front-and-back sheet of paper for all of the tests and the final. Plus, his tests are easier than the homework his review worksheets!! This is really rare at Tech! He is not necessarily helpful but he teaches slowly in class. Go to tutoring for help.

You can tell he takes his job seriously and tries to teach so that's good.  However, you tend to learn more in recitation and on your own with homework.  The class itself isn't hard.  His tests are super simple and easy especially after you do his practice tests which are way harder than the actual tests.

Lectures aren't too useful, because he spends them going over his handwritten notes which are already online. For the most part, I learned in recitation and on my own. That said, the class is extremely easy. For each exam he posts a practice test one week before that is almost identical to the actual test. He's a very fair grader too!!
Boring lectures, thick accent, but easy tests. Just do the practice problems and you will get an A.

He is definitely knowledgeable about what he is teaching, but he has a very thick accent and he is not good at answering questions. Whenever someone asks a question, he typically repeats whatever he already said about a topic, but louder and more angrily.
He has a heavy accent and does not know how to explain things very clearly. However, his tests are VERY easy and simple. Just do the practice tests and you'll get an A.
Do yourself a favor and avoid this professor. He is rude, incomprehensible, and downright boring. You will learn NOTHING from this guy.
A pure Mathematician with a deep  understanding of the subject. He could be little more friendly/easy to talk with. Overall he is a good professor.

He likes what he does and it is a good teacher. If you want an A in the class, just do the practice tests and that is it. I have not gone to half of his classes nor recitation but with the practice tests I have managed to get an A on his first 3 tests. His homeworks are online and you can re do them to get a 100 if you do them wrong the first time.

He gave us access to a free online textbook.  There are a few random quizzes(5%) during lectures(easy). Online homework(15%), which took me 2 hours to complete each week. 4 tests(3 worth 15%; lowest 5% and a final(30%).  Chen has an accent, but if you pay attention you'll be able to understand.
He does a have a bit of an accent, not too bad. His tests are easier than other Calc 1 professors and he does a fair job at lecturing. Overall, Not bad.
Easy Class. Made a 97 in the class and I never went to class. Dont ask questions during class or he will yell at you. Take him and do the practice test that are online and you will ace the exam.
He is a very practical teacher plus he's hilarious.Do your Work and you'd get an A.I got a 94 in this class.TAKE HIM.

He's incomprehensible. His lectures are basically useless. He cracks an occasional joke but otherwise, he's very boring. He assigns outrageous homework sets which, if done legitimately, take students 5-6 hours to complete. The tests are admittedly mostly fair, but the final exam is certainly unfair and won't help your grade. Take another professor.

Never went to class. Still got an A. He gives hard study guides to prepare students for the test. get to drop one of 6 quizzes. Best score on your test weighs more into your average than your lower score.
He's hilarious. And if you go to class, there's no reason why you shouldn't do well.

The lectures are not helpful. I learned everything I know about the class through my textbook which is great! The tests are long and you'll have just enough time to complete it if you know the material very well, work fast, and don't make mistakes that need correcting.  Office visits are sometimes helpful.

Very inflexible and stubborn. If you take his class expect to do everything 100% by the book. Shows no trace of any. Might as well have taken class with a robot, except a robot would not be borderline deceptive.

Tests are very similar to the practice tests, and it is easy to do well in the class. One test had a problem not on the practice test which threw me off. He seems to change his grading policy every semester, and he is useless in lecture. I never used the book and learned everything in recitation. He is also very rude when you approach him.

I had Chen for Differential Equations. He's a decent teacher, but not great. His tests are identical to the practice tests and as such, it is very easy to do well in his class. In short, he's an easy professor, but I honestly felt that I only did well because I memorized formulas while not actually learning and understanding the material.
Hard to understand, but it is possible. I never went to lecture because I never got much out of it. He only lectures on concepts and does few problems. I think recitation was way more helpful.

Can't understand him to save your life... the only way I did well is the fact that I did my homework and the tests were exactly like the practice tests... never went to lecture and did ok in the class..

His calc II class was fun.  I sat in the back with my rfiends and made jokes during his lectures, but my friends and I still made A's in his class.  His tests are very similar to the practice tests he posts with answers before each test, and he is pretty approachable.  His english is rough, but his great notes make up for it.  VERY FUNNY.

The best thing about Dr. Chen is that he allows you to use a 'cheat sheet' on the tests, AND drops up to two tests (although the more you drop, the higher the final counts.)  I managed to fail all but one test (because I never studied), get an A on the final, and get a B in the class.  XD
He's a really good teacher but the accent's hard to follow. The practice tests are just like the real ones so if you study them, you'll do well in the class. Really funny.

If you can figure out what he's saying (foo rank matrices...), he's as funny as they get. We go slow as hell but somehow are way ahead of the other Cal IIs and where most are failing. No comment.  Anyway, he's a great guy and he'll respond to emails at two in the morning, even with a class over 200.

Accents the wrong syllables on almost all of his words, gives you a headache after being in class too long.  On the flipside, practice tests are just like real tests making the class easy, especially if you are inclined to not go to class, b/c of accent.
Practice tests are almost exactly like the real tests.  I didn't do homework for months and still got an easy A.
Practice tests are just like the real thing. He lets you scale the quizes/final to find the best average. His accent in lecture didn't bother me. Wasn't a hard A.
I couldn't understand a thing he said the whole semester!
His tests are the same concepts as the practice tests...he will give you the benefit of the doubt.  Lecture is boring....
Impossible to understand, but goes through concepts like a high school teacher
No Comments
Tough but worth it. Pushes you to actually learn the material. One of my favorite professors.
Horrendous! Dr. Yahaya please quit your job or get a life because you can't take 20 points off a paper for not having headings or subheadings when you give us zero instructions.

Graded on 10 discussions and a final paper, each category was 50% of the final grade. The syllabus was outdated and had information about a project we didn't do. There was no rubric for the paper, just a loose set of guidelines. Minimal feedback was given for the final and he had expectations for the paper that were not explicitly stated anywhere.

His lectures were all over the place and provided very little concrete information, class discussions were frequently frustrating and contradictory, and most quiz and test questions came directly from the textbook but were often specific details and confusing definitions. Makes international affairs feel impossible.

Terrible at teaching with poor explanations, making it even harder for less-experienced students. Completely unacceptable.

The worst IE teacher I've had so far. She did not tell us what to study or know for tests. The tests always took more time than the class period. Has a terrible teaching style of writing derivations on the board, not explaining half of it, and not telling you if you need to know it for the test. Gets angry at the class for not knowing things.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: HWs aren't auto-100s but TAs are helpful if you reach out. Averaged 87 on both by just redoing the HWs and the sample exam. Group final project in place of final - directions pretty vague but just start early so you can ask her questions and the rest is easy. Relaxed class.
Parisa really cares about her students and actually wants them to do well and it's evident. It just comes down to you whether you seek out/use the help that she provides.
Good lecturer.

Definitely cares about her students and tries her best to spice up the material during lecture, but it's hard to make statistics fun.  3% extra credit boost and an easy group project instead of a final means you should get an A if you put in a reasonable amount of effort.  The two midterms are tough though, and attendance is randomly checked.

Good prof. The lecture structure was hard to follow, but the content easy enough that you can self teach everything. Not a hard class if you put in the work. She cares about student success and is always ready to answer student questions, even if she may be a little hard to approach. The group final paper was better than having a cumulative final.

This was probably the easiest engineering class I've taken at Tech. The content is a little boring but it's really easy to do well. There was a total of 6 homework, 2 midterms, and one final project  + could get  3% bonus for CIOs and she replaced the 1st midterm score if you did better on the 2nd. In other words, if you try, you should get an A!

In the beginning, I found myself struggling since I never took statistics. In class, I couldn't follow the lectures since I needed time to understand everything. When I explained my concerns, she allowed me to look at her old video lectures. If you take the time, you will learn a lot considering the professor understands the students!
cares about student success, curves. lectures and material isn't always the most engaging and clear
One of the best professors. If you do the necessary minimum, you should be good. She even gave us a 3% curve at the end for CIOS.

Lectures are a little dull, but Professor Zowj is really nice. Homeworks are pretty easy, there's one every week. Tests are a little difficult but there's tons of partial credit. The group project at the end was really straightforward and easy.
Boring lectures. Material is pretty easy.
