Taken during COVID as an online course. All the class was was hour long recordings of her working through powerpoint slides that were very dull to watch. Homework was easy and from the textbook. The tests were very fair, and the final was a group project. Easy class, but you will not learn anything if you don't want to.
She's not the greatest lecturer. By no means bad, just standard and dry sometimes. The content is super easy though, and she wants you to do well in the class.

She is a great teacher that makes very simple tests and homework. You still have to study for them, but everything in the hw and tests are covered in the lectures and there are no trick questions. If you practice, the class is a very easy A. She is a little boring, but otherwise great professor.

Course is extremely easy especially if you took AP Statistics. She isn't that great of a professor, but because the content is so easy, it is very easy to self learn. Class is weighted heavily on tests, but she allows a cheat sheet for them and gives practice problems/exams beforehand. Caring and nice professor, but not a great instructor.

Parisa is a very kind professor. Her lectures are pretty average, which is not a bad thing. Homework and exams are not that difficult. She allows use of a crib sheet for each exam. It is very clear that Parisa cares a lot about her students, and also remembers that we have lives outside of her class.
Very Tough on the grading. Tests much harder than other 2551 sections
Hard to understand
bruh i just cant. take that class at an easier school over the summer

Writes on a small whiteboard in the front of a classroom with 4 projectors (he doesn't use any of them, so it's difficult to follow his work), bad accent, makes tests impossible and unfair (first two tests had an average of 66/100, and the last one had a 61/100 average)

He doesn't run the class well and I would not recommend him.

Spring 2025. was very difficult for me even though I took it in high school. I'm not sure if I struggled so much due to poor teaching or my own stupidity. I thought he was a fine lecturer but obviously I didn't do so well in the class. He used the whiteboards instead of a projector, and it was really hard for me to see with the glare and distance.

Bad lecturer- mumbles and is quiet, only writes on whiteboard and stands in front of what he's writing. Gives less resources than others (seems that he took stuff off the syllabus when comparing with another section). Posts lecture slides, but unfinished, and we never get through them in lecture anyways, so I just watch Lehmann's videos.

He only writes on the small board at the front of the class even though there are four projectors for him to show his work, making lecture hard to follow. His tests are way harder than the slides and quizzes, and he often posts lecture slides with no solutions or methodology. He also has a big accent. First test average was 62/100.

Do not take.
Amazing professor, best multivar teacher, easy exams.
He does listen to students for feedback on exam content/difficulty and does offer extra credit for studio exams. He posts all of the lecture content on Canvas and the WebWorks are manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Genuinely cannot understand what he is saying, I went to lecture once and never went again. Easier just to self-study this course tbh. There's plenty of online resources.

Literally the worst professor I've ever had. He barely speaks english (not joking I tried asking him something after lecture and he didn't understand me) and has the worst accent ever. He is incomprehensible that 90% of the class stop going to lecture after week 1. Also does not allow formula sheets even tho they were allowed in prev semesters

He had an accent, and brushed over concepts at a very fast pace, but his overall understanding of the material was OK. If you ask him questions outside of class or during office hour then he'll explain better.

He taught me in my first year as a professor in general, so I tried to give him some grace. However, there is only a small amount of grace I can give. He has a very noticeable and almost not understandable accent and went too fast. It got to a point where 5 people were showing up to an almost 100+ student lecture. But... he tried his best!!!
ngl it's week 3 and I can not understand her majority of the time... her accent is so confusing.
test is the same thing as the practice test. take this class w her.

Had her the first semester she came to tech. Class was mostly on Pearson, but had 8am mandatory attendance. She took a point solutions participation grade, that was for accuracy, but then changed it after some feedback to completion. tests were easy and similar to practices. group project was an auto 100. really nice teacher.

It's a very straight-forward class and Prof. Mobini gives clear lectures and is very understanding. Attendance is required, but it should be because you won't understand strictly using canvas. It is very easy to do well if you just come to class and do the homework. The test mirrors the HW

Professor Mobini was great! I enjoyed being in her class and learning from her. Pearson is heavily used in the course and a substantial amount of material builds off of the management statistics course. She is extremely accessible and responds to emails very quickly. Would recommend!

I believe that this semester is her first time teaching the course. That being said, she did an amazing job and you can tell that she's very enthusiastic and wants you to get something from this class. The only pains of this class were that attendance was graded, and she made us buy a course pack for $10 that we used once. Overall, great Professor!
Good guy, good lectures, cares about students.

The professor is not caring about student and lecture accumulates a lot of materials and TAs are not respectful. Also, the quizes are so hard and the materials also disorganized. I feel the prof did not prepare the materials well.

Lectures are very dry and are just presentations with 60+ slides per, ended up not showing after a few weeks because it was hard to care, maybe its me but the lectures just were not interesting in the end.  Homeworks were annoying but did not take too much time.

Lectures were not that useful for me, so I can't comment on that. But the assignments are good and the project is cool. He's pretty generous and gives a grace period for every assignment as well, although I suspect he just uses it as an excuse to not let students who have submission problems complain to him.
Homework is hard and takes time, but you will learn much about ML. Lectures are cool and cover modern DL. Honestly, one of the most fulfilling courses I've taken at GT.

I don't know what's with the bad ratings here - Dr. Kira was just fine. His lectures were decent to good (more than adequate) and he did respond to questions well. The HWs were hard (unsurprisingly, since the subject itself is hard), but the TAs were helpful on that front - and I learnt a lot in general. If you do the HWs and project, guaranteed A

"-1 Too verbose: 5 or more sentences" for a question that did NOT say anything about being brief. Lost another point on another homework for another UNWRITTEN requirement (had 96% accuracy needed 97% or something for full points). They made a question that was IMPOSSIBLE to get full points (needed 100% accuracy with 0 model size).

The GT CS program was missing a rigorous deep learning class and Kira is great if you're interested in recent methods (diffusion, GPT). Homeworks are tough but fair, there are no tests, and the final project is graded generously. It's harder than CS 3600/4641 though - I came in as a senior with ML background and found the class challenging.
Unreasonable homework, not sure why he does this. Not related to lecture. No solutions for feedback.
The professor was good. The course helped me learn a lot about deep learning

If you are into DL theory and its math, you will love this class, else you'll abhor it. The slides are similar (sometimes copied) to CS 231N at Stanford, and homeworks are more difficult relative to lecture content and takes hours. If this is your first exposure to DL, it will be hard, and recommend taking another DL course somewhere else before.

Absolutely amazing professor, especially if you are interested in deep learning theory. The statements he gives in class are very precise and mathematically rigorous, which are sometimes not liked (considered redundant) by those who include more towards applied DL/ML -- the reason for the negative remarks IMO.

The slides & hw r not aligned I felt lost for the hw & had to use online resources. I took an intro online class: the examples & numbers were exactly the same as his module1 slides! He copied his material and taught them in an awful confusing way. Ironic since he is strict on not using online material & writing ur own code!
HWs need long hrs too.
Hard homeworks, vague slides, vague assignment statements! Do only if you have previous background in the course subject.

No relation between what's taught and what's on HW. You would spend days doing the HWs because there is no clear flow in the slides. So internet is all you would look at. The assignment statements are also not very clear. Totally killed my learning experience for Deep learning.

Class is heavily based off Dr. Isbell's course, including projects and the online Udacity course. Lectures are quite theoretical and hard to understand. Projects take time to complete but are not graded too strictly. Course is heavily curved, with attendance helping in some cases. Professor shows care towards students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Dr. Zeagler was a very kind and super chill professor. Lectures were mandatory but were short and concise and overall the class was not too difficult. Studio is where you need to actually interact but if you have a good group discussions are very fun. Would highly recommend.

He has amazing lectures and often tries to facilitate discussion among students. Lectures are short, but definitely informative, and he makes it abundantly clear that the class will be easy as long as you put in the work. If you do take him, make sure to participate! Most people don't, so it makes you stand out and will make lecture so much better!

Easy class; however, it entirely depends on your section TA. Some TAs legit don't care and give you a 100 for almost everything, and one in particular... is lets just say takes she takes her job too seriously.

Lectures were engaging and lasted 20-30 mins each. Tells you all the questions on the upcoming exams the class before, so you don't even need to study. 

Discussions vary based on TA, so this will be a hit or miss. Still, interesting and not difficult.

This is probably the easiest CS class you will take at Georgia Tech. 100% would take again.
Extremely good professor for this course, would 100% recommend taking him
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: TAKE THIS DUDE, absolute goat. tells you what's on the test and CIOS is up to 5 points on final grade. Mandatory lectures are easy to attend, easiest class I've taken at tech. Couldn't recommend more.

I got the impression he was tired of teaching the course since not enough people engaged properly, but he taught the class well. Section was great and the TA I got did a great job of facilitating conversation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: Very engaging professor. The readings can be very long, but you only have to skim them most of the time to be able to participate in lecture or studio. The class was interesting and I never dreaded going to lecture or studio (especially since he tells you what's on the exams). Don't procrastinate working on your term paper. CIOS bonus is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment:
HE IS THE GOAT I LOVE HIM!! And his CIOS incentive is great: 

75% of the class completes CIOS- 3 point addition to total grades.
85%- 4 point addition to total grades.
95%- 5 point addition to total grades.

so basically for us a 85.5 is an A

There is a lot of work for this class however. There is a lot of writing and a 10 page paper at the end.

It's unfortunate that you can tell most people aren't really engaged with this class, because Dr. Zeagler is a really enjoyable lecturer! He does a very good job of trying to spark discussion in class, while simultaneously making it as easy as possible to get an A. There is a TON of writing for this class, but none of it is graded especially harsh.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Respected

reviews.comment: Class wasn't too bad. Weekly readings can generally be skimmed over, there isn't an absurd amount of HW either and grading and exams are fairly easy. Dr. Zeagler tries to make class interesting and I did find the topic somewhat interesting - he was a fairly good lecturer overall. Please don't take until last minute to do the final term paper though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Class isn't hard and Zeagler makes the class interesting.

I loved Dr. Zeagler's class. If you go to lecture you won't regret it, he's quite entertaining. His exams are very fair and if you've done most of the readings you'll be alright. His TAs were also great, I really enjoyed studio. People tend to stay quiet in his class so you can easily stand out as a student by answering a question once or twice.

Good professor that made it a flipped classroom. The class mainly relies on a group project that you get to choose. The midterm was a paper on a topic of your choose and the final was open note and take home. He had a attendance policy but as long as you work with your group you'll be fine. Great starting grad class and he was understanding.

Professor was a great guy who made an annoying requirement class interesting and to take. Lectures were a little dry but not really to his fault, it's just a large class with mandatory attendance where very few people are actually engaged. Some of the discussions were super interesting. Overall he was a great prof teaching a mid class.

Nice guy, and lectures although sometimes boring are pretty straightforward. Class is pretty easy, just a lot of writing. Section TA can be hit or miss. If you have a good one the class is very easy. Pretty good extra credit for doing CIOS.

super nice, chill guy! tries his best to make lectures engaging despite most people thinking the class is a joke. genuinely always looking for ways to improve and open to criticism about the structure of the course. really approachable and generally made ethics a bearable time
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Zeagler is incredibly caring and understanding. He would push deadlines if they seemed a bit unreasonable. His exams are based on his lectures and are pretty simple. The hw assignments can be tedious but as long as you don't procrastinate too much, they should be fine.
Dr. Zeagler is a very enthusiastic professor who is passionate about ethics. I highly recommend taking his class.

Pretty good professor. Class wasn't too difficult, was maybe like an hour or two of work a week. Attendance was mandatory and the way it was done was a little messy.

Lectures were decently interesting. Tests were pretty easy and easy A's if you went to class
Dr. Zeagler is a pretty swell guy, though the lectures are sometimes flat. Tests were fair but not dead-easy. Tested mostly on material from slides. In-person attendance was mandatory for Fall 2022.

Do not take this course. I thought I was going to get a masters in HCI. This course killed that. Professors do not care about the course and copy/pasted assignments week to week. We rushed through "Design of Everyday things" reading 2 chapters a week only for the professors to stop showing up to lecture halfway through the semester. 

Disappointing

Took for ethics, you only need to go to recitations, lectures are not important. Nice and caring professor. Class is graded on recitation participation with TAs and a couple of papers that don't take too long to read, final was a longer paper about an area of our interests in ethics, easy A

Clint's a really mellow guy and that was translated into his teaching. He gave his students a lot of freedom and was receptive to the different approaches people took to their projects. He had a tendency to be vague at times, but he didn't mind answering lots of questions. It's obvious that he cares for his students.
I love this teacher! He really knows his stuff and he explains things in a funny way. He cares a lot about his students, too.

Brilliant professor and clearly a top-notch academic with a lot of knowledge about the history of the field. Comes across as intimidating initially but he's very approachable in truth. You'll learn to think about things differently from taking his class, and it's nice that the tests are very straightforward.

He is really smart, knowledgable and passionate which is great if you are interested in what he is teaching. His tests are pretty much exclusively beaded off his notes and I think he does a great job of testing the important stuff as opposed to the minutia.
Dr. Ackerman is a big name in his field and teaches quite well for a Georgia Tech Psychology Professor.
No Comments

He used a cheap microphone with a hurricane wind sound effect. Lectures felt like they were inside a wind tunnel, and the teaching style with many fragmented and repetitive sentences didn't help. All lecture notes appear to be created with an index finger and trackpad. Many students got tired of copying down random squiggles and left mid-lecture.
Difficult to understand is an understatement. His handwriting is atrocious. 100% go to a diff lecture.

Professor is hard to understand during lectures and has bad hand-writing. It's not that bad because lectures aren't attendance mandatory and you can always go to a different section, so if you have his class I would either go to another one or read through the posted lecture notes.

It's difficult to read his handwriting and even more difficult to understand what he is saying. I only attended class to get the extra credit, and I typically spent that time watching the lecture videos or reading the notes of other professors. You can succeed in his class, but only by learning the content elsewhere and paying attention in studio.

Just an awful instructor. Impossible to understand, terrible lectures and handwriting, no idea what he's doing. For 1554 I highly recommend sitting in on another professor's lecture and focus heavily on the studio, as that's likely your best bet to pass this class, not these lectures.

Neto is a really nice guy... unfortunately he just isn't the best professor for 1554. Instead of using Barone's PPTs (which every 1554 professor does) he insists on handwriting and projecting the notes - except his handwriting is unreadable. He also explains many concepts incorrectly. You'll be learning entirely with Barone's recorded lectures.

You can't understand any of his lectures. Most people stopped going to them before the third class. He would make many mistakes in class as well. I would take the class somewhere else before taking him.

There are 104 students registered in my class. For the past 2months, I am one of the only 2/3 students who show up. Don't take this professor. His accent is unintelligible, and so is his handwriting. He doesn't use the whiteboard/ppts/computer; instead, he writes on a messy piece of paper and projects that, but it is impossible to understand.

There were 105 people signed up for this class, I walked into a lecture recently and there were 2 people still showing up to class. He seems like a great and caring guy, but you LITERALLY cannot understand a word he says because of his accent. Avoid taking him, but if you do, understand you'll be watching online lectures from Barone/Mayer to learn

MATH 2552 is probably the easiest math class I've taken at Tech. However, Professor Neto's strong accent and difficulty with the technology made it difficult to understand him so I stopped attending class after the second lecture. But you can learn all of diff eq in studio

Lectures are rough because his English is not very good but he more than makes up for this by being extremely caring to students. Very consistently communicates with TA's course requirements so that recitation is all you need to do well. He's a very nice guy and he is a very good professor in the ways that are in his control.

Once he learned to speak up I could actually understand what he was saying and he actually explains things pretty well. That being said, lecture is not mandatory by any means, just go to studio. His tests are easy and his practice sets are almost exactly like the exams so you know what to expect. Genuine guy trying his best.

Prof Abdon had a rough first couple of lectures largely due to his thick accent and troubles with projecting his voice. After having come back to his lectures at the end of the semester, I can see he really improved his teaching style and speech. He is very kind and knowledgable, and his tests are fair. You can also learn everything in studio.

He is a very nice guy and I can tell he is trying his best, but he is nearly impossible to understand. The class is not hard by any means and most of the learning is done through studio anyway. Tests are very fair and not hard if you put in the work outside of lecture.

Professor Neto is by far one of the worst professors I've had at Tech. I stopped going to lectures the second week because he seemed to be a lost cause with his mumbling, general confusion, and constant mistakes. Either rely on video lectures or on the TA's. His only saving grace is that exams and quizzes are very fair.

Blud, do not take this man. Like I got respect for him, but he is impossible to understand. Class was less than 50% full on the second lecture. Class isn't hard, but when you can't hear anything it's impossible to learn.
Only writes on tiny whiteboard, uses mic wrong, cant hear him, and the words you can hear are unintelligible. Doesn't even seem to understand the content. Should not be a professor.

Attendance wasn't required for main lectures, but studios run by TAs were mandatory. The professor assigned many readings and writing-based assignments. She was very involved during lectures and explained concepts clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lots of reading. But the lectures were interesting enough. I didn't get a ton of feedback up front, but her office hours were great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's just rude. Like in class she seems nice but comments she leaves and emails she has ATTITUDE. Cant stand her tbh.

Mills is solid-- a good lecturer and great with offering resources. For 3127 though, attendance wasn't required for lectures but WAS for the studios w/ TAs. With how lenient she is with access to resources, you don't have to attend many lectures. Be weary of written assignments you get b/c they come up pretty often and are fairly long (1000 words).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Mills is like a breath of fresh air while at Tech. Her lectures are good, and tests are easy if you do the readings. Some of the readings are a bit long, but very helpful for the papers you will have to write.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Zureick is super laid back and insanely intelligent. His courses are on the unorganized side, but you will learn SO much. He is caring and wants people to learn. What I loved about this course in particular is that he reads through the code and dissects it in lecture, and then does example problems. It helped drill the concepts down.

I LOVE Dr. Zureick. He is so caring and helpful. He is very laid back and does not state due dates or a schedule. He gives 2 exams, a group project, and hw. The hw is average and he is very willing to help during office hours. The exams are a good reflection of the hw and open notes. He is willing to change lectures to what interests the class.

Homeworks in this class is pretty light, but a lot of the grade is from your exams and the research/special problem project. Lectures can be kind of boring. Class is very disorganized as you get very little instructions for expectations of the project, deadlines, etc. Midterm was easy but the final was rough imo

Awful professor, doesn't know what he's talking about. Uses TA's for everything and then doesn't check it leading to numerous errors. His teaching is writing another professors notes on the board that he messes up and doesn't understand. He overall seems to not know the content or care enough about the course to put in effort.
Super based. Gave me the highest grade on the project out of all the professors teaching the class.

Abramson was super apathetic towards the class. There were only 5-6 people in the class and he delegated lecture time to an uninterested grad student who was always unprepared and bad at teaching. There were also constant mistakes in the homework's. Just a poor job and I hope he improves. I would look for a more experienced prof.

Very nice prof, but lectures are not helpful for quizzes/hw. TA's run the lab completely separately from lecture, and there is clear disconnect between what is taught. He teaches his material well but the material on hw/quizzes are often different enough to stump you. TAs create hws & quizzes at professor discretion, but prof couldnt always help

He teaches very well but there is a slight disconnect in the material tested vs. what is taught in class. The TA's are not really helpful and even reading the textbook does not give the context needed. This is a survey course so it is different (3 exams + 1 final and 8 homework's other class has 4 homework's and 1 midterm and 1 final).

ngl at the beginning of the yr I hated this class, but Hillegass & TAs did great at taking feedback to fix the tests & structure. We had an AI tournament that was super fun and differen!  In general, I think I learned a lot from the hws (time-consuming but useful). Class is hard, but Hillegass is passionate about his subject and is a helpful prof!

Hillegass is the GOAT. Dude does it for the love of the game. He's a professor that actually cares about the content he teaches. Lecture is not required but I heavily recommend you go. You really don't want to miss out on them. If you genuinely put effort into learning AI for this class, you'll really come to enjoy his class, which I did.

Prof. Hillegass is a caring and genuine guy. From what I've heard, the exams were a bit harder than in previous semesters, but everything ended up working out, and studying for the difficult exams is rewarded with a deeper understanding of the material. The final competition project was super fun and was an amazing way to apply what we learned.

not an easy class by any means, but hillegass is a great lecturer who clearly knows and cares about the material. while i didn't get to interact with him directly, i've heard that he is very personable. there were some hiccups at the beginning of the semester, but he was more than fair with correcting and accounting for any issues with the course.

Hillegass is amazing! He's trying to change the class to be better so there have been some bumps with the exams and homeworks, but you can tell he really cares. It is challenging, but I think better for actually learning the content if you take it genuinely. Also has very real world experience that he likes to share.

If you want to actually learn the basics of AI, this is the best option. Hillegass is personable, you talk to him once and he makes his best effort to remember your name even in a class of 200+. Homework every week with only one submission a day but they provide local tests and if you pass those you get a 100 on the autograder.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
changed format to be very difficult and much more accelerated, making it difficult to understand. You basically have to read the textbook yourself.

Can only submit homework once a day. Exams are very difficult with a low average. Cool guy, but not worth it. Take the other section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: just take the other section.

The exams are extremely challenging (average 59, no curve given) and the homeworks are very time consuming and only 1 submission per day. The lectures are quick and do not give a good understanding of the topics. The textbook is also very challenging to read. Overall, this makes for a very challenging course.
Professor Hillegass was an absolutely amazing professor. By far the easiest professor I've ever had! The exams were so much fun! The professor is extremely nice and the projects are very easy!
Loved the exam and being challenged. I'm learning tons!
just take the other section

HW is already hard but the one-submission-a-day made it mad hard. Nice guy, hard course. I didn't like that all HWs and (especially) exams were completely autograded because no partial credits were awarded. At the end, there was a bonus quiz which is nice but some of the quizzes were really hard. Other sections are a lot easier.

Professor is very caring and willing to help. But the class is unexpected HARD. Other section is totally different and much easier(really). I think I prepared well for the exam and did well in the previous HARD homework, but the real one hurts me. Be ready to spend tons of hours weekly on this course if you really want to take his.

Professor only allows one submission to autograder per day, making it incredibly difficult to do homework. Homework is also extremely time consuming and covers material not taught in class. Material covered in lecture is very simple but then material expected to know in homework is complicated.

Amazing class. He really knows his stuff and wants to help the class succeed. Lectures were engaging and the homework concepts were cool. He added a lot of extra code so that you could visualize your results on the homework and play around with what you made after you finished.

Took both 3600 and 3510 with Professor Hillegass. Great guy, super understanding, and you'll actually learn the material. Explains things clearly and cares about students. One of the few professors where you walk away really knowing the content. He brings real industry experience, so he knows what actually matters. Highly recommend.
GOAT. He understands students better than any professor I've learned from at Tech.

I had him for both CS3600 and CS4641. He knows his stuff and does a pretty good job explaining difficult concepts. He was also successful in the industry and would drop lots of advice throughout the semester. He is also very caring and understanding. Overall, a very cool guy. Take him if you can
Passionate and nice young guy but extremely tough grading... no mercy
Big chiller. Great guy. Knows the stuff. Passionated about the class... when you're one of 20 people remaining in the class at end and learning about random stuff it's so much fun.
Hillegass is an amazing professor with incredible experience and life advice. Would definitely recommend him for any class.

Amazing professor, highly recommend. He has real-life experience in the industry which he brings to his lectures. Very caring, talk to him if you have a problem, he will more than likely help you out. Very smart, sometimes makes small mistakes on technicalities but then fixes it next class.
Great lecturer, fascinating life experiences, funny, very passionate about what he's teaching. The course itself is standardized materials.

Overall he was a good professor that cared about his students, but 1712 is a heafty class and the lectures were extremely detailed and in depth. The course is mainly graded on 3 Midterms and a final, but there were plenty of extra credit opportunities. If you struggle with probabilities, you will find this course very difficult.

Lectures are fine, very fast-paced. Doesn't fully answer questions when you ask, just reiterates the answer he got. TA was bad, didn't explain answers to worksheets well. I failed the first midterm (hardest one) and never seemed to recover (test heavy course). Will ask you to simplify difficult fractions in a short amount of time (EX: 9.5/5).

Class is very test heavy, but overall it was an easy class! Lectures jump around a bunch of different math topics and he posts the slides on Canvas if you miss them. Haiyu never hesitated to answer questions or give help if someone was confused. Make sure you go to studio, you'll get 1-2 extra credit points!
Actually the first time that I understood math! As long as you go over the midterm study guides and studio worksheets, you will most likely get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Honestly thought this class was great! You can finesse some of the exams by studying the day before if you go to studio and lecture!

i suck at math, but i loved Mr. Zou as a prof. He is funny and a very good teacher. Tests are fair and I always did better than expected (got -.6 buses on one question and covered the tests in tear stains but got an 80). the hw and studio questions def relate to exams and quizzes.

the goat for 1711 or 1712! yes the classes are hard, but he is by far the best person to take them with. He is funny and engaging in lectures and gives lots of extra credit for going to class and studio

Haiyu is a great professor for how deceptively hard 1712 is. While bad at responding to emails, he's very nice in his office hours and grades fairly. You'll need to put in more effort than you think and get extra support to do well in this class, and to accomplish that, Haiyu is a great prof. to get there.

He is a mid professor, my TA was awful which made this class more difficult than necessary. The grade inflation at the end of the semester goes crazy with homework and extra credit, so most people end with an A or B. 2 weekly homework and if you go to all the studios + lectures you get extra credit. Not the worst ever, but doable with some effort

The exams varied a lot in difficulty the first exam average score was like a B second a D and final a C. He ended up curving in the end. He provided homework assignments that could be used to add up to six points onto your final grade. Overall great guy.

Professor Zou does a great job of explaining topics in a simple and understandable way. Although, attendence isn't required (outside of quiz days), I highly recommend coming to class. Homeworks are not required, but are good for midterm practice and earn you extra credit. Quizzes are not bad and midterms are fair.

You can still succeed if math isn't your strong suit, but this class is easy for some and hard for others. Starts off fairly easy but kind of ramps up near the end. The studio worksheet problems show up on the quizzes and sometimes the exams. Partial credit given on exams, 4 extra points available for final grade. Won't respond to emails.

I have taken Zou for 1711 and 1712. I received a letter grade higher than expected both times, and I am extremely grateful (math is not my strong suit). This class is difficult, however Zou is the best teacher you can have. This class is graded by 3 exams + final, 4 quizzes, and homework. Attendance is Extra Credit.

This class was EXTREMELY difficult if you have never taken a calculus class. I went into my exam blind because of his lack of awareness of putting in grades. The syllabus quiz was given 6 weeks into the course. NEVER responds to emails in a timely manners, and also lies in emails. You will feel stupid when asking him questions.
Haiyu is amazing. I had him for a total of 2 math classes, and I would absolutely take another math class with him.

He didn't put grades in the gradebook so I never knew what my grade was (even going into the final). He would claim that he would add things to canvas and then NEVER do it or do it so late that it didn't matter anymore. He doesn't respond to emails in a timely manner. I went into the final blind bc I didn't know my grade.
Doesn't respond to emails ever

Much better at teaching this class (1711) than 1712, the lectures are much more engaging and easier to grasp. The homework is very helpful in learning the content but he often teaches it in a different way. Class gets easier as the semester goes along.

If you have previous experience with calculus you should be fine, but this class is not friendly to those who have little to no experience. Moves very quickly and his lectures are very uninteresting. Also very hard to reach outside of class, will take days or weeks to respond to emails.

Great, funny guy who understands the class is filled with non-STEM majors and teaches curriculum accordingly. Pearson homework sucked, but exams were easy if you did study guides. Goes fast during lectures, but overall relatively simple to follow. Office hours were helpful for additional questions. Attendance = extra credit.

I love him.An amazing teacher who really cares about his students understanding the material. Assigns homework pretty much every week/lecture but they really do cover the material and help you. Provides EC that is very beneficial in the end. Also really funny and goofy. if you fall asleep during his lecture, good luck.makes math fun but to a limit

His lecture style is extremely boring and unengaging. I took AP Calc / IB Math in high school and that is the main reason I understood what was going on. Studios / lectures are extra credit which helps. Def go to studio, it's a lot easier to learn content. Exams / quizzes are identical to studio worksheets and study guides. H

Easy material so easy A, but the prof frequently waited until the last minute to post homework and made mistakes on study guides- he would make a mistake, someone would point it out, he would tell them they're wrong, then they would take the test, get that question wrong, point it out to him, and he'd say "we did a problem like this in class".
Very good professor, just show up to class and take notes and the class should be an easy A.

I really enjoyed his class! The lectures were pretty engaging and easy to understand. I'd say the math wasn't that bad, but I know a lot of people who struggled with it. Quiz after every lecture for participation and homework 2x a week. Worksheets and study guides were very helpful. Great professor! (don't email, he won't answer. Go to OH lol)

Prof Zou will make you laugh in every lecture, and found a way to make probability fun. He is extremely clear, and the tests are based on the content on the study guides. Attendance is extra credit, and many tests had extra credit, or questions that wouldnt be graded. Some homework (that you pay $90 to access) but overall solid class and prof.
Professor Zou is a great professor. He has a clear voice and communication style. Just as good as watching a YouTube video and he goes through every step. I am taking him again for finite.

This course is easy if you already learned calculus in high school (AB). If you did not, it is very challenging because he goes through the material very quickly and the lectures are pretty unengaging. He is very good at answering questions and is a nice guy overall. The midterm/final was very similar to the study guides.

Haiyu is extremely kind, but his lecture style is TERRIBLE. I found his lectures boring, unclear, and hard to engage with, which sucked bc his slides are also USELESS for review as he does all of his teaching on the whiteboard. I got a B bc of youtube, textbooks, and a curve. This class is RIDICULOUSLY difficult, especially bc of how he teaches it.
You have a test every other week in the class. But his lectures are very good and he is always open for questions outside of class. He really cares about his students.

For a statistician, this guy loves to yap and seldom relies on visuals. If your class is quiet, maybe it's because nobody understands what is going on, you don't have to take it as a personal affront to you. 

If you want students to engage, make your lectures engaging. 

If you want to do well in this class, just do the HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took math 1564 with him as well. By that time he was the TA for 1564. So much better than the professor. Explains concepts so much more clearer. For math 3670, he does some review every class, but you still need to go to class. He is definitely the best professor for 1564 and intro to stats/prob. Just take him, you won't regret, promise

Zou is a funny and a great caring teacher but hard. Go to class or you will definitely get behind, and homeworks and tests are graded pretty ruthlessly. I ended up with an A as he curves the class at the end, but don't pick him if you want an easy A. Definitely made statistics more interesting for me!

Haiyu is prob one of the best math professors at GT. Explains things really well. Quizzes and tests can be hard but he gives lots of resources and hws give up to 6% EC. Def listens to feedback. Early grading was very harsh but def changed after receiving feedback. Overall very enjoyable course and feel like I actually learned a lot.
He is a very good lecturer and is perfect for college students. He is incredibly intelligent and always willing to help. Just talk to him every now and then. If you try, you will do well.
Bro is just one hell of a specimen.

I love Professor Haiyu! He gives wonderful lectures, and he cares about his students(he answers all the questions you ask in class or after class). Homework is heavy but meaningful, tests are hard but fair. It's is a challenging class, but if you love math and find that Prof. Haiyu will be teaching, then TAKE IT! You'll learn more than "a lot"!

Probably the best math instructor I have ever had. MATH 1564 is hard (especially if you have never taken a proof-based math class before), but Haiyu's lectures were excellent. He is very helpful if you ask him a question after class or in office hours (maybe a little too helpful when it comes to homework).

Professor Zou is the best!! He is super enthusiastic about the subject and you can tell that he really loves teaching it. Professor Zou also cares a lot about his students and holds many office hours sessions. The class is extremely difficult and mostly proof based. Be ready to put in a lot of time studying but Professor Zou makes it worth it!

The content was difficult and moved fairly quickly, but when Haiyu says things, they just get understood. He made me actually understand the essence of math and want to take more math. He's also just a great guy and gave everyone cookies during our final.

As I wanted to know the "why"s of linear algebra, Haiyu couldn't have done a better job. He is an engaging and passionate lecturer, interjects with jokes, and clearly cares about his students. The class was rigorous and challenging, but he is fair in assessment and I've learned so much. Truly a great professor, I only wish I could take him again.

If you go to lectures and studios, it is easy to pass this class. Professor Zou was engaged with his students and responded to emails quickly. He communicates what to expect on exams. The first half of the semester was much easier than the second half of the semester. The final exam was much harder than any other quizzes or exams.

This class is definitely difficult! That being said, Haiyu is an amazing teacher. His office hours are extremely helpful and he gives some opportunities for extra credit. Going to lecture is crucial. Hws are graded easily but tests are graded harshly.

He's a great professor. All of the resources available made it hard to outright fail the class. His lectures and studio work was also helpful in learning. This class taught very surface level calc 1 2 and 3, so I get why it's hard for some people if they aren't familiar with calculus already. His study guides are exactly the same as the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I learned so much from Prof. Haiyu's class which allows me to see math as a completely different subject compared with what I did in HS. It is very time-consuming but no regrets here. I know I will miss this semester.

If you go to all his lectures and TAs' studios, you get 4 extra credits, almost half a letter grade. That's how much Dr. Zou wants you to pass his class. His study guides tell you EVERYTHING that will be on the exam, which is why I finished the final in less than half the alotted time. There's people complaining how hard the class is? smdh.

Words simply cannot describe how amazing this man is, you just have to take him. He's a rare professor because he is not only extremely intelligent but knows how to communicate his genius to students who I found are often quite stupid to put it frankly. If you can't crack his class you shouldn't be at Georgia Tech, try UGA.

Professor Zou has been one my favorite professors by far. I personally found his class to be easy simply by attending lectures and participating in studio, plus he gives a study guide before every examine that is almost identical to the test. Some students complained his class was too hard, but surprise surprise, I never saw them once in lecture.

Though I find this course difficult and tests can be sometimes challenging; for the first time in my life I enjoyed taking a math class. Professor Zou is an amazing lecturer with a great sense of humor. I did not skip a single lecture and note that this class was at 8am. Prof Zou is also very caring and was willing to schedule extra Office hours

The class is tough, but Professor Zou is funny and genuinely enjoys teaching his students. His lectures are worthwhile to attend, and he often interjects long and arduous proofs with humourous tales. He is always available and listens to the students' concerns. He made this semester amazing.

I wouldn't take this class if you don't truly love math; the subject matter is very hard and takes much work to comprehend. If you just need a linear algebra credit, take 1553/4, trust me. However, that is not to attack Haiyu, there is no one who could teach this topic better than he did. He is caring, personable, funny, and generous with grading.

This is an insanely hard class but Prof Zou makes it so much better. He cares about his students, has a sense of humor, and can explain concepts simply. It will be hard to find a professor better than Haiyu.
Prof Haiyu is the GOAT!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Prof. Zou is excellent at teaching and cares about his students. This course is hard for students who did not have previous exposure to calculus. The lectures are interesting and difficult material is simplified well. Though I find the tests and quizzes to be quite challenging so I hope that the final will be doable.

Easy class. He understands that this is not stem math and makes his teaching super clear. He's really generous and flexible on midterms and quizzes. you can drop your lowest quiz. Hes a great math prof and will listen to any reccs or ideas. Also if you say like 1 think he will change half the exam to what you want.

Prof. Zou is extremely personable, and an amazing lecturer and teacher. I can't explain it, you have to take it for yourself. hands down one of the best teachers I've ever had. The class is challenging and will challenge your way of thinking, but it's so worth it and enjoyable and, dare I say, fun.
He taught difficult content very clearly and provided us with helpful resources to practice.

Don't take him if you are not ready to work. If you do decide to take him, your hard work will be rewarded. His lectures were packed with materal which made me feel that I learned a lot. I appreciate that he had his office hours right after class. I do wish he could go over more stats.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a good person, but his grader, Aryan Mittal, was extremely difficult and had averages of F's on both exams. Half of the class dropped, so Haiyu made the second half crazy easy, which passed everyone. Haiyu himself has memorized most of the textbook, and writes the theorems on the board, and does a few examples per class, decent lecturer.

Haiyu was my TA in MATH1564 and really helped me do well in the class. I did not understand much in lectures and it was his studio sessions and practice problems that helped me grasp linear. He was the only TA in the class of like 50-60 people and he did a great job of helping everyone.

Haiyu is such a great teacher! He is super approachable and very good at explaining seemingly difficult concepts. Watching him set up problems has helped me greatly in proving things. I am glad that I signed up for the honor version of Linear Algebra as my first math course. I can't wait to see what other interesting classes Teach has to offer!

Really tough class, even though he kinda tells you what will be on the tests. His study guides are very helpful and he is pretty accessible during office hours. Online class format is a struggle but if you go to his lectures and follow through, you should do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good professor if you really want to learn more about prob and stats. Super logical lectures and explainations. You will even learn t-distribution and chi-square which I thought will appear in 4-level math course. Go ahead and choose him if stats is important for your career in the future! Don't choose him if you just want an easy A.

Absolutely loved him :) he's super caring and flexible about things if you talk to him.  The grades are fair and if you attend/watch all his lectures, everything is verys straight forward, but if it's not, he's super willing to answer any questions you may have.  Highly recommend

MATH 3215 was a very difficult class for me. Through it, though, Professor Zou was tremendously understanding and responsive, and made lectures not only interesting and enjoyable, but also hilarious and personable at times. Would highly recommend the professor, even though I personally disliked the subject.
Probably the hardest math class I have taken at tech. If you do all his homework and understand what you are doing, tests are quite manageable. Oh yea, for your own sanity, don't cram for his tests!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class started out to be hard but he realized that students weren't doing too well and changed the quizzes and tests to be more practical and in line to what we were learning. Overall, I learned a lot in this class and it wasn't too difficult. Some homework questions do pop up in the tests and quizzes so do your homework.

The first test was pretty rough. However, Hiayu made sure later tests and quizzes were more doable. You can tell he really cares about students success and he is very helpful during his office hours. Hiayu, you are a great teacher! Dont let the students bully you!

I thought he was fine, and it was also his first semester teaching this course. The first test was harder than we prepared for but he ended up curving it and gave use harder practice problems for future tests/made them easier. Our last two tests had a lot of problems we had seen before. He does do learning catalytics to check attendance.

let's start by saying that this man began a Finite Math class (one of the easiest math classes at Tech) by saying "I anticipate this class will be harder than linear algebra and differential equations" and he didn't lie. he doesn't teach well, he's boring, and if you ask him questions, he doesn't know how to explain answers

Praise the curve! This class was tough, and you have to work for your grade. Homeworks cover future material as on what you have already learned, which can make them tough. He also makes up his own problems. His lectures are high paced. He is very helpful in officehours, he also wants to help you understand the material. The class was a struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: When he said the course was fast-faced in his syllabus, he was not kidding. If you do not go to class for a week, it feels like he is speaking a completely different language. His notes are very good, probably some of the best for the classes I have taken at GT. Oh, definitely go to his office hours, they are extremely helpful.

No matter who you take this is a difficult class. Haiyu (yes everyone calls him by his first name) is a very caring teacher. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS. He will work out homework problems with you. If you don't understand a concept, he will explain it until it makes sense. He will answer dumb questions without making you feel dumb for asking them.

Hardest class I've taken at Tech. Haiyu provides almost no resources to help you succeed. Homeworks are very difficult, often don't correlate to the material he covers in class. His lectures are not engaging and he spends most of the time talking to the board. Test's are very proof and notation heavy, with very little partial credit awarded.
Best math teacher I have had at Tech! He goes out of his way to make sure you understand the material. Go to his office hours!

Gave a lot of extra credit (20-10-10 points on the tests and final). Homeworks were pretty difficult, but the test questions were much easier. Took several test/quiz questions from homework or in-class examples. Not always the clearest lecturer, and made mistakes, but had a lot of office hours.

One of the best math teachers I've had at GT. Really accessible, friendly, and helpful (even when people take advantage of office hours to have him walk them through the homework, right before it's due).

All of his assessments were much harder than the material use to prepare. He moves very fast so it's hard to catch up if you don't understand a concept. He was very approachable and would make time to talk with you outside of class if you asked him. Very hard class in terms of a core math requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Best TA at Tech. Very patient.  He is the reason I survived the course.

This man's consistent clear explanations and niceness is the reason I am doing well in discrete math. He will sit with you and do problems even after recitation is over until you understand everything

Haiyu explained things very clearly. He was always very prepared and made going to the recitation worthwhile. He was also very funny, which kept the students awake. Hands down the best TA I have ever had so far. Good luck to you, Haiyu!
He's just beyond the average human in every way.
A very knowledgeable TA and he cares about our success. He gave too many problems in class and it can be a little overwhelming sometimes.

This class is rewarding, although difficult. The material is basically just learning how to program a GBA in C. Tests are quite difficult and graded harshly. HW5 is not for the faint of heart. The end of semester project is fun but lots of requirements, so will take up a good bit of time. For the love of god attend lecture, itll help on the HWs
bad professor

Professor Hansen is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is super passionate about this class and the topic is very interesting. Expect a lot of hw and labs! The tests are very hard and some might even consider harder than CS2110. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! Aaron is very good and caring prof. but the materials are better taught 1v1 than in class

The best class i've ever taken, that being said, get ready to WORK. Hansen's a great lecturer and clearly passionate but the nature of the course is super difficult. At least 5 hrs a week in the first 2 months and 10-15+ after that. He's very accessible and kind to all students, but the TAs carry the course. Go to office hours and recitation!!

The HW took up my wkends and especially the last ones had me (and the whole class) going crazy. Aaron is passionate about this topic, & I respect him. The TAs are FANTASTIC and work their heads off helping and explaining every important detail to us. I wonder sometimes if 2110 would have been less stressful...The final project is fulfilling though.

all-around good guy. he knows this class is insanely difficult and time-consuming, and is trying his best to make it bearable. the TAs really carry this class on their backs; i was practically camped out in office hours every single week. class is fun, but expect it to be your heaviest workload by FAR.

Professor Hansen is a nice guy, but his class is genuinely the most time consuming and work heavy class I've ever taken in my life. Homework and Lab is due every week. I've had project based courses where I spent less time on final projects than I did on a singular homework assignment in 2261. 

Expect to spend 20+ hours of work per week.

This class was tough. There is a lab every week and and homework almost every other week. The most time consuming class I've ever had. Expect to spend 10-15+ hours on homework. Aaron is not the best and can come across arrogant. The TA's are GREAT and really carry this class. The tests are also SO hard and he asks the most random stuff on there.

This class is infamously difficult, so it was very nice to take it from a professor that cares deeply about the content. The content can sometimes be difficult to digest, but Professor Hansen is very knowledgable and cares about the content and the students. The TAs are super helpful and will go out of their way to help you with your assignments

2261 is a pretty work-heavy class. Every week you have a homework and a lab. Every other week you have a quiz. At the end of the class, you have a final project. Quizzes cover things from lecture, but they are usually timed and tricky. Despite that, Aaron and the TAs are very helpful. You definitely have to put in the time and effort to get an A.

Prof. Hansen makes the lectures entertaining and engaging even when the topic itself isn't the most fun. The assignments (homeworks and labs) aren't too hard but they require a lot of time. Working on the final project can be awesome, a lot of creative freedom given. No test, just quizzes every other week. The TAs are super helpful too.

Class attendance isn't mandatory, but it definitely makes learning a lot easier when going. Not tests, but quizzes every couple of weeks and nothing is really cumulative. Really easy to get above a 70 on the quiz and I found it doable to study the night before. Class is composed of different GBA homeworks and untimed labs! TAs were super amazing!

Prof Hansen is a great guy, you can tell he cares about his students. The material itself is not the most interesting but he makes it bearable. Best to attend lectures even thou he posts the slides, you'll do better on quizzes of you attend. Labs and HW are easy if you pay attention in lecture/recitation
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher! Clearly has a passion for learning and is a phenomenal teacher! He was super respectful of all students, and willing to help people out. His grading feedback was also very helpful.

If you get the chance to take a class with prof Lanterman u need to do it. Im taking gpu programming with him rn, I pester him and his TA every 2 seconds and they respond within an hour. He runs all his chats through discord, his lects are all recorded. He is the best u can get as far as a professor goes. No exams in case you are a bad test taker
Great prof, but just let me turn my hw in on canvas like every other professor pls :(

Most accessible prof ever, he will answer questions on the class discord at 2 am. Really stress-free grading style. Spends a lot of time on helpful feedback and making sure the final project is doable for everyone. Absolutely insane library of top-notch youtube video lectures.

I'm taking him online in the summer of covid and in 5 weeks he was already 2 weeks behind schedule. He knows the material and presents it well, but doesn't give any tests or quizzes, just a final project. He asks out feedback about online classes which I appreciate, but he also inserts his political views into the lectures. Just teach me signals!

Amazing prof -- he's so incredibly passionate about what he teaches and it shows in his lectures for the class and just makes you want to learn more too. Grades fairly, and a genuinely great person too (COVID-19??? Was THE most humane professor I had with how considerate he was regarding all the outside factors the pandemic introduced)
Professor made the subject material interesting and had awesome lectures.
Great professor, really into the material. Class not too organized but he's very helpful after class. It's not an easy class for me but I learned a whole lot. Favourite class so far.

This class is still really hard and requires a lot of work.  However Dr. Lanterman's enthusiasm was essential to my success.  If lecture was boring I would have never made it.  He's goofy, but in a very helpful way.  Great class!! Also there is a lot of emphasis on the lab and homework, so one bad test won't kill you.  No curve in my class.
Great professor. He has funny stories and it keeps you awake. This was a newer class, and it has much less work than the 2025 class.
Good Professor.  Very Enthusiastic!
A nice professor and a really cool guy. Just wished his lectures made more sense---you'll have to study a lot on your own to compensate for this.
No Comments

What a cool guy. I didn't get very much out of lecture but he made it fun w/ his stories. He's one crazy guy but makes class very interesting. Academically he's pretty good and he's usually available after class for help.
No Comments
No Comments

Santesso is a great professor for LMC2000! He cares a lot about his work and makes assignments feel meaningful and directly related to all the texts gone over in class. He's a tough grader, but he is also willing to give feedback and support--he truly does want you to do well. If you're an LMC major, I definitely recommend starting with him.

The material is very interesting as it's mostly focused on satires in different mediums. Overall, the class requires dedication as the essays are long. Quizzes are weighed heavy, but simply taking notes and studying is enough. His feedback on essays is insanely thorough. Dr. Santesso is funny and passionate about the subject, making the class fun.

i think someone else mentioned but hes a good professor but i just didnt really vibe with him but thats different for everbody. why did i just find out he has a wikipedia page? He tears into your paper but dont take it personally; dont think your writing is goated he'll knock you off that peg.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A lot of people claim Santesso grades too harshly, but I disagree. I felt like all of my grades were fair, and the feedback was beneficial to becoming a better writer. I would say my only "issue" was that he did not use Canvas for grades, so you need to keep track of your own and do your own calculations. Also, participation in class matters!

most engaging professor i've ever had. genuinely loves what he's teaching. there's a LOT of assigned reading, but he goes over it well and in a way that could make a waffle house menu sound like an epic poem. very tough grader, but gives wonderful feedback and has clear expectations. class participation is a must, but you'll want to anyway.

Dr. Santesso is a great professor and clearly loves what he teaches. Lectures were also really interesting. Quizzes are very specific based on the readings, so you really have to read/watch the material he assigns. He's also a harsh grader on papers, so don't expect an easy A. Great class and professor overall though.

Mr. Santesso is a tough grader, but you can tell he's passionate about his work, he has faith in his students, and he wants his students to succeed. I was never very motivated and turned in all my work super late until he told me he saw great potential in me and invited me to an external literature seminar, which was really inspiring for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very engaging lectures but a VERY tough grader on papers. Sometimes the feedback felt subjective. Also attendance and class participation matters a lot even if he never expresses that (he doesn't). It could totally drop your grade even if you have an A.

Mandatory attendance, but unlike most classes I actually wanted to go. Lots of interaction with physical things in relation to course material (we made paper one day in class), interesting literature selection, and fantastic lectures. Tough paper grader, but fair. Helps your writing improve a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Santesso will push you to be your best! However, this felt discouraging when I received harsh grading & criticism on the essays (50% of your grade) I put a lot of time & effort into. Considering his lectures are very fascinating (& him saying B= "very very very good" but A= "exceptional"/"wow"), I recommend him to anyone wanting fun, a push or a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the second class that I've taken with Santesso and I am just obsessed with him. He is one of the most engaging professors I have ever had. That said, this course is not an "easy A" intro class that many expected. He is a rough grader and refuses to use Canvas at all for any reason. Take him if you can - it's worth the work!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing professor with amazing lectures. A genuinely and deeply interesting class. My only problems are personal. He is slightly condescending (as most profs with a wiki page are) and WILL NOT post anything on canvas in a timely manner, if anything at all.
genuinely fun class and a great, easygoing professor! gives amazing feedback on papers, and a fun final project. absolutely take this class with him if you have the chance

He is very passionate and knowledgable on his class topics.his lectures are actually hilarious and engaging. Theres short quizzes that cover the works and lectures (but as long as you go to the lectures and listen you'll be fine) He challenges you as a writer for sure.

Professor Santesso was a great professor! His lectures and the subject matter were engaging and he really cared about each student. We had two major papers that made up half our grade and were graded harshly, but quizzes were easy if you went to class and took notes. The group project was fun and left a lot of room for creative freedom.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Santesso seriously has some of the most interesting lectures I've heard. He focused our LMC 2400 class on satire in media, which was really interesting. Quizzes aren't too bad if you pay attention, some heavy reading at the beginning. Essays are graded harshly but fairly, make sure to use his feedback. 100% would take again, great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Santesso is an amazing professor. His classes is very reading heavy. Pretty much every class we had a reading unless we had to watch a film or view art pieces. He seems like a tough grader but he's actually really fair. Doesn't give clear rubrics but is happy to answer questions. His lectures are also really interesting and not boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Santesso's lectures are interesting and engaging. He does regular short quizzes; you need to go to class in order to do well on them. He's a harsh grader when it comes to papers, but he tells you exactly what he's looking for. His final paper is fun because he gives the option to write about whatever you want in relation to the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice guy, but I don't think an intro major class should be this hard. Didn't put any grades into Canvas, 2 papers and group project graded very harshly. He's unclear about what you'll need to know- like things he mentioned in passing in the lectures are the most important details (ex-the place a work is set in). Main details seem lost on him.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Santesso is one of my favorite professors. This was the second class I've taken from him because I loved the first one so much. The assigned take-home materials are a fun break from the rest of my classes and the lectures are very entertaining. Very tough grader on papers, so not a super easy A, but I feel like my writing has improved a ton.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the best! Super funny and entertaining. Not a lot of outside work. Hard grader on some things but gracious on others. Definitely attend class because you get all your notes from lectures. Definitely a must take, especially for LMC majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Santesso! He makes class interesting and is an amazing lecturer. The course load consists of a midterm short paper, a midterm, a final long paper, and a few quizzes. Definitely go to class if you can; a lot of the quizzes and midterm will have questions that we talk about in class. Overall, a really great guy and an amazing class.

Super funny guy, tells amazing stories. But you NEED to go to class, because the stuff he covers you need for quizzes, projects, and essays. He's super reluctant to give out A's on the papers, but always gives helpful feedback. Great in office hours. I really feel like I learned a lot in this class.

One of the best profs I've had. He's gotten rid of the pop quizzes and gone to announced quizzes, which are easy if you've done the reading. Really engaging lectures and discussions, and he's a hilarious guy. He's a tough grader on essays (doesn't give out A's easily) but that just makes you write better. Very fair grader on final project.

Santesso is by far the most amazing professor I have ever had. All of his lectures are entertaining and enlightening. I walk away from his classes feeling like I've learned something valuable, but I never feel like he tries to make things more difficult than they need to be. He's funny and incredibly knowledgeable!

Great professor- probably one of the best I've taken here. Makes the lectures interesting, unlike many of the LMC/humanities professors. Lots of reading, but usually skimming it is enough to do fine on the quizzes. If I needed another humanities credit, I'd take another course he taught.
Incredibly engaging, very helpful, and very funny.  Probably my favorite professor at Tech.

By far my favorite professor I've had at Tech. His lectures are interesting, and he genuinely cares about students. I've taken several of his classes, and he consistently gives about 50 pages of reading HW per class for the first half of the semester and then only assigns movies for the second half. He's a hard grader, but he wants you to succeed.

Santesso has a really fun lecture style. He's pretty current and is a funny guy. He's very clear about expectations and is really good with feedback. He is a pretty harsh grader. Forget everything you've ever learned about writing and get ready to learn how to write his way. He makes you work for your grade, but if you try you'll make an A.

I loved the structure of the class and the unified theory across multiple mediums. Dr. Santesso is excellent at keeping his class engaged during lecture, but is less deft with Q&A. He's good about responding to email if he feels it warrants a reply. Take the class, it'll make you a better scholar and you'll actually want to attend.
Awesome Professor. Makes class really fun to go to. Not very helpful emailing, but very helpful with assignment feedback. Do the work and you should do great in this class
He knows what he is talking about and makes lecture bearable. Doesn't hurt that he is hot. Recommend to anyone to take a class with him.
Best teacher ever! I really enjoyed the class. Just the right amount of difficulty and he is a very fair grader.

He kept lectures entertaining and was very enthusiastic about the class. We read about 4 or 5 Fantasy novels because of the class's topic and wrote a good bit but it was an awesome class. I loved attending every day. Definitely recommend.
He got the editor of Aqua Teen and Squidbillies to come talk to our class about villians.  He's awesome.

Professor Santesso is an excellent teacher. His lectures are entertaining (not mandatory but you should probably go to all of them because he gives pop quizzes that count as a final). Even though it's a hard class he's very helpful. I failed all the quizzes but ended up with an A. Definitely recommend.
Probably one of the best professors I've ever had here! Knows what he's talking about and is very approachable!

Strategic Brand Management with Professor Hackett has been one of my favorite courses taken at Tech. If you show up, read the book, and do good work on the presentations, you will no doubt get an A in the class. Professor Hackett is an incredible lecturer and professor, and I cannot recommend this class enough.

Incredible guy, incredible professor. This class was extremely applicable to the real world, and it was also probably the most engaging class I've ever had. Read the book very closely to make an A on the exam, but trust that it isn't as bad as he makes it sound. Super clear grading criteria. Fair amount of work (all done in class), but worthwhile

Dr. Hackett is incredible and very knowledgeable with a great background in brand management. He really cares about students learning the content. His lectures are interesting and the class is really only focused on two projects and one exam. Definitely READ THE BOOK to do well on the exam. Definitely recommend.

I absolutely loved his class. His lectures were very engaging and he uses real life examples. The book is not your ordinary boring text - it's very interesting and easy to read/understand. I would 100% recommend taking professor Hackett. You will learn a lot.

Really caring professor and engaging lecturer. He cares a lot about student feedback and always gave us time to discuss and voice concerns/ "I wish you had done this..." about the way his assignments were structured and presented to us, after an assignment was over. Listens and implements the changes too. Loved the course, had lots of group work.
The professor is a former P&G brand guy who connects theory to application in a way that's easy to understand. My favorite class at Georgia Tech!
Majority of your grade in this class will be a project where you work closely with a company of your choosing. Class times is super interesting and really fun.

Dr. Levine is an amazing lecturer and professor. For his Stem Cell Policy & Ethics class you have to write policy memos and he is very clear on what is needed to be addressed. He critiques your policy with worthy comments so you know how to fix. He is very accessible out of class and is willing to work with you. Definitely would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Levine is an amazing professor. He's very accessible and knowledgeable, and he cares a lot for his students. He only grades by a few assignments so don't slack and you'll be fine. Final was a take home exam and major grades were group research papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: please do not take this Professor. He doesn't care about all his students and he is not helpful at all when you ask him questions.

Definitely work the old tests and find those answers yourself in order to study for the tests. His tests are just as detailed as the practice tests with some of the same questions. IMO, lecture was somewhat boring, but you need the attendance grade. 3 tests. 2 papers. Attendance. Discussion section.

He's the best teacher I had at Tech. For an ethics class, he's surprisingly unbiased about... everything. This makes his lecture interesting, as he gives different perspectives on many controversial issues. There are clickers, so attend class. Difficulty level is fair, and I received an A fairly easily, even though I didn't give it my all.
Class is interesting and you don't really have to do the reading. Attendance is only necessary to do like 1 PRS questions per class. Also, he is really really attractive.

Class is very interactive which is fun. HIs grading can be weird, but is always accessible and he just wants to see students try their best. Heavy reading, but you can finesse it easily.. He's really invested in his topic which made the class more fun. Participate, put some effort, and you'll get the A. DO NOT BUY THE WOVEN TEXTBOOK FIND THE PDF.

The grades in this class are mostly projects, each project is different so it's a little more interesting than writing papers. Dr. Colton is really passionate about his subject and his feedback is really helpful. I was struggling in this class for a bit but with the chance for revisions, it helped my grade a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Not that many grades just projects. Gives lots of feedback on your projects and you're allowed to revise one project I only got a few more points when I fixed a major issue tho. You're allowed to miss 3 classes and there's a participation grade at the end so I guess if you miss more it'll affect that. We had books but we didn't use them too much.

Unorganized, no communication it seems between her and TAs. 3 exams no drop, no extra credit offered and says she doesnt believe in curves. Unwilling to meet or answer questions at times. Exams are extremely difficult and lecture is too vague. Nothing prepares you for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is a horrible teacher. The way that the test are written doesn't correlate to the lectures given in class . The point distribution on the test is ridiculous (15 questions and written response the written response is 22 point! out if the 35 pt test.
