The way that she grade as well is completely ridiculous if your response does not match you fail.

She's great. She doesn't lecture too much, but when she does she does a fantastic job. She provides interesting videos and gives us fun group exercises. We were given everything we could need to succeed in the class. As long as you show up to class and do the online assignments, an A is attainable. I definitely recommend taking Dr. Angra.

I know that my previous review was deleted from this page, somehow. Johnson is the worst professor that I have ever had at GT. He's rude and condescending, and he's impossible to talk to about grades. He pretends to care with his "motivational" lectures, but when you try to talk to him, he is very rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall an ok professor. Pop quiz on the topics he just went over in the same lecture, but they're not a big portion of the grade. While homeworks aren't mandatory, completing them will definitely help for exams. Pay attention to lectures and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Johnson's lectures are boring and he's not lenient with grading/extensions, but he's pretty fair. Not hard to get an A if you 1) Go to lectures and write down every in-class example problem (they are re-used in quizzes and exams), and 2) Participate in lecture (he will exempt students from the FInal who have participated and have high 80s.)

content of this class is easy but the grading scheme is rather unforgiving and weighs heavily on tests. Lectures are boring but attendance is required. No homework to turn in which is nice. If you have taken AP stats this shouldn't be a hard class but 1 or 2 mistakes might drag your grade down by a lot.

The worst teacher his students would ever have, for their whole lives. He is rude, both in person and in emails. His syllabus and grade distribution is def the worst ever. If you take a course with him prepare for a C even if you are used to As.

He writes the positive review here, and it is funny that he thinks he can trick us doing that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bad prof, that's all you need to know. He was an army general and def acts like it: extremely unforgiving. Grades are based on quizzes, and exams. He randomly decided to make Quiz 3 due at 8am instead of 11:59pm (like the first 2) and said he could do nothing about the 0's that many students received. In all interactions I had, he was very rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class can easily be self-studied. Lectures are very boring but attendance is basically required. He's rude in emails.

Pros:
- clear about what is expected out of a question/exam content
- exams are re-written in-class problems and HW questions
- get to make a formula sheet
- if you do HW and attend lectures you will get an A

Cons:
- exams and attendance are a HUGE portion of the grade
- you NEED to attend lectures or you will not get a good grade
- kind of boring
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: idk how hard the class is over the fall but i took this course during the summer and it was a joke. Don't get me wrong, the course material wasn't the easiest to understand, but with 4 people so far we haven't had any real exams. Our first exam we all took together as a class and he just gave us all 100s. Do with this information what you will.

Johnson pretended to care, but it's just a facade. In every conversation, he was passive aggressive and occasionally downright rude. His lectures are awful. He doesn't teach, just works examples with no explanation. You have to answer participation questions (graded on accuracy) and pop quizzes the same day he "taught" the material. Exams are ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Your grade will definitely not reflect your knowledge of statistics. It will be the result of the quickness by which you can correctly answer newly taught topics. The tests are easy, but the grading system, with so much weight on unannounced quizzes and participation for which you are given 2 minutes if you are lucky. 

Worst syllabus ever! Avoid
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very, very, very tough grader. Barely got any partial credits at all even though some questions showed understandings of the concepts, and the participation in this class can actually determine your final average grade. He may be a great person, but he is not a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Most of the 5-star reviews are written by himself which is pretty funny. Attendance is mandatory so if you miss one, you could be heavily penalized for as much as 2% of your grade. The exams question are easy, one can never listen in class and get easy 100s on exams. He will waive the final if your grade is 80% and above for every section. Avoid

He writes his own reviews on here so any of the 4/5 star ratings are most likely him. There were attendance quizzes and if you got them wrong you got a 0 for your attendance. I know a student was late to 1 exam and he held that over her head the entire semester. Horrible professor and horrible human being.

Tough but fair is probably an accurate description. Speaking from personal experience, he accommodates requests within reason as long your not trying to get out of exams. Even though participation might bring your grade down, the class had a pretty good curve and rewarded those who put effort into the class. However, other sections may be easier.

ISYE 3770 with this professor was a very frustrating experience because the grading was very harsh. Even small mistakes were heavily penalized, which made it difficult to earn a good grade in the class. Unless you are willing to put in a lot of extra work and have thick skin when it comes to grading, don't take his class.

The course is fairly easy as long as students show up to class every day for clicker questions and pay attention to the lectures. Professor Johnson runs through many, many example problems very quickly during class which are very similar to what will be on the tests and quizzes. Overall, Professor Johnson seems to be a caring and respected teacher.

You have to show up to classes at 8, which is the worst thing, but otherwise, he is amazing. He explained the materials very carefully and was easy to understand. As long as you can do the problems from the book and lecture examples, you will be well prepared for a quiz. The quiz problems are fair, and the grading is also fair.

Around the first week of classes, Ron Johnson claimed to be part of the OSI board. However, upon inspection of his rate my professor page, I have found an instance on December 5th, 2019 where General Johnson tries to impersonate students to inflate his rating. Many similar phrases were used, including references to "clickers". Don't take his class

Super cool dude. You have to show up to class. He grades on turning point participation, and he sets a radius from his computer, so you have to be in class to answer the questions. Otherwise, the material in class is easy.

His lectures are quick, so you NEED to stop him when you have a question. He is caring in class, but very terrible responses on emails, so email the TA's. He has participation questions during lecture, and your grade is pretty much determined by your tests. You can exempt the final if you have an A. Teaches you what you need for the exams.

His grade distribution and how he grades participation is abysmal and completely ruined the easy A that is ISYE3770. His avg GPA is .8 below other profs and, at 2.86, is lower than the avg GPA of many notoriously difficult classes. He simply doesn't understand how to structure a class. Don't be like me, check a prof's avg GPA before it's too late.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Johnson is one of the most understanding professors Ive had here at tech, he cares for his students well being in and out of the class. He attempts to make lecture a little more interesting but at the end of the day its still math so you can only do so much.

He is not a nice professor and does not cut you any slack. He's difficult in emails and is a tough grader considering your grade is determined by a few quizzes and two tests. He's not nice in the slightest and is the farthest thing from caring. The class isn't impossible by any means but you're going to have to rely on yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: General Johnson knows his material inside and out. He teaches quickly during class, going through dozens of practice problems, but he will always stop and clarify if someone has a question. Go to class, sit in the front, and participate in calling out answers/next steps during practice problems. Exams/quizzes contain 0 extraneous material.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This professor was the rudest and demeaning professor I have ever had in my entire life. The way he emails you back is extremely rude. He pretends like he wants students to succeed by saying encouraging things during class, but the course grade is based on two exam grades, pop quizzes, and mandatory participation. Avoid him at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had him in fall 2020, and I didn't enjoy going to his class to say the least. He was very rude to students during lectures if they asked questions during lecture and in emails. Taking stats with him means putting your entire grade on 2 exams and the quizzes (which are very hard to do well on bc they usually have 2-5 questions).

He's disrespectful and demeaning. He takes the power trip of running a required class too far. He makes the course complicated by not giving students marked up slides in order to encourage attendance. In short, he doesn't care if his students succeed, but if they do he takes credit cause it was in his "way". Won't plan quizzes so constant stress.

Quizzes and exams are extremely heavily weighted, miss one or do bad on one, you are guaranteed a non-A final grade. He doesn't take attendance but you will not have one single notes if you don't attend lectures. A very tough class with tough contents.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Heavily weighted on pop quizzes with 1-2 questions. No HW grade and only two exams. If you dont pay attention and fail quizzes you're done son. Could be an easy class but he makes it very difficult due to the grading scale.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He gives a lot of examples and is good about communication; however, he is demeaning to all students. The class is virtual so maybe he is just not good at communicating through piazza, but he is very incredibly rude. 100% would not recommend.

As a grad student, I've been taking college courses for 7 years. Prof Johnson is easily the worst/most disrespectful professor I have ever had. He makes it very clear to everyone that he has no sympathy or care in the world for the students. Quizzing students on material yet to be taught and mouthing off to students are my favorites.

Professor Johnson knows how to teach you stats. He is the best professor I have had at Tech! He is funny and really cares about his students. He gives pop quizzes and clickers, so as long as you go to class, they really help your grade and prepare you for exams.

Dr. Johnson has been my favorite professor at tech thus far! He teaches the material thoroughly, yet in an interesting way. Class is not mandatory, but he gives pop quizzes and clickers that really help your grade. The quizzes and exams are fair and based on the homework. This is definitely one of the few classes I have enjoyed going to.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Johnson will teach you statistics. Many people really hate him because he is not nice to the students, almost to the point of making fun of us. However, his tests are fair and he does lots of examples, so I think he is a good teacher. He will let you skip the final if you have an A and makes you get a physical clicker.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Go to class each day + listen, you'll get an A. HW optional, pop quizzes. Get old exams/quizzes-he reuses them+do HW IMO: I HATED this man. He's arrogant + demeaning to students. If he's wrong or makes a mistake, he acts like he meant it + that the students are idiots for thinking he could be wrong. That said, he isn't unfair, but VERY IRRITATING
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: General Johnson is honestly the best professor I've had at Tech thus far. If you attend lecture and take good notes you'll be fine (he doesn't post annotated notes online as he writes on the board during lecture). The exams and quizzes are very fair and the hws really help you study. Take the class seriously and you'll be fine!

Honestly the best professor I've had at Tech so far. Very motivational and respects you if you work hard. Not gonna lie, this class is tough. But General Johnson tells you exactly what is required for you to get a good grade. The exams and quizzes are very fair and he never tries to trick you. Highly recommend taking his class.

Johnson is quite the character. He's a great guy but makes this class unnecessarily hard. Takes points off for technique despite getting the correct answer. His lectures are good, but it's very easy to get off task or doze off in the class. Uploaded slides don't have answers to the examples discussed. TA only met once a week for this class.

The general runs his class almost like a stats boot camp. He expects a lot from you while not always making these guidelines clear so he will take off many points for minor mistakes. Pretty much teaches from PPTs. Not friendly to students and sometimes outright demeaning. He does care a lot about the subject but I think he grew to dislike us.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: General Johnson is very enthusiastic about the subject matter even though it can seem dry at times. He does grade tough, but is reasonable since he tells you what he wants you to know. Overall, one of the best professors at Tech and he allows you to exempt the final if you have an A going into it.
He's stern, but he's an amazing professor. I enjoyed his class and actually felt like taking it seriously. He sincerely is very interested in the subject and in the student's learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The General is a natural communicator and he seems like a good dude. He does like his tough-guy reputation and relishes being inflexible, so check your syllabus before you email him. He tends to jam though the technical terms too fast for you to sort through it in lecture, but the homework is usually pretty helpful.
Great professor,  but very tough
MOTIVATIONAL

He is a great professor, he really cares about his students. HW is really heavy so it will require lots of work. The only bad thing about him is that he takes forever to grade stuff so you dont really have a way to know how you are doing in class, but in the end he gives everyone good grades just for the effort shown.

I learned a lot and I wouldn't change anything about my experiences. If you don't like the road you're on, pave a new one. Or find a different road. But I stuck with this road, meaning I didn't drop this class.
HOT. Easy enough if you pay attention, which is pretty difficult when you can't stop staring at those perfect eyes...

Prof. Das connects course material to real-world examples. She occasionally goes on tangents, drawing on her own experiences and broader scientific topics which makes the class fun. The class required significant studying. I appreciated the open-note format, though she mentioned that future offerings may be closed to internet access.

Instructor was an expert in the subject matter and taught with a lot of enthusiasm. There was lot of opportunities to score through homework, quizzes, and open exams to promote conceptual learning. However the lectures was fast pace with occasional misalignment between lectures and exams. The FRQ portion of the exams were hard.

The class was engaging and rewarding . Dr. Das's enthusiasm and emphasis on understanding the “why” behind complex pathways helped me move beyond memorization. The course felt like a meaningful exploration of metabolism pathway and strengthened my appreciation for biochemistry as I pursue medical school.
Dr. Das's class brings enthusiasm to every lecture. Its a like a morning cup of coffee. She made the first class of the day truly engaging, and she is really accessible to the students.

This class prepared me for metabolism and the TCA cycle, which is great for MCAT. Real-life examples made complex ideas fun and memorable. She didn't make us memorize TCA cycle which was a big relief.  The mechanistic approach in the class and challenging ‘what if' questions pushed my thinking. Overall, I liked the class.

Professor Das is an inspiring, and dedicated educator. She really makes you think. If you don't like critical thinking and synthesizing information then don't take the class. She truly cares about students' growth.

Dr. Das is an engaging professor who explains complex topics clearly, making learning smooth. Her class is applied, with thought-provoking exams that go beyond lectures. HWs are tough but graded easily. Extra credit helps a lot. TAs do all grading, so office hours help. Her class is structured, supportive, and manageable.

Course was reasonably organized, engaging, and intellectually stimulating. It is application-based, with problem sets and exams that emphasize critical thinking. There are also a lot of easy quizzes. The professor is supportive and creates an inclusive environment. Exams are challenging and office hours are helpful. Gets you ready for med school.

Professor Das is sweet and explains complex concepts clearly, making learning enjoyable. Her class is highly applied, with thought-provoking exams, even with open notes. She is respectful, inclusive, and genuinely cares about student success. TAs grade tough, attending office hours helps. She fosters a welcoming, supportive environment.

Exams are challenging but mildly predictable based on what she says in lecture. Application-heavy; nitpicky is a good description. Extra credit & recorded lectures are super helpful. TAs grade hw & exams so go to their office hours for help. I would recommend Dr. Das, she's very nice and knowledgable. TB not needed. Overall not stressful

GREAT slides. No textbook/external reading or work needed. Very prepared to teach. Exams are tricky and grading is kinda nitpicky (open note/slides though); little practice material given before exams. Very caring and sweet lady, she will help you / answer questions fast. Grading scheme seems scary, but so much extra cred offered it isnt too bad.

Dr. Das is a good professor who cares about her students. I do feel like the tests could be difficult because they were always much more advanced than what we talked about in class and there was no study material available besides your notes.

His lectures were unengaging and by the end of the semester there were probably less than 10 people who would show up. I had to self study all the topics for the midterm and final which ended up being fine. Most of the grades came from the homework/projects so that helped a lot. He also gave us 3% extra credit added to our overall grade.

He cares about the class and is helpful if you ask, but he struggles to connect with students or make the material engaging. Lectures are long slide walkthroughs not reflected on exams. You're expected to learn SQL, Excel, and Orange on your own. Practice exams help, but most learning is self-taught, and in class content is not helpful.
Very intellectual guy, just not know how to teach a class.

Really interesting class, he is a really chill and funny guy, but lectures were dry, but you don't really need them for the assignments. Cool to see new ways to make business processes better including work with AI agents. Mainly includes group and individual assignments on various ways to improve business processes and individual work in SAP.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: took him for 2210, literally so easy. i went into this class scared because of the previous rmp reviews but if you just study you'll do fine

Had Prof Gardiner for 2200 & 3745. He's a nice person, but very boring lecturer, so its hard to make yourself go to class. His exams are always tricky & require a ton of studying. He pulls from the readings for the non-coding part of exams. There is a project in 3745 as well as coding challenges and HW that help your grade a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dudes rude. Class is super boring

This rating is meant to help future students as well as Adrian Gardiner if he is reading this:
The teacher only taught about theory in the class, speaking at about 15 words per minute. He taught a total of about 3 classes on the technicals of excel and SQL which is OUTRAGEOUS considering the homeworks included FAR more than what we learned in class

Prof. Gardiner was a amazing professor! The lectures might be boring, but he tries his best to make it interesting! A lot of readings and memorization for the theory exams. SQL/excel exams were easy As and the homework had detailed instructions but it was more of learn it yourself. Overall, the class wasn't that difficult and there were EC

Professor Gardiner was very kind, however, kindness doesn't mean you know what you're doing. This class is very much a teach-yourself class when it comes to SQL and Excel, as the functions he taught in class were very beginner, but the functions required for homework were extremely advanced. This requires us to do most learning on our own.

The lecture videos were quite monotonous, so it was hard to focus. The slides and textbook are your best friend. Yes, you need to use both unless you're just a really good mcq test-taker. The SQL/Excel exams were doable As, but the theory exams & final were worth more and were difficult. He's willing to help with exam review. Hw was hard. No EC.

Horrible at writing exams. They are super nuanced and require absolute mastery of the material. There is often 2 or 3 correct answers. The HWs are long and complex. The lectures are dry and boring. Exams often require 15+ hours of study time. Hes just bad at writing exams. Do yourself a favor and take anyone else.

His lectures can be a little "boring snoring" (a phrase he uses) but he's a good professor and he cares if people learn and is willing to help outside of class. I feel like his class wasn't too difficult  as long as you're studying and doing the homework. I took him for 3745 (Python) and 4057 and he was pretty chill for ITM which can be intense.

If the goal of this class was to discourage the love of learning, 10/10. Professor should not be in a position to influence anyone with an impressionable mind. The plethora of Shein orders, antidepressant research, and suicide contemplation conducted by 95% of those in attendance should give any administrator pause in how this class runs. AVOID
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor gardiner is truly knowledgeable and incorporates applicable and relevant content into the course. Grading criteria is fair, though there is a vast amount of content covered for the conceptual side of the course, so don't fall behind. Overall, if you put in a decent amount of work, you should do fine.

knows his stuff, but lectures are boring. do not expect him to teach anything on the homework in class. the hw is incredibly hard and you pretty much have to teach yourself, which is very annoying. and the instructions on the homework can be more confusing than helpful sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Put enough time in this class, and an A is totally achievable. Work hard on homework/assignments, and Gardiner is very helpful in answering questions so long as you're not just trying to get easy answers. To study for exams, memorizing the lecture slides and using common sense is enough. Lectures are dry, but Gardiner is super caring and helpful.

One of my favorite professors at GT. Super kind, super helpful and accessible. He's seriously underrated here.  2210 is historically the hardest class in business school, but he made it super manageable. He also is freaking hilarious without trying. Exams (60%) are a piece of cake if you study the slides. R HW is a nightmare, but only 5%. 10/10 guy
Professor Gardiner is a really good professor, I would recommend taking his class.

Professor Gardiner really cares for his students and wants you to succeed. He is quick to respond to emails and answers all queries! I would recommend taking his course to learn a lot about information systems.
Professor Gardiner is not a tough grader, but you have to get ready for the exam for sure. His lecture is kind of boring, so it was hard to focus and wake up during the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Gardiner is a great professor! Very knowledgable on the topics at hand. His lecture style is more of a monologue, so it isn't for everyone, but you can tell he cares for students and wants you to succeed. Lots of homework/weekly assignments in this class but nothing too 'over-the top.' Highly recommended if you're into data analytics!

Professor Gardiner is really caring. He gave clear guidance on each homework and I learned many skills like R, Tableau, and SQL. He respond to emails fast and solves many questions. Great teachers! His lecture is not that interesting but it is his style. Recommend!

Boring lectures - I could barely stay awake in his classes. As a professor, he is very knowledgeable about SAP and friendly but just doesn't know how to engage with a class to keep everyone awake. It seems as if he is talking to himself during class, often forgets a lot of things as well. Lots of homework throughout the semester, tests are fair.

Adrian is the slowest, most boring professor at Scheller, but he knows his stuff. If you care about SAP and all that, this class will help you become well acquainted with it. However, the tests are very difficult because it is hard to gauge what he is trying to teach us in class.

I took 2 of his classes, MGT 2210 and MGT 4057. Can't speak for previous semesters, but his online class for Spring 2021 runs smoothly without technical interruptions. A really caring professor and actively tries to accommodate for many people, and will help you out if you communicate with him. Grading criteria is clear, and he is a good lecturer.

(Taken during COVID-19 Fall 2020.) Avoid him if possible. There is so much work. Especially during a semester where we all needed extra support from professors, he just drowned us in assignments and projects. Tests were incredibly hard. He also is incredibly hard to listen to, as he's incredibly monotone. Try another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took course online in fall 2020 due to coronavirus. Gardiner had no idea how to conduct an online course. He was extremely disorganized, often not telling us about assignments until two days before they were due. Software was needed to complete the assignments and he would forget to post download instructions to Canvas. Class isn't easy either.

Professor Gardiner is a very kind person. His lectures, however, are extremely boring and it's difficult to pay attention. The homework assignments are difficult, and if you don't study intensely for the test and know many details, you won't do well.

Very nice guy, very accessible through email/office hours. Not the greatest lecturer, and does take attendance, but the homework assignments (Excel/SQL/R) aren't too bad. Tests are the hardest part of the class but even those only require a few hours of studying for a B; since nobody pays attention during lecture they require reading the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Best EE professor at Georgia Tech

Professor Adibi was awesome. Had him for ECE 3025 (not listed as a code) and was one of my favorite ECE classes. Amazing lectures, covers a lot of ground but in a way that made me interested in the subject and engaged the entire period. Exams were tough but he always had review sessions outside of class plus lots of EC.

Dr. Adibi is a fantastic lecturer who is clearly very passionate about the material in this course. Participation can grant you extra credit. While the homeworks are challenging, they are graded generously and also provide opportunity for extra credit. Exams are fair so long as you understand the examples from class.
Not knowledgeable, does not teach what would help you in future; try keep students interested by giving credits, while skipping his responsibility to teach useful material

He is a great teacher. He teaches very difficult topics in a way that everybody can understand. He asks questions during the class and offers extra points for that. For his grad courses, you can easily get A. So respectful, friendly, and caring professor. One of the best teachers I have ever had during my education.

Great guy, with a great way of teaching the course. Gives you extra points for answering correctly in class. Doing all your homework can get you up to 5% extra credit. Not an exceedingly strict grader either. Very approachable and all in all, a great teacher.

Great teacher, easy grading policies - 2 grading schemes based on whether or not you want to do the homework (+5 points if you do). Wants everybody to learn alot and do well in the class. Hands out extra credit points for class participation.
This guy is great!

Ada teaches super important OS fundamentals pretty well and provides a ton of insight into how the systems we learn about have affected the world. Midterm + final are pretty difficult, and there is some ambiguity on projects, but overall one of the better classes I've taken.

I strongly believe that anyone with any passion for computing should take this class, you learn about so many foundational papers and implement some of them in very interesting papers. Only downside is the TAs are not too helpful as they all say different things and constantly grade wrong but can be rectified with a piazza post

This course has the workload of 2-3 courses and needs to be rebalanced. Though the projects are super hard, the tests (midterm + finals) make up for 50% of the grade which is unfair as not everyone tests well. I also frequently ended up watching lectures on the same subject on Udacity to understand things.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ada is a great professor who is able to break down complex papers into easy to digest lectures. (while she does highly recommend actually reading the papers, I was able to get through using only lectures.) The tests and projects can be difficult, but overall I learned a lot from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took GIOS through the online MSCS. Projects in the class were excellent & very challenging. Unfortunately, the grading is imbalanced with the midterm & final weighted 55% of the final grade. The exams are also short, poorly worded, & almost no feedback, so they dampen an otherwise excellent class. I really wish they'd rebalance the class.

Prof. Ada cares about her students. She lectures well and knows the material inside out. Grades her tests very leniently. The projects we did (DS labs) were difficult, but rewarding. The TA was also very knowledgeable. Definitely would take again!

Difficult to understand as she speeds through topics in rote fashion. Can't keep up unless you are already familiar with the material, but then what's the point of her teaching? Basically worthless if you are actually trying to learn something. You're better off studying a good textbook, otherwise, the class only serves to validate prior learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: The projects are the most difficult projects I have done in the grad school. There are 46 papers to read in the entire semester. The exams were not so difficult but to prepare for the exams it takes a lot of time.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Awesome summer class! Learned so much about sensing methods and designing future devices. Assignments were engaging, and Prof. Adams was generous with guidance and resources. Put in the effort, and you'll create a project worthy of your résumé. Highly recommend for anyone interested in health sensing!

Super hands-on course with real health sensing tools like ECG, EMG, and RESP. Projects were practical and flexible, and there were no exams, just meaningful work. Alex is an amazing professor who genuinely cares and provides excellent feedback. One of the most unique and useful classes I've taken at Tech. Highly recommend!

Great intro to health sensing with hands-on use of ECG, EMG, RESP, and more. Alex is a supportive instructor who gave thoughtful one-on-one feedback and cared about our success. One of the most unique MS courses at Tech—covering biosignals, sensors, software, and many topics of your choice. No prior experience needed. Would definitely take again!

Alex is a very kind professor. I had minimal coding knowledge going into this class, and he and the TAs made sure I was supported throughout the whole course. The class emphasizes process over a perfect final project; if you show effort and growth through your work, you'll get a good grade (and likely learn some new skills, too!)

This is an enjoyable, project-based course with a strong hands-on component. Through practical labs, we learned various techniques for processing health-related signals. Professor Adams is approachable and fairly lenient with grading. He's also very supportive when it comes to helping refine the research topic for our final paper.

I really enjoyed Health Sensing and Interventions with Professor Adams. The class was interactive and project-focused, with hands-on work using real health sensing hardware. No exams, just meaningful projects that helped me apply what I learned. Highly recommend for anyone interested in health tech and biomedical applications!

I could write a dissertation about how badly Prof Adams handled this class. Opaque grading criteria, always late to class, docks grade points without explanation, barebones lectures, little to no meaningful feedback on assignments, left all the actual work to his poor TAs. I get it was the first time this class was offered, but good lord. Avoid it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 10/10 Love this guy.

The best thing about him was he didn't read of the powerpoint and made us understand the lecture but one thing is he writes most of the stuff on white board so if you sit really back you probably wouldn't see it clearly but overall still the best one I have had at tech
Answers all questions throughly and doesn't read off a ppt. My goat
Great teacher. Clearly passionate on what he is teaching. He explained everything really well and did a great job of creating connection between the class and real world applications.

Even without being a professor and teaching for one semester, he is the best you can get at GT: Easily understood lectures, numerous metaphors for concepts making them easy to grasp. As long as you attend lecture (they are a good time), you will get an A. He is just that good. More professors need to look towards how he teaches o7
HE CAN AUSTIN MY ADAMS I LOVE THIS MAN SO FUNNY. NOT A REAL PROFESSOR BUT HE'S THE PEOPLE'S PROF!

Got put on the spot to teach 2110 and did an amazing job with it. Super funny guy and very knowledgeable about the content, he had no problem answering any question thrown his way even if it was out of the scope of the class. Class is very project heavy (50% of grade) and content is not a walk in the park but Adams made it enjoyable and manageable.

The GOAT. Not even a real Professor, but he's a Professor in my heart. Piazza posts were fire, class was fire. Real zoomer energy, super approachable. Probably my favorite teacher this year; knows what he's talking about too, so not just a set of jokes in a trench coat but actual good educator. Wish he could teach the rest of my sysarch classes.
my heart goes out to this man
godbless his lectures and office hours
Greatest esquire.

This class has very little example and lots of derivations. He tends to repeat derivations that he already did the class before rather than doing actual examples. He's very accessible and helpful outside of class but he can be a bit condescending at times if you don't understand immediately. Overall he's pretty good.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great Prof. Extremely helpful outside of class. I struggled in Defbods, but he helped me out a lot.
His lectures were really good and he posts all of his notes online. Tests were fair, study the homework and practice problems and you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great at teaching the content of the class. Makes it very easy to understand.

Dr. Kumar is an incredibly kind professor, and he makes the material super easy to understand. Sometimes his lectures can be boring, but he posts all his notes later on. He was always willing to talk after class. The tests were pretty easy if you did the practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Awesome professor Biochem 2 is a p hard class. Grade is just 90% exams and 10% quizzes - quizzes are open note. Exams are straightforward for the most part but you definitely need to study for them and he provides a fair study guide and practice exam. He's really knowledgeable on the topics and good at explaining!

reviews.comment: Prof is knowledgeable and passionate about the content. Course is exam heavy so if you don't do well on one it may be very hard to recover but the level of difficulty is fair. Only complaint is the pacing of the semester, we spent way too much time on easy topics and flew through difficult concepts and processes. Funny & engaging otherwise.

Dr. Oyelere is an extremely educated man that KNOWS biochem but can not teach it well. This class was very poorly paced with him FLYING through the harder concepts in class. Would be better if this class was recorded and his teaching SLOWED DOWN. Near the end, I left class confused. Also he really didn't know how to use/organize Canvas rip

reviews.comment: Exams ask about small details he covers while on tangents during lecture. Uploaded notes are incomplete and surface-level; no lecture recordings are uploaded. reviews.comment: I'm guessing that the difference between current and previous semesters was the modality, but if you can take him in person, avoid it if you can. Lectures were extremely poorly paced, and tests were badly designed, which doesn't make sense for a class almost entirely graded by exams. Very little structuring or support materials, and no crib sheets.

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs for this class. Terrible lecturer, no practice or homework, and we are behind Biochem 1. Worst communication I've seen in a while. Even with GT documentation, he will not follow up for exam remakes. Class grade comprised of exams only and two random concept quizzes. Poorly paced and condescending. Tests don't reflect content.
