reviews.comment: This class is so weird. Nothing feels to match up and exams take up so much of the grade. If you can take another class, do it!
Super bad lectures and exams. Cant understand anything he is saying and then exams are completely different.

Organic Chem is a hard class, but Professor Oyelere made it interesting and possible to learn. He is very passionate about what he teaches which inspires me to learn the material. If you read the recommended book and use his lecture notes, you can do well in his class. Only thing I'd say is he speaks relatively fast and grades on few assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Oyelere is an amazing professor. He's very kind and wants to see his students succeed. His tests are fair and test knowledge mainly from his lectures. Best way to succeed in class is to study his lecture slides and review corresponding content from book.

Loved Dr. Oyelere. He is extremely passionate and very willing to help students understand the material. His tests are moderately hard, but he will always test what he covers. Won't be an easy A but won't be a hard A either. Fast-paced lectures; you'll get through a lot of material in a short period of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Oyelere was a very fair professor. His tests are moderately difficult, but nothing that you wouldn't expect. He provides sample exams and opportunities for extra points. However, lecture is sometimes hard to follow as he has a strong accent and can talk very fast. He is very approachable and is enthusiastic about Biochem.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is very enthusiastic about biochemistry and you can see that when he teaches. He made me love the subject even more despite its inherent difficulty. He will help you if you ask. Attend every lecture, pay attention and take notes and you'll be good. Accent takes getting used to but you do get used to it.
Grades incredibly harshly, test averages were in the low 60's high 50's. I took the course since many people gave him a high RMP rating, but I honestly regretted taking thermo with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Steinberg is phenomenal. AE2010 thermo-fluids is an extremely difficult course, but Steinberg made the material very clear. The homeworks are hard, as are the tests, but the TAs and professor grade rather generously. The lectures are optional, but I strongly recommend going. If it is too early for you, the professor posts the lectures online.

Genuinely great professor. The course isn't easy, but Steinberg really does his best to make sure his students understand both conceptually and practically. As long you as also put in the same effort as he does, you'll do fine. Tests are open note, open book, so they can get pretty difficult

Steinberg was a great professor, and his lecture style was beneficial to my learning. He explains concepts which we then apply in the homeworks (41% of total grade), but also does a few basic examples in class to help students. Tests are extremely difficult, but open notes and textbook, and he is a very lenient grader. Would recommend taking him
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Steinberg is a decent professor. Early on, he mainly lectures without examples, making concepts harder to apply. However, he improves over time, balancing examples and lectures better. Homework is challenging and heavily weighted. Exams are very tough, but the class is curved, so doing well is possible if you do a LOT of practice.

He somehow made me pay attention in an 8 am lecture. His examples were great, and the slides and lectures were very informative. The grading structure is very forgiving, as is the curve at the end of the class, and he tends to be very reasonable with how much homework he assigns.

Prof Steinberg is flat out amazing. 2010 is now one of my FAVORITE courses and a huge amount of that credit goes to him. He connects the material to the real world and for me that was one of the most interesting parts of lecture. He always answers questions positively and is very caring and involved in helping his students learn.

Professor Steinberg is one of the best professors I've had at Tech so far. Along with being super knowledgeable, he's also incredibly caring: I had a panic attack before our exam, and he let me step out and take it at another time. 2010 is notoriously difficult, but if you go to the lectures and stay caught up with the material you will be fine.

Other reviews are correct in that Steinberg is very knowledgeable and knows the material well. That said, he's definitely still approachable as he really enjoys teaching and engaging with students about the material. Exams and material will push you. Exam averages were around a 65, but ~80 is an A. Overall great professor.

Exams designed to make you think and averages were ~60. However, grades are determined by HWs (worth more than exams). Steinberg is very knowledgeable about the material and is always willing to answer questions. Don't be intimidated by him, he wants you to succeed. Very approachable outside of class and go to lecture. Take him, you'll learn a lot

Prof. Steinberg's exams are awful. Problem sets can take upwards of 10 hours, and the exams have questions that could have been on the problem sets. He also uses mixed units on his test problems, that seem designed to trick you. Generally, he is accessible, and seems to want you to succeed, but is not lenient on any sort of grading whatsoever.

Prof. Steinberg might initially come across as intimidating, but he is actually a great professor and really accessible for questions. You can tell he puts effort into lectures and making you understand the topic. Going to class is my biggest tip, you'll learn a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: During remote instruction, gave quizzes that required going to lecture AND live office hours. They were recorded with accessible notes, but this increased the time investment of this class from 3 hrs to 5 hrs. Final exam average was a 45, no curve, with an A being >80. Very difficult class with dense subject material, but you learn a LOT.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A great professor. He always tried to do a small demo at the beginning of class (particularly nice for an 8AM) and his lectures are very interesting. He clearly likes the things he teaches and is very knowledgeable about them. One things is that his tests are very hard (average between 50-60) but heavily curves them and your final grade.
Interesting lectures. He knew what he was talking about and could answer any questions. The tests are rough, averages being 50's and 40's; however the class is heavily curved.

Since the other two comments are misleading (Gesundheit), heres the truth. First Test Avg 52 after the curve, and it was big. Second Test Avg 58 after curve. The class was always dead silent. Steinberg is intimidatingly smart which I think prevented anyone from asking Qs. He cares ,maybe. In office hours,I sometimes felt belittled.
Professor Steinberg is an awesome and caring professor who wants all of his students to succeed. Gesundheit!!

His ratings are high for a reason. He makes lectures for a course that is almost strictly memorization entertaining. Anatomy always ends up with the worst lecture times and locations but it is always worth going. Attendance isn't mandatory, but I would strongly recommend going as he sometimes tests material not in the slides. Very caring guy too.

I was really struggling with anatomy and school/life  in general. He was the only professor that took the time with me outside of class to help me. I will forever be grateful for this man. I wish more professors on campus cared half as much as Dr. Decker did.

Hands down my favorite course at GT. I appreciated the course was very challenging and I was up for it. Dr. Decker takes difficult concepts and breaks them down in a unique way so we understand. We just finished drawing the brachial plexus and although challenging it was fun to draw along with him on the whiteboard. I can't wait for Human Pathology
Amazing lecturer, easy tests based off his slides, and overall great guy. He's also more biology-focused than the other 1040 professors if you're into that

Human Pathology was hands down the most useful class I've taken at GT in my four years. I working a summer job in a hospital in my hometown and I'm able to shadow a cardiologist. The cardiologist said, “where the hell did you learn all of this?” I simply said, “Dr. Decker at Georgia Tech.

WE LOVE DR. DECKER! Genuinely the best prof I've had at GT. Lectures are engaging, go to them! Even if you can pass the class without attending, the things he says in person will stick with you for the rest of your medical career. Exams are a bit tough, make sure you deeply understand the content and are not just memorizing. Flashcards are a must!
He has an insane amount of respect for his students and offered really cool extra credit opportunities. The lectures are kind of boring but prepare you well for the tests.

Dr. Decker was my favorite professor at Tech. He was very involved in his students' improvement and I highly recommend him for any class. The class requires memorization but after taking anatomy with him it was much easier. Physiology is a plus to have before or during this class.

Lectures aren't mandatory but contain the important information so attendance is heavily encouraged. He is very knowledgeable on the subject and genuinely wants to help students learn, an A is definitely achievable with regular attendance since his lectures are digestible and he tells you everything you need to know for exams
I'm taking human pathology with Dr. Decker.  The content is med school based, and I feel very prepared to take pathology when I get to Johns Hopkins this fall. Amazing professor!
Best anatomy and biology professor!!!!

One of the most respected professors on campus. You get out what you put into the course. It's a tough class, but taking Dr. Decker created a wonderful learning environment; even for 8 in the morning. Take any class he offers.

Dr. Decker is a great anatomy professor. He makes it engaging and interesting, which is hard to do. Weaving together personal stories, history, and facts, he makes lectures worth attending even at 8AM. Tests have a lot of content and are closed note, however, they are designed fairly. Great prep for pre-health people; I cannot recommend him more.

Amazing lecturer and tests are pretty straightforward. The resources provided outside of lectures are very lacking so make sure to attend lectures (no notes available outside of class and difficult to self study).
Anatomy has been difficult but I'm doing well. I wouldn't get behind in the course. One of my GT favorites I've taken

Favorite class yet! It was not too hard. Just study the lecture slides. It was very interesting if you are pre med. He does interesting in class demos with volunteers. He is so nice and helpful if you have questions. I had to reschedule an exam once and he made it very easy.

Dr. Decker provides amazing lectures to the students because he tells real, applicable stories during class. The course consists of a midterm (in-person), 5 quizzes (online), 3-4 case studies, and a final exam (in-person). You should attend class because he highlights and narrows down important information that will be on the assessments.

Dr. Decker's human anatomy is a tough class, but very important if you plan on going to med school. I took the course last year and plan to take his human pathology course this spring. I highly recommend his classes. He genuinely cares for his students and is very approachable.

I loved Dr. Decker. He truly wants everyone to do well in his class and gives you plenty of opportunities to succeed. Beware however, I took this class Late Summer 2024 and it moved incredibly quickly. Exams were in person and tough. Make sure you prepare!
Dr D. Was a very caring professor and mentor, the class was valuable.

I had Dr.Decker for the Ignite short summer semester and he was AMAZING. Even though there was more emphasis on tests because of the short term, tests were easy and had questions based on lectures and study guides. He is also a very caring professor who radiates good energy. Plus he gives plenty of extra credit.

Was a great lecturer and pretty funny although conversations can get sidetracked sometimes. Was very nice on the final by making it pretty easy (compared to the quizzes). Very clearly passionate about what he teaches and it makes the class very enjoyable.

Dr. Decker is a wonderful lecturer and amazing resource for pre-med students! His knowledge of medical schools (which he talks about during lectures) is insightful into the application process. He also knows how to make class both fun and engaging. The course is hard, but very doable given proper studying!

Dr. Decker is phenomenal! I have never met a professor who cares more about his students. Attendance isn't mandatory but I would highly recommend still going to classes as the quizzes do have material not on his slides. There is now an in-person final, but if you keep up with the material throughout the semester, it's very doable. Highly recommend!

Such an inspiring professor for anyone planning on going into the healthcare field. This was one of the few lectures I really looked forward to attending each week. Quizzes are online and a little difficult, but the final was in person and was pretty basic. He is funny and his lectures are super interesting. AMAZING PROFESSOR!!

Dr. Decker is very knowledgeable about anatomy and highly respected in the field. He is an awesome lecturer, and I looked forward to going to class each week. Attendance is not mandatory, but you must attend lecture to understand content because lecture slides do not provide all relevant content. Quizzes were all online. Great professor!
very nice, funny teacher. you must take the class honestly throughout its duration or you will not do well on its now in-person final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As the course just ended, I can give my honest assessment. Human Pathology with Dr. Decker was a phenomenal experience. My best friend is in his 2nd year of med school, and I showed him my course notes. He said they cover the same material. I was never prouder of Georgia Tech to hear that. This course will prepare you for sure. I love this man!

I wasn't a fan of Dr. Decker for anatomy, but he loves the pathology course and it really shows in his teaching. Classes were entertaining, engaging, and informational! Exams were tough and a lot of memorization but definitely doable!

Dr Decker is the most amazing professor I have ever had at Georgia Tech. He inspires you to learn and is so motivating and caring. If you go to lectures and take notes he tells you exactly what you need to know to succeed in this class. I plan on taking every class at Tech he offers just because of how amazing of a professor he was.

I am a second  year medical student at Vanderbilt, and it was Dr. Decker's human pathology course that helped me choose cardiothoracic surgery as my future specialty. The man is a gift and an inspiration to all who take his courses. Easily the most practical course in the GT pre-health undergraduate curriculum.

Amazing professor. Attendance isn't mandatory and all assignments are taken/turned in online, but it is absolutely worth it to go to class. His lectures are entertaining and he made me so excited to learn about the topics covered in this class. The material is easy to follow along with if you pay attention.

Great professor and a funny lecturer, he can go off track and fall behind in lectures sometimes by telling stories, but his stories are great and they are worth it. He occasionally brings in organs/bones in class for students to inspect. All quizzes are online, and our final was online. There are 7 quizzes 4 case studies and then the final.

I am in medical school and took Dr. Decker's Human Pathology course in 2021. Out of all the classes I took at GT, this class was the most applicable to what I am learning in medical school. My current pathology professor has been very impressed with my knowledge. Thank you, Dr. Decker! You are a GT treasure.

Dr. Decker is one of the greatest professors there is. His lectures are always incredible and never fail to make you laugh, and he teacesh anatomy in a way that makes it easy for anyone to learn and I couldn't imagine taking it with anyone else. If you have the opportunity to take his class, you have to do it, it's an experience you shouldn't miss.

I was recently accepted at the Emory School of Medicine. Dr. Decker, and his Human Pathology course, gave me the confidence to apply to such a great medical school. His knowledge as a human anatomist is unsurpassed. I will never forget what this man has done for me and my classmates pursuing medicine as a career. All CT is derived from mesenchyme!

Dr. Decker is a great choice for anatomy. He's so knowledgable and passionate, and never fails to make lecture engaging. It is helpful to come to class since some of the information is sometimes not listed on the slides and the slides can sometimes be disorganized. That being said though, I would definitely recommend him to anyone!
I took this class over the summer and he managed to make lectures for entertaining and easy to understand. All exams where taken over canvas at home. Great guy.

It's helpful to come to class as you may not always find everything you need on slides, but he keeps lectures very engaging and interesting. You can tell he really cares, and he's happy to help students with anything even outside of course material. You certainly need to keep up with material but the course load isn't too difficult.
I was going through a very difficult time last semester, and Dr. Decker was the only professor that took the time to listen and encourage me. I will forever be grateful. Just a great human being!
I took Dr. Decker for human pathology. Hands down the most useful pre-med course at GT. Loved every minute of it.

Decker is the best! This class was more focused towards anatomy and biology than I originally anticipated, but it was honestly pretty easy. I took it during the summer and all of our tests were online and there was no final. He's very passionate about the subject and a great person, and the class is an easy A.

Hilarious and understands that most people are there because the class is required. He makes it easy to do well in his class and the lectures are actually interesting, even if you don't care about anatomy. Also provides really cool out-of-class experiences that you normally wouldn't get as a non-science major (like holding a human heart).
I love this man!
Easy class- light work and easy exams.
Took him during summer semester and he made lectures interesting. 10/10 recommend
He's the best

Dr. Decker is as humorous as he is kind, and he's as kind as he is smart. And he is very smart. As for his lectures, they're informative and clear. You'll know what the tests assess, and if he goes on about another topic, he'll make it clear whether you need to know about it. 

Also, enjoy the day 1 icebreaker. You'll feel right at home!
He is leaving tech to teach anatomy in medical school. I took him  in 2018, during New Zealand/Australia/Fiji study abroad, and it was a great class. Thank you for everything, Dr. Decker!!

Pathology was an excellent experience. I am so glad I got to take anatomy and pathology with him. I hope it's not true, but there is a rumor he is leaving GT this year to teach at a med school out of state. He will be missed and I wish him well.

I had Prof Decker for human anatomy and have really enjoyed the course. A must if you are going to med school. he seems to have the class geared in that direction. Kind and considerate to his students.

Very passionate about anatomy and really engaging in class. Make sure to write down everything he says as his quiz questions are pulled directly from his lectures. 4 straightforward case studies and 8 or so quizzes that can trick you up if you aren't studying/paying attention to what he says in class. Overall a very cool and likeable guy

I am currently in human pathology. We covered our first case study and I found myself hanging onto every word Dr. Decker said. He actually uses students as demos which really makes the study come alive. I want to be a cardiologist, so I am excited to get to cardiac pathology.

Given the pandemic, I found out the course was modified from what is was previously, so I dont know how hell have it set up in the future. I think he mentioned all testing will be back in class, so online tests will most likely be no more. I found the course thoroughly engaging and very informative. Dr. D. has a true passion for the material.

Tests were open-note, but I still feel like I learned a tremendous amount in this class despite it being so. Don't fall behind in lecture and review the material every day, and you're guaranteed an A with him as your professor.

Dr. Decker is a great lecturer and really passionate about the course material. He'll be the first to tell you he's not super concerned about your grade in this course, he cares more about preparing you for the next phase in your education. You definitely have to work for your grade, but it's a great class.

Dr. Decker is very passionate about anatomy! The class content is generally going to be tough to learn just because it's anatomy but Dr. Decker makes it engaging and fun to learn by sharing these hilarious, relevant stories & mnemonics. Very caring & enthusiastic. I am a visual & kinematic learner so I didn't have cram/stress bc of how he taught.

I am taking human anatomy with Dr Decker and the lectures are very engaging. The man loves what he does for sure. I am definitely taking pathology in the spring. I have been on the fence between biomed engineering and medicine and he has changed my outlook. Seeing the cadavers in lab is something i am looking forward to

I took this class for the summer short session. I was loaded with other classes so I didn't attend his lecture, and was able to get an A by looking at the slides he sends out. His lectures are really interesting and diverse, so I would say go if you can, especially if you like anatomy.

Professor Decker is awesome. Lectures are super interesting and he is really fun. Tests are easy (if you take good notes) and assignments are simple. Has a delorean which he let us see which was really cool.

I had Dr. Decker for 4 classes: Anatomy, Pathology, 1040 and Cardiac Diseases. He was tough but fair. In Anatomy, dont get behind on the readings in Moores. He uses some of the book on his exams. The cadaver prosections were really cool. Holding organs was the highlight of my undergrad studies. Highly recommend him.

Dr. Decker did a great job with Human Pathology. The USLME step 1 style questions at the end of the course were difficult by doable. I am so ready for med school next year thanks to this man. He is a GT treasure.

Dr. Decker's an expert, no doubt about it. He's lecture-heavy and can be dry to listen to, but he gives an amazing foundation in Anatomy for anyone Pre-Health. He gives lots of acronyms to help you remember, and regularly reminds you not to wait til the last minute to study for his class. So, take good notes & pay attention to the little details!

I love Dr. Decker. He is very knowledgeable and good at conveying that knowledge in an engaging way. He sprinkles in lots of stories and anecdotes. I feel that I learn a lot in lecture. The tests are challenging because of the large information volume, so make sure you study.

A lot of students were screwed by the end of the semester. It is not recommended that you take him online. Maybe in person he is better when there are four exams and 1 final. He ended up dropping an exam and having the final over a small section with questions unlike any of the past tests. Seemed really inconsistent and it tricked many people.

Backloaded the entire semester and you grade through your first 3 tests is a joke. The self proclaimed most accommodating professor of the 21st century... it seems course stability is lost when too much accommodation is made and students who work very hard and get 4.0s are, by chance alone, left to get lower grades than the rest.

I love this man! Taking human anatomy online is not ideal, but he has made it actually enjoyable. Tons of information and detail, but the course is laid out perfectly and well organized. I cant wait to get back to campus and shake this professors hand. I hope I can take the human pathology course next time he offers it.
Pathology with prof Decker was an outstanding experience. I am currently a first year med student at Emory and am already using the info he taught me in path and anatomy.
He's the best! Very knowledgable and really wants his students to get the most out of the Health requirement.

Had him online for short summer session. His teaching format was powerpoints with attached audio narration on each slide. He seems very passionate about what he does, which makes the lectures interesting and engaging. He also adds some hilarious jokes in there. Really cool. Down to earth. The assignments teaches you about yourself. Take good notes.

Dr. Decker is a laid-back professor. I had him for the summer session and he was really understanding. The lectures, although some students find them drawn out, were really interesting. He makes jokes during the lectures. Assignments are easy and tests are mildly difficult if you don't study, though I can only speak for the online version of APPH.

His assignments were very easy and his exams came straight from the lectures. He's very specific about what is going to be on the exam. Lectures can be long but some parts are pretty interesting because they're applicable to real life.

Human anatomy with Dr. Decker was a great experience. I attended his human neuroanatomy seminar he conducted for the GT neuroscience club last fall. He used real human brains and spinal cords. We were all on the edge of our seats as we learned internal brain structures. Im taking pathology when he offers it next.

I am really thankful that Dr. Decker teaches at Georgia Tech. Because it is a research school, there are not many health base classes or professors that understand that some students want to become doctors. I am just so grateful for all the work you have put into anatomy/pathology for us to further our careers as physicians.

I had Human Pathology with Prof. Decker. The course was an upper level senior course and I worked for my grade. All the content was med school based and I feel I have a good foundation for medical school. I am applying to Emory and hope this class gives me an edge. Cardiac pathology was my favorite especially all the fetal septal defects.

Dr. Decker is a great and caring professor with a thorough understanding of the content he teaches. He occasionally goes off on tangents on material that isn't of importance, but he really does a good job of preparing students for pre-health programs and future anatomy courses. Given the course is anatomy course, memorization is key.

Dr. Decker is awesome. One of the funniest professors you will ever have. This guy is brilliant, but he knows that if you're taking 1040 you most likely are there just for the credit. He understands this and makes the class as painless as possible. Take him, you won't regret it.

He came in on his own time Sunday morning to give us a review for the big joint and muscle test this week. He tests on origin, insertion, innervation and action. He knew it would be our most challenging test so far. All I can say is start studying early! I will definitely take him for Human Pathology.

Dr. Decker is one of the preeminent anatomists in Georgia. This man loves what he does and is a valuable resource if you plan on going to graduate school in any healthcare field. He presents the material in a way that makes you want to come to lecture. He is also using human prosected cadavers in anatomy lab. The whole experience is outstanding!

Dr. Decker was so much fun, especially since his content could be boring at times. He teaches a mandatory class for all students, so I'd recommend getting his if you can. He genuinely cares that students learn something helpful from his course despite it being mandatory, and I feel like I did. GO TO CLASS because he gives exam hints.

Dr. Decker is THE BEST. He is so funny. The tests can be a little specific so make sure to actually study but he does give a lot of extra credit. I took this in the summer and he always let us leave like an hour early. Super chill guy!

Human Pathology course was outstanding. He introduced USLME licensing board questions to prepare us. I feel very ready for medical school .Dr. Decker loves this stuff and always gives 110% for each lecture. Watch out for exams . Your hand will be cramping after doing 4 -5 pages of essay style questions and case studies. Excellent course,,
Not too hard of a class if you put the time in. Heavily tested on small details and diagrams. He really cares about his students and loves what he teaches, but class can get a little boring.

Super easy class- tests are 100% a memorization game. But, you'll also have a ton of fun in the class and you will actually retain the information you learn. Though I believe I still could've ended with a 98 without attending, do attend the class!! Dr. Decker is engaging and funny, he really cares about his students' success. Awesome dude!

He's just a good-natured person who genuinely cares about what he's teaching. I took it over summer short semester which was over a 2-hour class, but he knows how hard it is to sit and focus for that long so he made it fun and often gave us breaks. He made what would normally be a boring class, amazing. 10/10 would recommend. Easy material.

I had Decker on Pacific Program, and I'm actually writing this review before even finished the class. Wonderful guy, absolutely hilarious, and very straightforward with his class. First day of class he told us "This is a 2 hour class, and I will treat it like a 2 hour class." He clearly also knows A TON about the subject, and is passionate.

Dr. Decker is an awesome professor for human anatomy! He always adds clinical examples and fun tidbits to accompany the lectures which keeps me focused and interested. His tests are very detailed and get into the nitty gritty of everything he covers, but I feel like I learned a lot in his class and had fun doing it!
I took this over the summer. So much material crammed in to such little time. Was a total of 6 or 7 lectures at 3 hours each. If you can, just take it during a full semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Decker is a great lecturer and a great guy. The tests were a little difficult, though, especially for APPH 1040. But I would take the class over again just for the lectures. You can really tell that he is passionate about the subject, and it rubs off on his students.

I had Professor Decker for human anatomy. I can honestly say I walked away from the class with a greater understanding of human anatomy that I will certainly take with me to medical school. He was extremely knowledgeable, caring and went above and beyond most teachers at GT. Take Dr. Decker if you plan on going to  grad school.
Very funny, very clear. Class in general is not the most exciting but he definitely makes it better.

Professor Decker was very knowledgeable in human anatomy. He took what could have been a very dry and boring subject  and brought it to life with many clinical examples. He made the course very relevant if you are going into a health professional field, like med school.  I will be taking him for APPH 1040 when he teaches it next.

I just finished my first semester in a graduate DPT program. Dr. Decker's human anatomy course saved me. I found myself teaching others in my class. I will never forget "skunkus in my uncus" highly recommend him for any class.

I took this class in the summer and the lectures were really long. There were only 2 exams and contained a lot of information to memorize. I wished Dr. Decker would take his time to explain the material rather than skip some of the major topics that are on the exams.

Dr. Decker is an amazing anatomist. The class is so relevant if you are going to graduate school, medical, dental, PT, etc... His lectures are clear, to the point and engaging. You never want to miss class. He has been my favorite professor so far at GT. highly recommend!!

Dr. Decker is a great instructor. He teaches everything you need to know in a very clear & precise manner. You'll need the book for the online quizzes. But his tests come directly from his ppts and lectures. He makes the lectures interesting with stories and facts from his past. Attend lectures because he'll give you answers for the tests.

I did bad on my first quiz. However If u spend the whole afternoon before each test you will easily get an A. Just study from the power points and memorize them by hear. I aced the remaining tests easily. Don't even buy the book. Just buy the access code online which contains an online version of the book.
I am really enjoying Dr Decker's class so far. He has lots of student participation and everyone seems engaged. He is easy to listen to.

Class was pretty boring, but Dr. Decker has some pretty good  stories. Tests are m/c and directly from lecture slides. 3 tests, 3 online quizzes, 2 easy assignments and one essay. 5 extra credit points are available on final average

Great professor. Makes health class actually interesting. Don't have to show up, but you might want to anyways. Also, easy A as long as you study for the tests and do all the assignments, of which there are not many.

What a refreshing professor.  I just took the summer session   and have to say I really enjoyed it. Dr. Decker was engaging,funny and very knowledgeable.  I will definitely recommend his class to my friends.
He is one of the better health teachers, but don't expect like high school health. You will need to put effort into it
One of the best HPS teachers. Fairly easy and gives easy opportunities for extra credit (up to 4 points on your average). Attendance not mandatory or necessary.

Great professor. Really cares about students. I hardly ever skipped a lecture. Not that I was interested in the material, but he made lectures interesting with his enthusiasm and humor. He tells you pretty much all of the details you need to know for the tests and they aren't hard. I studied for an hour or 2 the day of the exams and did fine.
It was a very informative class. Dr. Decker made a class I thought I would dread, very good. I would definitely recommend him. He is well prepared and always seems to have a smile.

A very nie man. He joked around a lot and tried to make the class not as boring as it actually was. He told lots of interesting stories in class. He would tell you what would be on the test the class or two before the test. We had the opportunity to earn 4 bonus points on our final grade. He gave a study guide for parts of 2/3 tests we had.
He is very passionate and knowledgeable on the topics.  He is a tough grader on essays, but he gives enough opportunities with projects and participation to make up for it.
HONESTLY A HERO

Dr. Afflerbach is great. Interesting/engaging lectures. While he can be a little bit of a tough grader on some things the main thing he's looking for is effort. If he sees you're trying, you will be rewarded. Any time I needed help or had any questions his feedback was always EXTREMELY helpful. I would recommend his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Afflerbach was an amazing English teacher! You can really tell he is passionate about teaching. Although there was a lot of reading, it was interesting and the discussions we had in class were always great. And go to office hours! He always gives very helpful feedback and seems to genuinely care about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Afflerbach is the kindest and coolest professor I have had so far. His classes are very interesting, and the projects assigned are very manageable. Though there is a lot of outside reading, be sure to do it so you can participate in class. 20% of the grade is participation. Afflerbach is very responsive to your comments in class and is  helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. A is hands down one of the best teachers I've had. His class is structured as a discussion that he facilitates incredibly well. He's knowledgeable,  fair and engaging. He sincerely wants to help you succeed as long as he sees your efforts.

If I had another English class to take, I would 100% take another class Afflerbach taught. If you need help, stop by office hours. They make a huge difference. He is very responsive to emails as well!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Roy is a great professor with very reasonable grading criteria and class structure. He is a solid lecturer, and I would highly recommend him to other students. As long as you keep up with the material and stay consistent, you will do fine in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Roy truly cares about his students. He is very understanding and will accommodate to his students as requested. His class is distributed by the homework, midterm, and final exam. You need to go to class and follow the textbook or you will be lost. As long as you work hard, you will get the grade you deserve. 10/10 TAKE THIS CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Roy is incredibly understanding and cares about his students - he was one of the only professors to modify the class and communicate with us clearly when we moved to remote learning. His lectures are interesting, and the weekly assignments aren't difficult. Exams are straightforward and fair, just study the lecture notes and do the HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Roy's classes and homeworks were very proof heavy, but the exams were pretty easy. He knows the material pretty well and really cares about his students. The exams often had extra credit too. He spent some time reviewing 1553/4, so there was only a little bit I had to do by myself. If you got through 1553/4 ok, this class won't be bad at all.

Although Dr. Agrawal does give difficult tests, he is a great lecturer and very willing to help you during his office hours. You will learn so much in the class and taking a class with Dr. Agrawal is very worthwhile. Definitely one of the best lecturers in the chemical engineering department.

AMAZING professor. You will here stories about this class, and while he is an extremely difficult professor, he is an excellent lecturer and is extremely willing to help you out! Also, if you put in the effort, a B is atleast manageable, because he has an enormous curve (anywhere above a 65 should guarantee you atleast a B)
Worst professor ever. English is bad and he cannot hear you too. Homework grading is harsh and unreasonable. Exam is hard too.

Passionate professor who cares about networking and his students. Admits his mistakes clearly and works with students when they have issues. Handwriting in notes can be hard to read / understand sometimes though. Tests ended up being pretty hard (Fall 2025) but they got curved pretty hard so it ended up being fine

The professor is knowledgeable about Networking, but the course management was lacking. ALWAYS REQUEST REGRADES for homework, as TAs rely HEAVILY on the autograder. The professor's handwriting is VERY hard to read, and lectures focus on concepts while exams are calculation-heavy. The midterm had unfair conditions that the take-home didn't balance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take-home midterm did not offset the unexpected technical difficulties of the original midterm, which had unfair testing conditions. Lack of feedback on HW and exams; many unanswered Ed posts. TAs/prof gave misleading info about HW/exam questions. Lectures are very conceptual while HW/exams are very computational. Prof Ahmed is pretty solid though.

Spam regrade requests on EVERYTHING! Make up any reason or else they'll never give u partial bc TAs only autograde (half can't even explain anything). Pray u don't have to talk to the prof bc he does not care. Take a diff prof, others are actually nice & don't expect u to "already know the answer" to the HW (which is why they never release answers)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: What a caring man. Truly understands that we are students EOD and wants us to succeed. Content was challenging but definitely an interesting class.

Incredible professor, cares a lot about his students. He knows a lot about networking as well and the lectures get pretty deep into the content. The exams are very difficult, but he applies a generous curve to accommodate for it.

Professor is super passionate about the material. Lecture notes are not great and the textbook is hard to read. Exams are super content heavy so its best to stay on top of it individually. Homeworks aren't that great of a prep resource as  hws use wireshark and terminal which aren't tested on exams. Programming Assignments are not really useful.

Solid professor all in all. He definitely understands the material and is very passionate about the field. Some lectures were hard to follow since the topics got pretty complex/abstract. But there is a textbook the lecture slides are based on which is helpful. The exams are difficult but final grades end up being  fair at the end

Professor that is clearly passionate and knowledgeable in the topics he teaches. He often tries to connect his lectures to real world events / topics. Also very sympathetic to students and doesn't try to make the class too hard (he handled the canvas test fiasco very well). 

The one bad thing I'll say is that his handwriting is horrendous

As a professor he is really nice and tries to explain everything that is relevant. You can tell he knows his material but the exams are incredibly difficult. Our class average was a 60 on the exam with the curve and we were given an optional retake that had an even lower average.

Took data center section with him. Extremely knowledge about the field and it is clear through his lectures. I would buy his data center book as soon as he finishes writing. Grading is easy as he cares much more about the students absorbing the materials. Very valuable class to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The professor is extremely knowledgeable and has a distinct interest in the topic. He's caring and tries to improve the class as he can. There was some disconnect between TAs and professor as homework/projects were poorly organized and communicated. They're working on improving.

Prof Saeed is extremely knowledgeable and eager in networking. He moves at a fast pace, hence, we covered more than the other section. There were 6 hws, 3 "quizzes", 2 labs, and a final - the "quizzes" were actually 75 minute exams and quite difficult, but he curved. Go to lectures and don't fall behind. Only complaint was the TAs were not-so-good.

Extremely easy class. The summer online class is asynch with a couple of weekly assignments. Each week, you have reading quizzes (very light) and discussion posts. The only major assignment was the final "exam", in which you had to create a presentation on one of the multiple Arabic topics learned. Overall, the class was very easy, and I recommend!

I took his class for ARBC 3501 (Men-Women in Islam) and I really enjoyed the class. Probably the easiest option for a humanities credit. Sometimes assignments could be annoying but even the slightest effort can get you an A. Also very understanding and let me turn in a lot of stuff almost a week late.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Ahmed was a very helpful and respectful professor who made this class an enjoyable experience for his students. You have to show up to class and you get 3 absences before it affects your grade. The quizzes are not worth much and are easy. Just participate and you should get an A for both 1001 and 1002. Great professor and cool class!

Great professor! He does a good job of teaching Arabic basics and providing lots of different types of practice (reading, listening, speaking, etc). At first the class was intimidating since many people were already able to read Arabic, but I felt much more confident by the end of the semester. Very welcoming class environment!

Very good professor, taught a hard language in a way everyone would understand. Grading is fair and doesn't require that much time. I will 100% recommend this class to anyone that is looking for a good humanities class.
You have to show up to lectures, but he cares about his students and teaches a hard language well
Ahmed is a great teacher, being in his class was so nice I enjoyed it a lot. He's super understanding and as long as you communicate with him and do your assignments you'll do great!

Prof. Ahmed is so so kind and really caring. Sometimes the lectures are sporadic as theyre based on what students need, which was more difficult for me. No previous experience for me, so definitely had to put in work. Once we sat in the dark and just relaxed for a bit during a miserable hell week. Prof Ahmed is so sweet and it was a great class.

Dr. Ahmed has been one of the best professors I've had ever. I came into his class only knowing how to read Arabic and had no idea what a single word meant, but he taught me a lot. His lectures are interesting and he never throws so much info at you all at once. He really tries to understand what we need and what helps us learn best. 1000000/10

Literally the NICEST professor I will probably have at Tech. He's so understanding and will extend deadlines if necessary. I had his class fully online and you only have to write one response and read a chapter of the book every week. Definitely take this class if you need a humanities, it's also interesting!!!

I'm giving him +1 pity point because he comes off as a nice genuine guy. His lectures are extremely dull and dry. He took an interesting topic and made it as boring as possible. Another major flaw was that all the projects were very poorly written and outdated. Errors in those instructions probably wasted hundreds of man hours across all students.
Course was poorly designed

Dr. Ahamad's CS 6238 course is challenging, but you learn a lot. One of his strengths is his weekly office hours, where he reviews the previous week's quiz (or exam) and allows comments and differing views. This time is very valuable as it helps reinforce concepts and prepare for the midterm or final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Provides around 30-50 pages of academic journals/articles per QUIZ, on a WEEKLY basis. I've never met another professor that's asked for this much reading. The content isn't difficult (or engaging) but the quiz questions are pulled randomly from journals. Projects are much better and don't rely on readings. Drops your lowest quiz/project grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
The coursework is related to systems security so it is lecture heavy with things like TCBs, DAC, MAC, etc as you 
would expect. The Professor and TAs in general are super approachable and in fact Prof. Ahamad encourages students to drop by for office hours. Overall pretty good course and hands-on experience with core system security principles.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took him for Secure Computer Systems and found him to be knowledgeable with great recorded lectures (online). Two exams are worth 60% of your grade, but grades on a curve based on class performance. There is a quiz each week (worst 3 are dropped) and 4 projects ranging from easy to hard (proj4, start early). I learned a lot, would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The most intense class I've ever taken. Stated I'd be doing about 6 - 8 hours of homework a week. I spend at least 30 hours a week (3 hours a night + entire weekend). Videos are very informative, and class structure is awesome for an online learner. I would not recommend taking two of his classes simultaneously.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Awful in general! Your teaching yourself!

His class is pretty useless, and his lectures are dry and boring. All you do is read boring papers that you learn almost nothing from. I did learn a little bit from the projects, though. I think his grading is predeterminedno matter what you do or don't do, it seems he's already decided what he's going to give you. Avoid if possible.

This professor is unclear and not helpful. He is unaware of what he is discussing in class and forgets what he tells students. He is not consistent with his grading, and changes his standards of grading each week without telling students. He does not understand the meaning of communication. Good Luck, avoid a class with this professor if you can.
Unstructured course, extremely confusing lectures, poor quality of assignments. Utter  waste of an elective.

This professor has vague expectations.  He does not grade anything in his courses, yet claims that each assignment is crucial.  He does not teach anything, and he often invites guest faculty to lecture.  Final grades are arbitrary based on how much he likes you.  If you're an InfoSec major, good luck because this professor's courses are mandatory.
Best professor I have ever met in my life. Extremely down to earth and very knowledgeable. Highly experienced and I am gratified to be one of his students.
No Comments
I thought Prof Ahamad was very good and inspiring. He is very sharp and abreast with the research in his field. His projects focus on creativity and can be a bit openended.
Hard course, great teacher

Dr. Ahuja is an expert on aeroacoustics. His lecture slides are very organized and handy to use for whatever purpose. He doesn't go through details in lecture so after-class reading is important, even though the exams are really easy. Be intuitive and active in his class!

Prof Ahuja is your good old-fashioned professor. He goes over the material quickly, and often refers to the textbook, which you can for tables. The slides are often a mess, which requires a better understanding of the subject. However, the tests and quizzes are very doable. You can get an A in the class, just make sure not to fall behind.
His course consists of filling in the blanks in his lecture slides. It's pretty boring. Mac-PC compatibility messed the pictures up. All in All pretty good.

He is an OK professor. His tests are almost easy if you have good memory. He is very quick in teaching, doesnt explain alot. always says "I dont have time to go in detail, please refer to you textbook". Tests consists of fill in the blanks which are directly from his slides, and the rest is problems. Thermo is supposed to be hard. but it was easy!
Funny as hell

Dr. Uzer is definitely one of the best professor at Tech. He is enthusiastic and he has a great sense of humor. The class is relatively difficult, its physics, but he is a generous grader. If you have a chance to take one of his classes, you need to.
If you go to Georgia Tech, you HAVE to take a class with Uzer - you'd be missing out on so much otherwise!

Really funny guy, a warm, helpful professor who clearly loves what he does and wants nothing more than to make you understand the material. If you ever have the chance to take Uzer, you will not regret it.

Insanely difficult class, but he definitely taught me how to think more like a physicist. He will take the time to make sure you understand the material, but he'll grade you as if you're taking classical mechanics, not intro physics. Very funny and intelligent. He will likely remain one of my favorite professors.

Uzer is a really funny guy who is more than willing to sacrifice time, even during lecture, to address confusions and misunderstandings. One of my favorite professors at Tech, really helps you succeed in physics.

Professor Uzer is by far the most entertaining professor I've had a Tech. His classes are known to be extremely difficult, but he is more than willing to sit down and reexplain most anything. Do not miss out on having him as a teacher.

The class is hard, but it isn't Uzer's fault. He explains the material VERY well. The tests are REALLY difficult, but all of them are. There is a lot of homework, but it's manageable. Whatever you do, DO THE BONUS HOMEWORK. It seems like a hassle, but it is definitely worth it. Uzer knows his stuff, and he's really funny. I recommend taking him.

Fantastic teacher, definitely worth going to his lectures. Took his honors physics class and his tests were pretty much impossible to finish within an hour, though.  But he's very fair and takes time out of his day to make sure you are on the right track
Very funny and will keep you interested. The tests aren't easy but what tests at Georgia Tech are? Very good professor and always willing to help if you need it.

Very cool and funny professor. He is good at explaining key concepts that appear on the quizzes. The quizzes are tough. The multiple choice questions are meant to trick you. I suggest reading the book and doing all previous quizzes.

The class in itself was pretty much a joke, but Uzer was an awesome prof. He is the ideal "college lecturer", meaning he's great at teaching the material and keeping you interested, but he's not available outside of lecture. HILLARIOUS! If anything, go to class for his jokes. (By the way, he looks like a crazy Ben Stein). Very easy class overall.
This man is awesome. He makes Physics fun and keeps us laughing
No Comments
funny guy. strange sense of humor. does go a bit slow but covers material piece by piece.
No Comments
Nice guy, he cares about the students. I just didn't like the course material very much, nor the in class participation assignments.
He clearly cares about students and what they think of the course, responds well to feedback.
The class wasn't very interesting, I didn't learn much in lecture. It's definitely the type of class you have to teach yourself, but it doesn't require much time outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Homework is just the right difficulty, enough to keep a solid grade and still learn a lot. Tests are all multiple choice, and he drops your lowest. Final is cumulative. Possible extra credit from CIOS. I don't like random attendance, especially for an easy class like this, but that is whatever. Good lecturer, you learn all you need to in class.

Great professor. Attendance is taken randomly over the semester. All material is covered in lectures, textbook is not necessary at all. All tests and final exam are all multiple choice, and they're all pretty straightforward (there will be one or two trick questions though). Overall a very fair professor. If you show up and pay attention, easy A.

Quality professor, or actually grad student. Gets grades back in an hour most of the time which was great. Good clear lectures. Fair exams. Very solid choice for an econ professor, would recommend. Only downside is random attendance checks.

Relatively enjoyable class. You get to drop your lowest test! The professor really knows and understands the material, so he is able to answer all questions clearly. His tests did sometimes have tricky or confusing questions, so read carefully.

Worst physics professor ever. All of his tests were MULTIPLE CHOICE (i.e. no partial credit!) with SIX questions!  The questions were also highly dependent on memorizing specific formulas, since his formula sheets sucked.  DO NOT take his class if you can avoid it.  There are much better science electives.

The class itself (Intro modern) was pathetically easy and shallow. Prof Erbil, however, is an incredibly passionate guy who clearly would have loved to just teach to anyone who wanted to learn, even without requirements/grades/external motivators. Seems to me he wants to go into more depth than the course allowed. He seems like a really cool guy.

I had Erbil for Physics 3. Physics 3 is much easier than Physics 2, and unfortunately he realizes this. Unlike Physics 1 and 2 where the worst test is dropped as a buffer, in his Physics 3 class there is NO hope of redemption after a bad test grade. The final was 10 MC at 25% of your grade: one stupid math error drops your final grade 2.5 points.

A solid professor overall. Very helpful. Holds review sessions the night before a test- even if the test is on a Monday. The class requires work, and the tests are pretty tough, if not borderline unfair, but hard work will pay off in his class. I'd take him again later for physics 3 if he's teaching it.
Very easy. Almost TOO easy; anyone's that's seen electricity and magnetism in high school need not attend lecture. You'll still get an A if you remember anything. Incredibly nice guy, though.

Without a doubt the BEST professor I've had at Tech.  He is always willing to help his students, and you can tell he enjoys teaching.  His tests are very reasonable with most of the averages turning out to be in the 80s, which is very high for a class at Tech.  I really enjoyed the class and would highly recommend it.

I had Erbil for Thermodynamics.  He's a fairly easy teacher as far as grading goes; he's well-grounded in reality and insists that his students do likewise.  He's average when it comes to explaining material or fielding questions.  Erbil's big advantage is that he's very, very concerned about his students' learning.  Overall a solid teacher.

Compared with other physics classes at Tech... his was awesome.  I really enjoyed him... and yes he does talk about himself a lot, but it's all interesting... he knows a bunch of random famous scientists (or so he says).  Anyway, if you can get the old tests... you'll be golden.  Oh yeah... and an 80 is like an A... so that's nice too....
Not the clearest lecturer when compared with other phys proffs, seemed to spend a little too much time talking about himself and his MIT degree.  But overall a likable guy.
I earned an A in his class (my first one at tech!) and enjoyed it as well. He was a very good and very helpful professor, and I hope to take another class with him in the future.

Dr. Erbil rarely teaches the intro classes, but I had him for each of them, and enjoyed every bit of it.  He regularly provided help sessions, many times at the request of his students, and has a love for the material.  "Isn't that great?" h

Great organization and structure throughout the course. Always accessible outside of class and clearly cares a lot about students' career placement. Consistently connects what you learn in class to real-world applications, which makes the material much more meaningful. Easily the best professor in the major.

Alex does a great job in teaching Intro to Construction Management. She introduces new concepts in a way that is digestible for all students. There were a lot of valuable lessons that came out of the semester-end project that could be applied to the Building Construction world.

Alex has a lot of industry experience and really cares about you paying attention in class. It's pretty obvious that she is teaching because she wants us to actually learn something, not just lecturing to lecture. Very open to questions and assigns work that is actually relevant to the industry and what we are learning.
sits around all day long a little bit to much

I 100% recommend her for legal aspects. You get an entire page front and back for a crib sheet on tests (type this). You do need to pay attention somewhat in lectures and show up. The last unit there aren't slides so be sure to pay attention and take down notes. Super easy class tbh.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super nice professor, very enthusiastic in lectures. She uses good examples and engages the class, easy to pay attention in her class. Tests were kinda hard but you get a cheat sheet. She was very available for help and going over past tests, genuinely cared for student success. Definitely recommend her as a professor

She is very enthusiastic about the topic and gave good examples in class. You get a double sided crib sheet for every test, so as long as your notes are good then the tests are easy. There are also 2 case studies which are hard to study for, but the class is easy overall. There is no homework which I liked and you don't need the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far my favorite professor I have had at Tech!!! I thought this class was going to be boring, but the material is actually really interesting and she is super passionate and knowledgeable about it. She makes sure her students are understanding the material and is easily accessible by email and office hours. TAKE HER!!

Literally one of the best teachers at Scheller. Explains concepts simply using real world, RECENT examples. She is super engaging and intelligent. Not a lot of grades, just exams, random attendance, and case studies. Exams are easy and multiple choice. Case studies are also easy, just review the content before. You also get a crib sheet for exams

Prof Alexander is good. However, there seems to be a misconception between easy to understand and easy material. The material is manageable without heavily studying, but her way of professing wasn't exceptional. Writing cases and test formats were unclear. Attendance is mandatory. Class is graded by point system.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Alexander was one of best professors I have had at Georgia Tech. I learned so much through her lectures while not having to do too much studying outside of class. I was engaged through her lectures completely! She also lets you get a crib sheet on each test. Definitely take her!

Easy A. Lets you use a crib sheet on every test. No final exam just 4 non cumulative tests. Very interesting material taught in course. Lectures are dull but straightforward ,and she is very passionate about material

She is one of the best lecturers and keeps you engaged the whole time. She is very knowledgable in law and passionate. Her tests also always follow along with her lectures and notes, never anything unexpected. Highly recommend!

She is a good lecturer and is always accessible outside of class. She answers all your questions and she posts practice tests that are similar to the test. She also lets you have a 8.5x11 cheat sheet front and back on the test. Her tests are not super hard. This class is an easy A.

TAKE HER!!! I was hesitant to take Legal because I was expecting it to be a snooze fest, but Prof Alexander is so engaging. You can really tell she enjoys teaching and is great at using scenarios to teach concepts. Theres a textbook but you dont need it. Just make sure to pay attention in class and thats all you need to get an A. She's great!!

She was an amazing professor. I typically don't enjoy going to lectures and I do other work while professors are talking, but she kept the class very interesting. I would definitely take her again if she taught any other courses. Her tests/case studies are very manageable and honestly you won't have to do much studying if you listen during lecture.

SHE IS AMAZING. I have never been more engaged in lectures until I took her class. She does require attendance but you'll want to go to class anyways because the content is so interesting. There is a textbook but if you take good notes in class you don't need it. She is super sweet and passionate about legal. DEFINITELY TAKE HER!
Super sweet! There's a textbook but you don't need it if you go to lecture.
Autistic teacher who thinks that equation wrangling is going to be the differentiating skill in the age of AI.
Seems like a nice guy but the lectures definitely need work. Doesn't connect to the course material though. However the projects are cool and engaging.

Ritter's class wasn't too bad, but lectures are boring and all mathematical. You're really just learning formulas and then coding them unless you put in crazy effort to understand everything, making ML seem uninteresting. However, the grading became really easy at the end of the semester. Coding HWs weren't bad but written HWs were excessively hard
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: His lecture is hard but rewarding if you are serious about machine learning. Come to class with a strong background in linear algebra, prob, and programming.

This professor abolished all interest I had in the field of machine learning. Instead of showing any cool or interesting applications of such technology, he taught everything from an almost purely clinical, mathematical perspective. Such math was difficult to grasp and apply to the projects and problem sets, making them needlessly long to finish.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: To his credit, Ritter seems to be a nice guy that wants his students to be successful. However, the assignments are vague and often unrelated to lecture content, with seemingly arbitrary grading criteria. Lectures are boring and come straight from the slides.

Professor Ritter absolutely killed my interest in machine learning. It is impossible to follow along with him in lectures as he simply circles and scribbles all over the slides. The projects and homework assignments are nothing like what he teaches in class -- at ALL. The only way to succeed is to teach yourself everything and pray you're close.

Don't go to the lecture, just read the textbook and online resources. He will only talk about the math, not the reasons or concepts behind. He is very good at killing your interest in machine learning. And you will never get answers for any assignments because he wants to re-use them in the future. God bless you if you have to take his class.

Ritter is a very nice guy, but I would not take this class if you don't need to. It's very confusing, the assignments are overwhelmingly tough and ambiguous, and the lectures are impossible to sit through.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Easily the most difficult class I have taken in my time at Georgia Tech. The tests and assignments in the class did not relate to the lectures or material and you are forced to heavy research outside of class to complete questions. Lectures are extremely math intensive, but not very useful since he just says exactly what's on the slides.

Awful lecturer and teacher - cannot communicate effectively at all. Assignments are unnecessarily tough and don't relate to what is taught in class or in the textbook, which differs from what is taught in class. Provides no or extremely vague guidance on assignments. Avoid at all costs, did not learn anything from this class.

Really horrible lecturing, shocking considering GT should be good at ML. He struggles with basic public speaking (every other word is um, like, basically, right) making it hard to stay engaged in the material. The assignments have little to do with his lectures so youre forced to learn it all on your own. Avoid Alan if possible, at least for 4641.

Professor Ritter poorly explains material in-class while only underlining the material he is talking about and not writing anything down on slides. Each lecture leaves students lost in the material. Assignments have very little relation to the material taught in the class requiring outside resources to help students guess at an answer.

Great professor! Love Professor Ritter. His lectures are really easy to follow and homeworks were really quite fair as well as fun. I am doing some NLP stuff in my summer internship and I think this will really help. Great class and would highly recommend! Thanks Professor Ritter!!

It's a good class. It can be difficult, but as long as you do the readings and put in good effort, you'll get a good grade. Professor Alonso is a little intimidating but has good spirits and wants all his students to be engaged and interested in the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Tough grader but honestly didn't care about that too much. What I did care about was busting my behind the entire semester with an A average, just to get a participation grade that dropped my average by a whole letter. Mind you I had documentation. Not understanding. Maybe he just didn't like me. Made me not want to minor in spanish. Devastated.

He is very knowledgeable on the subject, which made the class interesting. I learned a lot and developed my writing/speaking skills, however he is quite intimidating whenever you speak up (which is required for participation). He takes points off of assignments for seemingly no reason and there's a decent amount of homework so beware of that!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There was significant reading, but you learn a lot about Latin America. The instructor is passionate about the topic.

I took the course with the intent of improving my conversation skills, but the majority of our grade/work was comprised of doing research type presentations and presenting them to the class, which I did not overly enjoy. I feel as though this was specific to Prof Alonso's class, so just be ready for that. It did help with public speaking though.

Dr. Alonso is a tough grader but he grades the same way every time (heavy grammar focus). He is very organized and that made it really easy to do his class in an online format. He clearly has experience teaching online, and I would definitely recommend him for that setting.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: My class theme was Satire in the Americas and Dr. Alonso was very knowledgeable and clearly interested in the topic. Your grade comes from a combination of essays and presentations which are graded pretty harshly, no in-class assignments. Class time was for discussing the long readings/documentaries assigned for homework daily. Interesting class,
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Would not recommend, especially if you want an easy A. His grading is ridiculously harsh and he can't explain why he took off points well either. He also is intimidating and will call you out randomly to answer a question. As much as the content was interesting and he knew his stuff, the stress of going to this class was not worth it.

Not an easy A. He grades essays harshly, particularly on grammar and Spanish errors. A few presentations, and he assigns lots of reading and movies to watch - like 3-4 hours before each class. He really likes to talk (ramble). He does know his stuff and has strong background in journalism. His English isn't great which can lead to some confusion.
Great professor. Very humorous. Answers questions helpfully.

His lectures were really good, but the rest of the class was not great. The labs take way longer than the designated lab time, and the exams and lab quizzes are a massive time crunch. Thankfully, even though it takes a lot of time, it's not difficult to get good grades on the homeworks and lab reports.

Dr. Robinson is an amazing lecturer - writes everything out on the board. Cleared up many misconceptions from 2040. Exams are super time-limiting. Labs are extremely time-consuming. If you can separate the very stressful exams and lab structure from the great lecture content he is amazing.

~6 hours a week on lab. 6 HW ~3hr . Lectures are GREAT. you must go! Nice person but you need to contact him in person, because he is very slow to email. he has a lot going on (W/F in office only i think). Homeworks and exams graded very harshly, and prep material is limited, but I dont care because I like Robinson and I learned a lot. ~4 pt curve?

He is a good lecturer but has absolutely no concern for the well-being of students. Never replied to students' emails, and impossible to find for office hours. He had confusing due dates and assigned difficult homework, barely relevant to the class, which made everything seem poorly organized.

Robinson was a good professor, he had a deep understanding of the class content and taught relatively well. However, the structure of the course is very frustrating and the lab manual that guides this course is severely outdated and needs updating. There is no extra or supplementary material to learn from. Lab's are long and not well explained.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Robinson is very good at breaking down complex topics into simple ideas, but his lectures are only 50 minutes so they move fast and aren't long enough. Labs each week take varying amounts of time and closer to the end you almost will have to go to open lab hours. Though, if you read the theory in the lab manual beforehand it'll halve the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Labs are long, expect to go in during open lab, around 4-6 hrs on each one in general. Tests are straightforward but short on time since its 50 mins. Material is gone over quick, mainly use the lab manual/practice tests to study. There is barely any partial credit so double check your test and HW with multisim.

Robinson is a super strict teacher that grades very harshly on exams and has the TAs grade just as harshly for quizzes and homework. He sets the class grading up so that he can achieve a similar grade distribution every semester (mostly Bs and some A's and C's, but hardly anyone fails), so just do your best and put in a ton of effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The time taken per lab depends on mistakes, not knowledge. 2hr labs can take 9hrs, so you'll be using open lab. Lab quizzes and tests are tough, this class is graded like a weed-out class. Definitely use office hours, 1 hr/week of lecture probably isn't enough, and prof is REALLY good in office hours

Amazing lab. The assignments are well written and really help you learn. Prof gives extra time if he notices a lab is taking longer than usual. Lab reports are also pretty chill, as long as you did the work.

I don't understand all the bad reviews about Dr. Robinson. He is a very caring and helpful professor in my opinion. His lectures are extremely helpful and he's always down to help. The only thing I wish he did was be a bit lenient on grading exams.

This class is only lab. You have to come to every single one or else you will not do well. You are expected to know everything before class. The lab is run by TAs and all you do is get an experiment that takes 3 hours and a hard quiz each lab. This class was literally the bane of my existence as a non-ECE major.

He cares more about your final answers on tests than how you got there and tests go wayy above and beyond lecture material, which isn't great because other than a lab manual that doesn't cover that material either, you don't have a textbook. Also, tests don't provide enough space or time for you to finish.
Cool class! Play Name That Frequency!

He just read off slides and did not explain well. But a lot content with details showed in exams. Didn't give very useful resources to prepare for exams and the content from lectures did not fully cover content in final.
weartsydfuiohl

reviews.comment: Reads off slides and does not teach well. Does not give any resources to prepare for exams and lots of assignments.
Don't take this class if he is teaching.
Learned nothing from him. Don't take the class if you expect to come out of the course with any knowledge.

There was not a single practice problem or helpful example done the entire class, or posted online so the average grade of the final was a 56. He is a terribly boring lecturer and does not stick to the topics of his class. Terrible class, would not recommend

Professor Hsu is a cool guy, he was very passionate about his research and it sounded very interesting when he talked about it. That being said, he didn't really know much about how to teach this class (tbf, it was his first time teaching it). You are graded on 2 tests and 4 hws, and he doesn't release practice tests. Class wasn't too hard though.
