reviews.comment: Great teacher, nothing else to be said.
Love this dude honestly. His course isn't too bad as long as you pay attention and do your work.
these people leaving the reviews are crazy, this guy was a great genuine dude, who loves what he does.
One of my favorite professors at GT
horrible professor, lectures are 10 questions, 10 points each. Horrible questions too. He is nice as a person, but hard to get a good grade tbh

All the nice reviews are spam and written on the same day by children, go and read them. The class would be 100x easier if he did the bare minimum and released answer keys and work for practice problems. The class is difficult and the slides are horrendous and not helpful at all. He's definitely a chill guy but he's just so so so bad at teaching.

Cool guy but genuinely worst teacher ever. Won't give answer keys to practice problems or show work and his slides are so bad you literally don't know what you're doing. I have never called a teacher bad before until him. He does curve the class but thats bc if he didn't everyone would fail because he's so bad at teaching.

He is really smart and a solid guy but is genuinely so bad at teaching. He just yaps about math and starts examples before finishing others and is inconsistent with what he calls terms so you end up being so lost. While I do like him he is by far the worst teacher and worst class ive had in my life. The midterm and final are 10 multiple choice qs
He is not a good teacher and is not good at communicating with students.
Do not take if you want to learn something.

reviews.comment: Love this guy
Amazing Teacher
Great guy. Good personality
Favorite professor I've had.
Thank you. I dont know why so much hate. Genuine Christian man.
Amazing Professor. Nothing else really needed to say..
Great Teacher.
One of the best professors I have ever had in my college career. Great Guy.
He was an amazing professor and was really kind. Great teacher
I loved this class and it was amazing. Great teacher, I hear his son is good at soccer too.

No point in going to lectures. 65% of your grade is two tests with little to no provided practice. Lecture notes are super vague and barely help if you weren't there for context. Class is curved and easy to pass, but I wouldn't recommend it if you truly want to learn corporate finance. He's a chill guy though

One midterm and one final which make up 65% of the grade. I personally dislike the heavy emphasis on exam grade considering this is an introductory finance course for non-majors. Lecture wise I feel Prof. Hsu is fine but some lectures do go a little tangential off topics and I feel like some topics we spent too much time on and some not enough.

He seems like a decent person but he isn't a good professor. Projects were not pretty easy but they did involve quite a bit of self study. He used slack and told us that he would always answer in a timely manner, yet he went MIA two weeks before the final. The final slides were useless but if you need to take the class, you'll probably pass.

reviews.comment: Honestly good. Don't know what all the bad reviews are about. Like pretty chill tbh I like the guy he enjoys teaching.

Showing up to the lecture is worth the same as not going at all. He likes to talk about things that are barely related to the class. He is invested in the content, but he forgets that this class is for non-business majors. His practice questions for exams are useless because he barely includes questions about the concepts he actually tested us on.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I learned nothing. The were only 4 homework assignments and 2 exams (a midterm and a final). The midterm was 10 multiple choice questions, online, no partial credit. The final was also only 10 questions. His lectures are scattered, seemingly talking about things that have nothing to do with the homework material. Inaccessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor rambles all class about unrelated math interpretations, very boring lectures. Tests are very hard and have very few questions so it is easy to mess up. Very few examples in class to help learn. Homework is also not helpful to prepare for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wouldn't recommend the professor as hes poor at consultation and doesn't answer questions for practice midterms and finals or in general. The TA is the saving grace for this class, but the professor is poor at teaching. Not to mention, his exams have questions that one may never encounter in class or assignments. Overall, don't take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very caring professor. He brought great resources in for the GT1000 class.

Attending his lectures help. They're super clear, & I had a thorough understanding of the material just attending his classes. The assignments do take time, characteristic of any grad course. Super friendly & caring guy, with a sprightly sense of humor. Doing the previous year exams he gives is all the prep I needed to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The goat of Dynamics. By far the best teacher I have had at Georgia Tech. Super clear lectures followed by example driven classes to help you understand the topic. Super friendly guy and answers questions clearly. Love Dr.Ferri.

if ur hearing good things, it's all true. he's really funny and good at making dyn easy for u. his exams seem extremely scary when ur taking them but he is such a lenient grader that if u try to maximize points, you're completely set. offers around 3 full points of extra credit total if you use every opportunity (DO ALL HW QUESTIONS) take ferri!!

He clearly cares about teaching and it makes showing up to lectures rewarding. He clearly prepared his lectures to make them clear and understandable. Homework can be difficult, and unfortunately does not count towards much of the grade. Exams are 90% of class grade but he gives plenty to prepare for them, and they are not unreasonable.

Fantastic professor. Class can be hard, but that is just the nature of a masters level dynamics course. He is super accessible and a great lecturer. The homeworks are really helpful and he includes the final answer to make sure you are on the right track. The tests are very similar to the homework but don't require a ton of actual math.
Great lecturer, I love him so much. I want to be him. Exams are pretty easy if you're doing HW and going to class, there won't really be many curveballs.
Good lecturer that emphasizes the basics. Class is extremely hard though. He is lenient with his grading on the exams.

Dr. Ferri is an incredible professor and lecturer. Instead of using slides, he writes out on the board. This creates for engaging lectures, but does mean that if you miss a lecture you will fall behind. So don't skip class. Dr. Ferri assigns about 5 homework questions each week, and the grading schemes on tests are generous.

Dr. Ferri's GT 1000 class was easily my favorite class of the semester. GT 1000 in general is a very simple class and there's almost no way you can't get an A. Dr. Ferri is very knowledgeable about Mechanical Engineering at GT and you can tell he has a passion for what he does. He's well respected and has been doing this for a while now.

Professor Ferri is amazing. He's a fantastic lecturer and really passionate about the subject. The homeworks can be a decent amount of work, but they are usually closely related to in-class examples which he demonstrates to completion, so they're definitely manageable if you go to lecture. Overall, 10/10.

Took at GTL but his lectures were solid and homework answers were given; he wanted us to show to work to that answer. Tests were 25%, 25%, and 35%, and the 35% final was TOUGH with some material we may not have explicitly seen (only downside to the course)

Dr. Ferri taught def bods for the first time and, while not as good at dynamics, still was overall an effective teacher. The class consists of 2 tests, a final, and weekly homework and is manageable for time and grades. His understanding of the class is probably not the best at GT, but his teaching skills and clarity make up for it.

Prof. Feri was amazing for dynamics. He knew exactly how to structure the curriculum and explained concepts in a simple and clear way. He is a lenient grader and it is very feasible to get an A provided you show up. Tests make up a high percent of your grade so study carefully! Homework is essentially completion.

If you take dynamics in the spring, 100% take it with Ferri.  As other comments have said, it's a hard class but he makes succeeding very reasonable with extra credit and reasonable partial credit on tests.  If you put in the work and go to class, you'll not only do well but end up being super good at dynamics.

Super caring and understanding professor. It's a hard class and he doesn't water it down, but he does the absolute most to try and make sure to get and understand the content. Super awesome class and would def recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor I had at tech. Great at explaining and also clearly a good person. Class was the appropriate level of difficulty.
Even though I only had him for a ME specific section of GT1000, you can still tell his brilliance and passion for students and engineering.
One of the best profs at Tech. This was one of my favorite classes at Tech, yet it was also one of the hardest.

Great guy, great professor. Just make sure you never get comfortable because that's when your grade will tank. Be diligent about the homework and studying. Always make sure you do the homework even if you don't know what's going on. They were very lenient on grading homework this semester.

Tough class, but Dr. Ferri made it really enjoyable to learn dynamics.  The guy knows the material like the back of his hand.  Top 3 professors I have had at Tech for sure.  Really awesome guy outside of class.  I've heard he's an important figure in the ME school, as well.

My best teacher in undergrad/grad, hands down.  Very helpful, knowledgeable, and clear in teaching.  Respects students, and students respect him.  However, homeworks take time, and it is not an easy class.  However, he gives you all of the tools you need (as is always helpful during office hrs) to succeed.
Great professor for dynamics, very clear and helpful, and very straightforward lectures. Tests were average difficulty.
Very good professor ... exams are not TOO bad but they are quite lengthy so time is the only issue for that .. but all in all i definitely recommend him
Brilliant man. Good communicator. For GT, light on homework. Makes material interesting. Goes beyond what is required to help you understand the material, even in other classes.

Was an interesting lecturer but the class is way too difficult for an elective class, be prepared to put STEM level effort into a non-STEM class. He doesn't post lecture materials or notes and moves through his notes pretty fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Dr. Fuentes class, the lectures were fascinating; I learned tons. He's a fair grader. Just be ready to take detailed notes if you want to succeed. Readings are assigned 2x a week. Quizzes are on the readings, so take good reading notes too. Exams are bit difficult, but multiple extra credit opportunities at the end. True difficulty: 3.5.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Fuentes is great. His lectures are interesting, he's clearly passionate about the course material, and grades are diversified among reading quizzes, worksheets, and exams. I really enjoyed INTA 2050 and highly recommend taking his class.
Professor Fuentes was very engaging and made the class interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The class grading is 60% tests and 40% daily works. His lectures are very informative, and I didn't think they were boring, as he is very passionate. I'm not an INTA major and just took this class for "fun." There is definitely some reading but nothing too, too much. Cool guy!

Fuentes is great. Lectures are in-depth and thoughtful. He cares about what he is teaching and he's good at it. You actually have to do the reading assignments and attend class to complete the in-class worksheets. Exams are 60% lecture material, 40% readings, but it all really works together. Similar difficulty to an AP history class.

Dr. Fuentes is a great professor-- one of the best I have had at Tech. The work I had to put into to succeeding in this class was worth it since lectures were valuable. I left with so much more knowledge. I really appreciated the readings quizzes at the start of each class because it meant everyone was doing the work and made for a better class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Love Dr. Fuentes! His class, Intro to Global Development, was perhaps my favorite class last semester and his lectures are fantastic. The reading material he pulls for each topic are in-depth and thought-provoking and I thought him to be a fair grader and a sympathetic professor, especially with COVID times. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is reading heavy, which can be a lot at times. His grading can also be weird and inconsistent, but overall the class was enjoyable. As long as you do your work, read, and attend class, you'll do good in the class.
Professor Fuentes' 2050 class was very interesting. The class is reading heavy, and you must attend class to succeed, but if you do the work an A is both enjoyably and easily attained.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class has so many assignments so there is a lot of leeways. Dr. Fuente's lectures summarized the readings for the weeks & he gave the students a chance to ask questions about the assignments and readings. Readings could be a lot, depending on the week, but each assignment is due on a different day. Great professor & interesting material!

With online, his grading was simple, 11 worksheets and 11 discussion posts where you can drop the lowest of the two. Two different essays and a final that was two more essays but they're all 3 page double space. Video lectures are helpful. Worksheets get LONG and you need to read the articles he gives but they were straightforward which was nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Honestly, a fine class/professor. Your grade is determined mostly by exams, however, if you go to her lectures, which are helpful, and do some of the practice problems you should be pretty well off. She also provides the textbook which is nice. One thing to know is a lot of the answers for the practice problems are not provided.

Students who already took a calc course struggled less with her. There are suggested problems you HAVE to do to succeed (even though there is "no hw"). For an intro calculus class for non-STEM majors, she offered "reading the textbook" as a way to improve performance. She writes out definitions and walks through practice problems rather than teach.

She isn't even a true professor, this class took up tons of study time. By the end of the semester we had been given over 800 practice problems, not mandatory but they are the only way to prepare for the test. The problems she goes over in lecture are a fraction of the difficulty of what shows up on the test. 0/10 class avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I know many had a negative opinion on her, but she wasn't bad, I enjoyed lecture. At the end of the semester she went through everyone's grades and tried to get everyone to a C (minimum). Her exams were very difficult, if you have no calc knowledge, but she adjusted as we went on. Go to office hours, she noticed any effort on your part.

Ambiguous feelings about Dr. Hampton. All the lecture notes are posted online. Quizzes 1x a week. No homework. Lectures were straightforward, not in depth. Don't blow off lecture though. Exams are fair, she gives an extra credit Q on each. Not a great class for people who have never took calculus. She tries her best to help our grades. Just study.

Midterms and Exams usually have some sort of extra credit, and the bottom 5 quizzes are dropped. If Lectures aren't really your thing, you can probably only show up to the studio class, and do practice problems and still achieve a passing grade. She is a fun teacher and listens to student's concerns.

No attendance or homework, heavy portion of the grade is based on three exams. Teaches directly from the textbook and is unwelcoming to questions. In-studio quizzes are much much easier than exams, so we were unprepared for how hard exams would be. The tests don't give you an idea of how many points each question is worth.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not the greatest professor but the class is really easy especially if you took calc in high school. No attendance but if you don't know calc then I would recommend going because it's kind of hard to learn on your own. 15 quizzes and she drops the worst 5, and 2 midterms and a final.
Genuinely a miserable human being. A mean person who does little to nothing to help students, and your ENTIRE grade hinges on tough midterms. Avoid class at all costs.
optional hw but exams are hard
She does very good lectures, but it is important to go to all of them. Read the syllabus and don't ask dumb questions, she will clock you. I'd recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was surprised to see such negative comments about her because my experience wasn't terrible at all. Although some may find it boring, I actually enjoyed her lecture style. She gives so many optional practice problems that undoubtedly show up on the test, so literally just do the work and you're fine.

One of the strictest graders I've ever had and barely gives partial credit on exams that she makes hard af. Tests also weigh a big chunck of your grade in this class and it felt like the way exams are graded is pretty unfair/unforgiving given the grading scale. It wasn't communicated that the exams were gonna include such complex problems either.

Not a very engaging lecturer and sometimes made mistakes on problems in lecture so she would have to send out an announcement later in the day correcting herself. She seemed a bit unprepared as a new professor and was uncertain on what some of the conventions (like what content was emphasized) and homeworks were like at GT.

This professor is, without a doubt, the worst instructor I've ever encountered. She puts in the bare minimum effort to teach but somehow expects students to solve the most ridiculously complex problems on exams. She's unenthusiastic, unforgiving, and doesn't care about her students' success in the slightest.  

Avoid. Avoid. AVOID!!!

Made an objectively hard class pretty easy to digest. Attendance isn't mandatory & a lot of people didn't come to class, but lectures were extremely helpful. Work is straightforward but the tests are hard.

One of my favorite professors. Her lecture style doesn't work for everyone, but I liked that she was concise, explained concepts well, and made sure we learned what we needed to. You can always supplement her lectures with Barone's, as his are recorded online, to get a different way of teaching if you don't understand something.

Pretty good for first time teaching linear algebra at Georgia Tech. Tests can be hard, but there are plenty of practice tests online. Highly recommend watching and taking notes on the videos for each lesson before the lecture and do the homework assignments. You don't have to go to studios and I didn't find them to be too helpful.

Good pick for a non-math major looking for easy A. Pretty much just reads slides, not very engaging, explains well enough. Don't need to attend class, most people don't. imo, she has a really shallow understanding of the stuff she's teaching, does the bare minimum of required content, but if you don't need anything past LinAlg she's a good pick
Good Professor overall, very good lecturer, rather have her than any other professor, and arguably better than Barone and many ways.
Genuine participation class. Lots of projects but reasonable class time is given for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment:
Wish I had more space, but to summarize:
-Teaching style made the course's fiber arts theme surprisingly engaging
-Graded on participation points (only need 100/130 for an A)
-4 fun & easy projects with minimal writing (video, podcast, presentation, and embroidery)
-Most importantly, she is the kindest and most understanding professor I've ever had
Great teaching style, really enjoyable content and projects, easy grader.

I had a very pleasant experience taking the class. Homework mainly consisted of short readings that were to be discussed in class. The final grade was not done on a points scale and instead was about completion and shown effort over the semester, which took out a lot of stress.
It's very clear that Dr. Moore puts the student first.

Dr. Moore is a great professor! The projects we did were non-traditional, including making a podcast, a blog post, and learning a new fiber craft, which I really enjoyed. She makes it very clear exactly what we needed to do to achieve an A for each assignment, and gives great feedback. She is also flexible with deadlines and attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She was a wonderful professor! She cares heavily about her students and if you communicate clearly, she is always willing to listen to your situation and work with you. Attendance also has a fairly good policy! Definitley recommend her!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: some readings before class, but very doable and easy (you can also get by without doing the readings). class theme was toy stories (pretty interesting). all the assignments were either process assignments in preparation for the main artifacts or reflections on the artifacts (all easy). is boring occasionally. All the assignments are self-graded!

The class is pretty engaging overall, and she genuinely cares about her students. Best class this semester!! I used to look forward to class every week, because yes, it is THAT fun. Would take her again 100% . The exams can be challenging at first, but it's all centralized across all 1553 sections.

Overall super engaging class, she goes a little fast sometimes but takes on the somewhat complex topics in an approachable and clear way. Do not recommend skipping any lectures though as a lot of the concepts pile up on each other quickly, especially towards the end of the semester.
Sometimes goes a tiny bit fast but other than that, she is slay and had us learn a tiny bit of French for funsies. Some classes made me laugh out loud

In mathematics, understanding concepts and processes is essential. Learning should start with simple problems, building knowledge step by step; lectures often jumped very fast to applications relying on a single method. This limited students' flexibility and made it difficult for those without math backgrounds or extra support to succeed.
She is not knowledgeable about the subject, but has a great personality.

This teacher had a great personality and was very funny, but was a poor lecturer. She consistently made mistakes during lecture that confused us all. She would need time to figure out problems as if she didn't prepare for lecture. Most of what I learned was through research online in my own time since her lectures were inadequate.

Very caring, allowed me to do alternate assignment when I had not done the reading. Very engaging lectures, and the reading was genuinely interesting, even though there is a lot of it. Genuinely cares about the topics he teaches, and I feel better off having taken the class and learned about the topics we did.
He was a really great professor who is really concerned about his students. His class is kind of difficult, but it is very enjoyable.

Prof Amsterdam was the best history instructor I have ever had. His lectures were well structured as he gave outlines for each one and his test were all from the lectures (so u gotta go to take notes cuz he doesn't post notes). Tests were very straightforward and the required readings were actually really interesting to read. Really caring

He's an amazing instructor, and even though attendance isn't mandatory, you will need to go to class in order to get a good grade since he doesn't post the lecture content on Canvas. Very chill guy, he dropped a few questions in our tests if he felt that it was confusing. He also dropped our lowest midterm. Make sure to take good notes

Lectures are not mandatory but DEFINITELY reccomended. Studying the material on your own or based off the notes makes the class so much harder than it should. Amsterdam is an amazing lecturer who makes the content  engaging, concise, and easy to follow, additionally he makes it very clear what parts of lecture are important/on the exams

From what I had, you were required (and I advise you) to go to every lecture to learn the material. Even though you can get the lecture notes from others, Amsterdam's lectures are so good that you retain the information so much better. He's very caring and wants the best for everyone. Had a great time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The goat. That's it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Amsterdam is actually a really good professor. He's extremely passionate about his area of teaching, but his exams can be a bit tricky since a lot of the answer choices are the same so it's important to memorize details of specific events. He's also lecture heavy and doesn't post any notes after class, so you have to be there.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a great professor and very passionate about his lectures. If you go to lecture and listen, you will do well in the class. The tests are pretty easy (multiple choice) if you pay attention. He does not post notes or recordings for lecture so make sure to go.

Amsterdam is good at packing information in a lecture but its way too difficult for a history class at a Tech school. He also posts no lectures notes or anything and 90% of the information is based on what he says in class. The test questions have very odd answers and often have questions that are based on 1 sentence that was said in class.

If you like history, you will love this class. If you don't, prepare to have to study A LOT for the midterms and final. Mr. Amsterdam likes what he teaches and he does it well, but prepare to have to study a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof Amsterdam is amazing!!! His lectures are interesting and very easy to understand. You read 4 books throughout the semester with an easy 5 question quiz for each. The tests are medium difficulty I would say, as long as you pay attention to the lectures and read the take away points for the short readings you should do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great lecturer. Attendance is not mandatory but I would definitely recommend going to lecture because Dr. Amsterdam is very into everything he talks about. Not many grades, a few midterms and reading quizzes. Amsterdam clearly loves what he does and it shows.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a great professor because his lectures are engaging, loves to answer questions even in a large class setting, very straight forward to make an A. Only have midterms and 3 book quizzes. All books can be found online. I also realized he assumes that we have already had US History before.

Prof. Amsterdam is an amazing lecturer, he teaches history as if it's reading a storybook. He includes plenty of details to make the material relevant to the modern day and our lives. He makes it very clear what you need to know in order to pass with an A. Very little work outside of lecture as long as you pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He gives very long lectures that may seem to ramble  Easy class but you have to at least try and pay attention.

He will lecture all class, but is engaging and says what key words to remember for the test. I struggled on the first test because I was mixing up my facts, and asked if he could fact check my definitions after that, and he did. He is very nice, and helps you if you need it. It can be a lot of content at times, so just take good notes and study.

I would do anything for Daniel Amsterdam. Hands down my favorite HTS prof at Tech (I'm an HTS major). He's incredibly caring, enthusiastic, and knowledgeable. He really cares to make the work load reasonable, and succeeds. He also legitimately wants you to learn and succeed. He managed to make "research methods" an absolute blast so props.

Dr. Amsterdam is one of my favorite profs. I was dreading this required course but he made it legitimately fun, and was an extremely caring guy with a lot of respect for us. The class was definitely a decent bit of work, but I learned more than I expected to, and an A is very achievable, especially if you ask for help. Honestly a blast, 10/10.

Very minimal work for a GT class. His lectures are outstanding and are crucial for hitting marks on exams. Amsterdam's class was a rare instance in which I enjoyed learning history. My advice is to fill out the definitions from his study guides right after each class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Amsterdam is a super nice guy and his lectures are always enjoyable. He understands that most students at GT are STEM majors and are only taking his class for graduation purposes.

I usually despise history, but Dr. Amsterdam made the content genuinely enjoyable with his lectures. His test questions are based purely on the information he covers in class, so if you skip, good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Overall a great lecturer and a good guy. Also, the class is really easy- the only homework is 1-3 page readings for classes and 3 1-2 page "papers" throughout the semester which are essentially an automatic 100 if you do them. You have to go to class though bc notes are not posted online, but lectures are interesting and usually have a 5 min break

Dr Amsterdam cares about his students and is really passionate about the topic as well. He encourages participation even though it's a pretty big class. As long as you put some effort into the short essays and the study guide, it's a pretty easy and fun class.

Dr. Amsterdam understands most students take this class for the sake of the credit. He, therefore, makes it really interesting and the lectures are full of relevant jokes. He also has very few homework assignments. If you have a good study guide, it is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are extremely useful and if you attend class every day you will definitely succeed in the class. There's only a few assignments, but the homework is largely graded on completion and the tests are not extremely difficult. All around an amazing professor and I definitely recommend taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His lectures are genuinely Interesting and coming to class doesn't feel like a chore like some history classes do. He understands that we came to GT likely not to study history and doesn't overwhelm you with work. Generally a great professor and you should succeed if you put appropriate effort into the class.

One of my favorite teachers I have ever had. He has a plethora of knowledge on the subject and genuinely cares about the success of his students. Going to lecture is a must as his tests are word for word form his lectures. Overall a phenomenal experience and would take any course this professor offered.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Be sure to attend class! He gives away hints of the test and it would be impossible to study without lecture notes. He takes time to give breaks and makes jokes, so its not that boring (sometimes it gets pretty heavy though). The tests are clear cut and you know what you need to study/memorize.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Make sure you go to lectures. In my class, notes and powerpoints were posted, but lacked any content. If you don't go to lectures you will not be able to pass the class. Tests were multiple choice, but hard. Take notes in class and study them, and you will do fine. His lectures are also pretty interesting, and worth going to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You must attend the lectures to pass the class, but lectures are always interesting! The class requires a few readings here and there as well. He is truly a caring and understanding person. If you get to take his class, you are a lucky student.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Amsterdam is great! He always makes jokes during lecture, and he often gives breaks when he sees the class dozing. He is approachable in office hours and never turns down a question. The class is very lecture heavy, and there are few graded assignments other than tests. But the tests never have surprises or trick questions. 10/10 recommend
ENGH388: Instructions for all the assignments were very unclear. A very tough grader. She doesn't give extensions even there is a reasonable reason.

I took ENGH 388 at George Mason University. Worst professor ever. She deducts points for no reason and doesn't give much explanation. She doesn't help at all even when we are suffering. Doesn't reply to emails properly. Doesn't gives grades on time nor gives good grades. Best in the class was 70/100 for most assignments with an average at 52/100.
Awful professor overall. It appears she was terminated or forced out, which is suitable for a professor of this quality.

The worst professor I have had in my entire life. She simply reads off the slides in lecture, with absolutely no interest or care. Every class you miss beyond 2 drops grade a letter grade. She does not care about students learning or grades. Unfortunate because material could be interesting otherwise. That being said, the class is pretty easy.

She did not follow the Gatech ethics (which require instructor to give timely grading and feedback). More than 80% of grade come during the last two weeks of the semester. Even a lot of student file complaint against her to coc and school, nothing has changed much.

This is the most confusing course I have had in Tech. She copy the entire syllabus from her junior design class to this Tech comm. During the semester, she keep complaining how much work she have to do and add more and more assignment during the semester (put extra assignment in a vague category in grading).
Worst professor ever. Avoid if possible!
Great professor, easy to follow lectures, very chill assignments and grading.
Words cannot describe how awful my semester with Amanda was.

TERRIBLE and UNFAIR. This was an overflow class, so I understand. I gave the messiness of the assignments and her horrible feedback the benefit of a doubt. In the last 2 weeks of the semester, she gave lousy grades for assignments that lacked direction, feedback, or a rubric. Drafts were graded after finals. Lectures were awful too.

As everyone else mentioned, absolutely avoid this Professor at all costs. She grades based on her feelings, gives 0 useful feedback, expects you to be punctual w assignments but graded everything the day before graduation. Literally the worst educator I have ever had in my entire academic career dating to preschool. Drop her class immediately

You're better off dropping out than taking this professor. The alternative is getting kicked out because she randomly accused you of plagiarism, or having to do another semester because she threw a tantrum and gave everybody a zero on an assignment, or jumping off a bridge because I'd rather end it than have to endure her lectures again.

Avoid pls. Graded all assignments day before finals (likely drunk considering insulting nature of feedback and tendency to "lecture" hungover) and attempted to fail over half the class arbitrarily in everyone's graduating semester. Mandatory attendance, 4 "free skips" but if there was an assignment she gave a 0 even if it was completed virtually.
save yourself

Can only echo the other comments on what occurred during this class, but for context, our class was exclusively graduating seniors. Completely inconsistent grading standards, unfounded accusations of plagiarism, and an almost unbelievable lack of feedback. Would spend significant parts of lecture complaining about her personal life.

NEVER take this professor. Hands down the worst professor I've ever had in my entire life. Doesn't grade most assignments until 2 weeks before graduation. Without prior feedback on drafts or proposals, gives F's on the final assignment with condescending and belittling comments. She is not suited to be teaching at a university like Georgia Tech.

One of the worst professors I have ever had in my time at Georgia Tech. Decided to screw over the entire class less than two weeks before everyone in the class was graduating. She decided to give students F's on the final assignments with one word comments that were unprofessional that dropped students grade by over 20%.

Provides unclear or down right rude feedback on assignments. That is, when she decides to grade. For example she graded the final deliverable for the course BEFORE grading the proposal for said project. When she does decide to grade, many students would say that she seemed to grade blindly, providing no justification for how the student can improve

In all my years of education, I have never had such a horrible experience in a course and felt genuine animosity towards an instructor. She is extremely aggressive, hostile, and unhelpful in her written feedback and will take every opportunity to leave condescending remarks and belittle you in the comments of your assignment.

Horrible prof. Curses in every sentence. Drinks the night before lecture then complain about it in lecture. Disrespectful and seems to hate CS majors by insulting them in class with CS stereotypes. Admits to not caring about the class or teaching yet grades very harshly for some reason.

This is the first time in my life I have witnessed such an uncaring and rude professor. Always talks about her life and how much work she has; she openly hates her job and does not want to be there. Does not communicate and is insanely condescending when she's behind a screen: she openly threatens students while assigning Fs without any criteria.

This professor lacks respect for her position and students, often condescending and bitter. Her grading is inconsistent, and she's openly discussed being hungover and drinking after class. It's disheartening to see such behavior from someone in authority.

never has a class made me want to walk across the street without looking any way. I honestly would give up government secrets if you put me in her class. This was supposed to be a class about tech communication and not once has she ever communicated about anything to do with this class. Why does she talk more about her family than class concepts???

Grades everything last minute and extremely harshly. Talks about nonsense during class yet requires attendance. Has a major ego and is very mean to students. I feel like she's a deeply unhappy person that believes everyone else should be miserable as a result. I'd take an 8am over htis class any day.

Recommending avoiding this professor if possible. Truly does not seem to care about the students regarding their coursework they learn in the class. Unable to communicate the timeline of the class and what is expected for assignments. Assignments are graded extremely late and assignments are related. Makes it hard for students to improve.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR EVER!!!! Doesn't care about the students, gives way too much assignments, grades things way too fast and without much regard to actual quality of work. The worst professor I've had at this school and I pray for all those forced to take her as part of a graduation requirement.

(CS3803) AVOID AT ALL COST. WORST professor ever. RUDE, CONDESCENDING, DISORGANIZED. Does not understand either communication or anything technical, but teaches Tech Communication. More boring jokes and her life stories in class than useful lecture material, but taking notes is required as mandatory attendance. Changes syllabus arbitrarily.

(CS 3803) Terrible professor. teaches communication but cannot communicate themselves, students are constantly confused about instructions. Randomly cancels class and expects students to do several assignments in lieu of class. Randomly chooses assignments to grade very harshly. Very disorganized. Do not take if you have a choice.

(CS 3803 TC)
I have no idea what she is trying to teach and what I am doing with course

Attendance in lecture and studio participation was mandatory as it was part of the final grade. The final and midterm cover the most random topics in class but are not difficult. Your studio TA and participation will probably make or break your final grade.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS! By the time final exams had started, only 45% worth of assignments had been graded. On top of taking a long time to grade assignments, she grades harshly and on arbitrary criteria. You can adhere to the rubric all you want, but getting a good grade is near impossible. I was quite lucky to walk away with an A - take another prof!

Absolutely terrible at getting grades in on time and communicating through emails. She waits until the last day before grades are due to actually grade, so if you have weekly assignments due like weekly meeting agendas and you mess up on one, you essentially mess up on the rest of them because she doesn't give feedback on time. Hated her class.

Made this course much more difficult than it needed to be. Graded extremely harshly and did not consider historical averages for this class. Average GPA for this section was significantly lower than for other sections.

I took Amanda's class because it was at a convenient time. Brutal mistake. Grading was incredibly unclear, extremely hard to access outside of class, and the professor has literally zero technical knowledge, but seems to suggest that she does. Listen to the other reviews, take literally any other professor. To top it all off, she has quite an ego.
Lectures are easy to follow, and lecture slides are very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: (CS3001) She has some weird policies including dropping students' overall grades by 10% if they miss 2 lectures. Apparently she has instructed TA's to not give students above 90% in section participation. She is also very much NOT accessible and doesn't respond to emails, citing her "busy schedule". Overall mid prof but not the greatest person.

Avoid this professor. They are condescending and do not respond well to questions, grading is confusing and done on expectations that are never conveyed, and constant busy work detracts from things of actual value. Also, they lack the technical skills and soft skills to properly instruct/lead any class. Despite an A, this was a horrible experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. Is not qualified to teach the class, has no technical background and thus severely misgrades technical details. Grades assignments on expectations greatly beyond what is taught in class. Overall, would highly not recommend.

This is a person who literally doesn't deserve a job in academia. Do not take her if you can. I would even skip junior design if she was your only option. Every single assignment is incredibly vague and she grades super harshly. She is literally the most useless professor I've ever had.

This course itself is full of useless work, but Girard makes these assignments even more confusing. What you actually have to do is super unclear, and she is impossible to reach outside of class. She doesn't seem to care about students. They even released a final presentation / project less than a week before break with it due right as we got back.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Gives worthless assignments to waste your time, forces students to attend an expo she organized so it doesn't seem empty, gives vague instructions for assignments, takes off points seemingly at random, and made us give a presentation THE SAME DAY THEY TOLD US TO GIVE A PRESENTATION and much more. Literally the worst professor I've ever taken.

One of the worse professors I've had at Georgia Tech. Was incredibly rude and condescending whenever I asked a question in class. Half the lectures consisted on her complaining to the people who were present that no one was showing up (we had a class of 12) and the other half consisted of her talking about her dog or reading our assignments to us.

Terrible Teacher, she grades like she's blind, taking off points, saying we didn't submit it, when the submitted assignment is clearly in front of her face. The lectures are mandatory, and just serve to waste your time for the most part. Grades come in right before the end of the semester, such that you might not be able to get them changed. Awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She was better this semester overall considering she had some attitude issues. Her feedbacks did improve quite a bit as well. She is a late grader so it caused us unnecessary stress during the finals week. She clearly doesn't understand how canvas submission works because she took off 10 points for "not having video link" on May 9th night!
She grades super unfairly, saying that we missed parts of our assignments and when we showed they were there she said "Um, do you want me to add a point back or something?"

On the first day, we asked politely if we could choose our teams which is how the course has worked and the next class she claimed we were rude and ranted. This set the tone for the course. You'll do lots of writing for stuff that detracts from the project and she's an unclear grader so it's rough. You won't learn a thing but you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Should be a project-focused class, but gives busy work that wastes time from the actual client project. Gives vague feedback, often takes off for minor grammatical errors but messes up hear/here they're/their/there in the SAME feedback. On top of that, she grades harshly so you're more stressed about the grade in the class than the real proj.

Absolutely awful professor. She grades extremely harshly on assignments for seemingly no reason and her feedback on them is just terrible. It feels like she is looking for ways to make the class difficult for no reason. I have learned absolutely nothing useful from this class. Avoid her at all costs if you are taking junior design.

Prof. Girard is very interesting. If you don't follow the grading criteria extremely specifically, you probably won't get perfect grades on all the assignments. The class is a lot of busywork. However, you will find that it isn't her fault, the class is just designed horribly.

Girard is the worst professor I had at GT. She was very unclear when giving instructions and took off points on assignments for seemingly no reason. Going to her for help outside of class is useless as well. Avoid Girard for junior design at all costs.

I had Girard last semester and was not a fan of her. She still is pretty cold and her grading is just as harsh. However, she was pretty accommodating during the covid crisis so that's why I gave her a 2 instead of a 1. She eliminated some assignments, graded less harshly and didn't make lecture mandatory, which I truly expected her not to do.

Girard grades unnecessarily hard and takes off points for the smallest things. She also won't really clarify why she took off those points and can come off extremely condescending both in class and during office hours. If you see her name when registering, try to avoid her.

Her grading is extremely tough and random. She will take off lots of random points on a paper and her feedback will be extremely vague. Her lectures were really aggressive and she'll remind you every lecture that he has a PhD. Would avoid at all cost
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Amanda Girard is the worst instructor I have had at Georgia Tech. She lacks any compassion or care towards her students and does not grade any assignments on time. When she does grade assignments, she does not provide any feedback or grade to a rubric. She sets unrealistic expectation and does not provide feedback on drafts. Avoid her at all costs!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Taking a class with Professor Girard is a constant uphill battle. She does not clearly explain what she wants from students (she'll give you a rubric, but it's incredibly vague), will be condescending and rude when you ask for help/feedback, and has criticized students' work in front of the class to her co-professor. Avoid her at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Girard is the absolute worst LMC professor for junior design. Avoid her at all costs! Her grading feedback is very vague and she will take off points for absolutely NO reason. Her negative attitude, lack of awareness, and disrespect for student opinion is completely uncalled for.

One of the worst professors I have taken at Georgia Tech. Extremely slow and unreasonable grader with astronomically high expectations. She has quite the ego for an LMC professor and will not hesitate to defend herself when asked about grading. AVOID THIS PROFESSOR AT ALL COSTS!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Extremely and unreasonably tough grader for no good reason in what's supposed to be a fairly easy A class. Gave terrible and unclear feadback on assignments and didn't really follow the grading rubrics that were given. Overall awful, one of the biggest mistakes I made at GT was taking a class with this professor. 0/10

Dr. Alicea made it easy to understand the material, and the tests weren't difficult at all as long as you did enough practice questions. There's a lot of opportunities for extra credit and the grading scheme is very forgiving. The only thing that bugged me a bit was how she made it seem like no student could ever love physics as much as her.
Dr. Alicea was good at teaching

Dr. Alicia is an amazing professor who genuinely wants students to succeed. Do extra credit and stay on top of homework, it can take time some weeks. GPS helps explain concepts well, lectures are excellent, and tests are fair. Highly recommend!

Dr. Alicea is the best professor I had at my first semester of Tech. Patient, thorough and witty, she professionally handled the fearsome Exam 3 (alien question, iykyk), giving transparency in how the question was vetted then working through the full solution during her lecture – made possible when she is always, without fail, ahead of schedule.

Although I had a different instructor, I regularly attended Alicea's lectures because of her clear, structured teaching style. She explained each concept effectively, welcomed questions, and covered content efficiently without falling behind compared to other professors. I would highly recommend her for this course.

THE GOAT! Such engaging and easy to understand lectures. Cares about her students so much. At the end of the course, she literally individually reviews any borderline grades (ex: 89.45) to try and fairly bump up to the next letter grade, which tells you everything you need to know. Exam difficulty varies by unit, but partial credit carries.

díos mio my goat. if u are bad at physics and can't learn in these horrible 200+ person lectures for phys 2 i highly recommend watching her lectures. they are super thorough and she doesn't skip steps and verbalizes her work perfectly. i love her. wish i could've gotten an a but putting that on me and no fault of her. best resource here for gt phys

Dr. Alicea is hands-down the best PHYS 2211 prof you'll probably ever have at GT. She's amazing at going through key concepts and in-class problems (usually from old tests), making sure you truly understand how to solve everything STEP-BY-STEP. Her exams this sem were on the rough side but she is super accessible on Ed Stem and prepares you well!

She's pretty funny and her lectures aren't hard to understand. Actual concepts are doable, but exams are HARD. The problems aren't like the ones you do in class, so do ALL the test practice for each concept. But, Dr. Alicia truly cares about the success of her students and she's very approachable!!

She's the goat. Coming into Georgia Tech, I knew nothing about physics and was really worried for this course. Dr. Alicea was great, I feel like I now know physics on a high level and I was able to do well on the tests.

Not my direct prof. simply the coordinator however I will say, she genuinely loves her job. She subbed once for my section and I understood SO MUCH from her in that one lecture. Very responsive on Ed Discussion; I even asked her to create learning objectives for every weeks of the semester and she did! She really wants students to succeed.

AMAZING PROFESSOR! One of the best professors I've had at Tech! Her lectures explain the concepts so thoroughly and accessibly, and I've never had physics taught to me as well as how she taught. If you get her, you'll still have to work hard, but you'll be well-equipped for the exams/finals if you put in the work to understand. :)
Class was very difficult, Alicea gives a lot of resources to use to study outside, and on edstem has good information about what will be on each test.

As someone who doesn't have to take any physics classes besides PHYS 2211, this class and it's exams felt HORRIBLE. Still, Dr. Alicea is by far the best lecturer you can take for the class, to a point of making me look forward to the class at least a bit. The grading scheme still makes it fine to do well in the class, and labs are trivial.
She is a great teacher, and she makes physics fun. But the tests are extremely difficult for no reason. I feel like there is no reason for the test to be so much harder than the homework.
she's so funny and somehow makes physics relatively understandable. her tests are horrendous though!

Great Teacher, who truly cares about our students. You are given many resources to succeed, although the tests are difficult. However, with a nice grading scheme, and lots of partial credit on the exams, this class is very doable.

Her lectures are super helpful and consists of tons of examples that help you learn the material. Exams can be difficult as they cover material learned in class but is sometimes hard to understand what's going on at first to be able to start the problem. Luckily, there's partial credit and the 5/10/15 split of the 3 exams help with your grade.

Physics 2 is known to be a demanding class, but alicea tries to make it easier to grasp. Summer semester goes fast and is very time consuming, but doing the GPS, lecture videos, and practicing past exams will prepare you well. I took phys 2211 here last sem with alicea, and phys 2212 had higher average exam scores surprisingly.

Dr. Alicea is by far the best Physics Prof at Tech. She takes complicated information and presents it in an easy-to-understand way with TONS of examples. Physics II is a challenging course, and the tests reflect that. However, the grade breakdown allows you to succeed even if you don't do very well on the three midterms and final.

Dr. Alicea is by far the best professor for Physics. For those who say her exams are hard and beyond what they believe was taught, you're wrong. As long as you understand the content well and its applications, no matter the question given, you'll be able to apply what you know. Not to mention the generous partial credit given. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!!!

The lecturer does a great job at giving you ample amounts of practice material, relevant examples through labs and group-work problems over teams, and has access to many helpful TA's while being very responsive to emails and questions on Ed-Stem. Tests are hard, with self-studying being necessary to pass. Hard class, good teacher.
Best professor for physics 2. Took this course online and it was easy.

She is an outstanding professor. I took this class online and found it much easier than the in-person version. The recorded lectures explain the concepts very clearly, and the ample practice tests prepared me well for exams. As long as you pay attention to the recorded lectures and utilize the GPS and practice tests, this class is a breeze.
The professor is a very nice and engaging lecturer, but she makes the multiple exams so difficult! Nearly all the exams are curveballs.

EXTREMELY hard exams! The professor doesn't do a good job of preparing you for the tests that are unnecessarily difficult. On one of the lecture videos, the professor said that a test 3 median of around 74 is considered "better than expected"!

I don't understand the other positive reviews; the lecturer does the bare minimum and teaches the formulas and theorems, but that's it. The content and exams are also extremely difficult. The exams especially have questions you've never seen before. There's also too much busy work, such as homeworks, which are long and don't prepare you for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best PHYS2211 teacher available! Physics is a hard class in general so no matter what teacher you get, it will be hard and up to you to learn the material. However, Alicea explains the content amazingly and will help you graciously if you ask. She truly is amazing. She posts her annotated notes after class so you can look at them when studying.

She was very good at lecturing, but sometimes could forget that not everyone knew physics like she did, and skipped over some basic stuff in problems later on. She also has really millennial-like humor, which isn't a bad thing, just cringey. Very easy to get a B in class, if you are better at physics or really lock in, you can for sure get an A.

Dr. Alicea is the best physics 1 prof. I didn't have physics in hs, and this class was REALLY HARD. If you have never taken physics, get a weekly tutor. Grading scheme is kinda forgiving. You can bomb one test and still get an A (I got a 56 on exam 1 and finished with a 91). Go to class, do all the practice problems, and use the Ed Discussion.

The content in this class was just a lot over a short period of time. If you want to do well I'd say put in the extra effort to rewatch Alicea's lectures and make sure you understand the concepts. Labs peer graded so easy and plenty of extra credit available. Not all assignments are mandatory but it is still a lot of work. Alicea is an amazing prof

Dr. Alicea is nice, but this class is not structured well at all. There is barely any leniency with the grading and, after hearing how peers did in previous semesters, it seems that they have recently restructured the course to make it harder. No cios incentive, barely extra credit ("bucket points"), no grade replacement etc.

Dr. Alicea herself is a kind & caring person. However, this course as a whole is just brutal. I've never had to worry too much about my grades & have a decently high GPA. If your past physics experiences were poor, tests may be even worse as a certain thought process is required. Little opportunity to catch up if you lack beginning knowledge prior.

This class is not designed for success. Many people who did well in this class had prior knowledge from AP physics. Dr. Alicea was pretty dry and intimidating via ed-discussion, a platform that was supposed to make students feel more comfortable with reaching out. There are way too many students taking this class for you to actually learn anything.

Dr. Alicea is a great lecturer who cares about her students. She is very knowledgeable about physics and always provides proofs to support her claims, rather than saying, "trust me bro." This class is hard, especially for those with little physics background in high school, but Dr. Alecia makes it better by working out A TON of examples in class.

She is very nice and a great professor. She is very passionate about physics, and very accessible outside of class. There are attendance points that go into a bucket category, but you can do other things to get the points so you don't need to go to class. Partial credit on exams is very generous as long as you show some understanding of physics.

Don't go to class, just watch her videos. Alicea is miles better than any other physics prof. She is EXTREMELY sweet and a fantastic lecturer. She always gives enough time for clickers and does lots of explanations with physical objects to reinforce knowledge. The exams are notoriously very hard, but are graded fairly + you can regrade request.

She is a good lecturer and attendance isn't mandatory, you just need to do clickers. She also uploads a LOT of resources to try and help you. Her tests are crazy hard and way harder than any practice problems in lectures. Really sweet person. Be prepared for hard tests and hard labs.

Had her for PHYS I over the summer, meaning pre-recorded lectures. They were amazing. I am now watching her PHYS II lectures as I take it on campus, because she is x1000 better than my current lecturer. Highly recommend you take her course, or use her lectures to supplement your worse professor's lectures.

Dr. Alicea-Munoz is amazing! Her lectures convey physics principles in a way that is easy to understand (I daresay even fun!). I attended her office hours after missing 3 weeks with bronchitis and she was very patient and helpful. The grading structure was generous and in the students' favor. Do not take physics 1 or 2 with anyone else at GT.

Dr. Alicea is an amazing physics professor. Her lectures are engaging and she genuinely cares about student learning. The coursework is challenging but manageable with regular attendance and using resources like Unstuck AI for practice.

She's actually the GOAT. I always hated physics, but I LOVED the way she taught and made it accessible for everyone to understand. She was funny, and a true gem. The exams were not too difficult if you do practice problems and pay attention in class. The best thing is, she was very open to changing based on feedback, which many teachers don't do.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: actual goat teacher

I didn't do great in AP Physics C in high school, so I was scared coming into the course. But, the way Dr. Alicea taught the content made a lot more sense to me than how I previously learned it. Even if you don't have her, all of her lectures are recorded and posted on Canvas. The example problems she does in them are really helpful.

ALICEA THE GOAT! She's the best physics teacher ever. Watch her recorded lectures! I didn't even have her as a teacher but her video lectures were the only reason I got an A. She even healed everything that went wrong in high school AP Physics. She's also a super responsive and organized course coordinator. I understand physics now, thanks to her!

Since the course is graded by so many things, you do not have to do extremely well on exams to get an a. Dr Alicea is a wonderful person, she respects her students and is very caring. She streamed and posted her lectures online which made learning really accessible as I had difficulties physically going to lectures. Wonderful person 10/10 recommend
Dr. Alicea-Munoz is very caring and teaches very well. She cares a lot about people understanding the content and is generally responsive to students and with grade curves.

I took PHYS 2211 in the Summer of 2022 while it was an online course. Alicea-Munoz was an extremely caring professor who evidently loved what she was doing while she was teaching. The course consisted of difficult tests and Python-based homeworks. While the tests were difficult, partial credit was awarded which made it easy to do okay in the class.

She is an amazing professor that truly cares about her students doing well. She is always available to help you out to make sure you understand what you need to. Physics is a difficult class, but it is very easy to do well in it with her as a professor.

Alicea is passionate about the concepts she teaches and clearly cares for her students' understanding. I have never taken a class this organized that provides as many resources to succeed. Lectures are very helpful and offered virtually which is very nice. Many practice questions available to study for midterms and the final.

Stopped going to my professor's class after a few weeks and starting going to Alicea's. They were fine but Dr. Alicea is awesome, I do not understand how someone can be so consistently straightforward with all of their teaching. She cares a lot, and she always responds on the ed discussion board to all sorts of questions.

Her love for Avatar and Physics are apparent in every lecture. There are a lot of comments about Test 3 but me and most of my friends/lab ppl said they felt fine about it. Tests aren't easy, but fair. It's physics, it's hard. But if you put in the work, you will do well. The lowest test is only 5%. The course is designed so you can have "slip-ups".

She is truly an incredible professor, the best I've had at GT. I'm taking physics 2211 right now as a sophomore and she has really made things click for me unlike they did in high school physics. Homework really helps for tests and also the GPS worksheets so make sure you can do those on your own and you should be set for the exams

She's such an amazing professor! I'm not good at physics, but the way she teaches it makes the material a lot easier to understand. She goes over lots of examples in detail, and exams are usually pretty similar to questions she goes over in the lectures. There's also tons of material for extra practice in order to succeed

ONE OF THE BEST PROFESSORS AT TECH. Amazing lecturer, as well as a caring teacher, Tests are reasonably difficult. As long as you attentively participate in lectures, you do not need to stress at all in her class.  Basically recommended by everyone.

She has the lecture material online, so you can use it for review. But it's still recommended to attend lectures online or in person. You will have a lot of homework, but they're not too difficult. She prepares students for the exams well and has resources that can help you prepare for them. It's a difficult class, but she makes it manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The reviews are true, she really is a great professor. I could never manage to do well in high school AP Physics, but Dr. Alicea helped me finally understand physics concepts and make things click. Her lectures are very helpful, and if you do the practice tests you should be good for the exams, though they can be quite hard so definitely study.

Dr. Alicea is a wonderful course coordinator and lecturer! Her accessibility both in class and online provide a huge advantage to students, and she is really good at introducing new topics while being mindful of the level of preparedness of students!
Hands down best 2211 professor!

Physics 1 at Tech is super hard. In my opinion, it's the hardest class I've taken, but Dr. Alicea explained things so well. If you can't get her as your professor for 2211, don't worry because you can just watch all her videos that she puts on Canvas. The only downside is that the labs use a lot of coding and we are never taught how to code.

LOVE LOVE LOVE HER!! Her greatest quality are her lectures are also very easy to follow and learn from. Her in class demonstration is also very helpful. You can also see that she is very passionate in teaching physics!

AMAZING PROFESSOR!! If you get the chance please take her for physics 2211. I actually didnt even have her but i went to her lectures and she makes the class so engaging. She also has the most amazing online system for feedback, lectures, etc. All past material can be accessed digitally. I honestly appreciate her tech savviness so much.

SHE IS TRULY SPECIAL! The greatest professor I've taken and that's saying something considering she's teaching PHYS 2211. She is so funny, easy to understand in lectures. Easy midterms and she runs the course so well. If you're in the HP section, she even makes the final optional for them sometimes and they do an easy final project. Labs easy.

Amazing professor. Highly highly recommend making a one on one appointment with her in review for exams, shes amazing at explaining and clarifying concepts. Super nice and helpful, she wants you to do well in the class.
Such a good teacher. Super kind, very understanding, makes excellent videos.
Hands down the best physics professor on Tech. I had a different teacher but reviewed her lectures and was extremely helpful. Engaging and just a genuine good professor. 100% rec

The tests were pretty easy compared to the difficulty of the homework. Homework had a flexible deadline. Class was calc based but was almost exactly the same as algebra based. Labs were about 30 minutes of working on problems. You have to turn in lab assignments based in vpython. They take some time but aren't bad and were peer graded.

Dr Alicea is without any doubt one of the best professors at Tech - if not the best! Her lectures were in depth, and she always kept us engaged. She made sure to answer any questions, even though it was a very large class and cares a lot about the students. It is very sad that she is not teaching Physics 2 this semester. Take her if you can!!!

Though she was only the course coordinator, Dr. Alicea was one of the best professors I've had in my 3 years at Tech. She was caring about her students and really just wanted us to succeed. She was very understanding with deadlines (with technology crashes or personal issues) and her class was the most organized class ever. Would 10000% take again.

Phenomenal lecturer and great professor. I was never bored by the any of the lectures, and the instead of just reading bullet points she inserts a large amount of examples into her lectures. Even with the difficulties of Physics 2 as a subject, she made it easy and my favorite class I've taken thus far.

Physics is tough, but her grading system made it very possible to get an A even if you struggled with testing. Ample study materials provided, clear test topics, and great recorded lectures. No curve, but the grading system is fair enough to help you out. Very helpful in office hours.
I hardly attended in-person lectures, and instead used the online videos. It cannot be understated how much Alicea absolutely CARRIES this course with her content.

Great professor, there is an option to go to class or not, definitely go to class and don't fall behind in lectures, as content can build up quickly. There are weekly group problem worksheets, which can be difficult, but are only for credit and sometimes very similar questions to the tests.

didn't have her as my professor, but I watched all of her video lectures. I was behind about 3 weeks in lectures (don't do that please) so I binged all her lectures and did practice, and I was still confident on the exams. keep up with her and an A is beyond attainable. no boring lectures, very inciteful. there's a reason why she only has 5 stars.

Her lectures are not boring at all and she clarifies any questions you might have. She's very caring towards students and is obviously very passionate about what she does. Lectures are also streamed on Teams & recorded. There are a ton of resources! If you put effort into it you can do well (even if you're not good at physics).

At Georgia Tech, I have discovered that many professors don't have a passion for teaching. That was until I discovered Dr. Alicea. Because of her instruction style and engaging dialogue I started to look forward to her lectures, and rediscovered my eagerness to learn. As a woman, I look up to her and hope one day I'm as strong as she is!

If you get the chance to take her class, I highly recommend going to lecture and paying close attention. The lectures aren't boring and she seems to really care that everyone in the class understands what she is teaching. I won't say it's easy, but you have the tools to do well in the class.

Great professor, hard class. Always a tough combination but it's not an easy A. Easy B at best. Try not to fall behind on lecture, she will give you "bucket points" for attendance but not necessary and lectures are recorded.

Dr. Alicea-Munoz is by far the sweetest professor I have taken at GT. I took PHYS 2211 online over the summer, and watching her lectures made it so understandable. It is a hard class for sure, but she makes it easy for students to succeed. I wish I could give her 6 or 7 stars because she is truly amazing.
Best physics professor!! Awesome lectures that made content so understandable. Actually made me feel like physics 2 was easier than physics 1.

Greatest prof ever, she's actually the GOAT. Phenomenal lectures that make abstract concepts understandable and fun, well-structured resources, super caring and cares about not just your grade but your approach towards Physics. Reignited my love for the subject after high school. She should 100% be the face of teaching in GT.

Dr. Alicea is the best option for PHYS 2212! She has very helpful lectures and notes and is the most accessible professor ever. She really cares about her students and does her best to help us learn the material from physics 2, which was definitely harder than physics 1. Tests get harder as the semester goes on, but they are doable. You got it!

Dr. Alicea may be the best professor on campus. During the year, she took time to make sure all the students were doing ok in the class - whether it be their grade or their understanding of the concepts. At the end of the year, she went through each individual student's assignments to try and improve their grade as much as she could. 5/5 no doubt.
The best of the best! I'm so lucky that I got to learn from her! Absolutely incredible as a person and as a teacher

The greatest physics professor for both PHYS 2212 and 2211. I don't think I would've passed this class so easily without her because my professor was professor Jiang who is an okay lecturer but Munoz is on another level. I would watch her videos and understand concept easily and that would translate to good exam scores. Take her if you can!

I didn't even have Prof. Alicea as my professor for this class, but I had access to her lectures as she paired with my professor. Her lectures are super thorough and she does a really good job of explaining the content. She is also super nice and flexible with her students.

Dr. Alicea is not only the best physics professor but literally the best professor I had in all my four years at Georgia Tech. She provides many, many options to help student climb their grades up from difficult exams and also extra credits.
Just here to say anyone who hates her class is really just an Opp and is 1000% at fault. Best professor I've had for physics ever. took physics 1 and 2 with her !

Incredible Professor. I naturally suck at Physics, but she explained it thoroughly and did great demos during lectures. If you can't get her at least get modern so you can watch her videos. Truly a lifesaver, I thought I'd fail this class. Available to help students, and wants the best for you. She carries the entire Physics department on her back.

One of the best teachers I've ever had, absolutely incredible at teaching difficult concepts in ways students can fundamentally understand. Super fun and caring, and her lectures and PPTs are fantastic. Wholeheartedly deserves the only-5s rating she's got on here.

Dr. Alicea-Munoz is awesome for Physics I. She is extremely knowledgeable and approachable. All of her lectures were recorded in case you wanted to refer back to an example she covered (super helpful when studying for midterms and the final). You can expect to have a solid understanding of the concepts all while enjoying the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I did not have her as my physics professor, but I relied on her videos of the solutions to the Group Problem Solving sessions to succeed in Modern Physics 1. Absolutely phenomenal explanations! Tests were hard, but she gave me a great foundation to physics problem-solving. TAKE HER IF YOU GET THE CHANCE! Modern Physics 2 will be a breeze with her!

Hear me out: she is the best professor ever! Physics is a hard subject itself but her lectures are so comprehensive. She cares about her students, has the best humor, is very relatable, and has several grade repair options. If you want to survive physics, she is literally the best option at Georgia Tech. Make sure you do practice exams, lifesaver!
Dr. Alicea is amazing! I went into the class scared of physics and came out as someone who genuinely enjoyed the class! She is a great lecturer and the tests are fair. 10000/10 would recommend
I've never liked physics too much but Dr. Alicea was excellent in her clarity and ability to make physics effortless. 100% recommended!
