Probably the best teacher I've ever had. Phenomenal lectures and slides, enjoyed labs, loved the course structure and methods of teaching (the Procedures in the PPTs are amazing). Great resources, super caring + accessible. Genuinely understood concepts fundamentally as opposed to using formulae, and it really paid off. Undisputed teaching GOAT.

Dr. Alicea is the greatest professor! Her lectures are engaging and she makes hard physics concepts easy to understand by focusing on real-world problems instead of derivations and etc. She's also very caring and easy to reach out to when you have an issue.

Dr. Alicea is awesome! She has moved back some lab deadlines and is willing to be helpful in ed discussions (forum discussions) to answer questions about lectures and tests. I would 5/5 recommend taking her for either physics I or II as you will learn a lot and be entertained while doing so.

PHYS 2211 is a challenging class, no matter who you take it with. Prof. Alicea moves very fast which can take some time to get used to, but she breaks down & explains concepts very clearly and provides a plethora of study resources. She records all of her lectures which are incredibly helpful to review and beyond all, is incredibly caring & sweet.

I struggled with AP Physics C in high school, mainly with the angular momentum and motion topics. Also the mv^2/R stuff used to be confusing.
Dr. Alicea explains it really well and she's EXTREMELY helpful on Ed discussion and office hours. She made physics so engaging too for many, something that is quite the accomplishment. Take her if you can.

Amazing professor, provides video lecture recordings for all sections of PHYS 2211 so that even students outside of her lectures can be prepared to succeed in the class in addition to being extremely caring and flexible for her students

Alicea is the GOAT, you should absolutely take her class if you have the chance to. You'll be way better at physics for it, and you'll have a good time in class. Lectures are engaging and worth attending.

Dr. Alicea is an amazing professor! She is extremely passionate about physics, and her excitement made the lectures engaging. She does a good job of making physics fun. I came into the class knowing absolutely nothing of physics, and although I had a rough start, the resources she provides us with really helps! Definitely take her if you can!!

Most amazing professor I've had for any class. I've taken physics classes in high school and grown a hatred for them but she actually made it fun for me. As long as you do the work, it is very easy to succeed.  I am honestly kind of sad to be leaving her class because she was just such a kind hearted and enjoyable professor.
Great! Take her class if you can. Truly the best :)

I suck at physics, I was never able to do well in high school and then when I took Dr. Alicea's class I did really well. The labs are relatively easy and while the tests were hard, there's lots of partial credit. Dr. Alicea also teaches really well! Also, she's super accessible and there are weekly assignments with flexible due dates!

TAKE PROF ALICEA! I took it over the summer. She thoroughly explains concepts, her examples are always relevant, and she is very caring. She is also always available and wants to help you succeed! I didn't have any physics knowledge coming into this class, and she made it so enjoyable. Labs are very fun and GSP problems are very similar to tests.
i took the online version of physics over the summer and prof alicea made it so easy. interesting material and the tests were pretty similar to the hw

The course was asynchronous so my experience was pretty rough because of that. With that being said lectures were pretty good for prerecorded lessons. Professor had ~1 week lead time to respond to emails but was more than willing to have 1 on 1 meetings (She arranged one w me on an Institute holiday which was very nice).
Tests/HW similar to lecture

She's attentive to students and makes herself very available and transparent outside of class. She changed the lab report rubric based on student feedback and gave us a detailed reason why (based on numerous reports of unfair grading and harassment in the group chats). The tests were hard but not anything you wouldn't have been taught in class.

Took the online async version of 2211. Despite being recorded, lectures were clear, informative, and she does a great job of explaining student misconceptions and providing detailed answers. She did a great job of making herself known and accessible through weekly updates on Ed. Grading is very generous and she is an extremely caring person.

Physics 1 with Dr. Alicea-Munoz is the way to go. I was nervous since it's Physics at Tech, but if you go through all the recorded lectures and the homeworks you are completely fine. She is incredibly thorough and there was never a problem where I was confused after she went through it. Highly recommend taking it async with her over the summer.

I took this as a summer class online. Alicea herself was amazing; her weekly review videos were really clear to understand and she was easily available for questions. Not super happy with the formatting of the class as all the lectures were recorded from other professors. The class is difficult but there's generous partial credit.

Dr. Alicea is a great lecturer! Once you get used to her fast paced teaching style (takes about a week), her explanations are really easy to understand, and she answers questions thoroughly so you never leave feeling confused. Her lectures are fun, and she is very accessible outside of class through EdX and office hours.

One of the best profs I've had. Genuinely cares about her students both in and outside of class. Gave me some extensions and rounded some grades to help me finish with an A in the class. Makes boring topics more fun, and is super easy to reach. Overall an amazing professor that anyone would be lucky to have.

One of the best, if not the best, professors I've had at Tech.  Very caring and offers plentiful opportunities for success.  Always available through Ed, office hours, email, or even after class.  Exams were easy if you take the provided practice tests and get help if you need it.  Highly recommend!

Dr. Alicea was one of my favorite professors from this semester and the only reason I didn't get an A was because I kept sleeping through class and got really behind. She explains concepts very thoroughly and makes them easy to understand. If you are taking physics, take it with her and go to class.

Dr. Alicea-Munoz is an amazing professor, she teaches so well and really understands the needs of her students. The grading is super fair and she makes everything make sense. A super enjoyable professor and I recommend anyone who can takes her for physics.
She's a great professor, especially if you have never taken physics before. But, this class is not an easy A. She is the better professor out of everyone else. I highly recommend taking her!

Best teacher I have taken in Tech. Excellent lectures and great communication with students. Every lecture has in-class participation questions that are graded just for submission, so you will need to attend lectures. If you go to lectures and understand the examples she gives, you will do well. Use old exams to practice for tests.
Alicea is the sweetest, kindest, most generous, caring, and wonderful teacher I have taken at tech to date!!!

Dr. Alicea was a gem to have. She's extremely accessible outside of class- willing to help with lab or questions about homework. She posts very helpful review material and overall cares about her students/their grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Had her as the lab coordinator for physics 1. Always responds to emails quickly and really cares about her students. Def take physics with her if you can.

Dr. Alicea is the most understanding professor I've had thus far at Tech. I was going through some very unexpected health issues and not once did she make my life harder, she only offered her unconditional support and help. She also is excellent when it comes to asking for academic help. Overall, amazing professor and person.

Probably the most caring person at Tech. Genuinely a treat to have her and Professor Fenton for 2211. Her structure added to the class and communication with students is the biggest asset for anyone taking the class. Definitely do what you can to take her for 2211!
Very nice and helpful
Dr. Alicea is a very caring instructor who is always willing to help students succeed. She made physics 2 a very smooth and enjoyable experience.
This class was very good, very good lecturer. Explained the concepts well, and was super accessible
Truly cares about her students. Tried to make the course as doable as possible.

Dr. Alicia-Munoz is just awesome, plain and simple. She's so accessible, interactive, and helpful. She truly understands student needs and always makes sure to stay in touch with the general student population. She's also an amazing teacher in general and is just awesome all around!
Awesome Professor! The class was set up poorly, but Professor Alicia was able to adapt and release better lectures. She is kind and understanding, would 100% take her class again.

She is very organized, knowledgeable, and caring: exactly what you need to succeed in your first physics college class. She is very accessible outside of class and won't stop explaining material until you fully understand. Her lectures and office hours were great for studying for exams. Loved taking the class with her!

Dr. Alicea was a very involved lecturer, and extremely enthusiastic. There was a point where we had to ask her to stop answering every single question from students because she was just that involved. Take her class if you can.

Dr. Alicea made Physics 1 a very enjoyable experience. The mini-tests/final are all very reasonable, and she made an effort to reduce the stress caused by the pandemic. Multiple extra credit opportunities were given, and the textbook provided was optional.

Given the remote format and additional strain caused by the pandemic, Dr. Alicea was very caring and made the effort to make the class more flexible to accommodate students and reduce stress. There were many extra credit opportunities and easy participation points (HW, clickers) helped offset a low test grade. Textbook in syllabus but not used.

Professor Alicea was a great lecturer and explained physics concepts very clearly. She does a ton of practice problems in class and recitation which are very helpful for the tests. I didn't need to touch the textbook at all. She's very dedicated, enthusiastic, caring, and fun. Class grading scheme is pretty forgiving and the tests weren't too bad.

Dr. Alicea clearly cares about her subject and works hard to make class fun and interesting. She uses clicker questions, some of which were just Avatar and Spongebob memes, during lectures for attendance, however the attendance portion of the grade can be substituted with other optional assignments. She is the most caring, pure professor, 10/10.

Honestly the only reason I got through physics. Extremely caring and explains things very well. I actually took physics with the other section/professor but sat through her lectures and used her notes because she was so much more effective of an educator. Easily accessible outside of class and very kind and funny

Dr. Alicea is the only reason I was able to do well in Intro Physics I. The class is tough but she was very accessible and made it easy to ask her questions about homework, labs, or lectures. She is definitely a great professor and is dedicated to her students. She was also very engaging but beware the tests are tough!

Alicea was extremely helpful during office hours and clearly enjoys teaching the course content. Her summary notes before each test were incredibly useful. She is very responsive through email and Campuswire. Previously, she was a head TA for this class for many years and her experience really shows.
Just take Dr. Alicea if given the option. You won't regret it.
Very talented at lecturing, very accessible, very knowledgeable in Physics, and a wonderful person overall. Unbelievable that this was her first semester lecturing.

She's an amazing professor who cares deeply about her students. She trusts all of her students and wants them to succeed so bad. She even gave lecture right after getting surgery because it was right before a test. Please take her for PHYS 2211. You will not regret it. (Also her test problems are pretty easy :) )
Dr. Alicea is such an awesome professor! Her lectures are fun an interesting and she's very enthusiastic about class. It is very obvious that she cares about all of us, even in a 200 person class!

Dr. Alicea really cares for her students and this class despite being met with hundreds of student initials on her computer every morning. She's so dedicated that she would lecture even though she had to undergo surgery right before our final midterm. You can tell she knows the material well and makes sure to answer every question thrown her way.

Despite the course being online, Dr. Alicea did a great job of energizing the class and interacting with the students. She's a legend and was extremely invested in the class. You could tell she really enjoys teaching and makes classes fun. If you skip lectures or doze off, you probably will struggle but stay focused and Muñoz will carry you through

Although this class was online, Dr. Alicea really made it one that I enjoyed attending. She explained some complicated topics pretty well and made it an overall great experience. She also captures my attention nicely with some well-designed clicker questions to help our understanding of the subject. Labs were a pain, but to no fault of her own.

Dr. Amekudzi-Kennedy was an excellent teacher. You can tell she cares both about civil and about students learning and growing in her class. Exams are graded pretty leniently and she is incredibly kind and open to meeting and talking about anything CEE. The project was fun, and isn't bad if you incrementally work on it through the semester.

Group project heavy; you work with the same group all semester. some exams, but easy if you keep up with class content. the final is the group project, which is sort of graded tough. pay attention to techniques taught in class, because this is what they are looking for

Dr. Kennedy really cares about her students. Long homeworks/tests that are graded pretty tough but the group project should help with your grade. She is so kind and responds immediately to your emails. Overall an interesting class that really teaches you a lot about sustainability and civil systems. Probably more work than it needed to be though

Dr. Kennedy is the best! She has a great personality and is highly respected in the field of Civil Engineering and Sustainability. The class has tests, a group project, and homework all weighted equally with an optional final exam. If you attend class, do the hw and practice tests, and work well with your group members, an A is very achievable.

Personally, this is one of my favorite teachers here at Georgia Tech! I am very interested in Sustainable Urban Development and although the class is called Civil Engineering Systems, it is amazing how she focuses on sustainability analysis of systems as the basis of the class. Additionally, she is the most respected in her field! So much knowledge

Although a hard class, instructor is amazing! Knows concepts and explains them clearly. Although not apparent at first, she does care for you and wants you to be success. Just keep up with the lecture material and stay on top of your group project! The group project is a lot of work and its super important you work on it throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This class requires a lot of work. The final is optional; I was borderline so I had to take and somehow made an A. This class has readings, a group project which requires research, and homework assignments. The prof explains well enough. If you want to meet with her you have to make an appointment (she's busy). Very knowledgeable about her subject

If you're an A student who works hard for your grade, don't take her. If you only look for easy B with minimal effort, you've found your gem. Ridiculous grader (you'd get like 0.5 or 0.8 on "definition" about sustainability in an ENGINEERING class.) Does not have solution for in class problems. VERY inaccessible. Grades on project very arbitrary.

Decent professor who clearly cares about the subject. The class has easy material but you really need to work hard to do well. First test involves memorization so class average was low but the other 2 tests are math which is easy. Also, group project is tedious and there's a decent amount of homework in the class. Work hard and you'll get an A (88
Good professor, clearly passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. Lots of writing involved, as well as a massive group project.

Dr. Amekudzi-Kennedy is very passionate about this course but isn't the best at relating to students and student concerns.  The grading criteria is slightly strange and she expects you to do a lot for the class outside of lecture.  She is a great person and very nice but the class was just average and tedious at times.
Very willing to help anyone that has a question and very nice. She's very knowledgeable in the subject. I would recommend her!

Dr. Bruckman is one of the most engaged, passionate professors I've ever had. Every lecture kept me interested and was filled with stories that make the material memorable. She's funny, witty, and very kind. She gives clear expectations from the beginning. If you complete the readings and pay attention, you will do well. I highly recommend.

Online community was a pleasant surprise. Had a lot of fun working on the term paper. Lectures are interesting. Beware of the many and sometimes long readings. TAs were excellent as well. Generally an easy grader and very understanding about student concerns. A fun personality on top of all that. Definitely beating the reddit mod stereotype

Dr. Bruckman is just off. Her course is largely easy in that what is expected is clearly defined, but someone so unethical from the things she says during class to her object favoritism should not teach an ethics course. I got an A so I shouldn't really complain.

Dr. Bruckman's very caring towards students and her lectures are very engaging and interesting. At the start, there is quite a bit of reading + homework essays, but it gets way easier as the course progresses. Make sure you participate in Section and you'll be just fine. The 2 exams are detail-specific. Very easy course overall, would recommend.

In the first half, you have short papers due weekly. No final, but 2 midterm exams and a term paper due towards the end of the semester. There's a lot of reading assigned, but she basically reviews all of it in class the next day, so I don't read anything. Weekly discussion sections are long but interesting, depending on the people in your section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: she is a terrible person. Never go and talk to her as she has no sympathy for students her class is easy she just likes to ruin a handful of students grade every year.
So much writing, ridiculous, and required attendance every week.

It's ethics. Just show up, write papers, and talk about interesting politics/dilemmas in section. It's actually a fun class if you're at all interested in some of the dilemmas in the modern world. The grading is a little weird but it's still very easy to get an A as long as you are on time with assignments and go to section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Bruckman is the best professor I have had at Georgia Tech. As long as there is effort in the papers due each class, you will do fine. Dr. Bruckman is incredibly knowledgable, and she does a great job of conveying the material in a way that is easy to understand and engaging. This class is highly valuable and very applicable to the real world.

This is one of the most rewarding classes I have taken. Amy is a wonderful communicator - each one of her lectures is an experience and it seems like 75 minutes passes by way too quickly each time. The other reviews aren't completely wrong (we do have weekly readings and reflections), but their claims of length and commitment are exaggerated.
Don't take this course. There is more than 50 pages of reading due before every lecture and you have to write a 2-page reflection on the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: While Professor Bruckman is a good lecturer and she loves the content, she believes her students' lives only consist of her class. Before every class you must read 50+ pages (usually her own papers) and write a two page reflection paper (due exactly 24 hours and 15 min before class) on top of normal course work as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Super great lecturer and it is clear she loves the topic she is teaching. However, this course is a glorified writing course with weekly or biweekly writing assignments. Course is extremely TA dependent because your discussion TA will grade your homework and essays. I had a great TA, but some of my friends didn't. Overall, very easy course
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, really cares about her students. Lots of readings for the class, but she goes over them so it's easy enough to skip.
Prof. Bruckman is one of my favorite professors I've had a GT. She's a great lecturer, but there's a lot of reading and a lot of writing in the class so beware if you aren't a fan of either of those.

I took this course Spring 2022. I found the lectures to be extremely dry. Prepare yourself to participate in class discussions, which are highly philosophical. Your grade is almost entirely dependent on essays. It seemed to me that if he didn't agree with your stance on a topic, you would receive an unfavorable grade for the essay and vice versa.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The readings can be long at 15-25 pages on average but you will do well as long as you show up to class, participate, and complete the assignments. Discussions in class are engaging and Dr. Prasad is not heavy on lecturing. He cares a lot about students and can give a lot of guidance on the two essays (which were 50% of the class grade).

There was a lot of reading and the material was pretty dense. The class itself though was interesting and engaging and Dr. Prasad was very caring about the students. There are normally three papers and a few small assignments. It's expected you do the readings before class to participate but not required (i.e. no pop quizzes).
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Great Prof
No Comments
The most amazing professor I have ever had!!  Can we spell out NOBEL PRIZE

The grading was based on 3 homework assignments, 2 tests, and a final which didn't leave room for error. Don't let the fact that tests are open book make you think they're easy. The test averages were low (C's and D's) and grading was harsh. The professor was rude and often called students out for just asking questions.
Exhaustive class. A lot to learn.

You'll learn more by not attending his lectures. He doesn't curve at all, so ignore his 'don't worry about your grades you can make it up' and seriously buckle down. I highly suggest just not taking his classes, half the class got C's or below in a graduate class.  While the class topics sound appealing, teach it yourself, trust me.

Dr. Dixit's class is tough, but very close to real world experience. The amount of learning that happens is tremendous. I come from a family of carpenters and therefore had good CAD experience already. However, I learnt a whole lot more by taking his class. Two thumbs up.

The class may seem difficult at first. But as soon as you understand the expectations and ask questions. You will be fine. The professor is happy to answer all questions as long as rules are followed.

Dr. Dixit is one of the best Professors of my entire life.  He is devoted to teaching like no other. No needless Power point presentation or talking jargon. He faces the students all the times. Works with them  for all the problems. Moves around in the class and is always ready to help. A must take Professor!
Dixit is a very helpful professor who makes all assignments/project requirements clear. He is a good teacher who will take an interest in you and expects a lot of effort from you.
He super nice. In office hours he spent well over an hour making sure i understood the topic. His grading is a bit inconsistent... but overall he is very fair. He also curves very nicely.

This guy was incredibly frustrating to deal with. I would not take him. He digresses from directions, makes up his own, and then grades based on things that he doesn't tell you. He was really a bad teacher and you should not take him!

Do NOT take this professor. He does not follow a textbook, he does not teach in class at all, all of his instructions are unclear, and to top it all off his grading is very harsh and inconsistent. Though I got A's on the tests and obviously understood the material, I didn't do as well in the overall class because his projects were ridiculous.

I was not doing well in his class and went to him for help. He spent 1.5 hours trying to explain the labs when he could easily have asked me to go to a TA. No doubt he grades hard but gives curves the grades. He gave 18 exra-points for exam 1 for a very simple assignment.

I currently have this professor.  Although, his class is a bit difficult, he knows his subject matter really well. You just have to work hard and ask him questions. He is very approachable. This class is meant to be hard and this prof is one of the smartest I've had from whom you can learn the material at a very in-depth level.

She forces in class participation which is scary at first but you'll get used to it. Pacing is rough at first with the alphabets but the course load is pretty light afterwards. She grades super nicely and gives exam formats beforehand.

I had Matsushima-sensei for both JAPN 1002 & 1001. She is so incredibly accommodating to students, if you're sick and miss a quiz or exam she allows for make-ups. Very interactive lectures (expect to be called on at least once per class). I felt 1002 to be a significant difficulty jump from 1001, but matsushima-sensei made the transition easier.

Foreign languages are hard, let alone one that often uses three alphabets in the same sentence. Yes, you'll have to put in the work and you will have to memorize a lot, but Matsushima-Sensei is very clear about what she expects you to know and grow.

She makes it very easy. Great professor.

Matsushima-sensei is an amazing professor. She is very kind, makes expectations clear, and provides plenty of resources for studying and test preparation. Her lectures focus on speaking exercises. You are well-prepared for homework. Foreign languages take attending class and additional studying, but she makes the process very enjoyable. がんばって！

The Japanese language has always been on my list of languages I wanted to try out. Her classes did not disappoint, and there's lots of fun participation activities and slightly time consuming homework(They're not hard). It shouldn't be that hard as long as you put in effort. 10/10 class.

Matsushima 先生 is so sweet. Japanese was my favorite class this semester. Attendance is mandatory, but going to class never felt like a chore. There's group work too, but it's fun to get to know other classmates. This doesn't feel like a 4 credit hour class at all. There's lots of extra credit too, so I never had to worry about my grade. ありがとうございます！

I took almost all the introductory classes with her, at first I was planning to only fulfill my humanities requirements but I loved her class so much I got a major instead, went on study abroad, and met most of my friends through the Japanese department. Life changing class :)

I LOVE Matsushima Sensei! She is an absolute angel. Teaches very well and will always give reviews for any test. She is very easy to reach and you can tell she really loves and cares about her students.
She's the sweetest prof ever. Explains things so they're easy to understand, and cares a lot. I turned in a few assignments late and she takes off little to no points.
She is amazing, I enjoyed every single class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Matsushima is very kind and an amazing professor overall! No complaints here. She is very understanding and patient with students but is also clear about what she expects from them. Expect to find yourself practicing Japanese with other students in this course! There is homework, but it typically doesn't take much time.

Prof is amazing for an intro level course. Most of your grade comes from just participating in activities and doing homework. The tests and language practice is really easy, as long as you take 30 minutes to memorize the vocabulary provided. I highly recommend her classes, because she is thorough going through the material.

I had Matsushima-sensee for Fall, and she was amazing. While there were many HW assignments for practice, they were true to the types of questions asked on the tests. Practicing dialogue with every student in the class created some solid chemistry. I highly recommend learning all hiragana and katakana before this course to have the best experience!

Matsushima-sensei was my favorite professor in the semester that I had her in. Participation in class is important and the homework may be tough, but she is such a caring person and wants to see her students succeed. Definitely take her if you can.

Matsushima-sensei was great! Going to lecture and participating in class was really important. She explained grammar points very clearly. When it comes to learning characters in JAPN classes though, lectures are def not enough. You must self-study hiragana/katakana/kanji. If you grind out kana before taking 1001, you'll have a MUCH better time.

Matsushima sensei was the best! Definitely take JAPN1001 with her if you are wanting to learn Japanese. She is so kind and really helpful. The course requires that you study a lot because you're learning a new language, but she makes it fun and enjoyable. Highly recommend! It's a lot of work but it's so worth it and you learn so much!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Handles online classes very well. Good at encouraging participation. Fast grader and very helpful in office hours. I took JAPN 1001 and it was a lot of work but taking it with Matsushima sensei made it easier and more enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved taking her class. She makes learning Japanese fun and is always patient. Japanese is definitely not the easiest language to learn, much less teach, but she definitely does it well!
If you want to learn Japanese. Do it with Matsushima!

She's awesome! The classes are fun and we usually got out early. Matsushima is very patient and grades fairly. I never saw her mad or raise her voice or even get upset really. She will joke around with us a little and creates a fun learning environment.

Matsushima-sensei is so nice! She is super patient and cares a lot about her students. Most of the class will be spent practicing speaking Japanese, which helps a lot with learning the language. This isnt the easiest class, and there are tons of homeworks and quizzes, but if you do the work you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: If you take this class, you better be prepared to spend around half of class every day practicing speaking Japanese out loud with other students. Participation is expected, and it greatly pays off.

Matsushima-sensei is my favorite teacher in the japanese department so far. She's very helpful and relaxed although I wouldn't say she's easy. She expects a lot but doesn't make you feel awful if you need help.

??????, is an amazing person. She is willing to help out as long as you go to her. The class is easy but super intensive. She makes the class fun that the 50 minutes runs out before you realize it. There are a lot of tests and quizzes,so it is difficult to fail the class. If you're thinking about taking a class with her, i'll say go for it.

Matsushima-sensei is great. Very kind and helpful and she makes the content easy to learn. Going to class is actually fun and it's a great break in your day from some of your more stressful classes. This was a fairly easy class. Just attend the class and pay attention, you'll do fine.
Best teacher ever. Flexible, helpful, and makes you wonder why American professors should be so strict if a Japanese one is so relaxed.
Super easy class, if you know Japanese beforehand. It's an easy A if you do the homework and show up for class.
She made the class fun and the lectures were interesting. There were some assignments but they were all interesting to do and the group projects were fun.

Chill class. Not many assignments in her class and when you do have something due, she breaks it down to a tee what she wants making it really easy to do well. There's the group podcast project at the end which was fun to do and easy to do well in if you put in the effort. Try to take her if you can, you won't regret it.
took her over the summer but she was the goat; she only had short in class readings, graded lightly but gave good critique, and was chill all around

Very clear on everything needed to do well on any assignment, and was overall a fun class. Definetly one of the best English 2 professors; no horror stories (apart from in the novels we read/watch) that can be found from other classes.
Class was super easy and fun. Anderson is great and super easy to work with and is there to help with anything you need.

Outstanding professor. Took class over the summer so was a bit rushed with only 5 weeks of material, but one assignment was due at end of every week (Friday). Two day extension always available. No final exam but English Department requires reflective ePortfolio. A bit tedious, but plenty of time is given in class to complete. Def recommend.

Took this class over the summer. lectures are chill and there are no quizzes, just writing assignments and group projects. lenient grading and interesting lectures. can also leave class early if u want

Dr. Anderson is nice and laidback. Her lectures are interesting and the assignments she gives are usually pretty fun and low pressure. Her grading is super relaxed too so I'd say it's very easy to be successful in this class.

In my class she claimed Frankenstein was the 'first transracial and transsexual person' so yeh she's a little woke, but who really cares? What matters is the grade you get, and with Anderson you are guaranteed an A. She has like 3 total assignments in the semester each of which won't take more than an hour and lets you scroll tiktok in class.

Dr. Anderson was a wonderful english professor! She makes all grades and due dates very clear and also describes how to complete assignments to get full points. She grades very fairly and also makes her lectures engaging. She's also just a chill person that understands the schedules of students. Would highly recommend her!

we had a form we could submit for any (or all) assignments to get an extra 1-2 days no questions asked. lectures were very enjoyable, full of group discussion, entertaining documentaries, and an aquarium visit. she really cared about our wellbeing and feedback. very upfront about requirements and deliverables.

Incredibly clear grading criteria. We made the rubric in class on the first week of school so we all knew exactly what she expected of us. There is less talking and participation than typical english classes which dries up the lectures a little bit but at least it was easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I can't even fully blame him because the course is designed by the department in this way. Whoever thought thermodynamics is best learned through fill-in-the-blank notes should not be allowed to be designing courses. Professor is often not sure of what he is teaching as he is following someone else's lectures. ChBE should follow MSE and Dr. Speyer.

If possible, do not take him. He uses another professor's notes and it's often clear he isn't sure himself about what he's teaching us. I just couldn't understand how he wanted us to apply concepts we learned in class. Intentionally designs exams so nobody can finish and questions are worded weirdly too. But I can see he's trying.
He used fill in the blank notes that I did not find very helpful. Tests were unreasonably difficult.

HW and exams- Very difficult. Be strategic while answering exam questions. Really generous with grading, gives extra grades. Caring, ready to help always. Good grading criteria and lets you know about your condition (in term of grade) from time-2-time. You will definitely learn some mathematics and MATLAB but will need a lot of dedication.

Certainly cares about students and is very accommodating. Quizzes can be difficult, but extra credit opportunities mean you don't have to get anything less than an A on them. On the other hand, the tests are unnecessarily difficult (extremely time constrained) and are not designed to be finished.

Anant is very accommodating to students and genuinely cares about us. He has been more than considerate of outside circumstances and believes in 'not punishing students for being human.' He is difficult but has been one of the most rewarding classes I have taken.

Sense of humor that might not appeal to everyone. Quizzes are incredibly difficult or incredibly simple, no in between. Tests are super long and require understanding. Homework is paper/pencil and coding questions (6ish hours)but usually not too bad. He's available for office hours a lot and will really help you if you're struggling. Solid choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr Paravastu is a great teacher. He cares about his students well being and wants everyone to succeed. He has all of his notes online and includes sample code that is helpful when doing the homework. He is always available to clear up questions during office hours. The class will kill you, but he will help you come out the other side okay.

Dr. Paravastu cares about his students & wants them to become some of the best engineers, so because of that, his class is challenging. GO TO OFFICE HOURS & reach out if you need help (bc at some point you will prob be confused). After reaching out to Dr. Paravastu, he met with me outside of class and office hours just to make sure I understood

Dr. Paravastu doesn't fit in this class. He doesn't help develop a foundation, provides no relatable links to a student's previous knowledge, assumes the student follows all his disorganized derivations and messily structured notes, and makes his tests far harder than any examples or help provided. A worthless class that is unnecessarily hard.

Dr. Paravastu is very passionate, comes across nice and seems genuinely concerned, but he DOES NOT know how to teach 'Thermo'. He taught the class for the first time, only presenting derivations and concepts. But we are tested entirely on problem solving, with absolutely no practice given. His tests are nonsensical relative to what he teaches.
He doesnt know how to teach. Why do you become a teacher if you dont wanna teach? You have to teach yourself from his notes.

He was a good choice for a class that ended up not being required. I changed my major halfway through, but if you come to class you should get a B without much effort. Do participate in Piazza, it has a much bigger impact on your final grade than he lets you believe.
Good professor, MATLAB skills were questionable at times though. Very nice and really wanted students to succeed. He posts all notes online and the online notes are great.

He uses matlab very differently than 1371, so reference his example code and learn his style and adapt it to yours. He tries to be pretty accessible and cares about his students so put in the work and talk things out with him if you need help because he'll definitely tries hard to help his students.

The main grade for the class is a semester-long project, where you conduct user research and make Figma prototypes. It isn't bad if you have a good team, but it's a lot of writing and busy work. The lectures are honestly super boring and don't cover much to complete the project, so you don't need to pay attention to them.

I'm learning literally nothing in this class, it's the epitome of stupid busy work and wasting your time.
There's so much possible stuff to learn in the field of UI but she manages to avoid all of that useful stuff and find the most boring useless things to cover.

Great UX/UI course. I learned a lot and I found the class very useful since I want to do UX/UI as a career. The entire class is centered around group work however, so CHOOSE YOUR MEMBERS CAREFULLY. There is a lot of work, but they give you lots of time to work on it. Stay organized !!! Attendance done thru turning point/point solutions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class only consisted of attendance, small presentation, and semester long group project. The group project is the biggest part of the class worth 75% so choose your team members wisely. She had fun lectures to listen and learn more about UI/UX. Overall I enjoyed the class.
She's very nice and cares about her students a lot. Take English with her for your sanity, especially if it's your first semester at Georgia Tech.

Professor Shree was my favorite professor by far this semester! She is so passionate, interesting, and understanding. I am by no means a English major but she has a way of engaging you and making you want to contribute in class discussions. HIGHLY recommend her class, it was an amazing experience!
I LOVED prof Shree. She is the chillest prof. If the class needed an assignment pushed back, then it was. The most understanding and fair grader out
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Shree was a phenomenal professor. She cares about course content and genuinely wants students to learn. She sets clear expectations but is flexible. Her classes aren't boring and the assignment structure is good. I looked forward to attending class because of this. She cares about students, allowing extensions and flexibility if needed. 10/10!
A nice professor with a bit accent
Very thick accent and did not make engaging lectures. Horrible experience in linear.

Had an accent which made understanding slightly more difficult, but didn't bother me that much. Very knowledgeable about linear algebra and was helpful. As a new professor, he was pretty good and seems to care about becoming better. If you have problems with him, you could just watch Jankowski's recorded lectures since attendance isn't mandatory.

This course is tough, but Shubin is extremely kind and caring, and he's always open to answer whatever questions you have, even staying late after class ends. I watched Jankowski's lectures for exam review, but I fault this to this being Shubin's first semester, and I definitely think he'll improve bec he is very open to feedback.

Brand new professor, and his teaching style makes that clear. I ended up just watching Jankowski's lectures halfway through the year. He has an accent and tends to teach out of the textbook. However, he was a kind and caring person, and he was genuinely interested in improving as a teacher. I believe in a few years he will be a solid professor.

Shubin has a bit of an accent and doesn't elaborate that much but will any answer question you have no matter how long it takes. He is very smart but not the best lecturer. We fell a little behind towards the end of the semester

Really liked the professor and the class was fine and pretty interesting. Just speak up in class for your participation points. He was very considerate and would extend deadlines. He claims you need the textbook, but I would say it's not worth investing in it as we only discussed it a little bit.
Mannn to the person who said he stinks-- im taking him in the spring bruh pls dont be lying *crying emoji* , he's the only one I can take omg .

his class was easy and not difficult, but talks in circles about stuff that doesn't matter. stupid theme and provides feedback that doesn't apply. he smells and I dont personally like him. wouldn't take again but its whatever.

Hes a really kind proffesor he cares for his students and is really understanding would take again definetly. Just do the work come to class. He cares what he talks about and his class isn't boring he likes to have giant disccussions

The class was overall pretty easy. The professor is nice, but sometimes the class would get really boring. By this I mean that he would talk for a while about basically the same thing. However, overall a nice prof and will extend due date if needed.

Professor Kumar was my ENGL1101 professor for the Fall 2025 semester. He is extremely generous and kind. His course revolves a lot around 5 key projects/essays. These are honestly not hard to do and he makes it so the class is not too much of a time commitment. Would definitely love to be in his class again
Guys he brought us Lindor chocolates and Oreos on the last day of class

Professor Kumar is a very caring & understanding (gives extension whenever you ask). He is an easy grader, & 50% of essay grade is self graded. In class we watched this one movie, so we did not have any books to read. There was never really any homework except for the projects. Projects were 5-10 pages (2x spaced) & you basically choice the topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lectures were really enjoyable especially for a 1 credit class. Great sense of humor, assignments were fine besides the poster and learning portfolio at the end of the semester. Otherwise a very straightforward class.

He closes the clicker questions WAY too fast (basically encouraging student to use ai for quick answer), and he makes fairly simple concepts sound complicated(by shifting off to some theoretical stories). He also lacks enthusiasm in the content of these simple chemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The main benefit to this class is the grade replacement from the final. Wilkinson teaches in an annoying manner, glossing over some key concepts with his popular saying of "you should have already learned this previously." The exams are pretty difficult, and he leaves no time on the iClicker. Overall though, if you put in the work you'll be fine.
Illegible handwriting, like actually. Often lectured about overly detailed things that were irrelevant to exam content. Dr. Evans >>>>, it was nice when he came in to sub a handful of times.

Lectures aren't that helpful because he spends a lot of time off topic or talking about applications of chemicals and things we don't need to know. The class has graded in-class questions and he gives very little time to do them before closing them. Chill guy I guess but maybe more suited for upper level classes.

he's fine, his grading can be randomly kind of tough but nothing crazy. the final assignment for this course is annoyingly time consuming and pointless but everything else was fine. chill dude. cool accent.
A simple course with simple assignments not graded too hard. A checkbox kinda course.

Required for chem major. He did not seem to care. Often took months to get grades back. Teaches on subjects he does not know enough about. You can learn more about these tools from a 10 minute YouTube than this 50 minute class. Guest lectures were actually helpful. Big poster and paper due at the end that he will take points off without feedback.

Dr. Wilkinson is a great professor! He really cares about the course and all his students. I found his lectures to be interesting and worthwhile, plus he is super helpful and wants his students to succeed. Would definitely recommend him for CHEM 3111 or any other course.
CHEM1212K is difficult, but not impossible. Make sure to attend lectures, lab, and do the homework and textbook reading. Exams are difficult but you can make up for bad grades later on.

Prof Wilkinson was a very good professor. If you paid attention in the lectures and did the homework, you did well in the exam. You definitely need to study, it's not an easy course, but he made the classes enjoyable. He also offered a lot of opportunities to improve your grade, such as the grade replacement policy.
A kind soul with a handsome British accent. He was sometimes a little blunt but he made the class super easy. A charming fella. PRO TIP: call him Angus Beef and he will chuckle!

Dr. Wilkinson is an excellent professor, especially if Chemistry is a novel topic to you. He is always willing to answer all questions or re-explain past concepts. His use of post-lecture quizzes allows for students to easily avoid falling behind on the subject. His exams are fair and the best way to study is to understand problem sets thoroughly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: He gave a ton of room for error so missing a homework assignment (or several) was never a big deal. Tests are very fair and won't try to trick you. He is also very knowledgeable about chemistry and the impact it has on the world. He relates everything you learn to the real world and tells you exactly why it matters.

Dr. Wilkinson makes it clear that he cares about the success of his students. He's very personable & approachable, and is always happy to entertain questions during lecture. While sometimes he can get off on tangents or move a bit slow, his lectures are enjoyable. He knows the material, and his tests are 1000% fair. He's a really great professor!

Pretty nice. Each week (or two weeks) there is a chemical skill for students to learn (sometimes with different professors), so you will gain a lot. There are assignments associated with each week's skill, and a poster & a portfolio at the end of the semester, but as long as you follow instructions and turn them in on time, it's an easy A.

He's a nice dude but my semester he was gone a lot & the lady teacher pretty much took over. She made the tests and he didn't seem to know exactly what would be on them. Good guy though and I would definately take him over Schermeier- but maybe go to her class the day before tests bc she always would give them more info about what would be on tests
He's a cool dude. Pay attention and put in some work you'll be fine. He's really friendly  but never opens his eyes
He is very good at explaining chemistry concepts, but gets a little bit off topic sometimes. If you enjoy chemistry,  he is a great professor for it.

His lectures are very interesting if you are into chemistry, as he extrapolates and talks to other related things in the field every now and then. However, he doesn't spend much time on basic examples/concepts, so unless you're pretty decent at Chemistry/did AP,  you'll find him a bit hard. Very kind person though.

Maybe the best professor I have had here at Georgia Tech. My favorite part of his class was after taking a survey about his class, he took our feedback and decided to not listen to any of it. I love this teacher and he is definitely head and shoulders above the other teacher.

Love his British accent, it's awesome. He's an alright guy and lecturer, but he tends to be a bit tangential. He also did not have many office hours, and all the ones he had were during hours that I had class. Pretty average professor, would recommend Shepler more.

The lectures were good, though he tended to go off topic at times. If you can, try to get Shepler for this class; both Wilkinson and Shepler are good professors, but Shepler explained certain topics much better.

I liked Dr. Wilkinson.  He has a funny British accent that makes some of the chemistry language used interesting.  He initially explains topics well, but I think he is sometimes too smart for himself and gets caught up in his own ideas when he has to explain things in more detail.  He is still very nice and the lectures are usually helpful.

Dr. Wilkinson is great! He clearly knows chemistry very well and endeavors to answer students' questions. Answers can get confusing, so I recommend Piazza or e-mails for straightforward answers. Overall, he's a good professor that really does care. His lectures can be on the dry side, but he covers the necessary material.

He closes his eyes while lecturing and does not lecture very clearly. He seems like a nice professor; he just cannot communicate well with his students during lecture. He is very knowledgeable, but it's difficult to understand. Exams are 20 multiple choice questions. Overall, he's a decent professor.
He speaks to a higher level that someone who has never taken college chemistry before will struggle with.... alot...

Very nice professor. He knows what he is talking about, but can't really explain the material on a level students can understand. Reading the textbook and doing lots of practice problems will help in the class. Overall he is an ok chem 1211 professor.
The practice tests were very similar to the actual tests. Lectures kinda boring but powerpoint slides were helpful. Overall, pretty easy and nice professor.

If you pay attention in class and study the past exams, this class should be a breeze. If not, it's not the professor, it's that you probably should not major in anything related to chemistry... Good but somewhat boring lecturer. Never needed help, so not sure how he is in person.

This professor knew his material, but the tests were completely unfair. He used only multiple choice tests that included some of the most random bits of information. There was no room for error, even if you had a good argument. Free response questions would have been helpful. This was my first upsetting grade ever!

Pretty nice, always willing to help during office hours. His lectures are a little boring, but oh well. Tests are exactly like the practice tests--so moderate studying should give you a pretty quick A.
Horrible, horrible teacher. Very condescending. I ended up with an 79.3 after the final and he refused to bump me up even though I always went to his office hours and never missed a lecture.
He is always willing to help. You can always stop by office hours or ask him questions after class. His lecture slides help study for the course and the practice exams are a good guide for the exams.

Extremely nice professor, very helpful. Lectures are pretty boring, but if you can manage to stay focused, you'll learn a lot. Also, holds review sessions for each test, which are excellent, he really takes the time to explain everything asked. Hard tests, but I'd definitely recommend him, especially if you actually have an interest in the class.

Dr. Wilkinson is a very through lecturer, if a bit boring.  He has his moments where he captured the class during demos and slips of the tounge, but for the most part it was difficult to stay awake at 9am.  Very hard tests, harsh grader.

She is an excellent professor willing to be flexible on deadlines, and she gives well-constructed feedback to make students stronger writers. Outside of class, Dr. Fried is also very accessible. I couldn't recommend her enough if you have the opportunity to be a part of the class.

Dr. Fried is an awesome professor. She understands students are preoccupied with major specific classes and is flexible with deadlines as long as a student shows commitment in class and in other assignments.

Great professor, she actually cares that you understand the material and doesn't assign too much readings. Lectures could be a lot sometimes and the work can pile up fast if you aren't paying attention, not a free A but definitely achievable if you put in a bit of effort.

Overall, I would say Prof. Fried made lectures enjoyable and offered a lot of support for students even as a first-time professor at GT. I would pay close attention to the topic you want for ENGL1101 before choosing, but -- if you don't mind learning about the Victorians -- I would absolutely recommend taking Dr. Fried!!

Dr. Fried made English, a subject which I dreaded in high school, much more enjoyable. Empathized with students and focused on useful learning outcomes, rather than assigning endless amounts of readings. She is quite flexible with due dates, and gives plenty of chances for re-submissions on assignments.
Good enough teacher but do not take her if you want an easy A on the class

Overall structure of the class is super disorganized. His grading rubric wasn't clear the whole semester. Quiz almost every Tuesday and some Thursdays, pretty hard to study for them since all he says is "any previous work we've done is fair game." Practice exams are not helpful 85% of the time.
I did not enjoy this class. Lots of hard material, lectures are confusing. Prof does not explain concepts well. TA saved me. Thankfully, plenty of extra credit opportunities to get a better grade.

This is by far the hardest professor I have ever taken. Lectures consist of 50 slide powerpoints filled with words. Nothing is explained clearly. The lectures and the tests feel like completely separate courses. This is likely a weed-out class. This class tanked both my GPA and mental health. Made me question if I wanted to be in college.

Prof yaps a lot during lectures, lectures are quite disorganized and heavy with information that isn't explained thoroughly. Exams are very difficult and have questions that we have never seen examples of before. A redeeming factor is that he gives quite a bit of extra credit.

This is a joke. The professor and the TA just don't give s about it. I get it. As the chair, you'll be busy with who know. But if you can't afford time that you have to constantly cancel lectures 30 minutes before the class and give only four homeworks, you should've handed it to another one. What is the purpose of edDiscussion when nobody answers?
Very good professor.
Taught 2035 along with Prof Bhattacharya. He's very sweet and always checks in with us before lecture started. He explains things very well.

He reads slides word by word and assumes the students know everything already. I felt like he is always rushing and doesnt seem to care to actually explain the underlying concepts. He also misses lectures every other week!
Amazing lecturer and really cares about his students. Assignments for the class didnt make sense but he isnt the coordinator. Great professor, definitely someone Id want to take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr Raychowdhury is extremely knowledgeable and a super instructor. He knows exactly where students will have difficulty understanding and makes concepts clear. I wish he traveled less, would love to take more courses with him.
Amazing professor. He really cares for his students and is an amazing lecturer. The only downside is that he misses classes a lot but the experience overall is great.
Amazing Lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Raychowdhury is an amazing lecturer and extremely knowledgeable. He provided lots of practical examples from 70s, 80s, 90, and the present times. He seems to know both the state of the art as well as the history of computing. It was an amazing learning experience. Just wish he were around more often.

He misses class and is late to class, A LOT! However, that is not to say that he is a bad professor. When he actually makes it to class he is awesome. He is great at explaining concepts and seems to truly care that the students learn. He does a great job of moving from concept to concept and provides a nice overview of where we are in the course.
Awesome professor. Excellent in explaining material. Hope he teaches more ECE classes in senior years.
A good lecturer and teacher, Dr. Raychowdhury knows the material and makes sure you do as well. Homeworks often were very difficult but were relevant to the material.

Prof Raychowdhury is a great teacher and great at explaining the course material. He convered a lot of material but always took the time to explain the concepts slowly. He also found ways to make the whole course interesting throughout the semester.

Professor Raychowdhury was an excellent lecturer. He sometimes went fast but did explain new concepts with ease and clarity. However, his course organization was frankly awful and his lack of accessibility outside class was terrible too (traveled almost every week and did not hold regular office hours). Also, the grading criteria was unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher. He has taught some of the most difficult topics with such ease and coherence! I learnt so much in the class, yet never felt overburdened. He wants the students to succeed.

He explains things really well and also shows a lot of care for students. Class was curved quite a lot and he would constantly let the class know where the cutoffs were after each test. Although all his material is posted online, still highly recommend both going to class and reading his online notes, as they supplement each other quite well.

Would definitely recommend her for 2110, MUCH easier than taking it in ATL. She makes the class very fair with assignments, quizzes, and TLs. Reads off the slides from ATL, but you can tell that she knows what she's talking about. Slight language barrier that makes understanding hard sometimes, but overall a very solid prof who I would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Prior review was lazy & biased, didn't make it through the entire class. Extremely fair teacher & decent lecturer for her first time teaching the course. Could tell she was very knowledgeable, but language barrier hurt a bit. HW heavy, but a very very fair course compared to taking in Atlanta. Would highly recommend and I enjoyed. Also had for 2110

I was excited for CS3600, but quickly grew frustrated. The prof has no clear curriculum, comes unprepared, and answers Qs with “I don't know.” She skips key slides, gives unclear homework, and fails to relate content to AI. So far, we've done 8 graph search algorithms—none AI-related. A class w/ much potential became one I care about the least.

Fluid Mechanics is a difficult class, but Dr. Glezer's lectures are helpful and include plenty of relevant examples. The 45 min exams are stressful, but not overly complex. Grading scheme is extremely friendly, allowing you to drop the two lowest test scores (can exempt final). Homework solutions are posted with the assignment. Would recommend.

Handwriting was actually atrocious, we spend most of each class asking him what things say. His tests have too short of a time limit just so he can spend 10 minutes lecturing after we finish the test, you could go into the test feeling good and walk out confused if you even know the subject, Better than some professors friends had so ig worth it

Despite Dr. Glezer's incredibly stressful 30-minute exams, you can't help but like him thanks to his clear and interactive lectures, and great sense of humor. His fluids course is far from easy, but you will definitely learn and enjoy it.

really fast lecturer, but lectures are well organized and lots of content covered every lecture. he has horrible handwriting though so be prepared for 5 minutes of every class dedicated to questions of what a word on the screen is. exams are difficult, but similar enough to hw. doing hw and studying lecture examples is key to the class

He is a fast, smart teacher but he knows his stuff. He is kind of mean towards students, but his lectures are structured pretty well. His tests are tough, and are one prob worth 70 points and T/F. I would not have passed this class without the TA who is leaving after this year. Take with caution but his class is manageable if you put in the work.

Fluid Mechanics is a tough class. Dr. Glezers lecures are at times very helpful and interesting, but other times are very hard to follow. 2 Exams and a Finals make up the vast majority of the class grade which can be tough. Pop quizzes are not too hard. Homework can only hurt your grade.

Dr. Glezer is very knowledgeable professor and a good lecturer. However, his grading system is based only on 6 quizzes which are 20 minutes. The quizzes are often tricky and difficult to complete in the allotted time. He also assigns homework that can only hurt your grade. Aside from that, he is one of the better fluids professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Fluids is one of the toughest classes at Tech. Dr. Glezer teaches fluids every fall, and he is good lecturer. He has a great understanding of fluid mechanics as it is the primary focus of his research. He can assume that students know more about fluids before taking this class. He can also be condescending about not getting concepts immediately.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Glezer is one of the best professors I have had at Tech. Let me be clear: Fluids is HARD. Plain and simple. Dr. Glezer focuses his teaching on the concepts behind fluid mechanics, which makes his class difficult. But he is extremely clear in his lectures on what will be tested.

Lectures were a bit slow, but easy to follow from the slides alone. Great introduction to the finer points of C++. Programming assignments were excellent coding practice. Exams were quite challenging, with some niche questions on C++ syntax, but they were satisfyingly comprehensive and curved reasonably. Extremely understanding prof. No busywork.

Earned 95% without doing the extra credit project. Assignments taught me a lot about C++ and databases. Thought tests could be tricky due to potpourri style questions that could be on anything from lectures, but that was alleviated due to a generous curve. Participation was Point Solutions, but that was also curved. Overall, he's a nice professor

This class was great, Prof Joy gives a lot of real world applications and teaches all aspects of designing a complex database system. He is very kind and prioritize learning above grades or anything else. Lots of extra credit opportunities were given. I learnt a lot of C++ and systems fundamentals which were useful as I was new to it. Great course

This class was difficult and test-heavy. However, lots of extra credit was given out for an extra project. Teaching was not amazing but we did learn the concepts in class. Simply put, this class is an A if you put time in on the EC project and show up to every lecture, there was a curve too. The professor was also caring and occasionally funny.

Loved the classes, excellent teacher. Programming-heavy course, which was educationally useful IMO. Also teaches a bunch of useful systems fundamentals and advanced C++, very helpful. Only caveat is that grading is exam-heavy, though the prof provides multiple extra credit opportunities and generously curves grades.

Enthusiastic lecturer, showed lots of interest in lecture topics. Point Solutions quizzes in-class that are curved at the end (can skip quite a few lectures if needed). Very C++ heavy class. Homework was both very time-consuming and difficult if you are not experienced with C++ debugging. Exams are long, but have a decent curve.

He is a knowledgeable & excellent professor in database systems, but his teaching style could improve. No lecture recordings and a presentation heavy approach without practical demonstrations made it difficult to fully grasp concepts tbh. Exams were lengthy & allowing more time would be very helpful. I had high expectations but sadly disappointed.

The core content for this class is very interesting and is taught well, but it is formatted very poorly. Half of your grade comes from two written tests which contain numerous questions on irrelevant C++ trivia
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Systems classes at GT tend to be generally good, this is no exception. While sometimes it definitely felt more like a C++ class that happened to have databases than the other way around, I learned a lot and he's a good professor (kind, fair, intelligent).

Very weird class as all the time was spent on implementation details specific to C++ instead of the more broad concepts transcending language, which goes against the computer science teaching philosophy I have seen. If you want to specialize in C systems programming then it is a good class, otherwise I would just take 4400 and move on.
Really kind professor and worked with you if you went to his office hours or brought up any concerns via private posts. He was very kind and the class was very interesting
He's a caring professor, assignments could be challenging if you don't have a lot of experience with cpp. Highly suggest attending his lectures and office hours. Overall a great guy.

The lectures are very interesting cover a diverse range of ideas. I especially like how he not only discussed foundational things but also what's up and coming in the field. Plus learning more about intricacies of CPP was definitely a very good addition.
Clear lecture. Exam heavy but reasonable and does curve if the class doesn't perform well. Homework are ok if you have background in C++. I would recommend taking this prof's course.

Professor Joy Arulraj motivates students to understand internals of database and his lectures also involve the latest trends taking place in the database world. Take this class if you want to understand how databases work internally. i.e how the index is built, how caching operates in on-disk database etc.
good lectures and he teaches actual code in the lecture powerpoints, but the assignments are generated using chat gpt and often don't make sense.

Lectures are engaging, and the professor appreciates questions and participation. Not getting an A is extremely difficult, due to extra credit opportunities and low grade cutoff.
Assignments require considerable time commitment, but are a great source of learning.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Clear lectures and assignments.
Joy genuinely cares about teaching, and incorporates feedback. The course is challenging but the professor tries to help out the best he can.

He is a nice guy, yet, the class is challenging, and the HWs are long and hard and require tons of clarification on Piazza. He gives an extension on every assignment, however. On top, you get a term group project and hard exams, so you will be spending tons of your time on this class. The lectures are long and tedious. If you can skip it-- do it.
Bad lectures, difficult homework, wouldn't recommand

Joy is very very lenient on grading. I feel he tries so hard to make all students get an A. We have a pretty small size of class, so Joy knows everyone. The syllabus is well-designed: we have labs/homeworks/exams/participation/extra credits.
Very lenient in grading. Assignments are complex, and a lot to learn but the good part is you can do that in groups.

Very difficult course - no clear structure to the syllabus. Too many slides in one presentation and felt like he kept droning on and on. Hasn't structured syllabus for undergrad + grad mix of students - instead looks like only Ph.D. level course. Very partial to certain favorite students. Was disappointed and had to withdraw from the course.

If you're a Challenge student, beware. She acts superior, overexplains yes/no questions, and loves to use the “threes” like “I came, I saw, I conquered” plus her favorite phrase, “By design.” Midterm questions are confusing, so the study guide is useless. Her TAs don't give feedback around her. One of the worst classes I've had.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: In a world of 1s, be a 5, not me tho
I'm sorry for her
She's so mean 😪

A concerning number of questions on her assessments do not have an objectively correct answer; they are based on her own personal beliefs. Her directions, like others have said, are poorly worded and confusing. Her grading process is also unfair and it is difficult to discern exactly what she wants from you. Do not recommend.

Major superiority complex! She grades her students based off of whether or not they agree with her on everything. She tries to push her beliefs on everyone. Whatever you do, do not disagree with her, tell her she's wrong, or speak your mind. All her class is, is an hour and a half long rant of her beliefs and how she's above everyone else.

She thinks that she is some sort of prophet and will berate you if you do not exactly agree with what she does. Her exams are poorly worded and have objective answers with zero curve (nobody got an A) and she marks you absent even if you are in class if you don't do EXACTLY what she says as soon as she says it. Do NOT take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cocky, unfair and seems like someone trying to pretend to be intelligent/deep.
Intentionally marked absent even though I was present in class. So why should I come to class in the first place just to be marked absent?
Marked me absent even though I was present just because we were told to count the number of students in the lecture and she thought I didn't count.
This lady marked me absent for sitting in the back

I thought this class would be an interesting class to take for my first semester here at Tech. I hated this class by the second week. Her tests are so confusing. Most of the questions on her tests are horribly worded. I feel like I haven't learned anything. It also feels like that if you don't believe what she does and agree with her, you're wrong.
A very biased teacher in regards to to her opinions. Don't ask her a question or for clarification, she wont give it and will make you fell stupid in the process.

The professor is so obviously biased towards socialism that she forced us to write our final exam essays from that perspective. She cited non-peer reviewed research as fact in her lectures, which barely made sense to begin with. She was extremely argumentative and was a poor facilitator of class discussion. Does not round up decimal grades at all.
I thought she was nice, the tests are just hard to prepare for since her questions are random and strangely worded. She curves alright.
Class should be called race & racism, not sociology. Lectures and tests are written poorly, long-winded and very unclear.

Incredibly CARING and KNOWLEDGEABLE professor who has a knack for recontextualizing difficult mathematical concepts into intuitive lessons. She took the time to know all of the students in her lecture hall by name and regularly checked in with her students to make sure they were prepared. Easy to talk to!

Math 1552 was hard, but with Christina, she made it easier. She really cares about her students, she learned every single person's name in the big lecture class and made sure to check in with them to see how the class was going. The class itself is hard, and she tends to go very fast, but I would definitely recommend and would take again with her.
Pretty mid. I ended up going to Grodzinsky's lectures. She cares about students but she goes super fast and can be unclear.

Awesome professor that truly cares for each student. Was always early in class to talk to individual students, learn names, and chat. SUPER accessible outside of class. Great lectures with sufficient practice and test-application based problems. Tests are usually on the tougher side (especially multiple choice), but the optional final helps a lot.

Professor Anathasouli is amazing! Although Math 1552 is hard as a Tech class, she did an amazing job. She is always super prepared when she comes to class with slides, and she posts practice problems too. She genuinely wants her students to succeed and learned everyone's names and met them outside of class/office hours if they needed help.

She goes out of her way to remember every students' names and puts lots of effort into her lectures. I never attended since it was my 8am, but I used the online notes. I would still recommend attending. There are many ways to improve your grade and maintain an A, lots of extra study material and opportunities provided.
She is an amazing professor and has great powerpoint slides for class. She really cares about her students and is always available if you need help.
She is amazing, so caring, and learns all the names of her students. She explains concepts so well. I was not registered for her section but went to all her lectures.
Great professor and makes things very easy to understand. Participation was not necessary. The course is difficult (especially taylor series), but she made it bareable.

Calculus 2 (MATH 1552) is a hard class within itself. She was the best lecturer, and she had a TA named Yosia. She informed us she will not teach Calc 2 next semester. However I highly advise you to find Yosia and go to his recitations. Christina is very nice, and will work with you. Take her if you can, she is young and caring, makes math easy.
One of the best math teachers I have ever had. She is super caring and explains the material well. The tests are difficult, but these are standardized across all calculus classes.
Overall she was a good professor and very caring, her pacing during class was just off sometimes but she posts her notes on canvas so not a huge issue.

probably the best professor I've had at Tech so far. She explained the concepts very well and made integral calc so easy to understand. make sure to attend studio though to get a lot of practice problems to prep for tests and quizzes

No homework or textbook assigned. Lectures were absolutely phenomenal. Studios were required instead of HW by giving participation points (20% of grade). Tests were very reasonable and weekly quizzes were similar to material covered in studio. Professor was extremely accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class
