I took this class in Spring 2024. Babcock is passionate about the subject she is teaching, but I think she expects all of her students to be as well. There are group assignments that you will do in breakout rooms on Zoom. Overall, the course was pretty easy. Babcock was an effective prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: SUCH an easy class. participation counts towards your grade and is measured by random in-class assignments. dr. babcock is the sweetest and genuinely wants to engage us in class. outside of class, spent maybe 1 hour a week on assignments/studying for exams. no final, just a non-cumulative third exam. highly recommend!!

Dr. Babcock was an amazing teacher! I took the class as a late summer class, and it wasn't crazy. You can look at previous PPs, write stuff down in her study guide and study that. Not much need for textbook. She gives out SO much EC and she is very caring. There are EC assignments, EC on exams, and EC on CIOS. An "A" is most likely. Learned a lot!
Lectures are kind of boring, and homeworks are kind of tedious. Make sure you're turning in all of your assignments, so you don't end up with a grade like mine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very nice professor who clearly cares about her job and making students excited and want to learn. Class was kind of boring, and the content felt somewhat common sense, so given that it was an online class, I found myself getting distracted and not paying attention. Overall a pretty easy class with straightforward exams, and a good opener to psych.
Dr. Babcock is very supportive and replies to emails on time. The exams are a bit hard for me but mainly you have to memorize a lot of stuff from the slides.
AMAZING!! truly one of the best professors at GT. Love her teaching style and her energy. Could not recommend enough, always great feedback and available outside of class

Babcock is a solid prof. Her course is very well structured and lectures are well-done (but not the most engaging). I wish this class was not virtual, I think that would have helped. The group paper was not too bad, but can really suck if you have bad teammates.

psych research class - helpful because it frames statistical procedures through the lens of psyc experiments but psych is BS anyway. mandatory lecture :( reading the textbook is enough to get a 100. I had a sense she didn't deeply understand the math behind it (which doesn't matter anyway). Great slides, articulate lady, very accessible through OH

Dr. Babcock is such a kind, motivating professor. She truly wants to see you succeed. Meet online synchronous 2x a week, excellent PowerPoints, clear expectations on assignments, & even sends out reminders. Very quick to respond to emails and regularly stays after class to answer questions. Love her and how she teaches, wonderful professor & person

Excellent class and a genuinely fantastic professor that ignited my interest in the subject. Very interesting lectures that structures stuff in a digestible way, really fun weekly HWs, and tests were example specific and quite chill. Legit just did this class for Ethics req and I wanna do more Psych now.

She is a true angel! Her lectures are so fun to watch and listen to. She makes the exams exactly to her lectures. All of the assignments are pretty straightforward and she gives out extra credit. Always online to answer any questions, I would love to take her again if I could.

Superb class headed by fantastic lectures, PPTs were really well made, and both tests and homeworks were formatted in a really fun way -- stuff like situations/stories that questions were made out of. Definitely recommend, as a STEM student doing psych for just reqs, this actually built my interest significantly.

If you are trying to take Psych 1101, take it with Professor Babcock. She is an amazing professor who really wants the best for her students. Her classes aren't mandatory, but there are about 5 pop quizzes that you need to be on Zoom for. Assignments are not time-consuming and really do help prepare for tests. Easy A class
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Babcock was a great professor for PSYC 1101! Had her synchronous online class, would meet 2x a week, good powerpoints and cared about her topics clearly. Tests were reasonable, not super easy but not too difficult if you studied. A few homeworks and also a 4 SONA credit requirement which you can do through research studies or article critiques.
Dr. Babcock is an unfathomably powerful professor, easily in the top three classes I've taken at Tech, despite my aversion to Psychology, reading, and science in general.

Dr. Babcock is one of the best lecturers I have ever had. She presents the material clearly, providing numerous examples (both practical and research-oriented) to supplement her teaching. She is also very kind and cares about the success of her students inside and outside of the classroom. I wouldn't hesitate to take her again for another class!

Dr. Babcock is incredibly caring and obviously wants the best for her students. The reason I rated her a 4 and not a 5 is just because her lectures are not overly interesting, and I was kind of bored by being lectured at for an hour. I would have appreciated more in class activities to be included so the students were more involved.

Dr. Babcock is the epitome of an amazing educator. Her lectures are insightful, her assignments are relevant, her tests are a good measure of understanding, and her expectations are clear. She takes suggestions seriously and her knowledge is outstanding. I had to do extra credit for my A, but she makes succeeding and understanding psych enjoyable.

Hands down the best prof I've encountered! She makes the lectures understandable despite the info-heavy paragraphs the textbook gives, and always takes her time to answer questions people. She is super caring and understanding, and makes you feel excited about social psych, Her passion for the subject is contagious! 
TAKE HER!

If I was going to be a professor, I'd want to be her. Dr. Babcock makes an effort to get to know every student and covers the topics very thoroughly, and she's good at relating each topic to the lives of students (though it's easy to do that for social psychology). The assignments and tests are straightforward but not extremely easy.

I read the textbook maybe once all semester. Showed up to lectures, took notes, raised my hand every now and then, and learned a good deal about Social Psychology without much pain. Highly recommend. Also, Dr. Babcock takes the time to learn everyone's name, which is truly remarkable with the number of students she lectures.

Honestly one of the best professors at Tech. I'm not a psych major, but I consider her classes to be one of the most engaging and impressive classes at tech! She is very organized, explains materials in a clear and easy-to-understand way. Took her for Research Methods and Social Psych - there is no reason not to take her class!!

Dr. Babcock is a great, caring person. She genuinely wants you to succeed and sets up the class that way. The class itself is not difficult, but the lab is pretty time consuming. Overall, Dr. Babcock is a gem of a professor who truly cares.

Took this class online, and Dr. Babcock has engaging lectures and is very caring. She always answers your questions and even takes the time to research your question if she doesn't have the answer. While the lectures are not mandatory, I highly suggest that you attend, because then the exams are really easy and you won't need to read the book.
I love Dr. Babcock! Her lectures are very engaging, and she is the sweetest person ever. I wish she could teach all my psychology classes.

Dr. Babcock is a really good lecturer and she really cares about her students; it's fully online now and tests are open-note, which makes them easy if you understand the material. For lab you have a group research paper, and if you get a bad group you will hate your life so definitely choose people who will produce good work
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Babcock is amazing! Although Research Methods can be pretty dry material, she did a great job of making the learning process as engaging as possible. She is knowledgeable about psychology content, she clearly prepares a lot for lectures, and she is approachable outside of class. I appreciate such a thoughtful, hard-working, & caring prof.

Dr. Babcock has a very sweet, charismatic, and open personality. I took her for both Research Methods and Social Psych and she always put a smile on my face. Any class taken with her does not feel like a burden although with Research Methods, you do have to create your own group research design project.

Dr. Babcock is great! I would highly recommend taking her courses. She is organized, has great communication skills, and is the kind of professor that learns the names of everyone in a giant lecture hall. Her course was easy to navigate due to her clear expectations.

This class was a lot of work. I felt like every week was mostly working on the final project. Dr. Babcock, however, made it all a good experience. Her tests are pretty strait forward and her study guides and lectures help you study for that. Her lectures are some of the most engaging at Tech. You'll be in good hands if you have her as a professor

Dr. Babcock is one of my favorite professors I have had! She is so sweet & caring and presents material so clearly. She is so intelligent and passionate about what she teaches. The lab for this class can be a lot of work, but as long as you stay on top of it you'll be fine. Definitely recommend taking her!

I LOVE Dr. Babcock! She is hands down my favorite teacher I have ever had. Her lectures are amazing, and she puts so much effort into helping her students and keeping them involved and entertained during discussions. I've gone to her for career advice and she is the sweetest person ever! 10/10 recommend her all the way.

Had her for social psych, and I had a really rough semester with other classes so I wasnt doing too hot in her class, so I went to office hours. She gave me so many tips, and I saw instant improvement. She really cares about making the info accessible, and shes an incredible lecturer. She makes it super clear what it takes to succeed.

Meghan is such a sweet woman who really cares about making sure all of her students succeed. She gives every opportunity for students to do well. Exams are not too hard but not too easy. If you study the day before its more than enough to get a B, but getting an A is harder. Also, she is hot as heck so lecture is more enjoyable.

Dr. Babcock is an incredible lecturer, probably the best I have had during my academic career. She presents material clearly and in a way that college students find fun and engaging. Homework is reasonable length and interesting. TIP: Her online study materials are superb, but don't miss lecture if you want an A! Her lectures are awesome anyway!

Professor Babcock gives engaging and interesting lectures that are easy to recall when taking the tests. She gives specific examples and good triggers to remember information. I attend class and just listen, don't take notes, and get high As on the tests. The material isn't easy, but Professor Babcock makes it interesting.

Really friendly and engaging. She provides very comprehensive expectations for what it will take to succeed in her course. Lectures follow the textbook pretty closely (which was tedious if you had already read the textbook, but now I just do the readings afterward to supplement lecture). Would definitely recommend.
If you don't get a good TA, good luck. Horrendously run class with zero room for error.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You won't see this dude, quizzes depend on your TA. Go to class, read the manual beforehand. It's an annoying class but the TA's are helpful. You probably won't learn much from the labs but the circuits can be cool. Lab exam is fine, you'll get a study guide the week before. Just learn the book properly and YouTube the theory and you'll be fine.
Absolutely amazing would take again
The GOAT, absolutely amazing professor

He hadn't taught the class in several years, so maybe this will be a little biased, but the exams were really hard (until the final, when he deliberately made it easier). Everyone above an 89% got an A in the class. The homeworks also took a long time--they weren't graded for accuracy, but I still wanted to try and get them correct.
do not take during study abroad, he was unreasonably hard and his exams were ruthless. Most Ive ever studdied for a class and still did terrible.

This class is like ECE 3043 but improved. That being said it is still a difficult class that takes a lot of time but you learn a lot more and get a lot more out of it. There were 3 tests which were fair, a final project, and a handful of labs which all took longer than the dedicated lab time. However, Dr. Beck was very supportive throughout.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Beck genuinely cares about his students learning the material and is good at explaining it. The course material is difficult and homework is ungraded but essential to learning. 30% each for exams 1 and 2 and 40% for the final exam. He curved the letter grade cutoffs generously. He's very patient and good at answering questions in office hours.

Tough content but Beck makes his lectures extremely clear and there is no busy work / ability to get by without actually understanding the content.  40% final and 60% over 2 midterms that are closed note but make you really know what's going on.  Overall, cool professor for a tough course. Would recommend if you want to focus on learning/problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lab quizzes will make or break your grade in this class, curve or not. Grades average out to a 3.3 GPA for your section, but that will be mostly dependent on the quizzes, which is dependent on who you have as a TA. Thien was a great TA btw, if he has a section again try to get in with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is probably the least organized at Tech. Dr. Beck himself doesn't show up to lectures as the class is run by two TAs with each section being completely different than the others. On top of that the class is only graded on 10 labs, 10 quizzes, and an all encompassing final. Overall, zero consistency from class to class makes it an avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ECE 3741 has to be one of the most unorganized courses I have seen at this school. Beck, yeah he's a decent teacher but for him to allow the class to be structured so terribly is a bad reflection. Basically do labs where you learn minimal until they decide 1 week before the lab exam to give you solid material to study. Advice, take over the summer.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: TA dependent, but here is my advice: I spent 1.5hrs to study before each lab quiz, writing down important info/eqns/diagrams into a notebook before + after each quiz. When the final rolled around, I had a nice study guide that covered the key info from each lab. Get to know your TAs, and don't be afraid to ask for help.

Dr. Beck is very caring and helpful. The only issue is the class itself sucks. The labs are do-able but the weekly quizzes, everyone bombed. This is because student shave to teach themselves course material out of a lab manual. Why do I pay 50k for that when Dr. Beck is a talented an knowledgeable instructor. The course needs to be re-designed.

Doable to get "A". Prof has 0 presence in labs (TAs). Get a good lab partner, review prior & next lab for weekly quiz & you're solid. Prof is EXTREMELY understanding. I was horribly sick the week of the final & he postponed it twice for me when I still hadn't recovered. VERY understanding, approachable (via email) person. Lot of respect for him.

Grades on a curve, once giving out a quiz comprised of problems that had never been covered because the average was too high. Get a good TA and you'll do fine, but with a poor TA labs will drag on and you'll get lost in the quizzes and eventual final.

All the stuff you love and none of the stuff you hate about 3043. No checkoffs or lab quizzes. Really good lectures. Adjusts lab time based on difficulty. Tests can still be a little rough grade-wise but prof is an amazing teacher.

Dr. Beck was my recitation professor for ECE2026. He was absolutely essential in understanding that class and made one of the harder classes at Georgia Tech an absolute breeze. He was clear, concise, and thorough in his recitation.

ECE2020 is a disaster. There is no recitation, no textbook, no good TAs, and no explanation apart from the one provided by the professor. Sadly, Beck wouldn't even post his lecture notes online, so it was tough to copy all the circuit diagrams and understand what was going on. Also, his office is not even in the GT campus.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Beck was a very clear teacher. He gave relevant class examples and his notes were very thorough. His tests were similar to a combination of notes and homework. He was a really interesting guy who was always willing to talk. I would absolutely recommend him for ECE2020

Dr.Bhamla is very sweet and accessible outside of the class. The class is heavily about fluid mechanics, so be prepared for long and complicated math problems. Dr.Bhamla cares about his student and goes above and beyond to help. The material is difficult, so make sure you spend enough time to learn.

Professor Bhamla is the perfect example of a passionate, curious, and enthusiastic scientist. He engages the class in a way that unparalleled by any other professor I've taken a lecture from. Prof Bhamla constantly encourages audience participation and peer learning, and integrates fascinating videos showing the applications of Transport Phenomena.

I get the vibe that he doesn't actually know much thermo conceptually. He's not bad at teaching per se, though he doesn't give much explanation. Terrible at answering questions, but he does try. He likes the practical aspect more than the equations so he shows videos in class that are quite cool. Overall, 7/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Thermo is concept heavy, but Dr. Bhamla's biggest strength is explaining concepts. However, he doesn't have time in class to work out many numerical problems. 2130 deserves to be 3 credit hrs. Recitation/TA office hrs are key for understanding those. He expects you to be a good critical thinker. His homeworks are tough, but his exams are fair.
Doesn't understand much Thermo and classes are a mess.

PHYS 2231 (Honors Physics I) He's a super nice guy, not a super nice professor. I ended the class with a 79.4 and didn't get rounded up, but he rounded up another girl's 76 to a B. Tests were weighted pretty heavily and they were extremely difficult. Averages would be failing and he would say "I don't see any means for a curve"

Behrens is such a great professor and person. Took Phys2231 with him, and while it was an incredibly challenging class he worked hard to make sure every one of us succeeded. Put in the work to the class and he will put in the work to help you. Such a funny, earnest guy who really does care about his teaching. Got a 76 in class but rounded to a B.
He was so kind and genuinely cared about each of us. He made sure his office hours accommodated every single student. He cares so much about us and physics which made the class more enjoyable.

He felt bad when less than half of the class started showing up to lectures and genuinely asked what he could do to improve attendance. He is a very nice, student-oriented teacher and he gave us gummy bears after the final :)

He did a very good job of teaching the material and explained concepts well with good practice problems. Also is super funny and genuinely one of the most caring professors. Really wants his sections to succeeds, is super available outside of class, and frequently asks for and applies any feedback given very happily. Would definitely recommend.

The course is run by Dr Alicia, so tests are the same. There are enough online resources on canvas to self-teach this class. Bucket point system and extra credit make it not too difficult to get an A. Behrens lectures were good but sometimes a little scattered and hard to follow.

I struggled significantly in this course, but that was no fault of his. Honestly, I believe I may not have even had the chance at passing this course without him. Dr. Behrens is very kind and considerate of his students. He goes above & beyond to help his students succeed. If you have to take this course, he is by far the best professor.
Physics at tech in general is hard, but go to lecture, do all the practice given, and you'll be fine! I went to office hours a couple times typically before the tests and it was super helpful!

Loved him! Kinda bombed the final but the tests and stuff aren't up to him since it's a coordinated class. He's really funny and actual values your feedback and takes it insta consideration and moods how he lectures after it. Would recommend!!

Good lecturer and funny. Most notable thing is he really listens to feedback from students and applies it. He changed his lecturing style partway through the year based on student feedback, and it really improved his lectures
Slides were very helpful in studying for exams. Lectures pretty good to attend, he's a funny guy and explains things quite well.

Honestly, Behrens was a good teacher, but I didn't really use his resources as I didn't need it. If you're nervous about this class, just focus on learning via the GPS problems in the labs, and asking the TA's as many questions as possible. If you desperately need help, go to your prof's office hours.
Since Greco controls the class, the only difference between the professors are their lectures and office hours. I recommend Behrens because I thought his lectures were helpful and he is very kind.

I took this online during the summer fully online. The class is manageable as long as you watch the lecture videos provided (which are all taught by a different professor). Tests are tough, but fair, as he posts previous exams as study materials. Grading scale is great, and homeworks/labs are easy. Overall a great course.

I wouldn't recommend going to lectures for any Physics 2 class, as the videos and GPS practice problems teach well. But if you wanted extra clarification on subjects, Dr. Behrens was an amazing help. It's clear he cares about his students and will explain any topic you need help on, all while keeping 75-minute lectures from being sleep-inducing.

I never went to his lectures because most of the content can be learned online, but when I did, he did a great job of finding work arounds or explaining the content in new ways for the exams. The exams for our year were not difficult and many of the questions were the same as the GPS (but I think Dr. Greco did the exams) - Behrens was great though.
One of the best professors I had this semester. He is very accessible outside of class. His lectures are straightforward and based on what is on the tests.

Caring and wanted his students to succeed. Posts lecture slides before class and after class with annotations, answers questions in class, and keeps students updated on the course. At times lectures were long and monotonous but he tried to keep them interesting and covered a lot of examples. He also always stayed on pace with HW/GPS.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a really good professor. His lectures are concise, and he never goes on random tangents about non-PHYS 2212 stuff. He even sent out a mid-semester feedback form and actually adjusted his lectures based on student feedback. I think this was his first semester teaching 2212, so he'll probably be even better in the future.
Dr. Behrens gives engaging and fun lectures. He actually cares about the material and the students. Doing well is totally possible and his tests are fair.

Dr. Behrens provides one of the most balanced experiences I've had in the ChBE department at Georgia Tech. I really appreciate that he creates original exams and quizzes every semester even if he is teaching the same class. He is also an ACTUALLY funny guy, which makes it that much better to be in lecture. Overall, a PHENOMENAL professor!

Dr. Behrens was a great professor! Super passionate & gave great examples of the material we studied! Material is interesting and is presented in a way that facilitates understanding. Tests are average, Homework is tedious, project is easy. He was sometimes stubborn about certain answers on assessments that didn't (& still don't) make sense.

Transport is a difficult, math intensive class, but Dr. Behrens makes it as accessible as I think it gets. He posts lecture notes, offers many office hours, and generally seems to care about students. His grading curves were 85 for A, 70 for B, and 55 for C. Projects were graded leniently- class averge of 96. Exams are fair to challenging.

I had him in the Spring of 23 and I liked him a lot. I read through some of his previous reviews, and I thought he was fine. He's by no means an amazing lecturer, but for if you go and take some initiative and get involved in discussions, it's a good class.

I did not enjoy this course at all. I was excited to dive into OS but it almost killed my interest. He's nice and extended deadlines multiple times. However, his lectures are boring and do not help you in the labs nor the midterm. The labs were cool but hard with no feedback on the test cases. The midterm was weird since you had to rely on Google.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Lectures: not helpful & boring
Projects: very time consuming - hard to complete without office hours or help from friends
Test: felt like the lecture contents barely helped to actually answer questions - googling is much more effective

Easily the worst prof at GT. Changes grading criteria as he goes (his words). Lies to you (blatantly). Labs take 30 hours each. Autograder only gives pass/fail, no feedback. Lectures consist solely of HIM asking the CLASS questions, to which he does not give an actual answer. Just don't go to class, and read the excellent textbook instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor is the most inconsistent grader. The class had one exam on it and had nothing to do with anything taught in class. The labs are mostly on your own with very little (and crappy) instruction and the TAs are not much help. Interesting course, horrible professor. Don't go to class; read the xv6 textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: While I understand that he had never taught the course before, his lectures were still rough. He just copied pre-made slides from the course coordinator - I would recommend going to her if you need help instead. Handwriting was difficult to read. Seems like a great guy, but definitely does not need to teach MSE 2001.

Professor Brown moved slowly through material, leaving a full unit to learn on our own via online videos. Lectures were often unclear, but projects and test corrections were easy and boosted grades. Attendance was mainly needed for participation credit rather than understanding.
A slideshow could substitute lectures. Lots of practice exams posted. Quite a bore.

Really nice guy, but his teaching style was too slow. We sometimes weren't able to cover all the content for the day, so he would refer us to lecture videos to watch on our own time. Also, some of his explanations were difficult to understand and apply. However, there are built-in extra credit projects + corrections to boost your grade slightly.

Dr. Brown is great at explaining things. One thing that I particularly liked was the fact that when he did not know something, he would take the effort to find out and explain it. However, he is a bit slow during lectures and we didn't even get to the last unit. However, I'm going to give him a pass since it was his first time teaching the course.

The instruction is good but there is too much content to cover in this class. TA's are lifesavers with recitation and office hours. Past exams are helpful but be prepared to do a lot of self learning and outside the box thinking. Make a study group if you want to do well .Online final no partial credit was insane. You will never forget this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took this in my first semester here at tech. It was very difficult at first, but there are lots of resources like past exams and your TA to help you. Prof. Juang is a very chill dude and he's pretty caring if you just reach out to him with your problems. I would say the hardest part of this class (besides attendance) is doing well on HW.
You should just ask ChatGPT to explain the content to you during lectures, since attendance is mandatory, and this guy acts smug while proceeding to say nothing of value.

Prof. knows the content of the course well, but is very bad at transferring that knowledge to his students. Lectures are hard to pay attention to, there are no materials to study for the tests that actually reflect what the test will be like, and the only time I ever learned content was in recitation and by struggling on the HW. Take anyone else.
shoutout to my glorious goat chun wei other than that expect a panic attack the night before every quiz

The only issues I had with Professor Juang were more issues with how ECE 2026 is administered as a course. It's a weed out and is designed to be a little unfair at times. I can't fault Professor Juang for any of my complaints on that, as it would be the case with any 2026 professor. Very knowledgeable and helpful if asked for help.

Overall nice professor. ECE 2026 has always been known to be difficult but just don't fall behind and you should do fine. Exams are difficult and require you to have a true understanding of the material so take some time to study and review lecture slides.
ECE 2026. Fall 2022. Exam 3. phuck u
An old man truly out of touch with students. Horrible at lecturing and unfair exams. Avoid this pathetic thing like the plague.
A truly terrible Professor for an already difficult class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not very good at explaining anything, relates himself a lot, and doesnt seem to actually know whats going on. The second professor that taught the other section of the class did a much better job and seemed to be the only one that actually knew what was happening.

Would never take this class again. Stay away from ECE 3077. Studied for three weeks before a Test, only being able to get the professor to tell us the broad material that it will cover, and did horrible. Go from making +90 on all math and engineering course tests to failing with this class.

ECE 2026 at Tech is extremely organized and efficient. That being said, the class is very tough. I had Juang for recitation and I learned the concepts much more in there than the main lecture. Juang is very detailed and good at explaining things. He works relevant problems that are very helpful for homework and tests. I would take him again.

Concepts was easier than i expected but lots of work.Homework and lab every week. Do homework in groups or you'll be frustrated. Also use lots of office hours. For labs, do pre-lab before coming to lab. Take tests very seriously.

Pretty solid professor and class overall. The grading is pretty generous considering we have a pretty easy final project and can get up to 5% added to our final grade with extra credit. You get this ec by being in class though so attendance is required. All in all he's pretty nice and helpful and the class isn't too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One of the better stats professors out there. He has a very generous grading policy, gifting you up to 15% free if you just show up to lecture. Tests were a bit difficult but doable if you studied. Final project can be a lot of work. However, he does random attendance checks and you need to be in class.

First sem teaching but did his best. HWs are easy, but nothing is representative of exams. Cheat sheets allowed but even then exams are difficult. 5 entire points of EC from random attendance quizzes. One group project, last exam during regular class time on the week on finals. Nice and respectful, just a wonky class structure.

HW easy and only 6. Exams were not, and the exam reviews were very different than the exams despite the professor insisting that they'll be similar (at least you can have 2 cheat sheets). Good extra credit (5 points). This was his first semester, so there was disorganization, especially with the dates of when things were due and exam dates.
For INTA 3050- very nice professor and VERY easy class but her lectures are so disorganized. she tends to ramble for the entire class with no real point. Hated going to class, but worth it for the A!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class, caring teacher, amazing program.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Took the course in Fall 2021. Vicki has a notorious reputation for going onto tangents but she is an incredibly caring person and will do everything she can (both inside and outside class) to get to know you and help.
She was the program lead for FYFA and while she loved to go on about tangents, she is one of the nicest people I've ever met.
Great Professor who really wants her students to learn! If your at all interested in Europe, Dr. Birchfield has the class for you!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She does not directly use the book she says is "required" for class, but requires students to read several pages of it for each class module. Her field trips are not always well planned. Her slides are clumsy and filled with text, and scheduling of assignments is done verbally only.
She led a study abroad I participated in during Summer 2014. She was clear, concise, and was clearly vested in making sure we all learned from the trip. One of the best professors I've had at Tech.

I've had Birchfield for another class before. She can definitely be scattered and hard to follow sometimes, but overall, she's a very good professor. While she and I may not always have same or similar opinions, she's not the sort of professor to hold it against you or effect your grade. I'm looking forward to taking a third class with her.

She can't stick to her lecture at all.  She would get about 1/3 through her outline and then the whistle would blow because she spent too much time talking about pointless information.  But don't worry, you'll see it on the test.
Least organized prof I've ever had.  Brings personal politics into "lectures" (i.e. rants).  Nothing was clear, orderly, or understood in the class.
No Comments
extremely unorganized. goes off on rants during lecture. excessive, superfluous readings. tests have little to do with lecture material. lectures on abstract concepts, tests minute details.

HUGE AMOUNTS OF READING. LECTURES ARE NOT ORGANIZED AND YOU WILL BE TESTED OVER THE SMALLEST DETAIL.  NEVER FINISHES MATERIAL PLANNED FOR LECTURES, BUT YOU WILL BE TESTED ON THAT AS WELL. QUESTIONS ON THE TEST ARE DIFFICULT TO UNDERSTAND WHAT SHE WANTS.
Boring lectures and bad grader
I would not recommend taking Professor Bier's classes.

Her lectures tend to be kind of boring, but group discussions are engaging if you're caught up with all the readings. Assignments are extremely easy and tests consist of memorizing terms and writing an essay, which she grades fairly. I wouldn't recommend buying all the books, since you can get by without reading them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's super passionate about what she's teaching. Lectures can be long, but interesting. She took weeks to grade things, which was rough. Just pay attention in class and at least skim the readings and you'll get an A.

She is a nice professor. She gives out everything that is going to be on the midterm and final, so study that a lot. I thought she was going to grade easily because she is nice but she grades essays very strictly. I wish this class was more of a discussion, but instead she lectured a lot. Don't turn anything in late.

For the most part you will pass if you read and understand the textbook, which the tests are directly based on. Most classtime is devoted to lectures which ho more in-depth. The teacher is very enthusiastic about the topics she teaches.

4 textbooks barely used.dont buy. u can get by by gogling the readings. And unless you have to turn in a paper, dont bother doing the readings. Too much assigned and a complete waste of time. Ask her for her expectation on midterm papers because she is alot stricter when grading those. Class borng. she needs to learn 2 teach rather than readng ppt
Not the most exciting class but all you need to know for the tests she uploads online
needs training on how to teach and to lead discussions

Very open-minded and respectful of everyone's opinions in this discussion-based class. There is a lot of reading and writing involved, and while the material is interesting, I wish the class was more engaging. Positive attitude and willingness to listen to feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Favorite course of the semester! Classes were discussion based. The readings were extremely interesting, and our class got to vote on topics to cover for the last few weeks. Tests were based on ability to apply concepts from class, and were very similar to the short weekly responses. Professor was very kind and respectful of everyone's opinions.

I enrolled in this course as an elective but was pleasantly surprised by how engaged I became in its content, as the professor does a great job in conveying his enthusiasm. With few graded assignments, as long as you put in the expected effort, this is an easy course to succeed in. 100% would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Biegalski for NRE 3112, and on multiple occasions he made it clear that he really does care about his students. Dr. Biegalski also does a good job lecturing and answering questions, as well as just being a really chill and affable professor. My only complaint is that he oftentimes is too nice and students would heavily abuse that.

I encourage you to get to know Dr. Biegalski both inside ad outside  of class.  Assuming you like him, see if you can get involved in his research.  He send another girl from my class for a professional conference in Hawaii this past semester for her to present he research,  that would be a good GT experience,

Also ask him about fly fishing.

I took his class to graduate during Spring 2020. He is definitely in my top 5 favorite professors at Tech. He teaches the material extremely well, is interested in getting to know all of his students, and I had a ton of fun learning about nuclear reactions, reaction design, and nuclear energy. I wish he taught more classes.
One of the sweetest profs I have had. Really knows his stuff but easily gets sidetracked- Not a bad thing though. I spent maybe 1 hour per week on this class outside of lecture.

I'll be honest- I have no interest in Nuclear Engineering, and just had to take this class to graduate. However, Professor Biegalski was by far one of the best professors I had at tech. He teaches very clearly. His tests are extremely fair. He really cares about the well being of his students. I really wish I could have had him for more classes.
Best professor so far at Georgia Tech.
He makes the content more enjoyable and helps make complicated stuff easier!
One of the best professors so far! Really approachable and caring!
Caring towards students and very helpful!
Good into class. I enjoyed the lectures.
Very engaging professor and made me even more interested in nuclear engineering.

Very nice teacher who does his best to introduce the material in a lighthearted manner, although he does veer off course sometimes. Weekly homework is given and each student does a presentation to further interest in the major. Tests are similar to homework problems.

The most passionate professor I've had. Incredible guest speakers that changed my perspective on many things. Class is heavily participation-based, but I was able to get an A in participation only speaking twice all semester because I commented on Canvas group discussions and did some easy extra credit assignments. 2-3 easy essays 2pg double space

One of the best professors that I have ever had. Class is a mixture of case discussions and guest speakers. Grades are based on one test, three short essays, class participation. Prof. Todd has a wealth of industry knowledge and does a great job helping students understand healthcare. He's very lenient grader. Show up and try; you will make an A.
This was a great class with a bunch of guest lectures from people in the health care industry. I really enjoyed this class

Professor Todd really cares about his students.  I would suggest taking this class even if you are not interested in healthcare.  Straight up grades, two essay tests, case assignments, and class participation.  Professor really wants students to succeed. LOTS of guest speakers

Such an interesting course. If you have any interest in healthcare, take it. Professor Todd is the best professor! He has a discussion based class about half of the time and excellent guest speaker the other half of the time. He is genuinely interested in your success as a student. I wish I could take this class every semester!

Class was pretty easy. Just show up to class. Most of what you see on the test was said in class, so attendance is key. He's also a pretty cool guy. His stories are interesting. He has a lot of connections so he's someone you would want to know!

Course is very challenging, and lectures were long and content heavy. Despite it being confusing most of the time, going to the lectures was important to grasp the material. Professor was very generous with grading along with an easy project grade, however he expects that you do your part in the learning process meet him halfway to be successful

I couldn't tell you a single thing I learned in class, and by the end there might have been 5 people going. Crappy Lectures. The homework wasn't too bad as you were allowed to use AI for coding, and the exams were open note(not open internet), yet this didn't really help with his slides. The project was fine. I survived but never again...

Dr. Blumling is not a great lecturer, the examples he used in class were very hard and even himself had trouble solving the problems. The tests and quizzes were very different from what we practiced in PSS and in class. The class was extremely hard for a study abroad class.

At times, the only thing that got me through this class was knowing that his actor clips existed. While working on the hours of homework that I had every week, I would turn on one of those bad boys to feel better about myself. I didn't take MATLAB before this course (since it is no longer a prerequisite) and the exams felt nearly impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Blumling is a subpar lecturer. He likes to make material that is not just challenging but also often beyond the reach of the students. He wants to push students, but his methodology is not incremental, and it's frustrating because the class could be much more digestible and achievable if it were not made challenging for no reason.

This professor was horrible. There were no practice tests, and the only way to study for tests was by looking at Homeworks. However, there were no answer keys to Homeworks, so this class was immediately cooked. Also, BMED 2400 is supposed to be free, and he made it way harder than it needed to be. DO NOT TAKE HIM!

While a considerate person, he is not a considerate professor... Does not work through content clearly, no examples, no practice. He seems to throw everything at you and assume you are not a good student if you do not go to office hours or ask how to do something--especially if he says you did it completely wrong. His tests are an overkill.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Blumling is a nice guy, but not a great professor. This easy BME class may cost me my 4.0. Tests don't reflect class material, he provides no example problems or supplemental resources, and homework answers aren't available for practice. There's also no test review, making it impossible to prepare effectively.
I feel like he does not know that students are no longer required to take Matlab before this class, so if you took 1301, you have no chance. Take anyone else for this class.

Professor Blumling completely overhauled this course into one of the most difficult in BMED. Weekly homework assignments of well over 5 hours of work a week, and tests were very unrepresentative of his lectures with awful time pressure and averages well below passing. He also assumes you are fluent in matlab (1371), and makes you code on exams.

Absolutely do not take James Blumling for biostatistics. This class is supposed to be a free A, and with any other professor it is. His tests are way to hard and the homeworks take hours to complete. It is actually unfair to students who took his class compared to any other professor with this class. He's a nice guy, but he makes it way too hard.

Homework is long and lectures don't help with completing them. The tests are poorly structured and difficult to complete. He's nice and a welcoming professor but his lectures don't help with the actual course assignments and examinations.

This course should be one of the easiest courses for BMEs and the easiest stats course at Tech. You will have hours of homework and the lectures will not help you complete it. The tests are impossible to complete based on the lectures, and you do not even have enough time to complete them. Just steer clear from his class, IYsE stats would be better

Dr. Blumling is not great at teaching the content of this course. He doesn't explain the base concepts and just kind of expects students to undertstand them, then in lecture gives the hardest possible example problem with the material. The quizzes and exams were hard to even know where to start.

its biotransport, it was never gonna be easy. For lecture, it doesnt matter who you choose because lectures are online prerecorded and profs switch off (aboulnasr has the best ones though). I had Dr. Blumling for PSS, hes very caring and easy to talk to. Hes great about explaining anything you have questions about and hes pretty laid-back too.

Blumling is a great professor for BMED 1000. He is super chill, and we normally finish lecture early. The class is a breeze. Just do your work, and you will be fine. It is group project based, so be ready to collaborate. If you get a good group, you'll be golden for this semester. Just do the weekly assignments and show up to class.

This class was literally a semester-long group project. Your TA is probably a closer resource but Dr. Blumling was always open for questions. Many opportunities and office hours to attend if you need help. Not that much work really, just a group paper a week and an essay the next week. The schedule was confusing at first but makes sense later.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Made Orgo 1 so easy to understand. He's very nice and engaging in class as well, and is easy to contact for questions. So many options for extra credit. Exams were very similar to practice exams and textbook questions. Definitely have to put in work because its organic chem, but Professor Blackburn does not try to make it harder.

I was terrified to take organic chemistry this semester, but Nathan genuinely made the class interesting and less intimidating, and I ended up really enjoying a class that I'd dreaded taking my entire college career. He gives out a good bit of extra credit and is super accessible for office hours and stuff! Goated professor.

Genuinely made Orgo a breeze, you can tell he loves it and knows a lot. Flipped classroom, but the lectures really help you lock down concepts because practice is built in. He wants you to succeed and will give CIOS bonus and extra credit opportunities. Just such a nice guy overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I can't speak on Nathan's classroom style, as I've only had the pleasure of having him be a TA for my 2311 lecture and 2380 lab. However, I can confidently say that Nathan is an amazing teacher, and has a way of explaining and working through difficult concepts and making them significantly easier to comprehend. Take his class if given the chance.
He has a great way of making difficult concepts easy to understand and is an incredible lecturer.

Professor Bloch is an extremely caring professor, who is always willing to distribute knowledge on any subject he has on hand. Signal processing, machine learning, life lessons, he has and will teach about anything. Being in this VIP course has taught me so much, even when I started from no knowledge at all.

I don't think he deserves all the hate that these reviews have been giving him. The class was fair and the exams were very similar to the homework. He is a nice person and mostly accommodating. He is very slow, but he also doesn't normally teach, and his section was only added to accommodate the influx of freshmen. This is not a deadly class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have attended 4 funerals this year and didn't shed a tear at any. I bawled after his final exam and midterms. No preparation provided except for literally nothing. This class was the definition of doom and despair and everything unfair. Matthieu Ratoslav will take your soul - do not take unless you want to cross the River Styx.

Anyone who gives this guy a review over three stars is just straight delusional. He's clearly only here for research and doesn't really care about teaching (we were wayyyy behind what we were supposed to be covering), and most your grades is the exam. If you care about learning, avoid at all costs
The class overall wasn't too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Absolute joke of a professor. Hands down one of the worst i've ever experienced at Tech. Too focused on his family responsibilities instead of his class... Not judging because I would too but maybe don't decide to take on a class and teach if you have familial responsibilities.

Please do not take Matthieu ratoslav bloch. PLEASE DO NOT TAKE HIM. The worst professor at GT hands down. Just dont. Any other ECE 2020 prof will be better. He will not teach you anything. Pleas eplease please avoid

Extremely exam-heavy, and the exams felt like the entire grade was a few problems. On top of that, it's proof-heavy in a way that didn't feel necessary for an introductory course. Just absolutely dodge this guy at all costs, 1 month behind on content, don't feel prepared for 2031 at all.

I actually do like the professor, but the pacing of the class was much slower than other sections, exam and lab dates were postponed frequently, and he wasn't great at communicating logistics with the class.

Though we only covered half of the course material, Professor Bloch is a nice and accessible teacher. Tests are relatively easy and no tricky questions, but you will probably lose amount of points on some math and theory proof questions. The final exam is worth 33% of the total course grade, so really be prepared for that.

Cool professor, fun class. Exams and homeworks were easy. Pretty chill about labs - he allowed me to use a $10 arduino uno instead of the $250 mydaq, and didn't require lengthy reports.

Pacing was slow, but it seems all the reviews complaining about it forget to mention that this was his first time teaching an intro class.

Would recommend.

He is a decent lecturer, with my main criticism being that we were a month behind on content. Normally I wouldn't care, but the content in this class is interesting and important foundationally for engineers and internships. The tests model the homework and are not that hard, and the labs are lightweight and easy.

just pray you get bhattacharya. she's the only way. bloch makes this way too harsh for an INTRO class for FRESHMAN. anyone other than her i've heard makes this class way too demanding and tedious for the so called easy ece class.

Lied to our faces about exam questions multiple times. Emphasized proof-based math questions instead of engineering/ system design ones, where the slightest error could cost you half credit. Only covered half of the material listed in the syllabus; we have to catch up now. His reviews for the graduate-level classes have the exact same complaints.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
We got to early October's material in December. He regularly makes promises he doesn't keep.

He has described his own grading scheme as brutal. Every (lengthy) question is 2 points. If you write down anything you get 1 point. If you get the entire problem correct with no small errors at all, you get 2 points. 85% of the course grade was exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He does not provide practice exams, exams are EXTREMELY HARD and nothing like homework questions, he does not curve despite the low average, and he is test heavy (53% on 4 tests and 33% on final). Do NOT take his class if you want to make your life easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought he great, other guy talking about his french bit is just a hater. His lectures were super engaging and in depth, I feel like I really learned why things are implemented the way they are. The homework was also very helpful and translated well to the tests. It is true that he was behind in his material, but you can tell he's just passionate

Took his ECE2020 class, and struggled heavily due to how math-heavy he was in a "System Design" class. We were over a month behind and never finished the class. He also overpromises like crazy. No practice exams; extremely test heavy; never curves despite class average; spends way to long on a single topic. All-in-all TAKE ANOTHER PROFESSOR!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was his first time teaching an entry class since this section was added late. He's a good lecturer and nice guy but his pacing, approach, & grading scheme for tests were bad. We got through 1/2 the content on the sem & he has proofs on exams unlike other professors. He also grades stuff a bit late. Take him only if you like abstract questions.
He moves a little slow sometimes, but usually his lectures explain the topics quite well. We were like a month behind all semester though. His tests are extremely easy if you do the homeworks.
We were a month behind the whole semester. Explains well though.

RUN! DO NOT TAKE THIS GUY! Can't stop talking about how he's french, class is incredibly different from other ECE2020 professors, proof heavy, bad lecturer, avoid at all costs. Please take another 2020 prof like kj, rl, just anybody else.

I took Dr. Bloch's VIP for one semester, and I regret it. He does not provide a clear grading criteria and when he does not deliver something he promises on, he turns it on the students for not showing initiative. Maybe it's just his talking style, but he likes to repeat himself, and it sometimes gives the impression that he thinks we're idiots.

He often talks about the VIP being "student driven," but that stems from him being unable to properly allocate time towards it. He is also very long-winded, often repeating the same thing over and over. He attempts to connect what you do in VIP to industry which is funny cause he has no experience whatsoever in industry. Avoid this VIP at all costs

I was in his VIP and it's not letting me select that class. Dr. Bloch has poor time management skills and consistently overpromises and underdelivers. He clearly does not have enough time to conduct this VIP effectively. He consistently shows up late to meetings. Join another VIP if possible; unfortunately, I got stuck with him for three semesters.

He is quick to blame students for not studying correctly. He noted that he usually makes the midterm too hard/time constrained, so why not make it easier? If you have not taken a proofs course before I would not recommend Dr. Bloch, as he fails to provide resources on linear algebra and proofs.

Over promises literally everything, and fails to deliver. He's nice but does not prepare you at all for his exams that are twice as long as they should be. Your homework will be tangentially related to the topics in class, he'll say to come to office hours but he'll blow the entire time on the first one or two questions.

Dr. Bloch does take a while to grade things and sometimes over promised on deadlines, but I would fully recommend taking him. He's an excellent teacher and if you're willing to put in the work in the course, it'll be a good experience. If you care about the material and really want to learn it outside of just getting a grade, you'll do fine.

Many things haven't changed: late grading/proofs heavy/nice but disconnected/lots of office hours. Makes false promises about grading. Exams are based on HW but doesn't grade on time (most graded AFTER final exam). Midterm was awful, unreasonable expectations and didn't give enough time. Gave extra credit problem to compensate. Curves heavily.

There were fewer assignments than planned (6 vs 10+) with late grading feedback due to grading for 150+ students; most issues were due to him having too many responsibilities (1 y/o at home and ECE grad affairs chair). He was always communicating the situation, adjusting deadlines, and accommodating of the students. Office hours were very helpful.

Spends too long doing proofs/examples that he didn't prepare and would get stuck on. Promised min 10 HWs, but gave 6 (still due in as little as 6 days with revisions since he'd make mistakes). First test was way too long. Course didn't cover nearly as much material as promised. Class wasn't too hard but poorly taught. He's nice but disconnected.
Very hard. Very insightful. Very good educator.

Prof. Blann cared about his students, and wanted them to learn. He was especially attentive about ODS accommodations, and never once made me feel uncomfortable about asking for what I needed. His grading scheme was forgiving, so long as you put forth the effort needed. My only regret is not having more time to dedicate to his class.

Blann is very caring and considerate. The class is mostly comprised of 4 exams, 10 quizzes, and textbook work. To prepare for the exams you'll typically have 2-3 practice exams. Homework sets help you prepare, too. You'll also be allowed one note card for exams. For homework, the textbook is very helpful. Extra credit opportunities were given.

Such a fun class and professor! Unique approach of teaching valuable acct content in an enjoyable and low-stress format. Assignments include many small group projects, a few pop quizzes, and the final was a slightly larger group project. One of my fav classes I have taken at GT, so ABSOLUTELY take it if you need an extra MGT/accounting elective!

Professor Blann is super nice and accommodating!! His lectures are alright, but the class is pretty straightforward. I would only say that I felt like the online section got much better grades than the in-person section (I was in-person section). Attendance is basically mandatory since he has mini quizzes for attendance almost every class

Professor Blann is very kind and accommodating. The tests are pretty fair and there are daily quizzes to make sure you are keeping up with the content. He is always looking for ways to improve his course by asking for feedback and implementing it. I would recommend!
Very caring and sweet professor! He grades very fairly and leniently, sets clear expectations for how the class is laid out. Only downside is lectures are a little boring.

Professor Blann is a great professor! Although the class is a little boring and lectures are mostly just him reading slides, Professor Blann provided several extra credit opportunities, homework's that really helped for the test, and a flash card on each test. He also is very understanding and will help you if needed. Overall, good class!

Such a unique way to teach this course, but truly made my day every time I went to his class. It's not anything like any other accounting class here– it's more project based learning. But it's such a stress free environment. Love him.
Prof Blann is fair and kind. He is good at explaining concepts, accommodating, and works with you to make sure you get your best grade. He's awesome!

Graded on only tests and quizzes which were not too hard. He listened well to feedback and was able to adapt the class according to. Many extra credit opportunities and dropped lowest test grade too. Overall very kind and caring. Take him if you can!
Blazeck is tough, but a great lecturer and clearly a nice guy. No curve or crib sheet is absolutely brutal, but his exams are fair. His homework is very long.

I had him for chbe 2140 thermodynamics. He's a very nice and knowledgeable guy. I'm not sure how he put my name to my face seeing as I've never introduced myself but that shows how much he cares about his students. Definitely a difficult class with absolutely no curves. Homework is harder than the tests and graded harshly for accuracy.

No curve, longer homeworks than the other sections, reference sheet only on tests (other professors have open textbook or crib sheets), and no notes posted so attendance is "mandatory." However, he cares about his students and he has so many resources available. He prepares everyone really well for his class; I struggled but I'm glad I took him.

Blazeck was a great 2100 professor, his lectures were great and it was clear that he knew the subject well. He doesn't curve tests, but they're very do-able and lots of partial credit. He also doesn't upload his notes from lecture, so you won't pass if you don't go to class. The homework is time consuming, but you're given plenty of time to do it.

Fantastic professor. Had two TAs from his lab- one did HW, other did problem solving sessions each week (only 2100 prof with TAs to my knowledge). Made a horrendous weed out actually a class I enjoyed. Professor very caring and accessible outside of class. No curve so not much room for error but provides SO MANY resources to prepare well for exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Blazeck was a great guy. He was very relaxed and created a collaborative environment in his classroom. Just be prepared for fast-paced lectures. The tests make up the majority of the grade and they are pretty difficult. There is not much room for error either, as there is no extra credit or curves. Overall, he prepared me very well for CHBE.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Blazeck is a great professor. If you ever have a chance, I would recommend taking 2100 with him. He explains things very well in class, is accessible outside of class, and gets to know his students. The class itself can be challenging, but it's definitely manageable. Do ALL the HW, don't skip class, use any resources you need, and you're golden!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is really hard, and his tests didn't make it better.
2100 is a pain for everyone but this guys makes it manageable. Do the homeworks and go to office hours and you'll be fine

Great choice for 2100. If he sees that you care hell go through great efforts to make sure your okay at the end. Lectures are clear and if you need more understanding his office hrs are super helpful.

Dr. Blazeck was great! I was terrified to take this class, but it wasn't bad at all with his thorough, example-based lectures. He is very receptive to feedback and overall a super caring person. Even though the class was difficult, I would 100% take it again with Blazeck!

Had a great time learning in his class. Prof. is very caring for students. Thorough lectures. Would take again without hesitation. 2100 was difficult and hard work as expected, but I feel I got a good foundation from the class.

An overall good teacher. Covers everything in class and does examples in lecture. Seeing the process worked out over and over in lecture helps to ingrain the problem solving strategy. Really nice and easy to respect.

Actually ended up really liking chbe 2100 with Blazeck. Pretty sure it was his first time teaching, but lectures were well organized and straight forward. He made it pretty clear what you need to do to succeed. Grades pretty easy relative to other teachers for 2100 and tests weren't too crazy. Would definitely recommend. Very understanding as well.
Blumenthal's lectures are good, but I couldn't enjoy them because the course was super easy. A good load of homework, but not too bad.

Blumenthal is a chill professor, his lectures may be tangential at times, but teaches everything you need to know for the tests. HW's are varying in difficulty, however, they shouldn't take too much time. Overall decent professor, especially for math. Beware that midterm and final is worth 35% and 45% respectively.
Great professor! His lectures are great and easy to follow, the homework and tests help you learn a lot. Would definitely take him again :)))

He doesnt teach from the textbook, but he moves along it. His lectures are basically his thoughts/what's on his mind. That makes it sound unprofessional, but he's actually really good at explaining things, and even better at answering questions. Very approachable, and very helpful.

I took this course in Fall 2022. Blumenthal is very knowledgeable about 1554 topics; however, he sometimes forgets that his students are not. He rushes through the course content, which made it very hard to keep up - but 1554 is simply a hard class. He is caring for his students, but could be a better communicator. Take Barone!
Lectures were clear and on-topic, and Professor Blumenthal is funny enough to keep class interesting. I had substitutes for him while he was away for a week, and I think he's the best 1554 teacher.
Best professor you could get for 1554!! Prof Blumenthal's lectures are clear and easy to understand. Best math professor I've had so far.

Great Prof! Always very well prepared for lecture and very dedicated. Even when he was seriously sick, he provided zoom classes instead of just cancelling lecture altogether.  While these virtual lectures were not as good as his in-person, they were still well structured and superior to the in-person lectures of other linear algebra professors.

Prof. Blumenthal is clearly passionate about Linear Algebra and wants his students to succeed. However, he'd often get off course during lecture which led to incomplete lectures and playing catch-up for days on end. He records lectures (when he remembers) which is helpful for review. Overall, decent (and certainly one of the better) linear profs.

Where do I even start with ol' Blue. Blumenthal is one of the better lecturers and while he may move fast, he covers everything necessary to ace the tests. Just hope he doesn't eat Twisted Taco before class and you will be alright.

Great professor and a very knowledgeable person. Professor Blumenthal makes Linear Algebra as interesting as it can be and personalizes his lectures to be intriguing. Only problem is he sometimes moves quickly or spends too long on a smaller topic in the class.
Linear is hard but Alex makes it an easy A

Just an amazing lecturer and person overall, content, homeworks, and tests were not that bad, so there is nothing bad to say. Even though he was clearly affected by Covid, he still tried to do his best for his students. Hope I will take another class with him in the future.
Absolutely amazing lectures, and really showed he was dedicated to his students. He caught COVID and despite being extremely sick and probably miserable, he held an online review for us on exam day.

Linear Algebra is about as fun as it sounds but somehow he manages to make it tolerable. He definitely tries to breathe life into the otherwise static numbers, vectors and planes. It is clear that he is passionate about math. He'll crack a few jokes here and there and is very responsive and understanding. I actually began to like math.

Professor Blumenthal is a gifted lecturer and is passionate about his teaching. Analysis isn't often a course one would think of as 'fun', yet he made it extremely fun and thrilling. The feedback provided was useful, and his office hours were 10/10. If you take his course, definitely make an effort to attend office hours. He is the GOAT of GT math.

I loved Professor Blumenthal. I will recommend him until the day I graduate! He REALLY wants you to succeed and learn the material. He completely understood when I couldn't attend class when I had a cold and gave me extensions. Amazing professor and person!

Professor Blumenthal goes fast and covers a lot of content, but he is extremely willing to help if you just ask. He tries to work with your schedule as much as he can and clearly cares about his students' success. Make sure to come with questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor's Blumenthal's proofs class was great, he clearly explained the foundations of mathematical proofs in a way that made it easy to understand. His tests were straightforward and came from the weekly homework assignments. His enthusiasm for the subject made it easy to enjoy the course. This class made me want to major in math!

Prof. Blumenthal is a great teacher, and he interacts with students a lot in class which I really enjoyed and helped me stay focused. However, there's a lot of content and his class might be too fast for students to keep up, so you would either want to read before or ask questions in class(he encourages question asking though). A lot of hw(6h/week)
The first few weeks of homework were kinda like getting forged by hellfire, but it was worth it and you learn a lot of things from a stellar professor. I would highly recommend this teacher!
Wonderful professor. His lectures are clear and entertaining and his grading is rather lenient. One of my best experiences at GT. Take him if possible!

I love watching Professor Blumenthal's recorded lectures with a sparkling energy drink in one hand and a foot long chicken melt sub in the other. With raisin cookies and chips in the middle. He explains everything in lecture, has mad jokes, and tries to accommodate us as much as possible. What more could you want in a professor!!!
I really love his structured lectures and humor.

Professor Blumenthal did an okay job of explaining concepts in class. While he is clearly well versed in the subject, he often goes at a pace that is too fast for most students to comprehend, and does not do a good job at helping struggling students keep up. As a person, he's great; as a teacher, he's just alright.

Professor Blumenthal is great! He always logs into lecture prepared with a OneNote full of notes and pre-prepared problems, so time is never waste. In addition, he knows to avoid tangents and gets everything done in class that he needs to. Despite this, he is still quick to answer any questions thoroughly. The class is tough, but he makes it great!

Jacob Blevins is the GOAT. Excellent lecturer. Material isn't boring at all and he takes time on the details of the notes. Solves problems himself in class rather than just rewriting steps from notes. Homework prepare you well for the exams. Jacob Blevins is a professor that actually cares about the quality of his communication skills.
In a one on one decision between teachers, always bet on Blevins.

Dr. Jacob Blevins is not just a professor—he is an intellectual deity sent from the celestial realms to bless us mere mortals with wisdom. Grading? Fair and just like the scales of truth. Feedback? So insightful it feels like prophecy. Passion for the subject? Enough to make scholars weep. His class isn't just education—it's ascension. ⭐11/5⭐

What more can be said about the great Jacob Blevins that hasn't already been said. Much like Mithrandir in the Lord of the Rings, he is an unstoppable force for good, proliferating light and warmth to Tech Tower and beyond, a proverbial angel among men. His name can be heard spoken in the streets of Home Park, whispering of his greatness.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Blevins is hands down the best instructor for 2110. I took the 6:30 pm to 9:15 pm section but it was worth taking considering how much this man respected our hard work in the class. 2110 is hell, but he will make it WAYYY easier than the other instructors for 2110.
good professor

Jacob Barthelemew Blevins III is a wonderful man. I see him constantly sitting behind his desk located right outside the Hive (I think thats what they call it) I stop by his desk almost daily so he can put a smile on my face and put me in my place! Jacob is a kind and caring individual who deeply cares about telling you how much he loves his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Blevins has a reputation for being one of the most difficult professors on campus. He really makes you work for the grade and does NOT HAND OUT As. Every point that you get is earned and NOT GIVEN. His story of growing up alone on the streets and working his way to the top of the engineering department is inspirational to say the least.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: How else can I say this.... Jacob Creed Blevins is a man of quality. An engaging lecturer with excellent knowledge of the content. 5/5 on the hot factor too which never hurts ;)
Great guy

Dr. Blekherman is great. He is funny, insanely intelligent, and a great lecturer. His domain of knowledge stretches far beyond the course I took with him, and it shows. He is always able to answer questions I had and is highly available online and during his office hours. Great class, great professor. Would totally recommend.

His class was the hardest in my degree, but I always felt confident because I knew he was always there for us. Lectures were very good, and homework did a very good job preparing for the exams. He was also very helpful in office hours. He did have both a final project and exam, which always annoys me, but other than that, I highly recommend.

Disclaimer: I took this class dual enrollment 
I see so many people saying he was a very tough professor and that the practices were nothing like the exam. Practice exams don't have to look like the exam: they are designed to test you over the content on the exam, which they did. He was also generous with partial credit. The class had good rigor.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class dual enrollment, and it was clear that this was his first time with the online courses. Initially the difficulty was poorly managed and there was a general lack of materials and communication, but he acclimated rather well and the difficulty became reasonable by the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took gt math year 2 with him. Very vague hw key descriptions and the TAs suck as grading. Exams have weird questions in them and are only 5 questions. Practice tests are not like real tests.

Struggles to clearly explain the material. His graders have been abysmal. They mark you wrong on every homework problem, and then when you go and ask them for explanation, they spout out some vague explanation that isn't even mathemtically correct, then ignore your requests for a regrade. Painful class to take. Do not recommend at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor but test difficulty was harder than quizzes and practice given in studios. I really enjoyed his teaching style, but I felt that the questions asked on the exams were not a good representation of our knowledge on the subject.

Very passionate but lectures are hard to follow. Homework is easy, quizzes are okay, but midterm difficulty is all over the place. Not bad overall, but expect to teach yourself most of the time to get an A.

Not a bad teacher, very passionate about the subject, but I did not love his teaching style. He cares about students, but I did not love the grading scheme or difficulty of scale between tests and homework. Watch Sebastian Fernandez for diff eq.

A very nice professor who cares about his students. My only qualm is that sometimes his notes are hard to follow, so you'll also need to watch the lectures in order to get the full picture (this is irrelevant for non-covid semesters). Other than that I have no complaints.

Dr. Blekherman is a great guy, and he clearly cares a lot about his students. He is very patient, his lectures are fun (he tells daily jokes), and he encourages participation but doesn't mandate it. There were weekly homeworks, which was sometimes a bit much for me, but overall they were not too hard as long as you pay attention in lectures.

Dr Blekherman is such a nice guy. He gives clear expectations of his students and gives good feedback when asked. In this class, which is an upper level math class, he gave us asynchronous attendance, which means watching a lecture and doing the quiz which he gives questions for in class. Told daily jokes which is so fun.
