I don't think Dr. Blekherman was a good fit as a professor for me. Personally, his teaching style was not the most effective for my learning; it was a bit fast-paced. I also recommend not skipping class or you may fall behind.

Professor Blekherman has clear enthusiasm for the subject and he tries to make the class more fun for everyone. Lectures can go a bit fast and he does not do very many examples for each topic. However, he is easily accessible in office hours or another time.

At first I definitely thought his lectures were a bit fast-paced, but after a week or two, I got the hang of it and from then on it wasn't that bad! He would sometimes start off lecture with cheesy math jokes which was fun. He was always open to questions, and I enjoyed his class. I never read the the textbook, but it never hurts to read it.

Dr Blekherman was not a good choice for me. I found his explanations too fast-paced and his annotations in the board messy. I was always trying to write down what he talked about 5min before, and that made it hard to follow the lectures. The textbook helped a lot. Nonetheless, his lectures are entertaining and he's accessible for questions.

Blekherman is truly a funny guy. I appreciated how he injected humor into math, which is rare in my experience. The class itself is hard but Blekherman's lectures are fairly engaging. As far as 1553 goes, he is a fairly standard grader and the work is mostly the same across all professors.

I found that he was a decent lecturer, and I loved the textbook for this course! Probably one of the best textbooks I've ever had for a class, so if you have him for 1553 be sure to read the textbook in addition to going to lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor. Explained the concepts well, was always open to questions, and prepared us well for tests. Go to lectures, read the textbook, and take the practice tests, and you should be fine in his class. Also, his tests were usually easier than the other professors. I actually enjoyed this class a lot, and it wasn't too hard. Take Blekherman!!

Lectures are very clear and he covers exactly what will be on the exams. If you do the homeworks, know the content in the textbook, and do the worksheets you will do well on the exams. He often has time in class to answer questions before tests. He also has regular office hours and additional ones around when there are tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Take it with Blekherman or Janokowski they're the best 2 for linear. He's a pretty good teacher and our tests were a lot easier than the other classes. He seems like a really nice guy and offers lots of office hours but I never went.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really great professor, I thought his lectures were clear and helpful and he was engaging and funny. If you know how to do all the problems on the review sheet, the tests are more than fair and straightforward. Also very helpful during office hours, held a lot of them and answers any questions.

Dr. Blekherman was okay. Didn't explain all the concepts required for exams, True/False questions torture you on HW's and exams, and voice can be boring after a while. Typically if the class average is lower than the course average, a heft curve is applied, so expect the possibility of a bump with him.

One of the best math professors I have taken. If you like proofs/theory, take his advanced classes. He is fair, but still presents challenging material and expects you to know it. His lectures are really great, and he is very helpful when responding to questions.

Really funny and cool guy and very thorough in lectures. His reviews are almost the same as his tests. The biggest downfall is that he does not give you answers to his reviews, so I recommend starting early and trying to get help in office hours if you don't understand ANYTHING in the slightest and form a study group to help check your answers!

Overall, an amazing professor. The reviews that he provides before the exams are very similar to the test questions. If you do those by yourself and understand the method behind your work you will get an A hands down. He is very professional and seems like a nice dude. One of the best professors I've had at Tech.

Dr. Blekherman is great - his lectures are more clear and understandable than most at Tech. Office hours are important, and he will explain concepts even more clearly. Tests can be rough, but if you study using materials he gives, you can do well.  He also added 12% onto one of my midterm grades because it was graded too harshly.  Would recommend!

He's a huge goofball. Tests were pretty tough but he provides a lot of exam prep material and only tests on material he's covered. Office hours are helpful and he's generous with your grade as long as you're showing effort. Don't skip class, and go to recitation/office hours for extra help. Overall really solid
Engaging, funny lecturer who explains the material well. The tests were hard but fair.

Tests were not too hard, basically covering what we learned in class.  However, the final exam was all new material, nothing we had covered.  Had A's on all tests and got a 63 on the final  (class average was about 50) to end with a B.  No curve.
His voice is that of Gru from Despicable Me. He is clear.

Class is useful, learned everything there. Quizzes every week but those are basic and easy for the most part. Tests are fair, mainly solving and little theory. Homework is online but you get unlimited tries so easy 100 for that.

Seriously one of the best math profs at Tech. Lecture is useful; he does a really good job of explaining. His tests are hard though, the first test had a class avg of like a 55 so watch out. If you pay attention and study, you can definitely get an A. He replaces one test with the grade you get on the final.

Great professor.  Quizzes and homework every week, but not too time consuming.  What is explained in proofs in lecture is covered better in recitation if needed.  Gives practice problems for tests that prepare you well.  Tests are difficult but very fair!  Highly recommended!

Hilarious, very fair tests but still require you to know the material.  Office hours and practice problems were very helpful.  Ended up with a high A after a 63 and 76 on the first 2 tests because of grade replacement.  Definitely an awesome professor

This was not a bad class. He does a lot of proofs in lectures, but he never puts them on the tests. He gives you practice problems and if you do those the tests are not bad at all. Easy to make an A or B if you do the work. I would recommend him to anyone taking MATH 1502.
Class was not bad.

Great professor. He's fairly approachable, and is willing to explain concepts over and over until you understand them, whether it be during lecture or office hours. He often makes amusing jokes during lecture. Tests and quizzes are fair. He gives out practice problems before tests, and if you master them, getting an A is achievable.
Great teacher! Very clear and helpful in class!

He was really funny and clear in his lectures, his accent isn't terrible. Tests are fair! Quizzes are fairly easy, some are difficult. Homework is optional, but very necessary. He is one of the better Calc 2 professors to have. And this is coming from someone who was failing in the beginning and finished with an A, so that shows how great he is!

Pretty good teacher, but still a difficult class. He was really good about helping you if you talked to him, as well as answering questions during lecture. However, his tests/quizzes were much harder than most classes.
Best professor I've had so far. Very clear, great instructor. Tests are very fair and the class isn't so impossible to not get a good grade in. He's awesome both inside and outside of class!
Very helpful

Really helpful and funny professor. Apparently makes the fever joke across all classes haha. He would often modify his schedule at the request of students, reexplain anything, and always set reasonable expectations. Highly recommended.

He is very good. He explains the material really well, and he does so with a sense of humor. His explanations are fantastic, and he is always willing to help you. His tests are challenging, but not impossible, and there is an easy quiz every week. If you have the choice, I would definitely take his class again.

Awesome professor.  Easy to understand and he explains the material very well.  He has a pretty good sense of humor, too.  His tests are pretty tough and there is a quiz every week but they help prepare you pretty well.  As long as you do your homework and prepare for tests, there's no reason why anybody can't pull out a B at the least.

Provides pretty clear explanations, and has reasonable expectations on tests. Easy to understand and cares about doing a good job in teaching us. He's supportive and offers study guides, and quizzes each week are a great way to keep us on top of things. Also, good sense of humor... I've got a fever, and the only prescription is more Taylor Series!
Really funny, keeps class interesting, cares about students performance by providing study guides and office hours that are helpful
Awesome explanations, very funny. Great teacher.
Average at best.
He is funny.
Clearly presents information and is a very good lecturer

I don't know why everyone is hating on this professor. His class is actually so funny. He is a little goofy and loves to talk about all things GT but his class is SO easy. Literally all you need to know is read the articles for the week and only write two reports the entire semester. This class is so easy and he's so funny.
Loves all things GT so loves the athletes, but all in all a good prof who cares about his students
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Honestly surprised at how someone could talk so much but convey so little actual information. I learn less from the lectures than I do if I just read the slides myself. Sounds like a kid trying to give a presentation on a topic they just learned about 10 minutes ago.
Boring professor and very arrogant, talks a lot about himself. Likes to show a lot of attention to the female students. I would not take a class from him again.

I have had Professor Myers online during a COVID semester and in-person, and his in person lectures are awesome. Very interested in the subject and cares about his students. This course is basically reading and discussing cases and articles, in addition to leading a case discussion as a group and a final presentation. Overall, a good class.

He assigns a case study every night for homeworka rather lengthy one at that. Then goes over it in class at a high level but then expects you to know such specific details on the test. Tests are essentially all he grades on which makes it a very difficult class because the tests are completely unfair and cover material that was never mentioned.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Laziest professor I have ever had. Does nothing to help students learn. He posts a blank notes outline in which he covers maybe 60% of the notes through the semester. He gives very poor directions for assignments and then takes points off of things for the most meticulous reasons ans doesnt elaborate why. Dont take this professors class!

Hands down worst professor I have ever had at Georgia Tech, the professor goes on and on about random topics in class. In addition he has side conversations with individual students so it seems like he ignores half the class and it makes it super awkward. Definitely take another professors supply chain/IT elective if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kind of a waste of time and money. He doesnt really teach anything practical in this MGT3510 class. He essentially just goes over a lot of case studies as you have one every night for homework. The also gives you a blank notes packet to fill out in which he hardly covers any of the notes. Then on test days he asks super specific case questions
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Has to be the worst professor I had at Georgia Tech. He isnt a very nice person and has very little understanding of what goes on in students lives. His lectures are ultra boring as he goes on the incoherent ramblings that are just weird and awkward for the whole class. He assigns a case study every night for homework and his tests are so unfair!

Bob is a fantastic professor and does it because he loves it. He specifically designed the Process Innovation course himself, and it is essential if you are an Ops concentration. He is straightforward and gives you plenty of heads up for pop quizzes, and the group work/simulations are fun (you even use concepts you learned in class to solve them)

He's the actual goat. Recorded lectures, relevant homework, cool projects. Explains everything really well, very responsive, and tons of extra credit. Grade distribution is forgiving, if you learn the homework well you'll be fine on exams. Take home midterm, needed a 30% on the final. You will truly learn dynamics and not stress about the grade.

Great guy with good lectures. Multiple attempts on homework. Two big group projects. Open note take-home midterm, in-person final with cheat sheets. Both had multiple attempts for partial credit. Lots of extra credit available. Overall great class, fun projects, would recommend.

a great lecturer, learned a lot in class and its very clear he cares abt the students. projects and exams all have extra credit portions, everything is graded reasonably. hw is a bit difficult but he is very helpful during office hours and it is reasonable to what we are learning in class. great guy would definitely take him again.

one of fav profs at gt, great guy, hard class but explained clearly. very fair prof. 30% 10 hw 1drop, 1exam 15%, 3project 10% each but 1st is free, 2&3 use matlab. 25% final not cumulative. bonus on tests. has zoom link for class and records. only criticism: he talks quiet. you will actually learn dynanmics here unlike patil where its a free A lol
Dr. Deng is a great lecturer and seems to care about his students. Homeworks and exams were difficult, but feel like I learned a lot as a whole through this course. Recommend taking.

The class involved weekly homework assignments worth 40% of your grade, but he takes the best 8 out of 10. There are two midterms that are take home 24 hour exams. These are worth 15% each. The final exam is 30% and takes 2.5 hours in class. The textbook "Mechanics of Materials 9th" is not required but is very useful in the class.

He's awesome, made me want to do an econ minor. I think anybody who engages with the class and asks questions should be able to get an A. While he might come off as argumentative at times, he's really trying to get the students to think about the concepts at a deeper level so that they become more comfortable with application.

He is an amazing lecturer who is also very understanding and clearly just wants you to feel good about the topic. His exams are definitely more challenging than other ECON 2106 exams because he tests on applications not just concepts, but I think you get a far better learning experience.

Easy course. Grading relies on exams heavily but they're easy as long as you do the practice exams and homeworks on time. Generous EC opportunities. Required $70ish online textbook and homework system. Great lectures and slideshows, though exams are easy enough that it won't matter even if you skip a couple of lectures.
Fairly easy course and solid lecturer. Practice tests were similar to actual tests and many questions on tests were taken from achieve.
Such a good lecturer but his tests are hard.

Chill guy, has good examples in lectures and asks class for input. Lectures can sometimes get boring but he makes the content easy to learn homework almost every week but its not hard and helped me learn the majority of the content, plenty of extra credit. Solid professor who cares about economics, practice tests are super similar to actual tests

I thought I could get away with skipping the lectures bit it was almost 9% of my grade - I would've gotten an A otherwise. The class is not hard, the homework assignments can be tedious but there is extra credit. The tests are just like the practice ones he gives and he reuses the same format and types of questions.

Prof. Harris is nice but can be argumentative, and his lectures are often boring/hard to focus on. It's a solid class but covers a lot of material. Very exam-heavy (Midterms+Final = 64% of grade). The material can be tricky, so strictly memorize the practice tests—they are your best resource.

Lowkey not a bad or hard class. Really easy if you pay attention in class, but still manageable to get a good grade if you don't. Exams are exactly like practice exams and don't seem to change year to year.
Great professor and great lectures but the tests are difficult

Professor Harris is overall a good and caring professor who is very passionate about what he lectures. I personally thought midterms were testing on different material covered in the homeworks. You get what you put into the class. Overall, would recommend.

This class was okay. The lecture slides were extremely helpful, but the exams were hard. However, the homework and participation are weighted heavily, so it helps to boost your grade. Overall, I recommend taking this course.
Took for ECON4460. Great class and ever better professor. Make it engaging with his lectures. Especially with the pre readings we had to prepare for class. Would take a class with him again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I really liked professor Harris. His exams are tough, but the way his grading system works with attendance points and hw grades helps balance out exam grades. His lectures aren't the most interesting thing, but he explains everything well and expands on a lot of examples. Go to his office hours if you can- he does some good review before exams.

The material wasn't hard, but Harris overcomplicated it. Definitely do the extra credit and go to office hours if you're confused—he's more willing to help if you participate. He can be a bit sassy and likes to "argue" in class, which discouraged class discussion. However, he does reuse old test questions, so studying past exams is helpful.

Dr. Harris clearly outlines what you need to do to be successful in this course. If you're worried about your grade, I recommend doing the extra credit — he notices who does it. The tests can be on the trickier side, but he has very good practice tests accessible to everyone.

I really liked this class. HW was super chill and there is plenty of assignments to help grade. Tests are lowkey hard though so you need to study. I don't pay attention much in his lecture cause he goes off topic so much but I liked this class a lot. Note: he isn't a very approachable guy

Prof Harris is really passionate about economics and wants everyone to succeed. He tries to make lectures interesting but he speaks very monotone so its kind of hard to stay awake. Attendance isn't necessary but there are in class polls. All lectures are recorded and posted. There is extra credit and Prof Harris is very accessible outside of class.

Overall a good professor. He made microeconomics really digestible and although his tests were a bit difficult he prepared us pretty well I would say. Also, he comes off as understanding and relatable to us students. Would definitely recommend.

Professor Harris is extremely passionate about the subject. I found the lectures to be hard to follow at times, but he gave lots of extra practice to students for exams. Attendance policy is based off of accuracy on polls, so you might not get full attendance even if you show up to every class.

Not a bad professor at all, lectures are quite dry but he does genuinely care about the things he is teaching. The class gets more difficult later into the semester, but he is frequently available outside of class to answer questions. Attendance isn't taken directly but in-class electronic polls are used as participation grades. Curves most tests.

Poor attendance policy; you get points off for missing the questions, so it doesn't count for credit, which is unreasonable. But Harris really cares about his students. He gives resources for practice and offers plenty of help. Overall, nice guy and accessible. I find his tests to be a little more advanced than a principles course, so I struggled.

Great prof - clear course policies and test format. I personally found the course fairly easy but he curved the first exam and changed the weighting of the class to make it more fair for students who didn't do as well. Very nice person who seemed to actually care about his students.

Best professor I had all year.
His lectures cover the material so well, you don't have to read the textbook.
Participation and homework do reinforce material well.
Very interesting extra credit podcasts.
Asked him about some economic topic after class - an hour later he responded with well thought-out argument and a relating research paper.

wonderful prof. really cares about teaching and goes over lectures well. he changed weight of first exam because of poor scores. attendance is graded, but he gives many extra credit opportunities. very accessible-i email him questions about homeworks, and he responds with helpful detailed replies very fast. material/exams are fairly difficult

Professor Harris's lectures are really good. super engaging and explains everything at a understandable level. first exam we took was difficult but it's his first time teaching the class, so hes still learning how long to make exams. He changed the grade breakdown because a bad first exam. You can tell he really cares about teaching.

great professor, very caring, learned a lot from this class. Attendance is mandatory, but you only have to meet for like half the semester. The assignments are not too bad and are really useful. material does overlap some with ECE1100, but there is new material and she goes more in depth

All the materials have been covered in ECE1100. There is no reason for school to offer this course as required to earn students' tuition. The content taught in ECE1100 is more useful than this course btw.

They must've made this class even easier - there was only one take-home assignment and the rest were done during class. She is a very caring professor and the content is very relevant to anyone searching for internships/full-time jobs.

Extremely caring professor.  Class is the perfect difficulty for a 1 credit hour pass/fail required class.  Actually learned a lot and enjoyed every assignment.  It was perfect for what it was, and she is genuinely caring for your future as well.  Ensures you have access to her to get advise whenever and helps you without question.  Great teacher.

Professor Bourgeois is a genuine person who cares a lot about her students. She is insanely nice and wishes the best for everyone. That being said, the class was literally sitting simulator. Some cool topics and good information but there just really isn't much to it. Overall, eh class but really awesome professor.

A lot of people rag on this class because it's not engineering. They don't realize that her class teaches everything you NEED to know and probably don't know about interviewing, resumes, applying to jobs/grad programs, etc. Definitely take her class during your second year, first semester of CmpE to get a head start on internship applications.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof is super chill and easy going. Class is an easy A if you just do your assignments on time, which are straightforward and simple.

After the first two weeks, she didn't post a single thing. The syllabus said we would have class in person, but she has been completely silent for two months now (except for one announcement). I asked friends if I was missing something because nothing happened. The GTA's are active, but absolutely no lecture or interaction with the professor.
Good teacher overall and pretty cute.
She is full of herself and believes her work and teaching are actually important.
Good prof
No Comments

She is so sweet and does her best to make people participate and learn. The phonetics unit is rough but it's an interesting class once you get past that. Tests and homework are open note but long and pretty difficult, though she gives great explanations for why you lost points. If you want an easy, mostly interesting humanities I highly recommend.

Everything is open note but exams are BRUTAL. They take hours to complete, especially the last exam, which has essay, analysis, mcq, T/F, etc basically every type of question in existence. Wish she made shorter exams or did different assignments to test all of this, instead of these long time-consuming exams. Material is kinda difficult & annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Easy humanities credit. My only issue was that she didn't enter grade till late in the semester.
Dr. Kim was such a nice teacher and her class was easy with a little effort. She always responds to emails and cares a lot about her students. Put in the work and it's an easy A.

Dr. Bo Kyoung Kim was an amazing professor for linguistics. Her interest in the subject made classes more interesting and engaging. Assignments were fair; all exams were online; in-class quizzes were quick and given enough notice for preparation.

Pretty interesting class and she is a lenient grader. There's translation and speaking homework every other week or so, which can be time consuming but she is flexible when turning assignments in. She gives a lot of feedback and marks what points were taken off or given back. She does tend to grade everything at the end of the semester.

This course was possibly the easiest course I have ever taken at GT. The grade is entirely based on a few exams that take a LONG time. They are extremely easy, since you are allowed to use notes. Material was not very interesting to me, but it was to others.

Dr. Kim is a great professor! Although this class was online, she did a great job at explaining the concepts through videos and was always available to be messaged if you had any questions. She is a very fair grader and an extremely nice person. There are lots of opportunities for extra credit, and great CIOS. I highly recommend taking Dr. Kim.

Dr. Kim is, by far, the best professor I've had. She was extremely caring and answered emails quickly. I asked some dumb questions, but Dr. Kim always responded nicely and with patience. There were multiple extra credit opportunities and exams weren't difficult. She made me interested in what I thought would be a boring course. 10/10 recommend!!!
The professor is really nice

Good professor but her lecture videos had bad audio, but her lecture slides are good enough to read. Quizzes are kind of difficult, tests are online (no honorlock) and time consuming but fair. Overall good class, but the beginning content can be difficult if you dont try. Put like 30% effort into the class and you'll be aces.
Clear and straightforward video lectures. She was very thorough about the grammar and topics, and she gave really great feedback on my homeworks and essays. Highly recommend her.
No complaints about this professor.

Dr. Kim's lectures are great and engaging. She always starts off the class asking how everybody is doing and genuinely cares for students. The assignments were a bit challenging but were fair. Definitely take a humanities course with Dr. Kim.

I had literally no coding experience before going into class but found is really manageable. Lectures are recorded, so you don't have to go to class. I would recommend going to recitation and doing practice exams. Also there's like 2 points of extra credit added onto your grade at the end.

Very good lecturer! I can't emphasize enough how he is able to properly teach python in a way most can understand well. There are plenty of practice exams to get you through the tests and the homework helps a lot with them as well. The hardest part was figuring out how to do the webdev/robotics labs.

Although the course material itself was difficult, the lectures were very thorough. Attendance not mandatory, but sitting through lectures really helped a lot on the tests. TAs were all very knowledgeable and he was very approachable if you had any questions. Tests can be difficult but past exams were very similar. Very sweet!

rod is a great prof. he takes great care in his work, explains things very well, and is always open to questions and making sure you understand certain concepts. the only issue was the tests, which start off very difficult, but generally get easier as you become more CS competent.

I'm gonna preface by saying that I'm not good at CS, Rod was a decent teacher, he was quite passionate and funny and had pretty good lectures. For a GT requirement however, there was a lot of learning you had to do on your own that was not in the lectures, use the online textbook. Make sure you do the homeworks early and look at old exams.

Pretty good teacher!
I thought that the WebDev Lab was very useless and unrelated to the course content. I had to learn a lot of new, useless Python functions and syntax that aren't popular and used in other courses. 
The tests got a lot easier as the course progressed. 
The homeworks were good- make sure to do them!

Rod is awesome! His lectures are effective and interesting and really helped me to understand the material. He is also always willing to answer questions on homework, labs, etc. before or after lecture. Overall he is a great, caring person and does an amazing job of teaching this class.

very energetic and fun professor. the lectures aren't that difficult to follow and the homework is related to class content. personally, I felt like the lab was unrelated to class and forced me to learn a lot of syntax on my own (web dev track). exams seemed to get easier as the semester went on

Rod is a great lecturer; he makes the concepts super easy to understand. To get a good grade, go to lecture and do all the practice tests. Also, the TAs will be ur best friend in this class, so make sure to go to the helpdesk if you're struggling.

Enjoyable professor with fun lectures. Exams are similar level to the practice exams given by him. Labs were decent but they felt unrelated to the content of the class (was on web dev track). I did take this class already knowing Python, so difficulty level might not be accurate for a true intro class.

CS1301 isn't a real intro. Rod goes way too fast. Labs and TAs are awful. Never take robotics. They claim it's easier but it's hell, with async topics that don't belong in an intro. No lab help, TA helpdesk is slow and rude. Grading is sloppy, robots are disorganized. This class made me cry. Never again, made me reconsider my major as an EE.
I LOVE ROD SO MUCH. Great professor. Even as someone with no coding experience before the very first day of class, he made the content very digestable and simple. Definetly take him.

I really enjoyed this class! It is difficult to adjust to at first, but once you get into the swing of things it becomes more and more manageable. Make sure to utilize your resources in this class! There are so many opportunities to go to plus sessions or reach out to TAs, and it is totally worth it!

Rod is great. He's super funny, makes the lectures interesting, and codes with you instead of just talking and having you take notes the entire time. He is really easy to get help from and great at explaining how and why certain code does different things. Rod is the goat.
During lectures, he codes along with students for notes and has mini quizzes, which I found very helpful.

Rod was hands down one of the best teachers for 1301. He explained concepts really well and would explain it in different ways if someone didnt understand. The tests were really easy, just make sure to do the practice exams posted on Canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Rod is so kind and really cares about all of his students! The nature of 1301 can make it difficult to get TA help in office hours, but Rod was always available to help out. There is a good bit of homework outside of class, but really helps you prepare for exams. He wants you to succeed, so contact him if you ever need it!

This class comes with a lot of work - but Rod made the concepts digestable and made the 8am worth it. The homework and labs were tedious, but they definetly help you learn and cushion your grade. I also never got A's on the midterms, but got one on the final - his TAs and recitations are great too.
What an amazing professor and an ICON!!!!! Great guy, makes everything very digestible and less overwhelming. Amazing TA team as well. THANK YOU ROD!

I came in with 0 CS knowledge, and I feel like I've learned a lot thanks to Rod! He explains topics very clearly and slowly so that it is easy to understand! Some of the homework and labs were hard but it was helpful going to the helpdesk. I also recommend taking all the practice exams to study for the actual exams!

For an introduction class, it was very fun. There is a weekly homework and around bi-weekly lab due, but everything's done on your own time away from lecture. The lectures are very straightforward and, if you like Python, rather easy to understand. Mr. Rod's a great professor to have regardless though and all the TAs are so nice.

Great professor. Interesting lectures. Maybe I'm just bad at coding, but for this class, you MUST lock in. Go to every lecture. Go to recitation. Office hours were so bad because they never had enough TAs for everyone. Sometimes I'd wait hours during office hours for a TA to help me.
He was a great professor! The class was difficult in the beginning as someone with no coding experience, but I ended up doing well in the class.

Rod managed to make his lectures entertaining and highly informative. I failed the first exam only because I didn't know how to study for the class. Doing all of the past practice exams and attending all the lectures will set you up for success. I was able to end with an A after learning how the class was structured. Also attend recitation!

Rod is a really nice and approachable professor. He was very good at explaining the beginner CS concepts in the course, and we coded alongside him in lecture. However the course is really fast paced and important to keep up with (at least for a newbie to python and CS). You should make sure to work on the homeworks early.

Borela is super enthusiastic and really nice. His 1301 course is probably one of the best ones to follow along because he really knows what he's doing. He gives all coding notes through actual python programs that you will type with him in class, which I feel does a good job at preparing you for the homeworks (helpful for tests).

I love this professor! He's great and super passionate about what he does. Very easy to talk to and is patient with you with questions. Also super engaged during lectures. Some homeworks are long but doable if you set the time aside. The TAs are also super helpful. It's definitely beginner-friendly if you've never taken Python before.

He is awesome!! His teaching style is learning by doing, and he gives good homework examples to do each week. Tests are timed, but he is accommodating and pushes you to do your best. Gives around 3 points of extra credit through relatively simple assignments. If you don't procrastinate on homework/projects and study, you'll excel in this class!

Amazing professor! Went into this class with absolutely no python experience and ended up with an A. Does a very good job of explaining concepts. If you participate in lecture and do the Hws then you will absolutely pass the class with an A. Definitley recommend taking 1301 with Rod!
Lecture was interesting, great professor and makes it easy to be successful in the class. Labs and homework were a big time commitment.

I've never taken a CS before, and he is the best professor ever. His lectures were so detailed and engaging, and the homework assignments were at an adequate level. He also provides a lot of exam resources to help you ace the class.

Rod is such a great lecturer! He's so caring and funny, and genuinely made me excited to learn CS! Homeworks and tests are a little challenging, but the past exams should get you prepared pretty well.

Rod is a great lecturer. I believe his tests are difficult and completing them in 50 minutes is har. The TA's are very helpful for help but I do reccomend going to lectures as they help you code for the most part. There are three labs, and the third one is difficult for both lab tracks.

100% recommend! He is so good at explaining himself and making sure everyone understands. There's plenty of exam prep material and review sessions, and the exams align really well with homework/in class examples. TA's were very helpful in office hours too. If you want you can skip lecture and just do the in-class quiz during that time.

Good course that gives you a nice basis on python, but I hear that it is more heavier in terms of content than the online sections, but I learned a lot. Lots of TAs but they get backed up especially during just before deadlines. Tests are all paper coding.

Great professor. You get to code along with him during class. My favorite part of the class were the labs (I had web development). You have the labs, homework's, mini quizzes in class, 3 exams, and a final. The exams and finals were just like the practice ones. The recitations were helpful but optional.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best 1301 professor. Very engaging in lecture and his HWs, while hard, often felt more like interesting puzzles to solve rather than terribly egregious assignments or anything like that. Definitely take this class with Rod over any other 1301 professor!

There is really no reason to not pass CS 1301 with a professor as great as Rod! He is awesome, down to earth, and personable at all times. This class was an amazing introduction to programming, and it had dynamic and unique homework/projects. Please just go to class and pay attention and you will do great! :)

Rod is just about the best professor I could have asked for! I have never taken a CS course before, but he made the material engaging and understandable. His lectures were thorough and he explained the "why" of what he was doing very well. He is also hilarious and incorporates pop culture into lecture! Take this course if you can, it was a blast!
WE LOVE ROD!!! Literally best professor for CS 1301! There are also so many extra credit opportunities, he genuinely wants his students to succeed.
Great professor! Very clear lectures with lots of walkthroughs and examples. He cares a lot about his students and it shows. Tests are a little challenging, but if you study you'll do fine.

Rod is literally the best CS1301 professor there is. If possible take him for this class! His lectures are so clear and he thoroughly explains all the concepts in great detail. He is fun and engaging and even dresses up in costumes for the exams. This was my first CS class I've ever taken and I was super worried but Rod made it easy and fun!

Really good professor. Gives good lectures and does a good job of test prep, theres a little EC too. Only thing is there are a lot of gotchas on tests and labs are a good bit of work. Homework typically is time consuming too. Best 1301 professor. TAs are also amazing for this course too.
Excellent lectures that were easy to follow and made sense. Homeworks made great use of what you learn. Extra lab sections were a fun application of concepts, but organized somewhat poorly.

Clearly understood what he was teaching, explained not just what to type, but what Python was actually doing in the background. Clearly passionate about both CS and being a professor, fun guy, not too hard of a course.
Nice guy that actually talks about how the code works instead of just telling you what to type in the file. also didn't show up much because he has extensive notes online

Best teacher ever. Very kind and understanding, especially in summer. If you're struggling to understand, try not to focus too much on note-taking but rather on the actual lecture (it can be difficult to try and keep up while understanding material). Midterms can be daunting, but if you practice well enough and know the exam layout you'll be fine!

I love Rod. He is very soft spoken and kind. He is a really good lecturer! He is always super helpful. You can definitely pass with an A if you do the work, study correctly, and go to tutoring. He's awesome!

Probably the best professor I have had so far. Very engaging and breaks things down into easy steps. Plenty of chances for extra credit as well. All the midterms were themed, which made them not as daunting.

Very funny and very kind. Lectures can be slow but works out when topics get tough. HW can sometimes take a few hours but aren't too bad if you ask for help early (help desk, TA's, friends). I thought this class was very easy and straightforward. Tests can have trick questions but have fun themes. Easy if you look at practices and go to review.
Amazing and clear lectures, homework takes a while but you learn A LOT! Really awesome intro to CS class overall.

While the professor is a very nice guy and is willing to help, the course is not great at all. Unless you are already familiar with python or a computer science major this class is NOT for you.This class unfortunately is more in favor of those students. Understand your learning style as well because his teaching style may not be your learning style

Prof Borela is a really good lecturer, as a cs beginner, going to class really helped. He's really caring to his students. The only thing that stressed me out is the robot labs. DO NOT register for small sessions because you don't want to work on robot labs for like days and hours. Start HW early because they're hard too.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great professor, really cares about his students. Highly recommend.

The material gets piled on very quickly and although Borela is knowledgable, it can be hard to follow along during lectures. Homework assignments are often incredibly time-consuming if you don't have any prior experience with Python. The midterms themselves are usually way too long(9-14 pages) and you will struggle a lot to finish in time(50 min).

This is an intro class, and that's how he treated it. He would add lots of light hearted jokes and personal things into the code that made it more interesting, especially since I was taking it at 8:25 AM. He is a great lecturer and always posts his recorded lectures online. There is a participation grade, so go to class to ask questions.

Rod is an amazing lecturer for beginners in CS! He makes sure his students understand the material he's going over and takes time to reinforce material if needed. Definitely recommend for people for little to no CS experience!

Dr. Borela is really helpful and is very willing to help students outside of class. He broke CS 1301 down very well in a way it was easy to understand. Homework assignments were easy to do if you knew what was going on and tests were easy if you did a reasonable amount of studying and paid attention in class.
Good professor with understandable lectures and examples. Accessible after class at office and sometimes TA hours. Class is easy, just make sure to prioritize deadlines and pay attention in lecture.

Hw took a while and wasn't easy, but it is doable and is great practice for the tests, which were usually easier. Tests covered everything learned in lecture plus a few minor things, so make sure to go to recitation to fill the gaps.
Very kind and thoughtful towards students, notes are clear.

Rod is an awesome teacher, especially for a beginner CS class. SUPER thorough even on "easy" topics and loves to engage students to make sure the class completely understands. Homework can be pretty hard but really helps with your understanding of materials and TAS are accessible. The robot labs sucked though. Don't get a small section if you can.

Amazing, caring professor that has great lectures. Covers all content clearly, formats everything well, and has previous exams posted online that are extremely similar to exams in class. Great class bc Rod is an amazing person above all. Take him.

Rod was a very good and caring lecturer! He teaches pretty much everything you'll need for homework and tests. I did have some prior Python experience but this class wasn't bad at all and I would definitely take him again.

Rod is an amazing professor in lecture. He tries his best to answer whatever questions people have while there, and makes learning Python fun. The homework is much more difficult than the in-class examples, but going to recitation will help immensely. The first two labs aren't Python, but allows extra credit. Watch out for the tests.

Borela is good at teaching stuff in lecture, but the issue is that homework assignments--especially later in the semester--are more advanced than what he showed us in class, so you sometimes have to teach yourself python to do the homework. Also, make sure to register for the larger sections since he gives harder labs to the smaller one(s).

Pretty good professor for ML, he tries his best to make the complicated material easier. Lectures are pretty packed with content since it was summer. There's open note quizzes after each lecture (not too hard), a big group project which is kinda hard but he grades easy. Homeworks are kinda hard, but just start them early and you'll be okay!

Dr.Borela was a great professor, he would do hand tracing and hold live paper coding sessions for students who were confused. Make sure to stay on the deadlines of assignments and ask any questions you are confused about and you will do well.
Great guy but does really hard problems that are so difficult to understand because there isn't sufficient explanation.

Took Borela's CS1371 in Fall 2021. A great teacher who puts a lot of effort into making his lectures are effective and include plenty of examples. He really just seems like a chill and fun guy teaching MATLAB and I enjoyed just vibing through his class.

Prof borela was a really good professor. i took this course over the short summer semester, so it was kind of squeezed, but he did his best to make it work. in lectures, he traced problems and did live coding which really helped. the final was also really easy and you don't need a textbook or any extra stuff
Super nice, taught the material very well, would definitely reccomend.

Loved this professor. He's always trying to keep students engaged and he is incredibly nice. He explains a pretty hard subject in an easy to understand manner. Super helpful on homeworks too, just start early and ask questions if you're stuck. Hands down the best ML professor at Georgia Tech. Take ML with him if you can.

Borela is an amazing man and really cares for his students. As someone who finished the course with an 89, you need to prepare yourself to score high on tests so you can skip the final. Borela just does really hard problems with little to no explanation, youre better off to skip and watch Kantwon or Stalworth's lectures online. TOO MUCH HOMEWORK FR

1371 in general is a course that relies a lot of lectures and volume of homework so be prepared!
Borela as an instructor was extremely caring about his class. I was worried because hes a new professor but he took our criticisms very well and changed the format of the class to focus on practice problems instead of solely theory to prepare you for HW

All around great professor!  I saw other comments about lectures being too quick, but he always took time to go over explanations and ask us if he needed to slow down when explaining a concept.  Tests were a tad difficult, but if you go to lecture and do the practice tests, you'll be fine.  He puts in 110% and if you try, you'll get that back!

Boreal is a good guy, but he is terrible at judging student comprehension in CS1371. At times, the majority of students would be confused and he'd just keeping moving through the lecture, while other times he'd spend 15 minutes explaining a simple idea. He also makes a lot of mistakes. I know he can do better, hopefully in the future he does.

Professor is an amazing person. However, the lectures were rough. He would walk through example problems without much explanation and would use functions we hadn't used yet, trying to explain them as we navigate hard problems. The tests were graded with lots of partial credit, which was nice. However, the homework and prep for tests were hard.

Rod is very sweet and cares about his students, and he is willing to change his teaching methods based on constructive criticism. However, his lectures are hard to follow and have weird pacing, and he isn't great at explaining code examples. I highly recommend going to recitation over going to lecture.

Borela is a silly goofy fun-loving guy. His lectures are great and the kahoots he does keep people attentive. This is one of the few classes I wouldn't skip because lectures helped a lot for homework and it was fun to listen to him in class. Don't assume the tests will be super easy like me and not study, you need to prepare with reviewing old test

He was an amazing lecturer, especially for people with zero coding experience. He was very patient with students and well-organized. His post lecture notes were also really helpful for revision because of how detailed they were. Highly recommend him if you have never coded before and are looking for an intro CS class to take.

Oh man this guy is great! I was scared at first because he was new, but he made the classes so enjoyable and very easy to understand. Classes consisted of lectures and then Kahoot's at the end of class based on the last lecture so it was really fun and engaging. On Friday's the first place person would always get chocolate as well!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Borela is extremely caring and makes it clear exactly what you need to know to do well. Lectures are organized and easy to follow. Going to lecture and doing homework will teach you everything for exams.

Professor Borela is very passionate about making his students comfortable and making the material as clear as possible. For my part, completing the homeworks on my own and attending lectures was more than enough to succeed in the course.
Bryce is the goat, great professor, easy to understand, willing to help, and truly cares about his students.
Bryce Truitt is tough on the exterior, but he is an amazing professor once you get to know him.
Hes literally the goat. He may seem intimidating or like hes asking for a lot, but hes literally the best instructor and will make you into a great architect.

Bryce is intimidating at first, but he is a genuinely caring teacher. Architecture is VERY difficult & his teaching style (moves very fast/leaves no room to catch up) emphasizes that. But, if you put in the time, GO TO OFFICE HOURS & ask him questions, you'll be fine. There's only 10 assignments that make up your whole grade so lock in right away!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, don't be fooled by his tough, robotic exterior, he's a true sweetheart, cares a lot about his students. If you're willing to put in the work he'll work with you and make you incredibly successful. Difficult to understand his vocab at first, but you become accustomed to it and truly learn a lot.
Show up to class. Do your hw. Hard, but not impossible. I learned a lot.
He talks like a dictionary - you cannot understand him at all and he grades unnecessarily harshly.

Soft, squishy professor under a cool, detached exterior. Great at teaching; explaining concepts in clear, concise manner. Reasonably understanding about late assignments and exceptional circumstances. 

If you show a genuine dedication to your learning, he will match you.

Make sure to show up to class. Class is just walking through the homework assignments step by step. I learned a lot. The assignments are not something to procrastinate. He is intimidating/ AI-like at first, but he's pretty chill and is very helpful and understanding.
A little off-putting?

Prof. Zhu is a great lecturer who does a really good job of breaking down difficult concepts. He's clearly passionate about what he teaches, which makes lectures enjoyable, and he also offers Zoom options and recordings. The class is well structured with eight projects, a final project, and two online, open-note tests. I recommend taking his class.

Dr. Zhu is a goated professor. There are 8 straightforward programming assignments, 2 open-note take-home online quizzes, and the class overall is great. He's super knowledgeable and clearly knows his stuff, if you can take him for graphics, 100% do it

This class has 8 super easy hws, 2 medium-difficult quizzes (depending on whether you studied hard or not), and a final project. I expected this class to be difficult or take a lot of my time, but it was honestly so chill. The instructions for the hws are very straight-forward and clear, and I never got stuck at all. Bho Zhu loves what he teaches.

Took undergrad AI graphics (4803) but it was identical to 8803. Probably one of the more interesting and fun classes I've taken at tech. Projects are very approachable and the course is designed really well, but brush up on pytorch and NNs before taking. GOAT Zhu and TAs are very helpful on Ed. Hope this class becomes a permanent media/intel option

One of the best professor I've had at Tech. Assignment for CS8803 CGAI where very well designed as they weren't to difficult but still allow you to really understand the subject well. 

There is a single quiz where you be good with by just reading the slides. Very active on ed discussion which makes him really approachable.
bo zhu the goat best cs prof at gatech

Honestly one of the best profs at GT. Very enthusiastic and very knowledgable about the content. Class has 8 very easy homeworks, 2 quizzes, and a final project. My only criticism is that the class is almost too easy imo. I wish it went more in-depth, especially since it's the main media class. Most content can be learned on learnopengl.

Dr. Zhu is the best professor I've ever had at Tech. He is an incredibly caring professor and genuinely passionate about his field of study, which motivated me to be passionate about it too. Grading is incredibly fair and the work matches what we learn in class. Overall a fun, inspiring, and uplifting class with the best professor ever.

I took this course in Spring 2024. It was by far my favorite class I ever took at GT. Bo Zhu was an AMAZING professor. He cared for his students and was very passionate about the topic. He was highly accessible outside of class and was genuinely wanted to get his students interested in the subject matter. I cannot recommend taking this class enough

Bo clearly cares so much about the topic and the students. He asks people to optionally post their graphics creations for each homework and then comments on and highlights the coolest features from each post. He is super supportive and makes the class as clear and easy to get an A as possible. Very accessible too, highly recommend taking his class.

Absolutely amazing - so wholesome. He is clearly passionate about the course and is incredibly kind to students and active on the class discussion forum. Exams are very helpful and the class is great, especially the lecture slides. All time professor

Great professor is very knowledgable about computer graphics and clearly cares a lot about the students. The way the course is structured means that it should almost be guaranteed to get an A in the class. He records lectures and has zoom on during lectures and sometimes it feels like he is almost teaching more to the zoom than the in personlecture
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: very good professor, every single coding assignment was motivated from lecture, genuinely helped you learn, that being said - start them on time since hard to debug, but AI tools exist so pretty easy imo. active on Ed, generous with deadlines, quizzes incredibly easy with ChatGPT, so easy 100 really
Professor Zhu makes this class a lot easier than it should be. As long as you pay attention - you're good!

He is a great prof! He makes the content for this class so easy to understand. The final is a group project which was great. The HW makes up 64% of the grade which is great since the HW's are super easy. The midterms were all open note and he gives great quiz prep that helped with the exams. I was worried about this class but it turned out great.
Chill class with extra credits. Dr. Zhu is really nice and TA's office hour are helpful with clear hints for any problem. Easy in grading. 2 Quizzes are all very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took Professor Bo Zhu's Computer Graphics course and it was an amazing experience. 3451 is usually known for being complex, Professor Zhu made it engaging and fun. He created an environment where students could truly learn without focusing too hard on their grade. He was always available via Piazza, so reaching out to him was not an issue.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Zhu is incredibly nice to students and gives kind feedback.

I have never written a review for a professor but Dr. Zhu really deserves it. This was my favorite class at Georgia Tech. He is clearly very passionate about graphics and is wonderful at explaining. He has been extremely accommodating and flexible when I needed help. Projects are alot of fun and you get great results! Take his class if you can.
Bo is an amazing professor! He is definitely the best CS professor I've had at GT. He really cares about his students and the content is very interesting.

Great professor for graphics. Projects are pretty easy and can be done in a couple of hours. Quizzes are open notes and are easy as long as you look through the practice test before hand. Projects are in C++ and OpenGL and all necessary formulas to finish the project can be found on the slides.

Bo Zhu is a wonderful professor. He's accommodating towards students and a great lecturer. He's passionate about computer graphics, and he's very kind and helpful. The homeworks are fair. Start early. The mesh subdivision homework is the hardest. For the tests, study the test review. I highly recommend him as a professor.

Very nice professor. Lectures were pretty boring, but slides were really good to study off of separately. HWs were long but not too hard, we also only did 3. Course is split into aeronautics and aerospace halves. The exams and HWs for the aerospace half are much easier. Exam grading was kind of harsh, also grading for HW and exams took forever.

Prof. German is a really nice guy, and his lectures are super understandable. That said, he can drone during lectures which makes them a bit boring as he goes through slide decks. Homework was infrequent which made preparing for tests and quizzes difficult (2 test + 2 quiz = 80% of the course grade). Would recommend over other 3330 profs for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely nice, and great professor to go to lectures for. I didn't and still ended up with a B in the class, but an A is definitely an easy thing to get if you put in the work. Horrible at responding to emails/canvas messages/piazza though.

German is a great professor for vpro. His lectures felt very easy to follow and understand. Probably the most well spoken professor I've ever had. HWs closely model what the tests/quizzes look like so it's easy to prepare for those. The class does focus more on aeronautics than spacecraft, but overall worth taking regardless of which you prefer.

It is clear that German is vey passionate and excited to be teaching vpro. He tends to drag out lectures but is very clear and enjoys expanding on things not covered by the slides. Exams are very fair but homework often involves a scavenger hunt. He is super nice, caring, and will answer any/all questions. He is such a girl dad and girl boss
One of the best profs I've had at GT. Clear and concise on course content and expectations. Has passion for course content and instructing. Will be taking his AE option next semester.

German is legit my FAVORITE professor at this school. He is absolutely the nicest person you will ever meet, and he lectures like he's babying the class, NOT in a demeaning way but in a charming way. The homeworks are very straightforward and tests are IDENTICAL to homeworks (literally just apply eqns!). Low stress but you'll still learn a ton!

Very understanding. I got sick multiple times and he allowed me proper extensions (I had documentation). Very clear lectures, teaches well. Tests fairly and hws are useful to prepare for tests. Students like him a lot. I've taken 3330 with Dec as well, German is the clear option for me. Shares his lecture notes (ppt). Not much practice besides hw.
Brian German is the biggest teddy bear and best professor at Georgia Tech within the aerospace department. Take his class if you can, become his friend if you can.

Had him for an options and I love the class. The passion for this material is quite evident in his teaching style. Dr. German is also very accommodating with the course structure, and it is clear that he just wants his students to learn and share this passion. He makes this class feel easy but at the same time I have learned so much!

The reason that Dr. German is so good is because he's really passionate about the material he teaches, and that translates to being able to teach it well. The things he expects us to learn are very structured (mostly Powerpoint based lectures) and he always backs them up with the wealth of practical knowledge he's accumulated.
Class was pretty easy just have to come to class and take notes

Very generous professor that genuinely cares about his students. The material is pretty difficult, so studying is definitely a must. I'd recommend this teacher to anyone, though. He's got to be one of the best on the campus.

Took this Spring 2024, was a really fun class very interesting. Class was made up of mostly discussion posts/research project, with one multiple choice test that's a bit tricky (basically pure memorization) but totally doable. Professor is really understanding and willing to help if you reach out to him as well.

This guy's the goat. Such an easy class - if you do the work you should not only pass, but get an A as well. His lectures aren't the most engaging but he always ends well before class is over. The whole last month is a project and we didn't actually meet once. We don't really go over the readings on the syllabus in class.
Professor Woodall is a great lecturer and would recommend! He gives great feedback and lectures are easy to follow. All courses taught by him follow the same format.
Passionate about the subject, loves questions and feedback, and sets clear, easy standards for assignments.

Really easy class. I took this to fulfill my social science credit and even without previous knowledge it wasn't that bad. Almost because there was very little homework, one test the entire year (20 question multiple choice), and the entire last month is a group project

I always enjoy Dr. Woodall's classes immensely. He's an extremely kind and genuine professor and gives interesting lectures that are actually engaging. The structure of his projects is straightforward and it's easy to get an A as long as you put a little effort into the class. He's hands down the best professor I've had.
I loved this class! The professor is a great lecturer and the class was very easy. The two bests were both 15 simple multiple choice questions. The projects are graded leniently.
Great professor, clear about how everything is graded and what he wants out of assignments. Not work intensive besides end of semester. Lecture heavy but fun and interesting lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Woodall's class. His love for what he teaches reflects on the way he lectures, and it makes class really enjoyable. One of my favorite classes this semester, 10/10 recommend.

Dr. Woodall is the best INTA professor Ive had. His lectures are clear and he provides a study guide for his tests. Hes had some super interesting experiences and met some unique people which he ties into his lectures. I definitely would recommend

Dr. Woodall is a fair grader, and this course was not too difficult, although it was online and taken during the Summer. I recommend taking his INTA 3040 class as part of the global development minor.
Easily the best professor I have had. He really cares about what he does and who he teaches. Do not miss out on any chances to talk to him after class, ask questions, or express a genuine interest

Such a sweet professor! Several of my classmates in his INTA 3203 (Comparative Politics) class all agreed that it was the easiest international affairs classes that they had ever taken. If you take the notes and study a little bit before each quiz, then you should be able to get an A. There were two projects which were very clear & straightforward.

Dr. Woodall is a great professor! His lectures are full of important information. Hes got a caring energy and hes very kind. And he really knows whats hes talking about. He lets us know the concepts that will be on the test so as long as you go through all of those, youll get an A.

This professor is so genuine. You can tell he loves what he teaches and hes a great person. Lectures are very informative, hes able to condense a lot of information into just what we need to know. Tells you what he looks for on the tests, and the tests are really easy. Take him if you want a laid back yet informative class.

You'll learn a lot - there is plenty of content, but don't worry about being tested on ALL of it, just the main points. This is truly one of the classes where you go simply to learn with little pressure, which is nice. Professor is also very funny and passionate about their class so it makes it very enjoyable. Would absolutely recommend
One of the greatest profs in the econ department. Absolutely loved him, highly recommend. Took him for ECON 2106, Fall 2025. Class was rigorous, but he was excellent.

Good professor throughout the semester but does not round ANY grades. Emailed him about being 0.03% percent from the next letter grade and he did not care. That's less than 1 extra point on any assignment so be sure to do all extra credit.

Made sure that every lecture was engaging and provided examples that connected concepts to daily life. Lots of extra credit, including for attendance, but tests counted for a large amount of your grade. As someone who had never taken econ, I found the textbook useful because some small test concepts were not explicitly mentioned in lecture.
Professor Brewer is very caring and gives great lectures in an accessible way. He builds a lot of time for questions into his classes.
super chill and gave us extra credit just for showing up. the content itself was sometimes hard to follow but you can tell he really tries to make his lectures entertaining
Lectures are hard to follow and understand.
Pretty chill guy.

Great guy, great professor. Brewer is a very relatable and caring professor while also being interesting and knowledgeable in Environmental Economics. Class was engaging. Had reasonably difficult homeworks and readings of economics papers. Very understanding if you ever needed a due date moved. Actually cared about his students. Take home tests.

Dr. Brewer is an awesome prof. I took him for Environmental Econ and moderately enjoyed the class. With lectures being 75 minutes long, I felt it got boring at times, and my attention waned as the class went on. The class is interesting enough, I like Dr. Brewer's lecture style. He's a funny guy and you can tell he has a heart. Take his class!

I really loved Dr. Brewer's class. You really learn a lot and very in-depth about how economists think about climate change. It is a very econ-heavy class and assumes you have a fair amount of knowledge of micro econ. If you find a good group of people to do the homework with and do all of the extra credit it is very feasible to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Literal king always does his best to put his students first and make sure they're getting the grade they deserve. Completely failed the first test and still ended with an A.

I took the grad level PUBP version of environmental econ. Only difference is the TA grades a tad harsher. Prof Brewer is a talented lecturer. He's very funny, light hearted, and welcomes questions. The midterm and final were take-home and open note, so go to class and take thorough notes. Highly recommend forming a homework group.

Failed the first test by underestimated the difficulty. Take notes and study frequently. He does everything in his power to make sure that you come out of the class with the grade you deserve. So many extra credit opportunities helped me end with an A.

Absolute GOAT, loved his lectures as he has a great personality and interacts with students a lot, even though the entire class is online. The online aspect also adds a lot of flexibility, as I could do homework earlier in the week. The homework is what I'd expect, but the class is test heavy with tricky questions, but take notes and you'll live.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Brewer is a nice guy who cares about his students but his tests were insanely difficult for no reason. I ended with an A surprisingly with extra credit but this class is super test heavy and homework heavy. I recommend taking a different professor if u can for econ 2106!
I would not recommend taking this professor. The exams are extremely difficult, there is a lot of homework, lectures are not helpful but you only meet for 30 minutes a week.

I took this course online in Spring 2022. Although there's a mandatory meeting, you only meet once a week for a maximum of 30 minutes. Basically, this course is design where you read the textbook, do hw from the textbook, and use the mandatory meeting to ask questions and concern with the class.

Dylan Brewer is a nice professor, but this is class is extremely difficult. The two tests (midterm and final) were extremely different from the homework (sometimes containing material not even covered in class), and he is not lenient at all with grading. His classes are interesting, but this is not an easy class to get an A in.

Brewer is a good teacher and very kind, but his tests are impossible. The class was mainly graded by only two tests, which had C class averages both times. Even with all high 90-100s on homework assignments, my 2 C tests left me at a B average. If you want an A, you cant breeze by for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The class consists of weekly textbook readings that accompany the homework. Online lectures are 30 minutes per week and attendance is mandatory (taken through polls). He gives two tests: midterm and final which are pretty hard (I got a B and a C on them) but he gives out plenty of extra credit so I was still able to end the class w an A. Not bad
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Brewer is awesome. Super funny and chill guy. This class was remote and he makes a point to keep the once-a-week mandatory lectures to 30 minutes exactly or less. We had to read one to two chapters of the textbook every week and there was both completion and graded homework. He offered plenty of extra credit. Overall great guy.

Professor Brewer's class is very chill. You do have to read the textbook by yourself and that is your "lecture". The mandatory attendance professor hosts weekly is not a lecture but more of applying what you are learning this week to the real world of the economy. 

\
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof. Brewer is great. Class was held virtually, where attendance was only required for one weekly session. Homeworks and tests were virtual and all open note/open internet, although some were a little challenging. You need to watch the lecture vids to succeed. Overall super nice guy, cares about his students, and super passionate. I learned a lot!

I had Brewer for online microeconomics. Every week, he had good, pre-recorded lecture videos, a learning curve assignment (graded on completion), homework (graded for accuracy), and a short online meeting. We only had a midterm and final exam which were kind of hard, but, luckily, there was lots of extra credit! He truly cares about his students!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: ECON 2106 with Dr. Brewer this semester was amazing. 30 minutes of synchronous class per week, and then the rest of the content could be covered at your own pace over the week. Though test heavy (60% between midterm and final), he gives out an incredible about of extra credit. Overall knowledgeable teacher, amazing guy, and chill class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Intro to Microeconomics with professor Brewer was a blast. Content lectures are recorded so you can watch at 2x speed. There's one mandatory meeting a week that only lasts for 30 minutes. Midterm and final are open everything and multiple choice. The final can replace the midterm! Plus there's extra credit that can boost your final grade by 3.8%.

Dr. Brewer's incredibly understanding of the fact that no one wants to be online for more than 30 minutes. The mandatory lectures once a week are never more than 30 min. The homework is open to collaboration, and all the answers are on Chegg. Tests can be difficult, tho, but are open note, book, internet. Just make sure you take the exams seriously
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great professor who takes class at a good pace, not a lot of material is covered, however theres tons of outside reading (which I didnt mind and found interesting). Class is easy if you understand basic calculus, and you learn a lot about how economists approach the carbon problem.

The best way to describe this class was chill. There's weekly homework but it only ends up being 2-3 hours a week in total, and we met up once a week for half an hour. The midterm + final make up like 60% of the grade, but they're open note/internet (they're still hard tho so don't be fooled).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Brewer is knowledgeable and very accessible to students to discuss class content and economics in general. Take this class if you are interested in economics and are willing to work hard.

Prof. Brewer is a good guy and very knowledgeable about the course material but I was under the impression that this class would be pretty easy and it really isn't. The tests are pretty tough and the homework varies. If you're looking to take this as an elective for an easy A, don't unless you really love economics.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was p a i n f u l l y easy. Dr. Brewer assumed we knew zero math or econ going into this class, which caused it to have a ridiculously slow pace. Even before covid happened I was baffled by how little content we had covered by week 10. Take him if you want a very easy A, but certainly not if you want to learn new things

I took this for T&M so my experience was different, but I'd be remiss if I didn't mention how good of a lecturer he is. It's so rare for me to actually feel refreshed after lecture, but Bob knows how to talk to an audience and keep 'em engaged. If you're taking this class w/him for T&M, don't be afraid. Bob doesn't bite.
I hope I don't have to take his class again.

GREAT professor. Tests are open book and easy if you attend class and copy down exactly any notes he writes down. Lecture isn't mandatory but important to attend because examples he works are almost identical to the tests.

One of the best professors I've had at Tech. It won't be an easy class, but he keeps it interesting/amusing and is very helpful. You can easily get a B, just not the easiest class to get an A. Not really the point, he's the kind of professor you want to take for the teaching, not the grade.
Whatever class he teaches, take it. You will learn a lot and enjoy it more than any other class through college.
FUNNY

Extremely helpful and entertaining.  Easily the best professor I had in my time at Tech.  I was amazed that he was an associate professor, and knew more and could teach more than the tenured professors.  Highly recommmended.
He was the single best professor I had in my 6 years at Georgia Tech.  Loved his class.  Absolutely loved it.
Good professor--relaxed class environment, knows his stuff, willing to help, and can be pretty funny.
No Comments

An extremely interesting class that was taught incredibly well. Every lecture felt like it gave new information and the papers were extremely interesting. Just be sure to keep up with the weekly readings as some of the higher level contents are on the exams. Group project is also pretty interesting and isn't too much work.
Took her course in behavioral economics. Very direct and teaches you what you need to know. Course expectations were clear and reasonable. Learned a lot. Lectures were also fun and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very test heavy but easy as long as you review the lecture notes. I would recommend going to class because she wrote on the whiteboards primarily. Truly a great teacher, still consult her for advice today

Took this class with her over the summer and it was an easy A. Dr. Buser a kind and caring professor who makes the class very straightforward. I would definitely  recommend taking this class with her.
Had Dr. Buser for Summer iGniTe Macroeconomics, class was interesting and engaging. Grading was straightforward.
