It's been 2 years after took professor Conte's class and I still find the class projects very valuable whenever I need reference for computer architecture.

Lectures are very interesting, and grading breakdown is in your favor. Basically 50% of the final grade is completely autograded with unlimited submissions, but the in-person demos can get you if you didn't understand what you were doing. Tests are moderate, homeworks are a little rough, but all-in-all, probably your best choice.

He has in-depth knowledge about the class. The TAs are the one who save your grade. Attend the recitation, since Dr. Conte tends to teach topics not necessary for the course. He is funny, understanding, and helpful. Head TA Jason was amazing. The projects require time, but very interesting.

I loved Conte's section - the grading scale was 50% projects, which are doable if you start early! The projects solidified my understanding of the material as well. Halfway through the semesters the lectures were disorganized, but HW, projects, textbook, & recitation are all you need!

Conte is a great professor and really knows his stuff. 2110 is historically a difficult course, but it is mainly the subject matter, not the professor. Also, his version of the class is easier than the Southern section in my opinion. His lectures are good most of the time, and the projects, tests, and exams are balanced. The TAs are amazing too.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Conte is the best professor I have ever had. He is an incredible lecturer, and he makes CS funny. Every Tuesday/Thursday I was excited to go to his lecture. This class made me understand why I pay money for college. I will never forget the Lecture on John Van Neuman. It was mind blowing and it changed my way of thinking.

Conte is awesome. Workload is much more manageable than Southerns section. I found that his class focused more on the lower level computer stuff and hardware, and less coding than Southerns, but both end up teaching the same stuff. His grading scheme is quite generous, with projects making up the bulk of your grade (projects have autograders).

Dr. Conte's class was great. I had heard that 2110 was the "first hard class" for cs, but it wasn't that bad. Projects (with demos) make up the bulk of your grade, and the autograder is provided. Tests were easy and only make up 35% of the grade total (10% for exam 1 and 2, 15% for final). Conte's lectures are funny and engaging.

Really good class. Everyone knows 2110 is super difficult but his format (5 projects, 11 homeworks, no lab quizzes, 2 tests, 1 final) allows for way less stress than other sections. Projects are do-able but will probably need TA support and make up for majority of grade. Tests are light work, study lab guides. Lab recitations are really helpful.
Dr. Conte is one of my most favourite professors at Tech. His lectures are engaging and homeworks help to understand concepts. Totally recommend him.

Dr. Conte is a real gem of a lecturer in the college of computing. Consider yourself extremely lucky to have him as a prof for 2110. The class is mostly project-based, but the course covers a ton of material. Conte himself is extremely witty, knowledgeable, and funny. Don't hesitate, he makes a hard course fun.

Electrons live in the ground! :)
Dr. Conte is an outstanding profesor. His lectures are fun and informative. Tests are fair, and projects are well-explained. TAs are very supportive and approachable.

I loved CS 2110 because of Conte! He's funny and I went in person just for his class. The class is much less stressful than Southern's imo, which I think made me like the subject even more. The projects were really fun and you have 2 weeks to do them and there's so many resources that give students breathing space considering this is a 4 cred class

2110 is a hard course, but I feel with Conte, if you follow his guidelines, it is easily doable. He has a pretty generous grading scheme with 50% being projects, and half of that being demos for projects, and the other half being code with auto graders. His lectures are clear, concise, and entertaining. Solid professor for a hard class.

Conte is the best professor I've had at Georgia Tech. He has a lot of material to cover for 2110 but he makes sure to follow his syllabus and covers everything effectively. Easy to understand as long as you pay attention in lecture. Just make sure you don't miss a lecture or it might be hard to catch up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Conte was a solid professor. His lectures were decently informative, and if you attend those plus recitation and review material with the textbook, an A is very achievable. There are a decent number of projects and homeworks, and a few exams were hard, but nothing unreasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The projects were challenging but fulfilling once you figured it out. Start on the first day that they get released so you can ask ta questions. There were some errors in the projects and malloc was hard in the final project but overall I liked them. The only thing I didnt like was that Conte wrote the tests and was a harsh grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class is very difficult, but if you like the subject material, very rewarding. He's one of the best lecturers in the school, but he's a bit of a hard ass when it comes to grading. The projects are very difficult, be prepared to work very hard, but also be prepared to learn a lot. Not an easy A at all, but one of the most rewarding A's.
He knows how the university evaluates a class. He knows weak points of a student. He knows how to secure a job.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Other class 9 credit <<<<<<<<< This class 3 credit The projects are extremely difficult, among the most difficult I've ever done. Notes and lectures aren't helpful. Do yourself a favor: take this class with another professor.
Recommend to take another prof.

CS 2110 is not an easy class, but Conte is a great lecturer and makes the material not only interesting, but understandable. Projects were difficult, and got more so as the semester went on, but as long as you get started early it isn't too bad. Lecture and office hours were more than enough to complete the work at hand.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very smart professor, he can answer any question you throw at him. He also relates lessons in class to the industry which was cool. You gotta show up for lecture because if you miss you will fall behind and he does not slow down; however, if you show up the class should be easy.
Don't take from him. He claims he is a fair grader and never actually listen to student's request. Lowest grade statistic among all professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ignore questions during class. Piazza is a place for TA's unjustified answers, never trust 100%. Requesting assistance? -> He will guide you to contact the office of division, while the office of division tosses to the professor again.
Well... Tenured professor with giving lowest gpa among the course. Low accessibility.

Dr. Conte is a fantastic lecturer and professor. However, the course was completely unorganized with assignments, parts of projects, grades, and missing details being released way too late. However, these things were out of Dr. Conte's control.
Don't take his class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He only the one that claims he has a reputation as a fair grader. Only worse course professor that I took in GT.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Also took during COVID. Conte is not a bad man, okay. He doesn't do malicious things and wants you to succeed. My main issue with his teaching is that he doesn't prepare lecture notes, at least not often. The guy is super smart which is great, and there probably isn't a question you can ask him he can't answer, but his lectures are improvised.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took class online during COVID. His lectures were detailed & interesting, and he's always eager to answer questions. He's enthusiastic and knows the material well, but sometimes he doesn't explain things great because it's so simple to him. Class took a lot of effort (especially projects/homeworks) and quizzes were hard, but an A is attainable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Conte is a good choice for 2110. His class is structured around projects rather than timed labs like the other sections. Projects aren't too bad, and they carry your overall grade. He's a good lecturer but going to lab is the best way to prepare for exams.

He's a pretty solid professor. I took his CS2110 class online (during the mostly online fall semester), so the class might not be all the same going onward. The class was mostly project and homework based, which is cool. I also got in the ungraded untimed lab section which was great. If you do choose this class, please go to lab and lecture.
Wonderful professor. One of the best I have ever had on campus. Don't miss lecture though as it will get you behind and that will make it hard to catch up!

Conte is a great person and great professor. He along with the TAs made this class quite easy. Overall this did feel much easier than 1332 and I wasn't worried about the grade at all. This was an experimental section so timing of projects is something they need to work on. Tests were easy and short for 75 min.

Very good professor. Homeworks and projects can be a bit of work, but never too difficult. Tests are easy. My only gripe is that Conte is too nice and answers every single question students have, which really slows down the class. Does not allow electronics, but lectures are decently interesting.

Conte is a pretty good professor, but 2110 is just a super hard class at GT. The tests are tough, but the projects weren't too bad. He is a good lecturer, but can sometimes come across a bit condescending to students.

The material is dense, advanced, and complicated. The projects are extremely difficult, among the most difficult I've ever done, and there's a strict no collaboration policy. Notes and lectures aren't helpful. The tests are average in difficulty. Do yourself a favor: take this class with another professor.

As he will tell you within the first week or so, Conte is "tough, but fair". My experience has mirrored that exactly. He is an insanely good lecturer, and also goes out of his way to make himself available for consultation to clear anything up. His projects are very time consuming, and difficult. His class is tough, but doable.
Great professor Did an excellent job of explaining topics to students. Everything learned in one class tied in really well with the next class. Skipping class will really mess you up though...
Interesting, enthusiastic, and brilliant!
Great prof! Very reading heavy and class was just discussion over what was read. 4 essays very light grader with good feedback.
This guy is the absolute goat ! I loved having him as a teacher and I hope everyone gets to take his class !!!!

MY FAVORITE TEACHER EVER. I am impressed every lecture with how knowledgeable he is. He is so engaging. There is a discussion post for every reading and a reading every class. 2 take home essays & a final project but he's a very very easy grader as long as you try. an A is very achievable if you are attentive and enaged during discussion.

Took Literature and Medicine with him, super cool topic and awesome professor. Very understanding and easy grader. Basically if you put a little bit of effort in and have reading comprehension skills and participate in discussion once, you'll get an A. The material was good, prof has some fun lore, sometimes a little boring but overall great lmc.

Loved Dr. Crawford's class, he is very passionate about the material and a really funny guy. Sometimes he would go on crazy and interesting tangents, which were my favorite. We had discussion posts for every class which were easy, 2 take-home essay tests, and a final project. Some readings were long, but definitely rec taking any class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Grade was determined by participation, two tests (essay style), and a final project. He's very accessible and understanding if you just email/talk to him. Sometimes he goes on boomer rants or drops insane lore, but it's really fun. He's passionate about the material and genuinely interested in our perspectives.

Dr. Crawford's class was my favorite this semester. As long as you did the readings and discussion posts, participating in class was easy (and fun!
Our discussions were so interesting).
We had two take-home essays about the class content, and one final essay about a topic of our choice. Absolutely take this class/prof if you get the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: he was so awesome! his classes were so engaging! there were a few papers sprinkled throughout the semester and discussion posts with every reading (reading every class) but he is worth it to have him as a professor. his class was fun because he cared our learning. can't wait to take another class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is truly so well spoken. The way he is able to talk for hours on certain topics really did amaze even with how quite our class was at times. The grading was super easy too, we had two take home essay exams, a final project, and weekly discussion postings on what we were reading! He made me very eager to learn more about our readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really a great guy and very approachable. Took him for postcolonialism and as long as you do some of the readings, keep up with the discussion posts, and don't write pure garbage for the essays, you should receive an easy A.

This man was born to be a professor. He is probably one of the best lecturers I have had at Gatech. Depending on the class, you will have to read a lot but it's 100% necessary for the tests and final project. For LMC2100, the tests were all take home essays and he was super lenient with grading as long as he sees that you understand the readings.

This is my second time having a class with Dr. Crawford and I'm so glad I did! He is very clear about class expectations, and chooses very interesting readings for both his Intro to STAC and Postcolonialism courses. He really tries to help you out if you're struggling and will give you feedback on tests that can actually help you with the next one
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Gives great lectures. Very engaging, very understand, overall good guy. Amount of work required for class was very reasonable as were the tests. Pretty easy A, interesting guy to get to know.
This man. Just take him literally best decision ever. He cares about his students and tries to get everyone interested in the material he's teaching. He's also hot (lol).

Really interesting and passionate professor. As long as you do your wiki postings, write okay essays, and nail character matching on tests, you're guaranteed an A. He really tries to give you a high essay grade if your matching isn't too hot.

Exams 5 questions each (final 10). He is a generous grader all things considered but he writes the exams to have a median of 75, and if the median is lower, he curves everyone's grades to get there. Lectures are not great, most skip.
Mid1: Mean 84 Med 91; Mid2: Mean 77 Med 75; Final: Mean 72 Med 70 (pre curve).

By far least favorite professor at Tech. Was very rude when I asked questions during exams, lectures were extremely boring and really helpful, homework was unnecessarily difficult. There was a problem he had to un-assign because he realized even he couldn't solve it. That said, HW grading was generous, and he curved exams when everyone failed.

Clearly very knowledgeable about combinatorics and seems interested in the material he is covering but is a very dry lecturer. Tests felt fair but tough, though that might have be because I already had some knowledge of the course material thanks to CS 2050.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's dry, but solid, starts from the basics on every topic, he once checked if we knew what a prime number was. You need strong math instincts for rearranging problems because he goes quickly there. Use his bundled notes, they're great, 100 pages of study material, jump around, study what you need. Runs his office hours like the navy, in and out!

Genuinely cared a lot about students actually learning and understanding content. Clearly knows the content extremely well and lectures off the top of his head over whatever topic he's going over. Very lenient about homework and with test grading (everything curved to 80 average). Tests are 5 pretty hard questions but it's all fair game.

I stopped going to lectures just because I could not follow along, his teaching style just didn't fit me. You need to focus more on learning the theory to succeed. Tough tests, lenient grader, and there are curves.  He seems interested in the topics though, just wished he posted notes after class, his canvas page was empty all year. Not tech-savvy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just take a different professor he can't teach, don't risk your grade.

You either love Croot's teaching or you hate it. He teaches very well, and helps students develop math intuition, which I liked as a math major. Dense material, so studying for 5Q exams is risky, but there are practice exams and kind grading. He seems very cold/stern, but i.m.o people judge him too quickly. If you care about math, take his class.

The way Dr. Croot teaches the class means you'll be self learning a fairly difficult math class. His exams also give super abstract questions that make sense as hw but are difficult to attempt in a timed exam with no outside resources. He doesn't upload any materials to canvas and there is barely any student support. Just take it with someone else.
Excellent lectures! Many inspirational topics while not making it super hard. Test composes of 5 problems worth 20 points each seem intimidating yet partial credits are always available.

just don't take this class, unless you're ready for really really hard tests that are completely different from homeworks and notes. absurdly hard tests; they're so hard he uses a curve to get the median up to 75.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ernie is the worst professor I've ever had. HIs lectures are extremely boring and hard to sit through, as he is a very monotone, and non-inspirational. In addition to that, he is demeaning to students and non-accessible. His tests are extremely difficult (Avg 2/5 q's right Exam 1). My best guess is that he is just trying to get fired from teaching.

croot is very smart but unfortunately not as good at teaching. the exams were much more difficult than prior semesters due to him changing the textbook used. just choose someone else and save yourself the stress
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Croot's section is unnecessarily hard. I took it since it used I heard it is doable with his bundled notes, but this sem he changed up everything so no material to help/practice (still gave us the notes which are kinda useless now). Exam questions are completely different and ridiculously tough. Pls take another professor, you'll be less stressed.

Croot gives dry, difficult to follow lectures. He provides practice problems and past exams with solutions. When I took him, he changed the textbook used, so all past exam questions were very different from what was on ours. Final grade is replaced by final exam grade if it is better than your final average. Very difficult class overall.

Professor is very skilled at his field, but doesn't realize that the undergrads taking his courses aren't. The entire hurdle with this class is the exams, for which he releases practice tests, but they have solutions that aren't really helpful (he skips steps in the solutions and it ends up more confusing than anything). Wouldn't risk it tbh.

Horrible professor. Almost all lectures were scrambled as if he was hung over or really just did not care about us understanding a thing. Studied in groups for exams based on homeworks and exams were never related. Averages for midterms were always lower than 70 and the exams returned have no indication of what we got wrong, just the overall grade
Solid professor. Thats all.

Homework are bi-weekly and are textbook questions, which means you can study the textbook to finish it without go to the lecture. I don't like the textbook, but the Gatech Math 3012 youtube videos are really helpful. He gives lots of practice problems and practice tests. Very inclined to give partial credit on tests.

The class itself is decent. HWs are biweekly and aren't too difficult. The exams are difficult but Croot is lenient on the grading. Plus, if you get a higher grade on the final, the final replaces your final grade. The lecture is pretty bland though.

He's fine, a bit uninspiring. He has this set of practice problems which most test questions are based on, so tests are straightforward. His lectures are extremely dry and he's basically repeating the textbook. The textbook is pretty good though, and if you take the time to read / study it you'll get an A. Imo, try to take it with an easier prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Croot is a great mathematician, but that means that he is sometimes unable to explain concepts in an easy-to-understand way. Gives lots of practice problems and practice tests. Very inclined to give partial credit on tests
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Croot is a smart and knowledgeable professor who is very monotonous. If you are a smart student who is interested in learning in any capacity you would appreciate having him as a professor. While he does gets annoyed during exams, this comes from students asking for clarification over and over again and are in general not listening or learning.

Very straightforward math professor, practice problems from the textbook and handwrites notes on the whiteboard. There are no lecture notes posted so don't take the morning class if you can't wake up! The exams are 5 questions and can be tricky but not bad if you go to lecture. The final exam avg was BAD but was curved a lot.

Croot's class is basically all lectures and he does not post any lecture notes online. During lectures, he is usually just looking at his laptop and copying down stuff on to the board. His explanations are mediocre at best. His tests are much more difficult than the HW. People say he grades easily, which is slightly true but still not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor who provided a lot of insight into Number Theory. He is very intuned with the Number Theory community. If you complete your homework you will do just fine. His exams are usually short and contain two easy, two medium, and one hard problem. Don't be surprised if you never get a 100, but you will learn a lot at a deep level.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures are a bit all over the place, so I never went. However, he grades the exams super generously, and you can do well in the class by only studying from the textbook prior to exams. He curved me from an 87.5% to an A at the end of the semester without me asking.

I heard MATH 3012 is one of the most infamous classes in the CS curriculum, however Dr. Croot made it extremely enjoyable. He gives you a ton of practice questions from past exams. TAKE IT WITH DR. CROOT!

Solid professor. The best part is the huge safety net he gives you. Plenty of practice problems and previous tests that you can use to see what the test is like, as well as detailed answers to boot. The class is hard, there is no getting around it, but I think he does a much better job making people feel more confident than a lot of math teachers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He taught, the concepts made sense to me. A very no-thrills professor, but an effective one. Does get a bit easily annoyed though. Also grades pretty fairly.

Dr. Croot is not much of a lecturer. I thought this class would be a breeze as I have experience with combo, and I still had to study a ton for the exams and often was lost in lecture. I would not recommend him if you don't have an extensive background in this type of math. He is pretty lenient on grading exams, but the questions are no joke.
He clearly understands combinatorics and has a passion, however if you do not already know combo... don't risk taking his class. He teaches as if you have already mastered these concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's somewhat reasonable, but doesn't particularly care about his students. His lectures are so hard to get through and so confusing. His tests are very difficult to actually do, although he doesn't grade too harshly.

Professor Croot is decent. While he is definitely interested in the subject matter, he gets annoyed easily, especially with respect to tests. He explains concepts well and answers any student questions, but isn't very accessible outside of lecture and OH. Tests are difficult, so I recommend studying well in advance. Overall, decent professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Croot is excellent. The grading criteria is very generous, your entire grade can be replaced with only your score from the final exam. No matter if you're someone who learns in class or learns on your own, you should be fine. Dr. Croot is also a very interesting person and has a lot to say about mathematics in general if you're interested.

Croot literally couldn't care less about his students. He is there purely for research, and he really is a brilliant man and renowned in his field, but he can't teach at all. The saving grace of the course is that if you get an A/B/C on the final, then that can replace your entire grade. If you do take him, look up Trotter's online notes.

Very strong professor. Teaches fast, but that's because the course covers so much material. His lectures are super in depth, he works out everything on the board, and the exams are a combination of the textbook and his bundled notes online. Those bundled notes include 3-4 practice midterms for each midterm. Learn them well and it's an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't take this professor. He really cares more about not doing too much work than his students' understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor! He has taught the class multiple times and knows how to best do it. Great pace, not too slow and not too fast.

I remember how he said "iVe TaUgHt PrOdIgIeS aNd EvEn ThEy CoUlDnT gEt An A iN tHe ClAsS iF tHeY sKiPpEd" the first day of class. Too bad his class was at 8 and I didn't wake up early enough for his lectures. Read the textbook and do the practice problems and you'll be fine. Croot's a fun guy tho; you'll throughly enjoy his lecture(if you attend)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Don't do it. Just don't. Don't think you're special and be able to to outsmart these reviews. I literally had 2 tutors for this class -- Clough 1-1 and OMED. The LA is also helpful. But he was only available on Thursdays so that was a bummer. Croot curves all tests to 75, including final. hws are curved to be 90s or above. but still don't do it.

Lectures were extremely dry, and he was very bad at listening to questions and helping students understand. Both he and his chosen textbook made the material more difficult and boring than it needed to be. Very laid back about missed classes/exams. Often claimed that his brain couldn't function properly at 8am as an excuse for mistakes he'd make.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Croot could not possibly care less about the fate of his students. He spends his lectures reading bullet points off of his phone, rewriting them on the whiteboard, and then waving his hands and saying "So obviously, this is trivial." The book isn't incredibly helpful, but it at least points you in the right direction for figuring out what to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hard professor. Teaches in theory, relies on TA's to work through examples. If you get lucky with a good TA and you really understand Linear Algebra its possible to make an A. Studied for over 24 hours for the final and still made a high C on the final. Final grade was a B. Not the best but if you get stuck with him be prepared to study

Did a pretty good job of explaining difficult concepts, though he does talk somewhat to the board, so it's better to sit near the front. Reasonable tests and not too proofy, but the homeworks are long so get started early. Seems pretty passionate about what he does
He was a nice guy, but not a good professor, he didn't explain things well and his tests were extremely hard

very difficult instructor. lectures are hard to understand because he talks toward the board and very fast. ta's arent helpful either and tests and quizzes are VERY hard. very theory based tests. final was rediculously hard.
No Comments
Decent lectures but is an ass for the most part. Doesn't want to be bothered outside of class and loves to talk about how busy he is and doesn't have any time to help you.

Dr. Cross is genuinely not a professor. She did not teach our lecture section ONCE, just got up to preach about wellness and "doing what we've been doing". Only reason I'm not rating a 1 is because the TAs pretty much teach the course anyways, so it doesn't affect much. Homework and quizzes are difficult but if you study with a group its not bad.

Had her for BMED 1000 and it was fine. She is kind of mean and not very understanding. I interacted with her minimally since it was just a 1 credit class, but I would not take her for an actual class.
literally any other professor is better.

never showed up to class, and when she did it was to tell us to practice mindfulness, eat, sleep, and preach condescendingly to us about the course material. She does not know anything about the material. I asked her a question and her response was, "think about it." Im sorry, what did i take this class for? TA's make or break the course

Dr. Cross appeared to be a nice person but if I'm being honest, she didn't know anything in regard to BME. If you asked her a question, the first thing she would ask you is if your question made common sense, which is not something that I want to hear if I asked a question. She also shorted us on time for the final exam by an hour. Don't recommend

Ok so Dr. Cross isn't terrible. She just...wasn't really there. Only take her class if you're comfortable self-teaching 99% of it. I hear GT is making improvements to BMED 2110 for future semesters, though, so it might get better than it was for us. Her biggest mistake was giving 1/2 the class only 2 hours for what was supposed to be a 3 hour exam.

Dr. Cross lacks respect for students, dismisses feedback defensively, and doesn't provide the necessary support for learning. She also yells at her TAs for teaching students (when she doesn't) and has made comments about having to prove yourself as a "woman in STEM." Also mandates mindfulness exercises after administering unreasonably hard quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Holy moly, I made an account for this website just to let you guys know about the biggest mistake I've made in my entire life, taking BMED 2110 with this teacher. PLEASE Take my warning seriously, she takes pride in having a completely different teaching style than the other sections, this means no practice quizzes and no lectures. BEWARE!
Stay away from her, I would ask her a question on a worksheet and she would give me the wrong answer.
Please avoid if you can.

She teaches condescendingly to the students in demos and randomly chooses students to rephrase answers. She spent so much time on the teamwork aspects of 2110 that she quickly went over the actual important information. She is always more than happy to make pop quizzes as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She likes her authority over the students and makes sure to exemplify the "power" she holds. In essence, she treats her students like elementary school students and has them repeat things back to her and such. Her lectures were vague, confusing, and made me wonder if she was even knowledgable on the material. Do not take her if you can avoid it.

This course is great if you need an easy A humanities course. I took this course online over the summer, and it was async and ended in the first week of June. There were three exams and one paper, which can be exempted if you get 100s on all three exams. Crotts was very caring and lenient, and he provides all the material you need to ace the exams.

One of the most easiest class at GT if taken online. The classes is comprised of 3 exams and 1 paper, all of which are really easy. The summer online class is asynch and self-paced. All the resources to do good on the exams are provided in Canvas. The research paper is extremely light and templates are provided as guides. Extremely recommend!

Took MUSI 3630 during the summer semester for my humanities credit. Best humanities to take. Very interesting (especially is you love music) and easy to follow in a such a fast-paced semester. Crotts is super understanding, very helpful, and very accessible. Would definitely recommend if you want an easy, interesting GPA booster + humanities req.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: did maymester. great experience. one of easiest hum credits. 3 tests 30% each. if you get a 100 on them he lets you skip the 10% report. easy tests, easy grader. only con: tests are 3h long, class feels tight bc its only 3wk. but i still rec it and take it w another early summer async class for easy credits speedrun. very interesting + awesome prof
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Take this class!!! Great option for Humanities credit. I took the Maymester version, and the tests were easy, the professor was excellent, and the overall curriculum for History of Jazz was solid. 10/10 would recommend.

Take this course! Took it in May Asynch - this was such a chill and fun class. Dr. Crotts is accomplished in the field, super knowledgeable, and very chill. Exams are easy and straightforward. You actually learn a lot - I remember recognizing a jazz song playing in a cafe after this course. You get an excuse to listen to jazz, need I say more?

Took the Maymester async class. Lecture slides were straightforward & conveyed information needed to do well on the exams. Lots of memorization but relatively easy. Exams were very simple, no trick questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TAKE THIS CLASS!!! I took this class async as a Maymester course for 3 weeks and I 100% recommend. 3 tests and 1 paper. The tests are very easy and all the info can be found in the lecture slides. This class was very easy, interesting, and overall enjoyable. Crotts is a greater lecturer and even though it was async I still learned a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have the right mindset you will love this professor. I took him for granted until I started moving up in the Fundies courses. Grading is very dependent on the TA for Musi2010, but Prof Crotts can be very helpful with suggestions and/or guidance for your work.

The only grades for his MUSI 3630 class are tests and a final paper. The tests are extremely straightforward with details from the lecture videos he posts with extremely broad discussion questions. The tests are mostly common sense and he gives credit for a variety of answers on short answer questions. The final paper was graded very easily.

MUSI3630 was a course that I loved supremely. Because it was a maymester course, the span of time we'd cover in a week often spanned giant steps, but the asynchronous structure made it convenient to catch up on notes even while out to lunch. No prior music theory knowledge is needed, making it a perfect maiden voyage into the world of jazz.
Easy humanities credit. Non-mandatory attendance. This man really respects his students and has a passion for music. Take this class.

Chip is super nice in and outside of the classroom. He has a great passion for Jazz of course and you can tell from his lecture. The class is really chill and very basic. You don't need any musical background to get an A, but be prepared to use the textbook a lot and maybe do some self-learning because attendance is not mandatory.

Wonderful class. Laid back instructors and interesting material. Bonus: we got out early almost every day. Great choice for a humanities elective or free elective during the summer. If you do anything in this class, you will almost certainly make an A.

Took history of jazz with Prof. Crotts over the summer. Class was taught either by him or his coworker friend. Tests are not hard if you memorize the slides. Content is really interesting and a nice break from these rigorous STEM classes at Tech. Highly recommended for that Humanities credit.
Probably the best teacher at Tech. The difficulty was great not too hard and not too easy. Easy A if you practice and work hard.

His content in ISyE 2027 was much more difficult than that of other professors. At the beginning of the semester I was doing horribly on quizzes and feared that I ran the risk of failing the class. Later on he started administering all of his exams and quizzes asynchronously and people obviously did better. Very disorganized but funny guy.

I know he gets a lot of slack and as such he was the last professor available for 2027. With that being said, the content is more difficult than other 2027 professors but if you look at his GPA you can see that it's actually the best professor to take. Be nice, show up to class, and he'll work with you.

Worst ISYE professor I've had so far. He doesn't use slides during his lectures, is very slow, and gets distracted easily. The average for one of the midterms was a 34. Takes a long time to respond to emails + the TA was never seen in person. He gave both an optional final exam and a final project, which he barely gave any information on. Run.

Professor Tovey is an amazing conversationalist and genuinely cares about his students, but you will have to put in a lot of effort to understand the material. His pace is pretty quick and he doesn't utilize any lecture slides. He also gives you your Midterm & Final questions in advance and is really fair with grading.

oh where to start. he is one of the most interesting professors I have ever had. he gave us all of the questions to the one midterm we had (worth 30%) before the midterm, so I memorized the answers and got a very high score. he gave us chocolate in the middle of the midterm, too. he gets ticked off by random things.

He does care a lot ab his students (invited anyone w/o a place to go to Thanksgiving). Hardest exams I've ever taken, but content is directly from homework and the practice exams. Median exam 1 was a 38, but those students did not prepare themselves for the exam, and most cheated through the prereq material during covid.

This professor really deserves one star. The teaching style is difficult to comprehend yet unwilling to change, homework was difficult, the test was lengthy and ridiculous. If you are a genius and want some fresh air, you are welcome in his class. Else, RUN.

Horrible professor. I dropped the class after the first exam (which had a median of 38 in a class of 100+ students). Avoid this professor at all costs. Some people say he's caring, but he is flat out rude especially if you ask an "easy" or "dumb" question. Lectures, homeworks, and exams have zero correlation. Do not take this man!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took him in Fall 2021. Worst Professor I have ever taken. He is brilliant but doesnt know how to explain material correctly. Homework took HOURS to complete. The average of the first exam was a 38, and all he said was that we needed to learn how to solve problems better.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is nice and smart. He teaches well and you can learn much if you pay attention and ask questions frequently. However, the homework and tests are difficult, and only if you understand nearly all the materials he taught in the class can you secure an A because there is no real curve for the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Tovey is probably the smartest man I've ever met but the WORST teacher. 80% of the class failed midterm 1 with more than half scoring between 20-30% on a test with 10 points of extra credit. HUGE gap between lectures and homeworks/tests. The ISYE tutoring center, 1:1 tutoring, and TA's were not enough to help. Avoid at all costs

I wish I'd listened to everyone saying to avoid Tovey at all costs, please don't think you'll be fine even if you intend on working hard. Dr. Tovey means well, but he is incompetent at teaching a structured course at an appropriate difficulty. He WON'T prepare you well for his exams. Even tutoring services and TA's were unable to solve his homework

If you are given the choice of taking Tovey for a course or delaying your graduation by a semester, just delay your graduation. Median on exam 1 this semester was a 38, and there is no curve (worth 25% of final grade). He is way too smart to teach effectively and way too smart to understand what a fair test is. Avoid this professor at all costs.
Grading is late, announcements are late, revisions are not said and changed, and even class is the worst.
The smartest person I have ever met. He was a student of George Dantzig. Very cool experience learning from him.

If you can help it, do not take this class with Tovey. He is a nice guy but really doesn't seem to care about being clear or getting his ideas across in a way that the students can actually understand. He basically makes the lectures up as he goes along and nothing he says will relate to anything you can find on the internet so you're on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I do think he is a great lecturer, but his tests and homework do not reflect what we were taught in class (they're WAY harder). He doesn't follow the textbook whatsoever so try not to miss lecture or you will be completely lost. Only take if you are willing to fail things (the first test average was a 50...) but he does curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: best professor I've ever had at Georgia Tech. His lectures are very helpful and he is able to engage the entire class consistently. He barely gives homework, and the class is an easy A.

He is a great guy, one of the best lecturers out there. Honestly he is a very caring professor (no cap) and he does his best to accommodate his students' needs. May allah be with him in this coronavirus mess. 3232 was an interesting class and so was Prof Tovey.

This class is not an easy A, and was one of the hardest classes I have taken at Tech. However, Professor Tovey is one of the most intelligent, caring professors I have ever had. He truly wants to get to know each student, and if you try to do the same, you will learn that he is a really great person. I really respect Professor Tovey

If you're trying to get an easy A, stop reading and don't take Tovey. This class is probably one of the hardest you'll take as a second/third year; be prepared. If you're really interested in knowing the material and having a teacher who is truly interested in it, take Tovey. He made me truly love being an ISyE major. Plus, he'll make you chocolate

I went to his office because I thought one of my assignments had been graded unfairly. He threw a fit. He even said, "Don't push me, or I may explode!!" Then he patronizingly told me not to care about grades, because he (supposedly) didn't care about them as a grad student. I've never encountered a more angry, abusive professor. Please stay away.

Terrible professor. Yes, he's very smart, but so unorganized and unhelpful in class. If you show up to lecture or not it wouldn't even make a difference. Unable to reword problems/answers to make sense to class. Tests are extremely hard and are just made up questions that don't have any flow with lecture material. Hardest IE class taken yet.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Do not take AT ALL COST. His grading makes no sense and it seems like he doesn't even grade correctly. Just gives points where he wants. He makes up the questions for the tests, and the answers have no clear explanation or reasoning behind them. He just slaps answers together with no clear thinking. Ok class but bad professor.

There are good and bad professors and then there's Tovey. Literally the worst professor I've had so far. Not a good intro teacher to IE. Listen to the reviews and avoid AT ALL COST. Very disorganized, gives no partial credit, and should not be teaching at all. If you cherish your life and your sanity, you would listen to me and avoid tovey....

Class was always taught with higher expectations of students than he really expected - that is, tests were hard and then curving / extra credit saved the day. Final exam was absurd, didn't seem like the same course as the other tests. Prof was always available out of class and loved when students would meet in small groups to check understanding.
Nice guy, not the most clear or most interesting lecturer. Will help you out if you approach him.

He gives quizzes every Monday for homework. He's not the most organized, but if you email him for help he will be able to help you. Genuinely cares if you care. Tests can be difficult but he does give extra credit arbitrarily. *Exceptional* teacher with small groups of students.

This is the hardest class I've ever taken. I did not take AP stats in high school and I have no idea what is going on in this class. Every time I show up to lecture it feels like I've missed a lecture in between. He is very unhelpful and is often incredibly condescending to his students. Do not take 2027 with him or you're gonna have a bad time.

Smart professor , but teaching is not for everybody ! If you care about your GPA , don't do it !!!!!!!! Many students dropped this class because of the way it was taught . Expect ridiculously confusing problems and expect to get 10,5,20 out of 100 on your quizzes ! . (Did not get an A+)
Worst professor ever
If you haven't taken AP stats in HS , don't expect to get over a C in the class

Professor was unwilling to discuss or move assignment dates, frequently released assignments late, and didn't post lectures after she said she would. Essays questions were very complex for the maximum length. Lectures were randomly mandatory and often dull. Easy to get an A, but professor was not easy to work with.
Class taken was CS4263.
A pretty easy but interesting class! There are 4 short reaction papers and one large 10-page paper. Attendance is taken for one lab/class before each reaction paper. Grading is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Crooks is so knowledgeable in the field of cyberpsychology. Her lectures were so interesting and covered a lot of different topics related to online behavior and security in depth. Your grade is based on 4 short (2-3 page) reflection papers and 1 final (10-12 page) paper. She's a really easy grader and willing to help you out. Take her!
Majority online even though the class is held in person. Would refer her to anyone who needs a recommendation for PSYC. Clear grading materials and topics aren't too hard to grasp.
Easiest class ever. 10/10 would recommend. 5th grader could have gotten an A no problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Crooks's section of General Psych was so much easier compared to others. We had 5 tests that were not cumulative and easy. Going to lecture is completely optional. As long as you read the textbook and can answer her study guides, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Class was super chill. She largely reads off the lecture slides which she also posts. She also provides a study guide before each exam. The exams are also multiple choice. Easy A and very little effort put in.

Very nice, but essentially reads off of the lecture slides. Don't come to class unless you care about the small extra-credit pop quizzes, otherwise look at the study guides she posts as well as the definitions for the book's vocab words and the tests will be a breeze. Very easy grader, very simple tests.

AE6230 Actually. 
Professor Riso is amazing. She is extremely reasonable and helpful. The lectures are well structured and to the point. The lectures and assignments complement each other very well. I learnt a lot in her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, but the content in class as a whole is too advanced to be offered in undergrad imo (not Dr. Riso's fault). Unsteady aerodynamics - a graduate level topic appears in dynamic aeroelasticity, and you need a pretty good grasp of it to understand concepts such as aeroelastic flutter.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: AE 4220 is probably the toughest course in the AE curriculum, but Dr. Riso is fantastic. Her lectures are great, and she is SUPER nice. The homework and exams were brutal but fair. Do not expect to pass by just memorizing how to solve the problems. At the end if you're on the edge and you have an outlier score, she'll bump you.
the class was mad hard but dr. riso is the best

Difficult class. Extremely nice and caring professor. Dr. Riso is willing to sit with you 1 on 1 outside of regular office hours to ensure you understand the material. Everything is take home, but don't lower your guard. The exams are difficult because they require you to actually reason through the concepts to solve the problems.

Aeroelasticity is an extremely difficult class regardless of which professor is teaching it, but Dr. Riso is one of (if not my favorite) my favorite professors at Tech. Although this is only her 2nd time teaching, She's super caring and extremely flexible with deadlines, and is willing to hold additional office hours outside of her normal hours.

You can go to class but get ready to not understand anything he is saying. He doesnt teach well and you main have to learn it your self. Also for exams they are harder then the hw's and they are very short around 30min to solve 2 problems with parts. Hes a somewhat kind guy but wouldnt take again.

Genuinely the worst professor I have ever had. Do not take this professor, over 14 homeworks that are over 8 hours long every week, biweekly quizzes where the average is a 45%, and a final worth 45% of the grade, where the class average was a 55%. He doesn't teach well and is severely disconnected from how the students feel. Take with anyone else!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor is knowledgeable (wrote the textbook), but lectures are outdated—he mostly reads notes with little practical application. Few graded items; the final is 45% (avg was 57.5). Homework is time-consuming (5–8 hrs). Generous curve, so most get A/B. Advice: Skip class, self-study, and prep using past exams/homework, help classmates, pray.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the worst professor I have ever had in my life. He made me and several other students sob in his presence. We had an unruly amount (5+ hours) of homework every single day on top of 2 hours of lecture 4 times per week. I couldn't sleep, eat, or breathe anything but this class. He told us we were derranged. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Drop this class. You will probably get a B at the lowest but it is not worth it. Very homework heavy, lectures are tought from handwritten notes from 20 years ago and sometimes he doesn't understand his own writing. Does not work out problems in class. Saving grace was office hours. Not very forgiving on due dates.

WORST PROFESSOR IN AE! Craig has zero respect for students and no understanding of how to teach in the 21st century. Read the reviews below, and add 2 more projects to the already insane workload. He even forgot to print the formula sheet for our closed-note final and lied to our face about it. If he's teaching, take the class another semester.

Dr. Craig has a severe disconnection with the students. Even if you only take this class, he will make your life miserable. He will belittle you for not knowing structural concepts. You do not need to suffer through him, please just take it with someone else if possible.

The workload for this one class alone was equivalent to a full-time job. 14 homeworks, 5 quizzes, 3 tests, and 1 45% final. Absolutely no breaks in this course and you can get behind pretty quickly. Craig has a severe disconnect with students and makes it hard to want to ask questions by acting rudely and saying everything should be easy. Run away!

This was the worst class of my AE career at GT. Homeworks are incredibly long, and quizzes from a random question bank destroyed grades little by little. Add to that, a final worth 45% with average of 60. A big curve was given so that a chunk of students wouldn't fail/delay their graduation. Stressful, miserable experience.

Dr. Craig is the hardest professor Ive ever had at Georgia Tech. All of his exams are extremely time sensitive, having 10-minute biweekly quizzes and even 15-minute midterms. The lectures are extremely content heavy, the weekly homeworks take 6+ hours to complete, and the final is worth 45% of your entire grade. I do NOT recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: AVOID IF POSSIBLE! AE 3140 is a hard class by itself, but taking it with Craig makes it even harder with hours of boring video lectures where he just goes over pages of written lectures, long HWs every week, short (time-wise) midterms and a very hard final that counts for 45% of your grade.

This is the most ridiculous class I've ever taken. After liking structures somewhat coming into this class, I have no desire to do anything related to it because of this class. The final is 45% of the grade, and despite spending at least 6 hours a week on homework (oh yeah homework is weekly have fun), no one in this class has learned anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Enormous amount of homework (one every single week, start to finish). Lots of material to cover, of which my peers and I truly internalized very little. Final is worth 45% of the grade. Dr. Craig cares about students' success but this is certainly the hardest class I've taken over my time at Tech, and his teaching doesn't do it many favors.

If you want to suffer through hours of HW and quizzes that you will fail no matter how much you study, then definitely take this class! Craig's lectures are long and not helpful at all, then he will yell at you if you happen to have questions about the material. The final is worth half the grade, so if you've been doing well it could be for nothing

This is by far one of the most difficult classes I have taken in my 4 years at Georgia Tech. I have never had to work so hard for so little of my grade percentage wise. And chances are that none of it will matter anyway because the final is just under half of our grade for the course. Dr. Craig is well organized, but his class format is terrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Craig is the most challenging professor I have had at Tech, but not in a good way. Normally, challenging classes are good because we learn lots of material, but that has not been my experience with Dr. Craig. I feel like I have learned almost nothing in this class, despite spending 10+ hours a week to do homework. Every Single Week.

Random question bank 10 minute biweekly quizzes. Homework is 25% while each exam/project is 5%. Final is 45%. Dr. Craig is a professor who has a severe disconnect between the course material and his students. Uses custom notation, changes it randomly, and very unclear when explaining topics. Usually only prof to teach this class, best of luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Craig is a great professor. I generally hate statics/structures, but his clear enthusiasm for the material and his hatred for tedious algebra were welcome. Definitely cares about student well-being, but make no mistake: this is a difficult class. He grades leniently but fairly.

Under the system his name will be James just so you know. Run very very far away from this professor. Do not be fooled by his apparent higher than average GPA, take someone else. You will not learn the same stuff that everyone else does and you will not be able to use a crib sheet. Have fun memorizing every single formula, worst class I've had.

Bad professor. Tests are 30 minutes long, when they could easily take the hour. Rambles a lot during lecture, but doesn't actually teach much of the material. Very hard, long homework without the proper foundation to do it. Expects you to understand the material easily and doesn't like questions. First review I've ever written if that says anything

Incredibly smart, but has gotten so out of touch as to what it is like to learn new material. He will skip past the foundation for many topics because it's "so easy that anyone can do it." and skip straight to difficult problems. He only allows 30 min for tests that would easily take over an hour. Very condescending to any questions someone asks.

Took Dr. Craig for COE 3001 in Fall 2016. Homework assignments were incredibly difficult and time-intensive. Lectures lacked organization and were not helpful. Incredibly smart guy, great personality, but he made what should have been a simpler class much more difficult than it needed to be.

Yet another one of those GT profs who is plenty smart but has completely forgotten how to communicate to people for whom the material is new. He has lots of resources, which seems to be in lieu of streamlining the class. The homeworks are always huge and have to be done with one specific "method" he makes up. Each usually takes 8+ hours.

A very meticulous and organized instructor who can get boring/wonky at times with detail. Loves Mathematica, so if you aren't able to master it during the class, homework will be a nightmare. Can talk for hours on end without getting tired, and it's very easy to get drowsy in his class.

Probably the most helpful teacher that I've had at Tech. You can tell that he really wants his students to learn the material and puts out as many resources as he can to help. His tests and final were very fair if you just looked over his notes and past exams. He gets sidetracked in class sometimes, but overall he was a great professor.
The text used for this class was electronic and freely distributed by the professor. However Craig made extensive use of it.

Had him in Fall 03 for "CS for engineers" ...was apparently one of the foremost MATLAB-capable professors at the school at the time.  He was not good at teaching CS.  I did well 'cause I knew most of it already.  His blunders made lectures tolerable
This was the worst class in Aerospace, taught by the worst professor in aerospace!
I hated this class. DId not learn anything at all. TO make matters worse the tests are hard.
Excellent Prof, had a bad prof but watched his lectures and got an A. Highly recommend!

Grading: 3 Midterms + 1 Final (worst midterm 15%, all others & final 20%). "Bucket point" system for the other 25% (need 70pts/120 for full credit)

Lecture: 9/10; Passion: 9/10; Communication: 10/10; Flexibility: 9/10; Test Prep: 10/10

Quirks: Bad handwriting, likes teaching 8:25 a.m. MWF

Recommendation: Would be my first choice for this course.

W professor. The class is pretty hard but if you lock in you can definitely get a good grade. I would also recommend reading through the course textbook Lay Linear Algebra since it follows the course really closely and goes into more details than the lectures have time for, and you lowkey need that for the true and false sections on the tests.

Professor Warnock was great at making Linear clear and understandable. His lectures prepared me a lot for the FRQ questions and going to office hours helped clear up a lot of my confusion over true/false questions. Make sure to do the homework and practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Example of an amazing professor. I cant say much that hasn't already be said. Just make sure you attend every lecture, especially the ones near the end of the semester.
Great lecturer and funny guy!

great professor with great lectures. explained concepts pretty clearly and has a lot of passion. i didn't pay the most attention in lectures personally, but 1554 has a canvas masterpage with recordings from old lectures and a collection of past midterm exams to practice (and more) which helped me immensely.
this man is the next Gilbert Strang.
Very chill professor. Responds to emails, very accessible and friendly

Extremely accessible outside of class. Best linear lecturer by far, took his time to clearly explain material and did not rush through the content. Provided great reviews for the tests, and clearly cares about the success of his students. If you have a different lecturer and are struggling, try to come to his instead as attendance isn't mandatory.

Cuyler is awesome! If you can get him for linear you 100% should take it with him. He takes time to really explain everything in lecture, answer everyone's questions, is easily available for office hours, and genuinely cares about the students and the subject. Plus as the course coordinator he writes the tests and sometimes would drop small hints!

Warnock is the GOAT of 1554. He's a really great lecturer and makes everything super understandable. if you go to his lecture + his office hours + studio + do the homework + do some practice tests you will get a good grade

If you get a chance to take 1554 with him, do it. He is literally a 1 of 1 Linear Algebra teacher. I cannot reiterate how simple he breaks down Linear Algebra, and tells you what you need to remember for the exams. If you don't have him, he has recordings of his past lectures, I recommend watching those lectures, he's incredible.
Good professor in general. Very knowledgeable about the subject and gives good feedback to questions. Probably the best 1554 professor.

Great professor. Linear Algebra is not the easiest course and requires studying for sure. But, hes a great professor and makes it as easy as possible to understand the material. Very accessible and personable. Definitely take if you can! Only problem, you do have to do fairly well in the class to get an A. Exams are 75% of the grade, so do good.

Warnock is an amazing math professor who is really passionate about the subject he teaches. Math 1554 is a tough math class especially for incoming freshman, but Warnock is able to put complex ideas into simple terms that make digesting the material easy. He is easily accessible outside of class through office hours and is extremely active on Piaza

Great professor, probably would've done better if I attended more lectures. He's passionate and very, very nice if you go to office hours, answering almost any question. A little bit of theory in this course, but I would say fair.

Cuyler is the GOAT for 1554. His enthusiasm for linear algebra is genuinely contagious, office hours are great. Lectures are packed with many proofs and examples, which make it easy to build a great understanding for the subject. Very caring and listens to students. You'll end up appreciating the math.

Easily the most passionate math professor I've had at GT. Cuyler's lectures are amazing, and he's a really friendly and approachable guy. Honestly even if you end up in another prof's section, just attend Cuyler's lectures, they're that good.

And stop by his office hours! He explains even better there :)
He is really good lecturer and gives great examples if you attend lecture and follow along you should be fine!

Great professor. I have him for 8 am and he is so enthusiastic about linear algebra and math, it rubs off on you. He explains concepts so well in such little time he has. Everything on Canva is useful and the past exams help a lot for prospective exams.

Professor Warnock is an excellent lecturer with some of the most clear explanations I've experienced. I've heard of other students even saying they come to our lectures instead. He also projects his voice really well. Even in the back of a 200 person lecture hall with no mic, I can hear him perfectly. I recommend him to anyone who can get him.

WARNOCK MY GOAT THE GLAZE IS REAL whoever called him the Lorax is so accurate my guy knows anything and everything about math. He is so passionate about Linear it rubs off onto you and he really tries his best in lectures to explain everything in layman's terms. Linear is hard but he makes it doable/even easy. I will miss him and his teaching sm :(

I think it's only his second semester teaching linear at GT and his first over the summer, but he did a fantastic job. Very engaging in lecture, very good at explaining concepts and finding good examples for them, knew how to pace the class well, and was very active on Piazza.
WARNOCK THE GOAT

Prof. Warnock is a nice guy who wants you to succeed. He does a great job explaining material and records lectures / posts the notes for you to review later. The class is hard as hell, but he made it passable. IMO the professor for the course doesn't matter as much as your self-willingness to study the past tests, practice, and be attentive does.

Man this guy is like the Lorax for linear algebra. Wonderful at breaking down concepts and so passionate. Struggled very much early on but brought up my grade with Dr. Warnock's help in office hours. Generous with the MQE. Test are very hard but truly mimic the practice tests. Just a hard class in general but he will be a great course coordinator.

A great prof and a great guy. His lectures are amazing (he sometimes got behind homework pacing, but go to studio and you'll learn it) and it's very obvious that he not only knows a lot about the topics, but he is genuinely interested in them too. Gives great explanations, ample office hours, and responds to emails quickly. Take him if you can.

One of the nicest professors I've met here at Tech. Super friendly and accommodating no matter your skill level, and gives really good explanations, especially at office hours! He's also very good for people that like theory - The way he talks about proofs makes me laugh every time because you can just tell he loves the subject matter so much LOL

I would highly recommend going to Dr.Warnock for linear algebra lectures even if you're not in his section. He not only explains every topic thoroughly and simply, but also is knowledgeable enough to show you full derivations and proofs on the spot. If you're confused about anything attend his office hours as this course is fast paced.

I loved the lectures and the prof, however the content in class is substantially easier than the exams. These exams were extremely difficult compared to what we were taught during the class. I think it's just calc 1 in general here is so hard. My advice is to lock in and STUDY the hell out of the concepts.

He explained concepts really well, and was very attentive to any questions asked in lectures. Also, aside from going through the theory and rules, etc., he excelled at showing how the theory applied practically, which may really help students who have a hard time remembering all the rules for the various concepts. Lectures were also recorded.

I think it was his first time teaching at Tech, and honestly, he did a pretty good job compared to the other lecturers for 1551 that same semester. He was very straight forward and good at explaining and would always pause for questions. He would also slow down if he felt that a concept wasn't explained well enough. Overall, pretty good.

Dr. Cuba is one of the best professors in the ChBE faculty. His course is very organized, and he strongly prepares his students for success in subsequent courses. He is always accessible after class and truly cares about his students' success. As a result, students really respect him.

Dr. Cuba is one of the best Professors I've had at Georgia Tech. 2100 is arguably the most difficult class in the curriculum for CHBE students and he takes the time to make you understand the material very well. His notes are very comprehensive, and he goes through the example problems in great detail to help you.
Not a good lecturer, gives out notes but doesn't follow them. Hard to understand even though the content is not very difficult. Has one of the strangest grading styles I've ever seen.
Just not a good teacher, doesn't explain things well and his lectures are really boring

Dr. Cuba was super helpful and approachable. He was always willing to answer questions after class or during office hours when I needed help. He grades fairly and genuinely cares about how his students are doing, which you don't always see in CHBE. Definitely recommend taking any class with him!
His class was somehow difficult for no reason. I didn't even find the material that challenging, it was just his style of teaching. Nothing made sense. Needs to post notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The ratings who gave Dr. Cuba a 2/3 for kinetics are unreasonable. Though the midterm average was not the best, he kept that in mind and lowered the grade cut-offs based on our grades. He cares about his students. His fill in the blank notes are nice. He records his lectures, so if you miss something in the notes, you can always go back to watch.

I had Dr. Cuba for 2100 and he was absolutely amazing. However, I had him again for Kinetics, and he did not seem to hit the mark. His singular exam was nearly impossible, with the average being a 61. His quizzes' point distributions are kinda insane. His lectures are also slightly weird and hard to keep up with.
Dr Cuba is a great professor. If don't understand something and ask him after class he always has a unique of explaining it. His tests and quizes can be hard but practice is key like any CHBE class.

Professor Cuba-Torres is great! ChBE 2100 is inevitably a challenging class, but it is clear that he cares about his students' understanding of course material and success in the class. I would definitely enroll in other courses he took if given the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Cuba is a really good 2100 professor. He always makes an attempt to answer all questions we have in class, and records all his lectures so we can access them later. His lectures are also very easy to follow, and he provides us with skeleton notes that we can fill in to make note taking easier.

Dr. Cuba is hands down, the best professor I have ever had. I started this class not even knowing what chemical engineering really was, and he has made me so excited to pursue it. I have him at 9:30 am this semester, and have yet to miss a single class. He is extremely caring about his students' understanding. Take him if you can, he is the best!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There is not a tag for CHBE 2130, but he taught my thermo 1 class this semester. ABSOLUTELY THE BEST CHBE prof at GT from my 2100 and 2130 experience. In class fill in the blank handouts are all that are needed to succeed in his classes. While quizzes and tests are difficult (but fair), he is so humble and approachable that I can't spite the guy.

Probably the best lecturer I have ever had. I could tell Dr. Cuba loves transport and loves to teach. He made complicated topics simple and would spend an hour after every class answering students' questions in addition to office hours. Quizzes and tests are hard but rewarding once/if you get the hang of them. It will be a turbulent semester (;
Very willing to meet with students outside of class and an engaging lecturer.

Dr. Cuba is a great professor. Lectures are material heavy, but he constantly is checking student understanding and reviewing past material. Homework can sometimes take a long time. Tests are hard, but graded putting a heavy emphasis on understanding rather than the correct answer (you can get a good grade without finishing the test)

He's in no way a bad professor. I've had Professor Cuba a few times now and what I've found is that he is spectacular at presenting derivations for all formulas and explaining concepts, but he's not great at teaching problem solving and application. If you learn well from a textbook, this is your guy. If not, brace yourself.

Extremely tough course with lowish exam averages, but expect lowered cutoffs (for my class, it was 80/65/55 for A/B/C). Torres is a really good professor and gives handouts for notes. Very caring and respects his students. HW and exams can be difficult, but Torres and the UCA were very helpful during office hours. Overall a solid choice!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: So far, the professor has proven to offer several review material every lecture to allow for further review and practice what was read as homework. The class is small, so it's easy to ask questions. The class itself is tough, but if you're constant with your HW and review habits you'll be fine.

Intelligent and caring professor and a straightforward class! His teaching style is extremely clear, and he provides helpful "fill-in-the-blank" handouts so you don't have to waste time scribbling notes during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: This course is quite tough and requires constant practice; however, Dr. Cuba helps as much as he can by providing: useful notes, midterm reviews, and great lectures. The class averages for all three exams were quite low, but he compensates most everyone who never gave up. Not an easy A.

He respects all of his students and will help outside of class . He makes it clear what you need to do to succeed. The class is difficult but if you ask him for help, he will make things a lot easier.
Real solid professor. Has helpful handouts for each lecture. Clear and straightforward with everything.
He does a good job with his lectures and provides handouts to help students follow his lectures. He is available outside of class and grades/curves fairly.

Professor Cuba-Torres does not care about his students. If you don't know exactly what is going on in class he will not respect you. He made the hardest exam questions on each test that expected you to calculate things you could not possibly calculate unless you had more information. In all, this man made me hate chemical engineering
He is a great teacher who cares about his students. Will take him again gladly, even if he's only teaching an 8 am.

Professor Culbreth is certainly one of the best professors I've encountered at Tech! His enthusiasm for philosophy is clear to see in his passion infused lectures. He'll challenge your thinking and his own as well, and it's quite honestly a marvelous aspect of his teaching. There is a fair amount of reading, so just pay attention and it'll be fine!

I took Dr. Culbreth for his Philosophy 185 course Emory this past semester, and I have nothing but the highest regard for him. Dr. Culbreth challenges his students to tackle discussion, find meaning and interpret text. He is a passionate, caring and immensely intelligent professor whose courses are rewarding and I cannot recommend enough.
Great teaching style. Cares about students

The most passionate professor you'll find! He has definitely made philosophy fun, and during lectures/Q&A sessions you can see his eyes glow when he talks. Very reading heavy, but he supplies reading guides as well. Excellent class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: His accent is pretty heavy, but that aside he's a pretty good professor. Very straightforward with the content and more than willing to help if you need it. Assignments were reasonable and tests and quizzes were fairly easy.

Really heavy accent so it was hard to learn the already hard math subject. Tries to help out but I learned more from the TA. I just read the textbook, did the HW, and went to tutoring. Definitely more helpful than the professor himself.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria
