reviews.comment: Now, where do I even begin when talking about the sheer greatness of a man nay MYTH that is Jianbo Cui aka J.B. aka John Bow. J.B. is a common example of not to judge a book by its cover. What lies behind this facade of a non-assuming mortal is an infinite repertoire of knowledge and power. God have mercy on our souls. And finally, we won.

Very heavy accent, but fairly competent lecturer. The structure of his lectures can be hard to follow but you can adjust to the accent. The textbook is free, online, and is an absolute godsend that can carry you through the class, regardless of your prof. His tests and quizzes are on the easier side for 1553.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His accent is very hard to understand, and to be completely honest, I don't go to class very often because of it. Still, he's a really nice professor and is more than willing to answer your questions. He's very accessible outside of class and understanding if you have to make up quizzes. If you have concerns, you can email and get a quick response.

Dr. Cui's accent is very heavy and it's hard to understand what he says sometimes. However, he definitely knows his stuff and he tries very hard to help his students; he's extremely good at listening to student feedback and clearly wants you to succeed. As long as you sit up front, follow along in lecture, and do your homework, you should be good.
He speaks with a very thick accent that makes him hard to understand in lecture. He teaches the content fine it is just hard to understand him.

I took diff eq through the distance math program. Her exams for distance students were difficult, but she's great at explaining concepts and she puts in extra hours to make sure you understand the material.

She explains things clearly. She also moves at a very reasonable pace and reviews concepts in class instead of rushing through the material like the other profs. She's willing to answer all of your questions and she's super nice. She does make a few mistakes on the board though but she'll give out candy for every 15 mistakes she makes!

I had a lot of problems with this class, thankfully Amalia did her best to make my time easier. Gives very good feedback and is very responsive and helpful whenever you have concerns. She is very clear about the topics you should know for each exam and is more than willing to give a bit of a curve for the sake of fairness.

By far the best math teacher I have had at Tech. She explains things very clearly and moves at a pace so that you don't feel like the class is a week ahead of what you are understanding. The lectures are very interactive and she strives to get students involved during lecture. As long as you do the homework and go to lecture, the tests are doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved this class. Her lecture style is extremely clear, and she breaks down difficult math concepts into step-by-step processes that make the material very easy to remember. She's also just very nice and sociable to be around. I hope to take her for my diff eqs class next semester cause my first experience was so great.
She's great! explains things really well and is very reasonable
Her lectures are great, her tests and quizzes are topical, she's funny, and she makes an effort to get to know the students.

Tests are fairly straightforward, shouldn't have to study too much; weekly quizzes which help a lot; lectures are easy to follow; Amalia is easy to reach outside of class and gives good feedback; class curved at the end.

Math at Tech is HAAARD, but Amalia is both fair, supportive, humorous funny. The way she approaches lectures is very effective: she lays out the basic maths concept, explains it again in layman's words, then does a few examples. Practice your homework until you understand it WELL or you'll suffer. She curves, so don't freak out. Also: OFFICE HOURS.

Fantastic professor who actually made me interested in the content. He gives you everything you need to know in his lectures, and by the end of the semester, he makes sure everyone gets a fair grade, even if the semester is tough.
Disrespectful to students. Doesn't care about you.

The material in this class was super interesting to me. Dr. Cunefare has a definite interest in the material and does really try to get students to enjoy it as well. The class can get pretty tedious, and the homeworks are commonly over things we haven't covered yet in lecture.
Horrible
Enjoyed the IC Engines class.  It was difficult but Dr. C's lectures were well planned and the material was clearly presented.

Many times, she would skip over problems or an explanation stating that it was "easy", when I had no idea how to do it, or would make things much more complicated than necessary. However, she was funny which helped me not zone out in lecture sometimes. A lot of homework that is harder than necessary along with poorly written test questions.

decent prof/lecturer. she did make mistakes pretty frequently but most were caught by students and corrected, so i thought it was fine. the class was not too hard in my opinion, but i did take and understood ap physics 1 previously, which was basically the same as 2211. curtis obviously isnt as good as alicea, but she's still ok to take imo

She was okay as far. Her lectures were often harder to follow, and she explained concepts in a way that wasn't always productive. There are definitely worse physics 1 professors, but if you can get Alicea that would be the best. Overall, the class wasn't too bad, the labs/bucket points help with grades, but the tests are very difficult.

The other reviews are right... Dr. Curtis does make a lot of mistakes in lecture. Sometimes she would go deep and try to show the derivation of some principles but I think just ended up confusing people more or messing it up. She is nice and accessible but her lectures didn't make things easier for anyone.

Professor Curtis was an extremely difficult professor. Her lectures were not engaging and she made so many mistakes always asking students "Could someone point out where I went wrong?". How are we supposed to be able to point out your mistake when this is our first time learning it. Additionally her lectures were barely useful for the hard tests.

Good lecturer! In case things get a little rocky there's always Dr. Alicea's lectures to rely on. Overall Physics 1 is heavily scaffolded so professor choice doesn't matter as much, but Dr. Curtis is an amazing human.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Before taking that course I'd read on RMP that she made tons of mistakes when teaching;this is VERY TRUE. Every single lectures and every single examples she was making a mistake and followed it by "Oh, I made a mistake guys can you tell where" like no I can't I'm still in the learning process..? Class is an easy PASS though bcs of the grade scale.
Did not understand anything in class had to drop mid semester I do not recommend

Very nice professor but teaches pretty slow, would recommend watching Alicea's lecture videos instead of paying attention in this class. If you already took AP physics you will just need to brush up on the topics and you'll be fine. Labs are easy 100 and make up 25% of the grade.
She kind, but she messes up a lot and spends way too much time on easy questions(whole lecture)
mid class, good explanations but wayy too long and easy to get lost in
Caring and willing to explain but dry lectures
Very knowledgable on the subjects, but was super proof heavy such that it didn't quite fit the way I best learn. Overall can't terribly complain.

She is a very nice professor but honestly can't get her stuff together. More often than not, she would make a mistake while solving a problem in class and take 10 minutes trying to find it. In general I would say she explains topics in a convoluted way. Ultimately there are much better Physics 1 professors (especially Alicea).

Curtis is extremely knowledgeable and ACTUALLY cares if you grasp the material. She will make sure you understand it. She holds test review sessions as well. Only problem I had was how during some lectures she would mess up the math and confuse students. But, she is genuinely a sweet woman and you should be happy you got her. GO TO LECTURES!!!!!!!!

Lectures were boring, and she would often make mistakes in writing. But she was nice, not much to say about her. I watched Dr Alicea's lecture which pretty much everyone does, stopped going to her lectures.
She's fine! Good teacher, good lectures, accessible during office hours. Shows that she cares. Only thing is, she messes up so frequently on the in class examples that I used to get so confused.

If you aren't able to get a better professor, Professor Curtis is a good fallback. Her lectures are a little boring, but she explains problems and content very thoroughly In terms of grading, everything is done by the TAs or Alecia and they're pretty lenient. The labs aren't difficult for the class since previous student's work can be found on YT.
Lectures are kind of dull

stopped attending her class half way through semester despite it being mandatory, Dr. Alicea's video lectures are more than enough. Dr. Curtis lectures are fine and shes nice, it's just not enough time or legible for me to learn effectively personally. Would still recommend to go to her class for the clickers which are 5% of the grade.

She is very kind but her lectures are nothing special. She made the content make sense but she didn't make me enjoy learning it. She deeply cares about her students. Attendance is graded via TurningPoint clicker questions.

Plain jane prof with nothing really remarkable ab her except she's a nice lady. Lectures were p boring & I don't think they prepared u well for the tests, which were p difficult. Class participation graded on clicker questions but not for accuracy. HWs take hours but it's physics yk. Not the most helpful prof but not bad. Very average

Her lectures are not super exciting but they are easy to follow and she's clearly interested in the material and cares for the students. Homework is mostly from the textbook with a few topics not covered in class but found easily in the book. Closed note tests with formula sheet which are very fair and mostly easy. Participation credit in class.

Terrible lectures, most boring thing you'll ever experience. Consisted of her basically reading off of the slides, and going on about irrelevant things. Terrible handwriting, couldn't understand a single thing she wrote on those slides. You'll basically have to teach yourself. Tests were extremely difficult. She's not very approachable or caring.

PHYS 2211 is not an easy class, but Dr. Curtis did her best to make the content understandable and concise. There were technical difficulties, but she always tried her best to get through lectures and uploaded the notes plus any extra videos with worked out problems. She truly cares about her students and wants us to do our best.

Curtis is a good lecturer. She uploads slides before class and she'll post the finished ones after class. The lectures are decent and she works through problems clearly. HW was through the textbook, and while reading wasn't required, it definitely helped.
This is just a stupid hard class. Curtis is a great teacher though, and is willing to help her students. Good luck! Go with Curtis or Greco for modern physics 1, avoid the others.

Going to this class is completely useless because you basically have to teach yourself everything. The teacher didnt even try to have neat handwriting so I couldnt understand any solution to problems. It was such a bad lecture and it looked like she didnt even care if we were learning or not.
Worst teacher I have ever had. Very inconsiderate of her students when switching to online during the COVID pandemic. Always very rude and terrible at explaining. Get ready to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Terrible.
Monotonous voice. Had no care in actually teaching the class. Unprepared and only read from PowerPoint slides. Lack of empathy!

Lectures tended to be really slow at the beginning of class and really rushed towards the end. I had a hard time paying attention in class and mostly relied on reading the textbook and doing homework to learn. Tests are fairly difficult but she provides a lot of old tests to practice from. Show up to class & do your homework early for extra points.

Her lectures are decent, primarily focused on explaining clicker questions, but she is very accessible outside of class, and she explains concepts well. Attendance is not mandatory, but it is the easiest way to get bucket points. She was very understanding and flexible during COVID-19.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Overall a good professor. You can tell she cares about her students and the course. Given that I had Physics 1 with her (modern), your perception of difficulty may be different from mine, but her class's difficulty seemed to be about the same as any other Physics 1 modern class.

Physics, in general, is pretty hard, but Dr. Curtis consistently offers her time to help students; you can easily tell she loves what she does. She is good at explaining things as well, but the class is generally hard so in order to do well, you should utilize one-on-one time with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Prof Curtis is not the best, but you'll be fine if you have her. She explains things pretty well but make sure you pay attention in lecture. To do well in the class you definitely have to invest time and effort yourself because just going to class will not be enough. However, it is very doable and she seems like she wants to help.

Introduce yourself to her the first week and go to office hours, she's extremely helpful  1 on 1 and in small groups. Lectures aren't always the most helpful, but reading the book helped me a lot with homework. If you put the effort in this class is very fair.

Excellent professor. She definitely is teaching what she loves and knows what she is doing. Her lectures were somewhat boring and typically followed the book. Tests were hard because they were made my the chair of the Physics school. She is willing to help and is very nice and helpful one-on-one. She will also remember your name.

Lectures were horrendously boring. Tests were very difficult and she thought they were fair. Only held one review session during the semester. Lectures all class without any demos so you get very confused very easily. Was always behind the other class, so we always had to play 'catch-up' on the homework that was due every night.
Not a very good professor. Boring, doesn't teach you what you need, gets far behind the other class. Thinks tests are "fair" when they're really hard. Not helpful in learning physics.
She certainly knows her stuff, but her lectures are the most boring thing I've ever experienced. However, if you took physics in high school and had a firm grasp of it, the class won't be too hard.

Excellent professor. She doesn't make class very interesting, but she definitely teaches you what you need. Homework every night, lectures are mandatory, and long, hard tests. Also weekly quizzes in lab that are very hard. NO CURVE. She is willing to help you in person and email, though.

Best thermo proof at Tech. Does not make the class any harder than it has to be. All of the practice material is exactly like the exams so if you do all of it you will be all good. Super great guy he makes what could be an evil class so doable!!

One of the best professors I have had. Very accessible outside of class and lectures were engaging. Weekly homework. The grading scheme is very test heavy but he does give extra credit. Test are not very difficult if you do the practice tests.

The GOAT! Amazing, thorough, and incredibly helpful lectures. Super understanding guy. Tests are worth a lot of your grade, but they're incredibly fair, and if you do all the homework every week with fidelity and do the practice exam, you'll be set for an A. Overall, if you put in consistent but reasonable effort every week, you'll do very well.

He was great at adapting to the class and actually teaching the material. Very lenient and understanding in general. He was also effective at guiding his students through this coursework. The best professor someone can take thermo from.
He makes the otherwise difficult material easier to understand. He's humorous and a genuinely good lecturer.

Hands down the best professor I have ever had. He provides all lectures as printed, fillable pamphlets and is a very good lecturer. Homework follows lecture content and is harder than exams. Grading is done quickly and very fairly. I always wanted to go to lecture because he was very funny.

Absolutely named Dan GOATlyar, one of the best professors I have had. I would definitely take another course with him. All notes were very structured and the homework was challenging, but followed them closely and he was easily accessible for questions or office hours.

The class is hard and daunting and its easy to get lost, but: Homework is very representative of the lectures, lecture notes are clear and concise, and Kotlyar is genuinely interested in what he's teaching and is good at it. You will need to stay focused in class, but he's generous in grading and his tests are the most fair I've seen at Tech.

Had Dr. Kotlyar for NRE 4210. He is easily my favorite professor in the NRE department. He is able to clearly explain complex subjects with ease, and his lectures are full of useful diagrams and equations to support the theory. He made the class a bit too easy this semester, but it was still incredibly informative. GT is lucky to have Dr. Kotlyar.

Kotlyar is a really good lecturer. Your issue will not be with him but with the course material. There is a textbook but he's expecting you to learn his notes (which he hands out via paper in lecture), so if you ever get confused with his lectures, read the textbook for the concepts, and go to office hours to do the assignments

Kotlyar is by far the best NRE prof. 10/10 Amazing lectures. HWs (32%) start easy but get progressively harder until they are very very difficult. Tests and Final are hard but fair. He grades generously. Know ALL homework problems by heart (including derivations). Coding project (13%) is a long derivation and some basic python. He gives most of it.

Dr. Dean has been a very pleasant professor to have! Accepts late work and is not a harsh grader/most grades are completion. Very friendly and makes it easy to participate and do the assignments without feeling forced to. She won't be like those English professors that are always looking for a specific answer.

She was very caring and sympathetic towards the fact that many students at a tech school don't care about English. The topic for my 1102 course was very interesting and our assignments were not just standard essays. Every assignment was graded on completion (as long as you met all the requirements) aside from reading checks.
super easy A, no tests, pretty much everything is pass/fail, and she accepts late work
A bit boring at times, but assignments weren't bad and she didn't grade harshly

As long as you do your work and put in a decent amount of effort, you will get a 100 in this class. She is a very easy grader and she gives excellent feedback. She also really puts an emphasis on creating an inclusive and welcoming space for all students. 10/10 would recommend her!!!

While she didn't lecture much, she was quite friendly and made herself accessible. The assignments do take a little while to complete, but grading is practically for completion, and she gives incredibly clear feedback on how to improve your projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took Professor Dean blindly. She has a very interesting topics (Monsters), and she has a labor based grading system. She made attendance guidlines easier later in the sem so attendance is not too bad. She gives good feedback, and lets you redo assignments and projects. She is very understanding and helpful. Would def reccomend this English class.

Participation matters so much in this class. Don't miss any days or any assignments because she has a "labor based grading system" so even if you do the best work, you showing up determines your grade. I missed 2 days out the entire semester and received a B in the class due to me missing a workshop on one of the days I was absent. Ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Participation was a frustrating. You only get a minimum of 70% for showing up to all classes, so you have to do discussion boards & other activities to get the full credit. She wanted us to read books that I (& 99% of the class) have no time to read and expects a discussion in class. Nice professor with easy-ish hw, but lots of unnecessary work.

Overall great professor for ENGL 1101. She gives a lot of flexibility with project topics/groups and is a generous grader. Her lectures are generally framed around pop culture topics, and attendance is basically mandatory. Readings are usually long and have a pre-class quiz attached, and projects include multiple stages (outline, reflection, etc.).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: She had an amazing class topic with Stranger Things and Taylor Swift, which is why I took her. Overall, she's a good professor and I had fun working with the cool topics she had. However, she is a pretty tough grader and there's a LOT of assignments every week. And every artifact has like a brainstorm, draft, final, and reflection so get ready.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is so nice and caring. None of the work was over the top and the class/topics were very interesting. This class was actually very fun.

Her classes aren't that interesting (to me personally) but she's very flexible with extensions (if you ask ahead of time). There is a bit of work and we had to read 2 books which we were given multiple choice (5 pt.) quizzes on but if you have a friend you can collaborate. Just figure out what she likes (ideas wise) and cater to those in your work.

Dr Ruzicka is great! I took her for the English 1101 graphic novels class which was great. She is an easy grader and her classes are interesting, they hardly feel like lectures. We had four major grades, and the hardest one was making a 20-page graphic novel. Light on the homework. DONT BUY WOVEN TEXTBOOK its a waste of money and its free on reddit

The class is a fair amount of work but she's a pretty lenient grader. Readings are heavy, typically 50 or more pages per class. Quizzes are pretty easy. Choose the subject of your essay wisely, because you're going to be spending the rest of the semester developing it. A solid choice for 1101.

Readings are normally around 70 or so pages but they're pretty interesting. The only thing I actively struggled with was the Petcha Kucha presentation, other than that the class was pretty easy. She does give pop quizzes, but they're a piece of cake if you do the readings. Her lectures are highly discussion based.

It was difficult to follow lectures because he would talk about things that were not relevant. The exams were very difficult for Psych 1101 because they were more conceptual and on small details. The grading was also usually wrong and I had to go in after exams to fix questions graded wrong.
He gives random pop quizzes, lectures are mostly rambling, class isn't hard as long as you take notes and do your homework on time

The professor gives you a topic list to study off for midterms and finals, but questions are very confusing for an intro class. Some questions are too specific and frq grading is pretty strict. FIND A DIFFERENT PROFESSOR OR DONT TAKE THE CLASS. Seriously it's not worth it. Made psych way to diffuclt for what it is. This is an intro class, should not be that hard. Bro deserves more 1 stars

Fair and pretty good professor, but does have his shortcomings. Lectures are all over the place and he is a little unorganized. Terrible teacher, bogus tests, class average of a 65 or lower on some of the tests. Bro this is psych 1101 and he makes it an unbearable. Do NOT TAKE him. He's a mad yapper who doesn't know how to teach.

Lectures for the entire 1:15 twice a week and has occasional pop quizzes that aren't really that hard but still count towards grade. Hardest part of his class was his grading. There are weekly reading quizzes which are quite easy, but the exams are diabolical. Expect to stay up late studying and then regretting doing so, because whatever you studied is never on the actual exam. If you get stuck in this class, I will be praying for you and your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Required to purchase access to a $125 online textbook / learning platform. 10% of your grade is based on quizzes that require digital access from the publisher - no piracy. Attendance (in the form of random in-class quizzes) also counts for 10% of your grade. 4 participations in campus psych research is also required* (Coerced). I would say more.

He seems like a nice guy who's knowledgeable on psychology, but that doesn't translate to good professor. His tests were ridiculously hard for an introductory course being riddled with random facts and his lectures were hard to take much away from. His study guides are useful to a degree and he'll communicate what might be on FRQs but not great.

While a really nice guy who's clearly passionate about psychology, Dr. Spieler's class was extremely confusing. Don't take his class if you want PSYC to be easy, and expect to work if you take.

dont take him, hes so unorganized and someone told me he graded midterm 2 with the scantrons from midterm 1 because he lost the right ones. literally what?????? he should stick to research and stay away from teaching since he clearly doesn't know the first thing about educating people.

He has pretty good lectures and knows what he is talking about, however his tests are way to hard for both an intro class and  will often sneak random facts in the study guide that we never learned but turn up on the test. reviews.comment: lectures are interesting, very nice and knowledgeable about topics. some reviews on him are a bit dramatic but i do agree he emphasizes that "if it's not on the study guide it won't be on the test" but then about 1/3 of the things on the test weren't on the study guide. otherwise, cares for his students and is very understanding if you talk to him.

honestly a terrible professor. his study guides aren't accurate as he includes more topics on the exam. also, the exam average was a fail, he said he would improve his style, and very much did not. he doesn't give practice problems beforehand because he “doesn't have time”. definitely do not recommend as he overcomplicated simply topics too.
Boring lecturer. Can see that he's passionate about the topics, but lectures very unengaging. Slides are hard to understand. Emphasizes study guide has everything on test, but includes other topics.

Spends a lot of time during lectures talking about things unrelated to midterms so it's really hard to know what to take notes of. Plus, there are questions on midterm that aren't directly written on slides, making it hard to review. Very boring lecturer.

Bruh, this guy doesn't know what he is talking about. The slides are so bad and he will yap whatever comes to his mind. I am so lost in the lectures and have to learn all the materials from textbook. The textbook are super long and complicated to read.
The lectures were interesting overall. He was great at keeping the class engaged with jokes. Exams were heavily lecture-based and he provided great study guides.

I never followed his lectures as it often seemed like an "info-dump," which made it interesting for some. However, I thought there was a lack of a real curriculum. Interesting lectures that focus on studies and fun examples. Good course, tests align decently with lectures.

Would have given him a 5 if not for the $90 Macmillan textbook. 2 tests + final come straight from study guide (if you pay attention in class you don't even have to study). Quiz is online (the reason why we bought the book) so do your thing. Overall very fair and expect you to leave with intro knowledge in Psychology (PSYC1101).

Really interesting and cool guy. Very passionate about what he teaches and very knowledgable. Kind when answering questions and makes the class pretty interesting. Fast paced

reviews.comment: Still taking the class, but the two tests so far have been straight forward and very easy if you read the study guide. Class will be interesting if you choose to pay attention (barely any people do). He definitely knows what he is talking about and has a passion for it

On the first day of the semester, he showed us past feedback he received and then proceeded to say how he has not and will not improve/learn from the feedback. The semester showed how he doesn't care about being a good professor. Honestly, he just sucks. Try to avoid him.

This class was both an undergrad class and somehow a grad level course which didn't make sense from the beginning. There were assignments and lab assignments due on the same day every week. Dr. Spieler is a nice and caring person but is actually a terrible professor. Terrible. During lectures he says a lot of words but not a lot of substance, so it's hard to know what's important. He says a lot of irrelevant things in class and is bad at explaining. Spieler is so passionate & knowledgeable. His lectures were 70% engaging and funny and interesting, 30% boring enough to make me zone out. Overall a great prof. The grading is almost all tests which arent super hard but definitely require studying and are based on the lectures.

I didn't think I would enjoy a Psych class at all and only took it because it is a requirement for the intelligence CS thread, however Spieler made this class exceptional to me. Bad. Just awful.

reviews.comment: Tests are very book-based (recommend getting the book -- it paid for itself after the first exam). Lectures were very enjoyable to attend. He was funny and he very clearly loves what he was teaching.  Gives very low-stakes pop quizzes to encourage attendance.

He is a nice guy, but, he is one of the worst professors I have had at Tech. He is not very good at explaining concepts, which is needed in a stats class. Tests are extremely difficult, so don't be surprised if you fail them. He does curve the class though to compensate (I got a B). Go to class...even if it feels pointless. Good luck...trust me!
No Comments

Pretty interesting guy but lectures were still kinda boring (not mandatory). gives study guides for test 1 week before. gives 3 essay questions before and one of them will be on the test. essay is 1/3 grade and multiple choice is 2/3. 2 exams and 1 final.  each exam is 25 percent of grade. i recommend trying to get easier psych 1101 prof if you can
He's a very eccentric prof, I could tell he really enjoyed Psych and that made the lectures more interesting. Tests are pretty hard b/c it's mainly memorization

"No hope" is the advice he gave for studying for one of our exams. I really liked his lecturing style, he was very funny.

Be prepared to see things on exams you haven't seen before is my only warning.
Funniest prof i ever had

Where do I even begin with Denis... he's just been an amazing professor each time I have had him. He's nice and understanding and is by far one of the most human and enjoyable professors in the BMED department. If I ever see a course being taught by this man, I'm snagging it as fast as I can!

The lectures are okay. The PSS sessions are the most helpful and generally indicate what will be on the test or quiz.

He leans heavily on prior knowledge, especially from statics. He will teach you the problem solving methods which are straightforward, but get harder through the semester, and he expects a lot of self learning.

Great Professor! The real gem comes during PSS where his humor, talent, & knowledge shines. Makes PSS fun to attend and also allows you to learn a lot during class through focusing on problem solving. Biomechanics is primarily graded by (2 tests + final) which are 25% each, so watch out for them and DO THE HOMEWORK without looking at the answer key

He teaches concepts well and always points out the details that are important. His PSS is more helpful than the lectures. Just pay attention and ask questions during the PSS, you will learn everything you need for the exams.

This class is a mess. It combines def bods and dynamics into one class and is bascially graded all by quizzes and exams that will be as hard as they feel like making it that day. The only lectures that were helpful were Desai's in the last third of the semester. Learned everything else through youtube.
The class is difficult, but Denis is so fun and easy to understand. I am always excited to come to lecture. Attendance is very important.

Denis is a great professor. I had him for PSS and found it much more helpful than lectures. He does a great job explaining his work and really lets us know how to succeed in the course. He's pretty funny and blunt and makes class enjoyable. I would recommend him for this course!

Denis is one of my favorite professors I've had. He's funny, lighthearted, and wants you to succeed. "I want to give you all A's- you just have to help me out a little" - Denis. The class is math and computer science heavy. Recitation sections were set up as group activities that was similar to homework and exam questions.

Worst class I have ever taken. Denis is completely useless when it comes to teaching the material and leaves you incredibly unprepared for the tests that are created by the other class instructors. the goat. super compassionate and flexible. loved the content of the class (from Taylor Swift to Hadestown to Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes to Frankenstein, super fun material to work with). definitely take ENG1102 with her if you can!

Dr. Debelius is AMAZING! end of review. 

She's really caring about students, understanding, funny, and gives you extra time on assignments + chances to redo. Just make sure you manage your time and not take advantage of her extensions. Her class is such an easy A because she makes it engaging during class time w/ minimal homework. She's great!

No other explanation is necessary - TAKE THIS CLASS! She's a very caring professor who truly wants to see her students grow. You'll actually grow as a student and person in this class and it's very easy. Just take it.
Nice, respectful, and understanding. Topic for class was Romanticism. Not exactly an easy A, but if you put in what you expect out of it, you'll get the grade you want.

Dr. Debelius is such a caring, understanding professor, and you can tell how much she wants us to succeed. Our unit was Romanticism, and I genuinely enjoyed doing the projects that we had. She is very lenient with grading and late assignments. The assigned reading can be a bit of work, but the pieces are genuinely interesting. Highly Recommend!

Dr. Debelius is a very caring and understanding professor, especially with deadlines and if you have other things going on in life. The projects weren't super heavy and she gives plenty of in class time to work on the larger ones. Also gives detailed and concrete feedback on assignments.

Amazing professor, definitely take her for 1102!!

Course is actually ENGL1101. Amazing professor for a short summer course. Provided clear guidelines on all assignments and provided useful feedback on essays. Class theme was extremely fitting. All around a caring and passionate person. Would recommend to anyone taking ENGL1101 or ENGL1102.

Dr. D is a great professor, take her for English 1102. She is the most transparent professor I've had about grades ever, I was lowkey shocked by how helpful she is and how much she cares about YOU as a student. ez af take her if you want free credits or if you're taking difficult courses alongside 1102

One of the sweetest and kindest professor at Tech. Grading criteria was clear from start and depends on a few projects thru the sem. Flexible grading

Professor Deng is very accomplished in quant finance, but the teaching in this course did not match its importance as a core QCF requirement. Overall solid professor, with good lectures. Tests are difficult but fair for a graduate course.

Arguably one of the most important courses in the QCF program, but it's horribly taught by Deng. He spends most of class talking through the slides on theory/proofs and then glosses over real applications. Quizzes and tests are very hard.
I took his ISyE 6759 and this is the worst class I have ever attended. The exam are super difficult and the homework are completely out of the scope. Stay away if you have a choice.

It's boring and useless with an average GPA 3.03

The homework load was quite heavy and included many stuff that were never covered in class. The lectures and the requirements of the assignments were not clear enough. My biggest gripe were the homeworks. I was a math undergrad but the amount of effort expected for biweekly homeworks was ridiculous. The worst professor I have ever known. You don't want to take his lectures for sure. His homework questions are things that have never been covered in the class and the deducts 10 points from your exam score because you couldn't answer things that were never covered in the class.

This is the worst professor I've ever had. Gives an unreasonable amount of homework, and on materials that are never covered in class. His lectures make no sense whatsoever. And NOT approachable. reviews.comment: Exams from this professor are 100% incongruent with the content exposed in class.

Even though he doesn't have a 5.0 he's still the absolute goat. Notice he's got over 70 5s to Marty's under 30. Not dragging Marty but I've been hearing some Dorozhkin slander and had to come support.

Was an awesome professor. Classes were fun and somewhat interactive. Some of the home work can be quite time consuming to complete, but are fun to do. He is very understanding and considerate. He often gave extensions on homework. Cannot recommend him enough.

He is an awesome and very understanding professor. He makes his assignments very doable, although some might take longer than others. If he saw that few students had turned in a homework he usually gave an extension to all his sections, which was very nice, especially during exam heavy weeks. Can't recommend him enough!

Insanely funny and chill guy, he makes some of the most annoying parts of this class fun. Workload is a lot. The TAs are nasty graders and will take off lots of points for small things. Chill prof and very useful class. I learned almost everything through the VERY LONG hw and lab assignments, not his boring lectures. Assignments graded quite harshly, taking off for little things. Should be an easy A if you do your work with decent effort. Oh also he'll call you out in front of the class if you're late or on your phone or whatever.

There are many benefits of taking Professor Dorozhkin compared to others (access to the best project materials, has free voucher codes for ~$100 SolidWorks test certificates, more flexible for deadlines/requirements, etc.). Awesome prof. Not too tough but hard enough that you learn your stuff. Chill lecture style that's helpful & engaging. Accessible in office hours and happy to help if you have questions on wrangling SolidWorks into shape. Would totally recommend - made 8 am Friday lab fun.

Dorozhkin hasn't lived up to the hype. Rambles during lecture and rushes through the massive amount of content, meaning you rarely retain it. Labs aren't bad but the homework is BRUTAL: several hours a week with unclear requirements. On top of that, the TAs grade very harshly for no reason. There's also 2 projects but they're not that bad.
Lots of work but graded pretty fairly. He is pretty nice but can be a stickler from time to time. Also there is a group project for this class and he chooses groups for you, beware.

I loved Dr. D and his teaching style. He's definitely the most aura 1670 professor and tries to make the lectures more enjoyable even if its an 8am. The grading for the labs can be super harsh along with the assignments, and it can seem stressful. While it might be stressful at first, it keeps you on your toes and they aren't weighted too heavily.

I came into this class with no CAD experience and left it knowing a LOT! The lectures will seem boring, but he posts the slides after if you ever need to reference them. The labs are the most important - he walks through a CAD task and shows you all the necessary elements. It may seem fast a first, but if you need him to repeat a step, he will.

Dr. Dorozhkin is definitely the best choice for ME 1670. reviews.comment: Homework takes a while to do, but hes a great professor and a pretty good lecturer. He seems pretty understanding.

Start the homework early so you can get help if needed. He is great at teaching the content, and he clearly outlines what you need to do to succeed. Take him if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If he is availble then take him.
He is understanding of other classes, so if you have midterms than he will extend deadlines. Don't talk loud in class or he will call you out.
Fun professor, definitely a manageable amount of work. Great intro to Solidworks. Take him if you can, he added 3 points for CIOS and it's an easy A.

Dorozhkin is the goat. He was an amazing professor, and as someone who knew 0 CAD before taking his class, he explained the concepts in a very fun and interesting way. Two projects are worth the majority of your grade (30% each), but he is a lenient grader. ALSO MAKE SURE TO START ON THE HOMEWORK EARLY
this class gave me such a headache. never again.

Some of the topics that are covered in ME1670 are pretty dry but Dr. Dorozhkin made everything as interesting as possible. He was pretty lenient about deadlines. Final grades are mostly based on 2 projects so don't wait until the last minute. He's a very nice, funny guy and the best professor I've had so far.

100% recommend dr d for me 1670. really chill prof but his lectures are very informative. one hw and one lab assignment almost everyweek so start doing them early. the TAs are tough graders but use their office hours, very helpful. but u cannot choose ur team for the team project. gives loads of extensions and is very understanding.

Dr. D is an amazing prof. and he teaches the subject on a very high level. He has pretty lenient grading policies to let student be creative in class and has a really fun personality to boot. I personally think that the hardest part of this class is making sure everything is perfect, because even though he is nice, a lot of the TA's are not.

This dude is one of the most chill professors I've had. He taught us how to sketch (my drawing skills were inadequate before this), and gave us a large window to explore the world of CAD. I also got my nickname of the Backscratcher kid from him :)

To succeed, I recommend starting early on HW, and practice!

Prof. Dorozhkin is awesome, but the TAs are super picky about what they take points off for. I lost so many points on homework for miniscule things, but sometimes my major errors went unnoticed. You can't choose your group for group projects. Pay attention to his lectures whenever you start learning SOLIDWORKS design drawings!

Dr. D >>> Pucha is what you'll hear. Very chill, easy grader. Some assignments were time consuming and frustrating, but that's just the nature of a CAD class. It's significantly less work than other profs. Highly recommend.
He is absolutely amazing and engaging. The content is not bad at all, and you just need to be prepared for a lot of work.

Dorozhkin is the go-to-professor for ME 1670! Light grader, great explanations. Team projects require four SolidWorks parts per person while others may require ten! Meet the requirements: easy A. Always at office hours and willingly gives advices on professional development and CAD practice. He is so funny in lectures and clearly answers questions.
Legit went to like almost all his office hours. My favorite professor by far. He's really chill and super helpful. Take him. GOAT of GOATS

Probably my favorite professor so far. Funny, engaging, and caring. Made class so much fun and, his lectures were straight to the point and easy to understand. He also frequently gave the class extra time to submit assignments for various reasons. Was very knowledgeable and gave students everything they needed to be successful in the class.
Great professor! He was very good at getting straight to the point and always made it clear what he expected.

The class is easy. Any work assigned is usually busy work. There is an individual and group project that takes time. But, he was always willing to extend the deadlines. He is very funny and develops relationships with students. Lectures are kind boring and required, but towards the end of the semester he makes them optional and cancels labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very nice, and frequent funny quips in lecture made it engaging and fun. There were also several points in the semester where he visibly displayed that he thought what we were working on / what he was teaching was cool, which is important for students and is much appreciated.

If gigachad was a professor, Denis Dorozhkhin would be him. Lenient homework extensions (which are super convenient for stressed out weeks), good lectures, clear explanations, and an well-round great professor. Would definitely recommend.
Great professor, always made sure we were following along in class and you can tell he cares. Also can be very lenient with you as long as you talk to him first.
Love this man.

Dr. Dorozhkin has the wit and charm that makes his powerpoint slide lectures legitimately interesting and entertaining. He gives less work than some other ME1670 professors, but you won't miss out on any important learning. The assignments are concise and useful. Plan for the team project ahead of time.
best dude ever
Great professor. Clear explanations and his jokes land. The TA can be a tough grader, but he is not harsh.
Funny professor. Attendance is mandatory but there are no quizzes or tests, just projects, labs, and hw. French TA grades pretty tough though.

Great prof, attendance sucks. Better hope you get a good team. Also avoid the French TA, he loves to give you advice on assignments, then when he grades your work he takes points off because you listened to him. What kind of kink is this?

I'm pretty sure Dr. Denis is one of the best professors I'll ever meet here in Georgia Tech. I really admire and respect him. The material was kind of difficult to me since I'm an international student in my first year, but Dr. D never hesitated to help me with anything and he will even check on you if you are not feeling good. What a great guy.

I liked Dorozhkin a lot. Nice guy, very clear with expectations. The sketching part of the class was annoying, but that's the case no matter who you take. Labs were helpful. You get your individual project printed with a fancy SLS 3D printer with him, so that's cool too.

Pay attention to lectures; they are important for projects. Turn things in time.
Think while using SolidWorks

Lectures were not interesting and hard to follow. Homework was graded to extreme specifications and credit was heavily deducted for minor errors. Corrections were not made aside from labels of 'incorrect'. Professor was not very understanding of circumstances. I received a grade of 0.25/10 on a hw for the wrong file type and could not resubmit.

He is hilarious and knowledgeable about just about everything. The class isn't too challenging, SolidWorks may be a little confusing for beginners and proper dimension sheets (last few assignments) is tedious but other than that there should be no issues for you.
Tries to be funny, and does an admiral job of it. Very lenient and kind professor, willing to make accommodations as necessary, and graded the final project incredibly lightly. Would 100% recommend.
Chill and funny professor. Very knowledgable on Solidworks and will help you out. Lenient on grading. Gets to use awesome 3D printer for one project.

Super funny guy. One of the lowest homework loads for 1670 professor options, so highly recommend taking him! He 3D prints your individual project, so you don't have to coordinate that yourself. Extra credit opportunity given. Really lenient grader on final project reports. Very accessible at office hours. Homework can be long but not too bad.
Dr. Dorozhkin is the best, and I thoroughly enjoyed the class. The workload isn't terrible as long as you don't procrastinate on the cumulative projects.
Dr. Dorozhkin is actually the GOAT.  Man is so funny and really wants students to succeed.  Feel sorry for you if you didn't have him.

Dr. D is an awesome prof. The class is relatively easy, it's just a lot of work. I really enjoyed everything about it; the lectures were fun and chill, the individual project and group project were really fun and provided valuable experience with important skills, and the lectures were entertaining. If you just produce quality work, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: He likes to make jokes and he understands the room. We were right after lunch so he always read the room and ended class early if the mood was off. This class is literally just how much time you put in out of class to draw and CAD. You don't have to be good at drawing, just follow the steps and take your time.
Dr. D was consistently interesting in a class that could easily be painfully boring. He was very fair with grading and always willing to help after class.

Fun proff, learned quite a bit. Alot of assignments that take quite a bit of time but its relatively easy to get an A overall in the class. You don't really need to do the extra credit animation for the final team project unless you messed up alot of the other assignments.

Dr. Dorozhkin's ME 1770 class is hands down the most well-thought-out course I have ever taken, and arguably one of the best overall. He really knows what he's doing and will never give you a mediocre answer to a question. He has a great personality too.

Dr. D is a fantastic choice for 1770. His amazing dry humor enhances what would otherwise be a completely boring course, and he is clearly very knowledgeable when it comes to SolidWorks and engineering best practices.
Dr. D is an awesome professor and I would totally take again. Very funny and makes the class fun
Solid choice for ME 1770. The class itself sucks though.

Dr. D was very nice. He has a sense of humor which seems a bit dry but because it's dry it's hilarious. The class is a good workload. Just follow instructions for the assignments to get through the homework. The group and individual project take up a lot of your grade so make sure you do your best on those.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: TAs will give you bad grades. Don't fret! Give your best in your Individual and Group projects and you'll come through with an A. One of the best profs I had at GT till now!

Denis is an amazing professor! He is always energetic and brings life to what could easily be a boring class. Don't be discouraged if the TA's give you super low grades on the homework. They pretty much count for nothing compared to the 2 projects you do, which Denis will give you a very high grade on. TAKE HIM

Dr Dorozhkin was an amazing professor! His lectures were engaging and funny, the hw really helped develop CAD and drawing skills. Since the class is pretty much project-based you can do little work and get an A. I would recommend putting effort into the class to push yourself, you're gonna have more fun and learn more! TAs are also a good resource!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Gives good feedback--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dorozhkin is definitely the best professor for 1770. The class has a lot of work but some other professors have more work. Basically there's 1 homework assignment a week, occasionally a lab assignment, and 2 big projects that make up most of the grade. He's a funny guy, only complaint is the lectures got pretty boring due to the material.
Dr Dorozhkin is a fantastic, caring professor. His personal stories are very entertaining; especially when he talks about casting lead in the sand. Very accessible for feedback too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Definitely take Dr. Dorozhkin for 1770. This class was a lot of work, but I know people in 1770 with other professors had a lot more work. Pretty much there was one assignment per week and then two main projects. I procrastinated hard on both projects, causing some pretty awful weekends, but the grading was super easy. Pretty easy A if you try.
He's a nice guy but his lectures are boring. The class has a lot of work due to the homework and projects. The TAs grade the homework hard as well. However, you are able to learn a lot.

Dorozhkin is pretty lax on grading as long as all the necessary components are there. His lectures can be pretty dull but he occasionally cracks jokes that can keep it from being too boring. Has a good attitude towards the class and almost always end lab an hour early / lets you leave when ever if its a work day.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Don't take anyone except Dorozhkin for ME 1770. He's funny, good at what he does, and understanding of students. Class can be sometimes boring, but Dorozhkin's in-class attitude and humor makes up for it. Attendance is mandatory so definitely show up. The homework will be time-consuming, but put effort into it and you'll get a good grade. Take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: He is funny, relaxed, and cares for his students. Lectures reflect his chill attitude and aren't too crucial for understanding material. Assignments are simple, and help is always available if needed. They consume a lot of time, especially if you're new to drawing/modeling. The group project is a grind if you procrastinate, but is graded leniently.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Dorozhkin is a really great professor for 1770 and cares a lot about his students doing well in his class. The first section of the class on engineering sketching sucks, but the CAD portion of the class is very interesting. The class is completely HW and project based, there are no tests. Getting HW and work on projects done early is essential.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. D is really funny and tells you exactly what you need to do for the course. He is respectful, though sometimes the lectures get boring. Not hard to get an A.

It has been a wonderful semester with Dr. D. He teaches just enough where the students lose neither themselves nor their drive to learn more. You can do whatever you want and can in his class. He does not impose limits on your capacities. Given that, you will still make a great grade if you show up and follow easily understood guidelines.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. D was a great professor. He makes jokes and you can tell he really understands what he's talking about. I would definitely recommend taking ME 1770 with him!

Dorozkin is a great professor, he is very relaxed and not tough on grading. He is well respected and loves Solidworks. Lectures can be a snore but he is able to make them a little entertaining with his cool personality.

Dr D. is hilarious and does his best to add life to the lecture material, which is miserably boring. The grading criteria is listed on all assignments and as long as you do what it says you will get and A. Grading on the group project is super relaxed and the final presentation was very laid back. You will never have to stay for the entire lab.

Dr. D made ME 1770 really enjoyable. Lots of drawing work at the beginning and the final group project is difficult at times, but overall really rewarding. Gives creative freedom with most assignments. He also has some good jokes, but he can be hard to hear from the back of the class. Projects took awhile to be graded. Overall fun and easy class.

Dorozhkin is the best prof. for ME 1770. The homework was time consuming, but he was an easy grader. If you show that you tried and meet all of the criteria you're basically guaranteed an A. He was funny in lecture and kept the environment light-hearted. Just take his class if you can. You won't regret it.
I loved this class and Dr. D. Super easy. All you have to do is the hw and show up. He just wants to see that you are trying. Not a super hard grader. Would definitely take him again.
Gives some random pop quizzes, so show up. Fun professor overall and not too difficult.

Dr. D is really the best ME1770 professor. The assignments are easy to get full credit if you just meet the bare minimum he requires. The group project does have some stress but you will probably get a 100 on it. As long as you put in some effort, you will get an A. There are no tests or finals, just the group project presentation as a final.

Take. Him. Do. It. He is awesome! The most chill Russian prof at Tech by far ;). He is super nice, super hilarious, super helpful, etc., etc. You do have a good bit of homework outside this class, but it is not difficult, just time consuming, but the CAD homework I really enjoyed. If you are taking ME 1770, everyone knows you gotta take Dorozhkin.

Easy class if you put in the time and effort. He's very chill, but sometimes he seems a bit apathetic about the class. He doesn't do very much to make the material interesting, so I found the lectures boring most of the time, despite having mandatory attendance . Instructions and grading are clear, and his expectations are not too high. Easy A tbh.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Dorozhkin is probably the easiest ME1770 professor. He is very chill and a very lenient grader (although the TAs grade your homework). He is also fairly humorous and incorporates some Russian humor into his lectures, but the material is still quite dry. Also, Dorozhkin may not give as much work, but the class is still fairly time consuming.

Love him. Super easy going and cares about students. Very accessible, has lots of office hours. Only complaint would be sometimes he treats you like you're dumb when asking for help. But his feedback is very helpful. Overall cool guy, and would definitely recommend.

He is a very caring teacher that presents everything in a very accurate manner. He uses a presentation format and gives plenty of chances for extra credit. He has a very dry sense of humor that many people seem to enjoy, he even roasts his students in class sometimes.

Dr. Dorozhkin made class fun with witty remarks and was very helpful with CAD... If you have experience with CAD, the lectures can be a little bit boring (I didn't really pay attention and still got an A). Most HW grades are based on your ability to follow the directions for sketching and CAD; for the individual/final project he doesn't grade harsh

Dorozhkin is AWESOME! Super funny guy, very approachable, easy class. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! He is super helpful with homework and assignments. Funny guy, yet lectures are pretty pointless but that is mostly due to the course material, not Dorozhkin. DONT BUY THE TEXTBOOK. You wont even touch it.

Great professor for 1770. No extremely difficult assignments, willing to offer help when needed. Very nice guy who leads the class well. Overall no qualms. He literally said to our class, "You're really going to have to work hard to NOT get an A in this class." Go to class and do the weekly sketching/CAD homework and the A is yours.
Dr. Dorozhkin's class is extremely straight forward. Simply participate and do the assignments and the A is yours. Very approachable and just an all-around nice guy. Definitely recommend.

Dr. Dorozhkin is super laid back and always kept class very lively with his folksy Russian jokes. Deadlines in his class are usually very flexible and he's regularly available for extra help if you need any. He's also a really lenient grader, although a lot of the grading is done by TAs who may or may not be as lenient as he is .

Hilarious Russian guy that cracks semi-lame jokes in class (which I still found funny), but also teaches the material very thoroughly and is very likely to give points back on homework assignments if you ask him about it. Awesome teacher that made a overwhelming (work load) class easier. Also did not hesitate to push due dates back if necessary.

No tests, just an individual project and a group project.  He assigns intermediate deadlines so you don't get too far behind on either.  Frequent homeworks but not that hard.  I've heard he's a lot easier than the other ME 1770 professors.  As long as you do your work and don't fall behind the class is easy.

Dr. Dorozhkin is very good at teaching and is generally a very easy grader. I definitely recommend him for anyone looking to take ME 1770. He is very approachable and is always willing to help as well.

No tests, 2 easy pop quizzes.  Attendance is 100% mandatory.  I took him his first semester here for 1770.  He has a thick Russian accent but I never have trouble understanding him.  Lots of work, but that's the nature of the course.  Pick simpler topics for projects and pray to God that your group isn't bad.  Would take again.

I enjoyed this class and prof. I think the class is pretty standardized, because the homeworks are from UC Berkley's AI class, but they are interesting and helpful; they're also all autograded and you can submit as many times as you want. There's two midterms and some interviews, which aren't that bad, and you get good feedback from the interviews.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This was an easy course because the prof explained everything in detail. Course is graded by homework, tests and interviews which take time, but are easy using lectures and textbook. Making an A is relatively easy because of all the extra credit opportunities provided. He's very quick to respond to emails and answer questions. Highly recommended.

Really nice professor who clearly has a passion for teaching! The class was difficult but not unnecessarily so. It's hard to understand anything without going to lecture because the slides are not good, so I usually read the book. There are 2 exams which are super tedious for no reason, but they are take-home and you get a week to complete them.

Great teacher, had great examples for lectures and made coming to class very enjoyable! The best teacher to teach law, very nice and funny. The exams are online through canvas, and quizzes online through textbook! Would take again and highly recommend.

I took TBGEN 218 with him at UWT. He knows what he's talking about in class and is very engaging and makes the class interesting. You do need to show up to class to get the extra 14 max points. Doesn't really help you with tests/quizzes if you email but will answer in class and help you out. About 10 quizzes and 3 exams all online at home.

Dhooge was passionate about the subjects he taught. He made law very interesting and easy. There is an online textbook that connects with his lectures, and his exams and quizzes were all take home, so it was easy to digest information and succeed on his assignments. He just doesn't provide barely any feedback on exams and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The prof was really funny and made the class interesting. As long as you pay attention/take notes in lectures, then you'll be fine. Our exams were open-note and covered exactly the info that was discussed in class, so it's nothing unexpected. We also had a few days to complete the exams, so there is ample time.

Dr. Dhooge was an extremely engaging professor whose lectures were interesting on a day to day. Fair but firm grading criteria made of tests and quizzes. Assessments were open note, but not to be taken lightly, often tests stuff said only in lectures so be sure to attend. Great guy, but refused to round me 0.33% for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All tests and quizzes are taken from home, but you will struggle if you don't attend class. Information can be boring sometimes, but he tries to make it fun. He is a really cool guy, and I advise to take his class over any other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures can be a little boring, but all tests and quizzes are done online asynchronously so basically guaranteed A. Just pay attention in class and kinda interesting in class
God Tier. 100%

Dhooge is amazing. His lectures are engaging and easy to follow. The amount of reading was fair, do the reading before class it makes the material much easier to absorb during his lectures. There were two exams, a project and participation. The multiple choice exams were straight forward. Come to class and you get a 100 for participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures can be tedious because they are long and the material is not always exciting, but it's worth attending. He cares so much about the subject matter and really tries to make it interesting. One of the best professors I've had at Tech. He's a gem and is happy to help you with anything you need.
Outstanding professor. While the class is content-heavy, he makes it easy for students to remember cases through the use of relevant, relatable, and interesting examples.
I really liked him. He told us a bunch of cool stories about his time as an attorney. Lectures could get boring at times but they weren't that bad. Tests were all take home, open book, open note.

Professor Dhooge is an amazing teacher who has definitely adapted to teaching online. You do need to buy a textbook(over $100) in order to submit the quizzes, but the lectures are easy to follow and funny. Participation isn't required, but if you don't go to class and take notes, you will not do well in this class.

He's super passionate, lawyer who is really knowledgable about the field. Two, forty-question test and on group project. He lets you use a cheat sheet and gives you the topics that will be covered for the test. He gave a lot of points for attendance and his lectures are a joy to be in. He's an amazing person and prof!

Professor Dhooge is such an incredible teacher. He is engaging, interesting, easy to connect to, and it's obvious how much he cares for the class. I was not expecting to like a law class, but he made it so interesting that I found myself discussing the topics with him and my fellow classmates after class every day (without fail).

One of the best professors I have had! The lectures are very entertaining and he has a lot of fun stories about his own experiences. The test are pretty easy as he gives you study guide of what is going to be on it. There are only three test but he added in some reading quizzes this year. Pay attention in class and you should be good!

Professor Dhooge is by far and away one of the best professors at Scheller. There are only 3 test so yes each is high stakes but if you read your notes and pay attention in lecture no reason you cannot earn a high A. He tells funny stories. Lecture can get boring during certain subjects but he keeps it interesting for the most part.

Your class grade is made up of 3 tests that are equally weighted, and are easy if you study and pay attention in class. His lectures are wonderful. He is funny and has wonderful stories that bring the content to life. He recommends a textbook at the beginning of the textbook, but most of my notes came from the lecture.

This guy is AMAZING. He makes every class interesting and cares about his students. Honestly one of the best professors I've EVER had. He likes to tell lots of anecdotes, and if you understand the basic concepts he teaches, the tests are common sense. The only downside is that each test is 1/3 of your grade, no participation or extra credit points.

Professor Dhooge is the best! Always willing to help and is very caring. There are only 3 tests including the final, so it leaves little room to mess up. However, if you pay attention in class and take the time to study, you can get an A. It's for sure not a class where you can just read over the notes a couple hours, it requires a deep study.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I love this man!!! Really good teacher! I was terrified going into the class knowing there would only be 3 tests to make up your whole grade, but I made a 100, 90, and 93 on them so it wasn't bad if you put in the work and really study. Also didn't use the textbook at all - test material really just came from lectures so try not to miss any.

He only gives 3 multiple choice tests for the entire course so each test is heavily weighted and there's not a lot of places you can mess up on. He's not flexible about changing grades, he goes by the syllabus strictly. He also recommends the textbook but from my experience, it was mostly useless and a waste of money. Hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a lawyer, so he definitely knows his stuff and is good at teaching. Tests comprise of 40 Multiple Choice, and there are only 3 tests total (including the final). Very hard to make an A. Can make a B easily if you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Dhooge! He made lectures engaging and interesting. Although the tests are challenging, if you pay attention during class, you should be fine to get an A.
Good teacher but remember only 3 tests that comprise the entire grade and tests are very arbitrary. Overall, nice guy and very enjoyable class; it's easy to pass but hard to make an A.
Dhooge is a talented teacher but his tests are very tricky and since there are only 3 test grades in the class i would advise not to take.v Find professor with more grades.
Fun teacher, fun class, pretty hard tests though each test 1/3 of grade..

Good professor, very interesting, but tests were very confusing in terms of applying what was taught. Also no cheat sheets allowed, tests only consisted of 30 or so questions, so there was little room for error. Attendance wasn't mandatory but I highly advise it seeing the majority of the test was stuff he talked about in class.

Dhooge is a great professor.  Had 3 exams, which were 30 percent each, and attendance was 10 percent.  attendance consisted of him calling out your name to answer a question in class, but he stopped like 3 weeks in.  tests weren't bad, you could have a cheat sheet.  highly suggest taking him.  Easy A or B, depending on how hard you try

Very easy to get full credit on homework and participation. His lectures were not very good at all, but I think if you went and tried to pay attention you could understand everything you need to. I would not take him if you care about learning proofs, but I would say it is an easy A.

I don't remember him ever laughing at anyone, contrary to what the other reviews say, but I can attest to his strictness at times. Still, the lax grading allowed me good flexibility with doing my work. Homework is based on effort and not correctness. The weekly presentations may get you grilled if you don't put in the work, but they're alright.

He is mean and disrespectful to students. He will laugh at you in front of the class if you get something wrong during a presentation. Final was ridiculously difficult and was the only exam for the entire semester.
Avoid at all cost, exam is too hard to complete on time, and final exam contains all the previous content, which is hard to review all of them.

Class was incredibly easy as if you just showed up you basically needed a 40 on the final to get an A. Biggest issue was his accent but otherwise his lectures were not as bad as people say. If you're a math major and complaining about the difficulty of this class or "how tough the grading was." Yeah these are proofs. You need to find a new major.
do not take. laughs at students proofs and is rude, and expects you to know everything.

He had weekly presentation for proofs which was kinda odd. The class did a point system where you can earn 20 points for hw, 50 for presentations and 50 on the final, so 120 points total, standard cut off. He is super strict and doesn't understand english well, takes points off for saying things in way he doesn't understand,  also very dismissive
So much harder than every other semester of Combo.
This guy is so bad. He is basically impossible to understand, his exams have no similarity to the practice materials provided like previous exams. Avoid at all costs.

Comparatively his tests are easier, but with that said and emphasis on comparatively, they're easier just because he cannot teach or answer questions or even prepare us for exams. On the last exam the average was a 65, and with that being said he refused to curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had him for MATH2551. Notes and explanations are very confusing, and asking questions would just get you a confusing look.  Relied on recorded lecture videos throughout the semester.

I currently have him for Math 2551, honestly he's not the best, and please try to avoid him, his lecture notes make no sense and he doesn't either. I personally did not think his first two exams the averages were around 80s but for the third exam the average was a 65, he is also really dismissive and rude in office hours.

He knows the content, but in chinese. His accent and stutter gets in the way of every understanding anything, and his lecture notes often end up looking like chicken scratch so good luck understanding what's on the board if you look away. He often glosses over questions saying that he doesn't understand and then just moves on. Tests are easy though
Had him for multivariable calclus please avoid him for ur sanity and GPA
Ding's voice makes him seem funny and friendly at first. However, he is unhelpful. His thick accent makes lectures impossible to understand. I would definitely avoid him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very thick accent made it very hard to understand him. The class was very unforgiving since it was based on 3 exams and homework. If you can, avoid him.
I can't understand his explanations and his metaphors are weird
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Changxin was a decent choice for Applied Combinatorics. At the beginning of the semester, I had doubts as it was his first semester in Atlanta, but he did a good job teaching the information. My main gripe is that it was difficult to succeed as you are only graded on HWs, 2 midterms, and a final. But he did curve the final by 14 points.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Stopped going to lecture because he just read off of the slides that were posted anyways. He sped through class because he would skip things or not explain. He was nice if he understood what you were talking about. Has an accent but it's not impossible to understand.

His teaching was horrible. I don't know if it's because he's new to teaching but he basically reads off slides only; literally shows us what's on there and that's it with almost no explanations. Learned the entire course on Youtube with "Professor V" instead and used old exams as practices, got away with a solid B in the course

This professor is genuinely funny, and I really enjoy visiting his office hours—we always end up talking about our favorite video games. He's incredibly kind, and after every exam he reassures me that partial credit will be given, which is always comforting. The class itself is very straightforward as long as you attend PLUS sessions and studios.

Every calc 2 class takes the same exact exam, so the only difference between each class is who you take it with. Dr Ding is a very nice person but it is difficult to learn from his lectures. It's significantly easier to learn from Dr. Grodzinsky's lecture videos on canvas then go to class. 
Grade breakdown 
15% homework 
2% extra credit
85% exams

He's honestly a very caring person, but has a horrible teaching method. He has a habit of not thoroughly explaining the example problems and showing the full steps, just reads off the slides, and when asked a question, he doesn't explain it fully.

You're better off just attending another professor's lectures. My grades improved after doing that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He cares so much but very hard to understand. His pencil broke so he just shows the practice problems on the board with no context and poor explanations. Better off learning on your own or going to a different lecture. But he is very sweet and cares.

Only 2/3 tests count, including the final. Really clear and slow lecturer that goes over how inference tests conceptually work. She uses a random generator for attendance taking, so its a 50/50 that she'll take attendance on any given day. The lab component is also very easy and doesn't require attendance at all.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is an incredibly thoughtful professor who is aware that most people have to take it because it's required, brings a warm and positive energy to the class that is very refreshing. Tests are very fair and don't try and trick you with questions and are accurate to how you understand the material
Very thorough explanation and makes difficult concepts unbelievably easy to understand! Super sweet professor too.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things
