reviews.comment: BMED 1000 isn't a hard class, and Dr. Zerbe is great.

I took BMED 1000 with Dr. Zerbe and thought she was great. The class itself wasn't my favorite, but she clearly cared about all of us and was passionate and knowledgeable. All of her expectations with assignments are clearly laid out in rubrics and you have opportunities to resubmit work if you really mess it up. Overall great prof!
Shes a good professor. The class is very group project heavy and is graded by a few things, which she can be a little tough on. Very nice person, good for advice as well!

Made it clear how each unit was supposed to contribute to something broader. Some of the assignments felt redundant but none of them were hard. If you get a good group (they're randomly assigned at the beginning) then it's light

The professor is chill and passionate about what she teaches. The class is fine, but be careful of due dates since they don't post those on Canvas. You're responsible for submitting the assignments on time, but figuring out when is confusing.
Dr. Zerbe was a good professor. She was understanding and passionate about the field. The class, however, did not have due dates on canvas so it was a bit difficult to keep and turn in assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: It's a very easy class with a really nice professor. I got above 95% on all assignments. Lectures can be boring at times, but I still had a fun time in class.

awk lil guy most times. put in SOME form of effort and you'll end w an A. dont like how useless going to his classes felt w presentations every session about how to do work when we've been in school for quite awhile now... didnt LOVE the topic but also not the worst ever. dont take the 5-6:15 time you will never want to go. would retake!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class is very easy with a light workload. However, I would take another section of 1102 if available. The topic is Shakespeare which got very boring and the assignments were super repetitive. But if you are just looking to get the credit this course is by no means bad. Its just that there are better/more fun options with other professors.

while his lectures got a little boring from time to time, you can tell he's really passionate about his discipline. he is an extremely nice man, and before breaks would bring little treats for the class and wish us all happy holidays. he's a very easy grader but will also provide useful feedback on projects. he's very approachable as well.

Dr. Emiliano is a great professor, very sweet and enjoys what he teaches. The class isn't difficult, but the lectures were pretty boring. The workload is extremely manageable and there were plenty of group projects throughout his course.

I would recommend Professor Gutierrez for 1102! This class was focused on Shakespeare, and while I am not a huge Shakespeare fan, the class was interesting and not hard! No exams or essays; rather, you work either independently or in group projects. He is very accessible, and he loves when people participate in class. Overall, a very chill class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very easy grader and is very lenient and accessible outside of class. It is extremely hard to not get an A if you just do the work, which isn't that time consuming anyway. Overall just a great teacher, take him for 1102.

He's AMAZING! Genuinely cares about students and easily accessible outside of class. Textbook is recommended but not required. The course is project-focused and it's very easy to get an A as long as you put in the effort.
Dr. gutierrez is a very sweet and caring professor. He genuinely cares a lot about the material and talking to students and his class is very enjoyable
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Easy grader and a caring teacher. He loves participation in class and listening discovering new perspectives. All around, I kinda disliked his topic (Shakespeare) so be weary if you do not enjoy Shakespeare that much. I thought I liked it but I guess not to the extent of his scope. Either way, very chill guy and certainly a great person!

He genuniely cares about the course material and his students. The class is an easy A as long as you have decent quality work (won't take that much time) - I don't think anyone in my section didn't get an A. He is engaging and helpful, I asked plenty of questions and he would always be willing to help and answer me.

Dr. Gutierrez is a great English 1102 professor. If you put in the effort, you will get close to a 100 on all assignments. There are few papers, and the course focuses more on projects (group and individual). His lectures are mostly useless, but he does give you time in class to work on your assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a good professor that gives a lot of projects which are mostly essays or writing based but also some projects focused on video production and art. He also gives great feedback if you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not too much work. He looks for enthusiasm and effort
Great professor! Class was pretty simple and was not too much writing as I had anticipated, rather had more projects which were interesting. Highly recommend!

Really nice guy, and a good professor. My only criticism would be that some of the lectures were a bit boring and unnesceasry, but the overall class was great. He is a really fair grader and the assignments are not too difficult. The class was overall pretty interesting and the professor does a good job giving feedback. Should be an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Unconventional and interesting assignments which did not require a massive time commitment. Very approachable and flexible professor who is clearly passionate about his job. One of my favorite professors at Tech thus far (and I usually hate English).

Very kind professor and was always willing to work with students to resolve issues. Also generally a very light grader as long as work is completed on time and as specified in directions. Would absolutely take again

We didn't learn that much in MSE 3025 but I don't think that's really her fault. I think she was a fine lecturer but the content was just pretty simple and I think she was aware of that bc she didn't really care if we paid attention or not and would end lectures early/cancel class more than most to not waste our time

Lectures are extremely dull, covering what feels like 20 mins of content in 75, but tests are open notes and the content is extremely straightforward. Print the notes and take them to exams and you'll do well. Very little programming in this numerical methods class, except for one (very simple) project.

Class is based on participation, 2 tests, and a final. Participation is a bucket point system, and any extra points are extra credit. Tests are very similar to the practice tests she gives to help study. She gave very good lectures that taught what you needed to know. only complaint is that I wish she used piazza, ed discussion, etc.

Dr. Hu is a great teacher! She is very kind and she truly cares about each student getting a good grade. She always has office hours and reviews exam questions during them. The class is based off of homework memorization.

She had really good lectures often complemented with long textbook sections (optional). Her study guides did not do a great job of covering exam material, though. I also wish she was more accessible outside of lecture; it's tough reaching her, and there was no forum where students could ask questions. Not a bad professor all in all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sanders is the best option for 2016. Her lecture notes are very clear and you can probably get away with just that and the textbook, but I'd recommend going to class. Her lectures were directly related to the hw and exams (which had no matlab btw), which other 2016 profs had a problem with.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Sanders is very knowledgeable and super accessible for help. Homework can be hard, but she's ready to help if you're willing to work earnestly. Homework every week (Matlab coding) and written exams ( straight from lectures). I would take her again!

She is the best ME 2016 professor by far. While homeworks may take a little bit, office hours help a ton, and her homeworks are much more doable than other professors. Her lectures really help with the homework as well. Her tests are extremely fair and straight forward. Probably one of my easier classes this semester.

Lecture material is all there but the HW was sometimes very confusing and took minimum 6 hours weekly. Exams were fair and the practice exams helped a lot. Course itself is boring so can't blame the prof on that. 2 midterms 1 final and 10 HWs.

Professor Stas is a very entertaining and enthusiastic lecturer. He has a harsh style of lecturing and even harsher tests. However, he truly does care about the class and does want to see everyone succeed in their own ways.

I can't recommend him enough. He's explains complicated concepts very well holds engaging lectures. He's VERY flexible with due dates and is very down-to-earth with what he expects from students. Exams are very reasonable and can easily be studied for by reviewing HWs and previous exams.

Best professor I've had at Tech so far. Extremely effective lectures and is very accessible outside of class. Class is set up so that you don't have to stress about grades. Assignments and exams are very reasonable. Provides A LOT of resources.

Awesome professor, he knows the concepts and cares about students. One time when I didn't submit a homework assignment, he emailed me to check that everything was alright. He has a great brand of humor and makes concepts interesting and intuitive. Tests are average difficulty, as it homework. He has great availability for office hours.

Dr. Endert is a great lecturer and very caring professor. Topics were relevant and I learned a lot, even though I usually don't pay attention in "memorization-based" classes. That being said, the beginning is a little boring but it gets more interesting later, and the final project can be fun if you have a good group. Exams and HWs are easy.

Good choice for an easy elective. Endert is a good lecturer and is engaging to listen to. He is also in general a friendly guy and makes himself pretty accessible. Homework assignments were very straightforward, and so were the exams if you just attended/watched the lectures. The bulk of the class is the group project, so just pick good teammates.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lectures are recorded so attendance isn't required. Unfortunately the lecture content is very boring, but not difficult. There are also coding labs that progressively get harder in Javascript D3, and you need to learn it yourself since lectures don't cover it.
Exams aren't too bad, labs get harder as semester goes on. Records the lectures so you can go back and review even if you miss class.

Professor Endert doesn't really teach in this class, instead every class is led by a difficult student group who lead a presentation on an assigned paper and the class discusses. Class ended early every time but the discussions and topics were interesting. The assignments were graded easily and not very time consuming.

This course is structured with one paper each class, all culminating in a group project. The assignments were moderately time consuming but interesting and ultimately easier than other classes.

He is a great lecturer and has great command over the topics, and the class interactions were quite interesting.

The class was meh, he taught well but it was definitely a lot of content which made it hard to follow especially because you have to know so much for the exams just for half it to not be there. Make sure you start the labs early because they can catch up to you. Always use the TAs and other students in the class cause they'll be your life support.

6730 with Endert is a great class to take. He is super knowledgeable and tries to keep lectures engaging. Basically, if you just pay attention in class and keep up with the group project, you'll be all set. Homework assignments are not very time consuming, exam material comes straight from lectures, and everything is graded pretty leniently

You learn nothing useful from lectures. You have to learn all coding stuffs by yourself with a provided source that is not clear. Test contents are ridiculous and tedious. You need to memory over 300 slides for each exam. You might get a high score but this is the most boring course I took in GT.

Memorization of lists, taxonomies, etc. Not hard per se, but annoying. The labs have nothing to do with the lectures, and the recitation just covers what's in the labs. Just a strangely organized course, imo. The labs are super easy, and the material is too. I just don't feel like the structure fosters a very exciting or productive experience.

He's the typical average professor you get. Not the best, not the worst. The info viz class specifically is pretty heavy memorization and paying attention in his boring lectures only helps for the exams. Class says you don't need to know javascript but the programming labs are worth 40% and lectures / TAs are pretty useless for it.

Professor's teaching was alright. However I can't condone his behavior and unprofessionalism. This one time I went up to him after class to ask him about a question I got wrong on my exam, and he got all angry at me. How dare I even question the grade I got? All I wanted was to ask why I got it wrong since the grading didn't show me why..

Info Viz with Endert was pretty solid. He is passionate about the subject, however, a bit on the dry end in terms of lecture. The midterm is mostly memorization of slides and the homework and prog assignments were not challenging. He did mention that future semesters will have a lab component so it might be more work than previous semesters.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Weigel is a very caring and nice professor...but her style of teaching is somewhat vague and you need to know how to code (use R) for the final project even though she rarely teaches it and provides the prompts for assignments. Her test questions are also vague and the TAs are harsh graders. However, the grading scheme is fair.

She was very kind even though the content was a little boring. The grading criteria was very helpful - there's two schemes that maximize your grade! Each test had 2 parts with one being multiple choice and the other part being a "take-home" test that you can work on with a group. The final project was a lot of work so be sure to have a good group.
Amazing, kind professor. Very patient and caring, wants you to succeed. She was also my academic advisor and she went above and beyond to help me. She is a great person.

I took this course in the Fall of 2021. Professor Weigel is passionate about what she teaches. The coursework is not demanding, but does include a lab, which is where most of the work for this class will be done. If you find Biology boring, this will not be a fun class, but it will be easy. If you like it, you will love this class with Weigel

This course is online synchronous and there were two grading schemes. One was test heavy one was homework heavy which is very helpful if you are not a good test taker. There is a lot of group work during class (breakout rooms) and you can tell she genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed in this course.

This was one of the most pointless labs every at GATech. The instructions for the project were unclear, boring, and required WAY too much work. Does not give credit for small errors (like an extra space at the end of a word) even if everything else is perfect. Very passive aggressive to students as well and will not admit fault.

Dr. Weigel, as a lab director, is very open for communication and will respond to you promptly. That said, the structure of the Ecology lab is not great and many things are designed to force more work onto the students. Prepare to write lots of papers. It will, however, prepare you for future paper-heavy lab courses.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Weigel is strict on her policies and allows for no creative flexibility or room for failure. She expects constant attention and a passionate obsession for the subject.

She is one of the most considerate teachers i know, but her class is structured terribly. It is entirely flipped classroom and she requires you to teach yourself on your own and exams are very very difficult. This class made me switch my major.

Dr. Weigel is amazing. She not only teaches the material well, but she honestly cares about her students and tries to give them every opportunity to succeed. She's the first professor I've had that says "take care of yourselves" and tries to make it possible for you to do that.

Dr. Weigel is so caring and truly wants her students to succeed, and also provides some extra credit. The class is very content heavy so that is difficult but make sure you read the textbook and you should be fine. She's one of the kindest teachers I've ever had.

Weigel was in charge of the Ecology labs but you have a pair of TAs as your instructors so you don't ever see her in person during the semester. However, she's very responsive on Piazza and via email. Be prepared to code (R) during lab and write a LOT. You have a lab report due at the end of the semester. And she offers extra credit which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was so hard, but Dr. Weigel is an amazing professor and is so understanding if you do struggle. If you reach out for help/advice/feedback she will respond so kindly & her feedback is detailed and personalized to your own performance. She just really cares about her students. Her class will challenge you academically, but in the best ways

Lectures were amazingly informative and easy to follow. I wasn't a fan of the excessive participation and reading but it was a very structured class and everything helped build understanding and encourage students. Tests were open note but hard because of strict time constraints and LOTS of content. Don't be fooled into thinking it's an easy A.
Open note tests and your best test is weighted more. Class is listed as synchronous, but all lectures are recorded, so you can just watch whenever you want. Awesome teacher.

The textbook is free, but the units are ridiculously long and detailed. She included so much information on tests that I walked away learning less than I would have if she just taught the bare minimum. Grading depends on the TA, but be prepared to get points off for citations on papers. The class is "easy" but annoying/time-consuming for what it is
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Weigel's class was difficult, but she cares so much about her students and goes above and beyond to make sure they understand the material. I genuinely enjoyed the material because she made me so eager to come to class every day. Dr. Weigel is seriously the best.

Dr. Weigel cares so much about her students. She makes every student feel respected even in a class of over 100. She is a great lecturer who is passionate about the material. She made me interested in the material and want to learn. Highly recommend!

She taught alongside Dr. Harrison, and I prefer her over him. Granted, the content she teaches might be easier, as they said the class gets easier as you go, but her lectures make more sense than his, and she found ways to make the class more interactive and fun in an online setting. She really cares about the well-being of all her students.
Dr. Weigel was an amazing professor. She cares about her students more than any professor Ive ever had and was more than willing to help. Really great professor.

Ecology was taught by her and another professor, her half was much better. It is clear that she wants to make the content interesting and fun (she made a whole review session themed around her cat and a kitten she found). It is possible to get an A, but you might have to work for it.

Ecology can be a tough class, because there's not always a correct answer. However, Dr. Weigel really makes this class exciting for her students. She cares a lot about you, both in and out of the classroom. She's a great lecturer and she is always coming up with new activities to engage students. She works hard to make the class interesting.

BIOS 2301 is TA-led and a difficult class overall. It involves RStudio, and if you have a background in computer science it would be very beneficial. I did not, but I managed to get through the work with help. Overall the class is very interesting and relevant, and it's helpful to learn how to write research papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Weigel is super nice and a great professor. Participation in this class is important, but once you get the basics down the class isn't too bad. She'll answer any questions you have. She's also super down-to-earth and pretty chill. She dressed up as two dozen different characters during Halloween, if that gives you an idea.

She really cares about her students and she lectures really well. I didn't go to lecture often and just learned from the textbook though. Tests cover huge amounts of material, and often ask about random details you probably overlooked. The generous grading scheme with built in extra credit makes it very possible to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Weigel is a great lecturer. She is clear and engaging. On top of that, she very deeply cares about her students outside of the Biology classroom as well.

This is my second time having Dr. Weigel, and she continues to amaze me. She cares a ton about her students, is extremely helpful during office hours, and is really forgiving (in terms of the grading scheme of the class). Her passion is contagious, and it's something you want to be around especially if you have to take bio but aren't a sci major.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She cares a lot about her students.

Dr. Weigel is an amazing person. She is a very chill professor who cares a LOT about your well being. She is a very chill person and has a grounded and funny lecture style. If you have a chance to take her I would definitely recommend it.

this class is a ton of work and if you don't need to take it specifically do not take it!! Dr Weigel really cares about her students and will help you but I can not stress how much work this is. There are a lot of boosting assignments that will boost your grade up. If you get mid Bs on exams you can for sure get an A in the class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Weigel is a FANTASTIC lecturer. She's always prepared for lecture and brings a tremendous level of positive energy. She's young, which also makes her seem relatable. She's one of those professors with whom you feel comfortable right off the bat. You can tell that she really cares about her students and wants the best for them. 10/10 recommend.

Dr. Weigel is one of Techs gems. Shes an amazing lecturer, and the material is genuinely interesting. Shes super engaging, and although there is lots of reading, she can be approached for help both in and out of class. Not an easy A, but definitely can do well if you try. Recommend her wholeheartedly! You wont regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Weigel is very straightforward about what is required for this class. They do require that you do the lecture's reading before attending class; however, she then goes through it thoroughly in class. She also provides a practice test because she really does want you to succeed. Some modules are detail-heavy, but they don't make it too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: flipped class so lots of reading and self-learning. First two tests are pretty difficult, but after that the class gets a lot easier. Grading is extremely fair, and even despite the content being quite difficult, a lot of people consider the class easier than other intro sciences. Certainly requires work, but it's more than possible to do very well
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Weigel knows a lot about biology and you can tell she's passionate about what she's teaching. The class required a lot of reading, but all of the participation assignments were graded for participation. Tests were fairly easy and matched the structure of the practice tests pretty well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class has been a mess all semester, but Dr. Weigel has by far exceeded the other prof. She understands what she's talking about and is patient and very accessible. Tests are extremely fair and the class grading is not bad. Lots of reading because it is a flipped format. She will be a great prof when she understands how to run a class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She really cares about her students and always helps out in office hours. Some of the material is challenging, but always go to offie hours right before the test!

The course was flipped format, which I didn't like, and there was no textbook, but if you memorize/understand the material presented in class you'll do well. Dr. Weigel was nice and seemed to care. The final was made mostly of questions from the midterms, and there was grade replacement, so in the end everything worked out.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Great teacher. Her ecology class wasn't too bad, and she really wants the students to learn the material, so there are a lot of extra credit and grade replacements.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing professor she actually cares about what you say and will make adjustments based on your needs. Really engages with the material to help you understand it not just memorize it. There are only two tests but final grade replacement was used in our class.

She clearly cares about her students and about the subject matter. Her lectures engage the class and she really makes an effort to talk about things that are interesting to us. One of my favorite professors so far!

Dr. Weigel made the best out of an otherwise annoying class. Criteria for the tests was always very clear, and she was responsive to the concerns of the class. Take her if you can; she's very laid back.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Weigel is an incredibly witty professor and makes for a very good lecturer. Her tests are reasonable. Go to recitation. Attendance not mandatory, but keep up with the Learning Catalytics.
Weigel is the clearest professor about her exam criteria and make up. If you go by her given learning objectives, go to recitation, and do her IKE and TICAs, you've got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Weigel taught the latter half of general ecology which honestly saved my grade from the first professor. Her lectures and expectations are incredibly clear and comprehensible. She is an overall friendly and approachable, as well as knowledgeable, professor who cares a lot about student progress and feedback. 10/10 would recommend.

Out of the 3 biology professors that taught BIOL1510 for fall 2016 (Choi, Kerr & Weigel), her test was the most straight forward. Like her test was my first A, my first decent test score. Her lectures are pretty cool too. I feel like they probably planned this on purpose to give us hope that we might have a chance in the class or something.

By far the most frustrating professor I've had. Doesn't respond to piazza posts or emails (only when convenient), 2 quizzes worth 40% of your grade with extremely minimal prep, homeworks sometimes skipping lectures ahead. When I asked what I could do to improve my grade, I was told that she was not God from her directly. Do not take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The structure of this class has it to where two quizzes taken during the beginning of the course have a LARGE impact on your grade but really they are both tests. She is also not receptive if you don't form a quick understanding of topics in the course and is very hard on regrades even if there are actual mistakes in the grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 2 quizzes each worth 20%, 1 is a review of 2027. 2 projects each worth 20% with 2 hours to complete them. She's rude when you ask questions and moves to fast when going over simio. Half of her HWs have nothing to do with what we learned in class. Always finding myself using previous notes to do her HW. Not a "hard" class but she's unbearable.

SHOW UP TO CLASS. Zhou is pleasant and will use her lectures to walk you through problems; if you do not attend and take notes, you will fail your projects, but pay attention and you will be fine. Her quizzes are reasonable and she is quite lenient with homework.

The previous ratings don't apply anymore, she completely changed the course syllabus. She has two "quizzes" which are 20% each and covers maybe half the material in the class. The midterm and final project are really difficult and are not a good representation of the material taught. Teaching is ok but it is hard to follow the presentations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She knows the course materials well and is very clear in lectures (her lecture notes are amazing). Her classes are not math heavy and focus a lot on the application side. There are a lot of quizzes and labs. Some of them are challenging, but you can drop two of these. If you follow her lectures and do the homework carefully, you should get an A.

She is honestly one of the meanest professors I have ever had. Stops our presentation in the middle of the slide to tell us she doesnt need to know something. She laughs at us. Does not even read the documents we send her and leaves the rudest comments. Also interrupts all the time while we are still talking. Such a mean and rude professor.
The labs were incredibly difficult, but the tests weren't too bad. She has a very good layout for presenting material.
Great professor! A lot of quizzes and labs in one semester, but also offer more opportunities to gain points during the semester.  Plus, her grading policy is lenient.

She was very caring and considerate, and was incredibly focused on helping us learn the material. She always ensured there is enough room and comfort to ask questions about the material. She presented good background information. She knows the industry and had good examples. Her homework is difficult, but she offers great help at office hours.

Probably the worst professor at Tech. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. She will spring surprise assignments on you due dead week, if you ask her for help she'll tell you about her straight A college career, and she reads off of he other professor's slides. She has no idea what she's doing. 10/10 would not take her class again.

Dr. Ensley was a blast of a professor. One of the single nicest professors I've ever met. The class involved a lot of reading different books and passages as well as discussions about them, but Dr. Ensley made sure that engagement was interesting and worthwhile. Fully recommend for any class you have to take with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr Ensley was my Introduction to British Literature professor. She is incredibly kind and caring. Her lectures were always enjoyable and interesting, and class was never boring. One of my favorite professors. Highly recommend taking a course (or multiple) from her if you have the opportunity.

Very fun class. Most of the readings were interesting. Lots of class discussion. The grade is primarily in a few projects, which are graded generously. I asked for time extensions on nearly all of the projects, and Dr. Ensley was always happy to give them, even though I didn't give much of a reason (basically I had quizzes in other classes).

Best professor ever. She's so sweet and actually cares about courseload and your life unlike a lot of other professors. Getting an A is just making sure you do your work. Much better than the professor I took for 1101! Highly recommended.

Take her! She's a wonderful prof and was extremely considerate that I took her class from a totally different timezone (12 hrs ahead). Gave extensions as needed. Very clear with feedback and helped me with non-class writing for a personal project. Great person, wish I could have taken the class in-person with her.

Dr. Ensley is by far the best English professor I've ever had. Initially, the course topic ("What is English?") seemed boring, but the readings and projects she assigned made it a lot more interesting. While her grading is strict to the rubric, she gives great feedback and is flexible (especially during COVID). Great choice for ENGL overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Ensley is super sweet and caring, especially during COVID. She cares a lot about the class material, although I did not find it to be that interesting. She grades fairly and gives a lot of feedback, although some of the homeworks and assignments feel unnecessary and like a waste of time. Decent choice as a prof
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr Ensley is super passionate about the topics she teaches, and I had a great time in her class this semester. She also really cares for her students, and is always very understanding and helpful.

I loved Dr. Ensley's class! The theme was the supernatural in early english literature (which I had little interest in prior), but Dr. Ensley was engaging and very passionate. She did not take the class too seriously, but was serious enough (her expectations were clear and fair).
She is so sweet and kind, always willing to help you. As long as you put effort in your work, you will do well. She grades participation, so you should participate.

Dr. Ensley is great!! She is super understanding and willing to give extensions if you ask in advance. She grades fairly and gives you the opportunity to revise a project/essay if you get below an 85. I definitely recommend!

She is a fairly good grader, and I really hope I get her for ENGL 1102 next semester. She's passionate about what she teaches, and many of her homework assignments are completion grades. Very few graded projects for accuracy. So glad I had this professor. Love you Mimi!!

I had Engman for Math 2551 - I went to class three times and got an A on every test and a 97% on the final. He's not a great teacher (the voice is hilarious), but he's a kind grader and fair at the end of the class! I would suggest him for multivariable if you have a strong math/ calc background.
If I hadn't already taken calc in high school, this would have been terrible. Super confusing to listen to but not too much work overall.

He's a super nice guy, but not good at all at explaining things. He gets distracted during lecture, which makes it hard to know what to study. Lectures are dull and confusing. He also has to change the schedule a lot because of getting distracted in lecture and not covering the material. Go to recitation, it helps.
Not a great professor for a low level math class, just hope that your TA is good and can explain it to you. Honestly though you can pretty much get an A by just doing the problems he sets out

I had background in AP Calc, so this class wasn't terrible, but lectures were really boring and unclear. I felt like the lectures were more complicated than tests. Recitation was helpful and HW assignments were pretty easy. Tests were not difficult, often times we were given similar questions in recitation before the exam. I would take it again.

Marty is so boring and hard to understand (he mumbles a lot and sounds like he smokes a pack a day). His handwriting is terrible, and if you are confused and try to ask questions, he is not helpful. By the end of the semester his lectures were almost empty. The only way I learned was by teaching myself or at recitation. DO NOT take him.

Prof. Engman was extremely poor at communicating what he was teaching. He would just write illegibly on the board and not be clear about what he was writing or saying. The tests were fairly straightforward and similar to the practice tests, but I wouldn't take him again.

Mumbles a lot and talks into the board during lecture as he writes on the chalkboard. Tests seemed fair enough, but he does not curve and calculates your grade by just adding everything so its out of 500 or something. Homework was 3 mymathlab assignments and 3 written ones from textbook (not sure why we even had to use mymathlab with 3 homeworks).

A cool guy, helpful during office hours and obviously very smart, but the grading is harsh. He expects you to memorize everything but only tests a few things, so I always felt like I was wasting my study time. A lot of the homework is optional, but if you don't do at least most of it your grade will suffer.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Test are reasonable but if you make a few small mistakes, it can easily drop your grade. He is against curving the class and has a set grading scale. If you make  below an 80 on 1 test, it is very difficult to bring it up to an A. It is easy to learn from the book and in recitation. He has really bad handwriting and is difficult to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I found him really difficult to understand so lectures weren't helpful, and I relied on the book.  He has very few things he grades on (6 hws and 3 test + final) and there is absolutely no curve on anything.  He gives a recommended hw list  and you should absolutely do it.  Tests are pretty straight forward but some discontinuity in grading.

Marty is pretty cool, especially if you go talk to him in his office. All of his test questions are straightforward except the last one which will always be a challenging problem. It can be difficult to follow along with lectures. Make sure you do extra problems in addition to the homework, because it won't cover everything  you need to know.

Marty is an awesome person and is very entertaining to listen too. He is pretty good at explaining the calculus stuff, but not as good at explaining the linear algebra. His tests were EXTREMELY difficult. We got extra credit on the first test, but only on the first test. The averages were all C's or failing, but he doesn't curve AT ALL.

Marty is a really cool guy, and I really liked him as a person, but as a teacher...His tests were difficult and he DOES NOT curve. He grades on a weird scale by adding up total points. I attended every lecture and I ended up only a few points from a B, because the third test and the final were both terrible (really bad averages!).

While he was pretty nice as a person, his class was unnecessarily hard (fill in the blank TESTS & quizzes). You should attend class b.c he drops your lowest test grade, but I missed out on that. Do the extra credit, or you're SOL. I got an A, & he went over things you really should know in gen psych, but don't take this if you don't have to.

While he is not a bad teacher, I would say his class just isn't worth the difficulty level. His tests do not test critical thinking but instead require you to remember random vocabulary words that could have appeared only once before. I do not feel that his assessment style is fair to students, and he doesn't grade on a curve.
Great teacher, interesting lectures, but weekly quizzes mean you must keep up with the reading or you are screwed.

awesome lectures. very good instructor. supposed to be the hardest section of psych 1101, but the class is very interesting and by the end of the semester he knows everyone's name which is really awesome (you dont see this a lot at tech). great teacher overall. i would reccommend to any psych major.

Supposedly the hardest section for Psych 1101 but he did a great job in not making the lectures dull as hell, which they shouldn't be but somehow other teachers can make them that way. The quizzes are sometimes very detailed and tricky though.
Great!  Goes out of his way, compared to 99% of the teachers at Tech.

Not bad, but not outstanding. If you don't like proofing as much as I do, I was OK in class skipping lecture most days and going to studio with a fantastic TA. Homework is a decent amount of effort. The complexity of the material increases by a large margin.I had a hard time comprehending what she was saying and thought the lectures to be useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not bad, not great. Really proof heavy, so if you don't like that like me, I was fine in the class skipping lecture most days and attending studio with a great TA. Homework is pretty reasonable. Material increases in difficulty by a pretty significant margin, so start off the first couple midterms well.
Her exams are just like what she taught us in class. She is super kind and she even wrote me an email when I missed a quiz on accident.

Professor Steinbart is a great lecturer and know the material very well. Homeworks are reasonable (1 every week). Tests were difficult but fair, we were given a practice exam with similar questions. Definitely recommend taking her for 2551 if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She teaches well. We had tech issues for a bit but its good now. She is by far the best multi option. PROFESSORS MATTER FOR MULTI (things arent standardized). Her tests were pretty straightforward and quizzes exactly like homework (but no partial credit on quizzes due to MML). *note this was a COVID class so tests/quizzes may be different format

So, if you're just learning Calculus for the first time, I can't say how this will go for you. I took Calculus in high school, and this class was a breeze. Just make sure you understand the material, DO ALL THE HOMEWORK, and go to lecture. You'll be fine doing those things - her class shouldn't be that hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Had a very hard time understanding what she taught, and found the lectures unhelpful. Highly recommend taking a different teacher if you haven't taken the content before

Gives a lot of work. She's very approachable and sweet, but she makes every student work hard for their grades. Recommend attending lectures and making sure you understand the material in the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The mic always broke so nobody could hear her, and she wasn't good at explaining concepts anyway. If you get a good TA it might be different, but mine was only interested in showing off his own knowledge. I learned everything on my own on the online homework. No crib sheet, so lots of memorizing formulas. Take someone else if you can.

Ok so she is a really nice person, but her class is tough. I lost a lot of points because she had weekly quizzes which were worth 25% of the grade in the end. I would say make sure to give you all from the beginning because she doesn't curve or give any extra credit. Other proffs had huge curves with similar grades, so I wish I had someone else.

reviews.comment: Worst Professor I've had at Tech.

Prof Steinbart is extremely sweet and caring. Her lectures are proof heavy, which I'm not the biggest fan of, but she understands the concepts very well. There are weekly quizzes (get harder) and only 2 midterms but I found that more helpful. I personally learned a lot of the material on my own but she is extremely sweet and open to questions.
Good professor. Lectures are long but she has good examples. Homework and tests are straightforward.

Her lectures were extremely important. It didn't always make sense because she did teach a lot in terms of variables but she made up for it by including examples and provides realistic practice problems. She was a great teacher and was really trying to get feedback from students and help them based on the feedback. Tests are straightforward.
Lectures are long but useful, and homework is relatively easy. Dr. Steinbart is really responsive to feedback. She makes a lot of typos and writing errors, but otherwise she's great

Professor Steinbart is a great professor. Although sometimes what she says can be a little bit hard to understand simply because sometimes her terminology gets a little messed up, she is very willing to help you. Her tests are really easy and very fair. Also, she really cares about our feedback. She has lots of proof based lectures which I enjoyed.
I really liked the way she taught the class; her lectures were pretty engaging for a math class. Grading is super fair, and as long as you pay attention the class is manageable.

Lectures are long but worth going to, just be ready for lots of proofs that you won't be expected to know. She works lots of examples that are similar to what you'll see on a test. She's very approachable and wants to help her students. Tests are manageable. Only get 3 tries on MyMathLab homework questions.

Dr. Steinbart is a great instructor. She is well prepared every lecture. She will provide worksheets and chapter outlines. She will clarify  topics and concepts before moving on. Very approachable. Also the class is fairly easy provided you READ the chapter and take good notes. Using logic and proofs is a must for this class. Overall, you'll learn.

For Linear Algebra I highly recommend her. If you do your homework, pay attention, read the book, and not fall behind, you'll be fine, she's not cruel in her exams, and she tests in stuff that was covered.

Her class is tough but fair. Lecture can be confusing at times with all the proofs she does, but you're not tested on them. The exams don't throw curveballs at you but will really see if you know the material. The final was tougher than the regular exams but I passed it and got a B in the class (she says the class isn't curved, but I think it was).

Take her! She explains things well and gives handouts to make the lectures more bearable. She's helpful outside of class and cares. It's a lot of material, so the course moves quickly, but she covers everything well. Weekly quizzes, some graded homework, 3 tests and a final to check that you're keeping up. So keep up and you'll be fine.

Take her! She explains things well and provides handouts to help make the lectures more bearable. It's easy to talk to her outside of class and she seems to care about the students. It's a lot of material, but she only asks that you learn it -- some graded homework, easy weekly quizzes, 3 tests, and an exam.

Ok teacher but does nothing but proofs during lecture and makes things more difficult than they appear.  She does not curve at ALL!!  i made all B's on the tests and the class average was always in the 60's or 50's and there was no curve!!
HATE HER. does not curve

She loves to ask too much proof on her exam problems. If she asks you to prove that the integral of a certain function within a closed contour is a certain value, she also expects you (implicitly!) to find out what if the function is outside the contour, or she takes out points from your answer! Come on!

She flew through the material. Explained concepts clearly but did very few example problem. Seemed bothered when students asked questions in class. If you can learn from a book this prof. is for you. You better have a good TA thats all I have to say.

If you do not know what polar coordinates are or you have not taken calculus, then you do not belong in this class. Period. If you want to learn Complex Analysis at a brisk clip, then take this class. There is plenty of homework, the tests follow from it, and grading is fair. Leave plenty of time to take this course, as the workload is constant.

uh...don't take her. She goes way too fast, have quiz every week (which counts for significan't % of ur mark) exams are hard, lecture is boring and uses ****ty book written by one of her colleagues, (gatech prof) which is impossible to understand...

Bro was one of those teachers who was too smart to explain content as a teacher. Worst averages on his exams out of any section and would never curve. Only reason I got an A was from watching other teachers lectures.
if you're not religious then pick a religion and pray.

Genuinely take any other professor. Tests were triple as hard as any other class. 2/3 midterms had failing averages. Final also had failing average. He doesn't care to curve the class and you will get a lower grade. Grading scheme is also worse than other professors. On the way to exams I wished I got run over. Please don't do this to yourself!

Exams were hard, and the content was challenging, but realistically, if you paid attention in class and followed his examples, you would be prepared for the exams. Finals were an easy way to improve your grade in class. The professor got much better at explaining the content by the end of the semester.

literally take anyone else for multi. the worst professor i have ever had. he doesn't know how to explain anything in a way that makes sense, exams are extremely difficult to the point he can't even curve them because everyone would STILL be failing his class. genuinely the worst class and professor i have ever had.

I would not take him for Math 2551 because he doesn't explain material well and what we learn in class is almost never applied to what the exam is testing us on. He also makes the exams harder compared to all other teachers (Average of a 46 on the 3rd midterm). He also believes failing is a good grade, so don't assume he will ever curve.

I've truly tried to give this professor the benefit of the doubt. I've gone to tutoring, used all my resources, but he teaches as if we're already at his level and tests us on things he barely covers or explains in class. The midterm averages have been failing, yet he refuses to curve despite this. I'm sorry, but not curving a 46 average is INSANE

Do not take this class. Lectures are incredibly confusing, and going to class did not help at all. The midterms are very difficult and test on things that were barely taught. The averages on the midterms are very low, but when asked to curve, he says no. Worst professor I've had by far.

He doesn't know how to teach. Lectures only made things more confusing, so everyone resorted to watching Lehmann's lectures online and teaching themselves multi. Still, he wrote stupid exams where every average was failing (3rd was a 46), and refused to curve the exams or the class. Even with full HW and Quiz credit, I barely scraped by with a B.

Useless lectures, everyone stopped showing up after the first 2 weeks when they realized its impossible to keep up with him and his lack of structure when you could watch Lehmann's lectures. Lowest averages and hardest exams, had to grind out of getting a C after being 10-20 points above the mean on exams and having full HW/quiz credit. DONT TAKE
